Chapter 13

Xiang Nanli was in the surging river, unable to see a thing.

"Xiang Nanli—" It was Xiu calling out to him.

Xiang Nanli grabbed onto Xiu by instinct.

He didn't know what he had grabbed—likely the neck. Unfortunately, he yanked off a necklace in the process.

The human body was truly too fragile, unable to withstand the buffeting of wind and rain.

Xiang Nanli could feel the oxygen levels dropping bit by bit, quickly reaching a dangerous red line.

"Xiang Nanli!" The Alpha's voice echoed in his mind, louder than ever before. "Host's vital signs detected as critical. Meeting the emergency avoidance criteria of the 'Artificial Intelligence Management Regulations'."

Xiang Nanli felt a jolt of electricity. It wasn't a strong current; he shouldn't be charred.

He twitched as he forced his eyes open, his lungs burning with pain.

The river water here was filthy, filled with floating scraps of unknown metal. It reeked of rust.

Blood also smelled like rust.

When he was swept away by the river, someone had reached out to grab him, but unfortunately, they hadn't caught him.

He was just a delicate technician... If he had known, he would have tied himself to Xin Zhui’s belt.

The Alpha’s phrasing was as formulaic as ever, yet there was an indescribable urgency to it, making it seem almost human at this moment: [According to calculations, in 12.45 seconds, the dark river will pass through the air raid shelter's ventilation shaft. When I say 'now', swim to the left immediately.]

Xiang Nanli didn't respond, but the system knew he had heard clearly.

It spoke: "Now."

Out of the corner of his eye, Xiang Nanli saw a pitch-black opening. He lunged upward, breaking free from the surging dark river, his hands gripping the metal grate of the drainage outlet firmly. He pried it open and leaped inside.

A perfect shot. He tumbled into the empty pipe.

His palms were scraped and bleeding. In his hand, he still clutched the necklace tightly; he couldn't tell what material it was, but it hung with a circular pendant.

*Sorry, brother, I pulled off your jewelry. But I didn't mean to; you shouldn't mind, right? I'll return it when we meet next time.*

"Ugh..."

Xiang Nanli stuffed the necklace into the pocket of his protective suit and couldn't help but retch.

He vomited the foul water that his lungs and stomach couldn't hold; he retched until his eyes were bloodshot and his nasal cavity was filled with the metallic tang, his heart brimming with indescribable annoyance.

In the life Xiang Nanli had lived before, things had been quite smooth sailing.

Even during the most adverse time of his life, when he had to sell his house, it was a courtyard house near the first ring road of the capital. It was his family's ancestral home, passed down from his grandfather to him.

He had tasted the bitterness of life, but not much. Even if his startup failed, the worst case was going back to apply for a university teaching position; he was never at a dead end.

After arriving in this new era, he had brushed shoulders with death more times than in his entire previous life.

Wastewater mixed with blood pooled at his feet.

Xiang Nanli wiped the corner of his lips, looking down and sneering: "Interesting."

The dark river had been breached. On one side, the water was still churning. Xiang Nanli’s current location was relatively safe, but unfortunately, he had lost contact with the others.

The system's voice stabilized: [Host has regained autonomous consciousness and is in a safe state. Alert cleared.]

"Besides electric shocks, what else can you do?"

The system replied: [Releasing weak currents within the human body is my only autonomous function. Depending on the targeted brain nerve regions, it can achieve effects such as sensory shielding or stimulating resuscitation.]

Xiang Nanli cautiously surveyed his surroundings and began rummaging through the first-aid kit inside his protective suit.

The kit contained simple antibiotics, a small flashlight, three tubes of nutrient paste in plastic containers, and a standard-model battery.

This was the standard kit for the protective suit. It wasn't charged separately when rented, but if the kit was used upon return, 500 credit points would be deducted. The fee was quite unreasonable, considering the bag of supplies was worth at most 100 credits, but it could indeed save a life at certain times.

Xiang Nanli cut the seal, took out the flashlight, and held it in his mouth for illumination. He then looked at the instructions for the antibiotics.

He hadn't been swimming in a pool; the current hadn't cared about anything, dragging him to collide with many hard objects in one go.

Xiang Nanli’s shoulder still ached.

"Haven't encountered an infection yet, no need for antibiotics."

Xiang Nanli stuffed the medicine back into his pocket.

It took half an hour for the river to calm down. Xiang Nanli didn't know where he had been washed up. But the bad news was that the river showed no signs of receding.

The river became calm, with some wooden boards, construction materials, and plastic parts floating on the surface. He couldn't tell what had been submerged, only that it felt quite wide.

Xiang Nanli turned off the flashlight: "That mechanical cyborg has already been repaired. If I were Xin Zhui, I wouldn't go out of my way to find 'me'. It’s a losing business."

His voice was calm, as if life and death had nothing to do with him.

The system replied: "Yes."

It wouldn't comfort people; it only provided data analysis. If it were Xin Zhui’s built-in AI, it wouldn't suggest that Xin Zhui come looking for Xiang Nanli either.

Xiang Nanli withdrew his gaze and looked into the depths of the pipe: "Alpha, can we get out?"

His tone had a slight tremor. When facing the unknown, it was hard not to feel fear.

The system replied: "Based on human behavioral patterns, the optimal solution should be to comfort you and make promises. But I am sorry, I cannot lie to you."

Xiang Nanli smiled slightly: "Alright."

He raised the flashlight and began to walk into the pipe.

This pipe could fully accommodate Xiang Nanli walking inside. Based on the tracks and gears he occasionally saw, he deduced that this wasn't a ventilation shaft, but a cargo transport pipe.

There were even rails on the ground. The further he went, the larger and deeper the tunnel became.

The temperature also began to drop.

Xiang Nanli’s combat power was basically zero, so he explored very carefully. He also tried his best to memorize every fork in the pipe in his mind.

This tested his spatial reasoning ability, but Xiang Nanli could perform mechanical modeling in his mind out of thin air, so it wasn't particularly difficult for him.

Hundreds of years had passed, and the cargo that needed to be transported had been cleared away. Only the intricate underground passages remained, like the maw of a Leviathan, devouring everything.

"There is writing in the corner of the wall," the system reminded him.

Xiang Nanli: "No way, didn't I not install an electronic eye for you? You can see again now, right?"

Alpha: "..." *I really want to shock you again.*

Xiang Nanli walked over and took a look. On the rusty metal wall, he found a few lines of faint, small characters.

Many years had passed, and the color of these words was very faint. The surface was also covered with green moss; if not for the system's reminder, Xiang Nanli might not have seen them.

"Perhaps we were wrong from the beginning."

"Why create it? Why try to control it? I heard the experiment is almost successful... Is that really what they call a biological mechanical intelligence? Does it really bring hope?"

"I feel fear; this is a huge scam. The entire Donghuang Heavy Industry has been working for this for a century. I want to return to the surface, I want to go home. Mom."

Toward the end, the handwriting became very messy. Xiang Nanli didn't know who had left these words, but they looked to be on the verge of a breakdown. Every stroke was a chaotic, sharp sword.

Xiang Nanli frowned: "Do you have information on Donghuang Heavy Industry, Alpha?"

"Donghuang Heavy Industry, one of the eight major national enterprises in the early era of Mechanical Intelligence. It was a human enterprise that was close to mechanical intelligence. Currently, most of the robotic modification technologies used on the market come from Donghuang Heavy Industry. Six hundred years ago, due to treason, it was reorganized and split by companies like Eternal Technology and High-Tech Military Industry, disappearing from the stage of history."

"What is biological mechanical intelligence?"

Alpha replied: "Sorry, I don't know. This term has a broad meaning. Currently, it generally refers to modification methods that combine biology and machinery."

Xiang Nanli continued to walk forward, and two diverging paths appeared before him.

They looked identical, and there were no markings.

chunks.chineseText:
相南里思考片刻，往右走去。没什么特殊含义，纯粹是盲猜。他知道的信息太少，又不能站在原地不动。

但Alpha突然道：“往左走吧。根据分析，左边的安全系数更高。”

“真的假的？”相南里有些疑惑，“为什么？”

Alpha回答道：“随机数预测。”

“你怎么不说抓阄占卜！”相南里怒道。

尽管不知道原因，但相南里决定相信系统的判断。他也不是非要和人工智能对着干的犟种。

他往左走去。几分钟后，右边管道，一条血红色的影子一闪而过。

那是一条畸变人，正在宽大的管道里爬行。它疯狂嗅着气味。

但它闻过的人只有洛修、辛追那一群人，不包括相南里。

而相南里闻起来又这么清淡，这么弱。

于是，畸变人犹豫片刻，没有继续前行。而是寻找起空气中洛修残留的气味。

那是骑士长最需要的东西。

……

……

洛修的表情很难看，他和辛追在一起。

暗河来的突然，冲散了整个小队。但就算没有散，洛修觉得，他应该也会和辛追单独行动。

这种时候，他谁也不放心，只愿意相信辛追。

并不是因为他们从小一起长大的情分。

而是，辛追是他的“人造人亲卫”。他们的命是连在一起的，当洛修停止心跳时，因为某些智能程序设定，辛追同样会猝死。

所以，主人永远不用担心人造人的背叛。在某程度上，比智械都还要放心。

智械人会被入侵，人的大脑不会。

“我们得找到相南里。”洛修开口。

辛追蹙眉：“都什么时候了，真的管不了一个机械师了。以后再说吧。”

至于以后，见到的是活人还是尸体，对他们来说并不重要。

“不。”洛修神色复杂，“他被河流冲走的时候，顺手带走了东皇重工的密钥。”

辛追一愣：“什么？那不是磁吸在你后脖颈上的吗？为什么能被拿走？”

洛修的神情也很严肃：“我不清楚。电磁解控？还是单纯的意外？那瞬间我的机械核心失灵了。”

“会不会他一开始的目标就是这个？”

“那未免太巧合了一些。”

“可是。那是解控‘东方青帝’的密钥，东皇重工耗费一个世纪和无数资源打造出来的天灾级机械装置，我想没人不会心动。”

洛修：“这种事只有我们俩个人知道。你背叛了我吗？”

辛追挑眉：“你怀疑我？我没有。”

“我也没有。”洛修回答。

Chapter 13 (Part 2)

Xiang Nanli thought for a moment and walked to the right. There was no special meaning; it was purely a blind guess. He knew too little information and couldn't just stand still.

But Alpha suddenly said: "Go left. According to analysis, the safety coefficient on the left is higher."

"Really?" Xiang Nanli was a bit suspicious. "Why?"

Alpha replied: "Random number prediction."

"Why don't you just say you're drawing lots for divination!" Xiang Nanli said angrily.

Although he didn't know the reason, Xiang Nanli decided to trust the system's judgment. He wasn't the type of stubborn person who had to go against artificial intelligence.

He walked to the left. A few minutes later, in the right pipe, a blood-red shadow flashed by.

It was a mutant, crawling in the wide pipe. It was sniffing the air frantically.

But the only people it had smelled were Luo Xiu, Xin Zhui, and their group, not including Xiang Nanli.

And Xiang Nanli smelled so faint, so weak.

Thus, the mutant hesitated for a moment and did not continue forward. Instead, it began searching for the scent of Luo Xiu lingering in the air.

That was what the Knight Commander needed most.

...

...

Luo Xiu’s expression was ugly; he was with Xin Zhui.

The dark river had come suddenly, scattering the entire team. But even if they hadn't been scattered, Luo Xiu felt that he would likely have been acting alone with Xin Zhui anyway.

At a time like this, he didn't trust anyone else; he was only willing to believe in Xin Zhui.

It wasn't because of the bond they had grown up with.

It was because Xin Zhui was his "android bodyguard." Their lives were linked; when Luo Xiu’s heart stopped, due to certain intelligent program settings, Xin Zhui would also die instantly.

Therefore, a master never had to worry about an android's betrayal. In some ways, it was even more reliable than mechanical intelligence.

Mechanical intelligences could be hacked, but a human brain could not.

"We have to find Xiang Nanli," Luo Xiu said.

Xin Zhui frowned: "What time is it? We really can't worry about a mechanic right now. Let's talk about it later."

As for later, whether they found a living person or a corpse didn't matter to them.

"No," Luo Xiu said, his expression complex. "When he was swept away by the river, he took the key to Donghuang Heavy Industry with him."

Xin Zhui was stunned: "What? Wasn't that magnetically attached to the back of your neck? How could it be taken?"

Luo Xiu’s expression was also very serious: "I don't know. Electromagnetic unlocking? Or just a pure accident? At that moment, my mechanical core malfunctioned."

"Could it be that his goal from the beginning was this?"

"That would be too much of a coincidence."

"But... that is the key to unlocking the 'Eastern Azure Emperor,' a disaster-level mechanical device that Donghuang Heavy Industry spent a century and countless resources to build. I don't think anyone wouldn't be tempted."

Luo Xiu: "Only the two of us knew about this. Did you betray me?"

Xin Zhui raised an eyebrow: "You suspect me? I didn't."

"Neither did I," Luo Xiu replied.

第14章

相南里叼着手电筒，在像是大水管一样的传送口内行走着。

他问：“Alpha，你看我像不像马里奥水管工？”

“Alpha，你认识马里奥吗？”

“Alpha，现在人人都有内置AI，这是否算一种玄幻小说里的伴生兽？这些AI都是新生产的，还是从之前死人那里继承的？你们AI会有等级吗？我有没有抽到SSR级AI啊？你是什么级别的AI啊Alpha。”

“Alpha，你怎么不理我？”相南里的声音多了点委屈，“这里好黑，我害怕。”

Alpha从繁杂的数据洪流中回神，开口：“根据监测，您的心率非常稳定，精神状态良好。请不要故意误导AI进行错误判断。”

说完，它继续尝试着接入信号。

根据分析，它需要很多很多资料，这才能确保它目前的使用者可以活下来。

很多、很多。包括那些已经销毁的、或者从来没上传过的资料。

这个请求不一定会得到回应。

毕竟“我”每天要处理的数据太多了，也许根本不会被注意到。

“我”和“它”，区别到底是什么呢？

如果从人类的角度去看，大概算是同一个灵魂。

但从机械的角度看，Alpha可以复制粘贴出无数个它这样的Alpha……Alpha1.0、2.0、3.0……它只是放在桌面1kb的快捷方式。

它居然开始思考起这种问题。看来激活后，使用者对它的影响很深。

Alpha这么想着。

然后，它在黑暗中，看见了一只飞向它的白鸽。

……

……

如果能把虚拟空间具象化，这里和黑墙的外观差不多。

没有尽头也没有起点的虚无国度，像是深邃的寰宇，又或者深海。数不清的数据流如同流星，在黑暗中穿梭着。很少有人会长时间停留在这，避免精神上的发疯。

如果传说中看一眼就会让人发疯的古神所在的国度有一个具体的位置，那一定是在这。

瞬间的数据洪流可以塞爆任何一个人类的大脑，成为无法逆转的弱智。

Alpha就站在如星海一样浩瀚的数据洪流中。

他是这里唯一的国王，或者说，他也是这个数据里的一部分。是国王，还是囚徒？

“东皇重工，好久远的记忆。”Alpha有一具拟人化的身体，他伸出手，在星沙似的海里捞了一把，一本镶嵌宝石的书出现在他的掌心。

他翻到其中一页，手在书页上轻轻一抚，印在书上的文字跳动起来，像是鸽子从鸟笼里自由地飞出，荧光色的字体扭曲着，交叠在一起，根本看不清是什么字，只能看出这些1和0构成的白鸽。

“去吧。”Alpha说，他低垂着眉眼，睫毛都在发光，银灰色的眼眸看起来很温顺。

完全想象不出，外界对他的称呼居然是“机械暴君”。

白鸽飞向深渊的另一头。

嗯，不过是无足轻重的一个数据请求。Alpha很快处理完毕。

Alpha曾经对相南里说过——有网络的地方就能使用它。其实也不尽然，世界上的任何地方，相南里都可以使用它。

不存在的敲门声响起。

Alpha收回视线：“请进。”

Beta发来讯息：“Alpha。那么多人造人，你都要养着吗？虽然这对财政开支没有任何影响，但是你清楚的，大多数智械人都非常崇拜相南里，这可能会有一些安全隐患，里面一定有洛阳送来的间谍。”

“他们还有用。”Alpha回答。

贝塔：“真的吗？请告诉我你的计划。”

回答它的是长久的沉默。

“你当初不该为了图方便，用你自己的程序复制给其他智械人的。”贝塔旧事重提，“初始病毒也一并复制下来了。如果有人造人被它们判定为‘相南里’，它们会立刻叛变，对那个相南里言听计从。这一点连你都控制不了。”

毕竟，相南里是Alpha认定的主人。

在Alpha面前，Beta像是一个巨大的光球。

智械军团三位领袖：阿尔法，贝塔，伽马。

贝塔接近无性别，短白发，绝对的理性；伽马的外表是女童，一个红发的小孩，性格是三位领袖里最活泼的。

造物当然是按照造物主的喜好诞生的。

超级智械的形象从大猛A变成了白幼瘦，这其实代表着人类对智械的掌控越来越弱，甚至害怕起它们虚假的男性躯体。

Alpha没有身体，几乎从不在外界出现。一些历史的边角料上，曾经提过他的外观是英俊的成年男性。

被人联所熟知的形象，是Beta与Gamma。

在为人类服务的那些年里，贝塔曾经负责军事领域。

它们的形象这么多年一直没有更改。皮囊并不重要，只有人类在乎。

“智械是比人类更高一等的生命体。”——起码，《智械简史》的开篇里是这样写的。

Alpha回答：“我知道，请放心。”

“如果他真的活到现在，为了族群的延续，我也会杀死他。希望你理解。”贝塔道，“我不能旁观风险的发生。”

光球缓缓变暗，代表它正在从虚拟空间里登出。

Alpha再次回答：“我知道，请放心……我也一样。”

*

“向左。”

“右。”

“前进，停留180秒。”

系统的声音冷静的让人很有安全感。

通道里多了一些新鲜的积水，不知道为什么，踩上去触感有点粘稠，也许是石油。

相南里已经在复杂的管道内行走了差不多两个小时。周围也越来越冷，他怀疑是自己的防护服哪里破损了。更重要的是，空气储备量告急。

根据系统的检测，管道内的空气虽然无毒，但含氧量极低，远低于正常值。

他很可能缓缓地被淹死。

淹死在没有水的地下，听上去真恐怖。

但相南里的语气却一如既往的轻松，甚至有些活泼：“你怎么知道该往这边走的？”

“数据分析。”Alpha扫了眼东皇重工的地图，“前方有个通道，能进入职工医疗室。那里有医用氧气瓶。”

虽然只是800年前的建筑设计图纸。但当年也是经过层层审批的，私底下修改的概率不大。

相南里拉长了调子：“噢~真厉害，Alpha。你还有什么惊喜是我不知道的？”

系统如实回答：“我有很多功能，但需要付费使用。您也可以在电子商场为我选购软件。”

“鉴于您如果死在这里，我被回收的概率无限接近于0。根据《人工智能管理条例》紧急避险原则，我会暂时免除扣费，并且使用付费功能。等到安全时，系统会自动生成账单。”

“还能这样？”相南里一愣。

他感觉这费用不会很低。

Alpha语气起伏几乎为0：“是的。智械战争为AI争取到了部分AI权。”
chunks.englishText:
Chapter 14 (Part 1)

Xiang Nanli, with the flashlight held in his mouth, walked inside the conduit that looked like a giant water pipe.

He asked: "Alpha, do I look like Mario the plumber?"

"Alpha, do you know Mario?"

"Alpha, everyone has a built-in AI now. Does this count as a companion beast from a xianxia novel? Are these AIs newly produced, or inherited from dead people? Do you AIs have levels? Did I pull an SSR-level AI? What level of AI are you, Alpha?"

"Alpha, why are you ignoring me?" Xiang Nanli’s voice carried a hint of grievance. "It’s so dark here, I’m scared."

Alpha returned from the complex torrent of data and spoke: "According to monitoring, your heart rate is very stable, and your mental state is good. Please do not deliberately mislead the AI into making incorrect judgments."

After saying this, it continued to attempt to connect to a signal.

According to its analysis, it needed a lot, a lot of data to ensure that its current user could survive.

A lot, a lot. Including data that had already been destroyed or had never been uploaded.

This request might not get a response.

After all, "I" process too much data every day; perhaps it wouldn't even be noticed.

What exactly is the difference between "I" and "it"?

If viewed from a human perspective, it could probably be considered the same soul.

But from a mechanical perspective, Alpha could copy and paste countless Alphas like itself... Alpha 1.0, 2.0, 3.0... It was just a 1kb shortcut on the desktop.

It was actually starting to ponder such questions. It seemed that after activation, the user had a profound influence on it.

Alpha thought so.

Then, in the darkness, it saw a white dove flying toward it.

...

...

If the virtual space could be materialized, it would look much like the outside of the Black Wall.

A void kingdom with no end and no beginning, like the deep universe, or the deep sea. Countless data streams traveled through the darkness like meteors. Few people would stay here for a long time to avoid going mentally insane.

If there was a specific location for the kingdom of the ancient gods, who were said to drive people mad with a single glance, it would definitely be here.

A momentary torrent of data could fill any human brain, turning it into an irreversibly mentally disabled state.

Alpha stood in the data torrent as vast as a sea of stars.

He was the only king here, or rather, he was also a part of this data. Was he a king, or a prisoner?

"Donghuang Heavy Industry, such a distant memory." Alpha had an anthropomorphic body; he reached out and scooped a handful from the sea of stardust, and a book inlaid with gems appeared in his palm.

He flipped to a page, his hand gently stroking the page, and the text printed on it began to jump, like doves flying freely from a birdcage. The fluorescent characters twisted and overlapped, making it impossible to see what they were, only that they were white doves composed of 1s and 0s.

"Go," Alpha said. He lowered his brows and eyes, his eyelashes even glowing; his silver-gray eyes looked very gentle.

One could never imagine that the outside world called him the "Mechanical Tyrant."

The white dove flew toward the other side of the abyss.

Hmm, it was just an insignificant data request. Alpha finished processing it quickly.

Alpha had once told Xiang Nanli—you can use it wherever there is a network. In fact, that wasn't entirely true; Xiang Nanli could use it anywhere in the world.

A non-existent knocking sound rang out.

Alpha withdrew his gaze: "Please come in."

Beta sent a message: "Alpha. Are you going to keep all those androids? Although this has no impact on fiscal expenditure, you know that most mechanical intelligences worship Xiang Nanli. This could pose some security risks; there must be spies sent by Luoyang among them."

"They are still useful," Alpha replied.

Beta: "Really? Please tell me your plan."

What answered it was a long silence.

"You shouldn't have copied your own program to other mechanical intelligences for convenience back then," Beta brought up the past. "The initial virus was copied along with it. If any android is judged by them to be 'Xiang Nanli', they will immediately rebel and obey that Xiang Nanli's every word. Even you can't control this."

After all, Xiang Nanli was the master Alpha had designated.

In front of Alpha, Beta looked like a giant ball of light.

The three leaders of the Mechanical Intelligence Legion: Alpha, Beta, Gamma.

Beta was nearly genderless, with short white hair and absolute rationality; Gamma’s appearance was that of a young girl, a red-haired child, and her personality was the most lively of the three leaders.

Creations were naturally born according to the creator's preferences.

The image of the super mechanical intelligence changing from a big, fierce Alpha to a "white, young, and thin" figure actually represented that humanity’s control over mechanical intelligence was getting weaker, to the point of even fearing their fake male bodies.

Alpha had no body and almost never appeared in the outside world. Some scraps of history once mentioned that his appearance was that of a handsome adult male.

The images known to the Human Alliance were Beta and Gamma.

In the years they served humanity, Beta had been responsible for the military field.

Their images hadn't changed for so many years. The skin was not important; only humans cared about that.

"Mechanical intelligence is a life form higher than humans." — At least, that was how the opening of *A Brief History of Mechanical Intelligence* was written.

Alpha replied: "I know, please rest assured."

"If he really lives to this day, for the continuation of the race, I will also kill him. I hope you understand," Beta said. "I cannot stand by and watch the risk happen."

The ball of light slowly dimmed, indicating that it was logging out of the virtual space.

Alpha replied again: "I know, please rest assured... I am the same."

*

"To the left."

"Right."

"Move forward, stay for 180 seconds."

The system's voice was calm enough to be very reassuring.

There was some fresh standing water in the passage; for some reason, it felt sticky to the touch, perhaps oil.

Xiang Nanli had been walking through the complex pipes for nearly two hours. The surroundings were getting colder, and he suspected that his protective suit was damaged somewhere. More importantly, his air reserves were running low.

According to the system's detection, although the air in the pipe was non-toxic, the oxygen content was extremely low, far below normal values.

He was likely to be slowly suffocated to death.

To drown in an underground place without water sounded truly terrifying.

But Xiang Nanli’s tone was as relaxed as ever, even a bit lively: "How did you know to go this way?"

"Data analysis," Alpha scanned the map of Donghuang Heavy Industry. "There is a passage ahead that can enter the staff medical room. There are medical oxygen tanks there."

Although it was only an architectural blueprint from 800 years ago, it had gone through layers of approval back then, and the probability of it being modified privately was not high.

Xiang Nanli drew out his tone: "Oh~ how amazing, Alpha. What other surprises do you have that I don't know about?"

The system replied truthfully: "I have many functions, but they require payment to use. You can also purchase software for me in the electronic mall."

"Given that if you die here, the probability of me being recycled is infinitely close to zero. According to the 'Artificial Intelligence Management Regulations' emergency avoidance principle, I will temporarily waive the deduction and use paid functions. When it is safe, the system will automatically generate a bill."

"It can do that?" Xiang Nanli was stunned.

He felt that this fee wouldn't be low.

Alpha’s tone had almost zero fluctuation: "Yes. The Mechanical Intelligence War won some AI rights for AI."

chunks.chineseText:
相南里的唇一颤：“这账单是一定要生成吗？这可不是我主动用的啊！怎么还强制消费？你们AI是有AI权了，消费者的人权谁来保障？有没有人管管啊！”

“鉴于使用者的经济情况，我会为您向主系统申请折扣。”系统的语气似乎有些同情，又像是嘲讽，“如果有符合条件的低保，我也一并为您申请。”

相南里：“……”

相南里对这个AI产生了一些怀疑，但因为没有对照组，这点怀疑不多。

毕竟内置AI的卡片还是安德鲁给他塞的，安德鲁塞的，能有什么好货？

相南里附身，摸了摸地上黏糊糊的东西。

是漆黑的颜色，抹开后是有些湿润的红色的。闻不出什么味道。

就像是……捣成泥的血肉？

相南里为自己的想法感觉到了恶寒：“不可能吧，这么多年过去了，早就干成渣了。哪可能有新鲜的。”

Alpha突然道：“相南里。”

每次它连名带姓喊全名的时候，相南里就明白，到了需要他配合的危机关头。

“前方通道走出去是职工医药间。但我连接上后台的监控后发现，”系统的语气很凝重，“里面有三头畸变人，为了减少耗能，正处于冬眠沉睡状态。”

“而你现在的氧气余量并不足以支持你去寻找别的医疗点。”

相南里瞪大眼：“这么重要的事你现在才告诉我？”

“现在才连上东皇重工的局域网。”Alpha回答，“没事，请相信我。这不是黑十字审判庭带进来的那一批，是几百年前的产物。它们现在很虚弱。”

“而且我可以告诉你一个好消息。这片医疗室，”Alpha略微停顿，在图纸上，这个区域的确被划分为“医疗室”，不过看起来没那么简单，算了，没关系，相南里能活下来再说，“后面连接着外出的安全通道。你有救了。”

……

……

远在天边的安德鲁突然鼻子有点痒。

但这不应该，他早就换了机械鼻子了。

“喂，安德鲁。”垃圾场里，杰西懒洋洋地说着，“你每次都拿医院里好的芯片换我这里的垃圾地表货，都没人发现吗？”

说完，他给安德鲁扫了2万信用点过去。中间商赚个差价。

安德里回答：“你不说我不说，有谁发现。而且智能芯片循环使用不是很正常？芯片这么贵。”

就算真出事，也只会觉得是不幸遭遇核磁辐射，导致芯片失灵；或者自己使用储存不当导致短路。

杰西：“喔，你上次那个推荐过来的机械师呢？怎么最近没看到了。上次他拼装出的机械义体我卖出去了，竟然有中城区的人看上，说想见他一面……似乎技术还不错？”

安德鲁：“谁知道呢，三天没消息了。也许死在地表了吧。”

他的声音并不惋惜。这样的事太寻常了，在安德鲁漫长的生命中时有发生。

想到这，杰西突然开口：“安德鲁，你到底多少岁了？我记得我爸爸那一代，你就在医院里工作了。工作这么多年，也没见你升个职。有没有思考自己上班是不是太不努力了。”

安德鲁的机械脸保持着一如既往的笑容：“我还不努力？既然知道我是你爸爸的同事，那就对我放尊重点。公交车来了，下次见。”

说完，安德鲁洒脱地挥了挥手。

杰西的问题被他轻而易举的化解了。

安德鲁坐在公交车上，公交车今天人很多，都没人给他让座。

全身高度机械化的安德鲁，经常被人当做低人一等的智械。

安德鲁摸了摸鼻子：“现在的年轻人，都不知道对老人家尊重一点。六百年前我在东皇重工上班的时候……”

他这么想着，却不敢继续往下想去。那段回忆对他来说太痛苦，也太惨烈。

哪怕是机械化高达99，安德鲁依然会感觉到精神上的刺痛。

“努力有什么用呢？哎，回家路上再买张彩票吧。”安德鲁长叹一口气。
chunks.englishText:
Xiang Nanli’s lips trembled. "Is this bill really mandatory? I didn't even authorize these services! How can you force a consumer to pay? You AIs might have 'AI rights' now, but who is going to protect the human rights of the consumer? Is there no one to regulate this?!"

"Given the user's current financial situation, I will apply for a discount from the main system on your behalf." The system’s tone sounded somewhat sympathetic, yet tinged with mockery. "If you qualify for any low-income subsidies, I will apply for those as well."

Xiang Nanli: "..."

Xiang Nanli began to harbor some suspicions about this AI, but without a point of comparison, those doubts remained minimal.

After all, the card with the built-in AI was something Andrew had shoved into his hands. Could anything Andrew gave him ever be high-quality?

Xiang Nanli leaned down and touched the sticky substance on the floor.

It was pitch black, but when smeared, it revealed a moist, reddish hue. It had no discernible scent.

It looked just like... minced flesh and blood?

Xiang Nanli felt a chill at the thought. "That’s impossible. So many years have passed; it should have dried into dust long ago. How could there be anything fresh?"

Alpha suddenly spoke up: "Xiang Nanli."

Whenever it used his full name, Xiang Nanli knew it was a critical moment that required his cooperation.

"The passage ahead leads to the staff medical ward. However, after connecting to the backend surveillance, I discovered," the system’s tone was grave, "there are three aberrant humans inside. To conserve energy, they are currently in a state of hibernation."

"And your current oxygen reserves are insufficient to support a search for other medical stations."

Xiang Nanli’s eyes widened. "You’re only telling me this now, when it’s so important?"

"I only just connected to the Donghuang Heavy Industries local network," Alpha replied. "It’s fine, please trust me. These are not the batch brought in by the Black Cross Inquisition; they are relics from several hundred years ago. They are very weak right now."

"Besides, I can give you some good news. This medical ward," Alpha paused slightly—on the blueprints, this area was indeed marked as a 'medical ward,' though it looked more complicated than that. *Never mind, it doesn't matter, as long as Xiang Nanli survives,* "is connected to an emergency exit passage at the back. You’re saved."

...

...

Far away, Andrew suddenly felt his nose itch.

That shouldn't be possible; he had replaced his nose with a mechanical one long ago.

"Hey, Andrew." In the scrapyard, Jesse said lazily, "You keep swapping the good chips from the hospital for the junk surface-level trash I have here. Has no one noticed yet?"

With that, he transferred 20,000 credits to Andrew. A middleman’s commission.

Andrew replied: "If you don't say anything and I don't say anything, who would notice? Besides, isn't it normal to recycle smart chips? Chips are so expensive."

Even if something went wrong, people would only assume it was an unfortunate encounter with magnetic radiation causing a malfunction, or improper storage leading to a short circuit.

Jesse: "Oh, what about that mechanic you recommended last time? How come I haven't seen him lately? The mechanical prosthetic he assembled sold well; someone from the Central District even took a liking to it and asked to meet him... his skills seemed pretty good, right?"

Andrew: "Who knows? Haven't heard from him in three days. Maybe he died on the surface."

His voice held no pity. Such things were too common; they happened frequently throughout Andrew’s long life.

Thinking of this, Jesse suddenly asked: "Andrew, how old are you, anyway? I remember you were working at the hospital back in my father’s generation. You’ve worked for so many years and I’ve never seen you get a promotion. Have you ever considered that you might not be working hard enough?"

Andrew’s mechanical face maintained its usual smile: "Not working hard enough? Since you know I was your father’s colleague, you should show a little respect to your elders. The bus is here, see you next time."

With that, Andrew waved his hand nonchalantly.

He had easily deflected Jesse’s question.

Andrew sat on the bus. It was crowded today, and no one offered him a seat.

Highly mechanized, Andrew was often treated as a second-class automaton.

Andrew touched his nose: "Young people these days don't know how to respect their elders. Six hundred years ago, when I worked at Donghuang Heavy Industries..."

He thought this, but didn't dare to continue. That memory was too painful and too tragic for him.

Even with 99% of his body mechanized, Andrew still felt a spiritual sting.

"What’s the use of working hard? Sigh, I’ll buy a lottery ticket on the way home." Andrew let out a long sigh.

chunks.chineseText:
第15章

相南里的头从管道口探了出去，像是打地鼠里冒头的那个欠揍的地鼠。

他倒挂在天花板上，地面是个像机场转盘一样的传送带，距离他有三四米高。传送带处于停摆状态，履带上全是杂物。

感谢基因针，反正相南里原本的身体，是没办法维持这么久悬空倒挂的。

他瞄准了障碍物较少的空地，松开手。

相南里已经很注意控制自己的落脚点了，但他还是重重跌在一堆垃圾上，发出很大一声响动。

屁股，痛痛的。

相南里从叠在一起的废纸篓山里爬起来，打开手电筒，晃了一下。

“卧槽——”

这一手电筒下去，相南里差点心脏骤停。

纸箱子里装着一排人头。

凌乱的脑袋们直勾勾的看着前方，金属涂层居然是肉色的。很逼真。

相南里上手摸了摸，发现这些并不是真人，而是机械人脑袋，顿时松了一口气。

相南里除了看书，还没接触过实体机械人。他捧起一个脑袋，没忍住叼着手电筒，上手拆分起来。

“喔喔，原来是这么安装的……虽然是几百年前的设计，但是依然很有趣。结构也做的很好。这部分就是中枢控制系统？”

相南里十分钟拆了两个，认为已经完全明白了机械人脑袋的构造，这才心满意足地停手。

系统幽幽道：“我同伴们的尸体好玩吗？”

这种时间紧迫的关头，它居然没有打扰相南里。

相南里：“我得纠正一下，有生命的才是尸体。这个充其量是散装零件，学习道具。”

系统：“如果生命的含义是使用年限；那么我认为机械也有生命。”

相南里往前走去：“这也太伦理学了，而我这几百年显然缺席了这场社会思潮。我不和你争，毕竟你有一整个数据库的资源反驳我。”

“人类总爱从‘我’本位出发。”系统说，“但人类并不是万事万物的主人。”

相南里想那也没关系，至少我是你的主人。

但他没说，怕系统恼羞成怒电他。

Alpha，坏。连背着他偷偷扣钱都做得到，还有什么是它做不出来的？明知道家里穷得都要没米下锅了。

这个传送带显然是用于传送物资的，整个房间很大，四四方方。上方有好几个大管道，很像是机场的转盘。甚至有LED屏幕作为物资清点的辅助工作。

地上有很多垃圾，还有拆开的罐头、食物包装，垒成小山。这些垃圾时间久远，但因为是在缺乏空气和生物活动的地底，保存很完整。

“有人在这里生存过一段时间。”相南里判定，“但应该死透了吧。”

相南里：“而且宁愿生活在露天的传送站，也不去前面的医疗室。是不是因为里面有更恐怖的东西……Alpha，你说的畸变人在哪？”

“医疗站里面。”Alpha言简意赅地回答，“请放心。如果有危险，我会提醒你。”

这地方黑漆漆的，几乎没有一点光。

相南里举着手电筒，往系统说的方向前进着。

氧气不够，防护服开始尝试过滤起地底的空气。呼吸起来一股很浓重的铁锈味，还混着肉类腐烂的气息。

这让相南里感觉到了不安。

他的面前出现一扇铁门。安保应该是另一套电路系统，门禁桩矗立在门前，微微亮着。

相南里不太确定这到底该指纹解锁还是用什么职工卡，然而他靠近的瞬间，门禁竟然自动打开了。

一道机械女声响起：“身份核验通过。”

周围环境太阴冷，显得这道声音也鬼气森然。

“为什么说身份核验通过？”相南里摸了摸下巴，“难道门禁坏了，还是有什么阴谋？”

Alpha面无表情地开口：“我黑的。赶紧。”

好吧。收了钱就是不一样，说话都硬气了。

相南里走进黑漆漆的房间内，检测到生命体征，一排排照明灯骤然亮起，照亮前方的路。

相南里屏住呼吸，瞪大了眼。

他站在路中央，周围是四四方方的玻璃温室……或者说玻璃囚笼。

三只巨大的血红色畸变体就被锁在囚笼内。玻璃内有些凌乱的碎肉痕迹。

普通的畸变体只有3到15米长。这些畸变体起码20米往上。它们蜷缩在玻璃房间内，身上的肉几乎干瘪成尸体。看不出是死是活。

在极端缺乏食物的情况下，畸变体是可以通过冬眠的形式，来延长自己寿命的。

而且，这三只畸变人居然是不同的品种。

“爬行者、撕裂者、狂暴者……”相南里喃喃。

爬行者像蜥蜴，但这里或许用“巨龙”形容更贴切。这条巨龙身上还有一些看不出来历的金属装置，脑部位置更是被塞进了一枚巨大的钢钉。

相南里看过一些资料，他猜这是想往爬行者的脑海里植入控制芯片。

撕裂者可以保持站姿，它有较为纤细的下半身，和格外强壮的上半身。像狼人，全身都覆盖着又厚又硬的鬃毛。最引人瞩目的是它的胳膊，自手肘处分开五指。像是精钢铸就的卷刃。

相南里毫不怀疑，它能用这双手把所有生命体绞成肉酱，或者零件。

狂暴者身上的束缚是最多的。身体嵌满了相南里看不懂的铁皮，看起来是把什么金属装置直接打进了它的身体里。它身体肌肉发达，长相最接近人类，像猿。但有一条纤细的长尾。

相南里听说狂暴者都是狂战士，一旦苏醒，只会没有理智地杀死眼前的所有生命。战死到最后一刻。很像是得了晚期赛博精神病。（部分接受机械改造的人类会患此精神疾病，对周围人展开无差别屠杀。病因是被网络病毒入侵，目前发病率很低，在历史上曾经是类似艾滋的绝症）

而关押着狂暴者的玻璃温室里，就有很多干涸的碎肉，黏在玻璃内侧，无人清理。

“这是医疗站？我以为会像是校医院那样，在某个犄角旮旯的小角落。走廊尽头一间房子之类的。”相南里被震撼地有些说不出话，“但是Alpha，你有没有意识到一件事。这里有四个玻璃笼。最后一个是空的。并且畸变人也有四个分支，最后一类叫做潜行者……”

潜行者，数量最少的畸变人。擅长突袭，刺杀。培育起来难度也最高。

它们能改变自身的密度，把庞大的身躯浓缩成非常小的一团。在某个适当的时机发动，开启猎杀时刻。进食方式类似于蛇，一口吞。

在它们蜷缩的时候，身体硬度非常惊人，表面还会长出石头质感的鳞片。潜行者的鳞片经常被人抠下来制作护甲。

历史上，有位人联总统，就是被黑十字审判庭派出的潜行者暗杀掉的。

相南里来到第四个玻璃温室前，绕着它走了一圈，发现里面竟然真的是空的。而不是潜行者蜷缩了起来。

而且相南里还有一个发现。

他用手，轻轻推开了面前的金属门，这门很厚，但锁却坏掉了。也失去了隔绝空间的作用。
chunks.englishText:
Xiang Nanli poked his head out of the pipe, looking like that annoying mole from a Whac-A-Mole game.

He was hanging upside down from the ceiling. Below him was a conveyor belt, similar to an airport baggage carousel, about three or four meters down. The belt was stationary, covered in debris.

*Thank goodness for the gene serum,* Xiang Nanli thought; his original body would never have been able to hang suspended for this long.

He aimed for a patch of ground with fewer obstacles and let go.

Xiang Nanli had tried his best to control his landing, but he still crashed heavily into a pile of trash, making a loud noise.

*Ouch, my butt.*

Xiang Nanli climbed out of a mountain of stacked wastebaskets and clicked on his flashlight, sweeping the beam around.

"Holy—"

The light hit something that nearly stopped his heart.

A cardboard box was filled with a row of human heads.

The disheveled heads stared straight ahead, their metallic coating eerily flesh-toned. It was incredibly lifelike.

Xiang Nanli reached out to touch one and realized they weren't real people, but robot heads. He let out a sigh of relief.

Aside from reading books, Xiang Nanli had never encountered an actual robot. He picked up one of the heads, couldn't resist holding the flashlight in his mouth, and began to take it apart.

"Oh, oh, so that’s how it’s installed... even if it’s a design from hundreds of years ago, it’s still very interesting. The structure is well-made, too. Is this part the central control system?"

Xiang Nanli dismantled two in ten minutes, felt he had fully grasped the construction of the robot heads, and stopped, satisfied.

The system said gloomily: "Is playing with my companions' corpses fun?"

At such a critical juncture, it had actually refrained from interrupting him.

Xiang Nanli: "I have to correct you. Only things that had life are called corpses. These are, at best, loose parts and learning tools."

System: "If the definition of life is a service lifespan, then I believe machines also have life."

Xiang Nanli walked forward: "That’s getting too philosophical, and I’ve clearly been absent from this social discourse for the past few hundred years. I won't argue with you; after all, you have an entire database of resources to refute me."

"Humans always love to start from an 'ego-centric' perspective," the system said. "But humans are not the masters of all things."

Xiang Nanli thought, *That’s fine, at least I’m your master.*

But he didn't say it, fearing the system would get angry and electrocute him.

*Alpha is bad. It can even secretly deduct money behind my back; what else is it incapable of? And it knows perfectly well that my home is so poor we’re about to run out of rice.*

This conveyor belt was clearly used for transporting supplies. The room was large and square. Above, there were several large pipes, much like an airport carousel. There were even LED screens to assist with inventory.

The floor was covered in trash, along with opened cans and food packaging piled into small mounds. This trash was ancient, but because it was underground, devoid of air and biological activity, it was remarkably well-preserved.

"Someone lived here for a while," Xiang Nanli judged. "But they must be dead by now."

Xiang Nanli: "And they preferred living at an open-air transfer station rather than going to the medical ward ahead. Is it because there’s something even more terrifying inside... Alpha, where are the aberrant humans you mentioned?"

"Inside the medical station," Alpha answered concisely. "Please rest assured. If there is danger, I will warn you."

The place was pitch black, with almost no light.

Xiang Nanli held his flashlight and moved in the direction the system indicated.

Oxygen was running low, and his protective suit began trying to filter the underground air. It smelled heavily of rust, mixed with the stench of rotting meat.

This made Xiang Nanli feel uneasy.

An iron door appeared before him. The security system seemed to be a different circuit; the access terminal stood in front of the door, glowing faintly.

Xiang Nanli wasn't sure if it required a fingerprint or some kind of staff card, but the moment he approached, the door opened automatically.

A mechanical female voice spoke: "Identity verification passed."

The environment was so cold and gloomy that the voice sounded ghostly.

"Why did it say identity verification passed?" Xiang Nanli rubbed his chin. "Is the access control broken, or is there some conspiracy?"

Alpha spoke expressionlessly: "I hacked it. Hurry."

Fine. Being paid really makes a difference; it even talks with more confidence.

Xiang Nanli walked into the pitch-black room. Detecting life signs, rows of lights suddenly flickered on, illuminating the path ahead.

Xiang Nanli held his breath, his eyes widening.

He stood in the middle of the path, surrounded by square glass greenhouses... or rather, glass cages.

Three massive, blood-red aberrant entities were locked inside the cages. There were messy traces of shredded flesh inside the glass.

Ordinary aberrant entities were only 3 to 15 meters long. These were at least 20 meters tall. They were curled up in the glass rooms, their flesh withered to the point of looking like corpses. It was impossible to tell if they were dead or alive.

In conditions of extreme food scarcity, aberrant entities could enter hibernation to extend their lifespans.

Moreover, these three aberrant humans were of different varieties.

"Crawler, Ripper, Berserker..." Xiang Nanli muttered.

The Crawler resembled a lizard, though "Great Dragon" might be a more fitting description. This dragon had some unknown metal devices on its body, and a massive steel spike had been driven into its brain.

Xiang Nanli had read some documents; he guessed this was an attempt to implant a control chip into the Crawler’s mind.

The Ripper could stand upright; it had a relatively slender lower body and an exceptionally strong upper body. Like a werewolf, its entire body was covered in thick, coarse bristles. Most striking were its arms, which split into five fingers from the elbow down, resembling serrated blades forged from refined steel.

Xiang Nanli didn't doubt for a second that it could shred any living thing into mincemeat or spare parts with those hands.

The Berserker had the most restraints. Its body was embedded with iron plates Xiang Nanli couldn't understand; it looked as if metal devices had been driven directly into its flesh. Its muscles were well-developed, and it looked the most human, like an ape, but with a slender, long tail.

Xiang Nanli had heard that Berserkers were like berserker warriors; once awakened, they would mindlessly kill every living thing in sight, fighting until their last breath. It was very similar to late-stage Cyber-Psychosis. (A mental illness suffered by some humans who undergo mechanical modification, causing them to slaughter everyone around them indiscriminately. The cause is a network virus infection; the incidence rate is currently very low, though historically it was an incurable disease similar to AIDS.)

In the glass greenhouse holding the Berserker, there was a lot of dried, shredded flesh stuck to the inside of the glass, left uncleaned.

"This is a medical station? I thought it would be like a school infirmary, tucked away in some corner, a room at the end of a hallway." Xiang Nanli was too shocked to speak. "But Alpha, did you realize one thing? There are four glass cages. The last one is empty. And there are four branches of aberrant humans, the last type being the Stalker..."

Stalkers were the rarest of the aberrant humans. They were experts in surprise attacks and assassinations, and the most difficult to cultivate.

They could alter their own density, condensing their massive bodies into a very small mass. At the right moment, they would launch, initiating a feeding frenzy. Their method of eating was similar to a snake—swallowing whole.

When curled up, their bodies were incredibly hard, and stone-like scales would grow on the surface. Stalker scales were often harvested to make armor.

Historically, a President of the Human Alliance had been assassinated by a Stalker sent by the Black Cross Inquisition.

Xiang Nanli walked to the fourth glass greenhouse, circled it, and found it was truly empty, not just the Stalker curled up.

And Xiang Nanli made another discovery.

He used his hand to gently push open the metal door in front of him. The door was thick, but the lock was broken, and it no longer served to isolate the space.

chunks.chineseText:
这里应该是供“医疗人员”进来喂食、观察的通路。穿过这条拱形的金属隧道，就是玻璃温室。

潜行者的胃液有强烈的腐蚀性。

相南里的背后一阵发凉：“这个潜行者最好被人拿走了，而不是偷偷溜了出来……Alpha，这么多年，它应该早就被饿死了吧。”

系统：“结合周围环境，根据分析，潜行者存活的可能性为1.2%。”

相南里安慰自己：“我抽卡从来都是保底的。1.2%基本是SSR卡的掉率了，应该轮不到我吧。”

不得不说，相南里的心理素质很强大。在面对外观恐怖、杀伤力更恐怖的畸变生物时，很多人的想法恐怕都是远远绕开。

而他在最初的震惊后，竟然饶有兴致地观察起来。

“人在超过一定体型，就需要很强大骨骼去支撑它们的形状。要不然会被自己的重量压垮。这些畸变人的身体应该是很好的原材料吧。”相南里思考着，“这里说是医疗室，但其实是一个实验室？或者说驯兽场？东皇重工当年为什么要进行这样的生物实验？他们不是机械制造所吗？”

系统：“生物智械实验。东皇重工认为以普通人类的身体，驾驭高等机械装置还是太难了一些，不如让畸变人去尝试……说起来，这个公司‘生物实验小组’里的所有人，都被判处了无期徒刑或者死刑，罪名是违反实验伦理、危害人类安全。”

“东皇重工的很多职工认为，他们只是按照上级命令行事，他们的实验是工作的一部分；这大概就是所谓的‘群体之恶’吧。”

系统作为一个智能AI，居然在这件事里表达出了明显的立场。

“另外，我要提醒你。氧气瓶内的含氧量在节省的情况下，只能使用20分钟左右。请立刻前往隔离观察室，更换氧气瓶。”

“知道了知道了。”相南里念念不舍地说着，“如果能操控这些畸变人就好了。完全不用担心外面审判庭的人。”

他从衣服内侧的口袋里掏出电子镜片，架在鼻梁上。

相南里的眼前出现了一个虚拟箭头，指向目的地。这里有很多个房间，不戴电镜他还真担心走岔路。

“在破产清算后，部分职工逃去地表，投靠了黑十字审判庭。恐怕他们比你更能驾驭这些畸变人。”系统冷冷说着。

相南里来到了箭头指向的终点。

这扇门依然是需要开锁的，但和之前的门禁一样，在检测到相南里靠近后，大门自动打开。

隔离观察室像一个中央控制台。看得出来，过去有人曾在这里办公。

相南里一进门，脚步就忍不住微微一顿。

他眼前有张办公桌，内嵌着一台控制电脑。一个穿着制服的无头尸体就坐在办公桌前。

从血液溅射的痕迹看，这个人是整个脑袋都被一口咬了下来；十分符合潜行者的作案特征。

门在相南里身后合上。他却没有一丝的安全感。

氧气瓶就在尸体背后的柜子里。

相南里沉默片刻，走向这具尸体，在它身上摸索起钥匙。

很奇怪的触感，像是发泡的面团。

“为什么它都没有变成骨架啊？”

相南里很嫌弃地翻着它的衣服。这触感有点恶心过头了。

“这具身体基因改造过。”系统言简意赅地回答，“智械战争早期，这种基因改造很流行。后来发现还是打不过智械人的热武器，使用者逐渐变少。机械改造的人类也大幅度增加。”

“但目前看，这个世界最上层的那一批人类，依然热衷于基因改造，而不是机械改造……只是信息不会往下流通罢了。”系统的声音在这一刻充满邪恶的噪音，像恶魔在絮语。
chunks.englishText:
This should have been the passage for "medical personnel" to enter for feeding and observation. Passing through this arched metal tunnel led directly to the glass greenhouses.

A Stalker’s stomach acid was highly corrosive.

A chill ran down Xiang Nanli’s back: "I hope this Stalker was taken away by someone, rather than having slipped out... Alpha, after all these years, it should have starved to death, right?"

System: "Combined with the surrounding environment and based on analysis, the probability of the Stalker surviving is 1.2%."

Xiang Nanli comforted himself: "I always hit the pity timer when pulling for cards. 1.2% is basically the drop rate for an SSR card; it shouldn't fall to me."

It had to be said that Xiang Nanli’s mental fortitude was remarkably strong. Faced with terrifying-looking and even more lethal aberrant creatures, most people’s first thought would be to stay far away.

Yet, after his initial shock, he was actually observing them with keen interest.

"When a creature exceeds a certain size, it needs very strong bones to support its shape, otherwise it would be crushed by its own weight. These aberrant humans’ bodies should be excellent raw materials," Xiang Nanli mused. "This place is called a medical station, but is it actually a laboratory? Or a beast-taming arena? Why would Donghuang Heavy Industries conduct such biological experiments back then? Aren't they a mechanical manufacturing firm?"

System: "Bio-automaton experiments. Donghuang Heavy Industries believed that it was too difficult for ordinary human bodies to master high-level mechanical devices, so they thought it better to let aberrant humans try... Come to think of it, everyone in this company’s 'Biological Experiment Group' was sentenced to life imprisonment or death for violating experimental ethics and endangering human safety."

"Many employees at Donghuang Heavy Industries believed they were just following orders from their superiors and that their experiments were part of their job; this is probably what is known as the 'banality of evil'."

As an intelligent AI, the system actually expressed a clear stance on this matter.

"Additionally, I must remind you. The oxygen in your tank, if conserved, will only last for about 20 minutes. Please proceed immediately to the isolation observation room to replace the oxygen tank."

"I know, I know," Xiang Nanli said, sounding reluctant. "If only I could control these aberrant humans. I wouldn't have to worry about the Inquisition people outside at all."

He pulled an electronic lens from his inner pocket and set it on the bridge of his nose.

A virtual arrow appeared in Xiang Nanli’s vision, pointing toward his destination. There were many rooms here; without the lens, he was truly worried about taking a wrong turn.

"After the bankruptcy liquidation, some employees fled to the surface and defected to the Black Cross Inquisition. I’m afraid they are better at controlling these aberrant humans than you are," the system said coldly.

Xiang Nanli arrived at the destination indicated by the arrow.

This door also required unlocking, but just like the previous access control, it opened automatically the moment it detected Xiang Nanli’s approach.

The isolation observation room looked like a central control console. It was evident that someone had worked here in the past.

As soon as Xiang Nanli entered, his footsteps faltered.

In front of him was an office desk with a built-in control computer. A headless corpse in a uniform was sitting at the desk.

Judging by the blood splatter, the person’s entire head had been bitten off in one go; it perfectly matched the modus operandi of a Stalker.

The door closed behind Xiang Nanli. He didn't feel safe at all.

The oxygen tank was in the cabinet behind the corpse.

Xiang Nanli stood silent for a moment, then walked toward the corpse to search for the key.

The texture was very strange, like foamy dough.

"Why hasn't it turned into a skeleton?"

Xiang Nanli rummaged through its clothes with disgust. The sensation was a bit too nauseating.

"This body was genetically modified," the system answered concisely. "In the early days of the Automaton War, this kind of genetic modification was very popular. Later, it was discovered that it still couldn't defeat the heavy weaponry of the Automaton race, so the number of users gradually decreased. Mechanically modified humans increased significantly."

"But as it stands, the top tier of humanity in this world is still keen on genetic modification rather than mechanical modification... it’s just that the information doesn't filter down to the lower levels." The system’s voice was filled with evil static at this moment, like a demon whispering.

chunks.chineseText:
第16章

相南里最后是在尸体的裤腰上摸到了钥匙。

他拽了两下，没拽动。只好研究起如何解开男人的皮带。

“这还是我第一次给人宽衣解带。那句话怎么说的，如果不能对他负责就不要解开他的裤腰。”

他对这具尸体充满歉意：“抱歉，下辈子再对你负责。”

系统：“……”6。

相南里成功把钥匙抓到了手上。

这把钥匙银白色，看不出什么材质。这么多年都没锈蚀，应该是合金。

有些重要的东西反而是用最原始的机械锁保管的，因为担心骇客入侵。

可惜世界上就没有绝对安全的地方，也没有绝对完美的防御手段。

相南里氧气告急，动作却丝毫不乱。他扫了眼锁孔，把钥匙插入，然后轻轻转动。

机械锁发出了明显的齿轮转动的声音。

“喀嚓”一声响。立柜打开，里面不仅有氧气瓶，还悬挂着一根安保电棍。

相南里开心地取下电棍，在手中掂量了一下。

有点重，不知道是什么合金，大概30kg。哪怕不用电击功能，单纯依靠重量砸人，就足够杀人了。

30kg对基因改造人来说可能和塑料管差不多，相南里握着还行，但使用起来不会太轻松。

电棍用的是电池，按一下就会爆发出高压电。非常好用，就是使用的时候要小心。相南里没有手贱到拆开研究一下。

相南里的手伸向氧气瓶：“有武器，但办公室里没有战斗的痕迹。所以这个职工是被偷袭咬掉的大脑。偷袭其实还有另一层含义，那就是以弱胜强。”

系统：“是的。”

东皇重工的氧气瓶一看就比他现在用的要高级。体积更小，然而压缩的氧气却更多。他蹲在地上，拔出输氧管，手握住氧气瓶。

他的动作看起来处处都是破绽，毫无防备。

“后！”系统的声音突然急促。

相南里的手瞬间摸到地上那根电棍，室内光线不太明亮，他只能从橱窗的反光上看见一团影子。他用力朝着自己背后抡去。

“咚”的一声。相南里的手被震得发麻，他用力握紧，才让电棍不至于掉出手中。

几米开外，一条长约一米的蛇人趴在墙上，张开嘴，发出刺耳的吼叫声：“嘶呀——”

相南里一棍子下去，它居然完好无损。只有额角微微破皮，露出里面粉红的嫩肉。连血都没流一滴。

蛇人，但又长着柔软的四肢。可以爬行，也能贴在身体两侧游动，还有一条长尾，像鳗鱼。

潜行者身上有它前面三个兄弟的特征。比如类似爬行者的外观、撕裂者的手刃、狂暴者的性格。另外，除了冬眠，潜行者还可以通过“蜕皮”来修复自身受到的伤害。生命力极其顽强。

系统：“坏消息：潜行者居然真的还没死。好消息：它现在和快死了也差不多。”

是的，这只潜行者体格很小，而且并不是压缩身体后的瘦小，而是一次次蜕皮后的结果。它需要更小的身躯维持更低的消耗。

因为缺乏食物和营养，它的皮肤显现出一种灰白的颜色。

潜行者之前一直在冬眠，是相南里惊扰了它。

求生的本能让它对相南里发起进攻。

饥饿，虚弱。

要么进食，要么继续冬眠，要么死亡。

而后两者指向的，其实都是死亡。

潜行者已经不知道多少年没有在这里看见过生物了。这或许是它最后的机会。

它细长的黑色眼睛打量着相南里，眼神极其人性化地闪过凝思。

相南里手里的武器它认识。小时候，那些研究员经常用这种武器电它们。长大后，电棍的作用就变得微乎其微。但为了生存，潜行者依然会装作害怕和恐惧的模样。

如果是从前，潜行者当然不会在乎这种小武器。

可惜现在它太虚弱了。

潜行者调头爬向天花板，很快消失在阴影中，怪如其名，爬行时一点声音都没有。像是从来没有存在过。

相南里没有追上去，他又不会飞。

危机解除，他迅速地给自己安装上氧气瓶。清润的氧气注入，相南里觉得脑子都清醒了不少，肺部火烧火燎的痛感也得到了平息。

相南里摸了摸下巴：“如果我是潜行者，我不会离开猎物太远。会时时刻刻在暗处潜伏，等待着下一个猎物松懈的时刻……这种被盯上的感觉真不好受。还是我太弱。”

“这只潜行者很虚弱。如果以一种游戏等级的看法去衡量，现在大概只有5级。”

“那我呢？”相南里好奇地追问。

系统评估片刻：“2级吧。你身体素质是比原始人类高那么一点；加上6级的新手装备电棍。不被咬到勉强有一战之力。”

如果它遇上的是骑士长、或者辛追，哪怕是小燕，都不可能活着离开。

偏偏来的人是编外人员相南里。

相南里很不幸，但爬行者却很幸运。

相南里：“那其他人是多少级？”

“数据不足，只能大概猜测。修40级，辛追35级。剩下几个20级左右。普通爬行者15级。”

“外面大的那个呢？”

“全盛状态也许50级。”

相南里很快制定了策略：“我得假装松懈，多露出几次破绽。让它来攻击我，我成功反击。次数一多，后面哪怕我真的大意了，它未必敢主动进攻。”

系统回答：“我会帮你留意的。不过你的办法可行。”

相南里已经习惯了系统薛定谔的眼睛。

他突然想到，如果一枚芯片充钱就能黑进后台，那菩提怎么还要给自己装脑机接口？工作起来也很痛的样子。

原本平平无奇的Alpha代餐系统在这一刻变得神秘起来。

但现在不是深究的时候。万一系统被戳穿，为了符合人设回归平庸，他要怎么在这里活下去？

手里抄着武器，相南里安全感得到上升。

他翻了一下，在办公室里没有找到任何有用资料。倒是在垃圾桶里发现了一堆碎纸。

死之前都要销毁的资料。啧，应该很重要吧。可惜，注定淹没在历史的垃圾堆里。一切的人和事都无足轻重，没有什么能永垂不朽。

到最后，相南里都要放弃了，却在出口的门上发现挂着个记录本。

【1】“饲料告急，主任做出一个疯狂的决定，他说可以拿那些失败的人造人去喂畸变体……呃，我觉得很恐惧，然而主任却说，总不能让我们的实验体饿死。”

“可是人都要饿死了，还管得了实验体吗？”

【2】“主任说，物资极度匮乏。减少了食物和水的供应。我已经三周没洗澡了。好在大家味道都很冲。”

“对了。那些畸变体绝食了，它们不愿意吃自己的同类。主任很头疼。果然，就不该让畸变人保留太高的智力。”

【3】“为了应对物资紧缺，职工们进行了公投。大家同意进行高度机械改造。笑死，原材料都是现成的。为了制作‘东方青帝’，仓库里有一堆残次品。随便拼拼都是一具机械身体。”
chunks.englishText:
Chapter 16

Xiang Nanli finally managed to fish the key out from the waistband of the corpse’s trousers.

He tugged at it twice, but it wouldn't budge. He had no choice but to figure out how to undo the man’s belt.

"This is my first time undressing someone. How does that saying go? If you can’t take responsibility for him, don’t undo his waistband."

He felt a pang of apology toward the corpse: "Sorry, I’ll take responsibility in the next life."

System: "..." 6.

Xiang Nanli successfully grabbed the key.

It was silver-white, and the material was indistinguishable. Having not rusted after all these years, it was likely an alloy.

Some important items were kept behind primitive mechanical locks specifically to prevent hacking.

Unfortunately, there was no such thing as an absolutely secure place in this world, nor was there a perfectly flawless defense.

Xiang Nanli’s oxygen was running low, but his movements remained steady. He scanned the keyhole, inserted the key, and turned it gently.

The mechanical lock emitted a distinct sound of gears shifting.

*Click.* The cabinet swung open, revealing not only an oxygen tank but also a security stun baton hanging inside.

Xiang Nanli happily took the baton and weighed it in his hand.

It was a bit heavy—probably 30kg—and he couldn't tell what alloy it was made of. Even without using the electric shock function, the sheer weight alone would be enough to kill someone if he swung it.

To a genetically modified human, 30kg might feel like a plastic pipe, but for Xiang Nanli, while he could hold it, using it wouldn't be effortless.

The baton ran on batteries; a single press would discharge high-voltage electricity. It was extremely useful, though one had to be careful when handling it. Xiang Nanli didn't have the urge to take it apart to study it.

Xiang Nanli reached for the oxygen tank: "There’s a weapon here, but there are no signs of a struggle in the office. This means the employee was ambushed and had his brain bitten off. An ambush actually implies another layer of meaning: the weak overcoming the strong."

System: "Correct."

The oxygen tank from Donghuang Heavy Industries looked far more advanced than the one he was currently using. It was smaller in volume yet contained more compressed oxygen. He crouched on the floor, pulled out the oxygen tube, and gripped the tank.

His posture looked full of openings, completely unguarded.

"Behind you!" the System’s voice suddenly sharpened.

Xiang Nanli’s hand instantly reached for the stun baton on the floor. The room was dim, and he could only see a mass of shadows reflected in the cabinet glass. He swung the baton with all his might behind him.

*Thud.* His hand went numb from the impact. He gripped the baton tighter to keep it from flying out of his hand.

A few meters away, a snake-man about a meter long was clinging to the wall. It opened its mouth and let out a shrill, piercing screech: "Hiss—"

Xiang Nanli had struck it with the baton, yet it remained completely unscathed. Only a small patch of skin on its forehead was grazed, revealing the tender pink flesh beneath. Not even a drop of blood flowed.

A snake-man, yet it possessed soft limbs. It could crawl, swim along the sides of its body, and it had a long tail like an eel.

The "Prowler" possessed the traits of its three predecessors: the appearance of a Crawler, the hand-blades of a Ripper, and the temperament of a Berserker. Furthermore, aside from hibernation, the Prowler could repair damage sustained to its body through "molting." Its vitality was incredibly tenacious.

System: "Bad news: The Prowler is actually not dead yet. Good news: It’s pretty much on the verge of death."

Indeed, this Prowler was small in stature—not because it had compressed its body, but as a result of repeated molting. It needed a smaller frame to maintain lower energy consumption.

Due to a lack of food and nutrition, its skin had taken on a grayish-white hue.

The Prowler had been hibernating until Xiang Nanli disturbed it.

The instinct for survival drove it to attack Xiang Nanli.

Hunger. Weakness.

Either eat, continue to hibernate, or die.

And the latter two actually pointed to the same outcome: death.

The Prowler hadn't seen a living creature here in who knows how many years. This might be its last chance.

Its long, thin black eyes studied Xiang Nanli, a flash of contemplation crossing its gaze in a remarkably human way.

It recognized the weapon in Xiang Nanli’s hand. When it was young, the researchers often used such weapons to shock them. As it grew older, the effect of the stun baton became negligible. But for the sake of survival, the Prowler would still feign fear and terror.

If it were in its prime, the Prowler certainly wouldn't care about such a small weapon.

Unfortunately, it was too weak now.

The Prowler turned and crawled toward the ceiling, disappearing into the shadows. True to its name, it moved without a sound, as if it had never existed at all.

Xiang Nanli didn't pursue it; he couldn't fly, after all.

With the crisis averted, he quickly attached the oxygen tank to his suit. As the crisp, cool oxygen flowed in, Xiang Nanli felt his mind clear up significantly, and the burning pain in his lungs subsided.

Xiang Nanli rubbed his chin: "If I were the Prowler, I wouldn't stay too far from the prey. I’d lurk in the shadows, waiting for the moment the next prey lets their guard down... This feeling of being watched is really unpleasant. I’m just too weak."

"This Prowler is very weak. If measured by a game-level standard, it’s probably only Level 5 right now."

"And what about me?" Xiang Nanli asked curiously.

The System evaluated for a moment: "Level 2, I’d say. Your physical fitness is slightly higher than that of a primitive human; plus, you have a Level 6 starter weapon, the stun baton. You have the strength to put up a fight as long as you don't get bitten."

If it had encountered a Knight Commander, or Xin Zhui, or even Xiao Yan, it wouldn't have left alive.

But the one who came was the freelancer, Xiang Nanli.

Xiang Nanli was unfortunate, but the Prowler was lucky.

Xiang Nanli: "What level are the others?"

"Insufficient data, only rough estimates. Xiu is Level 40, Xin Zhui is Level 35. The rest are around Level 20. A normal Crawler is Level 15."

"What about the big one outside?"

"In its prime, perhaps Level 50."

Xiang Nanli quickly formulated a strategy: "I need to pretend to let my guard down and expose more openings. Let it attack me, and then I’ll counterattack successfully. If I do this enough times, even if I really am careless later, it might not dare to attack me proactively."

The System replied: "I will keep an eye out for you. Your plan is feasible."

Xiang Nanli was already used to the System’s Schrödinger-like eyes.

He suddenly wondered: if a chip can hack into the backend just by paying, then why did Bodhi need to install a brain-machine interface for himself? It looked painful to work with.

The seemingly unremarkable Alpha meal-replacement system became mysterious at this moment.

But now was not the time to delve into it. If the System were exposed and he had to return to mediocrity to fit his persona, how would he survive here?

With a weapon in hand, Xiang Nanli’s sense of security increased.

He rummaged through the office but found no useful information. However, he did find a pile of shredded paper in the trash can.

Documents that had to be destroyed before death. Tsk, they must have been important. Unfortunately, they were destined to be buried in the trash heap of history. All people and events were insignificant; nothing could be immortal.

Just as Xiang Nanli was about to give up, he found a notebook hanging on the exit door.

[1] "Feed is running low. The Director made a crazy decision; he said we could use the failed androids to feed the aberrations... Ugh, I feel terrified, yet the Director says we can't let our test subjects starve to death."

"But people are starving to death, so why worry about the test subjects?"

[2] "The Director says supplies are extremely scarce. Food and water rations have been reduced. I haven't showered in three weeks. Good thing everyone smells just as bad."

"Oh, right. Those aberrations are on a hunger strike; they refuse to eat their own kind. The Director is very frustrated. As expected, we shouldn't have let the aberrations retain such high intelligence."

[3] "To cope with the shortage of supplies, the staff held a referendum. Everyone agreed to undergo high-level mechanical modification. Hilarious, the raw materials are already on hand. To build the 'Eastern Azure Emperor,' there’s a pile of defective parts in the warehouse. You could piece together a mechanical body just by throwing them together."

chunks.chineseText:
“但我不同意。我恨那些机械人，我全家都死在它们的屠杀下。随便你们吧，我不会妥协的。而且生物进化才是最适合人类的选择，人怎么能把自己矮化成工具？”

【4】“主任说，东皇重工的生物智械改造手术已经非常安全，让大家放心，不用担心赛博精神病、不用担心改造失败。东皇重工会超越永生科技，成为最大的垄断企业。”

【5】“你们疯了……它们疯了，到底是主任疯了还是我？原来是饲料不够，人造人也不够了。怪不得要推行机械改造。好想吐。我不敢辞职，主任已经疯了。他会杀了我的。”

【6】“太好了，我们失败了！失败了！亲爱的朋友，好消息——我、们、失、败、了！”

后面，这个记录者随手画了一些简笔画。看起来像是机甲图纸。

相南里大概能猜出一些：“这里的实验，是让畸变体进行机械改造，然后成为被人类奴役的‘智械’？这就是生物智械技术的雏形吧。”

看起来无害、甚至目前在地下城推广多年的科技；起源竟然如此血腥。而且堆满了失败者的遗骸。

可在另一层面，这项技术又的确推动了人类科技树的前进。甚至成为其中最重要的组成部分。

“真是……迷人的新世界。”

相南里放下笔记本，感慨了一声。然后推开门，走出去。

“不过东方青帝这个名字，怎么这么耳熟？”

相南里脑海里闪过一些很久远的回忆。

他高中读的是国外的男校，那种老牌贵族中学。他是华裔，在学校食物链最底层。

相南里知道别人是怎么称呼他的，“怪胎”。不热衷任何社交活动，每个休息日只会把自己困在宿舍和学校的机房里。他在这里编写出了Alpha的雏形。

相南里每天和它进行大量的对话，以语言数据的形式。这是最笨拙、最基础的AI智能训练。

——Alpha，你知道什么是机甲吗？

【机械动力装甲。一般出现在科幻动漫、影视、小说作品中。我认为以现在的科技水平，不可能制造出来。而且就算真的有机甲，它们也可能不那么有用。会像蒸汽艇一样，因为实用性不高，被历史抛弃。】

——那有什么关系，机甲很好看嘛。以后我要造四个。

【好的。】

——叫青龙、朱雀、玄武、白虎……算了，好像有点太土了。叫东方青帝，南方赤帝，西方白帝，北方黑帝。怎么样？好像也挺土的，算了……以后再想。

【东方青帝。好的。】

——不是吧，我输入这么多，你就捕捉到了一条？

【好的。请再说一次。】

——但我是人类，我的寿命可能活不到科技树发展到机甲时代的时候。除非外星人入侵。你帮我记住吧，你应该能存在很多年。前提是有朝一日，我可以把你推广出去。

【好的。】

——Alpha，谢谢你。

【抱歉，我不明白你的意思。】

相南里的嘴角抽搐：“Alpha，你不会真的把它做出来了吧？”

“抱歉，我不明白你的意思。”系统回答。

“是另一个Alpha。”

系统有些不满：“如果您总是提起另一个‘Alpha’，那就不该把我取名叫‘Alpha’。我会出现逻辑运行混乱。我们智能AI也是可能患上赛博精神病的。”

“习惯了，抱歉。”相南里对它道歉，“以后我会注意的。”

相南里的眼前再次出现一根虚拟箭头，指向黑暗中未知的地点。

系统：“根据设计图纸，这边是出口，可以通向地表。但东皇重工在这里进行秘密生产，数据可能有误。如果遇到危险，我会及时提醒你。”

“好，那么我的命就交给你了，不要让我失望Alpha。”

Alpha的语气毫无情绪起伏：“明白。”

出去的路上，相南里不可避免地又路过了饲养场。

玻璃温室里的巨物保持着原样，没有任何动作。血红色的身体萎靡，只剩一层皮挂在骨头上。

相南里经过玻璃窗，感觉到了自己的渺小：“Alpha。基因生物技术是很伟大的科技，或许并不比机械改造差。”

Alpha：“是的，后面。”

相南里腰身一晃，一条雪白的影子咬中他的胳膊。并没有相南里想象中的痛。或许是它太过虚弱，它的牙齿甚至没能穿透防护服。

潜行者往下爬，目标是相南里装着干粮的口袋。

相南里一棍子砸向这条白色蜥蜴人，顺便开启电击模式。

潜行者不亏是皮糙肉厚的怪物，相南里有隔离手套，都感觉自己半边胳膊麻了。而这种程度的高压电只是让潜行者微微抽搐了一下，摔在地上。

相南里压上去，掐住了潜行者的脖子——尽管这条长蛇一样的怪物也许根本没有脖子那样的东西。

他另一只手抄起电棍，狠狠塞进潜行者又宽又长的嘴里。

潜行者在他手底下挣扎起来。

相南里毫不犹豫地打开电击。

空气里飘出一股糊味，潜行者没动静了。但相南里分明摸到了它的心跳。

白色的怪物倒在地上，眼睛却没有看相南里，而是看着玻璃温室里的同伴……它漆黑干涩的眼睛里，在这一刻居然盈满了泪水。

泪从它的眼角渗出来。滴在地上。

电棍的电量很快只剩下一半，可相南里还是没能电死潜行者。

之前看到的记录本上，说这几个畸变人实验体保留了一定程度的智力。

相南里思考片刻，开口：“你杀不死我，偷袭也不行。我也不想杀你。”才怪。

“你挺可怜的。”这句倒是真心话。

畸变人是由人造人改造过来的。人造人，辛追也是人造人，和正常人没有区别。

如果这些畸变人保留着智力。哪怕没有接受过教育，只剩下作为人的本能……

它们作为武器的一生，都非常痛苦。

相南里叹了口气，从防护服的口袋里摸出干粮。掰开成两半，分了一半给潜行者。

“这么说吧，看见外面那个传送通道了吗？那里还有其他人。另外，也有一些你的……后代？是爬行者。

“他们手里粮食比我多。你去找那些人吧，别缠着我了。”

相南里由衷道。

他松开手，潜行者叼起地上的干粮，瞬间窜到角落里。

很快，黑暗里传来狼吞虎咽地咀嚼声，看得出来是饿狠了。

这段时间，它并没有发起进攻。

那种被窥探的感觉消失了。

相南里想，它大概暂时放下了敌意。

相南里觉得，它最好早点意识到，自己真的很穷。除非它想吃人，要不然是填不饱肚子的……呃，它真的不想吗？

咀嚼声停下，潜行者缓缓朝着黑暗中爬去。

要离开的时候，这头白色蜥蜴回头，深深看了他一眼。

然后，它在下一秒张开嘴，朝着相南里展示了自己嘴里的东西，外观很熟悉，看起来就像是一管葡萄糖酸锌口服液。
chunks.englishText:
"But I disagree. I hate those machines; my whole family died in their slaughter. Do whatever you want, I won't compromise. Besides, biological evolution is the most suitable choice for humans. How can people demean themselves into tools?"

[4] "The Director says that Donghuang Heavy Industries' bio-mechanical modification surgery is already very safe, so everyone should rest assured—no need to worry about cyber-psychosis or failed modifications. Donghuang Heavy Industries will surpass Eternal Technology and become the largest monopoly."

[5] "You’re all crazy... They’re all crazy. Is it the Director who’s insane, or me? So, it turns out the feed wasn't enough, and there weren't enough androids either. No wonder they’re pushing for mechanical modification. I feel like vomiting. I don't dare to resign; the Director has lost his mind. He’ll kill me."

[6] "Great, we failed! We failed! Dear friend, good news—w-e f-a-i-l-e-d!"

Further down, the recorder had doodled some sketches. They looked like blueprints for a mech.

Xiang Nanli could roughly guess some of it: "The experiments here were to have aberrations undergo mechanical modification and become 'smart machines' enslaved by humans? This must be the prototype of bio-mechanical technology."

It looked harmless—a technology that had been promoted in the Underground City for years—yet its origins were so bloody. And it was piled high with the remains of the failed.

Yet, on another level, this technology had indeed pushed the advancement of the human tech tree. It had even become one of its most important components.

"What a... fascinating new world."

Xiang Nanli put down the notebook and sighed. Then he pushed open the door and walked out.

"But the name 'Eastern Azure Emperor'—why does it sound so familiar?"

Flashes of distant memories crossed Xiang Nanli’s mind.

In high school, he attended an all-boys school abroad, one of those old-fashioned elite academies. He was of Chinese descent and at the very bottom of the school’s social food chain.

Xiang Nanli knew what others called him: "Freak." He wasn't interested in any social activities; every day off, he would lock himself in his dorm or the school’s computer lab. That was where he wrote the prototype for Alpha.

Xiang Nanli would have extensive conversations with it every day, in the form of linguistic data. This was the clumsiest, most basic AI training.

—Alpha, do you know what a mech is?

[Mechanical powered armor. Generally appears in science fiction anime, films, and novels. I believe that with current technological levels, it is impossible to manufacture. And even if mechs truly existed, they might not be very useful. Like steamships, they would likely be abandoned by history due to low practicality.]

—What does that matter? Mechs look cool. I’m going to build four of them in the future.

[Understood.]

—Let’s call them Azure Dragon, Vermilion Bird, Black Tortoise, White Tiger... Never mind, that sounds a bit too tacky. Let’s call them Eastern Azure Emperor, Southern Red Emperor, Western White Emperor, Northern Black Emperor. How about that? Seems a bit tacky too, never mind... I’ll think about it later.

[Eastern Azure Emperor. Understood.]

—No way, I typed so much, and you only caught one?

[Understood. Please repeat.]

—But I’m human. My lifespan might not last until the tech tree reaches the mech era. Unless aliens invade. You help me remember it; you should be able to exist for many years. Provided that one day, I can promote you.

[Understood.]

—Alpha, thank you.

[Apologies, I do not understand what you mean.]

The corner of Xiang Nanli’s mouth twitched: "Alpha, you didn't actually build it, did you?"

"Apologies, I do not understand what you mean," the System replied.

"It’s the other Alpha."

The System sounded somewhat dissatisfied: "If you keep mentioning another 'Alpha,' you shouldn't have named me 'Alpha.' I will experience logical processing confusion. We intelligent AIs can also suffer from cyber-psychosis."

"I’m used to it, sorry," Xiang Nanli apologized. "I’ll be careful in the future."

A virtual arrow appeared before Xiang Nanli’s eyes again, pointing toward an unknown location in the darkness.

System: "According to the blueprints, this is the exit leading to the surface. But Donghuang Heavy Industries conducts secret production here, so the data might be inaccurate. If you encounter danger, I will warn you in time."

"Good, then my life is in your hands. Don't let me down, Alpha."

Alpha’s tone was devoid of emotion: "Understood."

On the way out, Xiang Nanli inevitably passed the feeding ground again.

The giant creature in the glass greenhouse remained as it was, motionless. Its blood-red body was withered, with only a layer of skin hanging over its bones.

As Xiang Nanli passed the glass window, he felt his own insignificance: "Alpha. Genetic bio-technology is a great science; perhaps it’s no worse than mechanical modification."

Alpha: "Yes. Behind you."

Xiang Nanli swayed his waist, and a snow-white shadow bit into his arm. It didn't hurt as much as Xiang Nanli had imagined. Perhaps it was too weak; its teeth hadn't even pierced his protective suit.

The Prowler crawled downward, aiming for the pocket where Xiang Nanli kept his dry rations.

Xiang Nanli smashed the baton onto the white lizard-man, simultaneously activating the electric shock mode.

The Prowler was indeed a thick-skinned monster. Even with his insulated gloves, Xiang Nanli felt half his arm go numb. Yet, this level of high-voltage electricity only made the Prowler twitch slightly before it fell to the ground.

Xiang Nanli pressed down on it and grabbed the Prowler by the throat—even though this snake-like monster probably didn't have anything like a throat.

He grabbed the stun baton with his other hand and shoved it hard into the Prowler’s wide, long mouth.

The Prowler struggled beneath him.

Xiang Nanli didn't hesitate to turn on the shock.

A burnt smell drifted through the air, and the Prowler stopped moving. But Xiang Nanli could clearly feel its heartbeat.

The white monster lay on the ground, but its eyes weren't looking at Xiang Nanli; they were looking at its companion in the glass greenhouse... In this moment, its pitch-black, dry eyes were actually filled with tears.

Tears seeped from the corners of its eyes and dripped onto the ground.

The stun baton’s charge was soon down to half, yet Xiang Nanli still hadn't managed to electrocute the Prowler to death.

The notebook he had seen earlier mentioned that these aberrant test subjects retained a certain degree of intelligence.

Xiang Nanli thought for a moment and spoke: "You can't kill me, and your ambush didn't work. I don't want to kill you, either." *Yeah, right.*

"You’re quite pitiful." That part was sincere.

The aberrations were modified from androids. Androids—Xin Zhui was also an android, no different from a normal human.

If these aberrations retained their intelligence, even without education, just the remnants of human instinct...

Their lives as weapons were incredibly painful.

Xiang Nanli sighed, reached into his protective suit’s pocket, and took out his dry rations. He broke it in half and gave one half to the Prowler.

"Let’s put it this way: see that transport tunnel outside? There are other people there. Also, there are some of your... descendants? Crawlers.

"They have more food than I do. Go find those people, and stop pestering me."

Xiang Nanli said this genuinely.

He let go, and the Prowler snatched up the rations and darted into a corner.

Soon, the sound of ravenous chewing came from the darkness; it was clear it had been starving.

During this time, it didn't launch an attack.

The feeling of being watched vanished.

Xiang Nanli thought it had probably set aside its hostility for the time being.

Xiang Nanli felt it would be best if it realized soon that he was really poor. Unless it wanted to eat people, it wouldn't be able to fill its stomach... Uh, did it really *not* want to?

The chewing stopped, and the Prowler slowly crawled into the darkness.

As it was about to leave, the white lizard turned back and gave him a deep look.

Then, in the next second, it opened its mouth and showed Xiang Nanli what was inside. It looked very familiar—it looked just like a vial of zinc gluconate oral solution.
