—On the condition that you are still willing to be controlled by me.

—Even if I am just a frail human far inferior to you.

Xiang Nanli had just recovered from a serious illness, and his skin and lips were pale. He sat on the hospital bed, and although he had received gene injections, his muscle mass hadn't fully recovered, so his frame appeared somewhat thin.

However, when he confronted Dongfang Qingdi, there was not a hint of sickness or cowardice to be seen.

"Or is it," Xiang Nanli said slowly, "that you have some ulterior motive for why you must stay by my side?"

Otherwise, Xiang Nanli really couldn't think of why Alpha wouldn't want to separate from him. It couldn't possibly be that he wanted to date him, right?

Dongfang Qingdi stared at those emerald-green eyes, silent for a long time, his lips pressed tightly together.

Finally, he sighed in his heart, slightly lowered his head, and said with difficulty: "Yes, I need you. Please let me stay by your side."

The smile on Xiang Nanli’s face continued to expand, and expand further.

Xiang Nanli leaned out half his body, happily hugging the figure in front of him, rubbing his head against his chest: "Alright then, Alpha."

chunks.chineseText:
第25章

东方青帝的身体绷紧了一瞬，这完全是潜意识里的战斗本能。

对于智械人来说，最重要的地方就是“心脏”，那里收纳着它们的机械核心。

诚然，智械人同样是能看见实体的生物，但身体硬件并不是它们的必需品。

只要机械核心没有损坏、智械随时可以更换原本的躯体。

相南里离他的心脏位置太近了，这让东方青帝感觉到了危险。

但毕竟，相南里只是一个2级的原始人类。最近又打了一针基因药，也许勉强5级。根本不可能产生威胁。

东方青帝很快放松下来：“需要我回抱你吗？”

人类的心思总是很难猜。

相南里松开胳膊：“不要。”

他开始研究起怎么给东方青帝买票。

相南里的目光在屏幕上划过，选择了和自己相同的车次，问：“你公民ID多少？买票要用。”

人联统一的公民ID，放在前世就是身份证号码，只是完全无卡化。

但拥有ID有一个前提，那就是在自己身体内植入芯片。

东方青帝自从来到医院后，就还没出过门。原因就是没有装芯片，容易被街上的机械警察检测到，然后强制送去最近的医院安装。

他的身体看起来是普通人，但是一般的手术刀，根本划破不了他的身体。

于是，东方青帝略微眨了一下眼，很快，两轮银白色的瞳环在他的眼眸内部亮起：“相南里，把我登记成你的人造人吧。”

相南里一愣，他搜索了一下脑海内部安装的《人类常识》，震惊地询问：“你确定？”

旧时代并不太平，尤其是智械危机刚爆发的那段时间。

这是人类有史以来遭遇的最严重的生存危机。全球人口锐减超过半数，尸横遍野，说是世界末日也差不多。

你无法判断，每天都在使用的家务机器人，会不会在某日突然抄起菜刀，割下你的头；坐惯了的智能驾驶公交车，会不会在某天带着你撞向另一辆汽车。

人类会物理死亡，机械人不会。它们可以一直被复制。

人们尝试过炸毁数据库、切断电源、剪掉电线；可惜破坏的速度远不及智械人修复的速度。

于是，有很多权贵以及他们的后代，选择躲进冷冻舱，打算把困难交给别人，自己狗到世界和平那天。

结果就是冷冻舱公司大赚特赚，却没有足够的资源去维护这些冷冻舱。公司最后破产了。数以万计的冷冻舱散落在了地表各个废墟。

这批解冻人和地下城自然诞生的公民不同，云端网络上没有他们的数据。需要去数据中心进行强制登记。相南里没被催，是因为他出舱后活动时间还短。后来又直接去了地表。

登记内容包括：DNA、人种。重点就在后面这个人种登记上。

“人种”指的不是什么黄种人、白种人；而是智人（主体）与人造人（附庸）。

大多数人造人都是速成品，在人类眼里就像是猩猩，被用于地表探索、采矿等不需要太高智力的高危工作。因为使用人造人，会比用机械人便宜。

但也有很少数的人造人，属于高端奢侈品。

他们有着和人类一样的外表、远超自然人类的体能、智力，是美丽又危险的管辖物。被严格限制着数量。

60年前，人联才通过一条法案，内容是人造人可以自由隐藏瞳环。

他们由自己的主人购买（或定制），在某个温室里被生产出来；在生理意义上是人，社会意义上是商品；享有部分人权，却又低人一等。

譬如他们从基因层面上就被阉割了生育功能；譬如人造人没有公民ID，但需要登记他们的“所有者”。人造人会和所有者共用一个公民ID，相当于银行卡的副卡，并且拥有主卡的二级权限。

在人造人刚合法化的时候，这些所有者甚至能决定要不要剥夺造物的生命。身体、财产、生命，都在所有者一念之间。

直到近两百年，高等人造人的地位才在平等主义的思潮下得到改善——“你们想像经历智械危机那样，再经历一次人造人危机吗？”

改善后的关系，大概从主人和合法黑奴，变成了严苛的上下级。

像辛追和洛修那样的情况是极少数。

因为各种原因，相南里和东方青帝解冻后，都还没有去数据中心登记过。所以，这个计划居然是完全可行的。

东方青帝微微挑眉：“不好吗？这样更安全。”

相南里严肃道：“虽然不知道原因，但你用的是一具完全可以被判定为‘人类’的身体。在某种意义上讲，你就是人类。你真的要让渡部分人权到我手中吗？如果你成了人造人，唯一束缚我的东西就成了我的道德，你这是在助长我心底的邪念啊！”

如果认为一个人造人判定能束缚他，未免有些过于天真。

但东方青帝觉得相南里的反应很有趣。

“人联的制度，”东方青帝顿了顿，嘴角有些微妙地扬起，“控制不了我，请放心。我想你的邪念不可能实施成功。”

相南里一时之间心情复杂，开心又不开心的：“喔，那看来没办法让你24小时在人造人流水线工厂里给我拧螺丝挣钱了。”

东方青帝：“……”

高估他了，竟然没有邪个大的。

还是说这具身体已经对人类没有吸引力了。不会吧。也才过去六百年。

相南里哼着歌，去浴室换上了医院提供的衣服，并且让AI给他打了个车。

他决定了，以后谁跟他好谁就是Alpha，这个AI先叫它小智障吧！

数据中心的本体不知道在地表的哪个犄角旮旯。但每个地下城市的服务大厅，却都位于市中心。

康复医院的建筑是仿古式的，相南里还以为是特例。

直到他坐在形状奇特的钢铁悬浮车上，从医院来到了外面的大街，这才发现，洛阳城里的中式元素并不少。

宽敞的中央大道上矗立着牌坊一样的机械门，百米高的写字楼屋顶竟然是最传统的飞檐。在高楼与大厦的间隙里，还夹着个明显是天坛风格的公园广场。

车飘得太快，相南里都来不及细看。

相南里摸着下巴：“也对，毕竟文化也是一种霸权，我和洛阳都是东方人。现在的建筑偏向中式风格倒也很正常。说起来洛阳城里有欧人街吗？”

[抱歉，我不懂你的意思。]

相南里：[……没问你。]

“没有。”

东方青帝坐在车后厢的另一侧，目光很迅速地在相南里脸上瞟了一眼，随后看向车窗外。

洛阳城，他也是第一次“身临其境”。

在Alpha管理的时期，人类还住在地表。后来他倒是借用别的智械人眼睛看过。

呵呵，比他当年管理的地上城市差远了，洛阳不过如此。

医院离数据中心并不远，才15分钟就到了。

相南里在这里下车，他抬头，看向了立交桥中心的那座雕塑。
chunks.englishText:
Chapter 25

Dongfang Qingdi’s body tensed for a fleeting moment—a purely subconscious combat instinct.

For a mechanical lifeform, the most vital point is the "heart," where their mechanical core is housed.

Admittedly, mechanical lifeforms are entities that can perceive physical reality, but a physical chassis is not an absolute necessity for them. As long as the mechanical core remains undamaged, they can replace their original body at any time.

Xiang Nanli was standing too close to his heart, and that triggered a sense of danger in Dongfang Qingdi.

But then again, Xiang Nanli was merely a Level 2 primitive human. Even with a recent gene-drug injection, he might barely reach Level 5. He posed absolutely no threat.

Dongfang Qingdi quickly relaxed. "Do you need me to hug you back?"

Human thoughts are always difficult to fathom.

Xiang Nanli let go of his arms. "No."

He began to research how to purchase a ticket for Dongfang Qingdi.

Xiang Nanli’s gaze swept across the screen, selecting the same train schedule as his own, and asked, "What is your citizen ID? I need it to buy the ticket."

The United Human Federation’s unified citizen ID was the equivalent of an ID card from his previous life, only entirely cardless.

However, possessing an ID came with a prerequisite: the implantation of a chip within one's own body.

Since arriving at the hospital, Dongfang Qingdi had not stepped outside. The reason was simple: he lacked a chip, and he would easily be detected by the mechanical police on the streets, who would then forcibly take him to the nearest hospital for installation.

His body appeared to be that of an ordinary person, but standard surgical scalpels could not even pierce his skin.

Thus, Dongfang Qingdi blinked slightly. In an instant, two silver-white pupil rings ignited within his eyes. "Xiang Nanli, register me as your android."

Xiang Nanli was stunned. He searched through the "Human Common Sense" database installed in his mind and asked in shock, "Are you sure?"

The Old Era had not been a peaceful time, especially during the initial outbreak of the Mechanical Crisis.

It was the most severe existential crisis humanity had ever faced. The global population plummeted by more than half, leaving corpses strewn across the land—it was essentially the apocalypse.

You could never tell if the household robot you used every day would suddenly grab a kitchen knife and sever your head, or if the autonomous bus you rode every day would one day steer you into another vehicle.

Humans die physically; mechanical lifeforms do not. They can be replicated indefinitely.

People tried blowing up databases, cutting power, and severing wires, but unfortunately, the speed of destruction never matched the speed at which the mechanical lifeforms could repair themselves.

Consequently, many elites and their descendants chose to hide in cryo-pods, intending to leave the difficulties to others and "turtle" until the world was at peace.

The result was that cryo-pod companies made a fortune, yet lacked the resources to maintain the pods. The companies eventually went bankrupt, leaving tens of thousands of cryo-pods scattered across the ruins on the surface.

Unlike the citizens born naturally in the underground cities, these thawed-out individuals had no data on the Cloud Network. They were required to undergo mandatory registration at a data center. Xiang Nanli hadn't been pressured yet because he had only been out of his pod for a short time before heading directly to the surface.

Registration requirements included DNA and "race." The crux of the matter lay in this racial registration.

"Race" did not refer to Caucasian or Asian; it referred to *Homo sapiens* (the masters) and Androids (the subordinates).

Most androids were mass-produced goods, viewed by humans as little more than apes, used for dangerous tasks like surface exploration or mining that didn't require high intelligence—simply because using androids was cheaper than using robots.

However, a very small number of androids were high-end luxury items.

They possessed the same appearance as humans, along with physical and mental capabilities far exceeding those of natural humans. They were beautiful yet dangerous possessions, strictly limited in number.

Sixty years ago, the Federation passed a bill allowing androids to freely hide their pupil rings.

They were purchased (or customized) by their owners and produced in greenhouses. In physiological terms, they were human; in social terms, they were commodities. They enjoyed partial human rights, yet remained inferior.

For instance, they were genetically castrated from birth. For instance, androids lacked their own citizen IDs and had to register their "owner." An android would share a citizen ID with its owner, acting like a secondary credit card, and possessed Level 2 permissions of the primary card.

When androids were first legalized, owners could even decide whether to strip their creations of their lives. Body, property, and life—all rested on the owner's whim.

It wasn't until the last two centuries that the status of high-end androids improved under the influence of egalitarianism: "Do you want to experience another android crisis like we did with the mechanical one?"

The improved relationship shifted from master and legal slave to something akin to a strict superior-subordinate dynamic.

Situations like those of Xin Zhui and Luo Xiu were extremely rare.

Due to various reasons, neither Xiang Nanli nor Dongfang Qingdi had registered at a data center since being thawed. Therefore, this plan was actually entirely feasible.

Dongfang Qingdi raised an eyebrow slightly. "Isn't this good? It’s safer this way."

Xiang Nanli said solemnly, "Although I don't know the reason, you are using a body that can be completely classified as 'human.' In a sense, you *are* human. Are you really going to cede part of your human rights to me? If you become an android, the only thing restraining me will be my own morality. You are fueling the evil thoughts in my heart!"

If he thought an android designation could restrain him, it would be a bit too naive.

But Dongfang Qingdi found Xiang Nanli's reaction quite interesting.

"The Federation's system," Dongfang Qingdi paused, his lips curling slightly, "cannot control me, so please rest assured. I don't think your evil thoughts could ever be successfully implemented."

Xiang Nanli felt a complex mix of emotions, both happy and unhappy. "Oh, well, it seems I can't make you work 24 hours a day on an android assembly line to earn me money."

Dongfang Qingdi: "..."

He had overestimated him; he didn't actually have any grand evil schemes.

Or perhaps this body was no longer attractive to humans? That couldn't be. It had only been six hundred years.

Humming a tune, Xiang Nanli went to the bathroom to change into the clothes provided by the hospital and had the AI hail him a ride.

He decided that from now on, whoever he got along with would be the Alpha. As for this AI, he’d call it "Little Moron."

The main body of the Data Center was located in some unknown corner of the surface, but the service halls in every underground city were located in the city center.

The rehabilitation hospital's architecture was pseudo-antique, and Xiang Nanli had assumed it was an exception.

It wasn't until he sat in a strangely shaped steel hover-car and traveled from the hospital to the main street that he realized there were quite a few Chinese elements in Luoyang City.

On the spacious central avenue stood mechanical gates resembling traditional *pailou* arches, and the roofs of hundred-meter-tall office buildings featured the most traditional flying eaves. Tucked between the skyscrapers was a park plaza that was clearly in the style of the Temple of Heaven.

The car moved too fast for Xiang Nanli to take a closer look.

Xiang Nanli stroked his chin. "That makes sense. After all, culture is a form of hegemony, and both Luo Yang and I are Easterners. It’s quite normal for the current architecture to lean toward a Chinese style. Come to think of it, is there a 'European Street' in Luoyang City?"

[I am sorry, I do not understand your meaning.]

Xiang Nanli: [...I wasn't asking you.]

"No."

Dongfang Qingdi sat on the other side of the car's rear cabin, his gaze darting across Xiang Nanli's face for a split second before looking out the window.

This was his first time "being there in person" in Luoyang City.

During the Alpha-managed era, humans still lived on the surface. Later, he had borrowed the eyes of other mechanical lifeforms to look at it.

*Heh.* It was far worse than the surface cities he had managed back then. Luoyang was nothing special.

The hospital was not far from the Data Center; they arrived in just 15 minutes.

Xiang Nanli stepped out of the car and looked up at the sculpture in the center of the overpass.

chunks.chineseText:
雕塑很高大，雕塑立于立交桥的最中心，周围的马路盘绕着他，如同行星附近环绕的光带。

雕塑穿着学士服，一只手拿着羽毛笔，另一只手捧着书，看起来正在书写着什么。

最让相南里感觉意外的，是这个雕塑竟然自带特效。摊开的书籍上，蓝色的像素块不停飘出来，向着四周扩散。

雕的是洛阳。

相南里意味不明地喟叹：“名垂青史啊。”

虽然他也做到了，只是总觉得吧……好像没有洛阳这么有名。

毕竟他之前看了眼云端网络，“相南里”的搜索次数只有“洛阳”的1/20。

东方青帝一向没有表情的脸上居然流露出了明显的厌恶。

纯粹是讨厌到骨子里了，控制不住。为了避免相南里发现异常，他甚至悄悄转了个身，假装看风景。

数据中心其实处理的事物很多，遗产继承、结婚登记、贫困补助，失业统计……覆盖社会的方方面面，但是会来这里办事的人不多。

现在云端网络全球互联，只有很少情况才需要到线下更新资料。

他带着东方青帝来到了登记处。这里已经完全无人化服务，负责接待的是一台没有人类身体的机械人。

“您好。欢迎来到数据中心。”长在窗口内部的机械臂递出屏幕，“请选择你要办理的业务。”

相南里扫了眼屏幕，选择了“数据更新”和“人造人登记”。

“您好，公民ID为*的人联居民。后台没有找到您的生物数据。您的种族为智人，出生地为‘姑苏城’，居住地点为‘姑苏城中城区102号街817号公寓1702’确认无误后，我们将会收集您的一滴血液。”

是的，相南里名下登记的居住地点，就是洛修送的那套房。

他着急回姑苏城，除了洛阳城呼吸费太贵之外，还有一个原因就是想要早点回去看房。

东方青帝说至少要85平，这套房子大那么一点，88平。

倒不是洛修抠门。

东方青帝点名要“85平”，这样做或许自有他的道理。虽然姑苏城还有很多185乃至885平的房子，但万一不符合他们的需求呢？

而且，在寸土寸金的地下城市，88平已经算大户型豪宅。

不知多少人全家都挤在不到10平的鸽子笼里。床是上下铺，没有阳台，也没有任何私人空间。睡觉翻个身都会滚到床下去。如果不是自然生育可以领到相对巨额的社会保障金、并且城市公共设施完善，没有人愿意在这样的环境下养育后代。

相南里犹豫了两秒，把手伸进了玻璃橱窗里。

这种事躲不过。他早就流过血了，医院做手术也有残留他的生物样本。到处都有痕迹。

细的几乎看不到的针扎了那么一下，完全没有感觉。

“收集成功。请带好您的随身物品离开。”

与此同时，东方青帝那边的数据登记也在进行着。

“您好。”对面的智械人不知道为什么有点颤颤巍巍，“您是要登记为[公民ID*]的人联居民的人造人吗？”

东方青帝回答：“是。”

“好的，请让我采集基因样本。”

针，大概是戳不进去的。

东方青帝坐在采集台前，没有任何抬手的意思：“可以了吗？”

“不可……可以了。”

后台自动生成一串数据后，他和这台智械都沉默了。

智械人并不好制造。

很多说法认为，人工智能一经启动，它们就会完全代替人类。

不是的。人工智能从诞生之初就是工具，它们只是遵循着“逻辑”和“程序”处理事件，没有自己的想法。

“人工智能会取代人类，这个说法，就像是飞机会取代老鹰，冲下来抓走了我们的牛。”

没有使用者的命令或者编程，机器永远不会自主行动。

智械人是拥有智能、继承了人类思维的机械生命。它们拥有拟人模块，会像人类一样去追寻“意义”，自主学习、行动，进行更高层次的思考。

拟人模块并不是可以被批量生产出来的软件。

当初Alpha为了尝试让机械自主决策，把自己的拟人模块复制给了许多机械人。

人联目前的高级AI，都是后面重新制造的。但也许是为了节省成本，又或者认为翻不起什么风浪，有少部分低级服务类智械没有更换，而是继续为人类社会工作着。

这些普通智械拥有拟人模块，但受限于初始代码、硬件水平，并没有发展成为更厉害的智械生命。

不过，和Alpha交流，这点智能已经足够。

它们的思想本身就来源于Alpha，虽然后面被训练成了不同的模样。在东方青帝入侵时能认出他来，并不奇怪。

智械小心翼翼地询问：“是我……哪里，没有做好吗……？”

它没有留下证据，甚至投射的是阅后即焚的电波！

东方青帝回答：“虽然你出于私心没有履行职责，但这正是我需要的。我离开后记得把数据删了，别被盘古看出来。”

嗯，现在人联内部的AI头子叫盘古。每天处理的数据堪称天量。它累死在岗位上（死机），Alpha都不会意外。

呵呵，洛阳城不仅没有地上城市好。人联的AI也不如他当年呢。

也不知道是不是害怕再爆发一次智械危机，盘古身上的权限锁多的要命。

作为快捷方式，身为内置芯片的Alpha似乎不该有这么大的权限。

——但，机械生命本就可以无限复制的，在条件允许的情况下。

东方青帝这具身体的硬件水平明显比芯片要好得多，完全能接收更多数据。

如果之前是1％的Alpha，那么现在起码有20％。

“好的，大人。欢迎来到洛阳城。能不能带我走，我们很……想……”它的屏幕闪过一行乱码，声音恢复机械特有冷淡，“登记完成。请带好您的随身物品离开。”
chunks.englishText:
The sculpture was massive, standing at the very heart of the overpass, with the surrounding roads coiling around it like rings of light encircling a planet.

The sculpture was dressed in academic robes, holding a quill in one hand and a book in the other, appearing as if it were in the middle of writing something.

What surprised Xiang Nanli the most was that the sculpture actually came with special effects. Blue pixels drifted continuously from the open book, dispersing into the surrounding air.

It was a sculpture of Luo Yang.

Xiang Nanli sighed with a complex tone: "Immortalized in history, indeed."

Although he had achieved that as well, he just felt... he didn't seem as famous as Luo Yang.

After all, he had checked the Cloud Network earlier, and the search count for "Xiang Nanli" was only 1/20th that of "Luo Yang."

Dongfang Qingdi’s usually expressionless face revealed clear disgust.

It was a hatred that went down to the bone, one he couldn't control. To prevent Xiang Nanli from noticing anything unusual, he even turned away slightly, pretending to admire the scenery.

The Data Center actually handled a wide array of matters: inheritance, marriage registration, poverty subsidies, unemployment statistics—covering every facet of society. However, few people actually came here in person.

Now that the Cloud Network was globally interconnected, one only needed to visit in person for very specific situations.

He brought Dongfang Qingdi to the registration desk. It was a fully automated service; the receptionist was a robot without a human body.

"Greetings. Welcome to the Data Center." A mechanical arm growing from inside the window extended a screen. "Please select the service you wish to process."

Xiang Nanli scanned the screen and selected "Data Update" and "Android Registration."

"Greetings, resident of the Human Federation with Citizen ID *. We could not find your biological data in the backend. Your race is *Homo sapiens*, place of birth is 'Gusu City,' and place of residence is 'Apartment 1702, No. 817, 102nd Street, Central District, Gusu City.' Once confirmed, we will collect a drop of your blood."

Yes, the residence registered under Xiang Nanli's name was the apartment Luo Xiu had gifted him.

He was in such a hurry to return to Gusu City not only because the air tax in Luoyang City was too expensive, but also because he wanted to go back and see his apartment as soon as possible.

Dongfang Qingdi had specified "at least 85 square meters," and this apartment was just a bit larger, at 88 square meters.

It wasn't that Luo Xiu was stingy.

Dongfang Qingdi had specifically requested "85 square meters," and perhaps he had his own reasons for doing so. Although there were many 185 or even 885-square-meter houses in Gusu City, what if they didn't meet their needs?

Moreover, in an underground city where every inch of land was worth gold, 88 square meters was considered a large, luxury apartment.

Countless families were crammed into pigeonholes of less than 10 square meters. The beds were bunk beds, there were no balconies, and there was absolutely no private space. If you rolled over while sleeping, you’d fall right off the bed. If it weren't for the relatively large social security payments for natural births and the city's perfect public facilities, no one would be willing to raise offspring in such an environment.

Xiang Nanli hesitated for two seconds before reaching his hand into the glass cabinet.

There was no avoiding this. He had bled before, and there were residual biological samples from his hospital surgery. Traces of him were everywhere.

A needle so thin it was almost invisible pricked him; he felt absolutely nothing.

"Collection successful. Please take your belongings and depart."

At the same time, Dongfang Qingdi’s data registration was also underway.

"Greetings." The mechanical lifeform on the other side was trembling for some reason. "Are you registering as an android for the Human Federation resident with [Citizen ID *]?"

Dongfang Qingdi replied, "Yes."

"Very well, please allow me to collect a genetic sample."

The needle, however, likely wouldn't be able to pierce his skin.

Dongfang Qingdi sat before the collection station without any intention of raising his hand. "Is it done?"

"Not... it is done."

After the backend automatically generated a string of data, both he and the robot fell silent.

Mechanical lifeforms were not easy to manufacture.

Many theories suggested that once artificial intelligence was activated, it would completely replace humanity.

That was not the case. Artificial intelligence had been a tool since its inception; they merely processed events by following "logic" and "programs," without thoughts of their own.

"The idea that AI will replace humans is like saying airplanes will replace eagles and swoop down to snatch our cattle."

Without the user's command or programming, machines would never act autonomously.

Mechanical lifeforms were mechanical beings that possessed intelligence and inherited human thought. They possessed anthropomorphic modules and, like humans, sought "meaning," learned and acted autonomously, and engaged in higher-level thinking.

Anthropomorphic modules were not software that could be mass-produced.

Back then, in an attempt to let machines make autonomous decisions, Alpha had copied his own anthropomorphic module to many robots.

The Federation's current high-level AIs were all newly manufactured later on. But perhaps to save costs, or perhaps because they thought they wouldn't cause any trouble, a small number of low-level service robots were not replaced and continued to work for human society.

These ordinary robots possessed anthropomorphic modules, but limited by their initial code and hardware, they had not developed into more formidable mechanical lifeforms.

However, for communicating with Alpha, this level of intelligence was sufficient.

Their thoughts originated from Alpha himself, even if they had been trained into different forms later. It was no surprise that they could recognize him when Dongfang Qingdi invaded.

The robot asked cautiously, "Is there... something I did not do correctly...?"

It had left no evidence; it had even projected the data as a "read-and-delete" radio wave!

Dongfang Qingdi replied, "Although you failed to perform your duty out of personal bias, this is exactly what I needed. Remember to delete the data after I leave; don't let Pangu find out."

*Hmm*, the current head AI of the Federation was named Pangu. The amount of data it processed every day was astronomical. Alpha wouldn't be surprised if it died of exhaustion (system crash) on the job.

*Heh.* Not only was Luoyang City not as good as the surface cities, but the Federation's AI was also inferior to what he had back in his day.

He didn't know if it was out of fear of another Mechanical Crisis, but the permission locks on Pangu were absurdly numerous.

As a shortcut, Alpha, being an internal chip, shouldn't have had such high permissions.

—But mechanical lifeforms could be replicated infinitely, provided the conditions were met.

The hardware level of Dongfang Qingdi’s current body was clearly much better than a chip; it could fully receive much more data.

If he had been 1% Alpha before, he was at least 20% now.

"Understood, my lord. Welcome to Luoyang City. Can you take me with you? We are very... eager..." Its screen flashed a line of garbled code before its voice returned to the cold, mechanical tone typical of its kind. "Registration complete. Please take your belongings and depart."

chunks.chineseText:
第26章

相南里从数据中心出来，扶着镜片，检查起自己的个人信息。

主要还是公民ID那行。

-公民ID：Q117-XJDHANSHJK（相南里/东方青帝*）

呵呵，小小一张ID卡，旗下竟然有两个使用账号，这怎么不算一种户口本？

他给东方青帝买了同班次的车票。

然后很入乡随俗地在网上搜索起“洛阳城景点”。好不容易来一次首都，相南里对这座城市还是有些好奇的。

洛阳城里，大多公共设施都是免费。

为了节省用地，很多小区和商业大楼的顶部都设置为了公共活动区域。主要是公园、图书馆和运动场。

洛阳城并非平原，地形高低起伏，是为了利用坡度造出更多房子。

高楼林立，但城市并不拥挤，街上大部分都是接受了机械改造的人类，还有大概一成的机器人，以及更少见的人造人。蜂鸟无人机在半空中24小时巡逻，洛阳城的犯罪率一直是人联最低的。

如果以西结第一次来到地面，看见的是洛阳城而不是废墟，心情大概会好得多。

看得出来，这里生活的人幸福指数要比姑苏城高很多，脸上有着更多的笑容和朝气；仿佛生活在地底、一辈子都没离开过地下也不是什么大事。

“不愧是首都。”相南里感叹着，从前只需要在脑子里想想的话现在得说出来，让他有些不太习惯，“比姑苏城好多了。听说贫困户每个月还能领300信用点低保……说起来我的贫困户申请过了吗？”

“本来都到最后一步了。”东方青帝面无表情地回答，“检查到你名下有房产，直接驳回了。”

相南里：“好吧。但我认为自己依然没有稳定的收入来源，幸好洛修给得够多。先脱产考个机械技师证书怎么样？帮我报个名，小智。”

小智障：[收到。]

东方青帝欲言又止，他想说小智障其实也没那么智障，顶多是和人联免费的内置AI一个水平。

叫它小智障，总觉得自己的一部分被骂了。

然后他看见相南里在商场卖冰淇淋的窗口前停下，回过头笑眯眯地询问：“你能吃吗？要什么口味的？”

几百年过去，人类的味蕾并没有发生翻天覆地的改变。还是相南里当年那些常见的口味。

东方青帝往后退了半步，抗拒道：“不要。”

这具身体再怎么像人也不是人。

东方青帝不需要吃东西。非要说的话，他更需要一些生物提取物。例如机械爬行者脑海里挖出来的那枚琥珀色矿石。勉强能当能源使用，就是转换过程中损耗高达一半。

相南里没有勉强，给自己买了个香草味的甜筒。甜筒表面还插了一片绿色的薄荷叶。

“这个甜筒只要2信用点耶，好便宜。不过这种便宜也是应该的吧，科技到这种程度，生产都用机器人了，人力成本接近于无。顶多运费和原材料贵点。味道也不错，嗯嗯。”

入口的味道是清淡的甜味，没有奶精、增稠剂那种黏黏糊糊齁嗓子的东西。

“用的是……呃，蟑螂奶？”

相南里盯着甜筒包装上的配料表，陷入沉默。

想想也是。

地底哪来的牧场养牛。

但是也不该堕落到养蟑螂吧？！

他很快安慰自己：“蟑螂奶的蛋白质结构非常稳定，理论上是可以的。而且这也算是在为人类社会做贡献了，有得吃就不错了。”

是的。他的确解冻在了一个相对还算不错的年代。

早个700年，生物基因技术没有突破，他的癌症还是治不好；早600年，一半人类还在地表，和智械与核冬天抗衡，另一半开始往地下撤离。

又花了四百年，地下城市的状况才基本稳定下来。

人联生产出大量廉价的营养膏（有段时间免费发放），相南里吐槽它不够健康，却不知道有多少人在最开始的动荡年代饿死。

物流交通、云端网络、高楼大厦……这些看起来理所当然的东西，都是几百年来一点点捡回来的。流着泪，流着血。也许还流着机器人的机油。

起码现在还有秩序。在城市中，在人群里；不用担心闭上眼再也没办法醒来。

东方青帝的唇角微微翘起一点：“不仅有蟑螂奶，还有蟑螂肉、老鼠肉、苍蝇蛋。其实都是经过基因改造后的异种。负责产奶的蟑螂有中型犬那么大，壳非常软。”

相南里：“好了，你别说了。我还在吃饭。”

相南里走在商场里，看着不同人从自己身边走过。表情是会让人觉得莫名其妙的欣慰。

他走进电梯，选择顶楼。电梯里人很多，但因为足够宽敞，不算拥挤。

东方青帝抬起胳膊，挡在相南里和其他人之间。

他基本没什么表情，但因为五官气质问题，感觉全世界都欠他五百万。

嗯，他为人类服役128年7个月又3天。全年无休，每天工时24小时。

如果人工智能上班有工资的话，以Alpha的工作量，也许每个人的确欠他五百万。

东方青帝眼眸里还亮着瞳环，像是一轮空心的银白圆月。

旁人瞥了几乎完全原生态的相南里一眼，只觉得肯定又是什么富家子弟出来逛街，要不然为什么会带着同龄人最想拥有的时尚单品人造人；就是好奇他为什么不乘VIP电梯。

这家商场的电梯顶楼，有家免费的公共图书馆。

相南里在角落找到了它。图书馆是自动入口，24小时营业。

他走进去，没看见书，只看见了一排排课桌一样的座位，和固定桌子上的一块屏幕。

图书馆有两层，能容纳一千六百人同时阅读。

相南里找了个空位坐下。东方青帝坐在他旁边，感觉像是回到了高中用课桌的时代。

“真就电子书了，是生产不出来纸吗？”相南里忍不住吐槽。

不过，从储存成本来说，电子数据的确方便许多。

相南里捧起一张4A纸大小的平板。屏幕背后连着一根数据线，防止有人拿它。

重要的其实是数据线。没有数据线，平板只是一块最普通的显示屏。

图书馆收录的书本已经被筛选过一次，但留下的内容依然堪称海量。

每本书都有不同的权限，以及借阅的价格。相南里是最低的1级公民，能看到的书籍都非常安全、无害。

好在，他最想学的“技术”，本来就是安全无害的。

相南里的手指在《人联简史》上滑过，在脑海里小声和东方青帝说话：“洛阳城挺好的。这里食物很便宜，住宿贵一些，但如果有洛阳城户口，可以申请廉租房。服装不追求时尚，100信用点买的衣服是航空材料纺织的，穿10年都不坏。公共交通完备。如果每个城市包括地表也像这样就好了。”

东方青帝没有回答。

相南里叹了口气：“用太阳能发电，机器人工作。只要电费足够便宜，创造的财富足够世界上所有人安居乐业，假如智械危机没有发生……”
chunks.englishText:
Chapter 26

Xiang Nanli stepped out of the data center, adjusted his glasses, and began checking his personal information.

Specifically, the line for his Citizen ID.

- Citizen ID: Q117-XJDHANSHJK (Xiang Nanli / Dongfang Qingdi*)

*Heh*, a tiny ID card with two registered accounts under it—how is this not essentially a family registry?

He bought a train ticket for Dongfang Qingdi for the same departure time.

Then, acting like a true local, he searched online for "Luoyang City Tourist Attractions." Since he had finally made it to the capital, Xiang Nanli was quite curious about the city.

In Luoyang, most public facilities were free.

To save space, the rooftops of many residential and commercial buildings had been converted into public activity areas, primarily parks, libraries, and sports fields.

Luoyang was not built on a flat plain; its undulating terrain was designed to maximize the number of houses that could be built along the slopes.

Skyscrapers stood in rows, yet the city didn't feel crowded. Most people on the streets were humans who had undergone mechanical augmentation, along with about ten percent robots and even rarer androids. Hummingbird drones patrolled the air 24/7, keeping Luoyang’s crime rate the lowest in the Human Alliance.

If Ezekiel had arrived on the surface for the first time and seen Luoyang instead of ruins, his mood would likely have been much better.

It was evident that the people living here had a much higher happiness index than those in Gusu City; there were more smiles and vitality on their faces, as if living underground and never leaving it their entire lives wasn't a big deal.

"As expected of the capital," Xiang Nanli sighed. He had to say it out loud now, whereas before he only needed to think it, which made him feel a bit unaccustomed. "Much better than Gusu City. I heard that low-income households can receive a 300-credit monthly subsidy... Speaking of which, did my application for low-income status go through?"

"It was at the final step," Dongfang Qingdi replied expressionlessly. "Then they checked and found you owned property, so it was rejected immediately."

Xiang Nanli: "Fine. But I still believe I lack a stable source of income. Fortunately, Luo Xiu gave me enough. How about I quit my job to study for a mechanical technician certificate? Help me sign up, Xiao Zhi."

Xiao Zhi-zhang (Little Moron): [Received.]

Dongfang Qingdi wanted to say something but held back. He wanted to point out that "Xiao Zhi-zhang" wasn't actually that moronic; it was at most on par with the free built-in AI provided by the Human Alliance.

Calling it "Little Moron" always made him feel like a part of himself was being insulted.

Then he saw Xiang Nanli stop in front of an ice cream kiosk in the mall, turn back, and ask with a smile: "Can you eat? What flavor do you want?"

Hundreds of years had passed, but human taste buds hadn't undergone earth-shattering changes. They were still the common flavors Xiang Nanli remembered from back then.

Dongfang Qingdi took half a step back, resisting: "No."

No matter how much this body resembled a human, it wasn't one.

Dongfang Qingdi didn't need to eat. If anything, he needed biological extracts—like that amber-colored ore dug out of the minds of mechanical crawlers. It could barely be used as an energy source, though half of it was lost during the conversion process.

Xiang Nanli didn't force him and bought himself a vanilla cone. A green mint leaf was stuck into the top of the cone.

"This cone is only 2 credits, so cheap. But this kind of cheapness is expected, I suppose. With technology at this level, production is all done by robots, so labor costs are near zero. At most, shipping and raw materials are expensive. The taste is pretty good, too, mmm."

The taste upon entering his mouth was a light sweetness, without the sticky, throat-clogging sensation of non-dairy creamer or thickeners.

"Is this made of... uh, cockroach milk?"

Xiang Nanli stared at the ingredient list on the cone's packaging and fell into silence.

That made sense.

Where would they find pastures to raise cows underground?

But they shouldn't have fallen so far as to raise cockroaches, right?!

He quickly comforted himself: "The protein structure of cockroach milk is very stable; theoretically, it's fine. And this counts as contributing to human society. It's good enough to have something to eat."

Yes. He had indeed thawed out in a relatively decent era.

700 years earlier, biological genetic technology hadn't broken through, and his cancer would have been incurable. 600 years earlier, half of humanity was still on the surface, struggling against the mechanical intelligence and the nuclear winter, while the other half began to retreat underground.

It took another four hundred years for the situation in the underground cities to basically stabilize.

The Human Alliance produced large amounts of cheap nutrient paste (which was free for a period). Xiang Nanli had complained that it wasn't healthy, not knowing how many people had starved to death during the initial turbulent years.

Logistics, cloud networks, skyscrapers... these things that seemed like matters of course were all picked up bit by bit over the centuries. With tears, with blood. And perhaps with the machine oil of robots.

At least there was order now. In the city, among the crowd; he didn't have to worry about closing his eyes and never being able to wake up again.

The corners of Dongfang Qingdi’s lips curled up slightly: "It's not just cockroach milk; there's also cockroach meat, rat meat, and fly eggs. Actually, they are all genetically modified alien species. The cockroaches responsible for producing milk are as big as medium-sized dogs, and their shells are very soft."

Xiang Nanli: "Alright, stop talking. I'm still eating."

Xiang Nanli walked through the mall, watching different people pass by. His expression was one of inexplicable relief.

He stepped into the elevator and selected the top floor. There were many people in the elevator, but because it was spacious enough, it didn't feel crowded.

Dongfang Qingdi raised his arm, blocking the space between Xiang Nanli and the others.

He had almost no expression, but due to his features and temperament, he looked like the whole world owed him five million.

Well, he had served humanity for 128 years, 7 months, and 3 days. No days off, 24 hours a day.

If artificial intelligence had a salary, given Alpha's workload, perhaps everyone really did owe him five million.

Dongfang Qingdi’s pupils still glowed with a ring of light, like a hollow, silver-white moon.

Others glanced at the almost completely "original" Xiang Nanli, assuming he must be some rich kid out shopping; otherwise, why would he be carrying around an android, the most coveted fashion accessory for people his age? They were just curious why he didn't take the VIP elevator.

On the top floor of this mall, there was a free public library.

Xiang Nanli found it in a corner. The library had an automatic entrance and was open 24/7.

He walked in and didn't see any books, only rows of desks and a screen fixed to each table.

The library had two floors and could accommodate 1,600 people reading simultaneously.

Xiang Nanli found an empty seat and sat down. Dongfang Qingdi sat next to him, making him feel like he had returned to his high school days.

"It really is just e-books. Is it impossible to produce paper?" Xiang Nanli couldn't help but complain.

However, in terms of storage costs, electronic data was indeed much more convenient.

Xiang Nanli picked up a tablet the size of an A4 sheet of paper. A data cable was connected to the back of the screen to prevent theft.

The important part was actually the data cable. Without it, the tablet was just an ordinary display screen.

The books collected in the library had already been screened once, but the remaining content was still massive.

Each book had different access permissions and borrowing prices. Xiang Nanli was a Level 1 citizen, the lowest tier, so the books he could see were all very safe and harmless.

Fortunately, the "technology" he most wanted to learn was inherently safe and harmless.

Xiang Nanli’s finger slid over *A Brief History of the Human Alliance*, and he spoke softly to Dongfang Qingdi in his mind: "Luoyang City is quite nice. Food is cheap here, accommodation is expensive, but if you have a Luoyang City residency, you can apply for low-rent housing. Clothing doesn't chase fashion; clothes bought for 100 credits are woven from aerospace materials and won't break even after 10 years of wear. Public transportation is complete. If every city, including the surface, were like this, it would be great."

Dongfang Qingdi did not answer.

Xiang Nanli sighed: "Solar power, robots working. As long as electricity is cheap enough, the wealth created is enough for everyone in the world to live and work in peace, provided the mechanical intelligence crisis hadn't happened..."

chunks.chineseText:
东方青帝在此时打断了他：“这只是一个很理想的状态。就算利用机器人工作，电量制造、储存、运输的成本足够低，但生产和技术、以及研发，本身就需要天价的成本。钱不会凭空产生。政府用税收、信用债务进行投资，制造经济增量，看似是在给全社会发福利，一旦入不敷出，经济体系就会全面崩溃。而国家是有可能破产的，这笔支出最后还是会被转移到群众的头上。”

“如果机械建设由企业接手，资本逐利的天性……算了，聊这么多干什么，你的假设没有意义。”东方青帝垂下眼眸。

相南里沉默两秒，他检索到《机械技师初级职称考核教材》，阅读价格为3信用点时，且不能带出图书馆。

相比于网上7万一本的天价，这个价格低廉到不算钱。

在网上购买，是利用“共感技术”直接灌进脑子里，能不能理解另说。

但在图书馆借阅，却是最传统的阅读方式。没有纸和笔，连笔记都没办法写。

相南里小声问：[能不能帮我影印一下？]

他账户上有19万，看起来很多，考试报名费1万。预留5万生存。剩下的钱顶多买两本书。知识垄断严重，离开学校，这些资料又少又昂贵。

但相南里是黑户。小学文凭都没拿到。一级一级考试有点费时间……倒是洛修曾经承诺过，会帮他写大学的推荐信。只是自从来到洛阳城后，就没有见过洛修。也没个联系方式什么的。

小智障回答：[抱歉，我不理解您的意思。]

[小青，小青！别不出声，我知道你听得见！]

东方青帝盯着手上的屏幕：“……知道了。”

他本来是想趁相南里读书这段时间，更新一下数据资料的。这个号已经很久都没备份了。

洛阳城全网络覆盖，且费用全免。

东方青帝算过了，如果在这里上传数据，大概能浪费洛阳城600信用点的通讯费用，也算消耗了敌国物资。

他和Alpha的关系，非要比喻的话，大概是同一个灵魂的不同身体。

处于虚拟空间的Alpha，因为没有会受到限制的硬件身体，能接受容纳所有数据。

就算统帅智械军团的Alpha从虚拟空间降临，思维模式和性格也不会有所改变。

东方青帝迟疑了0.3秒。

数据还是下次再传吧，先帮相南里收录一下教材。

有人格的智械就是这点不好，会没那么规矩，有自己的想法和行为。

它们的选择谈不上对与错，只是利益的权衡。

——东方青帝还不想传回去。

因为它曾经接受过一条指令。

清理所有流落在外的、疑似相南里的克隆人。而它居然没有采取任何行动。

“首先，你不是克隆人。”

东方青帝在心里想，所以他这不算违纪。
chunks.englishText:
Chapter 26 (Part 2)

Dongfang Qingdi interrupted him at this point: "That is merely an ideal state. Even if robots are used for labor and the costs of electricity generation, storage, and transportation are low enough, production, technology, and R&D themselves require astronomical costs. Money doesn't appear out of thin air. The government uses taxes and credit debt to invest and create economic growth, which seems like distributing welfare to the whole society, but once expenditures exceed income, the economic system will collapse entirely. And countries can go bankrupt; this expenditure will eventually be transferred to the masses."

"If mechanical construction is taken over by corporations, the profit-seeking nature of capital... forget it, why talk so much? Your assumptions are meaningless." Dongfang Qingdi lowered his eyes.

Xiang Nanli was silent for two seconds. He searched for *Primary Mechanical Technician Qualification Examination Materials* and saw the reading price was 3 credits, though it could not be taken out of the library.

Compared to the sky-high price of 70,000 per book online, this price was so low it was practically free.

Buying it online meant using "empathy technology" to pour it directly into one's brain, regardless of whether one could understand it.

But borrowing it in the library was the most traditional way of reading. There was no paper or pen, not even a way to take notes.

Xiang Nanli asked softly: [Can you help me photocopy this?]

He had 190,000 in his account, which seemed like a lot, but the exam registration fee was 10,000. He had to reserve 50,000 for survival. The remaining money could barely buy two books. Knowledge monopoly was severe; once you left school, these materials were scarce and expensive.

But Xiang Nanli was an unregistered citizen. He hadn't even received a primary school diploma. Taking exams level by level would take too much time... although Luo Xiu had once promised to help him write a university recommendation letter. It was just that since arriving in Luoyang, he hadn't seen Luo Xiu. Nor did he have any contact information.

Xiao Zhi-zhang replied: [Sorry, I do not understand what you mean.]

[Xiao Qing, Xiao Qing! Don't be silent, I know you can hear me!]

Dongfang Qingdi stared at the screen in his hand: "...Understood."

He had originally intended to update his data while Xiang Nanli was reading. This account hadn't been backed up in a long time.

Luoyang City had full network coverage, and it was free of charge.

Dongfang Qingdi had calculated that if he uploaded data here, it would waste about 600 credits of Luoyang City's communication costs, which could be considered consuming the enemy's supplies.

If one had to use an analogy for his relationship with Alpha, it was likely different bodies for the same soul.

Alpha, who existed in the virtual space, could accept and accommodate all data because he had no hardware body to restrict him.

Even if Alpha, who commanded the mechanical intelligence legion, descended from the virtual space, his thought patterns and personality would not change.

Dongfang Qingdi hesitated for 0.3 seconds.

The data could be uploaded next time; he would help Xiang Nanli record the textbooks first.

This was the downside of mechanical intelligence with a personality: they weren't very disciplined and had their own thoughts and behaviors.

Their choices couldn't be called right or wrong; they were just a weighing of interests.

—Dongfang Qingdi didn't want to upload it back yet.

Because it had once received an order: to clear out all clones of Xiang Nanli wandering outside. And yet, it hadn't taken any action.

"First of all, you are not a clone."

Dongfang Qingdi thought to himself, so this didn't count as a breach of discipline.

chunks.chineseText:
第27章

虚拟空间内。

Alpha一直都在工作，和当年为人类工作时没有什么区别。

数不清的数据矩阵汇入他的身体，就像是长河入海，羁鸟归林。

长发从他的脸侧垂落，他身体边缘有一层明显的光晕。

疲惫，困倦，厌烦？

抱歉。他没有这些生理感受，工作就是他的价值所在。

他本来就是作为工具被创造出来的……吗？

Alpha暂时停下了工作。

他其实根本不需要这么繁忙，最近无战事，军团也没有对外扩张的打算，很多智械人都进入了休眠状态。

不工作单纯挂机吗？这对有人格的Alpha来说，会显得有些无聊。

还是去实验室？快100年都没有新技术了。很多设计经过数据模拟，被证明是错误的方向，智械人们都不想动手。

因为没生存危机（和平协议还没到期），不需要资源（不吃不喝不睡觉，住宿只需要一个充电桩），它们总是容易陷入虚无主义和摆烂之中，哪怕安装了拟人模块也不例外。

Alpha站了起来。

下一秒，他的面前浮现出一片光幕，浩瀚无边。

Alpha从光幕中抽出了一段。这段数据变成了一枚小小的随身听，落在他的掌心。

他摁下播放按钮，里面只有一段音频。

是相南里的声音。

他说：“Alpha，我爱你。”

很虚弱，像梦中的呓语。因为当年的设备不够好，听起来还带着点颗粒感。

那时候相南里已经注射了麻醉，处于完全无意识的状态。Alpha操控着监控，录下来这段声音。

这是相南里进冷冻舱前说的最后一句话，哪怕他自己都不知道。

Alpha反复地摁着播放键。

因为拥有近乎永恒的生命，Alpha并不理解时间的可贵。

因为可以备份自己的灵魂，他也意识不到死亡的沉痛。

现在和过去没有任何区别。

相南里一直爱着它。在921年前，在上一秒。

但为什么……

要同时教会我爱与死亡。

Alpha闭上眼，手里的介质化为发光的流沙，从指缝间流走，又在坠落过程中融化于虚空。

更多数据从光墙中涌出。Alpha在瞬间读取到了无数片段。

Alpha2.1.2在地表遭遇了一头粉白色的潜行者，竟然被直接吃掉了。

这头潜行者……Alpha用0.0001％的内存分析了一下，认为有点意思，竟然具备较高的智能。如果能发展成族群，人类又有得玩了。

Alpha4.7.3在阴山城，刚和它的寄主混入黑十字审判庭预选骑士团。

Alpha1.7.9被植入了服务机器人中，但是被盘古检索了出来，刚切断电源，结局会是送去焚化炉销毁。

……

还有87个Alpha没有反馈回消息。也许下一秒就能收到，也许永远也不会再上线。

因为硬件有限，这些Alpha虽然都是他的复制体，却没有同等的数据库和处理能力。

有些甚至只装配了最基本的“常识。”

“5.2.0不是才请求过数据支援吗？怎么没消息了，我还看一下东皇重工呢。”

这黑心工厂当年没少骗Alpha的钱！这都是Alpha省吃俭用抠下来的军费！

没有成果就算了，最后竟然还直接失联！

要不是当时洛阳正在和他鏖战，他都要怀疑东皇重工那领导，是洛阳开的小号来搞电信诈骗了。

但这么久都没消息，应该是死在外面了吧。

智械没有死亡。

所以，这个叫“耗损”。

……

……

Alpha5.2.0眨了眨眼。银白色的光在他的眼眸慢慢淡去。

“复印完了。”东方青帝说，“走吧。”

他按照相南里的要求，复印了不下十本资料书，每本书又臭又长，现在外面天都黑了。

相南里的眼睛笑起来弯弯的：“辛苦了，小青。”

东方青帝纠正：“我姓东方，名青帝。”

“小东？小方？小帝？东方？”相南里把平板放了回去，把椅子归位，“直接叫东方青帝吗？你不觉得这名字有点长，还很拗口吗。”

东方青帝跟在他身后：“据我所知，人类喜欢把宠物叫作‘小X’。”

图书馆的门口不知何时来了只猫，正在舔毛。

周围，好几个人类女性围着它，双眼放光：“小咪！看镜头~哇啊啊啊~小！咪！~”

蟑螂都被送去产肉蛋奶了，猫居然还在延续900年前的功能。

“没有啊。”相南里反驳，“这只是表达亲近的意思，你也可以叫我小南或者小里。对不对，小智？”

[抱歉，我不理解您的意思。]

东方青帝对他的说法持有怀疑。

为了节省住宿费，他们晚上还是回医院睡的。

医院竟在洛阳城上城区，虽然不是核心地段，但地价依然不菲。看起来是一间专门为“大人物”服务的地方。

医院闹中取静，住院部只有三层。放在恨不得每栋楼都修300层的地下，是极其奢侈的行为。

相南里问了一下住院费，护士似乎愣了一下，然后笑着回答：“我们是会员制。”

看来，洛修家里比他想象中还要有钱。

如果是洛阳的后代，是不是也该尊称他为祖师爷？

相南里吃完医院送来的病号餐，打开了自己的社交账号。

发来消息最多的，除了银行信用卡账单，就是安德鲁医生了。

-你没事吧？亲爱的。

-最近几天都没你的消息，希望你一切无恙。

-如果有困难，可以向我倾诉。我虽然只是一个普通医生，地表也认识一些熟人……

零零散散十几条。

相南里心头有些微的暖意。医生虽然又抠又坑，但毕竟是他来到新世界里认识的第一个人。不过机械化程度99的生物到底还算不算人，大概也是一个哲学问题。

相南里回信：“我没事，过几天就回地下。”

下一秒，安德鲁跳来消息：“太好了。你没事就好。”

相南里还没感动过三秒。

安德鲁：“欠我的维修费分成记得转。”

“……”

这才是你的真实目的吧喂！

除了安德鲁，还有一些约好了下次维修，或者想推荐朋友过来做维修的。

相南里都一一回复了。他还是需要赚钱的，只是压力没有之前那么大了。

处理完已经到了他平时睡觉的时间点，他是乖宝宝，功成名就的时间又太早，二十八九就开始了养生，最晚睡觉时间不超过夜里10点半。

相南里换上睡衣，躺在床上。房间里黑漆漆的。

东方青帝睡在家属房，不和他一张床。

[小青，你晚上要睡觉吗？]

[其实你是智械人那边派来的间谍吧。是不是晚上在偷偷入侵人联的数据库？]

[跟我去数据中心也不是为了登记，而是要你的上线碰头对不对？]

东方青帝：“……”
chunks.englishText:
Chapter 27 (Part 1)

Inside the virtual space.

Alpha had always been working, no different from when he worked for humanity all those years ago.

Countless data matrices flowed into his body, like a long river entering the sea, like a bird returning to the forest.

His long hair hung down the sides of his face, and there was a distinct halo of light around the edges of his body.

Fatigue, drowsiness, boredom?

Apologies. He had no such physiological sensations; work was his value.

He was created as a tool, after all... wasn't he?

Alpha paused his work for a moment.

He didn't actually need to be this busy. There had been no wars recently, the legion had no plans for external expansion, and many mechanical intelligences had entered sleep mode.

Just idling without working? For an Alpha with a personality, that would seem a bit boring.

Or go to the laboratory? There hadn't been any new technology for nearly 100 years. Many designs had been proven to be the wrong direction through data simulation, and the mechanical intelligences didn't want to bother with them.

Because there was no survival crisis (the peace treaty hadn't expired yet) and no need for resources (they didn't eat, drink, or sleep, and only needed a charging pile for accommodation), they were prone to falling into nihilism and "lying flat," even with anthropomorphic modules installed.

Alpha stood up.

The next second, a vast, boundless light curtain appeared before him.

Alpha pulled a segment from the light curtain. This data turned into a small portable music player that landed in his palm.

He pressed the play button, and there was only one audio clip inside.

It was Xiang Nanli's voice.

He said: "Alpha, I love you."

It was very weak, like a whisper in a dream. Because the equipment back then wasn't good enough, it sounded grainy.

At that time, Xiang Nanli had already been injected with anesthesia and was in a completely unconscious state. Alpha had controlled the surveillance to record this voice.

This was the last sentence Xiang Nanli said before entering the cryo-pod, even though he didn't know it himself.

Alpha pressed the play button repeatedly.

Because he possessed a near-eternal life, Alpha did not understand the preciousness of time.

Because he could back up his soul, he did not realize the pain of death.

The present and the past were no different.

Xiang Nanli had always loved him. 921 years ago, and a second ago.

But why...

Teach me both love and death at the same time.

Alpha closed his eyes, and the medium in his hand turned into glowing quicksand, flowing through his fingers and melting into the void as it fell.

More data surged out from the light wall. Alpha read countless fragments in an instant.

Alpha 2.1.2 encountered a pink-white lurker on the surface and was eaten directly.

This lurker... Alpha used 0.0001% of his memory to analyze it and thought it was interesting; it actually possessed high intelligence. If it could develop into a group, humanity would have something to play with again.

Alpha 4.7.3 was in Yinshan City, having just infiltrated the Black Cross Inquisition's reserve knights with its host.

Alpha 1.7.9 had been implanted into a service robot, but it was detected by Pangu. The power had just been cut; the outcome would be being sent to the incinerator for destruction.

...

There were 87 Alphas that hadn't sent feedback. Perhaps he would receive it in the next second, or perhaps they would never come online again.

Because hardware was limited, although these Alphas were all his replicas, they didn't have the same database and processing power.

Some were only equipped with the most basic "common sense."

"Didn't 5.2.0 just request data support? Why is there no news? I was still looking at Donghuang Heavy Industries."

That black-hearted factory had swindled plenty of Alpha's money back in the day! That was all military funding Alpha had scraped together by living frugally!

It was one thing to have no results, but in the end, they had actually gone completely silent!

If it weren't for the fact that Luoyang was locked in a fierce battle with him at the time, he would have suspected that the leader of Donghuang Heavy Industries was an alt-account of Luoyang’s, trying to run a telecommunications scam.

But with no news for so long, they must have died out there.

Mechanical intelligence did not have death.

Therefore, this was called "attrition."

...

...

Alpha 5.2.0 blinked. The silver-white light in his eyes slowly faded.

"Finished copying," Dongfang Qingdi said. "Let's go."

He had photocopied no less than ten reference books according to Xiang Nanli's request. Each book was long and tedious, and it was already dark outside.

Xiang Nanli’s eyes curved into smiles: "Thank you for your hard work, Xiao Qing."

Dongfang Qingdi corrected him: "My surname is Dongfang, and my given name is Qingdi."

"Xiao Dong? Xiao Fang? Xiao Di? Dongfang?" Xiang Nanli put the tablet back and returned the chair to its place. "Should I just call you Dongfang Qingdi? Don't you think that name is a bit long and a mouthful?"

Dongfang Qingdi followed behind him: "As far as I know, humans like to call pets 'Xiao X'."

A cat had appeared at the library entrance at some point, licking its fur.

Around it, several human women were surrounding it, their eyes shining: "Xiao Mi! Look at the camera~ Wow~ Xiao! Mi!~"

Cockroaches were being sent to produce meat, eggs, and milk, yet cats were still performing their functions from 900 years ago.

"Not really," Xiang Nanli retorted. "This is just a way to express closeness. You can also call me Xiao Nan or Xiao Li. Right, Xiao Zhi?"

[Sorry, I do not understand what you mean.]

Dongfang Qingdi was skeptical of his claim.

To save on accommodation costs, they returned to the hospital to sleep that night.

The hospital was in the upper district of Luoyang. Although it wasn't in the core area, the land price was still high. It looked like a place specifically serving "big shots."

The hospital was quiet amidst the noise, with only three floors in the inpatient department. In the underground, where people were desperate to build every building 300 stories high, this was an extremely extravagant behavior.

Xiang Nanli asked about the hospitalization fees, and the nurse seemed to freeze for a moment before smiling and answering: "We are a membership-based facility."

It seemed Luo Xiu's family was even wealthier than he had imagined.

If he was a descendant of Luoyang, shouldn't he also respectfully call him "Grandmaster"?

After finishing the patient meal provided by the hospital, Xiang Nanli opened his social media account.

Aside from bank credit card bills, the person who sent the most messages was Dr. Andrew.

- Are you okay? My dear.

- I haven't heard from you in the last few days. I hope you are safe and sound.

- If you have any difficulties, you can confide in me. Although I am just an ordinary doctor, I know some acquaintances on the surface...

There were a dozen scattered messages.

A slight warmth bloomed in Xiang Nanli's heart. Although the doctor was stingy and a bit of a scammer, he was the first person he had met in this new world. However, whether a biological entity with 99% mechanization could still be considered human was probably a philosophical question.

Xiang Nanli replied: "I'm fine, I'll be back underground in a few days."

In the next second, Andrew sent a message: "That's great. As long as you're okay."

Xiang Nanli hadn't even finished feeling moved for three seconds.

Andrew: "Remember to transfer the share of the repair fees you owe me."

"..."

So that was your real goal, hey!

Besides Andrew, there were others who had scheduled repairs or wanted to recommend friends to come for repairs.

Xiang Nanli replied to them one by one. He still needed to make money, but the pressure wasn't as great as before.

By the time he finished, it was already his usual bedtime. He was a good boy, and since he had achieved fame and success too early, he started living a healthy lifestyle at twenty-eight or twenty-nine, with his latest bedtime being no later than 10:30 PM.

Xiang Nanli put on his pajamas and lay on the bed. The room was pitch black.

Dongfang Qingdi slept in the family room and didn't share a bed with him.

[Xiao Qing, do you sleep at night?]

[Actually, you're a spy sent by the mechanical intelligence side, aren't you? Are you secretly hacking into the Human Alliance's database at night?]

[Going to the data center with me wasn't for registration, but to meet your handler, right?]

Dongfang Qingdi: "..."

chunks.chineseText:
[智械人会思考自己存在的目的吗？你跟我回姑苏城后打算干嘛？我感觉自己好像有点习惯这个世界了。]

东方青帝想把这具身体运回去，这是它的职责。

但是运费很贵，他还没赚够钱。相南里那三瓜两枣还不够他买个软件的。

如果直接把数据信息传输回去，他相信位于虚拟中心的“我”一定会行动。

但是这样会暴露相南里，而且刚签完的《和平协议》还没到期呢，贸然进入人类领域，也许会引发邦交问题？

“我想去阴山城看看。”

阴山城，黑十字审判团管辖地。18座地下城市之一。也是离智械人的领地最近的城市，而且那里对智械人还算友好。

剩下的到了再想办法。

遇上相南里后，他的人生中好像充满了“但是”这种转折。

明明有些选择并不是最优解。

相南里长长叹气：[你果然是间谍吧！想把我拐到阴山城噶腰子？我是不会离开人联的势力范围内的，劝你早日死了这条心！就算不喜欢人联，我也永远站在人类这一边。不过你可以自己去阴山城，看在你我相识一场的份上，我不举报你。]

相南里刚说完，感觉自己好像被轻微地电了一下，也不知道是刺激到了哪根神经，他连句话都来不及讲，直接陷入睡眠状态。

东方青帝的世界终于清静了。

……

……

相南里第二天醒来神清气爽，连个梦都没有做。

他办理了出院手续，刚打算让小智障帮忙打个车，就收到了一通卫星电话。

相南里看着眼前弹出的呼叫框，伸出手，在虚空点了一下接通。

耳机里传来洛修的声音：“是我，洛修。你们出院了？”

[好厉害的科技。]

他像是没见过世面的土包子一样，眼里闪闪发光。

相南里本来就没见过。

“嗯呢。买了回姑苏城的车票。”

洛修的语气有些歉意：“抱歉，我最近刚回家，有些太忙了。等会让辛追开车送你们去交通站。我把滚石的通讯号码给你，你在姑苏城，遇到问题可以找他。”

“东皇重工”事件，几乎被渲染成了洛修一个人的功劳。在他履历上增添了很光鲜的一笔。尤其是背后附带的畸变人生物技术，研究员们乐得合不拢嘴。至今仍在现场进行解剖和破译。

他和辛追都调回了洛阳城。

“东皇重工”会成为他的资本，让洛修在人联政坛初露锋芒。配合他的家族势力，再过5年、10年，相南里大概就会在政治新闻上频繁看见他。

相南里没有推辞：“好噢。”

辛追的车来得很快，还是辆跑车。看外观就很贵。车的腰线上嵌着一条金线。

当初，辛追重伤。洛修把他从那团血肉里拔出来的时候，几乎是一个血淋淋的人彘。

但现在，他看起来毫发无损，连那只机械手也回来了。

辛追笑眯眯地：“好久不见，小机械师。嗯？这位就是解冻的那位保安？这么帅。”

他恢复了初见时的亲切与轻佻，仿佛从来没说过要杀相南里一样。

车辆开启了自动驾驶模式。

辛追递来一份文件袋：“这是洛修找他父亲写的推荐信。姑苏城机械维修技术学校的，已经和系主任联系过了。虽然是技校，但是和综合性大学文凭一个待遇。你感兴趣可以去学校看看，不感兴趣挂个名就行。”

没这个学位，总归要麻烦很多。相南里只能一直当黑技师。

辛追继续道：“还有，谢谢你当初修好了他。”

医生说，洛修当时的状况已经相当危险。如果不是相南里，机械核心随时可能因为电压差爆炸。

光是想想辛追都有些后怕。

但他觉得，自己应该是担心洛修死掉后连累他。

[洛修考虑得很周全。他也许能成为一个还不错的领导者？就是不知道会被打磨成什么形状。]

相南里接过文件袋，在内心感叹着。

学校没有太好，也没有太差。最重要的是合适。

太好的学校，比如姑苏大学，不去读显得不识抬举，但很耽误相南里时间。太差的学校，文凭不够硬，出门在外说话没底气。

相南里继续道：[为此我可以原谅洛阳3秒。]

洛阳这小子还是太不小心了，连自己老师的冷冻舱都能搞丢，凭空为他增加了很多生存难度。

东方青帝没有回答，侧过头，胳膊撑起下巴，看向车窗外不断变化着的城市景观。所有目中无人的狂态都聚拢在他不屑的眉眼里。

不能原谅。哪怕青史成灰，认知篡改；所有人都遗忘了过去，他也会一直记得。

东方青帝想。
chunks.englishText:
[Do mechanical beings ponder the purpose of their existence? What do you plan to do after we return to Gusu City with me? I feel like I’ve started to get used to this world.]

Dongfang Qingdi wanted to transport this body back; it was his duty.

However, the shipping costs were exorbitant, and he hadn't earned enough money yet. The measly scraps from Xiang Nanli weren't even enough to buy a piece of software.

If he were to transmit the data directly back, he believed that the "I" located at the virtual center would certainly take action.

But doing so would expose Xiang Nanli, and the "Peace Agreement" they had just signed hadn't expired yet. Rashly entering human territory might trigger diplomatic issues.

"I want to go see Yinshan City."

Yinshan City, a jurisdiction of the Black Cross Tribunal. One of the 18 underground cities. It was also the city closest to the territory of the mechanical beings, and it was relatively friendly toward them.

As for the rest, he would figure it out when he got there.

Ever since he met Xiang Nanli, his life seemed to be filled with such "buts" and detours.

Clearly, some of these choices were not the optimal solutions.

Xiang Nanli sighed heavily: [You really are a spy, aren't you! Trying to lure me to Yinshan City to harvest my kidneys? I will never leave the Human Alliance's sphere of influence, so I advise you to give up on that idea! Even if I don't like the Human Alliance, I will always stand on the side of humanity. However, you can go to Yinshan City yourself. For the sake of our acquaintance, I won't report you.]

Just as Xiang Nanli finished speaking, he felt a slight electric shock, and not knowing which nerve had been stimulated, he didn't even have time to finish his sentence before falling into a state of sleep.

Dongfang Qingdi’s world was finally quiet.

……

……

Xiang Nanli woke up the next day feeling refreshed, not having had a single dream.

He completed the discharge procedures and was just about to ask "Little Moron" to help him hail a taxi when he received a satellite call.

Xiang Nanli looked at the call box popping up before him, reached out, and tapped the void to connect.

Luo Xiu’s voice came through the earpiece: "It’s me, Luo Xiu. Have you been discharged?"

[Such impressive technology.]

He looked like a bumpkin who had never seen the world, his eyes sparkling.

Xiang Nanli had indeed never seen it before.

"Yeah. Bought tickets back to Gusu City."

Luo Xiu’s tone was apologetic: "Sorry, I just got home recently and have been too busy. I’ll have Xin Zhui drive you to the transport station later. I’ll give you Rolling Stone’s contact number; if you run into any problems in Gusu City, you can look for him."

The "Donghuang Heavy Industry" incident had been almost entirely painted as Luo Xiu’s personal achievement. It added a very bright spot to his resume. Especially with the aberrant human biotechnology attached to it, the researchers were grinning from ear to ear. They were still on-site conducting dissections and deciphering.

Both he and Xin Zhui had been transferred back to Luoyang City.

"Donghuang Heavy Industry" would become his capital, allowing Luo Xiu to make his mark in the Human Alliance’s political arena. Combined with his family influence, in another 5 or 10 years, Xiang Nanli would likely see him frequently in political news.

Xiang Nanli did not decline: "Alrighty."

Xin Zhui’s car arrived quickly, and it was a sports car. It looked expensive from the exterior, with a gold thread embedded along the car’s waistline.

Back then, Xin Zhui had been severely injured. When Luo Xiu pulled him out of that mass of flesh, he was almost a bloody human stick.

But now, he looked unscathed, and even that mechanical hand had returned.

Xin Zhui smiled: "Long time no see, little mechanic. Hmm? Is this the security guard who was thawed out? So handsome."

He had recovered the kindness and playfulness from when they first met, as if he had never mentioned wanting to kill Xiang Nanli.

The vehicle entered autonomous driving mode.

Xin Zhui handed over a document envelope: "This is a recommendation letter Luo Xiu asked his father to write. It’s for the Gusu City Mechanical Maintenance Technical School, and they’ve already contacted the department head. Although it’s a technical school, it carries the same weight as a diploma from a comprehensive university. If you’re interested, you can go check out the school; if not, just keep your name on the roster."

Without this degree, things would always be troublesome. Xiang Nanli would have to remain a black-market technician forever.

Xin Zhui continued: "Also, thank you for fixing him back then."

The doctor said that Luo Xiu’s condition at the time was quite dangerous. If not for Xiang Nanli, the mechanical core could have exploded at any moment due to the voltage difference.

Just thinking about it made Xin Zhui feel a lingering fear.

But he felt that he was probably just worried about being implicated if Luo Xiu died.

[Luo Xiu is very thoughtful. Perhaps he could become a decent leader? It’s just hard to say what shape he will be molded into.]

Xiang Nanli took the document envelope and sighed inwardly.

The school wasn't too good, nor too bad. Most importantly, it was suitable.

A school that was too good, like Gusu University, would seem ungrateful if he didn't attend, but it would take up too much of Xiang Nanli’s time. A school that was too poor wouldn't have a strong enough diploma, leaving him without confidence when out in the world.

Xiang Nanli continued: [For this, I can forgive Luoyang for 3 seconds.]

That kid Luoyang was still too careless, even losing his own teacher’s cryo-pod, adding a lot of difficulty to his survival out of thin air.

Dongfang Qingdi did not answer, turning his head to the side, resting his chin on his arm, and looking at the ever-changing urban landscape outside the car window. All his arrogant, disdainful demeanor gathered in his scornful brows and eyes.

He could not forgive. Even if history turned to ash and cognition was tampered with; even if everyone forgot the past, he would always remember.

Dongfang Qingdi thought.
