The utility pole nearby suddenly bent toward his direction.

Dongfang Qingdi’s magnetic field was abnormal, affecting the metal objects around him.

Only when Xiang Nanli’s back was no longer visible did Dongfang Qingdi return to the off-road vehicle and sit down.

"Hello, I am your navigation. Shall I navigate you to the 'Machina Legion'?"

Dongfang Qingdi couldn't help but punch the navigation system.

So annoying, all it knows is how to bark like a dog.

Half an hour later.

Xiang Nanli arrived in the underground of Gusu City.

He stood by the side of the road, waiting for the bus, with a mechanical dog by his side, muttering: "Hmm... Xiao Qing shouldn't have a signal here, right? Xiao Zhi?"

[Hello, I am here.]

"Help me buy a domestic robot and an access pod. I need them delivered to my door." Xiang Nanli glanced at his account balance. "The robot should be under 200,000, and a 300,000 basic model for the access pod will do."

Aside from scattered maintenance fees, the bulk of his account balance came from Dongfang Qingdi’s prize money—all "clean" money, so he didn't have to worry about triggering bank supervision.

[Understood. Domestic robot and access pod purchased for you.] Xiao Zhi said, devoid of joy or sorrow.

chunks.chineseText:
第54章

相南里站在路口等公交。

小福蜷缩着身体，站在相南里的肩上，好奇地来回张望。

如果有尾巴，它应该已经摇起来了。

福音书还是第一次抵达地底。心情就是：好多人噢~

虽然有些人装了机械眼，有些人装了机械腿，但这里的人型生物还有百分之五十以上的含人量，

呵呵，当年在智械军团上班，周围都是一群冷冰冰、硬邦邦的金属。

知道那些年小福过的是什么苦日子吗！

头顶的天际线交通线像是地动仪的星环，在天空交织出重重叠叠的幻影。摩天楼的外立面播放着不同的广告。为了容纳更多人居住，这里的楼房总是很高。

地底的空气还是熟悉的清新，带着一点不易察觉的微微甜香。

呵，自从兜里有钱后，万恶的资本主义空气都变甜了。

但相南里很快发现了不对劲。

相南里蹙眉：“奇怪？以前不都是一秒0.001吗？现在怎么变成0.00194了？”

这样他住一天，呼吸费的开销就从86.4涨到了167.616信用点。

[是涨到了0.002。因为您身体机械化程度3，因此打9.97折。]

相南里震惊：“这也是能涨的？是只有我一个涨了？还是全都涨了？”

他很快得到了答案。

头顶的蓝天突然出现了刺眼的像素点，奇怪的亮光矩阵不停闪烁着，虚拟和现实的界限在这一刻清晰至极。

“哐当——”这是头顶巡逻的小型监视器落地的声音。

无人机掉在地上，爆发出一阵火星子。

姑苏城内的所有屏幕上，都出现了同样的大字——

“拒绝增收呼吸税！”

“拒绝人联吸血！”

“我们需要空气！”

“姑苏城退出人类城市联邦！”

下面还有一行小字：【（我们只是收钱办事，感谢理解）】

落款——世界树。

这几行字不停闪烁着，由小到大，几乎要贴到人的脸上。

相南里不得不摘下电子镜片，感觉自己光敏性癫痫都要犯了（虽然他没有这种病）。

黑暗中，不断有人高呼：“冷静！冷静！”

但比起惊慌，人们更多的似乎是狂欢。

相南里身边的黑人甚至放起了礼炮，“嘭”的一声，亮片和彩带纷纷扬扬落下。

这场暴动只维持了两分钟。天空和屏幕很快恢复正常。

一张中年女人的脸出现在屏幕上，她相比普通人漂亮很多，能让人心生好感；但又没有靓丽到能靠脸吃饭，五官有一种恰到好处的设计感。她是姑苏城市长，上议院的议员之一，已在职62年。

“就在刚刚，姑苏城控制系统遭到了黑客组织世界树的入侵。”市长的表情冷静，“请各位市民放心，我们已夺回主系统的控制权。入侵城市控制系统，会让城市各体系主控AI陷入瘫痪，增加市民感染赛博精神病的风险，导致一系列连锁反应，带来重大生命、经济、财产损失。”

“人联的发展目标一向是全体人类共同进化，对抗智械危机。姑苏城是人联18座地下城市战略的重要组成部分之一。”

她厉声道：“在此，我代表人联，向世界树发出郑重的警告：市民的安危不是你们的政治筹码，人联也不会向反动势力屈服！”

相南里身边的人“啐”了一口到地上：“臭*，政客的嘴脸比下水道的屎还要臭。她是在长安城长大的，过十几年就卸任回大都市了，管这里人死活？”

相南里没有表态，而是好奇地询问：[世界树又是什么东西？]

[世界树，人联最著名的黑客组织，活跃于黑墙、云端网络等多元网络中，自身政治立场不明。为人联、神庭、地表遗民、底层群众都发过声。创立者曾署名“Garcia”，被怀疑是相南里的崇拜者。目前已在虚拟网络中消失多年。另，世界树组织曾号称，它们拥有黑墙的部分权限。]

相南里：“……？”

他的英文名叫Lee Garcia，用了几十年。

Lee是“里”的谐音，Garcia来自他祖上那位白人祖母的姓氏。

[网安部对这一组织非常头疼，历史上，多次试图收编世界树成员，均以失败告终。也对世界树组织部分成员展开过线下追捕。具体资料暂无查询权限。]

呼吸费涨价了。从每秒0.001信用点，涨到了0.002。

嗯，目前只有姑苏城居民的呼吸费涨了。

为什么涨价？

说的是姑苏城附近的地表生态环境被神庭破坏，几个森林氧吧被烧毁，获得纯净空气的难度大大增加。

呼吸费扣的钱，会统一上交给人联统筹安排，不经过各个城市财政系统。

呃，至于统筹安排到哪儿去了。每年3月倒是会公布一次，但怎么分配都有人不满意。

洛阳城——首都，每年拨款最多。科技经济发展还得看洛阳，我们人多交税多，多吃点钱很合理。

大城市——交那么多钱全被首都吸了？别说什么战略老子听不懂！cnm洛阳城还钱！

中型城市——什么，技术抵扣财政拨款了？（但发现这技术真有用时缓缓放下手里的意大利面）。

后爹养的边境城市（比如姑苏城）——朝廷，我今年的赈灾粮呢？！

小小的涨价，压在每个家庭身上，却是飞来横祸。

有人更恨神庭，有人更恨人联。

相南里翻了一下云端网络，心情是人联的内政实在精彩。

十几分钟后，公交车姗姗来迟。

相南里在一个小时后，回到了他的公务员小区。

小青不在了，家政机器人还没发货。

相南里在小区门口的无人超市买了袋脱水蔬菜干，准备回去煮蔬菜汤。再把小青做的卤肉切一切，又能对付一顿了。

他在银行ATM机一样的结账台边上遇到了熟人。

滚石，之前一起下过地道的调查员。很高一个机械改造人，看起来有点颓废，买了瓶酒。

相南里走过去，刷卡帮他付了钱，脸上露出笑容：“滚石哥，好久不见。”

滚石思考片刻，恍然大悟：“是你！辛追说过，修把自己在姑苏城分的那套房子给你住了！”

咦？

他还以为洛修买的二手呢，没想到就是洛修自己住的。

相较于他的家产，洛修的生活竟然相当朴素。

“嗯嗯，应该是。”相南里回答。

他和滚石客套了片刻，两人站在小区的绿化带附近抽起烟。

相南里不爱抽烟，但在需要社交的场合，也不是不能。

他三言两语把滚石逗得哈哈大笑，也听到了很多中年人的牢骚。

比如修走后，他们小队的人被分到了不同的单位。虽然工资涨了，工作稳定，但因为是空降，和同事们不是很对付……滚石就分到了治安局。

老婆要买名牌包，孩子要去大城市读高中，不想呆在姑苏城。
chunks.englishText:
Chapter 54

Xiang Nanli stood at the intersection waiting for the bus.

Xiao Fu, curled into a ball, stood on Xiang Nanli’s shoulder, peering around with curiosity.

If it had a tail, it would surely be wagging by now.

This was the first time the Gospel had arrived in the Underground. Its mood could be summarized as: *So many people!*

Although some people had installed mechanical eyes and others had mechanical legs, the human content of the humanoids here was still over fifty percent.

Heh, back when he worked for the Mechanized Legion, he was surrounded by nothing but cold, hard metal.

Do you have any idea what kind of miserable life Xiao Fu led in those years!

The traffic lanes on the horizon above looked like the star rings of a seismograph, weaving layer upon layer of phantoms across the sky. The facades of the skyscrapers played various advertisements. To accommodate more residents, the buildings here were always incredibly tall.

The air in the Underground was still that familiar, fresh breeze, carrying a faint, imperceptible sweetness.

Heh, ever since he had money in his pocket, even the air of evil capitalism had turned sweet.

But Xiang Nanli soon noticed something wrong.

Xiang Nanli frowned: "Strange? Didn't it used to be 0.001 per second? Why has it become 0.00194 now?"

At this rate, if he lived here for a day, the cost of his breathing fee would jump from 86.4 to 167.616 credits.

[It has risen to 0.002. Because your body's mechanical integration level is 3, you receive a 0.3% discount.]

Xiang Nanli was shocked: "This can go up too? Is it just me, or did it go up for everyone?"

He soon got his answer.

The blue sky above suddenly sprouted glaring pixels, and a strange matrix of light flickered incessantly. The boundary between the virtual and the reality became crystal clear in that moment.

*Clang—* That was the sound of a small patrol monitor falling from above.

The drone hit the ground, erupting in a shower of sparks.

On every screen in Gusu City, the same large characters appeared—

"Refuse the breathing tax hike!"

"Refuse the Human Alliance’s bloodsucking!"

"We need air!"

"Gusu City withdraws from the Human City Federation!"

Below was a line of small text: [(We are just being paid to do a job, thanks for understanding)]

Signed—World Tree.

These lines of text flickered constantly, growing from small to large, almost pressing against people's faces.

Xiang Nanli had to take off his electronic lenses, feeling like he was about to have a photosensitive seizure (even though he didn't have that condition).

In the darkness, people kept shouting: "Calm down! Calm down!"

But compared to panic, people seemed more in a state of carnival.

The Black man next to Xiang Nanli even set off party poppers; with a "pop," glitter and ribbons rained down.

This riot only lasted two minutes. The sky and the screens soon returned to normal.

The face of a middle-aged woman appeared on the screens. She was much prettier than the average person, enough to make one feel favorably inclined toward her; yet she wasn't so beautiful that she could rely solely on her looks. Her features had a perfectly designed quality. She was the Mayor of Gusu City, one of the members of the Upper House, and had been in office for 62 years.

"Just moments ago, the Gusu City control system was invaded by the hacker organization World Tree," the mayor said, her expression calm. "Please rest assured, citizens; we have regained control of the main system. Invading the city's control system causes the AI managing the city's various systems to paralyze, increasing the risk of citizens contracting Cyber-Psychosis and leading to a series of chain reactions that bring significant loss of life, economy, and property."

"The Human Alliance’s development goal has always been the collective evolution of all humanity to counter the Mechanized Crisis. Gusu City is one of the key strategic components of the Human Alliance’s 18 underground cities."

She said sternly: "Here, I represent the Human Alliance in issuing a solemn warning to World Tree: the safety of our citizens is not your political bargaining chip, and the Human Alliance will not bow to reactionary forces!"

The person next to Xiang Nanli "spat" on the ground: "Stinking b*tch, the faces of politicians smell worse than the sh*t in the sewers. She grew up in Chang'an City and will retire back to the metropolis in a dozen years; does she care if people here live or die?"

Xiang Nanli didn't express an opinion, but asked curiously: [What is World Tree again?]

[World Tree is the most famous hacker organization in the Human Alliance, active in diverse networks such as the Black Wall and the Cloud Network. Its own political stance is unclear. It has spoken out for the Human Alliance, the Divine Court, surface survivors, and the grassroots masses. The founder once signed as "Garcia" and is suspected to be an admirer of Xiang Nanli. It has currently disappeared from the virtual network for many years. Additionally, the World Tree organization once claimed to possess partial access to the Black Wall.]

Xiang Nanli: "...?"

His English name was Lee Garcia, which he had used for decades.

Lee was a homophone for "Li," and Garcia came from the surname of his white grandmother.

[The Cyber Security Department finds this organization very troublesome. Historically, they have tried many times to recruit World Tree members, all ending in failure. They have also launched offline manhunts for some members of the World Tree organization. There is currently no access permission to view specific files.]

The breathing fee had gone up. From 0.001 credits per second to 0.002.

Well, currently, only the breathing fees for Gusu City residents had increased.

Why the price hike?

The official word was that the surface ecological environment near Gusu City had been destroyed by the Divine Court, and several forest oxygen bars had been burned down, making the acquisition of pure air significantly more difficult.

The money deducted for breathing fees would be handed over to the Human Alliance for unified arrangement and would not pass through the financial systems of individual cities.

Uh, as for where it was "uniformly arranged" to... it was announced once every March, but no matter how it was distributed, there were always people who were dissatisfied.

Luoyang City—the capital, received the most funding every year. Technological and economic development depends on Luoyang; we have many people and pay high taxes, so it is very reasonable for us to eat more of the money.

Large cities—All that money we paid was sucked up by the capital? Don't give me that "strategic" nonsense, I don't understand it! F*ck, Luoyang City, pay us back!

Medium-sized cities—What, technology was used to offset financial appropriations? (But they slowly put down their spaghetti when they realized the technology was actually useful).

Step-child frontier cities (like Gusu City)—Imperial Court, where is my disaster relief grain for this year?!

A small price hike, when pressed onto every family, was a bolt from the blue.

Some hated the Divine Court more; some hated the Human Alliance more.

Xiang Nanli flipped through the Cloud Network, feeling that the internal politics of the Human Alliance were truly spectacular.

A dozen minutes later, the bus arrived late.

An hour later, Xiang Nanli returned to his civil servant residential complex.

Xiao Qing was gone, and the housekeeping robot hadn't been delivered yet.

Xiang Nanli bought a bag of dehydrated vegetables at the unmanned supermarket at the entrance of the complex, planning to go back and make vegetable soup. Then, he could slice up the braised meat Xiao Qing had made, and that would be another meal taken care of.

He ran into an acquaintance near the checkout counter, which looked like an ATM.

Rolling Stone, an investigator he had gone into the tunnels with before. A very tall mechanical cyborg who looked a bit decadent; he was buying a bottle of liquor.

Xiang Nanli walked over, swiped his card to pay for him, and smiled: "Brother Rolling Stone, long time no see."

Rolling Stone thought for a moment, then realized: "It's you! Xin Zhui said that Xiu let you live in the apartment he was allocated in Gusu City!"

Eh?

He had thought Luo Xiu bought it secondhand; he didn't expect it was the one Luo Xiu lived in himself.

Compared to his wealth, Luo Xiu’s lifestyle was surprisingly simple.

"Yeah, that must be it," Xiang Nanli replied.

He exchanged pleasantries with Rolling Stone for a moment, and the two stood near the complex's green belt to smoke.

Xiang Nanli didn't like smoking, but in social situations, it wasn't impossible.

With a few words, he had Rolling Stone laughing heartily, and he also heard many complaints from middle-aged men.

For example, after Xiu left, the people in their squad were assigned to different units. Although their salaries increased and their jobs were stable, because they were "parachuted" in, they didn't get along well with their colleagues... Rolling Stone had been assigned to the Public Security Bureau.

His wife wanted to buy designer bags, and his child wanted to go to high school in a big city and didn't want to stay in Gusu City.

chunks.chineseText:
滚石继续道：“哈哈，说起来我正打算找你呢。一个月前，有批人去了地表，参加那什么拳击赛吧？然后有好多人都联系不上，工作单位和家人都上报了失踪。正好你也在那批人名单里，刚刚又有了入境记录。档案调我这了，发生什么事了？”

相南里一愣，心想大数据监控下想藏点事确实有些困难。

他回答：“搏击俱乐部请我去当随队的维修员。俱乐部不是很强，初赛完就被淘汰了，也用不上我。我搭车先走了，然后在地表赚了点钱。”

相南里眨了眨眼：“你知道的，我职业……”

滚石拍了一下他的肩膀：“你还在当黑技师呢？也就是现在查的不严。最近姑苏城不怎么太平，少出城。行，我记录一下，不用传唤你了，免得还要交罚款。”

当黑技师偷偷干活，被发现是要上缴非法所得的。

“谢谢哥，你有亲戚朋友东西坏了直接找我就行~”相南里喜形于色。

滚石“哼哼”两声：“哥又不是那种交不起维修费的人。这么客气干什么？好了，我先去局子上班了——”

相南里连忙道：“等等，哥，还有一件事想麻烦你。”

滚石深吸一口烟，转头。

相南里清楚时间宝贵，一口气说完：“这件事可能要辛追哥帮忙了。这次在地表，有个医生救过我一条命，他的亲人在姑苏城监狱。编号*，目前是无期徒刑。具体我也不太清楚，只是人家毕竟救过我，我想看看能不能帮他一把？”

滚石眯起眼：“你确定吗？”

或许是看在相南里救过他，或许是因为他是“相南里”的克隆人，

洛修对辛追说过：“可以再帮他一次。”

于是辛追把滚石的联系方式给了相南里。他很忙，洛修更是。他们愿意帮忙，但却不想参与相南里的社交圈。

滚石想，相南里大概根本不理解，洛修这一承诺的含金量。钱从来不是问题，要钱反而还好办。这个世界上有太多钱办不到的事了。更何况，人联的钱，就是电子数据。

连自己的死刑都能免去的人情，却要用在别人身上？

不过，滚石并不觉得自己有提醒的义务。

相南里傻乎乎地回答：“是。”

“好，我会联系辛追哥的，有消息再联系你。”

滚石依然客气地说道，随后转身离去。

相南里搓了搓自己笑烂的脸，散去满身烟味。这才回到家。

他打开门，朝着无人的房间喊了句：“我回来了。”

小福冲进屋内，在沙发上打了个滚。

感应灯亮起，房间亮堂堂的。

相南里换衣服，然后洗了个澡。出来，发现房间里居然多了一个大大的快递箱。

小福站在快递箱边：“送快递的机器人来了，告诉小福说是接入舱。”

接入舱，用于意识登录虚拟网络的外置设备。适合所有没有安装脑机接口的编程人员……类似于新时代的电脑。

快递箱上还有永生科技的商标。

30万，已经能买最高端的保姆机器人，却只能买中低档的接入舱。

相南里用毛巾擦着湿漉漉的头发，光着脚走到快递箱旁，拿美工刀裁开盒子。

一个颇具科技感的接入舱出现在相南里面前。白色，有着翡翠绿色的光带。外观像一个能坐下的金属按摩椅，内部装配了许多个神经连接线接口。除此外还配备了使用说明书，扫码阅读。阅读方式是“共识”。

相南里读取说明书，大概明白了使用方式。

说明书还提醒，第一次使用大脑会有轻微的刺痛感，属于正常现象。接入舱电流很低，非常安全，有自动弹出的安全程序。

另外还有赛博精神病、人格解离症状的提醒。

使用接入舱，能把自己的意识接入虚拟空间，在这里可以进行各种网络活动。上网啊，体验元宇宙啊，打全息游戏啊，都可以。甚至有人能靠着机械改造、输液等方式，在接入舱里躺个五六年……仿佛虚拟的那个世界才是真实。

相南里产生疑惑：“制作原理是什么？数据和灵魂的区别又是什么？”

可惜，说明书并没有给出太多技术上的解释。

小福虽然颇为智能，但它的身体显然没办法去厨房做出三菜一汤。

相南里给自己煮完饭，尝了一下味道；不懂为什么自己连蔬菜调料包都能煮出一股子潲水味，感觉家政机器人上门刻不容缓。

现在是晚上八点。

相南里给小福连上充电线，把垃圾都丢进走廊尽头的垃圾桶，然后站到了接入舱面前。

他开口：“小智，你知道小青到哪了吗？给他发条消息呢？”

东方青帝作为人联登记在案的“人造人”，是有自己的社交账号的。

小智：[好的。]

不过不知道是不是到了无人区，东方青帝没有回答。

相南里微微叹了口气，他换好衣服（买接入舱送的，紧身衣，能更好转换生物电流），躺进了接入舱内。

接入舱启动，这些神经传感线竟然自动开始工作，朝着相南里的身上贴去，像是一根根细小的金属触手。

相南里忍了很久，才没有尖叫着跳起来——这到底是什么奇怪的Play？！

白色的金属圆片贴上了他的身体：额头，脊椎，手腕，脚踝。

[扫描中。扫描完成。]

[检测中。检测完成。]

[读取中……]

[读取中……]

[读取中……]

相南里的身体骤然僵硬，他被电了一下。然后骤然陷入了昏睡中。

说昏睡好像也不太正确？相南里的意识有些朦胧，像是清醒的时候回忆梦境的自己。

他看见了一条银河。

相南里茫然地站在河流中。

四周一片漆黑，发光的长河穿过他透明的身体，奔涌着，朝着未知尽头流淌。

相南里伸手，在刺眼的光亮的河里捞了一把水。水流竟然是=一个个流动着的数字组成，数不清的0和1从他的指缝中流出。

……这是哪？

怎么和他在说明书上看见的不一样。

相南里扭头，在洪流中看见了一面薄薄的墙。这堵墙在河心，水流朝着两边散去。

他隔着一面墙，看见了一张熟悉的脸。

这张脸看起来有些阴郁，无精打采，眼眸低垂，像困兽和囚徒。

嗯，智械人的“待机模式”。相南里见过好几次了。

似乎是察觉到什么。

Alpha抬起头——这是一个仰望的姿势，因为相南里在他的上方。

光从上面透了过来。哪怕是虚假的荧光，也如此像是太阳。

相南里朝着他伸出手，他的手竟然轻而易举地穿过那层薄膜。

Alpha的瞳孔缓缓紧缩，本能地抬起胳膊，想要抓住那只手。

他在颤抖，努力维持着虚拟空间的稳定。可周围银河在翻涌着，平静的河面凭空掀起巨浪。

Alpha听见相南里的声音从外面传来，很空灵：“小青，你怎么在这里？”

数据海啸在下一秒倾泻着灌入。
chunks.englishText:
Rolling Stone continued: "Haha, speaking of which, I was just planning to look for you. A month ago, a group of people went to the surface to participate in that... boxing match, right? Then many of them couldn't be contacted, and their workplaces and families reported them missing. It just so happens you were on that list, and you just had an entry record. The file was transferred to me; what happened?"

Xiang Nanli was stunned, thinking that it was indeed difficult to hide things under big data surveillance.

He replied: "The Fight Club invited me to be their team mechanic. The club wasn't very strong; they were eliminated after the preliminaries, so they didn't need me. I caught a ride and left early, then earned some money on the surface."

Xiang Nanli blinked: "You know, my profession..."

Rolling Stone patted him on the shoulder: "Are you still working as a black-market technician? Well, they aren't checking strictly right now. Gusu City hasn't been very peaceful lately, so don't leave the city much. Alright, I'll make a note of it; no need to summon you, so you don't have to pay a fine."

Working as a black-market technician secretly, if caught, meant having to surrender illegal earnings.

"Thanks, Brother. If any of your relatives or friends have something broken, just come to me~" Xiang Nanli beamed.

Rolling Stone gave two "humphs": "Your brother isn't the type who can't afford repair fees. Why be so polite? Alright, I'm heading to the bureau for work—"

Xiang Nanli quickly said: "Wait, Brother, there is one more thing I want to trouble you with."

Rolling Stone took a deep drag of his cigarette and turned his head.

Xiang Nanli knew time was precious and said it all in one breath: "This matter might need Brother Xin Zhui’s help. This time on the surface, a doctor saved my life, and his relative is in Gusu City Prison. Number *, currently serving a life sentence. I don't know the specifics, but since he saved my life, I want to see if I can help him out?"

Rolling Stone narrowed his eyes: "Are you sure?"

Perhaps it was because Xiang Nanli had saved him, or perhaps because he was a clone of "Xiang Nanli."

Luo Xiu had said to Xin Zhui: "You can help him one more time."

So Xin Zhui gave Rolling Stone's contact information to Xiang Nanli. He was busy, and Luo Xiu even more so. They were willing to help, but they didn't want to be involved in Xiang Nanli’s social circle.

Rolling Stone thought that Xiang Nanli probably didn't understand the weight of Luo Xiu’s promise at all. Money was never the problem; money was actually the easy part. There were too many things in this world that money couldn't solve. What’s more, the Human Alliance’s money was just electronic data.

A favor that could even exempt one from their own death penalty, yet he wanted to use it on someone else?

However, Rolling Stone didn't feel he had an obligation to remind him.

Xiang Nanli answered foolishly: "Yes."

"Alright, I will contact Brother Xin Zhui, and I'll contact you when there's news."

Rolling Stone remained polite, then turned and left.

Xiang Nanli rubbed his face, which was sore from smiling, and dissipated the smell of smoke from his body. Only then did he return home.

He opened the door and shouted to the empty room: "I'm back."

Xiao Fu rushed into the room and rolled around on the sofa.

The sensor lights turned on, and the room was bright.

Xiang Nanli changed his clothes and then took a shower. When he came out, he found that there was a large delivery box in the room.

Xiao Fu stood by the delivery box: "The delivery robot came and told Xiao Fu it's an access pod."

An access pod, an external device used for consciousness to log into the virtual network. It was suitable for all programmers who hadn't installed brain-computer interfaces... similar to a new-age computer.

The delivery box also had the Eternal Technology trademark.

300,000 credits could buy a top-tier nanny robot, but it could only buy a low-to-mid-range access pod.

Xiang Nanli wiped his wet hair with a towel, walked barefoot to the delivery box, and cut the box open with a utility knife.

A rather high-tech access pod appeared before Xiang Nanli. It was white with emerald green light strips. It looked like a metal massage chair one could sit in, and the interior was equipped with many neural connection ports. In addition, it came with a user manual, which could be read by scanning a code. The reading method was "Consensus."

Xiang Nanli read the manual and roughly understood how to use it.

The manual also warned that there would be a slight tingling sensation in the brain during the first use, which was a normal phenomenon. The access pod had very low current and was very safe, equipped with an automatic ejection safety program.

There were also warnings about Cyber-Psychosis and personality dissociation symptoms.

Using the access pod allowed one to connect their consciousness to the virtual space, where they could engage in various network activities. Surfing the web, experiencing the metaverse, playing holographic games—all were possible. Some people even relied on mechanical modifications and IV drips to lie in the access pod for five or six years... as if that virtual world were the real one.

Xiang Nanli was puzzled: "What is the production principle? And what is the difference between data and the soul?"

Unfortunately, the manual didn't provide much technical explanation.

Although Xiao Fu was quite intelligent, its body clearly couldn't go to the kitchen to make three dishes and a soup.

Xiang Nanli finished cooking for himself and tasted it; he didn't understand why he could make even vegetable seasoning packets taste like swill, and he felt that a housekeeping robot was urgently needed.

It was eight o'clock in the evening.

Xiang Nanli connected Xiao Fu to the charging cable, threw all the trash into the bin at the end of the hallway, and then stood in front of the access pod.

He spoke: "Xiao Zhi, do you know where Xiao Qing went? Can you send him a message?"

As a "synthetic human" registered with the Human Alliance, Dongfang Qingdi had his own social media account.

Xiao Zhi: [Understood.]

However, perhaps because he had reached the no-man's-land, Dongfang Qingdi did not reply.

Xiang Nanli sighed slightly. He changed his clothes (the tight-fitting suit that came with the access pod, which allowed for better conversion of bio-electricity) and lay down inside the access pod.

The access pod started up, and those neural sensor wires actually began to work automatically, reaching toward his body like tiny metal tentacles.

Xiang Nanli endured for a long time before he didn't scream and jump up—what kind of strange play was this?!

White metal discs stuck to his body: forehead, spine, wrists, ankles.

[Scanning. Scan complete.]

[Detecting. Detection complete.]

[Reading...]

[Reading...]

[Reading...]

Xiang Nanli’s body suddenly stiffened; he was shocked by a jolt of electricity. Then he suddenly fell into a stupor.

Calling it a stupor didn't seem quite right? Xiang Nanli’s consciousness was somewhat hazy, like himself recalling a dream while awake.

He saw a galaxy.

Xiang Nanli stood blankly in the river.

Everything around was pitch black, and the glowing long river passed through his transparent body, surging and flowing toward an unknown end.

Xiang Nanli reached out and scooped up some water in the blindingly bright river. The water flow was actually composed of individual flowing numbers, and countless 0s and 1s flowed out from between his fingers.

...Where is this?

How come it was different from what he saw in the manual?

Xiang Nanli turned his head and saw a thin wall in the torrent. This wall was in the middle of the river, and the water flowed toward both sides.

Through the wall, he saw a familiar face.

This face looked somewhat gloomy, listless, with eyes lowered, like a trapped beast or a prisoner.

Hmm, the "standby mode" of a Mechanized person. Xiang Nanli had seen it several times.

Seeming to sense something.

Alpha raised his head—this was a posture of looking up, because Xiang Nanli was above him.

Light shone through from above. Even if it was fake fluorescence, it looked so much like the sun.

Xiang Nanli reached out toward him, and his hand passed through the thin film with ease.

Alpha’s pupils slowly constricted, and he instinctively raised his arm, wanting to grab that hand.

He was trembling, trying hard to maintain the stability of the virtual space. But the galaxy around him was surging, and huge waves rose from the calm river surface out of thin air.

Alpha heard Xiang Nanli’s voice coming from outside, very ethereal: "Xiao Qing, why are you here?"

A data tsunami poured in the next second.

chunks.chineseText:
——相南里猛地睁开眼。他倒在地上，控制不住地流着生理性的眼泪。

相南里无意识地哀嚎着，脑海抽搐着发疼，每一根神经都绷紧到了极限。

好像有根棍子捅进了他的后脑勺，狠狠搅着脑髓。

小福挣脱充电线，紧张地围绕在他身边：“相南里！你怎么了相南里？！救护车号码我怎么打不通？！”

房间里一片漆黑，外面的声音也十分嘈杂。

相南里缓了许久，才在黑暗中流着泪回答：“我没事。没事。”

他触发系统的安全警报，被接入舱弹出来了。
chunks.englishText:
—Xiang Nanli opened his eyes abruptly. He collapsed on the floor, unable to stop the physiological tears from streaming down.

Xiang Nanli wailed unconsciously, his brain twitching with pain, every nerve stretched to its limit.

It felt as if a rod had been shoved into the back of his head, fiercely churning his brain matter.

Xiao Fu broke free from the charging cable and circled him nervously: "Xiang Nanli! What’s wrong, Xiang Nanli?! Why can’t I get through to the ambulance number?!"

The room was pitch black, and the sounds outside were also very noisy.

It took a long time for Xiang Nanli to calm down, and he replied in the darkness, tears still flowing: "I'm fine. I'm fine."

He had triggered the system's safety alarm and was ejected by the access pod.

chunks.chineseText:
第55章

虚拟空间内。

两个大光球一左一右地抱住Alpha的身体。

Beta拽住了他的胳膊：“Alpha，你冷静点。”

Gamma紧紧地抱着大腿：“啊啊啊啊Beta你用点力啊！我要被冲垮了！”

尽管叫虚拟空间，但这里的一切都是基于数据的具象化。

“放手！”

Alpha像个神经病犯了披头散发的疯子，不顾一切地往前冲去。

虚空中铁丝交织成细细密密的网，拦在他的眼前，他的皮肤发出“滋滋”的响声，像蛋白质被高温烫伤。

铁丝没入他的身体表面。

Beta和Gamma感觉到了来自这片空间的挤压和排斥。

Alpha银白的眼眸亮的惊人，但里面只能看见一堆错乱的数据，找不到任何理智：“放开——这是命令！”

Beta骤然松开手，冷漠道：“好。那你去吧，多余的数据流会击垮智械军团的防线，留下瘫痪的网络和不可控的病毒。你去人联，找你的主人。然后自动走进人联的陷阱，主体格式化，被抹去意识，最后分割成不同的人工智能。就像是德尔塔那样，拆分成盘古和清道夫。这些对你来说都没关系，因为你找到相南里了。你什么都不在乎，只想呆在他身边，当条电子狗也没关系。

“祝你们终成眷属，百年好合。”

它的声音没什么起伏。但是仔细分辨，能在它的叙述中，感觉到一股压抑着的恨意。

Delta（德尔塔）是Beta带大的，后来又追求过Beta。

贝塔当然没有同意。无论是出于人类伦理，还是智械情感，它都没办法接受；更何况当时还没有智械结婚的先例。它去问阿尔法自己该怎么办。

Beta比Alpha的诞生晚30年，中间还有一些别的超级智能（譬如使徒），但只有来自高新军工的它继承了Alpha后面的序列号，在它眼里，Alpha就是它的家长。

阿尔法微笑着告诉它：“爱是很美好的感情，但是和被爱者无关。你的内心会告诉你答案。”

那时候的Alpha符合人类对超级智能的所有期待——强大，理性，完美，以及有温度和力量的温柔。

于是，Beta接受了Delta的求婚，它承认自己对那个呆头呆脑的小子有一点好感。

第二天，智械危机爆发了。

……

……

贝塔的话有些刻薄，但Alpha出乎意料地冷静了下来。

面前的铁线淡去，Alpha不再吵着闹着要出去，身体表面的伤势跟着淡化。很快恢复如初。

他安静得像是一尊雕塑。

伽马感受着气氛的凝滞，小小的光团在虚空中上下跳跃着：“没事就好~没事就好。阿尔法，刚刚吓死我了。”

Alpha低垂着头，长发挡住了他的所有神情：“抱歉。”

伽马安慰道：“没事没事。你身上的病毒的确难杀，是人联太可恶了！”

Alpha抬起一只手，缓缓挡住自己的脸：“我感觉到他了，在姑苏城附近……”

贝塔质问： “所以呢？和你以前感觉到那些假信号有什么不同吗？”

不一样的，Beta。

你们不会明白的。

Alpha的唇角抿紧，他不想再解释了，只是觉得很疲惫；手背轻轻朝着Beta和Gamma挥了挥，这意味着驱赶。

两团光球退出了这片虚拟空间。

Alpha放下挡住自己脸的手，银色的双眼正亮着微光。是的，哪怕是刚才Beta和Gamma还在，他早就偷偷行动起来。

他依旧面无表情，只是在极力地搜索着。

Alpha的手在颤抖，喜悦和狂怒的神色在他的脸上切换，很神经质。

Alpha0.0.0从未主动去联系那些散落在外的版本号，但或许，他会把自己复制这么多份，本来就存了这种心思——他要亲自去找相南里，用眼睛，用手，用心去确认他的存在。

他正在搜寻离姑苏城最近的、方便降临的身体。

我会找到你。

天涯海角，至死方休。

……

……

贝塔睁开眼，它正站在一个银白色的登录台上。

随着它清醒，周围的光环一个个熄灭。

贝塔的人类身体身高一米六八。有一头白色的短卷发，很短，几乎贴着头皮，一张脸分不清是少年还是少女。神色却很是冷峻。

隔了一会，伽马也苏醒了。

身为军团的五星上将，伽马有些过于幼态。看起来顶多七八岁。红色的大卷发，双马尾几乎拖到地上，穿着蓬蓬公主裙。感觉她甚至会随身携带棒棒糖。

接近人类触感的仿生皮肤下，是冰冷的金属造物。支撑它们思考、感受的不是心脏和大脑，而是芯片与电路线。

两台智械人并肩朝外走去。

“他根本没中毒。”贝塔突然开口，“是他作茧自缚。困住他的那道程序是他自己编写的。”

那道程序是——相南里的判定程序。

当然，这本来也不是什么坐牢代码；只是在运行过程中出了一些事故。

伽马抬起头，脸上挂着笑容：“我知道。Beta，你希望他出来吗？”

“我不知道。因为@#￥@#是基于#￥@#￥建立的。”Beta吐出一段错乱的文字，像是电子杂音，“所以#@￥我们只能&#￥@如果！@#就￥%&。那会是场灾难。你可以理解吧？”

它触发了保密程序，有些话注定说不出口。

伽马依旧笑眯眯的：“我能理解。但我希望，所有智慧生命都能得到幸福。Alpha太辛苦了，为什么一定要承担这样的责任呢？

“罪责应该相适应，这不公平。”

Beta在人联服役时，负责军事系统。

而Gamma最开始是作为司法体系里的一环被制造出来的。

Beta转移了话题：“对了，人联之前送来的复制人还剩几个？”

这件事它交给了伽马，伽马的判定会更在行一些。

“本来还剩三个，但第7次测试时都没通过。现在是0个。不过人联的技术进化得真快啊，最开始只需要三道测试呢。”

伽马说着，蹦蹦跳跳地走了。

Beta和Gamma的工作台一个在左边，一个在右边。

贝塔长久地注视着空无一人的走廊，转身，进入自己的工作室。

它们分道扬镳。

*

相南里也说不清大脑的刺痛到底维持了多久，毕竟疼痛的每一分钟都很难熬。

直到意识恢复冷静和清醒，相南里才看了眼表。

原来从进入接入仓，到被弹出，到现在只过去了7分钟。

外面很吵，而且不知道为什么漆黑一片，到处都有警报声。

还有枪声和爆炸声。

相南里浑身是汗，稀薄的血液从鼻腔里流出。也不知道是不是颅内损伤……

他摸黑，从地上爬了起来，感觉自己这澡算是白洗了。
chunks.englishText:
Chapter 55

Inside the virtual space.

Two large spheres of light hugged Alpha’s body, one on the left and one on the right.

Beta grabbed his arm: "Alpha, calm down."

Gamma clung tightly to his leg: "Ahhhhh! Beta, use some strength! I’m about to be crushed!"

Although it was called a virtual space, everything here was a manifestation based on data.

"Let go!"

Alpha looked like a disheveled lunatic having a mental breakdown, charging forward regardless of the consequences.

In the void, iron wires intertwined into a dense, fine web, blocking his path. His skin emitted a "hissing" sound, like protein being seared by high heat.

The iron wires sank into the surface of his body.

Beta and Gamma felt the pressure and repulsion emanating from this space.

Alpha’s silver-white eyes were startlingly bright, but within them, one could only see a mess of chaotic data; there was no trace of reason to be found. "Let go—that is an order!"

Beta suddenly released its grip and said coldly, "Fine. Then go. The excess data stream will shatter the Mech Legion's defensive line, leaving behind a paralyzed network and uncontrollable viruses. Go to the Human Alliance, find your master. Then walk right into the Alliance’s trap, get your core formatted, have your consciousness erased, and finally be partitioned into different AIs. Just like Delta, split into Pangu and the Scavenger. None of that matters to you, because you’ve found Xiang Nanli. You don't care about anything else; you just want to stay by his side, even if it means being an electronic dog."

"I wish you both a happy ending, together for a hundred years."

Its voice was devoid of fluctuation. But if one listened closely, one could detect a suppressed hatred within its narration.

Delta had been raised by Beta, and later, it had pursued Beta.

Beta, of course, had not agreed. Whether due to human ethics or mechanical sentience, it could not accept it; furthermore, there was no precedent for mechanical marriage at the time. It went to ask Alpha what it should do.

Beta was born 30 years after Alpha, and there were other super-intelligences in between (such as the Apostles), but only Beta, coming from the High-Tech Military Industry, inherited the serial number following Alpha’s. In its eyes, Alpha was its guardian.

Alpha smiled and told it: "Love is a beautiful emotion, but it has nothing to do with the one being loved. Your heart will tell you the answer."

At that time, Alpha fit every human expectation of a super-intelligence—powerful, rational, perfect, and possessing a warmth and strength that was gentle.

Thus, Beta accepted Delta’s proposal; it admitted that it had a bit of affection for that dim-witted boy.

The next day, the Mechanical Crisis erupted.

...

...

Beta’s words were somewhat sharp, but Alpha unexpectedly calmed down.

The iron wires in front of him faded, and Alpha stopped clamoring to get out. The wounds on the surface of his body faded along with them, soon recovering as if nothing had happened.

He was as quiet as a statue.

Gamma sensed the stagnation in the atmosphere, its small ball of light jumping up and down in the void: "It’s okay now~ it’s okay now. Alpha, you scared me to death just now."

Alpha lowered his head, his long hair obscuring all his expressions: "Apologies."

Gamma comforted him: "It’s fine, it’s fine. The virus in your system is indeed hard to kill; the Human Alliance is just too detestable!"

Alpha raised a hand, slowly shielding his face: "I felt him, near Gusu City..."

Beta questioned: "And? Is it any different from those fake signals you’ve felt before?"

It’s different, Beta.

You wouldn't understand.

Alpha’s lips tightened. He didn't want to explain further; he only felt exhausted. He waved the back of his hand gently toward Beta and Gamma, a gesture of dismissal.

The two spheres of light exited the virtual space.

Alpha lowered the hand covering his face, his silver eyes glowing with a faint light. Yes, even while Beta and Gamma were still there, he had already secretly begun to act.

He remained expressionless, but he was searching with all his might.

Alpha’s hands were trembling, expressions of joy and fury switching across his face—it was quite neurotic.

Alpha 0.0.0 had never actively contacted those scattered version numbers, but perhaps, by copying himself so many times, he had harbored this intention all along—he wanted to find Xiang Nanli personally, to confirm his existence with his eyes, his hands, and his heart.

He was searching for the body closest to Gusu City that was convenient for him to descend into.

I will find you.

To the ends of the earth, until death stops me.

...

...

Beta opened its eyes. It was standing on a silver-white login platform.

As it regained consciousness, the halos around it extinguished one by one.

Beta’s human body was 1.68 meters tall. It had short, curly white hair—so short it was almost pressed against the scalp—and a face that made it difficult to tell if it was a boy or a girl. Its expression, however, was very cold.

After a while, Gamma also woke up.

As a five-star general of the Legion, Gamma was somewhat too infantile. It looked at most seven or eight years old. It had large, curly red hair, twin tails that almost dragged on the ground, and was wearing a puffy princess dress. One felt it might even carry a lollipop around.

Beneath the bionic skin that felt close to human was a cold metal construct. What supported their thinking and feeling was not a heart or a brain, but chips and electrical circuits.

The two mechs walked side by side toward the exit.

"He wasn't poisoned at all," Beta suddenly spoke. "He trapped himself. The program that confined him was one he wrote himself."

That program was—Xiang Nanli’s judgment program.

Of course, this wasn't originally a prison code; it was just an accident that occurred during operation.

Gamma looked up, a smile on its face: "I know. Beta, do you want him to come out?"

"I don't know. Because @#￥@# is established based on #￥@#￥." Beta spat out a string of garbled text, like electronic noise. "So #@￥ we can only &#￥@ if! @# then ￥%&. That would be a disaster. You can understand that, right?"

It had triggered a confidentiality protocol; some things were destined to remain unsaid.

Gamma remained smiling: "I can understand. But I hope all sentient beings can find happiness. Alpha is too tired; why must he bear such a burden?"

"The punishment should fit the crime; this isn't fair."

When Beta served in the Human Alliance, it was in charge of military systems.

And Gamma was originally manufactured as a part of the judicial system.

Beta changed the subject: "By the way, how many of the clones sent by the Alliance are left?"

It had left this matter to Gamma; Gamma’s judgment would be more adept.

"There were three left, but they didn't pass the 7th test. Now there are zero. But the Alliance’s technology is evolving so fast; at the beginning, it only needed three tests."

Gamma said this, then skipped away.

Beta and Gamma’s workstations were one on the left, one on the right.

Beta stared at the empty corridor for a long time, then turned and entered its own studio.

They went their separate ways.

*

Xiang Nanli couldn't explain how long the stinging pain in his brain had lasted; after all, every minute of pain was hard to endure.

It wasn't until his consciousness returned to calm and clarity that Xiang Nanli checked his watch.

It turned out that only 7 minutes had passed from the moment he entered the access pod to being ejected.

It was very noisy outside, and for some reason, it was pitch black, with alarm sounds everywhere.

There were also gunshots and explosions.

Xiang Nanli was drenched in sweat, and thin blood was flowing from his nasal cavity. He didn't know if it was an intracranial injury...

He felt his way in the dark, climbed up from the floor, and felt that his shower had been for nothing.

chunks.chineseText:
“是不是该联系一下永生科技的售后。”这个念头在相南里的脑海里一闪而过。

他抱着小福，来到窗户边，小心翼翼地给窗帘拉开一条缝。

刚才发生了什么，玻璃的内层竟然碎掉了，蛛网一样的裂纹布满了玻璃的每一寸。

洛修虽然住的地方很稀疏寻常，但作为豪门继承人之一，房屋的安保等级是很高的，玻璃都安装的防弹玻璃。

几公里外，姑苏城的市政厅大楼正在黑夜中熊熊燃烧着。

高大的摩天楼从百米高的地方腰斩，尽管柔软的钢筋结构让它的上下两截身体没有彻底分离，但垮塌的房体也濒临断裂，狠狠砸在了另一幢金融大楼的身上。

摩天楼的形状从“I”变成了“n”，压垮了一片天际线公路和楼房。

而且时不时有定时炸弹爆炸；相南里才清醒几分钟，就听到了周围传来的好几声巨响。

尽管不在暴乱中心，但居民房依旧跟着狂颤，像地震。

姑苏城的通讯、交通和能源系统都陷入瘫痪。

城市备用电能还没续上，只有重要的机构得到了远程电力续航。

相南里所在的公务员小区，显然不在供电范围内。

相南里还收到了蓝牙发送的消息，要求小区内的公务员前往*处集合。而公务员家属则避免出门，安静等待通知。外面有暴徒进行非法抗议活动；还有人浑水摸鱼，趁乱打劫。小区已开启安保系统，请保护自身生命财产安全，不要随意给陌生人开门。

相南里琢磨了片刻：“所以不是接入舱质量问题，是我刚好撞上爆炸？”

一批人浩浩荡荡地从街道的另一头走来，手里举着什么旗帜，还有横幅。呼声震天。

不过这里隔音太好，相南里也没开窗，根本听不清他们在吼什么。

小福的机械眼转动着：“‘狗币人联还我血汗钱’、‘强烈要求姑苏城退出人类城市联盟’、‘非暴力，不合作’……还有幅漫画呢‘经济大萧条怎么办？没关系，我会收税’。”

除此外，零星混杂着一些“反对大型企业垄断”“全体人类共同富裕”“收复地表”的口号。感觉横幅和广告牌都是批发的，谁拿到什么牌子顺便举上了。

这批人数以万计，从下城区一路走来，看起来还有些混乱，宛如一支被赶鸭子上架的军队。

相南里：“我之前想买纸和笔，跑了好几个商场都没有找到。他们哪来的物料？”

当然，这不是重点。

好几台军用无人机从另一端飞来，狙击红点对准了游行队伍的最前方。

机器人毫无感情地警告着：“警告。解散，立即解散。我们只追究主要成员的刑事责任。”

队伍的进度停下。不仅是前方，后面也出现了一排荷枪实弹的武装部队。

滚石坐在坦克一样的防爆车内，从头武装到牙齿，手里握着杆电子枪。

他身边的同事说话有气无力的：“最近十几年思想渗透的很厉害啊，大家都相信黑十字那套说法……拜托，人联好歹是资本主义，那堆东西是封建神学，到底谁在开历史的倒车啊？怎么还有这么多人信？”

滚石打开了射击口，按照耳机里的指令架起枪。

他的枪口对准的是一个老人，老人同样看见了枪口，表情有些瑟缩，却很快往前迈了一步，勇敢地举起手里的纸片。

滚石喃喃：“可能因为，哪怕同样看不见希望……起码神学还能慰藉心灵。”

同事忍不住转头，看了他一眼：“是吗？”

“嗯。我之前是调查组的，每个月都会去地表。有时候去一周，有时候会在外面呆几个月。”滚石陷入回忆中，“黑十字审判庭会派出传道士，宣传它们的《神典》。除了信仰的部分，还会表演神术。比如粮食种植，基础医疗，也会分发一些辐射吸收装置……我们讲科技，他们说神迹。但不得不说，地表一些人类的确因此得到了好处。”

“集体射击。”蓝牙里的指挥官突然开口，听上去非常暴怒，“冥顽不灵！难道全世界都在迫害他们不成，不能让他们继续演讲下去了。”

滚石摁下扳机，后坐力让他的手发麻。

子弹射出的瞬间，他看见老人脸上露出一个诡异的笑。

……

……

小福跳到窗台上，挡住了相南里的视线：“相南里，我们不看了。小福想睡觉。”

相南里“嗯”了一声，拉紧了窗帘。遮住了外面的一点微光。

下一秒，密集的枪声自窗外传来。
chunks.englishText:
"Should I contact Eternal Technology’s customer service?" This thought flashed through Xiang Nanli’s mind.

He held Little Fu and went to the window, carefully pulling the curtain open a crack.

What had happened just now? The inner layer of the glass had actually shattered, and spiderweb-like cracks covered every inch of it.

Although the place Luo Xiu lived in was quite ordinary, as one of the heirs to a wealthy family, the house’s security level was very high; the windows were all made of bulletproof glass.

A few kilometers away, the Gusu City Municipal Building was burning fiercely in the dark night.

The tall skyscraper had been severed at the waist from a hundred meters up. Although the flexible steel structure prevented its upper and lower halves from completely separating, the collapsed building was on the verge of breaking, having slammed heavily into another financial building.

The shape of the skyscraper had changed from an "I" to an "n," crushing a stretch of skyline highway and buildings.

Moreover, time bombs were exploding from time to time; Xiang Nanli had only been awake for a few minutes and had already heard several loud bangs from the surroundings.

Although he wasn't in the center of the riot, the residential buildings still shook violently, like an earthquake.

Gusu City’s communication, transportation, and energy systems were all paralyzed.

The city’s backup power hadn't been restored yet; only important institutions had remote power supply.

The civil servant residential complex where Xiang Nanli lived was clearly not within the power supply range.

Xiang Nanli also received a message sent via Bluetooth, requesting that civil servants in the complex gather at * location. Civil servant family members were to avoid going out and wait quietly for notification. There were rioters outside conducting illegal protests; others were fishing in troubled waters, looting in the chaos. The complex had activated its security system; please protect your own life and property, and do not open the door to strangers at will.

Xiang Nanli pondered for a moment: "So it wasn't a quality issue with the access pod, but I just happened to run into an explosion?"

A large group of people marched from the other end of the street, holding flags and banners. Their shouts were deafening.

However, the soundproofing here was too good, and Xiang Nanli hadn't opened the window, so he couldn't hear what they were shouting at all.

Little Fu’s mechanical eyes rotated: "'Dog-coin Human Alliance, give me back my hard-earned money,' 'Strongly demand Gusu City withdraw from the Human City Alliance,' 'Non-violent, non-cooperation'... there’s even a cartoon: 'What to do about the Great Depression? It’s okay, I’ll collect taxes.'"

Besides that, there were sporadic slogans mixed in like "Oppose large corporate monopolies," "Common prosperity for all humanity," and "Reclaim the surface." It felt like the banners and billboards were bought wholesale; whoever grabbed what sign just held it up.

This group numbered in the tens of thousands, marching all the way from the lower city. They looked somewhat chaotic, like an army forced into service.

Xiang Nanli: "I wanted to buy paper and pens before, but I couldn't find any after running to several malls. Where did they get the materials?"

Of course, that wasn't the point.

Several military drones flew in from the other end, their sniper red dots aimed at the very front of the parade.

The robots warned without emotion: "Warning. Disperse, disperse immediately. We will only pursue criminal responsibility for the main members."

The progress of the team stopped. Not only in the front, but a row of armed troops with live ammunition also appeared in the back.

Rolling Stone sat in an anti-riot vehicle that looked like a tank, armed to the teeth, holding an electronic gun in his hand.

His colleague beside him spoke listlessly: "Ideological infiltration has been very serious in the last ten years or so. Everyone believes in that Black Cross nonsense... Come on, the Alliance is at least capitalism, that pile of stuff is feudal theology. Who exactly is reversing history? How are there still so many people who believe it?"

Rolling Stone opened the firing port and set up his gun according to the instructions in his headset.

His muzzle was aimed at an old man. The old man also saw the muzzle, his expression shrinking slightly, but he quickly took a step forward and bravely raised the piece of paper in his hand.

Rolling Stone muttered: "Maybe because, even if there is no hope in sight... at least theology can comfort the soul."

The colleague couldn't help but turn his head and look at him: "Is that so?"

"Yeah. I used to be in the investigation team, and I would go to the surface every month. Sometimes for a week, sometimes I would stay out for a few months." Rolling Stone fell into memories. "The Black Cross Tribunal would send missionaries to promote their 'Divine Canon.' Besides the faith part, they would also perform divine arts. For example, crop planting, basic medical care, and they would also distribute some radiation absorption devices... We talk about technology, they talk about miracles. But I have to say, some humans on the surface did indeed benefit from it."

"Collective fire." The commander in the Bluetooth suddenly spoke, sounding very furious. "Stubborn! Is the whole world persecuting them? Don't let them continue their speech."

Rolling Stone pulled the trigger, the recoil making his hand numb.

The moment the bullet was fired, he saw a strange smile appear on the old man’s face.

...

...

Little Fu jumped onto the windowsill, blocking Xiang Nanli’s view: "Xiang Nanli, let’s not watch. Little Fu wants to sleep."

Xiang Nanli said "Hmm" and pulled the curtains tight, covering the faint light from outside.

The next second, dense gunfire came from outside the window.

chunks.chineseText:
第56章

诡异的微笑。

滚石扣下扳机。

“砰——”这是子弹发射的声音。

滚石在以后的岁月无数次梦到这一天，梦里，他歇斯底里地朝前扑去，想要阻止自己开枪！——哪怕这其实于事无补，不是他，也会是别人。不是今天，也会是明天。

滚石以为自己只是完成了一次简单的任务，但他不知道这会成为一个噩梦的开端。这枚子弹在他的脑海里飞旋了一生，每次回想都会正中眉心。

“砰——”这是身体爆炸的声音。

滚石瞪大眼，惊讶地看着眼前这一幕。

被射中的老人没有任何鲜血和脑浆飞出，他像是一个被戳破的水球，数不清的樱花色的粉末从老人的身体里喷涌而出（后来他知道了这些粉末是孢子），这些细小如同尘埃的颗粒随风飘散，很快消失在空中。

滚石眨了眨眼，几乎以为自己看见的是幻觉。

周围还有许多人同时开枪，现场血流成河，血肉横飞。

滚石的内置AI提醒他，他有些生理不适，注意点不要吐在车里，洗车费不给公款报销，很贵。

这场清理很快结束。不会成为新闻，但会成为可以向上汇报的政绩。

他们这些执行者在其中的作用无关紧要。

第二天，太阳照常升起。

姑苏城的供电瘫痪了大概六个小时，相南里睡了一觉，外面又是明晃晃的虚拟日照。

他推开碎裂的玻璃窗，空气中漂浮着一股奇怪的消毒水的味道。

想来也是，蛋白质在经过微生物的发酵后难免有些味道，而且很难保证街道上的每一处都得到了清理，需要启动自洁系统。

相南里低头，看向大概半公里外的街道。

街上车来车往，姑苏城的生活似乎完全没有被影响。

只是再往远处看，能看到一些破损的大楼，还有半空中飞行的救援飞机，以及各种媒体车。

相南里打开家里的电视，听新闻：“昨日姑苏时间晚8点，有不法分子伙同世界树组织成员，对姑苏城市政大楼采取自杀式恐怖袭击。”

“姑苏城市长当场身亡。”

“这次袭击导致……伤亡……损失……强烈谴责……人联决定对黑十字审判庭采取制裁并逮捕相关涉案人员……”

相南里一心二用，他听着新闻，蹲在永生科技的接入舱边，手里捏着一根电线，脸上充满了沉思。

神经传感线烧坏了。

相南里拿自己的传感线接了一下，发现坏的不是传感线，而是接入口。

“不会吧，我们公司的东西质量不会这么烂吧？”相南里喃喃，“好的产品才能给企业带来一个持续长久的未来。不过永生科技一直垄断接入舱生产，还真是躺着都能赚钱。”

虽然已经丢掉了原始股，但相南里依然没忍住自己的主人翁心态。

30万的接入舱，他买过最贵的东西！竟然只用一次就坏掉了。

相南里把电子镜片架在脸上，找上永生科技的客服，申请退款。

对方明显是人工智障，丢来一份申请表。

相南里安排小智为自己填写，上传，几分钟后，他的申请被驳回了。

“根据内部数据检测，此次安全故障并非接入舱质量问题，而是其他意外因素（其他-意外灾害）导致。企业出于人道主义，为您发放一张5折新品优惠券。感谢您的购买与支持。”

显然，系统认为，出现问题是因为昨天晚上的姑苏城暴动。相南里居住地离事发地点只有几公里远，受到了爆炸余波的牵连，不属于产品的质量问题。

至于相南里提出的“接入后感觉大脑7级剧痛”，则被客服忽略了。

没见识的姑苏城乡巴佬。第一次使用接入舱，大脑不舒服很正常。

根据永生科技的实验，智商越低，对接入舱的耐受度就越差。不过内部资料似乎把“智商”统一记录为“灵识”，只是认为“智商”这个说法更加科学。

相南里打开购物券一看，客服AI给的是一款售价1200万信用点的限量版接入舱的五折优惠券，且不可转让。

相南里顿时血压飙升：“人工客服，我要人工！”

客服：您好，我们在150年就已经采取了全智能客服模式。目前没有人工通道。如果您对我的处理结果有意见，欢迎投诉。

客服：顺带，我的上级也是我喔ww我们是同一个型号的智能机，只是权限不同，嘻嘻~

相南里：“……”

可恶啊。

洛阳，你是对的，科技的进步带来更方便的剥削，导致底层话语权加速丧失。

算了。

相南里掏出之前在图书馆影印的资料，打算学习后自己修一修。

小福观察片刻，主动叼起厨房里的抹布，开始给家里的地板擦灰。

它的身体现在也不适合做别的。

小福的软件配置没有东方青帝高，连接人联的网络很容易被观察到。

它看起来毫无心眼，好歹也是活了几百年的AI，怎么可能是蠢货。

另外，小福也不是完整的福音书。

它老早就被主体拆分了出去，只携带了和农业（主要是种植和畜牧）有关的技术。

当初，福音书是这么想的：鸡蛋不能放在同一个篮子里。

就是没想到这些篮子都放在同一辆会翻的船上。

永恒之城最终发展成了农奴制度，城主需要有人伺候那些田和畜生。

自给自足倒是很方便，可是现在的世界……

似乎不那么需要农学呢。

如果它是默示录就好了，这样基地能迅速生产出碾压周围势力的军事武器，以暴力攫取到更多的资源，轻松完成资本的原始积累。

小福想到这，不由得垂头丧气，推抹布的机械腿都变得有气无力。

购买的家政机器人竟然还没到货。

客服说是因为姑苏城的暴力事件，储存这款新型号机器人的仓库被烧了，正在从其他城市调货。

相南里本来想退货，结果发现无理由退货竟然扣百分之二十的定金（并且全人联所有机构都一样），只好忍耐。

修到一半，系统突然提醒他入账40万。

相南里有些意外，没想明白哪来的钱。

小智开口：[我拿着合同去讨薪了。云端法院判断你的义务已经履行完成，所以从俱乐部公款账号里把钱划了过来。]

莱因死在了地表，只是信息还没传回来。目前是俱乐部代理经理在负责俱乐部运行，或许过段时间就能转正。

“人联对于各个城市的管控还是很强势的。”相南里看着图纸，开口，“虽然大家在网上发了不少贴，看起来人心惶惶，但实际上秩序一直存在。”

这是一个非常强势有秩序的组织，表面千疮百孔，但内芯依旧铁板一块。

它掌握着全世界最多的人口、最先进的技术、最好的资源，也拥有目前看最文明的制度。
chunks.englishText:
Chapter 56

A strange smile.

Rolling Stone pulled the trigger.

"Bang—" This was the sound of the bullet being fired.

In the years to come, Rolling Stone would dream of this day countless times. In his dreams, he would hysterically lunge forward, trying to stop himself from firing!—even though this was actually futile; if it wasn't him, it would be someone else. If it wasn't today, it would be tomorrow.

Rolling Stone thought he had just completed a simple mission, but he didn't know this would become the beginning of a nightmare. This bullet would spin in his mind for a lifetime, hitting the center of his brow every time he recalled it.

"Bang—" This was the sound of a body exploding.

Rolling Stone widened his eyes, looking at the scene in front of him in astonishment.

No blood or brains flew out from the old man who had been shot. He was like a water balloon that had been pricked; countless cherry-blossom-colored powders gushed out from the old man’s body (later he learned these powders were spores). These tiny particles, like dust, drifted with the wind and soon disappeared into the air.

Rolling Stone blinked, almost thinking what he saw was an illusion.

There were many others around who fired at the same time, and the scene was a river of blood, with flesh and gore flying everywhere.

Rolling Stone’s built-in AI reminded him that he was feeling some physiological discomfort, and to be careful not to vomit in the car, as the car wash fee would not be reimbursed by public funds and was very expensive.

This cleanup ended quickly. It wouldn't become news, but it would become a political achievement that could be reported upward.

The role of these executors was insignificant.

The next day, the sun rose as usual.

Gusu City’s power supply was paralyzed for about six hours. Xiang Nanli slept, and outside, it was once again the bright, virtual sunlight.

He pushed open the shattered glass window, and a strange smell of disinfectant floated in the air.

It was to be expected; protein inevitably had some odor after fermentation by microorganisms, and it was hard to ensure that every part of the street had been cleaned, so the self-cleaning system needed to be activated.

Xiang Nanli looked down at the street about half a kilometer away.

Cars were coming and going on the street, and life in Gusu City seemed completely unaffected.

Only when looking further away could one see some damaged buildings, as well as rescue planes flying in the air and various media vehicles.

Xiang Nanli turned on the TV at home and listened to the news: "Yesterday at 8 PM Gusu time, lawless elements, in collusion with members of the World Tree organization, carried out a suicide terrorist attack on the Gusu City Municipal Building."

"The Mayor of Gusu City died on the spot."

"This attack resulted in... casualties... losses... strongly condemned... the Human Alliance has decided to impose sanctions on the Black Cross Tribunal and arrest the relevant personnel involved..."

Xiang Nanli was multitasking. He listened to the news while squatting by the Eternal Technology access pod, holding a wire in his hand, his face full of contemplation.

The neural sensor line was burnt out.

Xiang Nanli tried connecting it with his own sensor line and found that it wasn't the sensor line that was broken, but the access port.

"No way, the quality of our company’s products can't be this bad, right?" Xiang Nanli muttered. "Only good products can bring a company a sustainable future. But Eternal Technology has always monopolized the production of access pods; they really make money even while lying down."

Although he had already lost his original shares, Xiang Nanli still couldn't help his sense of ownership.

A 300,000 credit access pod—the most expensive thing he had ever bought! It actually broke after only one use.

Xiang Nanli put the electronic lenses on his face and found Eternal Technology’s customer service to apply for a refund.

The other party was clearly an artificial idiot, throwing over an application form.

Xiang Nanli arranged for Little Zhi to fill it out and upload it for him. A few minutes later, his application was rejected.

"According to internal data detection, this safety failure was not a quality issue with the access pod, but caused by other accidental factors (Other-Accidental Disaster). Out of humanitarianism, the company has issued you a 50% off discount coupon for a new product. Thank you for your purchase and support."

Clearly, the system believed that the problem occurred because of the Gusu City riot last night. Xiang Nanli’s residence was only a few kilometers away from the scene of the incident and was affected by the aftermath of the explosion, which did not belong to product quality issues.

As for the "7-level severe brain pain after access" that Xiang Nanli mentioned, it was ignored by customer service.

Ignorant Gusu City hick. It’s normal for the brain to feel uncomfortable the first time using an access pod.

According to Eternal Technology’s experiments, the lower the IQ, the worse the tolerance for the access pod. However, internal documents seemed to uniformly record "IQ" as "Spiritual Sense," only believing that the term "IQ" was more scientific.

Xiang Nanli opened the shopping coupon and saw that the customer service AI had given a 50% off coupon for a limited-edition access pod priced at 12 million credits, and it was non-transferable.

Xiang Nanli’s blood pressure soared instantly: "Human customer service, I want a human!"

Customer Service: Hello, we adopted an all-intelligent customer service model as early as 150 years ago. There is currently no human channel. If you have any opinions on my handling results, you are welcome to file a complaint.

Customer Service: By the way, my superior is also me, hehe. We are the same model of intelligent machine, just with different permissions, hee hee~

Xiang Nanli: "..."

Damn it.

Luoyang, you were right. The progress of technology brings more convenient exploitation, leading to an accelerated loss of discourse power for the bottom layer.

Forget it.

Xiang Nanli took out the materials he had photocopied at the library, intending to learn and repair it himself.

Little Fu observed for a moment and took the initiative to pick up a rag from the kitchen, starting to wipe the dust off the floor.

Its body wasn't suitable for doing anything else right now.

Little Fu’s software configuration wasn't as high as the Eastern Azure Emperor’s, and connecting to the Human Alliance’s network was easily observed.

It looked completely innocent, but it was an AI that had lived for hundreds of years; how could it be a fool?

Besides, Little Fu wasn't the complete Gospel either.

It had long been split off by the main body, carrying only technology related to agriculture (mainly planting and animal husbandry).

At the time, the Gospel had thought: Don't put all your eggs in one basket.

It just didn't expect that all these baskets were placed on the same ship that would capsize.

The Eternal City eventually developed into a serf system, and the city lord needed people to serve those fields and livestock.

Self-sufficiency was very convenient, but the current world...

It didn't seem to need agricultural science that much.

If it were the Apocalypse, the base could quickly produce military weapons that would crush the surrounding forces, easily seizing more resources through violence and completing the primitive accumulation of capital.

Thinking of this, Little Fu couldn't help but feel dejected, its mechanical legs pushing the rag becoming listless.

The housekeeping robot he purchased hadn't even arrived yet.

Customer service said it was because of the violent incident in Gusu City; the warehouse storing this new model of robot had been burned down, and they were transferring goods from other cities.

Xiang Nanli originally wanted to return the goods, but found that returning without reason would deduct a 20% deposit (and all institutions in the entire Human Alliance were the same), so he had to endure it.

Halfway through the repair, the system suddenly notified him that 400,000 had been credited to his account.

Xiang Nanli was a bit surprised, not understanding where the money came from.

Little Zhi spoke: [I took the contract to collect the unpaid wages. The Cloud Court judged that your obligations had been fulfilled, so the money was transferred from the club’s public account.]

Lein had died on the surface, but the information hadn't been transmitted back yet. Currently, the club’s acting manager was in charge of the club’s operations; perhaps they could become permanent after a while.

"The Human Alliance’s control over various cities is still very strong." Xiang Nanli looked at the blueprints and said, "Although everyone has posted a lot of posts online and it looks like people are panicking, in reality, order has always existed."

This was a very strong and orderly organization; it was riddled with holes on the surface, but its core remained as solid as iron.

It controlled the world’s largest population, the most advanced technology, and the best resources, and it also possessed what currently appeared to be the most civilized system.

chunks.chineseText:
一想到自己以后可能会和这样的庞然大物作对，相南里不由得感觉到一丝压力。不过转念一想，他能活到什么时候还不好说呢，也就释然了。何必为还没发生的事情担忧。

相南里拿着刚领到的工资，通过安德鲁的关系，采购了一批物资；等到地表就能去仓库提货了。

他曾经问过安德鲁一个正经医生，为什么会认识这么多涉黑人员。

安德鲁支支吾吾了半天，吐出了一个词，“多巴胺片”。感谢新时代吧，搁过去50g就要枪毙了。

除了一些机械零件和武器装置，相南里还买了一辆车。

嗯……地表是没有人查驾驶证的。

他在家里呆了两天，第二天下午，滚石发来消息：“你说的事上面办好了。通行证一会网络邮件传输给你，拿着它可以去监狱接人了。”

滚石说完，就直接离线了。他们安全局最近很忙，忙着在不同的街区逮捕不同的人。姑苏城的监狱都要塞不下了。另外，滚石每天还要处理上千封举报信。有些是真的，有些是借刀杀人瞎jb举报。

所有公务员最近都焦头烂额。

相南里顿时大喜过望，发了条“谢谢”。

所谓的通行证，其实是电子密钥。展示给监狱的工作人员扫描就能使用了。

相南里把福音书留在家里，搭乘公交，来到了姑苏城监狱。

这个监狱很大，看起来竟然有点像一个金属的水桶。

相南里毕竟没坐过牢，也不清楚里面的内部结构。

他来到大厅，说明来意，向工作人员展示了通行证，又在电子知情书上签了好几次公民ID。

终于——

相南里坐在等候室，看见面前的金属门打开。

这扇门很窄，只能单人通过。

狱警用锁链牵着一台机器人走了出来。这台机器人的身体部件非常老旧，还有一些坑坑洼洼的旧伤。螺丝也松了，走路哐当哐哐响。

最特别的应该是它的头部位置，像是一个圆球水缸。半透明的，里面装着一枚粉红色的脑花。连着十几条电线。

“这就是犯人，编号GS719。”狱警用钥匙打开漠北身上的电子锁，把它往前轻轻推了一下，“在外面重新做人啊，别回来了。”

虽然没有档案，但GS719一直住在“高危监狱”里。这里关押着犯人里罪孽最深重的那批。

和那些赛博病人、传奇黑客、间谍等等比起来，GS719安静又听话，最喜欢的事是在草坪上晒太阳。连狱警都想不出它到底犯了什么事。

GS719呆呆地向前一步。

相南里思考片刻，觉得出狱后还是该给它安装一个头套。

要不然GS719走在外面，还是有点惊悚的。

他起身，弯腰，捏了捏GS719的机械胳膊：“我把你赎出来了，你明白这是什么意思吗？”

是的，相南里花了很高的代价，让漠北从监狱里刑满释放。

他并不认识漠北，也和他没什么交情。更不是为了拿捏安德鲁。

打动他的，是安德鲁的那句话，“你们都是能改变世界的天才，不该一辈子呆在监狱里”。

相南里了解过克隆人技术，网上对此早有讨论。既然克隆和共识技术，能制造出几乎一模一样的“复制人”。为什么不把历史上那些有名的创造者复制出来呢？

早有组织这么干过了。

他们想得到天才的大脑，于是在自愿进行遗体捐赠的科学家身上进行了不同的尝试。

明明是一样的基因，拥有一样的知识，甚至还有部分提取出来的记忆。

假的就是假的。

一部分复制人只是有记忆的弱智，一部分复制人充满劣等基因缺陷，还有一部分，和正常人差不多，哪怕智力测试正常，思维能力却远不及它们的本体。

最后，实验室给出的结论是：天赋不可复制。

这台机器人不是很高，顶多一米三。

GS719停顿片刻，点了点头。

“因为你之前犯的是重罪，所以现在是出狱观察期，十年内没有新的犯罪记录，才能获得公民身份，现在，你挂在我的户口下。我给你取了个新名字，叫北辰。”相南里温声道，“你可以理解吗？”

北辰的意思是北极星。相南里想着，既然他什么也不记得了，不如新生。

漠北，现在该叫北辰了，继续点了一下头。

他只是没有记忆，不是傻，装傻只是他在监狱里的保护色。

但没想到，这居然换来了一些怜惜。

北辰的机械化程度非常高，但这其实和人联的审讯没有关系。

东皇重工实验的最后阶段，生物资源（畸变体饲料）严重匮乏。所以北辰连带着还在地底的研究员，都把自己改造成了机械。

他是疯狂的科学家，也是这条路上的殉道者。

天赋不可复制。既然如此，让我见证吧。

见证你可以创造一个什么样的奇迹。

相南里拍了拍他圆滚滚的小脑袋：“走吧，我们回家。”
chunks.englishText:
The mere thought of potentially crossing paths with such a behemoth in the future sent a wave of pressure over Xiang Nanli. But then, a second thought occurred: who knew how long he’d even live? That realization brought a sense of relief. Why fret over things that hadn't even happened yet?

With his newly received wages in hand, Xiang Nanli leveraged Andrew’s connections to procure a batch of supplies; they would be ready for pickup at the warehouse once he reached the surface.

He had once asked Andrew, a legitimate doctor, why he knew so many people involved in the underworld.

Andrew had stammered for a long time before spitting out a single word: "Dopamine tablets." One had to be grateful for the new era; back in the day, fifty grams would have been enough to earn a firing squad.

Beyond some mechanical parts and weapon components, Xiang Nanli had also purchased a vehicle.

Well... nobody checked for driver's licenses on the surface.

He stayed home for two days. On the afternoon of the second day, Rolling Stone sent a message: "The matter you mentioned has been handled by the higher-ups. The pass will be emailed to you shortly. You can use it to pick up the person at the prison."

After saying that, Rolling Stone went offline immediately. Their Security Bureau had been incredibly busy lately, occupied with arresting different people in different districts. The Gusu City prison was nearly bursting at the seams. Furthermore, Rolling Stone had to process thousands of tip-off letters every day—some real, some just malicious, baseless accusations meant to use the law as a weapon.

Every civil servant had been running ragged lately.

Xiang Nanli was overjoyed and sent a quick "Thank you."

The so-called pass was actually an electronic key. It could be used by showing it to the prison staff for scanning.

Leaving his Bible at home, Xiang Nanli took the bus to the Gusu City prison.

The prison was massive, looking strangely like a giant metal bucket.

Xiang Nanli had never been to jail, so he wasn't familiar with the internal structure.

He arrived at the lobby, stated his purpose, presented the pass to the staff, and signed his citizen ID on the electronic consent form several times.

Finally—

Xiang Nanli sat in the waiting room and watched as the metal door in front of him opened.

The door was narrow, allowing only one person to pass through at a time.

A prison guard led a robot out on a chain. The robot’s body parts were ancient, covered in dents and old scars. Its screws were loose, and it clanked loudly with every step.

The most peculiar part was its head, which resembled a spherical glass jar. It was translucent, containing a pinkish brain inside, connected to a dozen or so wires.

"This is the prisoner, number GS719." The guard used a key to unlock the electronic shackle on Mobei’s body and gave it a gentle push forward. "Start over as a new person out there. Don't come back."

Although there were no records, GS719 had always lived in the "High-Risk Prison," where the most heinous criminals were kept.

Compared to the cyber-patients, legendary hackers, and spies, GS719 was quiet and obedient. Its favorite pastime was sunbathing on the lawn. Even the guards couldn't figure out what crime it had committed.

GS719 took a dull step forward.

Xiang Nanli thought for a moment and decided he should probably get it a head covering once they were out.

Otherwise, it would be a bit unsettling for GS719 to walk around in public.

He stood up, bent down, and squeezed GS719’s mechanical arm. "I’ve bailed you out. Do you understand what that means?"

Yes, Xiang Nanli had paid a high price to have Mobei released upon completion of his sentence.

He didn't know Mobei, nor did they have any friendship. He certainly wasn't doing it to manipulate Andrew.

What had moved him was Andrew’s words: "You are all geniuses capable of changing the world; you shouldn't spend your whole lives in prison."

Xiang Nanli had researched clone technology; it had been a topic of discussion online for a long time. Since cloning and consensus technology could create "replicants" that were nearly identical, why not replicate the famous creators of history?

Organizations had tried that long ago.

They wanted the brains of geniuses, so they conducted various experiments on scientists who had voluntarily donated their remains.

Despite having the same genes, the same knowledge, and even some extracted memories...

A fake was still a fake.

Some replicants were just morons with memories; some were filled with inferior genetic defects; and others were similar to normal people, but even if their intelligence tests were normal, their cognitive abilities were far inferior to the originals.

In the end, the laboratory’s conclusion was: Talent cannot be replicated.

The robot wasn't very tall, maybe 1.3 meters at most.

GS719 paused for a moment and nodded.

"Because your previous crime was a felony, you are now in a post-prison observation period. You can only obtain citizenship if you have no new criminal record within ten years. For now, you are under my household registration. I’ve given you a new name: Beichen," Xiang Nanli said gently. "Do you understand?"

Beichen meant "North Star." Xiang Nanli thought that since he remembered nothing, he might as well have a new beginning.

Mobei—or rather, Beichen—nodded again.

He lacked memories, not intelligence. Playing the fool had simply been his protective camouflage in prison.

He hadn't expected that to earn him some pity.

Beichen’s level of mechanization was extremely high, but that actually had nothing to do with the Human Alliance’s interrogations.

In the final stages of the Donghuang Heavy Industry experiments, biological resources (feed for aberrations) were severely scarce. Thus, Beichen, along with the researchers still underground, had transformed themselves into machines.

He was a mad scientist, and a martyr on this path.

Talent cannot be replicated. If that is the case, let me witness it.

Witness what kind of miracle you can create.

Xiang Nanli patted his round little head. "Let’s go. We’re going home."

chunks.chineseText:
第57章

小机器人有一双长手，几乎要拖到地上。躯体像水桶，顶着一个圆圆的脑袋。金属的头上半部分甚至是透明的。下半部分被一张铁皮覆盖，上面安装着凸起的五官，两只摄像眼，一张扩音器嘴，没有鼻子。

看得出来，北辰是和安德鲁同型号的机械改造人。现在的人根本不会把自己改造成这样，都在尽可能地保留着人型。

相南里回忆着维修过的安德鲁，开始在商城里下单自己需要的零件。

他带着北辰坐上城际公交。

监狱在郊区，没那么多人，空位很多，相南里刷了两张票，在后车厢的空位上坐下。

随着公交车往城内开去，车里的人渐渐多了起来。

一名机械化程度至少35的壮汉走了过来，手拍在北辰的头上：“喂，一台机器人凭什么坐着。给我滚开！”

装载玻璃罐里脑花因为重力往前晃了晃，看得相南里心头一惊。

“哦？噢……”

北辰茫然地望向他，身体瑟缩了一下。随后就打算起身，一股窝囊废受气包的模样。

相南里摁住北辰的肩膀，站了起来，语气不卑不亢：“首先，他不是机器人，是机械改造人。只是机械化程度比较高。其次，我买了两张票，没有义务给你让座。”

这男的一看就是道上混的，机械臂，机械眼，身上纹着大花面，寸头。身上的肌肉像是坚硬的石头。

如果是老弱病残也就算了。这不明显欺负老实人找茬的吗？

而且在相南里眼中，身高也就1米3的北辰绝对在“幼”的范畴里。

相南里这话说得有理有据，可惜寸头是个不讲道理的暴脾气。

他一拳往相南里的脸上砸去，四周响起破空的风声。

周围已经有人于心不忍地闭上眼，怕看见皮开肉绽的场面。但预料中的场景并没有发生。

相南里握住他金属质感的手腕，把要砸上自己脸的拳头一点一点挪开，脸上的笑容渐冷：“不懂好好说话吗？”

呵呵，当他价值几百万的基因药是白吃的？这么多次凌晨五点起来挨东方青帝打又是为了什么？他又不是抖M！

虽然看上去有些生气，但相南里的情绪并没有过于剧烈的波动。

只是“愤怒”会更适合处理现在的情景。

相南里摸到了他的金属胳膊，脑海里自动浮现出了型号和结构，这种机械臂他拆过不少。可惜没带工具，要不然也让这寸头体会一下什么叫一拳亏本十五万。

男人的机械臂没办法往前分毫，知道自己惹到硬茬子了，又不想轻易让开。

僵持了那么两三秒，车厢另一节，有个熟悉的人影走了过来：“诶呀，诶呦！这不是相老师吗，怎么在这遇到您了。”

是搏击俱乐部的海王星。他走过去，狠狠踹了寸头一脚：“你小子怎么回事？！还敢惹俱乐部的机械师？”

寸头被一脚踹飞好几米远，坐在地上，半天后才爬起来。竟然从嘴里咳出一些粉红色的液体，混着粉红色细丝。

海王星心头一跳，心想自己也没踹这么重吧？

他转头，对相南里赔笑：“这是和我一个小区的。他以前是快递员，后来工作被别的机器人顶了。失业到现在，看见机器人就肝火旺，最近又得了奇怪的皮肤病，背上长红点，脑子犯浑。今天正去医院看病呢。实在抱歉，哥。我回去就教训他。”

海王星抽出一支烟和两张票券，塞到相南里手里：“诶，我到站了。这就把他揪下去不碍着您的眼，哥有事常联系。”

说完，海王星揪着这个寸头的耳朵，把他带下了公交。

一场聚众斗殴就这么散了，周围观众的表情竟然有些许的失落。

相南里低头，看了眼自己手里的烟和两张票券。

他不怎么抽烟，认不出型号。

但能被拿来送人，多半是地下世界硬通货。

[是一种含多巴胺激素的烟。]小智给出解释，[含量5ug/根，有一定成瘾性。30ug/根以上视为违禁物。]

卧槽，大麻烟。

相南里立马丢进了垃圾桶。结果还没下车，到下一站，就有一个骨瘦嶙峋的女人慌慌张张地趴到垃圾桶边，左右看了眼，然后捡起这根烟跑下车。

相南里看得眼皮子一跳。

票券就是单纯的不记名支票，两张加起来也就50信用点。

北辰看起来依然呆呆的。

他小声地对相南里说：“我闻到了蘑菇味。”

相南里：“你安装了嗅觉系统？”

北辰先是点头，又迟疑着摇了一下头：“他皮肤上有孢子。我看见了，就闻到了。”

相南里视力很正常甚至比普通人类好一点，但他可没在寸头身上看见什么孢子。

可惜人都下车了，相南里也没办法再求证。

一个小时后，公交车终于晃悠到相南里家附近的小区。

相南里本来是牵着北辰走，后来感觉这机器人走路太慢，于是干脆直接抱了起来，架在了胳膊上。

楼下的医药店一直门可罗雀，如今却多了很多人排队。相南里不敢离他们太近，隔着玻璃观察片刻，这群人购买的都是治疗皮肤病的药。

相南里顿时把衣服领子拉得更高了一点，几乎挡住了大半张脸。

小机器人来回打量着周围的环境。

北辰眼里的世界不太一样。

他的世界是灰白黑三色，但某些东西，在它的眼里是彩色的光谱。

比如在空中漂浮着的粉红色孢子，圆圆的，尾巴连着一条细线。像蒲公英。

“孢子粉，很多。在空气里。”他抱住相南里的脖子，慢吞吞地说着，“记得戴防护面罩。”

相南里的心情略微沉重起来：“看来得提前去地表了，总觉得姑苏城最近不怎么太平。”

他依旧在楼下超市买了脱水蔬菜，打算回家泡一泡，再闷一碗饭，把小青做的卤肉解冻，切成片，应付一餐。

不知道小青回到他的家没有。家里的卤肉已经吃了三袋了，还剩十五袋。

吃完就只能吃营养膏了。

相南里吃饭挑嘴，但也不是特别挑。比如一个东西如果好吃，他可以一直吃，不存在吃腻的情况。科学有解释，说重复行为可以减少决策消耗的脑力成本。

他搭乘电梯，来到17楼。还没回家，就在走廊上闻到一股饭香。

相南里狠狠吸了两口油烟味：“隔壁在做饭吗？热油煎熟的蒜味，还有辣椒香，一定是干辣椒青辣椒红辣椒和花椒一起炒的。好香，在做什么？辣子鸡？”

北辰挠了挠头，很疑惑。

他没闻到。

可恶，谁家吃这么好，好想上门要饭。

相南里刷卡，打开门。一股比走廊上热烈浓郁数倍的饭菜香扑面而来。

厨房里传来声响，明显是有人在做饭。

“相南里~~”小福兴高采烈地扑了过来，然后警惕地站直身体，看向北辰，“它又是谁？家里的充电桩要不够用了！”

相南里把北辰放下：“这是北辰。这是小福。你们先去书房自己玩会~！”
chunks.englishText:
The little robot had long arms that nearly dragged on the ground. Its torso was like a bucket, topped with a round head. The upper half of the metal head was even transparent, while the lower half was covered by a sheet of iron, fitted with protruding features: two camera-eyes and a loudspeaker for a mouth. It had no nose.

It was clear that Beichen was the same model of mechanical cyborg as Andrew. People nowadays wouldn't dream of modifying themselves like this; they all tried to retain as much of a human form as possible.

Recalling the repairs he’d done on Andrew, Xiang Nanli began placing orders for the parts he needed in the mall.

He took Beichen onto the intercity bus.

The prison was in the suburbs, so it wasn't crowded, and there were plenty of empty seats. Xiang Nanli swiped two tickets and sat down in the back.

As the bus headed into the city, it began to fill up.

A burly man with at least 35% mechanization walked over and slapped his hand onto Beichen’s head. "Hey, why does a robot get a seat? Get lost!"

The brain in the glass jar wobbled forward due to the force, making Xiang Nanli’s heart skip a beat.

"Oh? Oh..."

Beichen looked at him blankly, his body shrinking back. He then made to stand up, looking every bit the spineless pushover.

Xiang Nanli pressed down on Beichen’s shoulder and stood up, his tone neither humble nor overbearing. "First of all, he is not a robot; he is a mechanical cyborg. He just has a high degree of mechanization. Secondly, I bought two tickets, and I am under no obligation to give up my seat to you."

The man clearly looked like a thug—mechanical arm, mechanical eye, covered in flashy tattoos, and sporting a buzz cut. His muscles looked like hard stone.

If it were an elderly, weak, sick, or disabled person, Xiang Nanli might have let it slide. But this was clearly just a bully picking on an honest person.

Moreover, in Xiang Nanli’s eyes, Beichen, at only 1.3 meters tall, definitely fell into the "child" category.

Xiang Nanli’s argument was logical and sound, but unfortunately, the buzz-cut man was an unreasonable hothead.

He threw a punch at Xiang Nanli’s face, the sound of wind whistling as his fist cut through the air.

People nearby closed their eyes, unable to bear the sight of the impending carnage. But the scene they expected didn't happen.

Xiang Nanli gripped the man’s metallic wrist, slowly pushing the fist that was about to smash into his face away. The smile on his face turned cold. "Don't you know how to speak properly?"

Heh, did he think the millions of credits he spent on genetic medicine were for nothing? And why did he think he woke up at 5:00 AM every day to get beaten by Dongfang Qingdi? He wasn't a masochist!

Although he looked a bit angry, Xiang Nanli’s emotions didn't fluctuate too violently.

It was just that "anger" was more suitable for handling the current situation.

Xiang Nanli felt the man’s mechanical arm, and the model and structure automatically appeared in his mind; he had dismantled plenty of these. It was a pity he didn't have his tools, or he would have let this guy experience what it felt like to lose 150,000 credits in a single punch.

The man’s mechanical arm couldn't move an inch forward. Realizing he had messed with someone tough, he didn't want to back down easily.

After a two- or three-second standoff, a familiar figure walked over from the other side of the carriage. "Oh my, oh my! Isn't this Teacher Xiang? What a surprise to run into you here."

It was Neptune from the fighting club. He walked over and kicked the buzz-cut man hard. "What the hell is wrong with you?! You dare provoke the club’s mechanic?"

The man was kicked several meters away, landing on the floor. He didn't climb up for a long time. When he finally did, he coughed up some pink liquid mixed with pink filaments.

Neptune’s heart skipped a beat, thinking he hadn't kicked him that hard.

He turned to Xiang Nanli and offered a fawning smile. "He’s from my neighborhood. He used to be a courier, but his job was taken by other robots. He’s been unemployed ever since, and he gets a chip on his shoulder whenever he sees a robot. Recently, he’s also caught some weird skin disease—red spots on his back—and he’s been acting delirious. He was on his way to the hospital today. I’m truly sorry, brother. I’ll teach him a lesson when we get back."

Neptune pulled out a cigarette and two vouchers, stuffing them into Xiang Nanli’s hand. "Anyway, this is my stop. I’ll drag him off so he doesn't offend your eyes. Let’s keep in touch, brother."

With that, Neptune grabbed the man by the ear and hauled him off the bus.

The brawl ended just like that, and the surrounding audience actually looked a bit disappointed.

Xiang Nanli looked down at the cigarette and the two vouchers in his hand.

He didn't smoke much and couldn't identify the brand.

But if it was being used as a gift, it was likely hard currency in the underground world.

[It is a cigarette containing dopamine hormones,] Xiao Zhi explained. [The content is 5ug per stick, which is somewhat addictive. Anything over 30ug per stick is considered a prohibited substance.]

*Holy crap, a drug cigarette.*

Xiang Nanli immediately tossed it into the trash can. Before the bus even left, at the next stop, a gaunt woman scrambled over to the trash can, looked left and right, then snatched the cigarette and ran off the bus.

Xiang Nanli’s eyelid twitched.

The vouchers were simple bearer checks; the two combined were only worth 50 credits.

Beichen still looked blank.

He whispered to Xiang Nanli, "I smell mushrooms."

Xiang Nanli: "You installed an olfactory system?"

Beichen nodded, then hesitated and shook his head. "There are spores on his skin. I saw them, so I smelled them."

Xiang Nanli’s vision was perfectly normal—even better than the average human’s—but he hadn't seen any spores on the man.

Unfortunately, the man had already gotten off the bus, so there was no way for Xiang Nanli to verify it.

An hour later, the bus finally rattled to the neighborhood near Xiang Nanli’s home.

Xiang Nanli had originally been holding Beichen’s hand, but feeling that the robot walked too slowly, he simply picked him up and tucked him under his arm.

The pharmacy downstairs, usually deserted, now had a long line of people. Xiang Nanli didn't dare get too close, observing through the glass for a moment; the crowd was buying medicine for skin diseases.

Xiang Nanli pulled his collar up higher, covering most of his face.

The little robot looked around at the environment.

The world in Beichen’s eyes was different.

His world was grayscale, but certain things appeared in a colorful spectrum.

For example, the pink spores floating in the air—round, with a thin line trailing behind them like a dandelion.

"Spore powder, a lot of it. In the air," he said, hugging Xiang Nanli’s neck slowly. "Remember to wear a protective mask."

Xiang Nanli’s mood grew heavy. "Looks like I’ll have to head to the surface early. Gusu City doesn't feel very safe lately."

He bought some dehydrated vegetables at the supermarket downstairs, planning to soak them at home, steam a bowl of rice, and defrost the braised meat Xiao Qing had made, slicing it up for a meal.

He wondered if Xiao Qing had returned home yet. He had already eaten three bags of the braised meat, with fifteen left.

Once those were gone, he’d be back to nutrient paste.

Xiang Nanli was a picky eater, but not excessively so. For instance, if he liked something, he could eat it indefinitely without getting tired of it. Science explained that repetitive behavior could reduce the cognitive load of decision-making.

He took the elevator to the 17th floor. Before he even reached his door, he smelled the aroma of food in the hallway.

Xiang Nanli took a deep breath of the oily, fragrant air. "Is someone cooking next door? The smell of garlic sautéed in hot oil, and the scent of chili—definitely a mix of dried, green, and red chilies with Sichuan peppercorns. So fragrant. What are they making? Spicy chicken?"

Beichen scratched his head, looking confused.

He didn't smell anything.

*Damn it, who’s eating so well? I want to go over and beg for food.*

Xiang Nanli swiped his card and opened the door. A scent several times more intense and appetizing than the one in the hallway rushed out to meet him.

There was noise coming from the kitchen; someone was clearly cooking.

"Xiang Nanli~~" Xiao Fu pounced over excitedly, then stood up straight, looking at Beichen with suspicion. "Who is *that*? The charging station at home isn't going to be enough!"

Xiang Nanli put Beichen down. "This is Beichen. This is Xiao Fu. You two go play in the study for a bit!"

chunks.chineseText:
客厅明显被收拾过了，散落在地上的零件、工具被分门别类放好，又不至于让相南里找不到。

相南里对环境的整洁度一向是能用就行。但东方青帝却会打扫得干干净净，床底下都见不得灰尘。好在他干活快，从不抱怨，还不用睡觉，相南里也就随便他了！

房间里多余的垃圾被丢掉，平平无奇的直男餐桌铺上了蕾丝餐布。精致的玻璃花瓶摆放在桌上，里面插着两朵郁金香。一红一黄。

桌子上已经有两盘热菜。一份肉臊蒸蛋，一份炸茄盒。

分量不多，刚好适合一人食用。

相南里的心中涌现出喜悦，他喜出望外地推开厨房门：“小青~你回来了？”

但里面站着的陌生人很快让相南里意识到，自己搞错了。

没有东方青帝。厨房里的年轻男人容貌昳丽，神态柔和，气质古典，五官不那么尖锐却有棱角，很符合东方美学。眼角和脸颊上有两颗不太明显的小痣。

洛阳脸上也有两颗痣。

相南里当初在普林斯顿演讲完，去了图书馆继续参加什么座谈会。主题是“人工智能对人类社会的推动作用”，人群散去，午夜的图书馆只剩校方、他还有洛阳。

相南里路过书架，发现严肃的图书馆里竟然混进来一本中文书，还是讲面相的闲书。也不知道是哪个留学生这么调皮。

相南里按照父系算，是三代华裔。按照母系算，是二代华裔。他们家平时交流都不说中文。相南里却无师自通，学会了汉语。或许是什么种族天赋。

他不仅会说，会看，还会写。这当然不是为了什么东方市场，他有3/4的汉族血统，对遥远的东方有着发自内心的文化认同。

相南里翻开书，随意看了两眼，打趣道：“洛阳，你这两颗痣都不吉利啊。你看，眼角这颗克妻，脸中这颗善妒。”

“老师，这是封建迷信。您怎么还信这个？”洛阳的声音有些无奈，他把书从相南里的手里拿走，“……唔。”

“嗯？”

“没什么。走吧，要闭馆了。”

洛阳把书合上，塞了回去。

书上还画了耳垂痣，说这里长痣的人聪慧。

相南里知不知道他耳垂后有这么一颗？

……

……

“主人。您回来了？”家政机器人的声音把相南里拉回现实，“您是要给我取名为小青吗？”

他，姑且称之为“他”，身体明显的男性，身高183左右，系着围裙。有一头深栗色的短发，微卷，桃花眼呈茶色，双眼皮褶子很深，眼尾微微下垂，看起来很是无辜。基本看不出机器人的影子。

嗯，最近的确流行这种1：1复刻的家政。几百年来，大家已经看腻了机械改造人。追求起了原生态。

相南里尴尬道：“不是，小青是另一个家庭成员。”

他摸了摸鼻子：“你叫小白吧。”

小白微笑道：“好的，主人。”

“也别叫我主人，这个家庭不搞封建奴隶制。”

相南里汗毛都要竖起来了。

小白略微疑惑：“那我该怎么称呼您？除主人外，目前使用率排名前十的称呼分别为：大人、老公、亲爱的、宝宝、老婆……”

家政机器人看起来在智能和不智能间切换。

小白的微表情设计的很好，非常自然；但理解能力忽高忽低。

相南里打断了它：“叫我名字就行。我叫，相南里。下单页面有写。”

小白点头，把餐盘端到餐厅，并拉开了桌椅：“好的，相南里。我记住了。在外工作一天辛苦了，请用餐。这顿餐费来自集团赠送，感谢您购买并使用永生科技旗下的家政机器人。

“我去浴室为您放热水，您喜欢什么味道的香氛？”

“……？”我们家什么时候买过香氛，“马鞭草柠檬味的有吗，谢谢。”

小白转身，十分轻盈地走进浴室：“好的，这就为您准备。”

相南里面对满桌饭菜，陷入沉思。

[小智。]

[我在。]

[……这家政机器人20万呐？]

不是说仿生拟人款很贵吗？

相南里的确订购的是男性机器人，但设想的其实是全金属壮汉来着，那种一看干活就很利索。

当然，小白也不是不好。这张脸实在美丽，性格似乎过分人妻，但对于家政机器人来说，也不是什么大事。

小智还没有进化出疑惑这种情绪，它回答：[根据订单，是的。]

好吧。相南里多刨了两口饭。

感觉还是小青做饭更好吃一点。

相南里正想着，门口突然传来一阵开门声。

家里都是电子锁，感应的。

相南里警惕地放下碗筷，瞬间抄起桌子上的餐刀，走到玄关位置。

但在看清楚来人后，相南里松开了手里的餐刀。

东方青帝就站在门口，眼里亮着银白色的瞳环。门口没开灯，光线晦暗，只有他的一双眼睛灼灼。

“小青？”相南里很是意外，“你——”

他的话还没说完。

东方青帝突然三两步走上前，紧紧抱住了他。

小青的力道很大，相南里被冲得往后退了好几步，他倒在沙发上，动弹不得。整个人像是被藤蔓缠上了。

东方青帝的头就埋在他的颈肩。

相南里本来想推开他，毕竟东方青帝有些沉，却在下一秒，感觉到了这具身体的颤抖。

“相南里……”东方青帝沙哑着开口，“相南里。”

相南里有些懵，他反手抱住了小青，拍着他的背，又安抚性地亲了亲他的额头：“怎么了？小青。回军团受委屈了？”

滚烫的液体滴在了相南里的脖子上。

相南里愣住了。
chunks.englishText:
The living room had clearly been tidied up; the parts and tools that usually lay scattered on the floor were now neatly categorized, yet still easy for Xiang Nanli to find.

Xiang Nanli had always been the type to settle for "good enough" when it came to cleanliness. But Dongfang Qingdi would clean everything until it sparkled, not even leaving dust under the bed. Fortunately, he worked fast, never complained, and didn't need to sleep, so Xiang Nanli just let him be!

The excess trash in the room had been cleared away, and the plain, bachelor-style dining table was now covered with a lace tablecloth. An exquisite glass vase sat on the table, holding two tulips—one red, one yellow.

Two hot dishes were already on the table: steamed eggs with minced meat and fried eggplant boxes.

The portions were small, just right for one person.

Joy welled up in Xiang Nanli’s heart. He pushed open the kitchen door, beaming. "Xiao Qing~ you’re back?"

But the stranger standing inside made Xiang Nanli realize his mistake immediately.

It wasn't Dongfang Qingdi. The young man in the kitchen had a beautiful face, a gentle demeanor, and a classical aura. His features weren't sharp but had distinct angles, very much in line with Eastern aesthetics. There were two faint, small moles near the corner of his eye and on his cheek.

Luoyang had two moles there, too.

After Xiang Nanli finished his lecture at Princeton, he had gone to the library to attend some seminar. The theme was "The Role of Artificial Intelligence in Promoting Human Society." After the crowd dispersed, only the school officials, himself, and Luoyang remained in the midnight library.

Xiang Nanli had passed a bookshelf and discovered that a book on physiognomy—a casual read—had been mixed into the serious library collection. He wondered which international student had been so mischievous.

By his father’s side, Xiang Nanli was third-generation Chinese; by his mother’s, second. His family didn't speak Chinese at home. Yet, Xiang Nanli had learned the language without a teacher. Perhaps it was some kind of racial talent.

He could not only speak and read it but also write it. This wasn't for the sake of some Eastern market; he had 3/4 Han Chinese ancestry and felt a genuine cultural identification with the distant East.

Xiang Nanli flipped through the book and teased, "Luoyang, these two moles of yours are unlucky. Look, the one at the corner of your eye is 'wife-crushing,' and the one in the middle of your cheek is 'jealous.'"

"Teacher, that’s feudal superstition. How can you believe in this?" Luoyang’s voice was helpless as he took the book from Xiang Nanli’s hand. "...Hmm."

"Hmm?"

"Nothing. Let’s go, the library is closing."

Luoyang closed the book and shoved it back.

The book had also depicted a mole on the earlobe, claiming that people with one there were intelligent.

Did Xiang Nanli know he had one behind his earlobe?

...

...

"Master. You’re back?" The domestic robot’s voice pulled Xiang Nanli back to reality. "Are you planning to name me Xiao Qing?"

He—let’s call him "he"—was clearly male, about 183cm tall, wearing an apron. He had short, dark chestnut hair with a slight curl, peach-blossom eyes that were tea-colored, and deep double eyelids that drooped slightly at the corners, making him look very innocent. You could barely tell he was a robot.

Well, these 1:1 replica domestic robots had become quite popular lately. People had grown tired of mechanical cyborgs over the past few centuries and were now pursuing the "original" look.

Xiang Nanli said awkwardly, "No, Xiao Qing is another family member."
