赤夫发现自己落入圈套，却依然临危不乱，他的肌肉隆起，在瞬间硬的像是石块，皮肤表面浮现出鲜红的纹路。

这瞬间，赤夫爆发出了惊人的巨力。他一把推开压在身上的三个人，反手就是一拳砸了过去。

葛根正脸挨了一拳，头脑还有些发懵。

枪声在下一秒响起。

小周几乎是本能地歪过头，子弹擦着他的脸划过，他的皮肤表面被烫伤，露出一块淋漓的血色。

小周愣了一下，摸着自己的脸侧，摸到了一手的鲜血。伤口还很烫。

他的内置AI则提醒：“您购买的保险套餐生效中，已为您开启身体保护机制，暂时切断感觉神经的传递。您会有一定时间的四肢麻痹、头晕等副作用。如需停止保护，请按T退订。”

小周一直觉得，去地表支教是很好玩的，也很有意义。

他是人联的公民，所有地表据点对他们都很客气。

小周知道，自己的格斗水平在机械改造人里相当一般。

他能在地表横着走，是因为有人联当后盾。

子弹擦着他脸划过的时候，小周才意识到自己是很怕死的。生活不是虚拟游戏，没有重来一次的机会。

而他短暂体验的生活，却是地表遗民时刻都要面临的困境。这枚子弹会因为食物、水、女人，甚至可以没有任何理由地射出去。

狂血战士解开基因锁后，战斗力会比平时提高一大截，而且伤势越重，攻击力越强。但维持的时间却很短。

并且，在短暂爆发后，狂血战士会陷入瘫痪状态。

巡逻队这次逮捕用上了从支教大学生那学来的“战术”，车轮战轮番上阵，并且在爆发最高的时刻避其锋芒。

渐渐的，葛根有了一种错觉。那就是他们面对的不是恐怖的基因战士，而是囚笼里的猎物。和他过去猎过的那些獾子、鹿、野猪没什么不同。

十分钟后，巡逻队生擒了三名罗马城大使；并且收押进地底监狱。

监狱里是很安全的，也不用怕有人劫狱，因为隔壁就是蛇夫座的窝。

它本来以为是相南里送来了加餐，被告知不能吃后，失望地盘卧了回去。

东方青帝正在郊外，和相南里联系用的是无线电。

黑夜里，他的身影和阴影融为一体，眼前是罗马城的一堆强盗，耳边是相南里絮絮的唠叨声。

“小青，他们人到齐了吗？”

“等会打架要小心点，咱们没钱买漆。”

“这批人领头的砍了。剩下的看看能不能劳动改造，给个机会重新做人。毕竟都是壮劳力，拿来修电网也是很好的，刚好缺人手。”

永恒城的贵族好歹是“神庭后裔”，他们更像是制度上的吃人。

罗马城是物理上的吃人，每个人起码都能死刑三次。当耗材用起来，相南里是不会心痛的。

现场除了他，还有悄无声息从森林深处爬出来的畸变体们。

太大号的畸变体容易被发现，这次，被以西结叫过来的，都是小体型的畸变体。他们在族群里属于底层，只能吃大红它们的残羹冷炙。

以西结看在眼里，却并不会帮忙。

弱肉强食是畸变体的天性，只有最强壮的怪物才有资格活下去。

地表资源稀缺，在过去，这种小畸变体都撑不过冬天，会被自然淘汰。

以西结认为，让它们有口饭吃已经是族群的进步了。

不过，在需要对付人类的时候，这些小畸变体却很合适。它们不怕痛，咬合力惊人，也不怕死。

以西结站在树梢的高处，长尾悄无声息地垂落着。

以他的角度，能看见位于战场另一端的东方青帝，他们一东一西，其他畸变体在两侧，把毫无知觉的罗马城战士们团团围住。

以西结的唇角不由自主地瞥了一下，不是很想看见东方青帝。

他被相南里拉去开了个会，以西结原本以为自己只是跟着旁听，没想到听着听着，相南里就安排上了。说罗马城那些人潜伏的地点，刚好就在畸变体的栖息地附近。

说完，用一种期待的目光看向了以西结……

以西结想，他并不是在听相南里的指挥。

嗯，只是这些小畸变体也应该囤积一些脂肪。
chunks.englishText:
Chapter 98: Harvest Festival (Part 4)

Chifu realized he had fallen into a trap, but he remained calm under pressure. His muscles bulged, turning as hard as stone in an instant, and bright red patterns appeared on the surface of his skin.

In this moment, Chifu erupted with astonishing, immense strength. He shoved away the three people pressing down on him and threw a punch backward.

Gegen took the punch square in the face, his head still reeling.

Gunshots rang out the next second.

Xiao Zhou tilted his head almost by instinct. The bullet grazed his face, scorching the surface of his skin and revealing a patch of dripping blood.

Xiao Zhou froze for a moment, touching the side of his face and coming away with a handful of blood. The wound was still hot.

His built-in AI reminded him: "The insurance package you purchased is in effect. The body protection mechanism has been activated for you, temporarily cutting off the transmission of sensory nerves. You will experience side effects such as numbness in the limbs and dizziness for a certain period. If you wish to stop the protection, please press T to unsubscribe."

Xiao Zhou had always felt that going to the surface to teach was very fun and meaningful.

He was a citizen of the Human Alliance, and all surface strongholds were very polite to them.

Xiao Zhou knew that his combat level was quite average among mechanical cyborgs.

He could walk sideways on the surface because he had the Human Alliance as his backing.

It was only when the bullet grazed his face that Xiao Zhou realized he was very afraid of death. Life was not a virtual game; there were no chances to start over.

And the life he had briefly experienced was the predicament that surface survivors had to face at every moment. This bullet could be fired because of food, water, women, or even for no reason at all.

After a Blood-Berserker warrior unlocked their genetic shackles, their combat power would increase by a large margin compared to normal, and the more severe their injuries, the stronger their attack power. However, the duration was very short.

Furthermore, after the brief burst, the Blood-Berserker would fall into a state of paralysis.

This time, the patrol team used the "tactics" they had learned from the college student volunteers, taking turns in a wheel-battle, and avoiding the brunt of the enemy's force at the moment of their highest burst.

Gradually, Gegen had an illusion. It was that they were not facing terrifying genetic warriors, but prey in a cage. No different from the badgers, deer, and wild boars he had hunted in the past.

Ten minutes later, the patrol team captured three Rome City ambassadors alive and locked them in the underground prison.

The prison was very safe, and there was no need to fear anyone breaking them out, because next door was the nest of the Ophiuchus.

It had originally thought that Xiang Nanli had sent a snack, but after being told it couldn't eat them, it coiled back up in disappointment.

Dongfang Qingdi was in the suburbs, using a radio to contact Xiang Nanli.

In the dark night, his figure blended into the shadows; before him was a pile of robbers from Rome City, and in his ear was Xiang Nanli’s incessant nagging.

"Xiao Qing, are they all there?"

"Be careful when you fight later; we don't have money to buy paint."

"Kill the leader of this group. See if the rest can be sent to labor reform and given a chance to be reborn. After all, they are all strong labor, and using them to repair the power grid is also very good; we happen to be short of hands."

The nobles of Eternal City were at least "descendants of the Divine Court"; they were more like institutional cannibals.

Rome City was physical cannibalism; everyone there deserved the death penalty at least three times over. When using them as expendable materials, Xiang Nanli wouldn't feel a shred of heartache.

Besides him, there were also the aberrants crawling out silently from the depths of the forest.

Aberrants that were too large were easily discovered. This time, the ones Ezekiel called over were all small-sized aberrants. They belonged to the bottom of the hierarchy in their group and could only eat the leftovers of the big ones like Da Hong.

Ezekiel saw it all, but he wouldn't help.

Survival of the fittest was the nature of the aberrants; only the strongest monsters were qualified to survive.

Surface resources were scarce. In the past, these small aberrants wouldn't survive the winter and would be naturally eliminated.

Ezekiel believed that letting them have a bite to eat was already progress for the group.

However, when it came to dealing with humans, these small aberrants were quite suitable. They didn't fear pain, had astonishing bite force, and didn't fear death.

Ezekiel stood on a high branch, his long tail hanging down silently.

From his angle, he could see Dongfang Qingdi at the other end of the battlefield. They were east and west, with other aberrants on the sides, surrounding the oblivious Rome City warriors.

Ezekiel’s lips couldn't help but twitch; he didn't really want to see Dongfang Qingdi.

He had been dragged by Xiang Nanli to a meeting. Ezekiel had originally thought he was just tagging along to listen, but he hadn't expected that as he listened, Xiang Nanli started making arrangements. He said the location where those people from Rome City were lurking happened to be near the habitat of the aberrants.

After saying that, he looked at Ezekiel with an expectant gaze...

Ezekiel thought, he wasn't following Xiang Nanli’s command.

Hmm, it was just that these small aberrants should also store up some fat.

第99章 丰收节5

现在是半夜，郊外一点月光都没有，伸手不见五指。
　　但在红外镜头下，没有任何东西能藏住自己的身影。
　　四头爬行者悄然从树林间探出头。
　　视频里没有声音，相南里只能看见它们整齐划一的行动。这是一群行走的生物坦克。而现在，它们要对上真正的坦克。
　　罗马城的执政官就在车内，装甲车里的空间不算大。他却独占了接近1/3。中间留出一片泾渭分明的空隙。
　　剩下的狂血战士像是小鹌鹑一样，瑟瑟发抖地挤在一起。
　　注射过“狂血基因药”，会让这些战士染上一些不怎么愉快的副作用，这个叫血脉压制。
　　只有最强壮的几个儿子，在面对执政官时，才不会因为恐惧而瑟瑟发抖。
　　执政官盘坐在地上，闭目养神。他今年97岁，却并不苍老，是须发皆白的中年人长相，胸口疤痕新旧交错，一身肌肉看起来很是健硕。
　　执政官正在等着赤夫发回信号。
　　郊区的夜晚总是如此寂静，执政官有些心神不宁，空气里飘来一股令人不安的腥味。
　　“是爬行者的味道。”执政官嗅了嗅，眉头不安地蹙起。
　　执政官时常出入荒区，偶尔会遇上这种怪物。神庭的人有办法操控，因此在大草原上无往不利。
　　畸变人就是一团没有意识的恐怖腐烂物，体型大的能有二十多米。
　　畸变人几乎是地表最恐怖的怪物，比它强大的没它数量多，比它数量多的没它战斗力强。它们甚至还很记仇。
　　但没关系……
　　执政官不是普通人，在他漫长的生涯里，也杀过好几只畸变体。他在年轻时，单挑过一头四米长的狂暴者。这些成功的经验让他在面对畸变体时不至于被吓破胆。
　　罗马城的暴徒们有些许的骚乱，但很快被执政官的自信感染。有时候，执政官的儿子们很有野心，想取而代之，又恨自己父亲的无情和暴虐。
　　但他们也不得不承认，执政官的存在就像一座遮风挡雨的大山。
　　执政官看向车边的十七子：“诺夫，你带着弟弟，下车去看看。”
　　亚夫心想，执政官上次喊他名字还喊的褐夫，这次又叫诺夫，就没一次对过。
　　没办法，执政官的儿子太多了，儿子又生了一堆儿子。喊错名是不可避免的事。
　　亚夫抄起武器，翻身下车。
　　他打开手电筒，灯光像探射一样向四周射去。
　　四周很安静，连虫鸣都没有。只能听见远处河流的潺潺。
　　亚夫忍着恐惧，往深处走了两步。他刨开碍事的灌木，在看清周围的瞬间，心头悚然，汗毛竖起。
　　他本能地解开基因锁，进入了暴血状态——
　　周围有四头畸变体。
　　其中一头猛地朝他脸上扑来。亚夫能看见那双大得夸张的嘴在半空裂开，更恐怖的是，这只爬行者是站着的！
　　站着的！
　　亚夫的手电筒掉在地上，他扭头狂奔：“爸爸！救命！”
　　蜂鸟无人机转动着角度，屏幕角落出现了东方青帝的脸。
　　他的神态有些漫不经心，明明是灰色的视频，一张脸依然帅得有些突出。像是独自加了一层滤镜。
　　相南里忍不住放大欣赏了两秒，随后放了回去。
　　狂血战士已经和四头畸变体打在了一起，畸变体不愧是地表的肉身坦克，肆无忌惮地横冲直撞，相南里余光里瞥见好几个人被踩中了，从人肉变成了人肉馅。
　　画面在此时打上了一团马赛克。
　　电脑里传来小福的友情提醒：“里里，你该休息一下了！不要长时间盯着屏幕，要保护好眼睛。”
　　小智：[我认为福音书说的对。]
　　现在是凌晨两点。
　　相南里总觉得，在他们眼里，自己恐怕还是未成年。
　　小青说，外面太危险了，希望他在安全的地方等着。
　　道理相南里其实都懂，君子不立危墙之下。目前阶段，基地里的重要成员都是因为他团结在一起的，他还不可以被取代。所以他的安全非常重要，基本等于这个新生政权的存亡。
　　但相南里心里难免有些小猫刺挠。
　　“赤夫抓住了吗？”他问。
　　小福回答：“在地下监狱里关着。蛇夫座堵在门口，很安全。市里人手不足，让罗马城的人逃出去了三个，不过问题不大。”
　　毕竟就他们逃跑的方向，不是被以西结逮住，就是被东方青帝逮住。
　　相南里微微点头，开始整理罗马城的资料。
　　根据调查组7年前登记在案的报告，罗马城一共4000人，其中3000人是奴隶；负责伺候老爷们的衣食住行，平时负责繁重的农活和劳役。这也是地表最常见的搭配。
　　相南里曾经思考过，为什么奴隶们待遇都这么糟糕，还甘愿被压榨。
　　事实就是：环境如此。
　　跑？往哪跑。荒野上游荡着异种，普通人毫无还手之力，没有武力，在荒野上流浪，就像是小兔子跑进了狼群。而且，别的地方难道会更好吗？
　　听说地下城不错。可光是一个准入资格，都能卡住普通人的一生。他们的世界就这么点大，出生，劳作，繁衍，死亡，能吃饱饭就是万幸。
　　大多数人都是麻木的，甚至带着愚钝的笨感。这就是相南里见过的大多地表遗民的精神面貌。
　　他们甚至都不是封建时代的帝王和子民；而是人和可以压榨的物资；红色的牛奶从农奴的身体里流出来。
　　小青和以西结是半夜出发的，早上六点天还没亮，装甲车就载着一车俘虏回到了永恒市。
　　这些狂血战士往日总是趾高气昂，如今却像是被吓破胆的小鸡，蜷缩在一起。每个人或多或少带点伤。
　　早餐摊还没支起来，血腥味浓郁的大车碾压着石板路，朝后山角斗场的方向开去，那边直通地牢。
　　小青战斗力很强。但他毕竟只有一个人，就那么点体积，使用起来还很耗电。
　　但有畸变人协助就不一样了，小青只需要负责爬行者啃不动的变异人类。
　　——比如暴血后的执政官。
　　暴血状态的执政官肌肉膨大，身高将近三米，如同一头失去理智的野兽；全身肌肉强度惊人，宛如钢铁。
　　他挥舞的拳头依然孔武有力，可惜连敌人的衣角都摸不到；充分感受到了相南里在训练时的绝望。
　　可惜相南里没看见执政官是怎么死的。
　　留在郊外的尸体像是一张血肉全蒸发后巨大的人皮，以西结说他的畸变人小弟会负责收拾。
　　战争只是大永恒区战略里，最不重要的一环。
　　难的是如何让罗马城的奴隶变成人。
　　相南里从守了一夜的监控前起身：“小智，给厨房师傅说一声，晚上给以西结还有他的小弟加个鸡腿，要纯菌鸡肉馅的。”
　　算算时间，小青应该快到楼下了。他得去接一下。
　　小智“哦”了一声，不是很想，但因为是相南里吩咐的，只好不情不愿地安排了下去。
chunks.englishText:
Chapter 99: Harvest Festival (Part 5)

It was midnight, and there was no moonlight in the suburbs; you couldn't even see your own fingers.
But under the infrared lens, nothing could hide its figure.
Four crawlers quietly poked their heads out from the woods.
There was no sound in the video; Xiang Nanli could only see their uniform movements. This was a group of walking biological tanks. And now, they were going to face a real tank.
The Governor of Rome City was inside the vehicle, and the space inside the armored car was not large. Yet, he occupied nearly 1/3 of it alone. A clear, distinct gap was left in the middle.
The remaining Blood-Berserker warriors huddled together like little quails, shivering.
Injecting the "Blood-Berserker Gene Drug" would cause these warriors to suffer from some unpleasant side effects, which was called bloodline suppression.
Only the strongest few sons would not shiver in fear when facing the Governor.
The Governor sat cross-legged on the floor, eyes closed to rest. He was 97 years old, yet he didn't look old; he had the appearance of a middle-aged man with white hair and beard. His chest was covered in crisscrossing scars, old and new, and his muscles looked very robust.
The Governor was waiting for Chifu to send back a signal.
The night in the suburbs was always so quiet. The Governor felt a bit restless; a disturbing, fishy smell drifted through the air.
"It's the smell of crawlers." The Governor sniffed, his brow furrowing uneasily.
The Governor often went in and out of the wasteland and occasionally encountered such monsters. The people of the Divine Court had ways to control them, which was why they were invincible on the vast grasslands.
Aberrant humans were just a mass of terrifying, rotting matter without consciousness; the large ones could be over twenty meters tall.
Aberrant humans were almost the most terrifying monsters on the surface. Those stronger than them weren't as numerous, and those more numerous than them weren't as strong. They were even quite vengeful.
But it didn't matter...
The Governor was not an ordinary person. In his long career, he had killed several aberrants. When he was young, he had soloed a four-meter-long Berserker. These successful experiences kept him from being scared out of his wits when facing aberrants.
The thugs of Rome City were in a slight panic, but they were quickly infected by the Governor’s confidence. Sometimes, the Governor’s sons were very ambitious and wanted to replace him, while hating their father’s ruthlessness and tyranny.
But they also had to admit that the Governor’s existence was like a great mountain shielding them from the wind and rain.
The Governor looked at his seventeenth son: "Nuofu, take your brothers and get out of the car to take a look."
Yafu thought to himself, the last time the Governor called his name, he called him Hefu; this time he called him Nuofu. He never got it right once.
There was no help for it; the Governor had too many sons, and those sons had given birth to a pile of sons. Calling the wrong name was inevitable.
Yafu grabbed his weapon and flipped out of the car.
He turned on his flashlight, the light shooting out into the surroundings like a searchlight.
Everything around was quiet; there wasn't even the sound of insects. He could only hear the gurgling of a river in the distance.
Yafu endured his fear and walked two steps deeper. He pushed aside the obstructive bushes, and the moment he saw his surroundings, his heart turned cold, and his hair stood on end.
He instinctively unlocked his genetic shackles and entered the Blood-Berserker state—
There were four aberrants surrounding him.
One of them lunged straight at his face. Yafu could see that ridiculously large mouth split open in mid-air, and what was even more terrifying was that this crawler was standing!
Standing!
Yafu’s flashlight fell to the ground, and he turned and ran wildly: "Dad! Help!"
The hummingbird drone rotated its angle, and Dongfang Qingdi’s face appeared in the corner of the screen.
His expression was somewhat nonchalant. Even though it was a grayscale video, his face was still strikingly handsome. It was as if he had added a filter all by himself.
Xiang Nanli couldn't help but zoom in to admire it for two seconds, then zoomed back out.
The Blood-Berserker warriors were already fighting with the four aberrants. The aberrants were worthy of being the flesh-and-blood tanks of the surface, charging recklessly. Xiang Nanli caught a glimpse out of the corner of his eye of several people being trampled, turning from human flesh into human meat paste.
The screen was mosaicked at this moment.
Xiao Fu’s friendly reminder came through the computer: "Li-li, you should rest for a while! Don't stare at the screen for too long; you have to protect your eyes."
Xiao Zhi: [I think the Gospel is right.]
It was now two in the morning.
Xiang Nanli always felt that in their eyes, he was probably still a minor.
Xiao Qing said it was too dangerous outside and hoped he would wait in a safe place.
Xiang Nanli actually understood the logic; a gentleman does not stand under a dangerous wall. At the current stage, the important members of the base were united because of him; he could not be replaced yet. Therefore, his safety was very important, basically equivalent to the survival of this new regime.
But Xiang Nanli couldn't help but feel a little itchy in his heart.
"Did you catch Chifu?" he asked.
Xiao Fu replied: "He's locked in the underground prison. The Ophiuchus is blocking the door; it's very safe. The city is short-handed, so three people from Rome City escaped, but it’s not a big problem."
After all, in the direction they were fleeing, they would either be caught by Ezekiel or by Dongfang Qingdi.
Xiang Nanli nodded slightly and began to organize the information on Rome City.
According to the registered report from the investigation team seven years ago, Rome City had a total of 4,000 people, 3,000 of whom were slaves; they were responsible for serving the masters’ food, clothing, housing, and transportation, and usually responsible for heavy farm work and corvée labor. This was also the most common setup on the surface.
Xiang Nanli had once pondered why the slaves were treated so poorly yet were still willing to be exploited.
The fact was: the environment was like this.
Run? Where to run? Mutants roamed the wilderness, and ordinary people had no power to fight back. Without martial strength, wandering in the wilderness was like a little rabbit running into a pack of wolves. Besides, would other places be any better?
He heard the underground city was good. But just the entry qualification could block an ordinary person’s entire life. Their world was only this big: birth, labor, reproduction, death. Being able to eat one's fill was a great fortune.
Most people were numb, even carrying a sense of dull stupidity. This was the mental outlook of most surface survivors Xiang Nanli had seen.
They weren't even emperors and subjects of the feudal era; they were humans and exploitable materials; red milk flowed from the bodies of the serfs.
Xiao Qing and Ezekiel set off in the middle of the night. By six o'clock in the morning, before dawn, the armored vehicle returned to Eternal City with a carload of captives.
These Blood-Berserker warriors, who were usually arrogant and haughty, were now like frightened little chicks, huddled together. Everyone had more or less some injuries.
The breakfast stalls hadn't been set up yet, and the blood-scented heavy vehicle rumbled over the stone road, heading toward the direction of the mountain-back arena, which led directly to the dungeon.
Xiao Qing had strong combat power. But he was only one person, after all, and with his small size, he consumed a lot of power to use.
But it was different with the help of the aberrants; Xiao Qing only needed to be responsible for the mutated humans that the crawlers couldn't bite.
—For example, the Governor after his blood boiled.
The Governor in the blood-boiling state had bulging muscles and a height of nearly three meters, like a beast that had lost its reason; his entire body’s muscle strength was astonishing, like steel.
The fists he swung were still powerful, but unfortunately, he couldn't even touch the corner of his enemy’s clothes; he fully experienced the despair Xiang Nanli felt during training.
It was a pity that Xiang Nanli didn't see how the Governor died.
The corpse left in the suburbs looked like a huge piece of human skin after all the flesh and blood had evaporated. Ezekiel said his aberrant little brothers would be responsible for cleaning it up.
War was just the least important part of the Great Eternal Zone’s strategy.
The difficult part was how to turn the slaves of Rome City into people.
Xiang Nanli rose from the monitor he had been guarding all night: "Xiao Zhi, tell the kitchen master to add a chicken leg for Ezekiel and his little brothers tonight, pure fungal chicken meat filling."
Calculating the time, Xiao Qing should be arriving downstairs soon. He had to go pick him up.
Xiao Zhi said "Oh," not really wanting to, but because it was Xiang Nanli’s order, he had to arrange it reluctantly.

chunks.chapterTitle: 第100章 罗马城贵族的改造 (Part 1)
chunks.chineseText:
第100章 罗马城贵族的改造

他回到宿舍洗了个澡，认认真真擦干净了身上的血迹和别的污渍。还不忘喷上之前在姑苏城买到的淡香水。

理智告诉他，最好不要把宝贵的电量浪费在这种事上，但根据计算，相南里有百分之九十九的概率会喜欢这种味道，是偏向浓郁的小苍兰味。

东方青帝听说，一些雄性大猫为了求偶，会特地去寻找野外的木天蓼滚一圈，用于勾引雌性。

只能说自然界里，雄性求偶的手段竟然是通用的。

美丽的外观和强壮的身体。

东方青帝换好衣服，用吹风机烘干头发，把洗衣机里的衣服晾干。顺便把相南里挂在阳台上的衣服收进衣柜里，叠好。又熟练地把手伸向了扫帚和拖把。动作娴熟自然，一气呵成。

东方青帝认为，做家务和造核弹没有高低贵贱之分，都是人类无差别的劳动。但人类会用创造的价值去衡量这些劳动，自动在内心划分出高级和低级。

在这样的价值体系中，繁琐家务下蕴藏着的，一个人对另一个人不可替代的爱意，总是被忽略掉。似乎那并不重要。

但对于东方青帝来说，保持相南里居住环境的舒适，比造十颗核弹还要重要。

和赤夫见到的五星级酒店风卧室不同，相南里自己居住的地方相当简朴。家具都是东方青帝挑挑拣拣选回来的。虽然也在城堡内，但原本只是一间书房。

书架上摆满了相南里的零件，有些修了一半，有些散落在地上。卧室很小，只有一张单人床，衣服之类的东西都收在床下。

没有客厅和厨房，但有工作台、卫生间以及晾衣服晒太阳的阳台。

相南里推开门回家时，小青的家务活已经快做完了。

平时乱糟糟的宿舍，现在整整齐齐的。

相南里脸上的笑容灿烂：“小青，我回来了~家里好干净，谢谢。”

他走上前，给了东方青帝一个拥抱，随后上下摸了摸：“我看监控全是马赛克，你应该没有受伤吧。小青，挨打你会疼吗？”

嗯，为了保持对外界的敏锐，东方青帝皮肤上有和人类近似的感知元件。不但能自由开关，还可以调整敏感度。

东方青帝思考片刻，回答：“可以关，不会很痛。”

“那就好，不要受伤。我还不知道要怎么修好你。我看了一下审讯记录，罗马城情况和人联给出的资料差不多。过段时间派人去接管，说那么多大道理他们也理解不了，把永恒市里的方式再复刻一次就行。我观察了一下，让学校那个校长去吧，他有经验。刚好，罗马城人也不多。还有军队，派永恒市一半的民兵去。正好最近农闲。”

这次对外战争，除了以西结的援军，城内民兵们的表现也很亮眼。面对远超自己身体素质的狂血战士，没有丝毫的胆怯和退让。

1级小兵们靠着数量和车轮战，硬生生磨死了这批10级基因怪。

战争是最糟糕的外交手段。

攻城又是所有战役里最糟糕的方案。

如果可能，在没有贵族阶级阻碍的情况下，相南里更希望和平接管罗马城。

东方青帝“嗯”了一声，相南里没松手，他也就一直没推开。反而微微调整了一下站姿，能让相南里靠得更舒服一点。

相南里不认为这是侵略。尽管确实造成了一定程度的伤亡。

无论是战争的原因（罗马城想偷袭）、目的（解放农奴）还是手段（精准打击），基地方都相当正义。上人联的军事法庭都没什么掰扯的余地。

当然，就罗马城人均素养，大概都不知道“侵略”这个词怎么读。

相南里越说越困：“其实对于现在的基地来说，接手罗马城的奴隶更像是负担，但没关系。北辰实验室里催生的包菜送来了一批种子，据说产量很高，而且非常耐低温，冬天也能种。

“嗯，监狱里那批人，我看了眼档案，想都杀了，但他们确实还有用，只有想办法改造了。全杀了对后续收编别的据点也会有些影响，那些食利阶层会抵抗得更厉害……小青，你身上好香……”

相南里一夜没合眼，太困。

他眯着眼，靠着东方青帝的肩膀睡着了。

东方青帝微微垂下眼眸，叹了口气，认命地把相南里抱了起来，放到床上。蹲在床边，开始给他脱鞋拖外套。拿湿毛巾擦了擦，然后盖上了被子。

根据小智传回的数据，相南里的状态差不多等于昏迷。现在往他脸上打一拳，只要不太痛，估计也不会醒。

于是，东方青帝拉上窗帘，又关掉床头灯。最后低头，在相南里有些干燥的唇上啄了一口。啄完后感觉有点淡，又没忍住舔了舔。

小智震惊后勃然大怒：[你小子怎么还偷吃！你等着，等相南里醒了我——]

小智话还没说完，又一次失去了宝贵的数据。

*

一直到被关进监狱里，赤夫也不太明白，事情为什么会变成这样。

尤其是在和一起被关进监狱的亚夫交流后。

他们的计划好像很理所当然的完美——内城武器库是花架子，巡逻队兼职民兵，总数量一百出头，里面只有二十多个基因战士。而且赤夫敢打赌，这二十多人里，没一个是父亲的对手。

他们完全可以像以前一样。去几百公里外的据点抢劫，靠强大的身体和充足的火力进行降维打击。最后满载而归，执政官会朝天空开枪庆祝，载满物资的装甲车上，兄弟们一齐载歌载舞。

他们是荒野上横行无忌的飙风，是提起来都忍不住胆寒的悍匪。

但是，基地的人居然能像神庭的人一样，操控畸变体听他们的话。

这群恶心的怪物咬死了他的不少兄弟，幸存者在隔壁牢房特殊看护，抱着自己的残肢，有气无力的哀嚎。

熟悉的血腥味。

在以前是最好兴奋剂，现在却唤醒了赤夫本能的恐惧。

“我们居然输了……”赤夫的牙关打颤，他抱着膝盖，蜷缩在牢房的墙边，脚上戴着沉重的电子镣铐。

赤夫没有见过这种电子锁。金属的，铐在一只脚的脚踝上。摘不下来，有一个黑匣子贴着小腿。

他被迫戴上的时候，胆颤心惊的问了一句，里面是不是有炸药，对方扫了他一眼，没有回答，只是意味不明地笑了一下，回了句：“别摘喔。”

很快有人以身试法，在想拆除这个电子锁的时候，下场就是被电到口吐白沫，不省人事。

这个电子锁是相南里设计的。里面有高压电极管，和蛇夫座身上用的是同款。只不过电压要小很多。

电子锁的原材料较为昂贵，基地里的库存不多，因此，相南里只挑了部分一看就不老实的人戴上。

果然，第一天就有人中招。当着所有人的面被拖走了。

电熟的人糊糊的，散发出一股原生态的烤肉味，很安心。

躁动的牢房果然安静了很多。

而等到蛇夫座睡醒，出来溜圈，畸形恐怖的双头蛇人慢吞吞地从牢房门口路过，大家就变得更安静了。
chunks.englishText:
**Chapter 100: Reforming the Roman Aristocracy**

He returned to his dormitory and took a shower, meticulously scrubbing away every trace of blood and grime from his skin. He didn’t forget to spritz on the light perfume he had purchased back in Gusu City.

Reason told him it was unwise to waste precious battery power on such trivialities, but his calculations indicated a 99 percent probability that Xiang Nanli would enjoy this scent—a rich, lingering note of freesia.

Dongfang Qingdi had heard that certain male big cats, when seeking a mate, would specifically seek out wild silvervine to roll in, hoping the scent would entice a female.

It seemed that, in the natural world, the methods of male courtship were universal.

A beautiful appearance and a powerful physique.

Dongfang Qingdi changed into fresh clothes, dried his hair with a hairdryer, and hung the laundry from the washing machine. While he was at it, he gathered the clothes Xiang Nanli had left hanging on the balcony, folded them neatly, and tucked them into the wardrobe. Then, with practiced ease, he reached for the broom and mop. His movements were fluid and natural, executed in one seamless flow.

In Dongfang Qingdi’s view, there was no hierarchy between doing housework and building a nuclear bomb; both were simply forms of human labor. Yet, humans tended to measure such labor by the value it created, automatically categorizing tasks into "high" and "low" in their minds.

Within such a value system, the irreplaceable affection one person held for another—hidden beneath the tedium of chores—was always overlooked. It seemed that, to most, it simply didn't matter.

For Dongfang Qingdi, however, maintaining the comfort of Xiang Nanli’s living environment was more important than manufacturing ten nuclear warheads.

Unlike the five-star hotel-style bedroom Chifu had envisioned, the place where Xiang Nanli actually lived was remarkably spartan. The furniture had all been hand-picked by Dongfang Qingdi. Although located within the castle, the space had originally been nothing more than a study.

The bookshelves were crammed with Xiang Nanli’s spare parts—some half-repaired, others scattered across the floor. The bedroom was tiny, containing only a single bed, with clothing and other personal effects stowed away underneath. There was no living room or kitchen, only a workbench, a bathroom, and a balcony for drying clothes and soaking up the sun.

When Xiang Nanli pushed open the door to return home, Xiao Qing was just finishing up the chores. The dormitory, usually a chaotic mess, was now impeccably tidy.

A brilliant smile lit up Xiang Nanli’s face. "Xiao Qing, I’m home! The place is so clean—thank you."

He stepped forward and wrapped Dongfang Qingdi in a hug, then began patting him down, checking him over. "I checked the surveillance footage, but it was all pixelated. You weren't hurt, were you? Xiao Qing, does it hurt when you get hit?"

Indeed, to maintain a keen awareness of the outside world, Dongfang Qingdi’s skin was equipped with sensory components similar to those of a human. Not only could they be toggled on and off at will, but their sensitivity could also be adjusted.

Dongfang Qingdi pondered for a moment before replying, "I can turn them off. It doesn't hurt much."

"That’s good. Don’t get hurt—I haven’t the faintest idea how to repair you yet. I’ve gone over the interrogation reports, and the situation in Rome is much as the United Front’s intel suggested. We’ll send a team to take over in a while. They won't understand all those high-minded theories, so we’ll just replicate the system we used in Eternal City. I’ve given it some thought; send the headmaster from the academy. He has the experience, and Rome doesn't have a large population anyway. As for the military, send half the Eternal City militia. It’s the off-season for farming, so the timing is perfect."

In this foreign campaign, aside from Ezekiel’s reinforcements, the city’s militia had performed remarkably well. Facing Blood-Berserkers whose physical stats far eclipsed their own, they hadn't shown a shred of cowardice or retreat.

The Level 1 grunts had relied on sheer numbers and attrition tactics to grind those Level 10 genetic monsters into the dirt.

War is the worst form of diplomacy.
And a siege is the worst possible strategy in any campaign.

If it were possible—and provided there were no aristocratic factions standing in the way—Xiang Nanli would have much preferred a peaceful annexation of Rome.

Dongfang Qingdi let out a soft "Mn." Xiang Nanli didn't let go, so he didn't push her away. Instead, he subtly adjusted his stance, making it more comfortable for her to lean against him.

Xiang Nanli didn't consider this an invasion. Even if it had, admittedly, resulted in a certain degree of casualties.

Whether it was the casus belli (Rome’s attempt at a sneak attack), the objective (liberating the serfs), or the methodology (precision strikes), the Base’s position was undeniably righteous. Even before a United Human Federation military tribunal, there would be little room to argue otherwise.

Of course, given the average level of education in Rome, they probably didn’t even know how to spell the word "aggression."

Xiang Nanli’s voice grew drowsy as he spoke. "Actually, for the Base right now, taking in Rome’s slaves is more of a burden than anything else, but it doesn't matter. Beichen Laboratory just sent over a batch of seeds for their genetically accelerated cabbage. They say the yield is massive, and it’s highly cold-resistant—it can even grow through the winter."

"As for those people in the prison... I glanced at their files. I wanted to have them all executed, but they’re still useful. I’ll have to find a way to reform them. Killing them all would complicate the integration of other strongholds; the parasitic elite classes would only resist more fiercely... Xiao Qing, you smell so good..."

Xiang Nanli hadn't closed his eyes all night, and he was beyond exhausted.

He squinted, leaned his head against Dongfang Qingdi’s shoulder, and drifted off to sleep.

Dongfang Qingdi lowered his gaze slightly and sighed. Resigned to his fate, he scooped Xiang Nanli up and carried him to the bed. He knelt by the bedside, carefully removing Xiang Nanli’s shoes and coat. After wiping his face with a damp towel, he tucked him under the covers.

According to the data transmitted back by Xiao Zhi, Xiang Nanli’s current state was practically a coma. You could probably punch him in the face right now, and as long as it wasn't too painful, he wouldn't even wake up.

With that, the Azure Emperor of the East drew the curtains and clicked off the bedside lamp. Finally, he leaned down and pressed a quick peck to Xiang Nanli’s slightly chapped lips. Finding the taste a bit bland, he couldn't help but give them a lingering lick.

Xiao Zhi, after a moment of pure shock, flew into a rage: *[You little brat, how dare you sneak a snack! Just you wait, once Xiang Nanli wakes up, I’m going to—]*

Before Xiao Zhi could finish his sentence, he once again lost his precious data.

*

Even after being thrown into prison, Chifu still couldn't quite grasp how things had spiraled out of control.

Especially after comparing notes with Yafu, who had been locked up right alongside him.

Their plan had seemed perfectly logical, practically foolproof. The inner city’s armory was nothing but a hollow shell, and the patrol squads were just glorified militiamen—barely over a hundred in total, with only twenty-odd gene-warriors among them. And Chifu would bet his life that not a single one of those twenty could hold a candle to his father.

They should have been able to do what they always did: raid outposts hundreds of kilometers away, using their superior physiques and heavy firepower to crush the opposition with ease. They should have returned home laden with spoils, with the Magistrate firing shots into the air in celebration, while the brothers danced and sang atop armored vehicles overflowing with supplies.

They were the gale-force winds that rampaged across the wasteland, the ruthless bandits whose very names struck terror into the hearts of men.

But who could have guessed that the people in this base could command aberrations just like the ones from the Divine Court?

This pack of wretched monsters had mauled many of his brothers to death. The survivors were being kept under "special observation" in the adjacent cells, cradling their severed limbs and wailing with listless, broken cries.

The familiar stench of blood.

In the past, it would have been the ultimate stimulant, but now, it only stirred a primal, instinctive terror within Chi Fu.

"We actually lost..." Chi Fu’s teeth chattered. He huddled against the cell wall with his knees pulled to his chest, his ankles weighed down by heavy electronic shackles.

Chi Fu had never seen such locks before. They were metallic, clamped tight around his ankle, impossible to remove, with a small black box pressed flush against his shin.

When he had been forced to wear it, he’d asked with trembling breath if there was an explosive inside. The guard had merely glanced at him, offered no answer, and let out an inscrutable laugh before saying, "Don't try to take it off."

Soon enough, someone had learned the hard way. The moment they tried to dismantle the device, they were met with a high-voltage shock that left them foaming at the mouth and unconscious.

These electronic locks were designed by Xiang Nanli. They contained high-voltage electrode tubes—the same model used on the Ophiuchus subjects, though the voltage was dialed down significantly.

Because the raw materials for these shackles were expensive and the base’s inventory was limited, Xiang Nanli had only selected those who looked like they wouldn't play nice to wear them.

Sure enough, someone had fallen for the trap on the very first day. They were dragged away in front of everyone, a grim warning to the rest.

The charred remains smelled of scorched meat—a raw, primal scent that was strangely comforting.

The restless prison block had finally quieted down.

And when the Ophiuchus woke up to take a stroll, the sight of that grotesque, two-headed serpent-man slithering sluggishly past their cell doors made the silence even more profound.

chunks.chapterTitle: 第100章 罗马城贵族的改造 (Part 2)
chunks.chineseText:
天狼星的眼神还好。有些空洞和木然，像没有灵魂的人偶。看久了甚至有些恐怖谷。

而蛇夫座，那分明就是很饿想吃饭的眼神。

赤夫曾经在郊外遇到过狼。他们几个人重伤，又没等来支援。狼群围绕着它们，一直尾随着，守了三天两夜。最后，是另一个哥哥赶来救援，狼群才兴致怏怏地离开。

那时候，那些狼看他，也是这样的眼神。像在考虑一盘菜要从哪里下口。

蛇夫座的目光在牢房的人脸上扫过，被盯着的人汗毛竖起。

蛇夫座吐了吐蛇信子，不是很满意相南里送来的新邻居，但因为打不过东方青帝，只好慢吞吞地游走了。

赤夫在牢里呆了一天一夜，这里光又弱，还没有水。

有人大小便失禁了，散发出一股怪味。

也不知道过了多久，两名巡逻队员拎着一桶馒头走了进来。牢房里有六十多个人，饿了好几天。馒头只有四五十个，显然是不够分的。

送餐的人什么也没说，丢下一桶馒头走了。

“这样做的目的是分化。资源足够的时候，他们以执政官为核心，血缘为纽带，亲如一家。但我们不需要铁板一块的家族。”

这样持续了十几天，狂血战士们都饿得不成人形。

他们的身体消耗本来就大，一开始，大家还能商量分着吃，到后来，恨不得一人独占。

赤夫年轻的时候伤了身体，现在抢饭又抢不过人家。没有人在乎谁是哥哥，谁是弟弟。只在乎自己能不能吃饱。

更恐怖的是，他们都是吃过两脚羊肉的。

赤夫最近夜里总睡不好，因为同样饥饿的亚夫总是在夜晚时，一动不动地盯着他。

所以，当巡逻队的人说，需要一批人干活、并且管饭的时候，赤夫第一个举起了手。

他们的工作是铺设电网。赤夫被带去洗了个澡，然后换上了一件显眼的橙色马褂，被丢进了一个10人小组。

除了他，其他人的马褂都是蓝色的。

小组的领队是永恒市的原住民，叫肉桂。也是巡逻队的成员之一。

肉桂说，他们是永恒市第一批“基建队”。

每个小组11人，组长是巡逻队队员，剩下9人，则是永恒市、罗马城还有光辉市里挑出来的“工人”，都是身体较为强壮的良家子，有工资拿。还有1人，是像赤夫这样的劳改犯。

肉桂接受过培训，对赤夫并没有特殊对待，就像是不知道他身份一样。他先是自费1工分券，带赤夫去食堂吃了顿饭。赤夫一口气干了五六碗，一边吃一边哭。

像他这样的劳改犯，还有三十多个。他们被发配到了郊区建设电网。

一共四百余人，在冰天雪地里开始挖地道，安装电缆。希望能抢在冬日的第一场暴雪来临前，把电网铺好。

基建队的技术顾问是小王。一个有些学院派的严肃小男孩。戴着电子镜片，表面不苟言笑，实际上只是有点呆。

他不擅长教书，是实干派。每次遇到问题，求助他基本都能得到解决。

而小王遇到解决不了的问题，就会发给相南里。

小王听易横行老师说，相南里是解冻人，掌握的技术比较落后，让他们这批大学生多教教他。

但实际操作下来，小王觉得，易横行和相南里总有一个在撒谎……

考虑到相南里看起来热情又质朴，他怀疑是易横行在撒谎。

穿橙马甲的人都是劳改犯，在雪地上很显眼，目的是为了防止他们逃跑。

但这批人真的逃走，相南里也不是很在意。

一群狂血战士确实有些难搞。但一个？算了吧。

赤夫的身体素质强悍，干活总是又快又好，频频让小队得到大队的表扬。每周，能额外领到1个鸡蛋的加餐。

小队成员对他也逐渐热情起来。

赤夫和他们同吃同睡，晚上在同一个帐篷。基地还派了老师过来，给他们上扫盲课。考虑到劳作辛苦，课程每两天一次，每次半天。第一节是基础课，必须听。上课时间是下午，这段时间可以不用干活。第二节则是选修，在晚上。

赤夫不算文盲，对这些东西不是很感兴趣。但肉桂却很执着，每次都拉着赤夫一起学。

课堂里，除了最基础的扫盲，还会教一些郊外生存急救技巧。比如怎么把东西收纳到最小，方便装进包里带走；野外遇到不同的异种用什么策略应对。

赤夫有些意外。因为这些都是他们多次出生入死的经验，没想到基地的人居然能免费学到。他难免有些羡慕。

如果一开始就有人教他们这些知识，那么7岁时，他的姐姐不会因为误食蘑菇中毒死去；他的哥哥也不会在22岁时成为残废，失去狂血战士的资格，从贵族沦为平民。

修电缆到第二个月的时候，基地送来了教科书。课本是光辉市的工厂印刷的。

赤夫震惊地在“地表野外生存指南”这本书的课本上，看见了自己几个叔叔的名字。他们的名字在顾问那一栏。

赤夫在帐篷里，点着灯，摸着那几行字，心想，这应该不是同名同姓。

书上教的知识他可太耳熟了。

这段时间，有狂血战士成功逃走过。赤夫不知道他们的下场，但他已经听说，罗马城被永恒市接管了，现在叫“幸存者基地下辖永恒区罗马镇”。

去投靠别的势力，当朝不保夕的悍匪，真的会有现在的生活安定、幸福吗？

越是融入基地，接受基地的理念，赤夫就越发厌恶之前的生活，甚至不敢面对过去的自己。

他甚至有意疏远起别的橙马褂，就怕想起一些不堪的往事。

肉桂和几个工友上完晚课回来了，赤夫下意识地把课本塞进枕头底下，装睡。

肉桂掀开帐篷，摇了摇他的身体。

赤夫装作刚醒，迷迷糊糊应了声。下一秒，肉桂塞了颗巧克力到他的怀里：“拿着吧，这次的标兵小组奖励。我们组的电缆三分之一都是你铺完的。”

他们组分到的地方很差，是一片山坡。电缆要架在悬崖上，看着都发愁。

但这却是可行度最高的方案了。

赤夫仗着自己是狂血战士，脱掉马甲，解开基因锁，直接抱着电缆杆子爬了下去。工作完成的相当出色。

这也是他今天没去上课的原因。太累了。身体储存的能量跟不上自己的新陈代谢。

肉桂又继续道：“我问了大队长，可不可以让你穿蓝马褂。大队长答应了。我听说，这次队里有5年的减刑指标。”

他没有多说别的话，更没有保证什么。

“嗯，嗯。”一向能言善辩的赤夫木讷地回答着。

罗马城活下来的贵族都被判刑了。刑期在70年到140年不等，还有一批直接死刑。

赤夫紧紧握住那颗巧克力，翻了个身，心想，就这样吧。

他生来就是恶鬼，每一个毛孔里都流着罪恶的血。但有机会当人，为什么还要当鬼呢？
chunks.englishText:
Sirius’s gaze was unsettling—vacant and wooden, like a doll devoid of a soul. If one stared long enough, it even triggered a sense of the uncanny valley.

As for Ophiuchus, his gaze was unmistakably that of a starving beast looking for a meal.

Chifu had once encountered wolves in the wilderness. Back then, he and his companions were severely wounded, waiting in vain for reinforcements. The pack had circled them, trailing them for three days and two nights. It wasn't until another brother arrived to rescue them that the wolves, looking disappointed, finally slinked away.

Back then, those wolves had looked at him with the exact same eyes—as if calculating which part of the dish to bite into first.

Ophiuchus’s gaze swept across the faces of those in the cell, making the hair on the back of their necks stand up. He flicked his forked tongue, clearly dissatisfied with the new neighbors Xiang Nanli had sent over. However, unable to best the Eastern Azure Emperor in a fight, he eventually slithered away, slow and languid.

Chifu had been in the cell for a day and a night. The light was dim, and there was no water. Someone had lost control of their bowels, filling the air with a foul stench.

It was hard to tell how much time had passed when two patrol members walked in, carrying a bucket of steamed buns. There were over sixty people in the cell, all starving for days. There were only forty or fifty buns—clearly not enough to go around.

The men delivering the food said nothing; they simply dropped the bucket and left.

"The purpose of doing this is to divide them. When resources are abundant, they center themselves around their magistrates, bound by blood, as close as family. But we have no need for an impenetrable, monolithic clan."

This continued for over ten days until the Blood-Berserkers were starved to the point of being unrecognizable. Their bodies required immense caloric intake; at first, they had managed to divide the food, but eventually, everyone grew desperate to claim a share for themselves.

Chifu had injured his body in his youth, and now he couldn't compete with the others for food. No one cared who was the elder brother or who was the younger; they only cared about filling their own stomachs.

What was even more terrifying was that they were all people who had tasted "two-legged mutton" (human flesh) before.

Chifu hadn't been sleeping well lately, because Yaofu, equally starved, would stare at him motionlessly throughout the night.

Therefore, when the patrol team announced they needed people for labor—with meals provided—Chifu was the first to raise his hand.

Their job was to lay power grids. Chifu was taken to bathe, then issued a conspicuous orange vest and tossed into a ten-man squad. Everyone else wore blue.

The squad leader was a native of Eternal City named Rougui, who was also a member of the patrol team. Rougui explained that they were the first batch of "Infrastructure Teams" in Eternal City.

Each squad consisted of eleven people: the leader from the patrol, nine "workers" selected from Eternal City, Rome City, and Glory City—all sturdy, decent folk who received wages—and one convict like Chifu.

Rougui had undergone training and treated Chifu no differently, as if he were unaware of his status. He even spent one of his own work-point vouchers to take Chifu to the canteen for a meal. Chifu inhaled five or six bowls in one sitting, weeping as he ate.

There were over thirty convicts like him, all dispatched to the outskirts to build the power grid.

Over four hundred people began digging tunnels and installing cables in the freezing snow, hoping to finish before the first blizzard of winter struck.

The technical consultant for the infrastructure team was Xiao Wang—a serious, somewhat academic young boy. He wore electronic lenses and appeared stern, though in reality, he was just a bit dense. He wasn't good at teaching; he was a man of action. Whenever they encountered a problem, he could usually solve it. If he couldn't, he would forward the issue to Xiang Nanli.

Xiao Wang had heard from Teacher Yi Hengxing that Xiang Nanli was a "thawed" man whose technical knowledge was quite outdated, and that they, the university students, should teach him a thing or two. But in practice, Xiao Wang felt that either Yi Hengxing or Xiang Nanli was lying... and given how warm and simple Xiang Nanli seemed, he suspected it was Yi Hengxing.

Those in orange vests were convicts, making them highly visible against the snow to prevent escape. But Xiang Nanli didn't really care if this group tried to run. A group of Blood-Berserkers might be troublesome, but one? Forget it.

Chifu’s physical constitution was formidable. He worked fast and well, frequently earning his squad praise from the main team. Every week, he received an extra egg as a reward. The squad members gradually grew warmer toward him.

Chifu ate and slept with them in the same tent. The base even sent teachers to provide literacy classes. Considering the grueling labor, classes were held every two days for half a day. The first session was a mandatory basic course, held in the afternoon, during which they were excused from work. The second was an elective, held at night.

Chifu wasn't illiterate, and he wasn't particularly interested in these things. But Rougui was persistent, always dragging Chifu along to learn.

In class, beyond basic literacy, they taught wilderness survival and first-aid skills—how to pack items into the smallest possible space for transport, or what strategies to use when encountering different types of mutants in the wild.

Chifu was surprised. These were lessons learned through life-and-death experiences, yet here, they were taught for free. He couldn't help but feel a pang of envy. If someone had taught them this knowledge from the start, his sister wouldn't have died from eating poisonous mushrooms at age seven, and his brother wouldn't have become a cripple at twenty-two, losing his status as a Blood-Berserker and falling from nobility to commoner.

By the second month of cable laying, the base delivered textbooks. They were printed in the factories of Glory City. Chifu was shocked to see the names of his own uncles in the "Surface Wilderness Survival Guide" textbook, listed under the consultants' section.

Lying in his tent, lighting a lamp and tracing those lines of text with his fingers, Chifu thought, *This can't be a coincidence of names.*

The knowledge in the book was all too familiar to him.

During this time, some Blood-Berserkers had successfully escaped. Chifu didn't know their fate, but he had heard that Rome City had been taken over by Eternal City and was now called "Rome Town, Eternal District, under the jurisdiction of the Survivor Base."

Would defecting to other factions and living as precarious, desperate bandits really offer a life as stable and happy as this?

The more he integrated into the base and accepted its philosophy, the more Chifu loathed his former life, to the point where he couldn't bear to face his past self. He even began to intentionally distance himself from the other orange vests, fearing the memories of those sordid days.

Rougui and a few workers returned from their night class. Chifu instinctively shoved the textbook under his pillow and feigned sleep.

Rougui lifted the tent flap and shook him. Chifu pretended to just be waking up, responding with a mumble. The next second, Rougui pressed a piece of chocolate into his hand. "Take it. It’s the reward for the model squad. You laid a third of our squad's cables yourself."

The area their squad was assigned was terrible—a mountainside where the cables had to be strung across a cliff. It looked daunting, but it was the most feasible route. Chifu, relying on his Blood-Berserker constitution, had stripped off his vest, unlocked his genetic shackles, and climbed down while clutching the cable pole. He had done an outstanding job. That was why he hadn't gone to class today; he was too exhausted. The energy stored in his body couldn't keep up with his metabolism.

Rougui continued, "I asked the squad leader if you could wear a blue vest. He agreed. I heard there’s a five-year sentence reduction quota for the team this time."

He didn't say anything else, nor did he make any promises.

"Mm, mm," Chifu, usually eloquent, replied woodenly.

The surviving nobles of Rome City had all been sentenced. Terms ranged from seventy to one hundred and forty years, with a batch receiving the death penalty.

Chifu gripped the chocolate tightly and rolled over, thinking, *Let it be.*

He was born a demon, with sinful blood flowing through every pore. But if there was a chance to be a human, why would he choose to be a demon?

chunks.chapterTitle: 第101章 来自阴山城的求援 (Part 1)
chunks.chineseText:
第101章 来自阴山城的求援

两个多月过去，衣柜里除了当初从神庭骑士那打劫的几套礼服，家里还多了不少便装。

他的房间依然乱糟糟的，甚至没有床。以西结平时睡觉盘在地上，头可以枕自己的大尾巴。

今天要去上课。上一次，相南里说，他们马上要回基地了，这会是最后一节识字课。

以西结犹豫片刻，还是挑选了一件偏向日常的衣着。

他顺着树洞爬了出去，外面下雪了。整个森林银装素裹，树干的颜色黑压压的。

在以西结住着的树干周围，伐出了一片宽阔的空地。树都是以一种蛮力给撞断的，原地只剩下一个光秃秃的树桩，偶尔，小畸变体们会用这些树桩磨牙和爪子。

大大小小的畸变体围绕着最中心这棵巨树盘卧。头顶用塑料布，搭设出了一个温室大棚。

现在是畸变体的冬眠时间，它们一天中有23小时都在睡觉；不吃不喝不运动，以降低身体的消耗。这是食物短缺时的应急策略。

如今，族群一共有27只畸变体。

以西结摸了摸离自己最近的一只畸变体，这只叫白斑，身长3米。有些瘦弱。它是一只狂暴者，外观长得很像希伯来。

对于人类来说，畸变体长相都差不多。但畸变人自己却可以分清楚那些细微的差别。

以西结已经很少回忆起当年一起关在实验室的那些同伴了，并不是他薄情，只是沉浸在痛苦和回忆的生活不值得过。

白斑在梦里闻到了以西结的气味，闭着眼，用头拱了拱以西结的手。蹭了一手黏糊糊的肉屑。

以西结的唇角忍不住微微扬起一点。

在所有畸变体种类里，狂暴者的体型是最大的。正常情况下起码有10米。

自然状态下，白斑这样瘦小的狂暴者，很难活到成年。但现在，因为有稳定的食物来源，它也能度过一个温暖的冬天。

以西结为此感觉到了骄傲。

牧场扩建了一点，北辰改良了一些菌牛品种，又用抑制剂让菌牛的传染性进一步降低。总之，畸变体们暂时不用担心食物匮乏了。

在地表，它们本该是强者。但能生存下来的并非强者，而是适者。庞大的身躯意味着海量的消耗，每头畸变体同样在为活下去而拼尽全力。

族群里长得最胖的还是小红。

地表资源不足，自私应该是所有人的天性。

小红占据了离大树最近的位置，这里也是最暖和的地方。它用身体绕了树干一圈。剩下的畸变体都贴着它睡。

“你出来了？”沙利叶的声音有些揶揄，他靠在树桩上，双手抱胸，“又要去见老相好？这都几个月了，还没拿下吗？”

听到他的话，以西结有些不悦地蹙起眉，但又懒得解释。

沙利叶先是在树洞了被关了小半年，最近一个月，才取得了外出放风的时间。但不能走出森林中心，所有畸变体都在以西结的命令下监控着他。

当初，那么严重的伤势，沙利叶居然靠着自愈能力恢复了，不愧是神殿的领主级骑士。

据说神庭的撒旦级骑士被核弹轰一下都还能谈笑风生，是真正的人间兵器。可惜暂时没有人试过。

在不切换到“相晨曦”状态时，以西结对沙利叶其实没有那么反感。

沙利叶教了他很多事。

而且，似乎是发现以西结对历史和地理相当感兴趣，沙利特经常主动提起这些东西，试图刷一下以西结的好感度。

可惜，相南里上课时也会讲。让以西结对他的小把戏产生了极强的免疫力。同样的知识，从相南里嘴里说出来就很深入浅出，清晰明了；而沙利叶喜欢说一半留一半。

但也有些事，是相南里教不了的。

比如神庭对于畸变体的研究。神庭饲养畸变体数百年，教会里的祭司人均兽医。

沙利叶在温室大棚里给自己搭了个人窝，里面家具都是木头做的。有床、书桌。

多亏了那些罗马城战俘，电网建设比预想中快得多，赶在有人冻死前竣工了。居民生活质量有了显著提升，起码再也不用担心晚上睡过去醒不过来了。

得益于电网的建设，造纸工厂重新开始了工作。印的最多的就是教程，以西结带回来了一本，现在就放在沙利叶的书桌上。

沙利叶没有见过相南里，但他对基地那位司令的评价是这样的：现实的理想主义者。

说他是理想主义者，是因为明明有更好的统治策略，而相南里却选择了“正确”，而不是“方便”。

永恒市是农业区，明明需要人种田，他却妄图让所有人都有机会成为知识分子。可这些人，原本该是听话劳动力的人，学了那么多知识，回头看着自己家的一亩三分地，真的不会心有不甘吗？

神庭当然知道封建神学、政教合一的制度是落后的。

当然知道，但是这样方便。强大的意志凝聚在一起，无数凡人自己造出来一尊统御四方的神。

相南里在书里写的东西，放在神庭的辖区，是会被当成邪教禁书烧了的。

他身上现实的地方就更明显了，看永恒市蒸蒸日上的状态就知道了。

沙利叶想，给基地一点时间，以后神庭在地表必然会多一个强势到极点的对手。可惜他被关押在这，没办法通风报信。

沙利叶当时受伤太严重，又失去了赖以生存的生物机甲。现在的战斗力和强化的基因战士差不多。根本不是以西结的对手。

以西结对他处于一种半放养的状态，但沙利叶清楚，他只有一次逃跑的机会。结局要么逃出生天，要么死。

见以西结不搭话，沙利叶熟练得举起晒干藤蔓裹成的磨牙棒，给沉睡中的畸变体们挨个磨起了爪子和牙齿。

这根磨牙棒有沙利叶人这么高。他干活非常娴熟，甚至心情还算愉快地哼起了神庭的礼赞歌。

哼着哼着，沙利叶的表情突然变了一下，他的神色更加温柔，用一种亲切地声音叫着：“以西结。等等。”

相晨曦转头回到小木屋，从里面拿出一捧干花，都是相晨曦从森林里采的。晒干后，颜色依然鲜艳动人。

“去见喜欢的人要带花。”

相晨曦不愧当过几十年的圣子，举止看上去亲切又自然。他似乎天然有一种魔力，能让人产生出好感。

可惜沙利叶的身体偏向壮汉，效果顿时大打折扣。

以西结下意识地反驳：“我不喜欢。”

但相晨曦只是微笑不语。

以西结想了想，还是接了过来。他的背影消失在了森林中。

以西结走后，相晨曦的表情开始扭曲起来。

他站在原地，一个人对用着两种截然不同的表情和语调对话，像极了多重人格的分裂期患者。

“还要在这里待多久？！我要回神庭，沙利叶！”

“现在还不是时候。”沙利叶对付相晨曦的发疯很有经验，此时还能耐着性子安慰一下。

相晨曦崩溃地蹲在地上：“我不管，我今天就要回去！这里好恶心。我讨厌这些怪物。”
chunks.englishText:
Chapter 101: A Plea for Help from Yinshan City (Part 1)

More than two months had passed. Aside from the few formal outfits he had looted from the Divine Court knights, his wardrobe now held quite a few casual clothes.

His room remained a chaotic mess, lacking even a bed. Ezekiel usually slept curled up on the floor, using his own large tail as a pillow.

Today was a day for class. Last time, Xiang Nanli had mentioned that they would soon be returning to the base, and this would be their final literacy lesson.

Ezekiel hesitated for a moment before selecting an outfit that leaned toward the casual side.

He crawled out through the tree hollow; it was snowing outside. The entire forest was draped in silver, the tree trunks standing out in stark, oppressive black.

A wide clearing had been cleared around the tree where Ezekiel lived. The trees had been snapped by brute force, leaving only bare stumps behind. Occasionally, the smaller aberrants would use these stumps to sharpen their teeth and claws.

Aberrants of all sizes lay coiled around this central giant tree. Overhead, a greenhouse had been constructed using plastic sheeting.

It was currently the hibernation period for the aberrants. They slept for 23 hours a day, neither eating, drinking, nor moving, to minimize their body's energy consumption. It was an emergency strategy for times of food shortage.

Currently, the tribe consisted of 27 aberrants.

Ezekiel stroked the aberrant closest to him. This one was named White Spot, three meters in length and somewhat thin. It was a Berserker, and its appearance was quite similar to Hebrew.

To humans, all aberrants looked more or less the same, but the aberrants themselves could distinguish the subtle differences.

Ezekiel rarely recalled the companions he had been locked in the laboratory with back then. It wasn't that he was cold-hearted; it was simply that a life immersed in pain and memories was not worth living.

In its dream, White Spot caught the scent of Ezekiel. With its eyes closed, it nudged Ezekiel’s hand with its head, leaving a smear of sticky meat scraps on his palm.

The corners of Ezekiel’s mouth couldn't help but lift slightly.

Among all types of aberrants, Berserkers had the largest builds. Under normal circumstances, they reached at least ten meters.

In the wild, a thin Berserker like White Spot would struggle to survive to adulthood. But now, thanks to a stable food source, it would be able to make it through a warm winter.

Ezekiel felt a sense of pride in this.

The ranch had expanded slightly. Beichen had improved some of the fungus-cow breeds and used inhibitors to further reduce their infectiousness. In short, the aberrants no longer had to worry about food scarcity for the time being.

On the surface, they should have been the strong ones. But those who survived were not necessarily the strongest; they were the most adaptable. A massive body meant massive consumption, and every aberrant was also fighting with all its might just to stay alive.

The fattest one in the tribe was still Little Red.

With surface resources scarce, selfishness should be everyone’s nature.

Little Red occupied the spot closest to the giant tree, which was also the warmest place. It wrapped its body around the trunk, and the remaining aberrants slept pressed against it.

"You're heading out?" Saliel’s voice held a hint of mockery. He leaned against a tree stump, arms crossed. "Going to see your old flame again? It’s been months—haven't you sealed the deal yet?"

Hearing this, Ezekiel frowned in displeasure, but he was too lazy to explain.

Saliel had been locked in the tree hollow for nearly half a year, and only in the last month had he been granted time to go outside for fresh air. However, he could not leave the center of the forest, and all the aberrants monitored him under Ezekiel’s orders.

Despite such severe injuries, Saliel had actually recovered thanks to his self-healing ability; he was truly worthy of being a Lord-level knight of the Divine Court.

It was said that a Satan-level knight of the Divine Court could still chat and laugh even after being hit by a nuclear bomb—they were true weapons of the world. Unfortunately, no one had tested that yet.

When not switched to the "Xiang Chenxi" state, Ezekiel didn't actually dislike Saliel that much.

Saliel had taught him many things.

Moreover, seemingly having discovered that Ezekiel was quite interested in history and geography, Saliel often took the initiative to bring these topics up, attempting to earn some favor with Ezekiel.

Unfortunately, Xiang Nanli also covered these topics during class, which had made Ezekiel highly immune to Saliel’s little tricks. The same knowledge, when spoken by Xiang Nanli, was always simple, clear, and easy to understand, whereas Saliel liked to say half and leave half out.

But there were some things Xiang Nanli couldn't teach.

For instance, the Divine Court’s research on aberrants. The Divine Court had been raising aberrants for hundreds of years; every priest in the church was essentially a veterinarian.

Saliel had built himself a personal nest inside the greenhouse, with furniture made of wood—a bed and a desk.

Thanks to those Roman prisoners of war, the power grid construction had been much faster than expected, finishing just before anyone froze to death. The quality of life for the residents had improved significantly; at the very least, they no longer had to worry about going to sleep at night and never waking up.

Benefiting from the power grid, the paper mill had resumed work. The most printed items were tutorials, and Ezekiel had brought one back; it was currently sitting on Saliel’s desk.

Saliel had never met Xiang Nanli, but his assessment of the base’s commander was this: a realistic idealist.

He called him an idealist because, despite having better strategies for rule, Xiang Nanli chose what was "right" rather than what was "convenient."

Eternal City was an agricultural zone. Even though they needed people to farm, he harbored the delusion of giving everyone a chance to become an intellectual. But these people, who were originally meant to be obedient labor, once they learned so much knowledge and looked back at their own small plots of land, would they really not feel resentful?

The Divine Court, of course, knew that feudal theology and the integration of church and state were backward.

They knew, of course, but it was convenient. Powerful wills were gathered together, and countless mortals created a god to rule over all directions.

The things Xiang Nanli wrote in his books would be burned as heretical texts if they were found in the Divine Court’s jurisdiction.

The realistic side of him was even more obvious—one only had to look at the thriving state of Eternal City to see it.

Saliel thought that if the base were given time, the Divine Court would inevitably face a formidable opponent on the surface. Unfortunately, he was imprisoned here and had no way to send word.

Saliel had been too severely injured at the time and had lost his bio-mecha, which he relied on for survival. His current combat power was about the same as an enhanced gene-warrior. He was no match for Ezekiel at all.

Ezekiel kept him in a state of semi-captivity, but Saliel knew he only had one chance to escape. The outcome would be either freedom or death.

Seeing that Ezekiel didn't respond, Saliel skillfully picked up a teething stick made of dried vines and began to sharpen the claws and teeth of the sleeping aberrants one by one.

This teething stick was as tall as Saliel himself. He worked with great proficiency, even humming a Divine Court hymn with a relatively pleasant mood.

As he hummed, Saliel’s expression suddenly changed. His demeanor became gentler, and he called out in an affectionate voice: "Ezekiel. Wait."

Xiang Chenxi turned back into the small wooden cabin and took out a bouquet of dried flowers—all of which Xiang Chenxi had picked in the forest. Even after being dried, the colors remained vibrant and moving.

"You should bring flowers when going to see someone you like."

Xiang Chenxi was worthy of having been a Holy Son for decades; his manners appeared natural and intimate. He seemed to possess a natural magic that could make people feel favorably toward him.

Unfortunately, Saliel’s body leaned toward that of a brawny man, so the effect was greatly diminished.

Ezekiel subconsciously retorted: "I don't like him."

But Xiang Chenxi only smiled without a word.

Ezekiel thought for a moment, then took them anyway. His back disappeared into the forest.

After Ezekiel left, Xiang Chenxi’s expression began to twist.

He stood where he was, one person conversing with two completely different expressions and tones, looking exactly like a patient in the midst of a multiple personality split.

"How much longer do I have to stay here?! I want to go back to the Divine Court, Saliel!"

"Now is not the time." Saliel was experienced in dealing with Xiang Chenxi’s madness and was able to patiently comfort him.

Xiang Chenxi collapsed onto the ground: "I don't care, I want to go back today! This place is disgusting. I hate these monsters."

chunks.chapterTitle: 第101章 来自阴山城的求援 (Part 2)
chunks.chineseText:
这一点，沙利叶其实知道。

神庭的圣子必须具备的一个素养，那就是能和非人物种沟通。

为了训练这些候选人，他们从小就会被丢进畸变体巢穴里，这个阶段会持续整整一年。活下来的才有资格进入后面的程序。

死在这一轮的候选人是最多的。相晨曦虽然是幸存者，但很难控制自己对畸变体的厌恶和恐惧。只是为了生存，他把这一点藏的很好。

沙利叶会发现，是因为之前一次解开基因锁，还没来得及恢复。相晨曦看见后直接崩溃到大哭。

沙利叶又耐着性子安慰了几句，但相晨曦依然哭闹不止，他终于忍不住了，反手抽了自己一耳光。

“神庭现在还没派人找来，你就不能想想原因吗？真以为自己是什么重要的货色？你这样的东西教宗陛下眨眼间就能复制出几百上千个。”

沙利叶的表情狰狞着：“不止是你，我也一样。我消失的这一年里，骑士团里肯定也有了新的沙利叶。

“过去我能护着你，是因为我还有用。现在的我和普通的天启骑士没什么差别。我们回去只会被人弄死，成为畸变体的饲料！神庭已经没有我们的位置了。”

相晨曦显然也是清楚的，只是总是心存幻想。

如今幻想被戳破，他忍不住捂着脸，嚎啕大哭起来。

沙利叶只好继续安慰道：“再等等。等我找机会，和基地的那个相南里见上一面。”

……

……

以西结开车到了永恒市。

车是相南里给配的，用之前仓库里的报废汽车改了改。颜色还涂成了以西结喜欢的红色。

以西结靠着自己的努力，成功吃上了相南里的软饭。

他把车停在了停车场。

比起一年前，永恒市繁荣了许多。

丰收节大获成功，基地解放了令周围小据点闻风丧胆的“罗马悍匪城”；这座城市名气日益高涨，甚至有了“姑苏小神庭”的称号。

每天，都有附近的人过来，从事经济活动。

永恒市的“工分券”甚至在周围区域（主要是罗马城和光辉市）流行起来，成为硬通货。

相南里不是很喜欢这个称谓，但想了想，这也算硬蹭神庭热度，四舍五入是基地赚了，遂忍。

以西结的大尾巴很显眼，更别提他有些奇怪的四肢和身上的鳞片。

但以西结隔两天就会来一次，常住人口都已经见怪不怪了。

以西结理了理衣服，捧着花，朝着相南里的办公室赶去。

相南里的办公室就在安德鲁办公室的隔壁。整栋楼里人来人往，声音明明很嘈杂。但以西结隔着十几米，都能敏锐地捕捉到他的声音——

相南里：“小青。”

看来东方青帝也在，晦气。

相南里的语气有些疑惑：“这段电波是什么意思？你们智械军团的密码也太难破译了吧。”

东方青帝的声音略微一顿：“嗯，我又收到了同事的求救信号。”

上一次是没用的福音书的。

这一次，是失踪多日的黄枫的。

定位的地址在阴山城。
chunks.englishText:
Chapter 101: A Plea for Help from Yinshan City (Part 2)

Saliel actually knew this.

One of the essential qualities a Holy Son of the Divine Court must possess is the ability to communicate with non-human species.

To train these candidates, they were thrown into aberrant nests from a young age, a phase that lasted for a full year. Only those who survived were qualified to enter the subsequent procedures.

The most candidates died during this round. Although Xiang Chenxi was a survivor, he found it difficult to control his disgust and fear of the aberrants. He simply hid it well for the sake of survival.

Saliel had discovered it because of a previous time he had unlocked his genetic limit and hadn't yet recovered. Xiang Chenxi had seen it and immediately collapsed into tears.

Saliel had patiently comforted him a few more times, but Xiang Chenxi continued to cry and make a scene. Finally, Saliel couldn't help it and slapped himself across the face.

"The Divine Court hasn't sent anyone to look for us yet—can't you think of the reason why? Do you really think you're some important commodity? His Holiness the Pope could replicate hundreds or thousands of things like you in the blink of an eye."

Saliel’s expression was ferocious: "Not just you, me too. In the year I’ve been missing, there must already be a new Saliel in the Knights Templar."

"In the past, I could protect you because I was still useful. Now, I’m no different from an ordinary Apocalypse Knight. If we go back, we’ll just be killed and turned into feed for the aberrants! There is no place for us in the Divine Court anymore."

Xiang Chenxi was clearly aware of this, but he always harbored fantasies.

Now that the fantasy had been shattered, he couldn't help but cover his face and wail.

Saliel had no choice but to continue comforting him: "Wait a little longer. Wait until I find an opportunity to meet that Xiang Nanli from the base."

……

……

Ezekiel drove to Eternal City.

The car had been provided by Xiang Nanli, modified from a scrapped vehicle in the warehouse. He had even painted it the red color Ezekiel liked.

Relying on his own efforts, Ezekiel had successfully managed to live off Xiang Nanli.

He parked the car in the parking lot.

Compared to a year ago, Eternal City was much more prosperous.

The Harvest Festival had been a great success, and the base had liberated the "Roman Ruffian City," which had once struck fear into the hearts of surrounding small outposts; the city’s fame was growing daily, and it even earned the nickname "Little Gusu Divine Court."

Every day, people from the vicinity came over to engage in economic activities.

Eternal City’s "work-point vouchers" had even become popular in the surrounding areas (mainly Roman City and Radiant City), becoming a hard currency.

Xiang Nanli didn't particularly like this moniker, but after thinking about it, it was essentially free publicity off the Divine Court’s fame—rounding up, the base was profiting—so he endured it.

Ezekiel’s large tail was very conspicuous, not to mention his somewhat strange limbs and the scales on his body.

But Ezekiel came every couple of days, and the permanent residents were already used to it.

Ezekiel straightened his clothes, clutched the flowers, and hurried toward Xiang Nanli’s office.

Xiang Nanli’s office was right next to Andrew’s. People were coming and going throughout the building, and the noise was clearly chaotic. Yet, from over ten meters away, Ezekiel could keenly capture his voice—

Xiang Nanli: "Xiao Qing."

It seemed Dongfang Qingdi was there too. Bad luck.

Xiang Nanli’s tone was somewhat puzzled: "What does this radio wave mean? Is your Intelligent Machine Legion’s code too difficult to decipher?"

Dongfang Qingdi’s voice paused slightly: "Hmm, I have received a distress signal from a colleague again."

The last one had been from the useless Gospel.

This time, it was from Huang Feng, who had been missing for many days.

The location was in Yinshan City.
