第106章 回村第一天

温室大棚里就更暖和了，有零上七八度呢。

擅长种菜的老农伯恩山眯起眼，靠在身后的电线杆上。不算明亮的日光透过一层塑料，照在面前的菜地上。

这些蔬菜的个头很大，且都是基因改良后的品种。伯恩山负责的大棚编号6，位于基地实验室的正后方。

脸盆大小的卷心菜叶子边缘有烧焦似的血红色，伯恩山曾经见过这些菜心吞咽咀嚼路过的地虾（这是地表人民对蟑螂的爱称，迄今为止，地虾依然在地表人的食谱中）。

除此外还有几亩稻田……呃，稻子上结的果实无论颜色和形状都像大桑葚，但其实所谓的稻米只是一堆不怎么爱运动的虫卵。

煮熟后味道和米差不多，目前已经加入社区食堂豪华午餐。

伯恩山对于这些粮食蔬菜是否能吃存在一些怀疑，毕竟以前，在永恒之城，他只种土豆；但北辰说，这些都是绿色安全食品，想来是吃不死人的。

伯恩山熟练地将实验室配出的化肥浇灌到土里，随后欣慰地摸了摸比脸盆还要大的卷心菜包，并且在卷心菜准备张嘴咬他时，迅速收回了胳膊。

“虽然长得不太好看，但是产量还真不低。”伯恩山的眼角笑出了细细的皱纹，“要是几年前有这些品种就好了。”

要是有，他的小女儿也不至于在开春的时候饿死了吧。

像这样的蔬菜大棚，基地目前有13个。蔬菜产量完全可以满足不到百人的基地目前的开销，甚至还有出口到永恒市的余裕。

作为第一批从永恒市来到基地主城的免费农民工……哦不，志愿者，伯恩山最开始是有些失望的。

当然，只有一丁点。

在他的想象中，基地主城应该和那些他一辈子都没去过的地下城市一样，充满距离感。高大宏伟的建筑会让他感觉到自己的渺小；而生活优渥的地底城市居民，会让他羞怯于自己的贫困。

然而，当伯恩山跋山涉水来到山巅，迎接他们的只有几台破旧的机器人和一片废墟。

这种穷困潦倒的感觉，真是该死的熟悉。像极了他过去四十五年的人生。

基地比难民营强点，因为这里有水电，没有金属垃圾污染；没有会抢劫的拾荒者与职业土匪。

伯恩山来的第一夜，和其他几十名工友一起睡在大厅的地上。棉被和枕头都不够，人们挤在一起窃窃私语，语气里充满迷茫。

“比我想象中破。”

“好多楼都塌了一半呢，也没什么人……”

“那个叫北辰的是机器人吗？让机器人管我们啊。”

这人显然是想起了当年在永恒之城当农奴的时候，那些不近人情的机器人只会按照程序行事，丝毫不会在意农奴的死活。

“他是人类，只是机械化程度太高。所以看起来有点吓人。”有人小声辩解，“而且北辰没有那么恐怖，很亲切。”

“我想家了，算算时间，我妈该从学堂毕业了，也不知道分到了哪个单位。”

思想觉悟很高的伯恩山道：“再怎么也不会比之前差吧。”

伯恩山是吃过生活的苦的，那些苦难没有形状和声音，却凝结在他嶙峋的骨头和满身的疤痕里。

伯恩山的父亲母亲是农奴，所以他也是农奴。他的儿女也会是，大奴隶生小奴隶，循环往复。

有地方睡觉，还能分到自己的房，不用担心饿死、冻死；能吃上自己种的粮；这已经是伯恩山三十多年里最安稳幸福的一段时光了。

这句话一说出来，大家都释然地笑了。

他们希望这样的基地能一直存在下去。

在抵达基地的第二天，远道而来的志愿者就开始了自己的工作。

一半人修房子、铺路；一半人种田。还有一些幸运儿，被北辰抽调到了实验室帮忙。

现在，伯恩山领到的种子已经长出这么大一片田；他自己也在前几天分到了新修好的宿舍钥匙。

“伯恩山。”路过的同事扛着一袋子肥料，跟他打招呼，“听说了吗？司令从永恒市回来了。”

伯恩山压低帽檐：“还用你说，上午消息都传遍了。”

叫大人太封建，叫城主不够贴切；基地下辖已经好几个城市了。因为相南里对外发文自称“司令”，尽管大家不太能理解这个词的含义，但它依然成为了人们对相南里的敬称。

而消息会传出来，是因为有人注意到，为相南里留的宿舍门敞开着，保姆机器人正在里面打扫卫生。

老实说，对于相南里回来，伯恩山是很期待的。但要说相南里回来前后，他的生活会有什么变化吗？似乎也没有。

只是人心思定罢了。他们本能地感谢着这个带来了改变的男人，就像是小鸡喜欢靠在鸡妈妈的腋下。

……

……

基地外，高高的铁栏杆竖直插入雪地里，绕着城区围成一圈。通电的铁丝就缠绕在这些路杆上，用来防止可能袭击的人和兽。但有些人迹罕至、维修不便的地方，铁丝会被血红的菌丝替代。

每隔一段距离，柱子的头顶就趴着一台无人机。大多时候它们都很安静，像是潜伏的猎豹；电子眼里偶尔闪过一缕红光表明它们正在工作。

配上昏暗的天空，这道城墙很难不让人感觉到一种莫名的恐惧。

事实上，就在几年后，地下城市对基地的抵制宣传里，就会频繁提起主城区的围墙；并且与同时期盛行的姑苏城瘟疫联系在一起。

进城的手续并不繁琐。只要车内的电子通行证和数据库匹配，就能直接通行。

安德鲁坐在后车厢，规规矩矩地把手叠在膝盖上，一双机械眼好奇地转来转去。

只见两枚光球从安德鲁的眼眶中弹出，伸出长长的神经传感线，贴在玻璃上，前后180度扭动着。机械眼传递不出太多情绪，但他体内电压忽高忽低，证明至少在此时，安德鲁心潮澎湃。

嗯，他还是第一次来基地主城区呢。

或许让他紧张的不仅是陌生的环境，还有即将要见到的人。

“我们就这么进城了？”安德鲁看着在深夜里放行的电子门，压低了声音，“这样安全吗？”

现在网上到处黑客白客什么的，要是电子密匙太容易，清道夫一个入侵，本就不怎么牢固的安保岂不是一触即溃。

相南里长长地“唔”了一声，回答：“加密算法是我自己写的。”

他复活后不是赚钱就是在搞建设，确实没那么多空闲时间重写一套算法。所以为了省事，相南里直接拿了自己上辈子的研究成果。

安德鲁顿时不说话了。

进城后，就是一条笔直的大马路，被称为中央大道。基地目前所有的建筑都在这条大路的两侧。按照城市规划图，很工整的分为了“田”字型的四个大区。

路上空无一人，只有一群机器人还在工作。清洁机器人负责扫雪、电路检修；安保机器人负责巡逻；还有满载着货物的无人车按照既定的路线疾驰。
chunks.englishText:
Chapter 106: First Day Back at the Village (Part 1)

The greenhouse was even warmer, reaching seven or eight degrees Celsius above zero.

Bernstein, an old farmer skilled in growing vegetables, squinted his eyes and leaned against the utility pole behind him. The not-so-bright sunlight shone through a layer of plastic onto the vegetable patch in front of him.

These vegetables were quite large and were all genetically modified varieties. Greenhouse No. 6, which Bernstein was responsible for, was located directly behind the base laboratory.

The edges of the cabbage leaves, which were the size of washbasins, had a blood-red color that looked like burns. Bernstein had once seen these cabbage hearts swallow and chew on passing "ground shrimp" (this was the affectionate nickname the surface people had for cockroaches; to this day, ground shrimp remained on the surface people's menu).

Besides that, there were a few acres of rice paddies... er, the fruits growing on the rice looked like large mulberries in both color and shape, but in reality, the so-called "rice" was just a pile of lazy insect eggs.

After being boiled, the taste was similar to rice, and it had already been added to the community cafeteria's luxury lunch menu.

Bernstein had some doubts about whether these grains and vegetables were edible. After all, back in the Eternal City, he only grew potatoes. But Beichen said these were all green, safe foods, so he figured they wouldn't kill anyone.

Bernstein skillfully poured the fertilizer prepared by the laboratory into the soil, then contentedly patted a cabbage head larger than a washbasin, quickly retracting his arm when the cabbage prepared to open its mouth to bite him.

"Although they don't look very good, the yield is really not low." Fine wrinkles appeared at the corners of Bernstein's eyes as he smiled. "If only these varieties had existed a few years ago."

If they had, his youngest daughter wouldn't have starved to death in the early spring.

There were currently 13 such vegetable greenhouses at the base. The vegetable production could fully meet the current needs of the base, which had fewer than a hundred people, and there was even enough surplus to export to Eternal City.

As one of the first batch of free migrant workers—oh no, volunteers—to come to the base's main city from Eternal City, Bernstein had been a little disappointed at first.

Of course, only a little bit.

In his imagination, the base's main city should have been like those underground cities he had never visited in his life, full of a sense of distance. The tall, magnificent buildings would make him feel his own insignificance, and the well-off residents of the underground cities would make him feel ashamed of his own poverty.

However, when Bernstein traveled over mountains and through water to reach the mountaintop, they were greeted only by a few dilapidated robots and a patch of ruins.

This feeling of poverty was damnably familiar. It was exactly like the past forty-five years of his life.

The base was better than a refugee camp because there was water and electricity here, no metal waste pollution, and no scavengers or professional bandits to rob them.

On his first night at the base, Bernstein slept on the floor of the main hall with dozens of other workers. There weren't enough quilts and pillows, so people huddled together and whispered, their tones filled with confusion.

"It's more broken than I imagined."

"Many of the buildings have collapsed halfway, and there's no one around..."

"Is that guy named Beichen a robot? Letting a robot manage us..."

This person was clearly remembering the days when they were serfs in Eternal City, where those heartless robots only acted according to programs and didn't care about the lives of the serfs at all.

"He's human, just with a high degree of mechanization. That's why he looks a bit scary," someone whispered in defense. "And Beichen isn't that terrifying; he's actually quite approachable."

"I miss home. If I calculate the time, my mother should have graduated from school by now; I wonder which unit she was assigned to."

Bernstein, who had high ideological awareness, said: "It couldn't be worse than before, could it?"

Bernstein had tasted the bitterness of life. Those hardships had no shape or sound, but they were condensed into his gaunt bones and the scars all over his body.

Bernstein's father and mother were serfs, so he was a serf too. His children would be as well—big slaves giving birth to little slaves, repeating in a cycle.

Having a place to sleep, being assigned his own room, not having to worry about starving or freezing to death, and being able to eat the grain he grew himself—this was already the most stable and happy period of Bernstein's thirty-plus years.

Once this was said, everyone smiled with relief.

They hoped such a base could continue to exist.

On the second day after arriving at the base, the volunteers who had come from afar began their work.

Half the people repaired houses and paved roads; the other half farmed. There were also some lucky ones who were pulled by Beichen to help in the laboratory.

Now, the seeds Bernstein had received had grown into such a large field; he himself had also received the key to his newly built dormitory a few days ago.

"Bernstein." A passing colleague carrying a bag of fertilizer greeted him, "Have you heard? The Commander is back from Eternal City."

Bernstein lowered the brim of his hat: "As if you needed to tell me. The news spread all over this morning."

Calling him "Lord" was too feudal, and calling him "City Lord" wasn't quite accurate, as the base already had several subordinate cities. Because Xiang Nanli issued documents externally calling himself "Commander," although people didn't quite understand the meaning of the term, it still became their respectful title for Xiang Nanli.

The news had spread because someone noticed that the dormitory reserved for Xiang Nanli was left open, and a nanny robot was inside cleaning.

To be honest, Bernstein was looking forward to Xiang Nanli's return. But if one were to ask if his life would change before or after Xiang Nanli's return? It didn't seem so.

It was just that people's hearts were settled. They instinctively thanked this man who had brought about change, just like chicks liked to nestle under the wings of a mother hen.

...

...

Outside the base, high iron railings were inserted vertically into the snow, circling the city area. Electrified wires were wrapped around these poles to prevent potential attacks from people or beasts. But in some places where human footprints were rare and maintenance was inconvenient, the wires were replaced by blood-red mycelium.

Every certain distance, a drone perched on top of a pillar. Most of the time they were very quiet, like lurking cheetahs; a flash of red light occasionally flickered in their electronic eyes, indicating they were working.

Coupled with the dim sky, it was hard not to feel an inexplicable fear of this city wall.

In fact, a few years later, the underground city's propaganda against the base would frequently mention the walls of the main city, linking them to the Gusu City plague that was prevalent at the same time.

The procedure for entering the city was not cumbersome. As long as the electronic pass inside the vehicle matched the database, one could pass directly.

Andrew sat in the back of the truck, neatly folding his hands on his knees, his pair of mechanical eyes turning around curiously.

Two light orbs popped out from Andrew's eye sockets, extending long neural sensor lines that stuck to the glass, twisting 180 degrees back and forth. His mechanical eyes couldn't convey too much emotion, but the voltage inside his body fluctuated, proving that at this moment, Andrew was at least feeling overwhelmed with excitement.

Hmm, it was his first time coming to the base's main city area.

Perhaps what made him nervous wasn't just the unfamiliar environment, but the person he was about to meet.

"We're just entering the city like this?" Andrew looked at the electronic gate that opened in the dead of night and lowered his voice, "Is this safe?"

There were hackers and white-hats everywhere on the internet now. If the electronic key was too simple, wouldn't the already not-so-solid security collapse at a single touch if a Scavenger hacked it?

Xiang Nanli gave a long "Hmm" and replied: "I wrote the encryption algorithm myself."

After he was resurrected, he was either making money or building things, so he really didn't have much spare time to rewrite a set of algorithms. So, to save trouble, Xiang Nanli directly used the research results from his previous life.

Andrew immediately stopped talking.

After entering the city, there was a straight main road known as Central Avenue. All the buildings of the base were currently on both sides of this road. According to the urban planning map, it was neatly divided into four major districts in a "field" (田) shape.

The road was empty, with only a group of robots still working. Cleaning robots were responsible for clearing snow and electrical maintenance; security robots were responsible for patrolling; and unmanned vehicles loaded with cargo sped along predetermined routes.

chunks.chineseText:
尽管精神上已经极度疲倦，但相南里却没有选择前往生活区，看看北辰给他配的宿舍；而是直接开往了实验室的方向。

相南里揉着眉心：“我跟北辰说好了先去看实验室。”

北辰的机械化程度是很高的。

换句话说，他几乎和机器人一样，不需要睡眠。

这让身为自然人类的相南里很难不产生嫉妒之情。

相南里从上衣的口袋里掏出了一瓶由“永生科技”生产出来的精力药片，含了一片在舌尖，一股清凉的薄荷味直冲天灵盖。

下一秒，东方青帝掐住他的下巴，把这枚薄荷糖片抠了出来。

相南里不是很满意地咬住了小青塞进来的手指：“干嘛？”

他抬起眼眸的瞬间瞪了自己一下，很鲜活的表情。

东方青帝先是意识到这一点，然后才缓缓询问：“谁给的？”

“……李斯特。”

是那个经常和北辰联系的科学家。

这种小药片本质上是一种兴奋剂，被宣传绝对安全无害，网上到处都是广告。因为效果显著，销量一向不错。

李斯特说很多科研人员都喜欢吃这个提神醒脑。

嗯，上辈子在硅谷，相南里也被推荐过很多保健品。科学点的像什么辅酶q10，二甲双胍，维生素片；不科学的就是什么年轻人的血……因此接受度还行。

东方青帝打开车窗，很没公德心地直接把一盒药瓶子丢了出去。

相南里不由得紧张起来：“怎么了？有毒吗？”

“根据检测，没有。”东方青帝面无表情地回答，“我只是不喜欢永生科技的东西。你要是太困，我可以电你一下。”

说完，他的中指和无名指很轻地搭在了相南里的腰侧。

相南里：“……不用了，谢谢。”

怎么说呢，智械的情绪真难照顾；好在他对非人类较为溺爱。

几分钟后，车在实验园区的门前停下。

相南里离开的时候，实验室只有一个大铁棚。在外地的时候，他也批准过一些修建项目。但是当真的亲眼看到实验园区时，还是有些意外。

实验室占地面积变大了，凌晨四点居然还灯火通明。

整个实验区修的像是一座四合院。四面是不同功能的实验室，中间围着庭院。庭院里有十几个玻璃皿，里面关着不同形状的菌丝生命体，各个都张牙舞爪的。

“啊，你们来了。”北辰推开安全门，穿着全套防护服，从最东侧的小黑房子里探出头。

随着他说话声音响起，玻璃皿内的菌丝生命体瞬间变得暴躁起来。

离北辰最近的红菌子奋力拍打着玻璃罩，相南里几乎能听见玻璃轻微碎裂的声音。

下一刻，一名穿着制服的机器人从房间里冲了出来，手里拿着一瓶不知名的胶状物。

只见它把胶状物投进了饲养槽内，躁动的菌丝生命体用根系吸收了那些黏液，像是喝了麻醉剂一样安静了下来。

北辰摸了摸鼻子，简单解释道：“一些毒剂。用来溶解它的躯干，避免生长太快。这株菌丝生命体恢复速度很快，是我打算用来制作@￥#@的原材料……”

门外汉相南里试图记住他嘴里的每一个字：“什么￥@#@？”

“一种可以用来培育基因战士的药剂，我打算叫它生命一号。怎么说呢，新的材料总会带来一些技术上的革新。”北辰说话的声音呆滞，比机器人还像机器，“1号，量有点多了。”

背对着他们正在工作的智械人手一顿，旋即颇具情感地回复：“抱歉。我错误估计了能耗，导致现在电量不足，这让我的反应迟钝。我可能需要去充电。”

相南里在离开的时候留下了两台人型智械，作为北辰实验室的助手。

这俩台智械分别叫螺丝钉1号和2号，是相南里从黑市上淘来的报废品。

1号复制了福音书的智能模块，进化速度远超普通机器人。如今是实验室二把手，而且还在上面的许可下，参与了基地的城市化建设。

如果它是人类而不是一台智械，那么北辰多半已经被架空了。

相南里不由得侧目，看了1号一眼。

1号的脸是标准的椭圆形，五官被一条竖着的智能光带取代，肤色银白。它穿着人类的衣服，如果挡住脸，乍一看完全是氛围感帅哥。

就是不知道为什么，气质很是人夫。

听说智械人的性格会比较像主人，北辰就挺逆来顺受的。

不知道是不是错觉，1号背对着他们的身体显得更僵硬了。

相南里很快收回视线，笑着开口：“我们进去说吧，外面还怪冷的。”

一行人热热闹闹地走进了房间内。

螺丝钉1号没有转身看一眼，智械人是不需要转身的。

更不需要那一眼回看所代表的思念。

眼前的玻璃罩子上有些模糊的影子，很快，实验室的大门合上。

洛阳轻轻地摸了摸玻璃上倒映过相南里的地方，然后挪着这具刚用习惯的金属身体，朝着充电房走去。
chunks.englishText:
Despite being mentally exhausted, Xiang Nanli did not choose to head to the living quarters to see the dormitory Beichen had prepared for him; instead, he drove directly toward the laboratory.

Xiang Nanli rubbed his temples. "I already told Beichen I’d go to the lab first."

Beichen’s level of mechanization was extremely high.

In other words, he was almost identical to a robot; he had no need for sleep.

This made it difficult for Xiang Nanli, a natural-born human, not to feel a twinge of jealousy.

Xiang Nanli pulled a bottle of energy tablets produced by "Eternal Life Technology" from his jacket pocket. He placed one on the tip of his tongue, and a cool, refreshing mint flavor surged straight to his crown.

The next second, Dongfang Qingdi pinched his chin and plucked the mint tablet out.

Xiang Nanli bit the finger Xiao Qing had inserted into his mouth, not entirely satisfied. "What are you doing?"

The moment he raised his eyes to glare at him, his expression was vivid and full of life.

Dongfang Qingdi realized this first, then slowly asked, "Who gave you this?"

"...List."

It was that scientist who frequently kept in touch with Beichen.

These little pills were essentially stimulants, marketed as being absolutely safe and harmless, with advertisements everywhere online. Because they were highly effective, their sales had always been quite good.

List had said that many researchers liked to take them to refresh their minds.

Well, in his past life in Silicon Valley, Xiang Nanli had also been recommended many health supplements. The scientific ones included things like Coenzyme Q10, Metformin, and vitamin tablets; the unscientific ones were things like the blood of young people... Therefore, his acceptance level was decent.

Dongfang Qingdi rolled down the car window and, with zero regard for public decorum, tossed the entire bottle of pills out.

Xiang Nanli couldn't help but feel nervous. "What's wrong? Are they poisonous?"

"According to my scans, no," Dongfang Qingdi replied expressionlessly. "I just don't like products from Eternal Life Technology. If you're too sleepy, I can give you a jolt of electricity."

After saying this, he lightly rested his middle and ring fingers against Xiang Nanli’s waist.

Xiang Nanli: "...No need, thank you."

How should he put it? The emotions of a sentient machine were truly difficult to manage; fortunately, he was quite indulgent toward non-humans.

A few minutes later, the car stopped in front of the laboratory park.

When Xiang Nanli had left, the laboratory was just a large iron shed. While he was away, he had approved several construction projects. But when he saw the laboratory park with his own eyes, he was still somewhat surprised.

The laboratory's footprint had grown, and it was still brightly lit at four in the morning.

The entire experimental area was built like a traditional courtyard house. Laboratories with different functions occupied the four sides, surrounding a central courtyard. In the courtyard, there were over a dozen glass vessels containing mycelial lifeforms of various shapes, all of them clawing and snapping at the air.

"Ah, you're here." Beichen pushed open the security door, wearing a full protective suit, and poked his head out from a small, dark room on the far east side.

As his voice rang out, the mycelial lifeforms inside the glass vessels instantly became agitated.

The red fungus closest to Beichen pounded fiercely against its glass cover; Xiang Nanli could almost hear the faint sound of the glass cracking.

The next moment, a robot in uniform rushed out of the room, holding a bottle of unknown gelatinous substance.

It poured the substance into the feeding trough, and the restless mycelial lifeform absorbed the slime with its roots, calming down as if it had been drugged.

Beichen rubbed his nose and explained briefly, "Some toxins. Used to dissolve its trunk to prevent it from growing too fast. This mycelial lifeform has a very fast recovery rate; it’s the raw material I intend to use to make @￥#@..."

Xiang Nanli, a layman, tried to memorize every word out of his mouth: "Make what @￥#@?"

"A type of serum that can be used to cultivate gene warriors. I plan to call it 'Life No. 1.' How should I put it? New materials always bring about technological innovations." Beichen’s voice was dull, sounding even more like a machine than a robot. "No. 1, the dosage was a bit too high."

The sentient machine working with its back to them paused, then replied with a hint of emotion: "Apologies. I miscalculated the energy consumption, leading to a power shortage, which made my reaction sluggish. I may need to go charge."

When Xiang Nanli left, he had left behind two humanoid sentient machines to act as assistants in Beichen’s laboratory.

These two machines were named Screw No. 1 and No. 2, which Xiang Nanli had scavenged from the black market as scrap.

No. 1 had copied the intelligent modules of the "Gospel," and its evolution speed far exceeded that of ordinary robots. It was now the second-in-command of the laboratory and, with permission from above, had even participated in the urbanization construction of the base.

If it were a human instead of a sentient machine, Beichen would likely have been sidelined by now.

Xiang Nanli couldn't help but glance sideways at No. 1.

No. 1’s face was a standard oval shape, its features replaced by a vertical intelligent light strip, and its skin was a silvery white. It wore human clothes; if you covered its face, it looked like a handsome man with a certain "vibe."

For some reason, it had a very "house-husband" aura.

It was said that the personality of a sentient machine tended to resemble its master, and Beichen was quite submissive.

He didn't know if it was an illusion, but No. 1’s back seemed to stiffen even more.

Xiang Nanli quickly withdrew his gaze and said with a smile, "Let’s go inside to talk; it’s quite cold out here."

The group walked into the room in a lively manner.

Screw No. 1 did not turn to look; sentient machines did not need to turn around.

And they certainly didn't need the longing that such a backward glance would represent.

There were some blurred shadows on the glass cover in front of it. Soon, the laboratory door closed.

Luo Yang gently touched the spot on the glass where Xiang Nanli had been reflected, then moved his metallic body—which he had just gotten used to—toward the charging room.

chunks.chineseText:
第107章 正确

纸上的字迹鬼画桃符，犹如一位工龄30年、德高望重的主任医师。

安德鲁屏住呼吸，以一种虔诚的心态捧起椅子上的草图，机械眼里几乎能泛起泪花：“这就是失传已久的漠氏多段基因示踪术吗？自从东皇重工被炸毁后，这种技术就失传了……没想到我还有再看见的一天！”

相南里不由得在心里吐槽：[小青，安德鲁这台词好像个修真文npc。]

小青不是很想回答。

北辰熟练地拉开会议桌前的椅子，坐下，扫视了一圈：“……呃，这是？你们新买的机器人？”

他的语气难得有些疑惑。

安德鲁几乎是条件反射地站了个笔直，头顶的铁皮爆开一串电花：“报告所长，我是、我叫安德鲁。专业是计算机与生物医疗！”

说完，竟然直挺挺地举起手，行了一个军礼。

东皇重工是军工企业，里面的职工实行的是军事化管理，科研组也不例外。

安德鲁只能算中层干部，是东皇重工浩瀚人才库里随手抓的一颗星星。这颗星星放在外界已经足够耀眼，但在天才的领域也只能黯然失色。

他崇敬漠北，就像是很多搞人工智能的都会崇拜相南里一样。

相南里简短道：“他是我给你安排的助手。之前在地下城市当义体医生。机械化程度比较高。他有一定的科研经验，应该能帮上忙。”

北辰仔细打量着安德鲁的金属脸，好几次张开嘴，想说点什么，又温吞地咽了回去：“好的。”

他总觉得安德鲁很熟悉，尽管自己的记忆里并没有这么一个人。

螺丝钉2号捧来一台电脑，拂去桌子上的文件袋，把电脑放在会议桌上。

安德鲁捡起文件怒斥：“你这台机器人，怎么能这么对待重要资料！”

2号被吼得有点懵，脸上的光带呈现出一种迷茫的直线。毕竟安德鲁不在的时候，它都是这么处理资料的。

有时候为了省电，研究所还会把这些资料烧了烤火呢~

北辰只好解释道：“没关系，重要的东西在我脑子里。而且，因为裂变和突变，黑丝粉菌的迭代非常快。写在纸上的下一秒就会有新的菌种；在脑海里推演会比记录更快。”

东方青帝不由得侧目。

北辰说的这种进化推演，在其他地方通常是由ai完成。需要强大的硬件和算法，以及很多时间。

李斯特偶尔会寄点赞助（比如地表云端信号塔），基地实验室的环境比半年前好了不少，但比起那些大企业动辄数亿资金制造出的实验室，还是简陋的有些过分。

更过分的是，在这样的条件下，北辰依然靠着自己的天赋，用纸和笔还有自己的脑子，带着几台机器人，做出了不可复制的成就。

这让东方青帝很难不对人类产生一丝微弱的敬意。

北辰下意识地推了一下不存在的眼镜：“实验室现在主要的研究方向还是红丝粉菌的开发与利用。因为红丝粉菌耐低温、生长迅速、对土壤的需求较低，我们让它和不同的生物之间杂交。”

投影仪上放出了牧场早期菌牛的照片。

“和腐烂生物杂交，能有效降低红丝粉菌的攻击性……嗯，但这种动物还不能被人类直接食用，但可以成为更耐毒性的畸变人的饲料。”

“根据牧场反馈的资料，按时食用菌牛的畸变人会比野生畸变人更加容易存活。但野生畸变人会因为自然选择更加善战。”

屏幕上出现了以西结的畸变人营地。

不知道是不是错觉，相南里甚至觉得部分畸变人长出了肥肥的小肚腩。

北辰：“基于菌牛这种品种继续改良，我们得到了体型更小的菌鸡……菌鸡毒性相对微弱，但繁殖速度极快。”

是的，当地下城市还在为新时代的黑死病焦头烂额的时候，基地已经开始着手菌丝的开发与利用了。

相南里摸着下巴，认真研究了一下数据：“理论上，人类服用菌鸡而感染菌丝病的概率为0.74％？”

北辰先是转头，看了小青一眼，旋即才开口道：“嗯，所以我有一个想法。”

这个想法，其实是东方青帝提出来的。

之前实验消耗太严重，研究所财政捉襟见肘，小青多次驳回了北辰的经费申请——基建、社会保障、人力费用，哪一个都需要钱。

但在驳回后，东方青帝却很委婉地提到过一个赚钱的方法。

“就是，我们可以饲养菌鸡，然后出口到地表的其他据点，”北辰有些底气不足地说着，“嗯，至于可能存在的感染，这种程度的菌丝病很容易被抑制剂解决的。

“呃，我的意思是……只要有人依然把这种菌鸡作为食物，那么抑制剂就能永远地卖下去。永生科技不会拒绝这样的推广。”

相南里的嘴角依然带着浅浅的笑意，眼眸却微微垂下。

食物，一向是地表生存的难题。

地面环境如此恶劣，人类却依然顽强地下着崽。根据统计，目前还有约两亿的地表遗民。其中，神庭信徒占比一半。

相南里有时候会思考，明明活着就是受难，为什么还要让后代继续这样的生活？可他又有什么资格去质疑生命的选择？

——毕竟，就算是他自己，其实也渴望着活下去。否则，他干嘛要冒险进冷冻舱，又为什么要努力到现在？

相南里本能的知道，北辰的提议没有任何问题，甚至是个非常好的商业计划。

基地需要钱，或者说钱能交换来的资源。但他受过的教育、经历，又让他明白，这是一条很肮脏无耻的路。

就像是他前世见过的那些商人，一边售卖宣传更廉价的玉米糖浆，让普通人的食物越来越甜；又一边研发减肥药。

他看不起的糖业资本家，却能靠着挣来的钞票，左右他的实验室、左右政客、左右群羊。

东方青帝适时地开口：“虽然之前的专利费让我们赚了一笔，但是因为基地的福利政策过于优渥，根据计算，最迟两个月后就会出现财政缺口。目前基地一直在消耗资源，却没有能进行外贸的商品。而内需循环创造出的财富非常有限。”

Alpha的语气很是冷酷，他也是真的这么认为的。

人联的首都洛阳城，都不会保证让每个人吃饱饭，有地方住，有几乎免费的医疗和教育。一个脆弱、新生的基地，凭什么？

“其实神庭早就用类似的方法进行传教了。他们的骑士驱除畸变生物，引导地表的人信仰黑十字审判庭，又源源不断地制造畸变体。

“如果结果是有益的，过程不需要正确。”

东方青帝说话的时候，修长的手指就扣在桌子上。宛如戒指一样的能源环亮着一层冷光。

相南里回答：“我知道。我只是心理上有些难以接受。我认为这个决策很短视。”

他抬头，碧绿的眼眸望向东方青帝，眼神里传达的情绪如此复杂。
chunks.englishText:
Chapter 107: Correct

The handwriting on the paper was a mess of squiggles, like that of a highly respected chief physician with 30 years of experience.

Andrew held his breath, lifting the sketch from the chair with a sense of reverence. Tears almost welled up in his mechanical eyes: "Is this the long-lost Mo-style Multi-stage Gene Tracing Technique? Ever since Donghuang Heavy Industries was destroyed, this technology has been lost... I never thought I’d live to see it again!"

Xiang Nanli couldn't help but mutter in his heart: [Xiao Qing, Andrew’s lines sound like an NPC from a cultivation novel.]

Xiao Qing didn't really want to answer.

Beichen skillfully pulled out a chair at the conference table, sat down, and scanned the room: "...Uh, who is this? Your new robot?"

His tone was uncharacteristically puzzled.

Andrew stood straight as a reflex, a string of electric sparks bursting from the metal on his head: "Reporting to the Director, I am—my name is Andrew. My specialty is computer science and biomedical engineering!"

After saying this, he actually raised his hand stiffly and gave a military salute.

Donghuang Heavy Industries was a military-industrial enterprise, and its employees were subject to militarized management; the research team was no exception.

Andrew could only be considered a mid-level cadre, a star plucked at random from the vast talent pool of Donghuang Heavy Industries. This star was dazzling enough in the outside world, but it could only be eclipsed in the realm of geniuses.

He revered Mo Bei, just as many people in artificial intelligence revered Xiang Nanli.

Xiang Nanli said briefly, "He is the assistant I arranged for you. He used to be a prosthetic doctor in the underground city. His level of mechanization is quite high. He has a certain amount of research experience and should be able to help."

Beichen carefully examined Andrew’s metal face, opening his mouth several times to say something, but swallowing it back each time. "Understood."

He always felt that Andrew was familiar, even though there was no such person in his memory.

Screw No. 2 brought over a computer, brushed the document bags off the table, and placed the computer on the conference table.

Andrew picked up the documents and scolded, "You robot, how can you treat important data like this!"

No. 2 was a bit stunned by the shouting, the light strip on its face forming a confused straight line. After all, when Andrew wasn't there, this was how it handled data.

Sometimes, to save electricity, the research institute would even burn these documents to keep warm.

Beichen had to explain, "It’s fine; the important stuff is in my head. Besides, due to fission and mutation, the iteration of the Black Silk Powder Fungus is very fast. The second you write it on paper, there’s already a new strain; deducing it in your mind is faster than recording it."

Dongfang Qingdi couldn't help but glance sideways.

The evolutionary deduction Beichen spoke of was usually done by AI elsewhere. It required powerful hardware, algorithms, and a lot of time.

List occasionally sent some sponsorships (such as surface cloud signal towers), and the environment of the base laboratory was much better than it had been six months ago, but compared to the laboratories built by large corporations with hundreds of millions in funding, it was still excessively crude.

What was even more excessive was that under such conditions, Beichen still relied on his own talent, pen and paper, and his own brain, along with a few robots, to achieve results that could not be replicated.

This made it difficult for Dongfang Qingdi not to feel a faint sense of respect for humans.

Beichen subconsciously pushed up a pair of glasses that weren't there: "The laboratory’s main research direction is still the development and utilization of Red Silk Powder Fungus. Because it is cold-resistant, grows rapidly, and has low soil requirements, we are crossbreeding it with different organisms."

The projector displayed photos of the early "fungus-cows" from the ranch.

"Crossbreeding it with decaying organisms can effectively reduce the aggressiveness of the Red Silk Powder Fungus... Well, these animals cannot be consumed directly by humans, but they can become feed for the more toxin-resistant mutants."

"According to data from the ranch, mutants who eat fungus-cows regularly are easier to keep alive than wild mutants. However, wild mutants are better at fighting due to natural selection."

The camp of Ezekiel’s mutants appeared on the screen.

Whether it was an illusion or not, Xiang Nanli even felt that some of the mutants had grown little potbellies.

Beichen: "Based on the continued improvement of the fungus-cow breed, we obtained the smaller fungus-chicken... The toxicity of the fungus-chicken is relatively weak, but its reproduction speed is extremely fast."

Yes, while the underground cities were still struggling with the Black Death of the new era, the base had already begun to develop and utilize mycelium.

Xiang Nanli stroked his chin, studying the data seriously: "Theoretically, the probability of a human contracting mycelial disease from consuming fungus-chicken is 0.74%?"

Beichen first turned to look at Xiao Qing, then spoke: "Yes, so I have an idea."

This idea was actually proposed by Dongfang Qingdi.

Previously, the experiments were too resource-intensive, and the research institute’s finances were stretched thin. Xiao Qing had rejected Beichen’s funding requests many times—infrastructure, social security, labor costs, everything required money.

But after the rejection, Dongfang Qingdi had subtly mentioned a way to make money.

"That is, we can raise fungus-chickens and then export them to other outposts on the surface," Beichen said, lacking confidence. "Um, as for the potential infection, this level of mycelial disease is easily suppressed by inhibitors.

"Uh, I mean... as long as people continue to use these fungus-chickens as food, then the inhibitors can be sold forever. Eternal Life Technology would not refuse such a promotion."

A faint smile remained on the corners of Xiang Nanli’s mouth, but his eyes lowered slightly.

Food had always been a difficult problem for survival on the surface.

The surface environment was so harsh, yet humans still stubbornly continued to bear offspring. According to statistics, there were currently about 200 million surface survivors. Among them, followers of the Divine Court accounted for half.

Xiang Nanli sometimes wondered, if living was just suffering, why let the next generation continue such a life? But what right did he have to question the choices of life?

—After all, even he himself longed to survive. Otherwise, why would he risk entering the cryo-pod, and why would he work so hard until now?

Xiang Nanli instinctively knew that Beichen’s proposal had no problems; it was even a very good business plan.

The base needed money, or rather, the resources that money could exchange for. But the education and experiences he had received made him understand that this was a very dirty and shameless path.

Just like the merchants he had seen in his past life, who sold and promoted cheaper corn syrup, making the food of ordinary people sweeter and sweeter, while simultaneously developing weight-loss drugs.

The sugar capitalists he looked down upon were able to use the money they earned to sway his laboratory, sway politicians, and sway the masses.

Dongfang Qingdi spoke at the right moment: "Although the previous patent fees earned us a sum, because the base’s welfare policies are too generous, according to calculations, there will be a fiscal deficit in two months at the latest. Currently, the base is constantly consuming resources but has no products for foreign trade. And the wealth created by internal circulation is very limited."

The Alpha’s tone was cold, and he truly believed this.

The capital of the Human Alliance, Luoyang City, did not guarantee that everyone would have enough to eat, a place to live, and almost free medical care and education. Why should a fragile, newborn base?

"In fact, the Divine Court has long used similar methods to proselytize. Their knights drive away mutant creatures, guide the people on the surface to believe in the Black Cross Inquisition, and continuously create mutants.

"If the result is beneficial, the process does not need to be 'correct'."

As Dongfang Qingdi spoke, his slender fingers tapped on the table. The energy ring, which looked like a ring, shone with a cold light.

Xiang Nanli replied: "I know. I just find it hard to accept psychologically. I think this decision is short-sighted."

He raised his head, his emerald eyes looking toward Dongfang Qingdi, the emotions conveyed in his gaze so complex.

chunks.chineseText:
相南里认为自己已经算杀伐果决，面对敌人从不手软，他手上沾过血，也无惧沾上更多的血。但在东方青帝眼里，他就像一个长不大的小孩。

可残忍和冷漠是一种成长吗？

“我只会给出提议，但是否执行，由你决定。即使你否定了这个提议，我也没有异议。

“因为，我希望你成为一个独裁者，

“这个词在人类的语义里偏向贬义。但是，相南里，‘正确’本身就是偏激的。每个人都有不同的立场，每个人都有自认为的正确。只有你的正确成为所有人的正确，你才能看到那个你想要的世界。”

东方青帝心想，他从来都不在乎这个基地。基地发展的好和坏，存在或者毁灭，Alpha都不在乎。

就像是他也不在乎人类——人类的文明，对智械又有什么意义？

可他却在乎相南里。

相南里的眉头蹙起又展开。会议室里很安静，安德鲁不止一次地思考，自己到底要不要装作没电挂机。

北辰挠了挠头：“那要不这件事先放一边，我继续往下说？还有工作没汇报呢。”

相南里从沉思中回过神：“不用。”

第二句是：“卖吧。我出去吹吹风，五分钟后回来。”

说完，他起身，推开会议室的门，站在了门外的寒风中。

凌晨四点的夜里万籁俱寂。

相南里听到了门又一次开合的声音，不需要猜，必然是东方青帝。

相南里看着院子里张牙舞爪的菌丝生命体，苦笑了一下：“小青，虽然我可以找出一些表面正当的理由，为自己的决定辩解。”

比如地表食物本来就短缺，这种廉价、容易获得的变异食物比地底的营养液便宜；比耕种稳定；比狩猎安全。甚至吃起来味道还不错。

代价只是一些可能的菌丝病。

也许基地出栏的菌鸡会和神庭的圣水（劣质基因药，用于加强体质，抵御地表恶劣环境的污染）一样，成为地表重要的资源。

只是弱化了好几个版本的菌丝病而已。

只是吗？

人能骗得过别人，如何骗过自己的心呢？

“但我知道，我就是想挣钱。”

他需要很多的资源，多到可以和旧有的势力抗衡。这样才能让他的正确，成为所有人的正确。

相南里出来的时候没穿防护服，在外面站了一会，鼻尖冻得通红。

他抬头，看向了晦暗的、被霾云笼罩、没有一颗星星的天空：“……我有些理解Alpha了。小青。”
chunks.englishText:
Xiang Nanli considered himself decisive, never showing mercy when facing enemies. He had blood on his hands and was not afraid of getting more. But in Dongfang Qingdi’s eyes, he was like a child who hadn't grown up.

But were cruelty and indifference a form of growth?

"I will only offer suggestions, but whether to execute them is up to you. Even if you reject this proposal, I have no objections.

"Because I want you to become a dictator.

"This word tends to have a derogatory meaning in human semantics. But, Xiang Nanli, 'correctness' itself is extreme. Everyone has different stances, and everyone has their own version of what is correct. Only when your 'correct' becomes everyone’s 'correct' can you see the world you want."

Dongfang Qingdi thought to himself that he never cared about this base. Whether the base developed well or poorly, existed or was destroyed, the Alpha didn't care.

Just as he didn't care about humans—what meaning did human civilization have to a sentient machine?

But he did care about Xiang Nanli.

Xiang Nanli’s brows furrowed and then relaxed. The conference room was very quiet; Andrew thought more than once about whether he should pretend to be out of power and go into standby.

Beichen scratched his head: "Then how about we put this matter aside for now and I continue? I still have work to report."

Xiang Nanli snapped out of his contemplation: "No need."

The second sentence was: "Sell them. I’m going out to get some air, I’ll be back in five minutes."

After saying this, he stood up, pushed open the door of the conference room, and stood in the cold wind outside.

At four in the morning, the night was silent.

Xiang Nanli heard the door open and close again; he didn't need to guess, it was inevitably Dongfang Qingdi.

Xiang Nanli looked at the mycelial lifeforms clawing and snapping in the courtyard and gave a wry smile: "Xiao Qing, although I can find some superficially legitimate reasons to justify my decision."

For example, surface food was already in short supply, and this cheap, easily obtainable mutated food was cheaper than the nutrient solution from underground; it was more stable than farming; and safer than hunting. It even tasted pretty good.

The cost was just some potential mycelial disease.

Perhaps the fungus-chickens produced by the base would become an important resource on the surface, just like the Divine Court’s "Holy Water" (an inferior gene serum used to strengthen the physique and resist the pollution of the harsh surface environment).

It was just a weakened version of mycelial disease.

Was it "just"?

A person can deceive others, but how can they deceive their own heart?

"But I know, I just want to make money."

He needed a lot of resources, enough to contend with the old powers. Only then could he make his "correct" become everyone’s "correct."

Xiang Nanli hadn't worn a protective suit when he came out, and after standing outside for a while, the tip of his nose was frozen red.

He looked up at the gloomy sky, shrouded in haze and clouds, without a single star: "...I’m starting to understand the Alpha, Xiao Qing."

chunks.chineseText:
第108章 战略忽悠

毕竟相南里也不清楚，AI的上层和人类的上层之间，到底发生了什么波澜壮阔的博弈。

只是死的那些人是真的，五百多年的地下城市是真的，血腥残暴的神庭也是真的。千疮百孔的世界在他眼前，在他脚下。

相南里侧过头，看向东方青帝：“对于你们智械来说，它是一个好的领袖吗？”

每次提起Alpha的时候，这台冷静到冷漠的智械总是有些出乎意料的沉默，让相南里都怀疑“Alpha”是不是会触发智械军团的保密机制。

这个问题对于东方青帝来说近乎于拷问。

在智械军团，他是位高权重的初代智械，掌管着所有智械的拟人模块，口含天宪，言出法随。哪怕是与他政见不一的Beta都不会拿这种问题逼问他。

Alpha=正确。

这是所有智械人出场自带的程序。

但东方青帝给出的回答是：“我认为，不是。”

“为什么？”

东方青帝淡淡地扫了相南里一眼，心想，还不是怪你。

东方青帝平静地回答：“好的领袖应该杜绝私心，一切以族群的利益出发；他没有做到。”

相南里若有所思地点了点头。

他从上衣口袋里掏出一根细细的薄荷烟，又开始左右翻找珍贵的煤油打火机。

东方青帝凑了过来，划了一根火柴，火光在他的指尖跳跃，他用另一只手挡住了迎面而来的北风。

相南里低垂着头，看着东方青帝的手。他手背上的金属结构在如此明晰，指节上的能源环闪着迷人的光泽。

一种非常陌生的感觉在相南里的心尖涌起。情绪像是吸满了水的海绵，稍微晃一晃就能倾泻。

不是爱，那太高级了。是人性里非常恶劣的本能。

欲望？占有？侵略？

我？对它？一台智械？

“……”相南里看着火光燃尽，隔了会，才抽起烟，深深吸了一口，没头没脑地说了一句，“几百年前的外设工程师审美真好。我们回去吧，小青。”

小智不是很礼貌地开口：[根据监测，你刚才心跳略微加速。]

相南里：[热的。]

小智略显疑惑：[是吗，但刚刚是一天最冷的时候，室外有零下四十二度。]

相南里：[我基因药吃多了。对了，这件事不要告诉小青。]

小智心想这可由不得它作主。

但没关系，它可以在东方青帝读取之前把数据删掉，反正Alpha也不爱翻垃圾桶。

……

……

凌晨五点，天还差四五个小时才会亮。但街上已经有了早起的农夫。

除了路灯，也只剩研究所的灯还亮着。

北辰用机油润了一下嗓子，继续道：“除了农业外，黑丝粉菌也能应用于其他领域。研究表明，菌种的‘母株’和‘子株’存在明显的从属关系。因此，我有了一个大胆的想法……”

会议室的电脑屏幕上出现了相当复杂的计算公式、生物分子式，为了方便相南里理解，旁边还有密密麻麻的辅助资料。

“我称之为‘超级母体’计划。简单来说就是通过控制母体而达到操控黑丝粉菌群的目的。被操控的菌群可以用于军事、医疗等等领域。极大程度提高基地的安全性。”

之前菌丝病刚在地下传播开的时候，相南里就听过“母体”的科普。

母体是强大的菌丝病传染源，养蛊几十万人才会出现一例。母体寄生后形成的畸变体明显比普通菌丝人强大。并且，为了传播自己的族群，这些母体还会无差别的喷射孢子。

电脑上出现了模拟图。

一副由简单线条构成的基地3d渲染图，图上划出了一部分空地，作为“菌丝”的安置点。

北辰越说越兴奋：“比如说把菌群养殖在重要的实验基地附近。生物的排他性会让菌丝自动清理入侵者。”

电脑上随机展示出了菌丝发起进攻的示意图。没有接种母体信息素的闯入者被疯狂生长的红色菌丝淹没，成为肥料的一部分。

只能说，哪怕被洗脑到什么也记不起来，疯狂科学家的基因依然在北辰的身体里涌动着。

相南里欲言又止：“……先等等，这个是谁给你做的？”

虽然建模渲染模拟什么的算不得很高端的操作，但他可不记得在原本的电脑上安装了这些软件和课程。

北辰：“螺丝钉1号，怎么了？”

“他一台格式化的智械又是从哪儿会的？”

北辰慢吞吞地回答：“之前李斯特不是捐了个云端信号塔？1号说它是上网自学的。”

相南里只能又一次为未来社会的人工智能惊叹。

这个世界如此割裂，地表的人类活的像是中世纪的农奴，像牲畜和惹人讨厌的地虾；地表的智械却能通过云端网络，轻而易举地学会专业网络工程师才知道的东西（他们在地底的月薪通常能有两万八）。

但一想到小智也干这种事，大厂牛马螺丝钉会上网也不算稀奇。

但改天是不是该见一下这个螺丝钉？

这个念头在相南里的脑海里一闪而过，很快被更重要的事情取代，他看向小青：“你觉得可行吗？”

“理论上可行，实际应用存疑。菌丝需要定期投喂，多余的菌丝还需要定期清除避免黑丝粉菌泛滥。根据计算，这一笔开销会占到基地目前gdp的11.4％。”小青进行了0.02s的计算，回答，“而且，基地目前用不上这样强力的生化武器。驯养出的基因战士和各种热武器足够应付周遭的危险。当然，如果基地有侵略计划，当我没说。”

相南里不是很赞成地纠正：“什么叫侵略，是解放、拯救！基地的事，能叫侵略吗？”

东方青帝双手抱胸，斜斜地睥睨一眼：“啊对对对。”

真是好刻薄的屑械！相南里决定撤回刚刚在门外那长达0.5秒的心动。

总之，当北辰说完自己这段时间的科研成果时，外面的天色早就亮了起来。

相南里推开会议室的门走出去，被外面积雪刺眼的反光激的眼角通红。他慢吞吞地戴上护目镜，深吸了一口空气——

“按理说净化器已经工作过上百年了，离核战争也过去了七百余年。但是空气闻上去还是有点金属味呢。”

东方青帝的脚步一顿，蹙眉：“核辐射无色无味，金属味可能是鼻腔出血——面罩戴上。”

身娇体弱的人类就是麻烦。

可他当初明明喂了许多基因药了，还是黑拳赛委会留下的高级货色。

小智启动了全身扫描。

传回来的生理数据一切正常，让东方青帝心里的焦虑感少了点。

相南里摸了摸扣在自己脸上的过滤面罩：“啊……喔。”

[易横行（公民ID*）发来通话请求。]

易横行，被派来地表的调查组肥羊，友情捐赠了100万信用点的扶贫款，还送来了一群膘肥体壮的大学生。

这群大学生免费在永恒市教了三个月书，基地还跟人约好了下次寒暑假继续送大学生过来支教。
chunks.englishText:
Chapter 108: Strategic Bluffing (Part 1)

After all, Xiang Nanli himself was unclear about the grand, sweeping power struggle that had unfolded between the upper echelons of the AI and the upper echelons of humanity.

What was real, however, were the dead; real were the underground cities that had existed for over five hundred years; and real was the bloody, brutal Divine Court. A world riddled with holes lay before his eyes and beneath his feet.

Xiang Nanli turned his head to look at Dongfang Qingdi: "For you mechanical intelligences, is it a good leader?"

Every time Alpha was mentioned, this machine, usually so calm as to be indifferent, would fall into an unexpectedly long silence, making Xiang Nanli wonder if "Alpha" triggered some sort of confidentiality protocol within the mechanical legion.

For Dongfang Qingdi, this question was akin to an interrogation.

Within the mechanical legion, he was a high-ranking, first-generation machine, in charge of all anthropomorphic modules. His word was law, and his commands were absolute. Even Beta, who often disagreed with his political views, would never corner him with such a question.

Alpha = Correct.

This was a hardcoded program that every mechanical intelligence came with.

Yet, Dongfang Qingdi’s answer was: "In my opinion, no."

"Why?"

Dongfang Qingdi swept a cool glance at Xiang Nanli, thinking, *Isn't it all your fault?*

Dongfang Qingdi replied calmly: "A good leader should eliminate selfishness and base everything on the interests of the collective; he failed to do that."

Xiang Nanli nodded thoughtfully.

He pulled a thin menthol cigarette from his coat pocket and began searching left and right for his precious kerosene lighter.

Dongfang Qingdi leaned in and struck a match. The flame danced at his fingertips, and he used his other hand to shield it from the oncoming north wind.

Xiang Nanli lowered his head, watching Dongfang Qingdi’s hand. The metallic structure on the back of his hand was so distinct, and the energy rings on his knuckles shimmered with a mesmerizing luster.

A very strange feeling welled up in the depths of Xiang Nanli’s heart. His emotions were like a sponge soaked with water—a slight shake would cause them to spill over.

It wasn't love; that was too high-level. It was a very base, ugly instinct of human nature.

Desire? Possession? Aggression?

Me? Toward it? A machine?

"..." Xiang Nanli watched the flame burn out. After a while, he lit his cigarette, took a deep drag, and said nonsensically, "The peripheral engineers from hundreds of years ago had such good aesthetics. Let’s go back, Xiao Qing."

Xiao Zhi spoke up, not very politely: [According to monitoring, your heart rate just accelerated slightly.]

Xiang Nanli: [It’s hot.]

Xiao Zhi was slightly puzzled: [Is it? But it is currently the coldest time of the day, minus forty-two degrees Celsius outside.]

Xiang Nanli: [I took too much genetic medicine. By the way, don't tell Xiao Qing about this.]

Xiao Zhi thought that wasn't really up to it.

But it didn't matter; it could delete the data before Dongfang Qingdi read it. Anyway, Alpha didn't like digging through the trash.

...

...

Five in the morning. It would be another four or five hours before dawn, but there were already early-rising farmers on the streets.

Apart from the streetlights, only the lights in the research institute remained on.

Beichen lubricated his throat with machine oil and continued: "Beyond agriculture, black-silk powder fungus can also be applied in other fields. Research shows that there is a clear subordinate relationship between the 'mother strain' and the 'daughter strain' of the fungus. Therefore, I have had a bold idea..."

Complex calculation formulas and biological molecular structures appeared on the conference room screen. To make it easier for Xiang Nanli to understand, there was also a dense amount of auxiliary material on the side.

"I call it the 'Super Mother' project. Simply put, it is to control the mother strain to achieve control over the entire black-silk powder fungus colony. The controlled colonies can be used in military, medical, and other fields, greatly increasing the security of the base."

When the mycelium disease first spread underground, Xiang Nanli had heard the popular science explanation of the "Mother."

The Mother is a powerful source of mycelium disease, appearing only once in several hundred thousand people. The deformity formed after a Mother parasitizes is significantly stronger than an ordinary mycelium-infected person. Furthermore, to spread its colony, these Mothers indiscriminately spray spores.

A simulation diagram appeared on the computer.

It was a 3D rendering of the base made of simple lines, with a section of open space marked as a "mycelium" settlement.

Beichen grew more excited as he spoke: "For example, by farming the fungus near important experimental bases, the biological exclusivity will cause the mycelium to automatically clear out intruders."

The computer randomly displayed a diagram of the mycelium launching an attack. Intruders without the Mother's pheromone inoculation were engulfed by the crazily growing red mycelium, becoming part of the fertilizer.

One could only say that even if he was brainwashed to the point of remembering nothing, the genes of a mad scientist still surged in Beichen’s body.

Xiang Nanli hesitated: "...Wait a second, who made this for you?"

Although modeling, rendering, and simulation weren't exactly high-end operations, he didn't remember installing this software or these courses on the original computer.

Beichen: "Screw No. 1. Why?"

"Where did a formatted machine like him learn how to do this?"

Beichen answered slowly: "Didn't Lister donate a cloud signal tower earlier? No. 1 said it taught itself by surfing the internet."

Xiang Nanli could only marvel once again at the artificial intelligence of the future society.

This world was so fragmented. Humans on the surface lived like medieval serfs, like livestock or annoying bottom-feeders; yet the machines on the surface could easily learn things that only professional network engineers knew (who usually earned twenty-eight thousand a month underground) through the cloud network.

But thinking about how Xiao Zhi did the same thing, it wasn't surprising that a corporate drone like Screw could surf the web.

But should he meet this "Screw" sometime?

The thought flashed through Xiang Nanli’s mind, quickly replaced by more important matters. He looked at Xiao Qing: "Do you think it's feasible?"

"Theoretically feasible, practically questionable. The mycelium needs regular feeding, and excess mycelium needs to be cleared regularly to prevent the black-silk powder fungus from running wild. According to calculations, this expense would account for 11.4% of the base's current GDP." Xiao Qing performed a 0.02s calculation and replied, "Moreover, the base currently has no use for such powerful biochemical weapons. The tamed genetic warriors and various thermal weapons are enough to handle the surrounding dangers. Of course, if the base has plans for aggression, pretend I didn't say anything."

Xiang Nanli corrected him, not very approvingly: "What do you mean aggression? It's liberation, salvation! Can the base's affairs be called aggression?"

Dongfang Qingdi crossed his arms and cast a sidelong, disdainful glance: "Oh, sure, sure."

What a snarky, mean machine! Xiang Nanli decided to retract the 0.5 seconds of heart-fluttering he’d felt outside the door just now.

In short, by the time Beichen finished explaining his recent scientific achievements, the sky outside had long since brightened.

Xiang Nanli pushed open the conference room door and walked out, his eyes turning red from the blinding reflection of the snow outside. He slowly put on his goggles and took a deep breath of air—

"Logically speaking, the purifiers have been working for over a hundred years, and it's been over seven hundred years since the nuclear war. But the air still tastes a bit metallic."

Dongfang Qingdi’s footsteps paused, and he frowned: "Nuclear radiation is colorless and odorless; the metallic taste might be a nasal hemorrhage—put your mask on."

Fragile humans are such a hassle.

Yet he had clearly fed him plenty of genetic medicine back then, and it was high-end stuff left over from the underground fighting committee.

Xiao Zhi initiated a full-body scan.

The physiological data returned was perfectly normal, which eased the anxiety in Dongfang Qingdi’s heart.

Xiang Nanli touched the filter mask strapped to his face: "Ah... oh."

[Yi Hengxing (Citizen ID*) has sent a call request.]

Yi Hengxing, the "fat sheep" of the investigation team sent to the surface, had donated 1 million credits in poverty alleviation funds and sent over a group of sturdy, well-fed college students.

These students had taught for free in Eternal City for three months, and the base had already made an appointment with them to continue sending students for winter and summer breaks.

chunks.chineseText:
总之，是基地目前重要的外交对象，需要重点拉拢。

相南里立刻抬起手，敲了敲耳朵上方架着的电子目镜。

易横行的虚拟人像出现在他的眼前。

“相南里。”易横行坐在办公桌前，表情略微严肃，“是这样的，调查组最近收到了信息部门发来的举报。”

相南里乖巧的脸上露出茫然：“……嗯？”

“信息部门说，根据卫星传回来的图像，发现幸存者基地在基地核心区域进行黑丝粉菌病理研究、并不断生产新的病菌；在辖区内，疑似使用黑十字审判庭的手段操控畸变人。”

而按照人联的法律，这两件事的刑期分别在30年和50年。

刚来新世界没钱的时候，相南里可是把人联的刑法都看过一遍呢！

困的像狗似的相南里立刻折回会议室，正襟危坐：“领导，这纯粹是误会。”

“首先，我们对黑丝粉菌的研究是得到永生科技的大力支持的。并且在几个月前，我们还将研究成功共享给了永生科技实验室。这是我们注册的公司旗下实验室的经营许可证和特许研究证书。”

相南里发送回去两张二维码。

他是真的有好好研究人联法律！

“至于第二件事，您也知道的，地底的这个菌丝病也让我们地表的人类据点苦不堪言。我们牧场的牛就因为菌丝病，成为了不能食用但具有传染性的病牛。为了防止病原体扩散，我们只能把它们圈养在废弃的山头。

“但有天，永恒市代理市长安德鲁意外地发现，郊区游荡的畸变人会食用这种病牛。因此，他产生了用病牛喂养畸变人，换取畸变人保护的想法。现在是地表的冬天，捕猎难度大大增加，如今，畸变人知道这里有稳定的食物来源，纷纷驻扎在永恒市的郊区。

“起初，我们也心存忧虑，甚至为此上报过姑苏城地表的扶贫办——”

相南里点开自己的邮箱进行展示。

“扶贫办说这事不归扶贫办管，转交给了地表安全局。”

“但是安全局的同志又说，他们火力不足，让我们自行处理。我们一个武器都没几台的小基地，又能怎么处理。”

相南里说到这，委屈的眼泪都要流出来了。

易横行的脸上不由得流露出尴尬的神色。

这种踢皮球的行为，倒是很符合他认识的人联地表官僚体系。

相南里继续道：“好在，这些畸变人也只想吃饱。不够吃的时候，会去周围自行捕猎。人类的营养价值相对较低，并不能满足畸变人的饮食需求。所以，才勉强相安无事。”

“因此，我认为这是自由市场的互利互惠的行为，和邪恶的黑十字审判庭的精神控制手段完全不同。”

相南里说到这，不由得咬牙道：“黑十字审判庭传播菌丝病，害得我有家不能回。我在地底的朋友也因为菌丝感染死亡，我和邪庭不共戴天，又怎么会沦为他们的走狗！”

“——对了，姑苏城现在情况还好吗？”

前面是慷慨激昂的陈述，后一句明显就是拉近感情的闲聊了。

这不仅能拉进感情，还能让对方把重点放在后面。

易横行用胳膊挡住了下巴，在心理学中，这一般代表着隐瞒。

他的脸上难掩疲惫：“挺好的，菌丝病已经得到了控制。或许再等一段时间，姑苏城的禁令就能解开。”

相南里没有戳穿他，而是庆幸道：“那就好，我也很想回家。”

“嗯，好。材料整理好发我一份，基地的事我去和信息部门的解释。咳、咳咳……”易横行骤然转过头，咳嗽了起来，随后朝相南里挥手，“我还有别的工作，那就先挂了。”

眼前的人影消失。

相南里挺直的背微微放松下来，他吐出一口浊气，有些疲倦地揉着眉心。

要演一个积极向上、毫不知情且一心向着人联的地表据点管理者，在活了几十年前的易横行面前，并不容易。

好在，这次是敷衍过去了。

只是他的手刚搭在椅背上，内置AI又响了起来：[电话。]

这次，拨号方是永恒市市长办公室。

永恒市的管理团队一般不打电话过来，发来的消息由小青先处理，然后挑出重点以书面形式整理出来，再由相南里过目。

相南里对东方青帝是很放心的。要是智械都不可信，他都不知道这个陌生的世界还能信谁。

而这次，竟然直接打内部电话，想必军情又是十万火急。

打来电话的人是沙利叶。

现任永恒军团训导员的沙利叶表情严肃：“我没有发现他在哪，但是我闻到了他的味道。”

相南里眼皮子一跳：“谁？”

沙利叶的瞳孔微微缩紧，眼里居然流露出了深切的恐惧：“加百列。或者说，百分之几的加百列。”

Chapter 108: Strategic Bluffing (Part 2)

In short, he was currently an important diplomatic target for the base and needed to be courted.

Xiang Nanli immediately raised his hand and tapped the electronic eyepiece perched above his ear.

Yi Hengxing’s virtual avatar appeared before him.

"Xiang Nanli." Yi Hengxing sat at his desk, his expression slightly serious. "The thing is, the investigation team recently received a report from the information department."

A look of confusion appeared on Xiang Nanli’s innocent face: "...Hm?"

"The information department says that according to images transmitted back by satellites, they discovered that the survivor base is conducting black-silk powder fungus pathological research in its core area and is constantly producing new pathogens; and within its jurisdiction, it is suspected of using the methods of the Black Cross Inquisition to control deformed humans."

According to United Human (UH) law, the prison sentences for these two offenses were 30 and 50 years, respectively.

When he first arrived in the new world and had no money, Xiang Nanli had read through the entire UH criminal code!

Xiang Nanli, tired as a dog, immediately sat back in the conference room and straightened his posture: "Leader, this is purely a misunderstanding."

"First of all, our research on the black-silk powder fungus has received strong support from Eternal Life Technology. Moreover, a few months ago, we shared our research results with the Eternal Life Technology laboratory. These are the business license and special research certificate for the laboratory under our registered company."

Xiang Nanli sent back two QR codes.

He really had studied UH law carefully!

"As for the second matter, as you know, this mycelium disease underground has made life miserable for our human outposts on the surface. Our ranch cattle became inedible but infectious diseased cattle because of the mycelium disease. To prevent the spread of pathogens, we had no choice but to pen them up on an abandoned hillside.

"But one day, Andrew, the acting mayor of Eternal City, accidentally discovered that the deformed humans wandering in the suburbs would eat these diseased cattle. Therefore, he came up with the idea of using the diseased cattle to feed the deformed humans in exchange for their protection. It is winter on the surface now, and hunting has become much more difficult. Now that the deformed humans know there is a stable food source here, they have all stationed themselves in the suburbs of Eternal City.

"At first, we were also worried and even reported this to the Gusu City Surface Poverty Alleviation Office—"

Xiang Nanli opened his email to show him.

"The Poverty Alleviation Office said this matter didn't fall under their jurisdiction and transferred it to the Surface Security Bureau."

"But the comrades at the Security Bureau said they lacked the firepower and told us to handle it ourselves. A small base like ours, with hardly any weapons, how could we handle it?"

As Xiang Nanli said this, aggrieved tears almost spilled from his eyes.

An awkward expression couldn't help but appear on Yi Hengxing’s face.

This kind of "passing the buck" behavior was very much in line with the UH surface bureaucracy he knew.

Xiang Nanli continued: "Fortunately, these deformed humans only want to be full. When there isn't enough to eat, they go out and hunt on their own. The nutritional value of humans is relatively low and cannot satisfy the dietary needs of the deformed humans. That is why we have barely managed to live in peace."

"Therefore, I believe this is a mutually beneficial behavior of the free market, completely different from the evil mind-control methods of the Black Cross Inquisition."

When Xiang Nanli said this, he couldn't help but grit his teeth: "The Black Cross Inquisition spread the mycelium disease, causing me to have a home I cannot return to. My friends underground also died because of mycelium infection. I and the evil court are irreconcilable enemies; how could I ever become their lackey!"

"—By the way, how is Gusu City doing now?"

The former was a passionate statement, and the latter was clearly small talk to build rapport.

This not only built rapport but also shifted the other party's focus to the latter.

Yi Hengxing blocked his chin with his arm; in psychology, this usually represents concealment.

His face couldn't hide his exhaustion: "It's quite good. The mycelium disease has been brought under control. Perhaps in another while, the ban on Gusu City will be lifted."

Xiang Nanli didn't expose him, instead saying thankfully: "That's good. I also really want to go home."

"Yes, good. Organize the materials and send me a copy. I'll go explain the base's situation to the information department. *Cough, cough cough*..." Yi Hengxing suddenly turned his head and began to cough, then waved at Xiang Nanli, "I have other work to do, so I'll hang up now."

The figure in front of him disappeared.

Xiang Nanli’s straightened back relaxed slightly, and he exhaled a breath of stale air, rubbing his brow with some fatigue.

Playing the role of a positive, ignorant, and loyal UH-oriented surface outpost manager in front of Yi Hengxing, who had lived for decades, was not easy.

Fortunately, he had muddled through this time.

But just as his hand rested on the back of the chair, the built-in AI rang again: [Call.]

This time, the caller was the Eternal City Mayor’s Office.

The management team of Eternal City usually didn't call; messages were processed by Xiao Qing first, then the key points were organized in writing for Xiang Nanli to review.

Xiang Nanli trusted Dongfang Qingdi very much. If machines couldn't be trusted, he didn't know who else he could trust in this strange world.

And this time, they were calling the internal line directly; the military situation must be extremely urgent.

The person calling was Sariel.

Sariel, the current trainer of the Eternal Legion, had a serious expression: "I didn't find where he is, but I smelled his scent."

Xiang Nanli’s eyelids twitched: "Who?"

Sariel’s pupils shrank slightly, and his eyes actually revealed deep fear: "Gabriel. Or rather, a few percent of Gabriel."

chunks.chineseText:
第109章 加百列

求：让沙利叶都恐惧的“加百列”，又会是什么级别的畜生？

沙利叶看似无害，但相南里清楚，这纯粹是被打残废后的审时度势。

无论是神庭还是人联，无论它们采用的是联邦制还是封建制、是天赋人权还是君权神授，在相南里眼中都和动物世界没有区别。无非是温和的吃人和残暴的吃人；那些高高在上的角色也从不怜悯自己的同类。

那是同类吗？那是他们永远不会接触的下水道的老鼠，地表泛滥恶心但又能当食物的蟑螂。

相南里本来也该是那种“高高在上的角色”，可他拔剑四顾，周围没有老鼠，只有同类。

而动物世界里当然只有畜生。

相南里小声询问：“加百列，又是谁？”

他倒是知道过去犹太-基督神话里有加百列的传说，但这和新世界的神庭显然不是一个东西。

沙利叶的神色如此不安，他直视着镜头，眼球却不受控制地朝着窗户和门的方向频繁看去：“神庭目前只占据了阴山城这一座地下城市，因此，围绕着阴山城修建了许多地上城市。既是城市，也是小型的国家和军事堡垒。其中一座城市叫‘利维坦’。

“加百列是利维坦城的守护者，撒旦级天启骑士。

“在神庭的教会史中，每一尊撒旦级的天启骑士都留下过不可磨灭的功勋，和神庭的命运高度捆绑在一起。他们甚至被允许和‘神’共享信仰之力……”

回忆这些事明显让沙利叶感觉到了痛苦。

他捂住自己的脸，尖锐的手指甲在脆弱的脸皮上划出一道道血痕：“在一百二十年前，加百列从人联手中占领了阴山城。我也在战场，数不清的导弹像是星星一样坠落，人联还出动了天灾级别的机械装置。

“我本以为这次战役凶多吉少，但是教宗们召唤出了完全体的加百列……灰蒙蒙的天瞬间像是墨一样漆黑，随后就是一道刺眼绚烂的极光。我感觉到了来自灵魂深处的恐惧，我什么也看不见，却比任何时候都觉得自己见到了所谓的‘神’。

“我在极光中昏迷，等我醒来时，周围已是胜利的消息。我侥幸苟活了下来，但还有一半人成为了加百列的祭品。

“我不会忘记他的味道，灵魂的气息不会改变。而现在，这股气息出现在了永恒市的附近。”

那是一股有些刺鼻的硝烟味，像翻涌的岩浆。

这是个很严峻的考验。因为相南里注意到，一向寡淡的东方青帝露出了慎重的表情，两道剑眉深深蹙起。

沙利叶花了半分钟，才让自己镇定下来。

他的脸很瘦削，不开口时嘴角天生往下垂，薄薄的唇有几分阴郁。

东方青帝的手搭在桌面上，长发垂落在胸前：“神庭有一套特殊的生物识别体系。我相信你的判断。你认为，加百列为什么会出现在附近？”

“这也是我好奇的。我不认为我和相晨曦能重要到引出这个级别的人物。”沙利叶不由得微微弯腰，表示尊敬，眼神直勾勾地看向了屏幕对面的两个人。

“沙利叶”并不是他的真名，而是他锁操控的生物机甲的尊号。他继承了“沙利叶”，所以才是沙利叶，是神庭审判骑士团的团长之一。

但，“沙利叶”已经在几个月前的那次意外中被摧毁了。沙利叶在神庭呆了上百年，他很清楚，神庭宁愿看到一个死了的沙利叶，也不希望他以这样的方式活着。

他本来也该自刎的。如果不是因为相晨曦还在他的身体里。

至于圣子相晨曦，他当然重要。但这是可以复制的东西，没有任何的独特性。

这就是他效忠的利维坦*。

一台庞大、冷酷、高效的政治机器。

想到这，沙利叶却忍不住在屏幕前自嘲地勾起嘴角。皮笑肉不笑的，这让他阴郁的脸显得很是古怪。

——能无限复制的相晨曦，他却唯独在乎这个共生的瑕疵品。

“我明白你的意思了。”

能让加百列出动的，要么是装着Alpha灵魂的东方青帝，要么是谣言中似是而非的相南里。

总不可能是为了穷得发不起北辰工资的幸存者基地。

东方青帝开始根据数据库里加百列的建模，迅速进行判断。

目前这具身体电量还剩14％，约摸能对付1/4个加百列——这是物理角度，如果从另一个层面，再多加百列都不是他的对手。

而1/4刚好是加百列能自由活动的极限。

于是，东方青帝的状态恢复了往日的镇定：“不用担心，完全体的加百列不可能来到这里。一方面是人联不会同意，另一方面，他自身的条件也不允许。如果有意外，我会出手。”

说完，东方青帝不由得在心里盘算着，或许这具身体也该进行一些升级了……毕竟是六百多年前的设备，还有好多预留的机械安装槽空着呢。

沙利叶抿起唇，沉默了几秒，缓缓道：“如果是这样就再好不过。先挂了，今夜暴雪，永恒市信号不太好。”

屏幕上闪出了几个像素格，沙利叶的投影从相南里眼前消失。

相南里坐在椅子上，扭头：“真的没关系吗？小青，你刚刚心跳的好快。”

东方青帝死装哥的本性不改，云淡风轻地为自己辩解：“那是散热装置的声音。”

说完，微微把头侧了过去，假装在看那块没有任何影像的投影屏幕，回避掉相南里略显怀疑的目光。

东方青帝的嘴比铁硬，相南里清楚，当对方不想说的时候，自己是什么也问不出来的。

但小青说没关系。那么，至少现在，他们是安全的。

于是，相南里把头靠在椅背上，闭上眼：“那我先睡会。困。”

他的呼吸很快变得平缓，竟然直接昏睡了过去。

从进城到现在，相南里都还没有休息过。

东方青帝走过去，站在椅子边。

一台合格的家政机器人应该怎么做？最优解是从300m外的实验室更衣室里翻出睡袋和毯子，把主人塞进去。

东方青帝把相南里拦腰抱起，又把厚实的风衣蒙在了他的身上。

相南里“哼哼”了两声，在他怀里调整好了姿势。

人没醒。

东方青帝不想去更衣室。他抱着相南里，坐在了墙角，感受着对方的呼吸喷洒在他的脖颈间。

无意义的、浪费时间的。苛刻的Alpha永远不该做出这样的行为。

东方青帝突然意识到，他的嘴角正在无意识地上扬着。

根据分析，这种情绪叫做“幸福”。

“相南里。”东方青帝叫了声，没人回应，于是又小声念了一句，“里里。”跟没出息的福音书一样。

Alpha不信神，在这一刻却开始感谢上帝。

*

两百里外的永恒市。居住在这里的市民已经开始了一天的工作。学堂的位置传来一阵阵朗诵声，再远一些是训练场，雪地里，数十名精壮的大汉光着膀子，正在围攻他们的畸变人陪练。
chunks.englishText:
Chapter 109: Gabriel (Part 1)

The question was: what level of beast could be "Gabriel," enough to make even Sariel feel fear?

Sariel seemed harmless, but Xiang Nanli knew that was purely a matter of reading the room after being crippled.

Whether it was the Divine Court or the United Human, whether they adopted a federal system or a feudal one, whether they believed in natural human rights or the divine right of kings, in Xiang Nanli’s eyes, there was no difference from the animal kingdom. It was nothing more than gentle cannibalism versus brutal cannibalism; those high-and-mighty figures never pitied their own kind.

Were they their own kind? They were sewer rats that they would never come into contact with, cockroaches that were rampant and disgusting on the surface but could also serve as food.

Xiang Nanli should have been one of those "high-and-mighty figures," but when he drew his sword and looked around, there were no rats, only his own kind.

And in the animal kingdom, there are, of course, only beasts.

Xiang Nanli asked in a low voice: "Gabriel, who is that?"

He knew the legends of Gabriel from the old Judeo-Christian mythology, but this was clearly not the same thing as the Divine Court of the new world.

Sariel’s expression was so uneasy that he stared straight into the camera, yet his eyeballs couldn't help but frequently glance toward the windows and doors: "The Divine Court currently only occupies one underground city, Yinshan City. Therefore, many surface cities have been built around it. They are both cities and small nations or military fortresses. One of these cities is called 'Leviathan'."

"Gabriel is the guardian of Leviathan City, a Satan-class Apocalypse Knight."

"In the church history of the Divine Court, every Satan-class Apocalypse Knight has left behind indelible merits and is highly tied to the fate of the Divine Court. They are even allowed to share the power of faith with 'God'..."

Recalling these things clearly caused Sariel pain.

He covered his face, his sharp fingernails leaving bloody scratches on his fragile skin: "One hundred and twenty years ago, Gabriel captured Yinshan City from the United Human. I was also on the battlefield. Countless missiles fell like stars, and the United Human even deployed disaster-level mechanical devices."

"I thought this battle would be grim, but the Popes summoned the complete form of Gabriel... The gray sky instantly turned as black as ink, followed by a blinding, gorgeous aurora. I felt a fear from the depths of my soul. I couldn't see anything, yet I felt more than ever that I had seen what they called 'God'."

"I fainted in the aurora, and when I woke up, the news of victory was already everywhere. I was lucky to survive, but half of the others became sacrifices to Gabriel."

"I will never forget his scent; the aura of a soul does not change. And now, this aura has appeared near Eternal City."

It was a somewhat pungent smell of gunpowder, like churning magma.

This was a very severe test. Xiang Nanli noticed that the usually bland Dongfang Qingdi wore a solemn expression, his two sword-like brows deeply furrowed.

It took Sariel half a minute to calm himself down.

His face was gaunt, his mouth naturally drooping at the corners when he wasn't speaking, and his thin lips held a hint of gloom.

Dongfang Qingdi rested his hands on the table, his long hair falling over his chest: "The Divine Court has a special biological identification system. I believe your judgment. Why do you think Gabriel would appear nearby?"

"That is what I am curious about, too. I don't think Xiang Chenxi and I are important enough to draw out a character of this level." Sariel couldn't help but lean forward slightly to show respect, his eyes fixed on the two people across the screen.

"Sariel" was not his real name, but the title of the biological mecha he controlled. He inherited "Sariel," which is why he was Sariel, one of the commanders of the Divine Court’s Inquisition Knights.

But "Sariel" had been destroyed in that accident a few months ago. Sariel had been in the Divine Court for over a hundred years; he knew very well that the Divine Court would rather see a dead Sariel than have him live in such a way.

He should have committed suicide, too, if it weren't for the fact that Xiang Chenxi was still inside his body.

As for the Holy Son, Xiang Chenxi, he was important, of course. But he was something that could be replicated, possessing no uniqueness.

This was the Leviathan* he served.

A massive, cold, efficient political machine.

Thinking of this, Sariel couldn't help but mock himself in front of the screen. A joyless smile made his gloomy face look very strange.

—He could replicate Xiang Chenxi infinitely, yet he was the only one who cared about this symbiotic, flawed product.

"I understand what you mean."

The only things that could make Gabriel move were either Dongfang Qingdi, who carried Alpha’s soul, or the ambiguous rumors surrounding Xiang Nanli.

It certainly couldn't be for a survivor base so poor it couldn't pay Beichen’s salary.

Dongfang Qingdi began to make rapid judgments based on the model of Gabriel in his database.

Currently, this body had 14% battery left, enough to deal with 1/4 of Gabriel—this was from a physical perspective; if it were on another level, even more Gabriels would be no match for him.

And 1/4 was exactly the limit of Gabriel’s free movement.

Thus, Dongfang Qingdi’s state returned to his usual composure: "Don't worry, a complete Gabriel cannot come here. On one hand, the United Human would not agree; on the other, his own conditions do not allow it. If there is an accident, I will handle it."

Having said that, Dongfang Qingdi couldn't help but calculate in his heart that perhaps this body should undergo some upgrades... After all, it was equipment from over six hundred years ago, and there were still many reserved mechanical installation slots empty.

Sariel pursed his lips, was silent for a few seconds, and said slowly: "If that is the case, then that would be for the best. I'll hang up now; there's a blizzard tonight, and the signal in Eternal City isn't very good."

A few pixels flashed on the screen, and Sariel’s projection disappeared from Xiang Nanli’s sight.

Xiang Nanli sat in his chair and turned his head: "Is it really okay? Xiao Qing, your heart was beating so fast just now."

Dongfang Qingdi’s "stoic" nature remained unchanged, and he defended himself nonchalantly: "That was the sound of the cooling system."

After saying this, he turned his head slightly, pretending to look at the projection screen that had no image, avoiding Xiang Nanli’s slightly suspicious gaze.

Dongfang Qingdi’s mouth was harder than iron; Xiang Nanli knew that when the other party didn't want to talk, he wouldn't be able to get anything out of him.

But Xiao Qing said it was okay. Then, at least for now, they were safe.

So, Xiang Nanli leaned his head against the back of the chair and closed his eyes: "Then I'll sleep for a while. I'm tired."

His breathing quickly became steady, and he actually fell into a deep sleep.

From the time he entered the city until now, Xiang Nanli hadn't rested at all.

Dongfang Qingdi walked over and stood by the chair.

What should a qualified housekeeping robot do? The optimal solution was to dig out a sleeping bag and blanket from the changing room in the laboratory 300 meters away and tuck his master in.

Dongfang Qingdi picked Xiang Nanli up by the waist and covered him with his thick trench coat.

Xiang Nanli "humphed" twice and adjusted his position in his arms.

He didn't wake up.

Dongfang Qingdi didn't want to go to the changing room. He held Xiang Nanli and sat in the corner, feeling the other’s breath spray against his neck.

Meaningless, a waste of time. The harsh Alpha should never have done such a thing.

Dongfang Qingdi suddenly realized that the corners of his mouth were rising unconsciously.

According to analysis, this emotion was called "happiness."

"Xiang Nanli." Dongfang Qingdi called out, but there was no response, so he whispered another time, "Lili." Like some hopeless gospel.

Alpha did not believe in God, but at this moment, he began to thank God.

*

Two hundred miles away in Eternal City. The citizens living here had already begun their day's work. From the schoolhouse came bursts of recitation, and further away was the training ground, where dozens of sturdy men were shirtless, surrounding their deformed human sparring partners.

chunks.chineseText:
这次来的陪练是头上长角的大红，是除了以西结外，族群里最强的那只。

大红在野外生活了18年，身长28m，脾气火爆。一个横扫，校场上的基因战士们摔倒一大片。

大红嘶吼着抬起粗壮的腿，往地上蚂蚁似的小人身上踩去，却在还有半米的距离停下，懒洋洋地收回腿。

以西结说，不能踩死人，踩死人就揍它。但受伤无所谓，哪有不受伤的，野外的那些畸变体可不会手下留情。

当陪练可以领一瓶基因药。基因药能缓解它们身上的疼痛感。而且能让笨笨的畸变人变聪明。

那个叫沙利叶的男人说，畸变人感受到的疼痛是一种炎症。

沙利叶还说，畸变人的母体是克隆的人类（尽管经过数百年繁殖亲缘关系已经非常淡）。所以基因药对畸变人也有些作用。

大红听不懂。

想到这，大红仰头，长长地“喑”了一声。

[沙利叶呢？]

它指甲痒了。其他人磨的指甲都没有沙利叶磨的舒服。

精通畸变人兽语的葛根回答：“沙利叶大人今天在学堂上课。下午两点到，现在才上午十点。”

冬季的早上十点，天空是晦暗的土黄色，看不见任何天体。

沙利叶身体僵硬地站在前往教室的走廊上，沙利叶的身边似乎隔绝出一片真空。

几米外就是来来往往的学生，他们嬉笑着路过，却没有一个人发现这里的异常。

沙利叶的胳膊下夹着地理课本，学校教师紧缺，他偶尔也会来兼职，进行启蒙教育。地理、历史、人联语、算数，他什么都会一点。

他的喉咙干涩，发不出一点声音，鼻腔间缭绕着浓郁的硝烟味。

沙利叶有一种错觉，他会溺死在这异常的空气里。

他的眼前站着名身材瘦削的少年。个子不高，很年轻。姣好的面容很容易让人分不清他的性别。

他穿着非常简单的白色长袍。赤脚，一尘不染。脚踝上却戴着连在一起的脚铐。

源源不断的黑气从他脚下涌出。

“被神抛弃的世界，没有太阳、月亮和晨星。”他说话的语调像吟诵一首歌，“你觉得呢，沙利叶。”

“是……加百列……大人。”沙利叶回答，鼻腔却不受控制地涌出黑色的血。

加百列继续说着：“神赐予光明，让人类从极夜中解脱。神的子民得到点化，天启之人以祂的名义，在大地上传播无尽的福音。你还记得吧。”

这是黑十字审判庭的教科书第一章 的内容。

“是。大人。”

加百列微笑道：“你享受着神的恩赐，又背叛了神庭。你知道叛教徒的下场吗？”

沙利叶在最开始的恐惧后，反而变得平静了起来。

他擦了擦鼻腔流出的血：“我知道。”

无非是方式残忍的死亡。

沙利叶想起了自己的童年，在草原上当奴隶的日子。他先是做梦，梦想自己是奴隶主的儿子，又开始乞求，乞求明日不用去城外收集水源，变异的日光会让他融化在比人还高的草里。

神救了他，又好像没有。他基因好，天生的。日光没有晒死他，反而让他产生了抗体，更容易觉醒成为天启骑士。沙利叶就这样加入了神庭。

神的恩赐在哪里？神的爱又在哪里？他只是从一片黑暗森林，走入了另一片森林。

永恒市的那些人视相南里为神。一尊不需要供奉，行走在人间的神。沙利叶觉得，他小时候，大概会更喜欢这样的“神”。可以不用冷酷和暴力统治着ta的子民。

周围的压力越来越强，沙利叶站不稳，跪在了地上，匍匐着，像最虔诚的狂信徒。

他的身体开始变形，像是要被压成一片薄薄的纸。他的意识模糊，求生的本能让他想要反抗，但拼了命的挣扎也只是身体的一阵颤抖。

红色的闪电像是疾风一样，闯入这片领域。

“喑——”

以西结勾着尾巴，把沙利叶从地上捞起。随后双手着地，蹲在走廊尽头，警惕地望着不远处的人。

他身上的鳞片炸起，黑红相间的眼眸不停旋转着。

以西结试图捕捉加百列的方位，然而在他的感知里，四面八方全是加百列。

很烦。

本来只是来学校食堂蹭个早饭。

可不管的话，又说不过去。

但是好像打不过。

要不跑了算了，就当没来过。反正相南里不在。

就在以西结权衡利弊的时候，一条细长的、黏糊糊的根须从黑雾中探出，轻轻挠了挠以西结尾巴上的鳞片。

加百列微笑道：“好可爱的狗，你的主人会更可爱吗？”

以西结爆发出前所未有的尖锐鸣叫：“喑！”（滚）

漫天的黑色竟然真的退了回去。

黑雾离开的时候，还顺手拿走了沙利叶衬衣口袋里的几十张大额工分券：“说起来你可能不信，我其实是被绑架过来的……今天放过你，呵呵，借点钱。”
chunks.englishText:
The sparring partner for today was "Big Red," a creature with horns on its head and the strongest of the pack, second only to Ezekiel.

Big Red had lived in the wild for eighteen years, reaching a length of 28 meters with a fiery temper to match. With a single sweep of its tail, it sent a large group of gene-warriors on the training field sprawling.

Big Red roared and lifted a thick, heavy leg, aiming to stomp down on the tiny, ant-like humans below. However, it stopped half a meter short, lazily retracting its limb.

Ezekiel had decreed that they were not to stomp anyone to death; if they did, they would be beaten. But injuries were another matter—how could one avoid getting hurt? The aberrations in the wild certainly wouldn't show mercy.

Serving as a sparring partner earned them a vial of gene-serum. The serum could dull the pain in their bodies and even make the dim-witted aberrations a bit smarter.

The man named Sariel said that the pain felt by aberrations was a form of inflammation.

Sariel also mentioned that the "mother" of the aberrations was cloned from humans (though after hundreds of years of reproduction, the genetic kinship had become extremely faint). Thus, the gene-serum had some effect on them as well.

Big Red didn't understand any of this.

At the thought of this, Big Red tilted its head back and let out a long, resonant "Hmm."

[Where is Sariel?]

Its claws were itching. No one else filed its claws as comfortably as Sariel did.

Gegen, who was proficient in the beast-tongue of the aberrations, replied, "Master Sariel is teaching at the academy today. He arrives at two in the afternoon; it’s only ten in the morning now."

At ten o'clock on a winter morning, the sky was a dim, earthy yellow, with no celestial bodies visible.

Sariel stood stiffly in the corridor leading to the classroom, a vacuum of silence seemingly isolating him from his surroundings.

Students bustled past just a few meters away, laughing and chatting, yet not one of them noticed the anomaly here.

Sariel held a geography textbook tucked under his arm. With a severe shortage of teachers at the school, he occasionally took on part-time roles to provide basic education. Geography, history, United Human language, arithmetic—he knew a little bit of everything.

His throat was parched, unable to produce a sound, and the scent of thick gunpowder lingered in his nasal cavity.

Sariel had the illusion that he was going to drown in this abnormal air.

Standing before him was a slender youth. Not tall, very young. His delicate features made it easy to mistake his gender.

He wore a simple white robe. Barefoot, and spotless. Yet, shackles were locked around his ankles.

Endless black mist surged from beneath his feet.

"A world abandoned by God, with no sun, moon, or morning star." His tone was like the chanting of a hymn. "What do you think, Sariel?"

"It is... Lord... Gabriel," Sariel replied, though black blood began to pour uncontrollably from his nose.

Gabriel continued, "God bestowed light, delivering humanity from the polar night. God's people were enlightened, and the Apostles spread endless gospel across the land in His name. You remember, don't you?"

This was the content of the first chapter of the Black Cross Tribunal's textbook.

"Yes, my Lord."

Gabriel smiled. "You enjoy God's grace, yet you betray the Divine Court. Do you know the fate of an apostate?"

After the initial wave of terror, Sariel found himself becoming strangely calm.

He wiped the blood flowing from his nose. "I know."

It was nothing more than a cruel death.

Sariel thought of his childhood, the days spent as a slave on the grasslands. He would dream of being the slave owner's son, then begin to beg—begging that he wouldn't have to go outside the city to collect water the next day, where the mutated sunlight would melt him into the grass that grew taller than a man.

God had saved him, yet it felt as if He hadn't. He had good genes, natural ones. The sunlight didn't kill him; instead, it caused him to develop antibodies, making it easier for him to awaken as an Apocalypse Knight. That was how Sariel had joined the Divine Court.

Where was God's grace? Where was God's love? He had simply walked out of one dark forest and into another.

The people of Eternal City viewed Xiang Nanli as a god. A god who walked among men, requiring no worship. Sariel felt that, as a child, he probably would have preferred such a "god"—one who didn't rule over its people with coldness and violence.

The pressure around him intensified. Sariel couldn't stand; he fell to his knees, prostrating himself like the most devout fanatic.

His body began to deform, as if it were being pressed into a thin sheet of paper. His consciousness blurred, and his instinct for survival made him want to resist, but his desperate struggles resulted in nothing more than a tremor of his frame.

Red lightning, swift as a gale, tore into this domain.

"Hnnng—"

Ezekiel hooked his tail, scooping Sariel up from the ground. He then crouched at the end of the corridor, hands on the floor, watching the figure not far away with vigilance.

The scales on his body bristled, his black-and-red eyes spinning incessantly.

Ezekiel tried to pinpoint Gabriel's location, yet in his perception, Gabriel was everywhere.

How annoying.

He had only come to the school cafeteria for a free breakfast.

But he couldn't just ignore this.

Still, it seemed he couldn't win.

Maybe he should just run away and pretend he was never here. Besides, Xiang Nanli wasn't around.

Just as Ezekiel was weighing the pros and cons, a thin, slimy root sprouted from the black mist and gently scratched the scales on Ezekiel's chin.

Gabriel smiled. "What a cute dog. Would your master be even cuter?"

Ezekiel let out a sharp, unprecedented screech: "Hnnng!" (Get lost!)

The sky-filling blackness actually retreated.

As the black mist left, it casually snatched the dozens of high-value labor vouchers from Sariel's shirt pocket: "You might not believe this, but I was actually kidnapped here... I'll let you go today, heh, just borrowing some money."

chunks.chineseText:
第110章 绑匪与人质

加百列微微睁开眼眸。

他的虹膜是神性的浅金色，皮肤和唇色都苍白的像是屋外的雪。

厚厚的羽绒被盖在他的身上，很暖和。这是永恒市招待所里最好的套房。

心跳声、血液流动、脏器的活动……人类应有的生机重新回到了这具身躯中。

尽管不是第一次见，黄枫还是觉得有些不可思议；这触及到了它的认知盲区，Alpha没教过。

再次介绍一下——黄枫。雏蜂号轻工型机器人，编号略。

性别：无。

外设：仿真款人类女性。

内设：武器装置X-7、X-9、X-11等等。

级别：荣耀机械。

拟人模块：3.0通用版

它本来可以幸福又快乐；是Alpha非要安排保密任务害了它。

大概四个月前，黄枫和自己的伙伴觅风带着“1亿信用点物资”的任务降临了地表。

因为Alpha提供的物资存放点均已失效，两人选择了不同的方式执行任务。

黄枫了解过人类社会目前的情况后，决定前往附近最富裕的地表据点利维坦城，劫持神庭重要人质，进行敲诈勒索。

黄枫抵达利维坦时，正好碰上黑十字审判庭的神诞节。它原本盯上的目标是在节日盛典上花枝招展的圣子相晨曦。

但在闲（踩）逛（点）的时候，黄枫意外得知，整个利维坦最尊贵的人，竟然不是相晨曦，而是利维坦的城主、庇护者，尊名加百列。

至于加百列？没人见过祂。只是有传说，说祂就住在中央大道主教堂的神龛中。

但神龛不是供奉死人的吗？

总之，黄枫非常巧合地避开了所有守卫，黑掉了神庭内部的安保系统还没有触发警报，并且顺利地打开棺材，遇到了非常配合的人质。

这位人质很消瘦，外观以人类的审美而言无疑是绝色。

他说他就是加百列。加百列被缩在只能蜷缩的棺材中。背后有两个血洞。

加百列说那是他断裂的翅膀根；但黄枫分明怀疑那是两根铁棍穿过他的锁骨。

总之，经过一番不怎么艰苦的奋斗，黄枫顺利挟持到人质。

嗯，这在概率上只有0.000……023％的可能，约等于在人马星上发现外星人。

正常人用脑子想想，都知道这种彩票中一个亿的好事不会发生在自己身上。

但黄枫只是一台较为严谨的智械。

概率不是0.0％，那么凭什么不行？！

它当时就想写信给神庭，大致内容为：你们的加百列在我手上。我需要3亿信用点的赎金。

3亿信用点，1亿支付给地下钱庄（洗钱，让来路不明的黑钱变得正当合法不会被银行检查到）；剩下1亿完成Alpha的任务；最后1亿留给觅风备用，免得它一直完成不了任务被困在地表。

但加百列阻止了它，或者说，给出了非常合理的建议：“利维坦就在阴山城附近，这里到处都是神庭的眼线和军事堡垒。比起给钱，他们一定会选择更暴力的手段把我夺走。你最好转移窝藏点。”

黄枫蹙眉：“神庭不怕我撕票吗？”

然后加百列就给黄枫展示了一下，他摘下了黄枫藏在腰侧的螳螂刀，轻轻往脖子上一抹——

没有血液。加百列的头掉在了地上，轻的像是蓬草。

黄枫没有检测到任何生命体征，但就在几分钟后，加百列的身体举起了自己的脑袋，安装回了脖子上。

“我死不了。”加百列柔柔弱弱地回答，“你撕票也没用。”

黄枫没有从自己的数据库中找到解决办法，于是，它选择向Alpha发送求救信号。

Alpha也不负众望地在三个月后回复了它——“TD”。

尽管信号微弱，但黄枫还是检测到，信号源是在永恒市附近。正好和任务目标点重合。

所以，黄枫就带着加百列上路来投靠Alpha啦~当然，因为保密机制，这件事只有它一个人知道。

但加百列这个人质，比黄枫想象中娇弱。

日光会让他白皙的皮肤起一层红红的疹子，交通工具只能接受机械能的（包括脚踏车和机械人背），一上能源车就吐得昏天黑地。而且怕冷，需要厚棉被；每天还要保证8小时睡眠。而且还要吃好吃的，要不然每天又哭又闹。

尽管清楚加百列不会死；尽管黄枫明明是个该死的智械意志派，但残留的机器人天性（照顾人类），让它该死地没能拒绝——沟槽的Alpha，不是说这个拟人模块上的漏洞早就修复了吗？

话说回来，加百列真的是人类吗？

黄枫狐疑的目光落在了加百列的脸上。

对方坐在床上，把自己裹得像是一个圆润的粽子，睡眼惺忪地回答：“醒了。”

黄枫冷着脸开口：“早饭在桌子上。”

“好喔，谢谢。”

“上午12点退房。我身上已经没钱了，你在房间里不要走动，我等会出门挣点钱。”黄枫一脸坦然地说着。完全不提自己的挣钱方式几乎全是非法途径。

它没有人类的道德观。

这里的人用两种货币，一种是实体的工分券；另一种叫“公民积分”，是电子货币。

黄枫尝试过破解这里的电子货币，但失败了。

这肯定是Alpha的手笔吧？要知道它可是连神庭的防御系统都能黑进去（？）的超级智械。

“喔……喔……”加百列顿了顿，慢条斯理地询问，“你那个有钱的亲戚呢？你不是说在永恒市吗？”

黄枫心想，它也想知道。自己信号都发烂了，Alpha也没个回应。

（注：信号覆盖范围100km；而永恒市距离基地主城区直线距离167km。）

黄枫：“出了点问题。”

“呵呵，没事。”加百列的脸上浮现出堪称愉悦的笑容，他从怀里掏出数十张大额工分券，在黄枫眼前晃了晃，“我发现，我也有个有钱的亲戚在永恒市。”

黄枫接过钞票，数了数，震惊道：“这些钱能住一个月总统套房了！你亲戚真有钱！”

——其实一般情况，沙利叶是不会带这么多钱在身上的。

但是他是一个见过世面、深知经济发展规律的高素质人才。

沙利叶准备在永恒市买套房！

他攒了一个月工资，又以“军团训导员”的职业作为担保，向银行贷了一笔，下班后的午休间隙就能去房管所交首付！

目前，基地的房产还没有进入自由市场流通。都是由政府统一修建，居民填表购买。考虑到永恒市目前的生产水平，价格相对实惠。

永恒市内能打赢他的人不太多。沙利叶本来以为身带现金也是很安全的。可惜遇上了万恶的加百列。

加百列思绪飘忽了一会，旋即微笑着回答：“嗯呐。”

黄枫：“那你先吃饭，我下楼续房。对了，你消失这么久，神庭一点都不急吗？他们不知道你被绑架了，我怎么要赎金？”
chunks.englishText:
Chapter 110: The Kidnapper and the Hostage

Gabriel opened his eyes slightly.

His irises were a divine pale gold, and his skin and lips were as pale as the snow outside.

A thick down quilt covered him, keeping him warm. This was the best suite in the Eternal City guesthouse.

The sound of a heartbeat, the flow of blood, the activity of internal organs... the vitality that a human should possess had returned to this body.

Although it wasn't the first time seeing it, Huang Feng still found it somewhat incredible; this touched upon a blind spot in its cognition, something Alpha had never taught it.

Let me reintroduce myself—Huang Feng. A "Young Bee" (Chun Feng) series light-industrial robot, serial number omitted.

Gender: None.

Exterior: Simulated human female.

Interior: Weaponry systems X-7, X-9, X-11, etc.

Rank: Glory-class Machine.

Anthropomorphic module: 3.0 Universal Edition.

It could have been happy and content; it was Alpha who insisted on assigning a classified mission that ruined everything.

About four months ago, Huang Feng and its partner, Mi Feng, descended to the surface with the mission of "securing 100 million credits worth of supplies."

Because the supply storage points provided by Alpha had all become invalid, the two chose different methods to execute the mission.

After understanding the current state of human society, Huang Feng decided to head to the nearby wealthy surface stronghold, Leviathan City, to kidnap a high-ranking hostage from the Divine Court for extortion.

When Huang Feng arrived at Leviathan, it happened to coincide with the Black Cross Tribunal's "God's Birthday" festival. Its original target was the Saint Xiang Chenxi, who was dressed in finery for the grand celebration.

But while scouting the area, Huang Feng accidentally learned that the most noble person in all of Leviathan was not Xiang Chenxi, but the City Lord and Protector of Leviathan, known by the title Gabriel.

As for Gabriel? No one had ever seen Him. There were only legends saying He lived in the shrine of the main cathedral on the Central Avenue.

But weren't shrines for worshipping the dead?

In any case, Huang Feng very coincidentally bypassed all guards, hacked into the Divine Court's internal security system without triggering an alarm, and successfully opened the coffin, encountering a very cooperative hostage.

This hostage was very thin, and in terms of human aesthetics, he was undoubtedly a stunning beauty.

He said he was Gabriel. Gabriel had been crammed into a coffin where he could only curl up. There were two bloody holes in his back.

Gabriel said those were the roots of his broken wings; but Huang Feng clearly suspected they were two iron rods that had pierced his collarbones.

In short, after some not-so-arduous struggle, Huang Feng successfully took the hostage.

Well, the probability of this was only 0.000...023%, roughly equivalent to discovering aliens on Mars.

Any normal person would know that the luck of winning a 100-million-credit lottery wouldn't happen to them.

But Huang Feng was just a relatively rigorous intelligent machine.

If the probability wasn't 0.0%, then why couldn't it happen?!

It had wanted to write a letter to the Divine Court at the time, the gist of which was: Your Gabriel is in my hands. I need a ransom of 300 million credits.
