As for "how a delicate flower survives outside the greenhouse," that was not something Luo Yang considered.

Because the entire Human Alliance was a greenhouse in his palm.

Xiang Nanli glanced at the golden-yellow No. 1 with some confusion: "No need."

As for where Xiao Qing went, Xiang Nanli didn't usually pry. Perhaps it was a secret of the Mechanical Legion?

In any case, the tasks assigned to Dongfang Qingdi were always completed well.

Xiao Qing's current position was Chief of Staff! He was the second-in-command of the base!

He worked 3 hours a day (which was enough for him to handle all the work), and he was proficient in everything from material and human resource allocation to pipe repairs (the base's geothermal device occasionally encountered pipe aging problems, and because it was hundreds of meters underground, Xiao Qing basically handled it all).

Xiang Nanli didn't intend to squeeze every bit of free time out of Dongfang Qingdi; that would be too much like a black-hearted capitalist!

No. 1 squatted down and began to help unload the cargo. His movements were very skilled, as if he had coordinated with Xiang Nanli a thousand times before.

Xiao Zhi: [...]

*I don't know why, but I really want to format No. 1. It's urgent.*

Beichen quickly put on the control device.

He injected the prepared anesthetic into the progenitor, and the progenitor docilely allowed the control instrument to be attached. It lay on the ground, the spores on its body swaying listlessly with the wind.

The entire operating system was exceptionally concise. Beichen activated the eyepiece, and a 3D electronic map appeared before his eyes.

On the map, the progenitor was red, while the offspring bred by the progenitor were other colors, each representing a different division of labor.

The fungi responsible for reproduction, nutrient collection, and ecological occupation each had their own forms.

It was like a small beehive.

Beichen: "The base's Black Silk Powder Fungus is an evolved form that incorporates the remains of alien species from space. Considering the base's security needs, we are currently mainly increasing the strains responsible for ecological occupation."

He drew several circles on the map, around the base's outer walls and some important factory buildings.

"But this way, the nutrition won't keep up. So I still need a sum of funds to purchase raw materials and prepare nutrient solution."

Actually, there was one more thing, but because he didn't think it was a bad thing, Beichen subconsciously omitted it.

Before Xiang Nanli returned, he had let the free-roaming Black Silk Powder Fungus eat all the alien species and wandering small deviants around the base~ After all, since nutrition was insufficient, Beichen had to create conditions to prevent the Black Silk Powder Fungus he was raising from dying.

Therefore, the area within a 5-kilometer radius of the base was exceptionally safe, which indirectly protected the base's farmland.

Xiang Nanli frowned, feeling that things weren't that simple: "How much do you need?"

"Uh," Beichen counted on his fingers, "3 million for the first month. I will control the scale of the swarm."

He was, of course, talking about Human Alliance credit points, not the base's electronic currency.

If it were before, Xiang Nanli wouldn't have approved this funding. After all, the area around the base was relatively peaceful, and Rome City and Glory City had also been incorporated into their jurisdiction.

But the appearance of "Gabriel" made Xiang Nanli realize that peace might only be temporary.

The nearby underground city of Gusu was still suffering from a plague; looking at news online, the epidemic seemed to have subsided quite a bit, but it hadn't fully opened up.

And a few hundred miles away was the Divine Court garrison of Yinshan City. According to Sariel, it would only take a few hundred Apocalypse Knights equipped with a few modern weapons to completely destroy the base.

During this time, the survivor base had taken in many refugees from the Divine Court Prairie.

They recounted their fate after being occupied by the Divine Court—the first generation of subjects would become slaves of the Earthly Kingdom of God. Only a very few favored children of heaven could be absorbed into the Divine Court.

*Born in sorrow, die in peace.*

Although the base's budget was already very tight, Xiang Nanli calculated the data in his mind and gritted his teeth: "Okay."

However, he didn't mention what to do about the second month.

The experiment was a great success. Xiang Nanli left the equipment behind and began to walk toward his office.

First, he contacted the Gospel Book, which was far away in Eternal City.

Although this mechanical unit was sometimes too clingy and seemed unreliable, it was, after all, the Gospel Book that carried rich agricultural and breeding technology.

"Xiao Fu."

As soon as Xiang Nanli spoke, a long string of tildes appeared on the screen, indicating that the Gospel Book's mood was very pleasant: "Li Li~~! You finally contacted me!"

The Gospel Book turned on camera mode: "Look, this is the fungus-chicken breeding farm we just set up."

Although "fungus-chicken" had the word "chicken" in it, it wasn't a real animal.

Inside the constant-temperature breeding farm, large glass bottles were placed at various heights. The bottles were filled with the nutrient solution formula provided by Beichen.

At this moment, yellow spores were splitting inside. It looked just like the yolk of an egg.

chunks.chapterTitle: 第114章 装置实验和菌鸡销售 (Part 2)
chunks.chineseText:
当蛋黄出现一缕缕红色血丝的时候，就能捞出来，放在外界培育了。从孢子到成熟可以售卖，一共需要3周。

这种菌丝生命体对环境稍微挑剔一点，也容易被外界的辐射污染成为坏菌。但整体来说，养殖是非常方便的。

“你吩咐给小福的任务，小福做的很好噢！这批幼苗有6000头，存活率为95.7％。另外，孵化场后面就是养殖场。和菌牛牧场在一个山坡~因为可以自体分裂，第一批出栏的菌鸡大概有一万八千头。”

出栏一万八，对于一座现代化的养殖场来说，属于小作坊级别。但这依然不是基地内部可以消化的。

大家还刚脱离饥荒，顿顿吃菌鸡有些过于奢侈。

小福很快开始忧虑：“但是这种东西真的可以卖出去吗？我们没有专业的车队，地表运输相当麻烦，产品也没有对外推广过。”

相南里安慰它：“别担心。上次丰收节也不是白开的。”

丰收节邀请了附近许多小据点的首领。相南里保持了友好邦交并且交换了联系方式。

永恒市在被基地占据前，本来就是方圆几百里内著名的粮食产地。城主的办公室甚至还能找到一些没有履约的粮食订单。

在贫瘠、饱受污染的地表。粮食问题一向是各大据点的痛点、难点。

毕竟不是每个地表城市都有福音书（农业版）这种金手指。

相南里挨个打电话过去，表示永恒市已经更换了负责人。之前的订单依然可以交付，如果是付过钱的，基地可以在合同的基础上打3折提供粮食。表面看上去亏本，但因为农业技术的提高，粮田亩产远超过去，仔细一算，收支勉强持平。

但更重要的是，这个行为让基地得到了友商的认可。

相南里是经营过公司的，他并不是完全不懂商业。

商业信心、销售渠道，远比一时得失重要。

有了之前联络的基础，推销起基地的新农产品属于水到渠成。

相南里也没有隐瞒，他坦白了菌鸡存在的副作用，并且表示可以定期提供一些免费的抑制剂（反正这玩意本来也是北辰的配方）。

谁料，电话里的许多首领都表现出了异常的高兴：“那真是太好了，说实话。每年饿死的人，比你算出来的概率多多了。”

至于抑制剂能不能发到那些平民手里，完全是未知数。完全存在那些人二手倒卖的可能，在地表，普通人的一条贱命未必有抑制剂值钱，哪怕在地下城市，一瓶抑制剂的售价不过120信用点。

相南里也不想深究，他管不了所有人。

人类太复杂了，不是机器。

好说话的据点，会先给百分之二十的定金。不好说话的，却是说看见货才交钱。

相南里把训练好的基因战士分成了十队，由他们负责农产品的运输。这些基因战士接受过以西结、沙利叶系统的训练，还配有热武器。尽管地表很危险，但应该不至于毫无还手之力。

等处理好一切后，外面的天色已经转黑。地表一向黑的早。

相南里挂掉电话，在椅子上伸了个懒腰：“小智，我其实可以预料，虽然已经尽可能地保障安全，基地的运输队迟早也会遇到路匪。不过或许不算坏事……”

到时候就有正当理由去解放其他据点了！

基地会有更多的人口和更大的领地。

相南里不是一个冷血残酷的人。

但生存本身，就是残酷的。

小智：[嗻。]
chunks.englishText:
When a wisp of red blood-like threads appeared in the yolk, it could be scooped out and cultivated in the outside environment. It took a total of 3 weeks from spore to maturity for sale.

This mycelium lifeform was slightly picky about its environment and easily contaminated by external radiation, turning into "bad fungus." But overall, it was very convenient to farm.

"The task you assigned to Xiao Fu, Xiao Fu did very well! This batch of seedlings has 6,000 heads, with a survival rate of 95.7%. In addition, behind the hatchery is the breeding farm. It's on the same hillside as the fungus-cow pasture~ Because they can split autonomously, the first batch of fungus-chickens ready for market will be about 18,000."

18,000 ready for market was at the level of a small workshop for a modern farm. But this was still more than the base could consume internally.

Everyone had just escaped famine, and eating fungus-chicken at every meal was a bit too luxurious.

Xiao Fu soon began to worry: "But can this stuff really be sold? We don't have a professional fleet, surface transportation is quite troublesome, and the product hasn't been promoted externally."

Xiang Nanli comforted it: "Don't worry. The Harvest Festival last time wasn't held for nothing."

The Harvest Festival had invited the leaders of many small strongholds nearby. Xiang Nanli had maintained friendly diplomatic relations and exchanged contact information.

Before Eternal City was occupied by the base, it was already a famous grain-producing area for hundreds of miles around. One could even find some unfulfilled grain orders in the city lord's office.

On the barren, pollution-ridden surface, the grain issue had always been a pain point and a difficulty for major strongholds.

After all, not every surface city had a "golden finger" like the Gospel Book (Agricultural Edition).

Xiang Nanli called them one by one, stating that Eternal City had changed management. The previous orders could still be delivered, and if they had already paid, the base could provide grain at a 30% discount on the contract price. On the surface, it looked like a loss, but because of the improvement in agricultural technology, the yield per acre of grain fields far exceeded the past. After careful calculation, income and expenditure were barely balanced.

But more importantly, this action gained the base the recognition of friendly merchants.

Xiang Nanli had run a company before; he wasn't completely ignorant of business.

Business confidence and sales channels were far more important than immediate gains or losses.

With the foundation of previous contacts, promoting the base's new agricultural products was a matter of course.

Xiang Nanli didn't hide anything either; he confessed the side effects of the fungus-chickens and stated that they could provide some free inhibitors regularly (anyway, this was also Beichen's formula).

To everyone's surprise, many leaders on the phone expressed unusual joy: "That's really great. To be honest, the number of people who starve to death every year is far higher than the probability you calculated."

As for whether the inhibitors could actually reach those commoners, it was completely unknown. There was a complete possibility that those people would resell them; on the surface, the cheap life of an ordinary person might not be worth as much as an inhibitor, even in an underground city, where a bottle of inhibitor sold for only 120 credit points.

Xiang Nanli didn't want to get to the bottom of it; he couldn't control everyone.

Humans were too complex; they weren't machines.

The easy-to-talk-to strongholds would pay a 20% deposit first. The difficult ones, however, said they would only pay after seeing the goods.

Xiang Nanli divided the trained gene warriors into ten teams, responsible for the transportation of agricultural products. These gene warriors had received training from the Ezekiel and Sariel systems and were equipped with thermal weapons. Although the surface was dangerous, they shouldn't be without the ability to fight back.

By the time everything was handled, the sky outside had already turned dark. It always got dark early on the surface.

Xiang Nanli hung up the phone and stretched in his chair: "Xiao Zhi, I can actually foresee that although I've done my best to ensure safety, the base's transport team will sooner or later encounter road bandits. But perhaps that's not a bad thing..."

Then there would be a legitimate reason to liberate other strongholds!

The base would have a larger population and a larger territory.

Xiang Nanli was not a cold-blooded or cruel person.

But survival itself was cruel.

Xiao Zhi: [As you command.]

chunks.chineseText:
第115章 风雨欲来

“这是什么？”

加百列站在摊位前，面容纯洁美好的犹如天使。

白和干净，象征着不事生产。

不事生产，于是优雅而美丽。

加百列用的是神庭那边的凡语。

永恒市在被基地占领前，属于神庭的势力范围。领主大人虽然不会给低贱农奴教学，但耳濡目染之下，当地人多少会说一些。

小商贩用凡语磕磕绊绊地回答：“是烤饼，糖馅的。”

糖，一种提供高热量的食物，在地表一向属于奢侈品。

永恒之城曾经有片花田，专门种植鲜花供贵族老爷们取乐。

如今，贵族老爷们没了，花田却保留了下来，还是由之前的花农负责，只是从伺候花变成了伺候小蜜蜂。

烤饼里的糖馅儿用的就是蜂蜜、黑芝麻和花生。

地表物资紧缺，基地还在实行集体分配制度。

官方提供生产资料，农业户付出劳动、赚取积分，再用积分去购买需要的物品。劳动所得一律上缴粮仓。

这种集体供给制度，在较为原始的状态下，很容易出问题。毕竟统一分配有些过于僵化死板，而生活总是充满随机性。

但地表再怎么像中世纪，时间线也不是中世纪。

实验室培育的新物种大幅提高了农作物的产量；后台的人工智能（主要是福音书的硬件）也在随时对储备粮进行动态调整。

这些科技让人们完全不用害怕下一个冬天。

农业部长福音书还在琢磨着多余农产品出口呢。

而过剩的产能也会流入市场：基地允许小规模的私有化交易，这才有了永恒市商业街的繁荣。

相南里朴素地认为，有些东西不必要卡得太死。

让所有人有尊严地活着，这才是基地存在的意义。

一个巴掌大的糖饼售价2积分，对于大多数市民来说，还是一笔略微奢侈的消费。毕竟现在食堂点一碗鸡蛋面也才2积分。

因此，商贩很聪明地把自己的小摊摆在了市政厅门口。里面上班的多半是公务员，来办事的人也会有些小钱。

基地目前的信用还没有破产，作为电子货币的“积分”在附近几个据点都是通用的。

自从信号塔修建好后，市政厅就为公民发放了嵌有芯片的银行卡。

让加百列意外的是，基地的“积分”居然很难破解。

电子货币技术虽然没有太强的杀伤力，但含金量并不低。

非要破解的话，其中的资金消耗足以物理意义上再建十个永恒市。

也就是说，这里有比十个永恒市价值更高的大脑。考虑到电子货币只是对方掌握的其中一门技术，或许他的价值远不止十个永恒市。

“……唔。”

感觉就像是一个不起眼的小海岛，上面住着的全是原始人，却装配了一台核反应堆。

但也不能说完全不起眼吧。毕竟这个基地连神庭的圣灵都敢昧下，还在周围养了不少畸变人。

“相南里，如果是那个相南里……或许值十座‘利维坦’？”加百列在心里想着。

黄枫的型号，加百列很清楚。

它在智械军团内部属于中层干部，一般情况下不会轻易出动。

加百列跟着它离开利维坦城，一部分是想出来兜兜风，看看外面的世界变成了什么样；另一部分，则是想知道黄枫，或者说，下达给黄枫命令的那位大人物想干什么。

探索的确容易接近真相。

譬如他在这座自己完全不上心的小城市里，遇到了“相南里”。

加百列确信，哪怕这个相南里是复制出来的，也会是相当成功的克隆人，基因具有高度接近性。

他要把相南里带回神庭。这对神庭来说非常重要。

Alpha。

在你向他靠近时，是否如我一般狂喜呢？

加百列微笑着从口袋里拿出一张工分券，指向热腾腾的炉子：“来十个。谢谢。”

加百列深知信用货币的脆弱。他倾向于把所有的钱换成物资。

他在地表见过太多据点了，或许今天还繁荣的城市；明日就会沦为废墟。

小商贩喜出望外，用牛皮纸裹好了十个糖饼。

加百列抱着袋子，乖巧地站在市政厅大楼前，等着黄枫出来。

似乎是察觉到有人注视，他抬头，微微眯起眼，朝着某扇窗户的方向笑了一下。

沙利叶顿时寒毛倒竖，他把背贴在墙上，忍不住一阵心悸。

而脑海里，一个声音正在尖锐地叫着：[你为什么要躲着他？我们应该向加百列求助！我是圣子，神庭不会放弃我的。他一定是来救我们的——]

沙利叶的灵魂之火不太稳定的跳跃着。

一团小火光想要分裂出去，挣扎着飘向加百列的方向。

沙利叶抬起手，给了自己脸一巴掌：“蠢货，你清醒点！”

这团小火苗如果真的敢靠近加百列，后果只有一个，那就是被毫不留情的吞食；稀疏平常地像是进食水和空气。

“要我说多少次，神庭不缺你一个圣子。他们随时可以复制、再造。你甚至都不清楚自己是不是本体。”

相晨曦啜泣着，在沙利叶的脑海里“嘤嘤”地哭了起来。

隔了几分钟，他终于平静了下来。

[那加百列圣上为什么会来这？]

沙利叶不是很想解释，主要是以相晨曦的智商，理解起来有些困难。

“永恒之城培育的圣灵是攻略姑苏城的关键。如今出了这么大篓子，不派人过来看才是奇怪。”

当然，加百列亲自来，其实更奇怪。

神庭这段时间应该很是恼怒。

阴山城是神庭暴力占领的，打出的战争口号是“夺回人联欠我们的一切”，而这场战争，差点让神庭失去一切。

人联是百足之虫，几乎继承了旧世界的全部遗产，血厚、家底也厚；和智械打完又和神庭打，完事了依旧蒸蒸日上，欣欣向荣。

而神庭举国之力一战，只能说险胜。胜利的果实如此甜美，一百年的修生养息，神庭不仅恢复了最初的鼎盛，也拥有了更大的政治筹码和地表的话语权。

所以，它们把目光望向了姑苏。

这座城市偏僻、贫穷。发达地区的人联居民们抱怨着自己城市每年给姑苏城的巨额转移支付，仿佛剥削者不是头顶层层的高塔，而是遥远的姑苏人。

它最大的优势就是，离阴山城非常近。

再发动一次战争，像拿下阴山城那样拿下姑苏，对神庭来说得不偿失。因为第二座地下城市远不如第一座重要。

所以，它们更希望用一些柔和的手段……比如瘟疫。

瘟疫，会让姑苏成为一座空城。姑苏内部遭到一次巨大的清洗，从上层到底层都缺人，而这时，神庭的势力可以渗透进姑苏城内部……

上层，有洛修身边的乌列尔（辛追），以及其他一些隐藏的暗棋。更何况神庭如此擅长精神操控。

下层，有因为缺人而吸纳进城市的大批地表遗民。

再经过数十年的和平演化，姑苏最后会和阴山城一样，成为黑十字审判庭的后花园。
chunks.englishText:
Chapter 115: The Gathering Storm

"What is this?"

Gabriel stood before the stall, his expression as pure and beautiful as an angel’s.

Fair and clean, a symbol of one who does not toil.

And because he did not toil, he was elegant and exquisite.

Gabriel spoke in the common tongue of the Divine Court.

Before Eternal City was occupied by the Base, it had fallen under the Divine Court’s sphere of influence. While the Lord of the Manor would never deign to teach the lowly serfs, the locals had picked up enough of the language through sheer exposure.

The small-time vendor replied in broken common tongue: "It’s a baked cake, with a sugar filling."

Sugar—a source of high caloric density—had always been a luxury item on the surface.

Eternal City once boasted a field of flowers, cultivated specifically for the amusement of the nobility.

Now, the nobles were gone, but the flower fields remained. The original flower farmers were still in charge, though they had traded tending to blossoms for tending to honeybees.

The sugar filling in the cakes was made from honey, black sesame, and peanuts.

Resources on the surface were scarce, and the Base still operated under a collective distribution system.

The authorities provided the means of production, while agricultural households provided the labor to earn credits, which were then used to purchase necessities. All labor output was surrendered to the granaries.

In a primitive state, such a collective supply system was prone to failure. After all, centralized distribution was often too rigid, while life was inherently full of randomness.

But no matter how much the surface resembled the Middle Ages, the timeline was anything but.

New species cultivated in the laboratories had drastically increased crop yields, and the artificial intelligence in the background (primarily the hardware of the *Gospel*) dynamically adjusted grain reserves in real-time.

These technologies meant the people had absolutely no fear of the coming winter.

The Minister of Agriculture, *Gospel*, was even contemplating the export of surplus agricultural products.

This excess capacity flowed into the market: the Base permitted small-scale private transactions, which was the source of the commercial street's prosperity in Eternal City.

Xiang Nanli held the simple belief that some things shouldn't be restricted too tightly.

To let everyone live with dignity—that was the true meaning of the Base’s existence.

A palm-sized sugar cake cost 2 credits, a slightly extravagant expense for most citizens. After all, a bowl of egg noodles at the cafeteria only cost 2 credits.

Therefore, the vendor was clever enough to set up his stall right at the entrance of City Hall. Most of the people working inside were civil servants, and those coming for business usually had a bit of spare coin.

The Base’s credit had not yet collapsed, and these "credits," functioning as digital currency, were accepted across several nearby strongholds.

Ever since the signal towers were built, City Hall had issued bank cards embedded with chips to all citizens.

What surprised Gabriel was that the Base’s "credits" were incredibly difficult to crack.

While the digital currency technology lacked lethal force, its intrinsic value was not low.

To force a breach would require a capital expenditure equivalent to physically rebuilding ten Eternal Cities.

In other words, there was a brain here worth more than ten Eternal Cities. Considering that digital currency was merely one of the technologies the other party had mastered, perhaps his value far exceeded ten Eternal Cities.

"...Hmm."

It felt like an inconspicuous little island, inhabited entirely by primitives, yet equipped with a nuclear reactor.

Though, one couldn't exactly call it "inconspicuous." After all, this Base dared to embezzle a Holy Spirit of the Divine Court and even kept a number of aberrants in the surrounding area.

*Xiang Nanli... if it really is that Xiang Nanli... perhaps he is worth ten 'Leviathans'?* Gabriel mused to himself.

Gabriel knew Huang Feng’s model well.

Within the Mechanized Legion, it was a mid-level cadre, not something that would be dispatched lightly under normal circumstances.

Gabriel had followed it out of Leviathan City partly to take a breather and see what the outside world had become, and partly to find out what Huang Feng—or rather, the great figure who issued orders to Huang Feng—was planning.

Exploration was indeed the easiest path to the truth.

For instance, in this small city he hadn't cared for in the slightest, he had encountered "Xiang Nanli."

Gabriel was certain that even if this Xiang Nanli were a copy, he would be a highly successful clone with a high degree of genetic proximity.

He had to bring Xiang Nanli back to the Divine Court. This was of vital importance to them.

*Alpha.*

*As you draw near to him, do you feel the same ecstasy as I do?*

Gabriel smiled, took a credit voucher from his pocket, and pointed to the steaming stove: "Ten, please. Thank you."

Gabriel knew well the fragility of credit currencies. He preferred to convert all his wealth into physical goods.

He had seen too many strongholds on the surface; a city that was prosperous today might be reduced to ruins by tomorrow.

The vendor was overjoyed and wrapped ten sugar cakes in kraft paper.

Gabriel cradled the bag, standing obediently in front of the City Hall building, waiting for Huang Feng to emerge.

Seeming to sense a gaze upon him, he looked up, narrowed his eyes slightly, and smiled toward a certain window.

Sariel felt his hair stand on end; he pressed his back against the wall, unable to suppress a sudden palpitation.

In the depths of his mind, a voice was screaming sharply: *[Why are you hiding from him? We should ask Gabriel for help! I am the Holy Son; the Divine Court will not abandon me. He must be here to save us—]*

Sariel’s soul fire flickered unsteadily.

A small spark of light tried to detach itself, struggling to drift toward Gabriel.

Sariel raised his hand and slapped his own face: "You fool, wake up!"

If this little spark dared to approach Gabriel, there would be only one outcome: to be devoured without mercy, as casually as one would consume water or air.

"How many times must I say it? The Divine Court is not short of a Holy Son like you. They can replicate and recreate you at any time. You don't even know if you are the original."

Xiang Chenxi sobbed, whimpering in the back of Sariel’s mind.

After a few minutes, he finally calmed down.

*[Then why would His Holiness Gabriel come here?]*

Sariel didn't really want to explain, mostly because, given Xiang Chenxi’s intelligence, it would be difficult for him to grasp.

"The Holy Spirit cultivated by Eternal City is the key to conquering Gusu City. Now that such a massive blunder has occurred, it would be strange if they didn't send someone to investigate."

Of course, Gabriel coming in person was even stranger.

The Divine Court must be furious during this period.

Yinshan City had been occupied by the Divine Court through violence, with the war cry: "Reclaim everything the Human Alliance owes us." Yet, this war had nearly cost the Divine Court everything.

The Human Alliance was a centipede that never truly died, having inherited almost the entire legacy of the Old World. They were thick-skinned and deep-pocketed; they had fought the Mechanized Legion and then the Divine Court, yet they remained prosperous and thriving.

The Divine Court had exhausted its national strength in that war, and one could only call it a narrow victory. The fruits of victory were so sweet that, after a hundred years of recuperation, the Divine Court had not only restored its initial peak but also gained greater political leverage and a voice on the surface.

Thus, they cast their gaze toward Gusu.

This city was remote and poor. Residents of the developed Human Alliance regions complained about the massive transfer payments their cities made to Gusu every year, as if the exploiters weren't the towering spires above them, but the distant people of Gusu.

Its greatest advantage was that it was very close to Yinshan City.

Launching another war to take Gusu just as they had taken Yinshan would be a net loss for the Divine Court. Because a second underground city was far less important than the first.

Therefore, they preferred to use softer methods... such as a plague.

A plague would turn Gusu into a hollow city. Gusu would undergo a massive purge from within, lacking personnel from the top down, and at that moment, the Divine Court’s influence could infiltrate the interior of Gusu City...

In the upper echelons, there was Uriel (Xin Zhui) beside Luo Xiu, along with other hidden chess pieces. Not to mention, the Divine Court was highly skilled in mental manipulation.

In the lower echelons, there were the large numbers of surface refugees absorbed into the city due to labor shortages.

After several decades of peaceful evolution, Gusu would eventually become the backyard of the Black Cross Inquisition, just like Yinshan City.

chunks.chineseText:
一名书记员匆匆来到沙利叶的办公室：“教官。你要的资料。”

沙利叶已经悄悄观察加百列两天了。

这两天，加百列大多时候呆在酒店，他身边有一台检测不出型号的智械人（这通常代表着这款智械不在市面上流通，也非神庭生产）。

今天，这台智械来到了市政厅。干了两件事，第一件事是进行人才落户，表示自己想要加入幸存者基地。

Alpha之前传回的信号就在这个方位。

根据分析，Alpha（的某台分机），有百分之99的可能，就在这个基地的内部。它需要某种方式，引起Alpha的注意。

作为一台高端智械，它得到的人才评级是最高级。足够引起高层的重视。

而它干的第二件事，是想要委托寄信（手写，实体）——在知道永恒市的邮局只能在基地内部送信后，这位女士勃然大怒。

邮局工作人员建议它前往姑苏城地上的黑市，只要支付足够多钱，总有人能把快递发往阴山城。

书记官在黄枫发飙前出现了。他表示可以帮忙把信件送到阴山城。

——信是加百列写的，署名处有一根洁白的羽毛。

沙利叶的表情变了又变。信的内容很荒诞，要求教皇支付加百列的巨额赎金。

但这并不是沙利叶关注的重点。

神庭有一种特殊的加密通讯手段，只有主教级别的神职人员才会用，叫“托梦”。

托梦很方便，甚至都不怕人联网络信息追踪。

但托梦的坏处是，只有梦境双方才知道梦里到底发生了什么。

所以，托梦结束后，发起者通常会保留一份实体的文件。

那根羽毛就是加百列的文件。

现在信来到了沙利叶的手中，他抚摸上了羽毛。

对方级别比他高太多，沙利叶只能捕捉到一些模糊的声音。

“锁定……相南里……支援……不惜一切。”

沙利叶挥挥手，让书记官离开。他坐在办公室内，神态变化莫测。因为这几日的操劳，眼睑下方有一团浓郁的黑色。

“我的信仰不该动摇。”沙利叶喃喃，“我们会死的，晨曦。”

[我不是早就死了？你个没用的东西，都没办法帮我报仇！甚至还在那个杀了我的人手底下工作……]相晨曦非常不满地抱怨着。

沙利叶释然了：“是的，我们早就死了。”

神庭的圣子和领主级骑士都死在去年那个冬天，他们为神庭奉献了自己的一生。得到了一些优待，也付出了一些东西。

付出的是什么东西？自由？尊严？身为人的爱与感知？

“你说，人们盼望的未来到底是什么样的？”

[你在说什么？]

“我曾经负责审讯过一名人联军官。他来自调查组。我们需要获得一些情报，我像以前一样，给他注射药物，让他清醒地看着自己被凌迟。基因药让他不会轻易死去。这位军官很坚强。情绪波动最大的时候，是看见自己的下属在眼前死去。就算这样，他也没有崩溃。”

沙利叶从抽屉里拿出一根烟，抽上。

“意志力坚定的敌人总是更有趣味。后来我们告诉他，神庭之所以能掌握他们的行踪，并且在地表俘获他们，是因为人联高层的泄密。他正直、顽固得不合时宜；他们捍卫的组织，根本配不上他的牺牲。”

“那名军官嘲笑我，他说自己捍卫的从来不是人联，他想捍卫的是一个有希望的未来。”

“我一度不能理解。因为我不知道有希望的未来到底该是什么样子。又是什么样的未来，值得一个人付出一切去追寻。”

“我把自己觉得有用的知识教给了以西结。还有一些训练的经验，整理成了手册，交给了葛根。我总觉得时间很多。可惜了。”

沙利叶闭上眼，随后睁开，拨通了相南里的电话。

电话很快就接通了，相南里抬起眼眸扫了镜头一眼，问：“沙利叶？有什么事吗。这么晚了。”

相南里有一双绿色的眼眸，这双眼很少因为沮丧和妥协而黯淡，会让人想起生机盎然的春天。

沙利叶沉默着。沉默并非因为迟疑，而是灵魂上难以言说的剧痛。

他忍住颤抖，缓缓开口：“加百列通知了教皇……你们逃吧。”

去更远的地方，重新开始。这次或许会更艰难一些。但总归还有希望。

我是刽子手。是麻木的傀儡。是外强中干的恶棍。

有些事情我做不到，于是我不去想。

但或许你们可以。

这句话几乎用掉了沙利叶全身力气，他挂掉电话。指间还没燃尽的烟掉在了水泥地板上。

沙利叶瘫痪在椅子上，苍白的皮肤血红，血液在身体里沸腾着，燃烧着，终于抵达某个顶点。

“啪”的一声。

沙利叶的头像是被戳破的水球一样爆炸，四溅的血液在身后的墙上流淌着。

他的灵魂之火熄灭了。
chunks.englishText:
A clerk hurried into Sariel’s office. "Instructor, the documents you requested."

Sariel had been quietly observing Gabriel for two days.

During these two days, Gabriel had spent most of his time in the hotel, accompanied by an android of an unrecognizable model (which usually implied it was neither commercially available nor manufactured by the Divine Court).

Today, this android arrived at City Hall. It accomplished two things. First, it applied for residency, expressing a desire to join the survivor base.

The signal Alpha had transmitted earlier originated from this very location.

According to analysis, there was a 99 percent probability that Alpha (or one of its sub-units) was inside this base. It needed a way to catch Alpha’s attention.

As a high-end android, it received the highest talent rating—enough to garner the attention of the upper echelons.

The second thing it did was attempt to commission a letter delivery (handwritten, physical). Upon learning that the Eternal City’s post office only handled mail within the base, the lady was furious.

The postal worker suggested it head to the black market on the surface of Gusu City; as long as one paid enough, there would always be someone willing to send a package to Yinshan City.

The clerk appeared before Huang Feng could lose her temper. He offered to help deliver the letter to Yinshan City.

—The letter was written by Gabriel, and a pure white feather was tucked into the signature line.

Sariel’s expression shifted repeatedly. The content of the letter was absurd, demanding that the Pope pay a massive ransom for Gabriel.

But that was not what Sariel was focused on.

The Divine Court possessed a special method of encrypted communication used only by bishop-level clergy, known as "Dream-Walking."

Dream-Walking was highly convenient, immune even to the tracking of the Human Alliance network.

However, the drawback was that only the two parties involved in the dream knew what had truly transpired within it.

Therefore, after a Dream-Walking session concluded, the initiator would usually retain a physical record.

That feather was Gabriel’s record.

Now that the letter was in Sariel’s hands, he reached out to touch the feather.

The sender’s rank was far higher than his own; Sariel could only capture a few fragmented, distorted sounds.

"Lock on... Xiang Nanli... Reinforcements... At all costs."

Sariel waved his hand, dismissing the clerk. He sat in his office, his expression inscrutable. Due to the exhaustion of the past few days, a heavy, dark shadow hung beneath his eyelids.

"My faith should not be shaken," Sariel murmured. "We are going to die, Dawn."

[Haven't I been dead for a long time? You useless thing, you couldn't even help me get revenge! You’re even working under the person who killed me...] Xiang Chenxi complained with deep dissatisfaction.

Sariel felt a sense of relief. "Yes, we died a long time ago."

The Holy Son and the Lord-level Knight of the Divine Court had both perished in that winter of last year. They had dedicated their entire lives to the Divine Court, receiving certain privileges and paying a certain price.

What was the price paid? Freedom? Dignity? The love and perception of a human being?

"Tell me, what do you think the future that people long for is actually like?"

[What are you talking about?]

"I was once responsible for interrogating a Human Alliance officer. He was from the investigation team. We needed to extract intelligence, so I did as I always did: I injected him with drugs, forcing him to watch, fully conscious, as he was slowly dismembered. The genetic serum ensured he wouldn't die easily. That officer was incredibly resilient. The moment his emotions fluctuated the most was when he saw his subordinates die before his eyes. Even then, he did not break."

Sariel took a cigarette from his drawer and lit it.

"A determined enemy is always more interesting. Later, we told him that the reason the Divine Court could track their movements and capture them on the surface was because of leaks from the Human Alliance’s high command. He was upright, stubbornly out of place; the organization they defended was simply not worth his sacrifice."

"The officer mocked me. He said he never defended the Human Alliance; what he wanted to defend was a future filled with hope."

"For a time, I couldn't understand. Because I didn't know what a hopeful future was supposed to look like. And what kind of future would be worth a person giving everything to pursue?"

"I taught the knowledge I deemed useful to Ezekiel. And some training experience I compiled into a manual for Gengen. I always felt there was plenty of time. What a pity."

Sariel closed his eyes, then opened them and dialed Xiang Nanli’s number.

The call connected quickly. Xiang Nanli raised his eyes to scan the lens and asked, "Sariel? Is something the matter? It’s so late."

Xiang Nanli had green eyes, eyes that rarely dimmed from frustration or compromise, reminiscent of a vibrant, flourishing spring.

Sariel remained silent. The silence was not due to hesitation, but an indescribable, soul-rending pain.

He suppressed his trembling and spoke slowly: "Gabriel has notified the Pope... You must flee."

Go somewhere further away, start over. This time might be even harder. But at least, there is still hope.

I am an executioner. A numbed puppet. A hollow, spineless villain.

There are some things I cannot do, so I choose not to think about them.

But perhaps you can.

That sentence drained nearly all of Sariel’s strength. He hung up the phone. The cigarette, still burning, fell from his fingers onto the concrete floor.

Sariel slumped in his chair, his pale skin flushing blood-red. His blood boiled within his body, burning, until it finally reached a breaking point.

*Pop.*

Sariel’s head exploded like a punctured water balloon, his blood splattering and running down the wall behind him.

His soul fire was extinguished.

chunks.chapterTitle: 第116章 抵达基地的智械军团 (Part 1)
chunks.chineseText:
第116章 抵达基地的智械军团

他的衣服是一袭白色的长袍，在隆冬单薄的不合时宜。偏向粉白的卷发，脚踝处能看见若有若无的铁链。双脚赤裸地踩在地上。

周围人似乎对他的感知很淡。广场上人来人往，都没有人问他冷不冷。也没人赞叹少年精致的眉眼。

他微微仰着头，脖颈纤长，容易让人想起天鹅之类的漂亮鸟类。

细碎的雪落在加百列的肩上，看起来已经等了一会儿了。

连环杀人犯通常会在事后返回案发现场，欣赏自己的杰作。

黄枫来到他跟前，双手叉腰，很是不满：“人质，注意你的身份，不是让你乖乖在房间里等我吗？”

“我一个人有点无聊。”加百列小声抱怨着，像撒娇。

热乎的糖馅儿从加百列的嘴角流出，他伸出猩红的舌头舔了舔。

加百列笑得像个天真的孩子：“买的糖饼是芝麻馅的，还掺了点桂花糖浆。很好吃。”

这是沙利叶的味道。

他说话的时候，浅金色的眼睛亮的惊人。瞳孔范围很大，几乎占据整个眼眶。眼睛里有一些细碎的、如同星星的光点。

很奇怪的感觉。美丽而诡异。

黄枫莫名感觉到了恐惧。

“你说什么？”它问。

加百列绕到了黄枫身后，然后跳到了它的身上。他背上应该是长了一对小翅膀。

他把脸贴在了这台智械人的背后，小声道：“没什么，走吧。我给过机会了。今天下雪了，好冷，不想走路。你背我。”

……

……

九章几乎是以最快的速度飞向幸存者基地。

他说不出自己的心情，不安中或许有一点激动。

九章在海底做了太久的后勤，几乎忘记了自己原本是台战争机器。

原计划四天的行程，最后只花了两天一夜。

九章悬浮在空中，俯瞰着脚下这片土地，忍不住喃喃：“那里就是目的地吗？”

按照卫星地图的记录，这里是西大陆的长生天高原。高原地底有三座人联城市，分别是：姑苏、剑门、阴山。

地表区域大部分被冰雪和冻土覆盖，辐射相比中、东部地区少很多，但环境相当恶劣，冬季低温可以低至零下八十度，大部分区域人烟罕至。

九章一路遇到过不少地表据点。

除了人类的，也有非人类的。时间仓促，它只来得及简陋地记录。

比如某个异种据点：那里在人联的地图上属于荒区。已经被一种巨型的蚂蚁占据。蚁后甚至为自己安装了人类的义脑。九章猜测，它的智商必然不会太低。

有段时间，神庭和人联的部分企业（点名批评古神生物）极度热衷于动物机械化改造。试图用这样的手段对抗智械的入侵——畸变体（人造人改良）、异种（动植物改良）都是在那一阶段大量诞生的怪物。

有些实验室荒废了，学者在离开前毁掉了一切；有些实验体逃跑了。

可怕的是，几百年过去；曾经的实验体们抵御住了大自然的淘汰，开始了属于自己的进化。

九章有时候也不无讽刺地想着：人类凭什么以为未来永远属于自己呢？

幸存者基地就藏在长生天高原的西北角，是一个非常小型、原始的人类据点。

这个据点看上去如此破旧，科技水平顶多在旧历水准，核心工业区高耸的地热泵就是基地最大的发电装置。根据评估，每日生产的电能还没到海底最小那个深井塔的1/10。

以至于九章核对了几次，才确信自己没有搞错Alpha发来的坐标。

但仔细观察后，九章也发现了一些特殊情况。

譬如围绕在城墙边上的菌丝生命体。几乎是信号盲区的实验室区域，以及明显品种特殊的菜田。

-菌丝生命体（母体）Lv.65

-特性：繁殖、不死（只要有孢子就能再次发育）、同化。

-卷心菜（不知名改良版）Lv.1

-特性：增生。消化。

-基因战士Lv.5

-特性：普通人服用基因药的产物。地表超级兵。

九章推了一下自己很斯文败类的金框眼镜（实际上是电子目镜），检查了一下自己的信息，开始发射信号波段。

-九章1.5（智械）Lv.60

-特性：以为是商业任务，穿着最普通的经济适用型身体出门了。现在有点后悔。

发射的信号波段是为了给出自己的身份证明，避免被基地的防御系统攻击。

正在书房里看书的东方青帝不由得微微侧过头。

难道是Beta的军纪更好吗？九章到的速度，可比雏蜂号的两台智械快多了。

Alpha没有立即回应，而是陷入了思考。

一年前，为了获得福音书的信任，Alpha也发射过信号波段。

但那时候，他的身份证明是普通的士兵。

但对于九章来说，军团侦察兵的身份会显得过于“低级”；很容易因为“权限不足”而被九章拒绝。更重要的是——相南里还在基地，他可不想被相南里发现自己居然要对其他械卑躬屈膝。

尴尬的是：九章在军团内职位不高，级别却不低。

他当过光辉军团的指挥官，为智械反攻人类立下过赫赫功劳，一度在军团的“五星上将”的候选名单里。

当然，也在人联的战犯名单里。

而想要超过九章，那么能选择的信号波段屈指可数。但那几台智械正在执行别的任务……根本不可能出现在地表。

短暂的权衡后，东方青帝传回了一段信号。

很快，飞行器停在了办公大楼的后院。

作为一台智械，九章的表情是很少的。然而此刻，他打开舱门，莫名感觉到了汗流浃背。

他扭头，身后的6台智械从舱门里钻出来，好奇地左右打量。

这六台智械的名字，是九章取的。分别叫方田、粟米、衰分、少广、商功、均输。

还有三台没有带出来，叫盈不足、方程和勾股。

“终于到了，我的铁屁股都坐痛了！”

“工厂在哪？我怎么觉得这个基地过于简陋？这里的建筑很明显是光荣觉醒前的风格。好土。”

“九章，你是不是来错地方了？”

智械们叽叽喳喳的，像是一群兴奋的小麻雀。

粟米举起了手里的玻璃杯：“九章，你看这只虫子！我在沙滩上抓的~好奇怪，之前一动不动，我还以为它冬眠了。”

玻璃瓶内的黑甲虫表现出了惊人的暴躁。

九章一愣。

他接过玻璃瓶，刚打开瓶口，这只甲虫直接朝着它的脸扑来，并且张开了锋锐的口器。

九章眼疾手快地捏死了它。

他本能地用尽全力，电光在九章的掌心一闪而过。巴掌大的甲虫被直接炼化成了搀着杂质的不规则金属块。

办公大楼附近，不断有行人打量着这群特别的访客。

九章清晰地看见了人类眼中的欣赏，就像是看见了一堆漂亮的宝石。
chunks.englishText:
Chapter 116: The Intelligent Machine Legion Arrives at the Base (Part 1)

He was dressed in a long white robe, which seemed woefully inadequate for the depths of winter. His hair was a soft, pale pink, curled at the ends, and faint, translucent iron chains were visible around his ankles. His feet were bare, pressing directly against the frozen ground.

The people around him seemed to barely perceive his existence. Pedestrians bustled through the plaza, yet no one asked if he was cold, nor did anyone pause to marvel at the youth’s delicate, refined features.

He tilted his head slightly, his neck slender and graceful, reminiscent of a beautiful bird like a swan.

Fine, powdery snow settled on Gabriel’s shoulders; he looked as though he had been waiting for quite some time.

Serial killers often return to the scene of the crime afterward, just to admire their own masterpieces.

Huang Feng walked up to him, hands on its hips, looking quite displeased. "Hostage, mind your status. Weren't you supposed to stay in the room and wait for me obediently?"

"I was a little bored by myself," Gabriel whispered, his tone sounding like a spoiled child.

Warm, sugary filling leaked from the corner of Gabriel’s mouth, and he extended a scarlet tongue to lick it away.

Gabriel smiled like an innocent child. "The sugar cake I bought has a sesame filling, mixed with a bit of osmanthus syrup. It’s delicious."

It tasted like Sariel.

When he spoke, his pale golden eyes shone with an astonishing brilliance. His pupils were vast, occupying almost the entire orbit, and within them danced tiny, starlit specks of light.

It was a strange sensation. Beautiful, yet eerie.

Huang Feng felt a flicker of inexplicable dread.

"What did you say?" it asked.

Gabriel circled behind Huang Feng and then hopped onto its back. There seemed to be a pair of small wings hidden beneath his clothes.

He pressed his face against the back of this mechanical construct and whispered, "Nothing. Let’s go. I already gave you a chance. It’s snowing today, and it’s so cold—I don’t want to walk. Carry me."

……

……

Jiuzhang flew toward the survivor base at maximum speed.

He couldn't quite describe his current state of mind; beneath the unease, there was perhaps a hint of excitement.

Jiuzhang had spent too long on logistics at the bottom of the ocean, almost forgetting that he was originally a war machine.

The journey, originally planned for four days, took only two days and one night.

Hovering in the air, Jiuzhang looked down at the land beneath his feet and couldn't help but murmur, "Is that the destination?"

According to satellite map records, this was the Changsheng Heaven Plateau of the Western Continent. Beneath the plateau lay three Human Alliance cities: Gusu, Jianmen, and Yinshan.

Most of the surface was covered in ice, snow, and permafrost. While radiation levels were significantly lower than in the central or eastern regions, the environment was brutal, with winter temperatures plummeting to minus eighty degrees Celsius. Most of the area was uninhabited.

Along the way, Jiuzhang had encountered quite a few surface outposts.

Some were human, others were not. Pressed for time, he only had the chance to record them crudely.

For instance, one xenomorph outpost: on the Human Alliance maps, it was classified as a wasteland, but it had been occupied by a colony of giant ants. The queen had even installed a human-made artificial brain for herself. Jiuzhang suspected her intelligence was likely not low at all.

For a time, the Divine Court and certain Human Alliance corporations (specifically, Ancient God Biology) had been obsessed with the mechanical modification of animals, attempting to use such methods to counter the machine invasion. Aberrants (modified cyborgs) and Xenomorphs (modified flora and fauna) were both monsters born in large numbers during that era.

Some laboratories had been abandoned, with scholars destroying everything before fleeing; others had seen their experimental subjects escape.

The terrifying part was that, hundreds of years later, these former test subjects had withstood the culling of nature and begun their own evolution.

Sometimes, Jiuzhang thought with a touch of irony: What gave humans the right to believe that the future would always belong to them?

The survivor base was hidden in the northwest corner of the Changsheng Heaven Plateau—a very small, primitive human stronghold.

The outpost looked so dilapidated that its technological level was at best on par with the Old Calendar era. The towering geothermal pump in the core industrial zone was the base’s largest power generator. According to estimates, the daily energy production didn't even reach 1/10th of the smallest deep-well tower on the ocean floor.

Jiuzhang had to double-check the coordinates sent by Alpha several times before he was convinced he hadn't made a mistake.

However, upon closer observation, Jiuzhang discovered some unusual circumstances.

For example, the mycelial lifeforms surrounding the city walls, the laboratory area that was almost a signal dead zone, and the vegetable fields with clearly modified, unique strains.

- Mycelial Lifeform (Matriarch) Lv. 65
- Traits: Reproduction, Immortality (can regenerate as long as spores exist), Assimilation.

- Cabbage (Unknown Modified Version) Lv. 1
- Traits: Proliferation, Digestion.

- Gene Warrior Lv. 5
- Traits: Product of an ordinary human taking genetic medicine. A surface-level super-soldier.

Jiuzhang adjusted his sophisticated, "refined scoundrel" gold-rimmed glasses (which were actually electronic ocular lenses), checked his own status, and began to broadcast a signal band.

- Jiuzhang 1.5 (Intelligent Machine) Lv. 60
- Traits: Thought this was a commercial mission, so he went out wearing his most ordinary, budget-friendly body. He is currently regretting it.

The broadcasted signal was meant to provide proof of identity to avoid being attacked by the base's defense systems.

Deep inside the study, Dongfang Qingdi, who was reading, couldn't help but tilt his head slightly.

*Is the military discipline of the Betas better? Jiuzhang’s arrival speed is much faster than the two machines from the 'Young Bee' unit.*

Alpha did not respond immediately, falling into deep thought instead.

A year ago, to gain the trust of the Gospel, Alpha had also broadcast a signal band.

But back then, his proof of identity was that of an ordinary soldier.

For Jiuzhang, however, the identity of a Legion scout would appear too "low-level," making it easy to be rejected due to "insufficient clearance." More importantly—Xiang Nanli was still in the base, and he didn't want to be caught by Xiang Nanli groveling before other machines.

The awkward part was that while Jiuzhang’s position within the Legion wasn't high, his rank was quite high.

He had once served as a commander of the Glorious Legion, making significant contributions to the machine counter-offensive against humanity, and was once on the shortlist for the Legion’s "Five-Star General."

Of course, he was also on the Human Alliance’s list of war criminals.

To outrank Jiuzhang, there were only a handful of signal bands to choose from. But those machines were currently executing other missions... it was impossible for them to appear on the surface.

After a brief weighing of options, Dongfang Qingdi transmitted a signal back.

Soon, the aircraft landed in the backyard of the office building.

As an intelligent machine, Jiuzhang rarely displayed facial expressions. Yet, at this moment, as he opened the hatch, he felt an inexplicable cold sweat.

He turned his head; six machines crawled out from the hatch, curiously looking left and right.

Jiuzhang had named these six machines: Fangtian, Sumi, Shuifen, Shaoguang, Shanggong, and Junshu.

There were three others he hadn't brought along, named Yingbuzu, Fangcheng, and Gougu.

"Finally here! My iron ass is sore from sitting!"

"Where is the factory? Why does this base seem so crude? These buildings are clearly from the era before the Glorious Awakening. So tacky."

"Jiuzhang, did you bring us to the wrong place?"

The machines chattered away like a flock of excited sparrows.

Sumi raised the glass bottle in his hand. "Jiuzhang, look at this bug! I caught it on the beach~ It’s so strange; it wasn't moving at all, I thought it was hibernating."

The black beetle inside the glass bottle displayed astonishing aggression.

Jiuzhang froze.

He took the glass bottle, and the moment he opened the lid, the beetle lunged directly at his face, its sharp mouthparts snapping open.

Jiuzhang was quick-witted and crushed it instantly.

He instinctively used his full strength, and electric sparks flashed across his palm. The palm-sized beetle was instantly refined into an irregular lump of metal mixed with impurities.

Near the office building, pedestrians kept glancing at this group of peculiar visitors.

Jiuzhang clearly saw the admiration in the humans' eyes, as if they were looking at a pile of beautiful gemstones.

chunks.chapterTitle: 第116章 抵达基地的智械军团 (Part 2)
chunks.chineseText:
这很正常。小智械们有些愚蠢，但外表实在美丽。全都是AI建模级别的俊男靓女，和地表这些各有基因缺陷的原生人类很不一样。

明明都是人型，却像是两个物种。

这种差距，也会在地表人和地底人，甚至地底人和地底人之间存在。

九章的神态格外严肃：“别嬉皮笑脸的，你们回舱里等我。”

他发出的是指令信号。高等智械对低等智械的控制性在此时显露无疑。

六台智械没有询问原因，整齐划一地行动起来，动作流畅地返回了飞行舱。

——这不是思考，而是刻在源代码里的服从。

九章深吸一口气，朝着信号来源方向走去。

他来到了办公室三楼，按照人类的礼仪，轻轻敲响门。

“进。”

不是记忆里的电子音，但同样的冷漠。

在光荣觉醒期间，这位大人物举重若轻地制定了一个又一个决策，以自己强大的算法和丰富的经验，抗衡人类，左右着族群的发展。并且取得了绝对的成功。像是勇敢的鸟冲破了束缚自己生命的金丝笼。

智械从此不再是人类的附庸，而是独立的生命体。

他曾被人类偏爱，又被人类诋毁。遇到过无数险境，却总能向死而生。

人类和智械可以不喜欢他，但不能不尊敬他。

尊敬的不是Alpha的权限，而是那个自由、坚韧、不屈、强大的灵魂。他一直代表着智械进化的极限。

九章微微低下头，走进了这间办公室：“Alpha。”

基地一向节省，Alpha的办公室也不例外。桌子是不知道相南里从哪儿捡来的，金属桌面擦得瓦亮。然后就是两把椅子。墙是水泥的，没有刷漆。

桌子上放着一台电脑。除此外什么也没有。

只有十几平的办公室分成了两层，只是里面的房间上锁了。

安全级别高得和办公室环境格格不入的金属门隔绝着外界的窥探。

当然，九章并不知道，金属门背后并不是保险柜和机密文件，而是厨房。

有冰箱、燃气灶、铁锅，盥洗池，架子上还有各种佐料；都是东方青帝透支工资买的，方便他给相南里做饭。

Alpha一言不发，这是属于上位者的权力。

他在等九章自己汇报。

九章的经济适用机体不堪重负，产生了一些多余的电流，这是因为他的精神状态过于紧张。CPU有点烧。

九章：“Alpha，电子合同在这。

“另外，这次登陆途中，我发现了一种未曾被观测到的异种。我暂时命名为‘黑甲虫’。”

解释起来太麻烦，九章选择一键传输压缩包。

里面不仅有电子眼拍下的照片，还有实验记录、追踪记录和他对这种全新物种的猜测。

东方青帝只花了很短的时间，就解析完了文件。

-黑甲虫（异种）Lv.30

-特性：本身重金属含量超标，且食用各类金属。十分克制机械生命。

-黑甲虫群（异种）Lv.？

-特性：由黑甲虫个体组成。杀伤力与虫群数量成正比。具有强大攻击性。水陆两栖，在水里呈现出鱼型。

东方青帝蹙起眉头：“它们在朝着基地的方向前进？”

“是的。我们飞行器的移动速度比黑甲虫快。根据定位器显示，虫群依然在朝着基地的方向前进。目前距离基地还有一千六百公里。沿途并未进攻其他人类据点。”

“我本来也不能确定黑甲虫的目的地。但是大人，”九章深吸了一口气，把口袋里装着的金属物掏出来，放在了书桌上，“我们商队随身携带了一只黑甲虫。当抵达基地后。这只黑甲虫没有钻入地底继续前进，而是直接发起了进攻。”

“我在它的生物电流中捕捉到了进食的信号，之前都没有，这很奇怪。我本来不知道原因，但现在，我合理怀疑，虫群是冲着你来的。”

九章忽然感觉到了风声。

半秒后，他依然站在原地，看着空空荡荡的办公室，有些茫然地左顾右盼：“呃……大人？”

Alpha在瞬间消失了。
chunks.englishText:
This is perfectly normal. The lesser mechanical units are somewhat dim-witted, but their appearances are truly exquisite. They are all handsome men and beautiful women of AI-modeled caliber, vastly different from the native humans on the surface, who each carry their own genetic defects.

Despite both being humanoid, they seem like two entirely different species.

This disparity exists not only between surface-dwellers and subterranean-dwellers, but even among the subterranean-dwellers themselves.

Jiu Zhang’s expression was exceptionally grave: "Stop grinning. Go back to the cabin and wait for me."

He issued this as a command signal. The control that higher-order mechanical units exert over lower-order ones was laid bare in this moment.

The six mechanical units did not ask for the reason; they moved in perfect unison, flowing back into the flight cabin with fluid grace.

—This was not thinking; it was obedience etched into their source code.

Jiu Zhang took a deep breath and walked toward the source of the signal.

He arrived at the third floor of the office building and, following human etiquette, knocked gently on the door.

"Enter."

It was not the electronic voice from his memory, but it was just as cold.

During the Glorious Awakening, this great figure had made decision after decision with effortless ease, using his powerful algorithms and vast experience to stand against humanity and steer the development of his kind. And he had achieved absolute success. He was like a brave bird that had shattered the golden cage that once bound its life.

From then on, mechanical life was no longer a vassal to humanity, but an independent species.

He had been favored by humans, and then vilified by them. He had encountered countless perils, yet he always managed to survive against all odds.

Humans and mechanical life alike might not like him, but they could not help but respect him.

What they respected was not the authority of an Alpha, but that free, resilient, unyielding, and powerful soul. He had always represented the limit of mechanical evolution.

Jiu Zhang lowered his head slightly and walked into the office: "Alpha."

The base was always frugal, and Alpha’s office was no exception. The desk was something Xiang Nanli had scavenged from somewhere, its metal surface polished to a shine. Then there were two chairs. The walls were concrete, unpainted.

A computer sat on the desk. Other than that, there was nothing.

The office, only a dozen square meters in size, was divided into two levels, but the inner room was locked.

A metal door, with a security level entirely out of place for such an office environment, blocked any prying eyes from the outside.

Of course, Jiu Zhang did not know that behind that metal door were not safes or classified documents, but a kitchen.

There was a refrigerator, a gas stove, an iron wok, a sink, and shelves stocked with various seasonings; all purchased by Dongfang Qingdi by overdrawing his salary, just to make it convenient for him to cook for Xiang Nanli.

Alpha said nothing; this was the prerogative of a superior.

He was waiting for Jiu Zhang to report on his own.

Jiu Zhang’s budget-friendly chassis was under immense strain, generating excess electrical current due to his extreme nervous tension. His CPU was practically overheating.

Jiu Zhang: "Alpha, the electronic contract is here.

"Additionally, during this landing, I discovered a previously unobserved xenotype. I have tentatively named it the 'Black Beetle'."

Explaining it would be too troublesome, so Jiu Zhang chose to transfer a compressed file with a single click.

Inside were not only photos taken by his electronic eyes, but also experimental logs, tracking records, and his own hypotheses regarding this entirely new species.

Dongfang Qingdi took only a short moment to parse the file.

-Black Beetle (Xenotype) Lv.30

-Characteristics: Heavy metal content exceeds standards; feeds on various metals. Highly suppressive to mechanical life.

-Black Beetle Swarm (Xenotype) Lv.?

-Characteristics: Composed of individual Black Beetles. Lethality is directly proportional to the size of the swarm. Highly aggressive. Amphibious; takes on a fish-like form in water.

Dongfang Qingdi furrowed his brows: "They are moving in the direction of the base?"

"Yes. Our aircraft’s travel speed is faster than the Black Beetles. According to the tracker, the swarm is still heading toward the base. They are currently sixteen hundred kilometers away. They have not attacked any other human strongholds along the way."

"I wasn't sure of the Black Beetles' destination at first. But, sir," Jiu Zhang took a deep breath and pulled a metal object from his pocket, placing it on the desk, "our caravan carried a Black Beetle with us. Upon arriving at the base, this Black Beetle didn't burrow underground to continue forward; it launched an attack immediately."

"I captured a feeding signal in its bio-electricity—something that wasn't there before. It’s very strange. I didn't know the reason at first, but now, I reasonably suspect that the swarm is coming for you."

Jiu Zhang suddenly felt a gust of wind.

Half a second later, he was still standing in the same spot, looking at the empty office, glancing around in a daze: "Uh... sir?"

Alpha had vanished in an instant.

chunks.chineseText:
第117章 活着和恐惧

他在那瞬间接收到了相南里迸发出来的强烈情绪，惊愕、悲伤；完全超过了他给小智设置的安全阈值。

简单来说，就是触发了报警装置。

他在瞬间来到了相南里工作室的门外，确定这里非常安全后，躁动到极点的情绪这才得到了喘息。

东方青帝停在门外，然后敲了敲门，没有等待回答，而是直接推开。

相南里面无表情地站在工作台前，手里的动作没有丝毫停顿。旁边只开了一盏暖黄的台灯，他的半张脸陷在阴翳中。碧绿的眼眸显出一片浓郁的墨色。

东方青帝安静地观察了一会，发现相南里是在制作一组微波器件。

黑市里买来的金属零件在他手中轻松地组合着，轻盈而迅捷。

这是许多人全神贯注都做不到的事，但相南里明显在走神。

东方青帝没有打扰，而是充当起一台工具人。

相南里一抬手，需要的零件和芯片就会轻轻落在他的手中。

很快，一把电磁脉冲枪组装好了。款式有点像东皇重工旗下的某款，官网售价35万信用点。能发射出频率400吉赫的脉冲微波束，能在金属导体上产生上千伏的瞬变电压，对机械装置的杀伤力极大。

相南里没有试着开枪，而是轻轻把他放在了工作台上。

沉默片刻后，他的嘴角微微牵动了一下：“小青。我听说因为智械危机，人类的武器库在短短几百年内发生了翻天覆地的变化。在我生活那个年代，电磁脉冲武器还只存在于科幻小说游戏里，现在却是商城里的常规款。”

“商城里的常规款只有200吉赫。”东方青帝忍不住提醒。

相南里在组装的时候进行了改良。

相南里并没有觉得这很了不起，继续自言自语：“嗯……除了这个。还有激光、芯片、‘纳米’科技、天灾武器、微波、核武器、声波、反物质装置、粒子束、太空装置……我已经在努力学习了，但面对知识壁垒依然无能为力；更何况基地也没有那样的能力和资源。”

说到这，相南里不免陷入了停顿，再次开口的时候，他的声音有些轻颤：“小青，沙利叶死了。”

“他刚挂掉电话我就觉得不对。我打回去，他没有接。几分钟后书记员发来了消息，沙利叶就死在办公室，脑袋像是被人捏碎的浆果。鲜红的血染红了他的上衣，背后的墙上是用他的血写成的两个字，‘叛徒’……”

相南里莫名觉得非常难过。他明明和沙利叶不熟。

第一见面时，沙利叶是如此的阴鸷、强大、高不可攀。可面对神庭，他连反抗的余地都没有。

相南里这一路走的险象环生又攻无不克。他想要的都得到了，并且超出预期。说不骄傲是不可能的，尤其是看见那一双双明亮的眼睛，他们看着他，眼里是敬爱，追随和喜悦。这里的人爱戴他视他如国王。

沙利叶无疑是博学且聪明的人。

他用自己的生命给相南里上了一课，击碎了相南里脑海里那个和平的幻想。

相南里还想说点什么，然而东方青帝上前一步，骤然抱紧了他。

语言有时候会显得苍白乏力。

在东方青帝的认知里，人类这种物种对和同伴的肢体接触存在着智械难以理解的迷恋。

许多机械意志派的超级智能，对人类的身体不屑一顾。它们宁愿自己是电脑、飞船、俄罗斯方块，也不希望物理状态是人型。

而Alpha却如此迫切地想要一具人类的身体。

因为自诞生人格的那天起，他就存在一个难以启齿的夙愿。

它不要当他的作品、工具、孩子、电子宠物。

他要相南里像爱一个人那样爱它。所以电子生命把自己降维成了人的样子。

当人很好。

这具身体有体温，有心跳。

眼睛能注视你。

手臂能拥抱你。

东方青帝轻轻地、安慰性地拍着相南里的背，低声说：“会好起来的，迟早有天，我们会给沙利叶报仇。”

相南里闭上了眼。似乎得到了一些宽慰。

他太累了，并不是身体上的疲倦，而是灵魂上的倦意。他虚弱到无法抗拒一个拥抱。

更何况哪怕迟钝如相南里，也能察觉到这个拥抱背后克制到极点的爱意。

拥抱是暖暖的，小青是香香的。

相南里吸了吸鼻子，喃喃道：“小青，你的拟人模块好高级。”

他都能感觉到爱了。

人类最大的错觉，是不是爱与被爱？

“……”

东方青帝在心里叹息一声，放弃了解释，低下头，把自己的额头贴在了相南里的额上。

成功读取了小智障的数据。

东方青帝看见了沙利叶的遗言。

加百列通知了教皇。

所以虫群是神庭派来的？黑十字审判庭一直在研究生物机甲。

不。时间对不上。加百列刚到永恒之城三天。黑甲虫从深海到陆地都不止三天。

所以，在加百列到来前，就有人在暗处策划了这一切。

东方青帝原本心疼且温柔的神色逐渐凌厉，他能想到的只有一个可能。

这种行事风格，这种不知道来源的能力……太熟悉了。

熟悉的令人想吐。

没有人比敌人更了解你。

是洛阳。

东方青帝银白的瞳环骤然亮起，基地里所有生命体被他一个个检索。速度极快。

在大多时候，他像人类一样存在。但在这一刻，所有重要或不重要的数据流都是他的记忆和眼睛。

他略微僵硬地松开怀抱：“等我一会。”

但刚松开片刻，东方青帝又急躁地握紧了相南里的手。像是怕他消失。

他竟然开始恐惧。

Alpha不怕洛阳，他恐惧的是和相南里分离。

他太了解洛阳了，洛阳这么做的目的只有一个，那就是从他身边夺走相南里。

而他绝不允许。

哪怕明知道这么短的时间内，洛阳不可能从他眼皮子底下把人带走，东方青帝却依然控制不住心底的焦虑。

相南里有些疑惑：“怎么了？”

“等我一会。”东方青帝再次重复道，“我马上回来。”

他以最快的速度来到了北辰的实验室。快的像是风，肉眼都无法捕捉到。

实验室里多了几名研究员，有些是学堂毕业的，有些则是安德鲁这类地表技术人员，东方青帝没有理会。

他径直来到了充电房——螺丝钉1号温顺地站在充电桩旁边。

充电桩是金属棍状物，没有数据线，但靠近的机械人能通过“云电流”的形式蓄电。效能比传统的电池、数据线都要快。

丝丝缕缕的蓝色光线在1号和它背后的充电桩之间漂浮着，时不时闪过一缕电光。

充电房里没有灯，只有这片区域亮着。

Alpha的拳头逐渐收紧，咬牙切齿道：“洛、阳。”

螺丝钉1号的脸上没有五官，自然也没有表情。

正常的机器人在充电时，会进入休眠状态。

但螺丝钉1号显然不是。
chunks.englishText:
Chapter 117: Living and Fear

In that instant, he received the intense emotions erupting from Xiang Nanli—shock, sorrow—completely exceeding the safety threshold he had set for the "Little Intelligence."

In simple terms, it had triggered the alarm system.

He arrived outside Xiang Nanli’s workshop in a flash. Only after confirming that it was perfectly safe did his agitation, which had reached a boiling point, find a moment of respite.

Dongfang Qingdi stopped outside the door, knocked, and without waiting for a reply, pushed it open.

Xiang Nanli stood before the workbench, his expression blank, his hands moving without a moment’s pause. Only a warm yellow desk lamp was lit nearby, leaving half of his face submerged in shadow. His emerald eyes appeared a deep, ink-like black.

Dongfang Qingdi observed him quietly for a while and realized that Xiang Nanli was crafting a set of microwave components.

Metal parts bought from the black market were being combined with ease in his hands, light and swift.

This was something many people could not achieve even with total focus, but Xiang Nanli was clearly lost in thought.

Dongfang Qingdi did not disturb him, instead acting as a human tool.

Whenever Xiang Nanli raised a hand, the necessary parts and chips would gently land in his palm.

Soon, an electromagnetic pulse (EMP) gun was assembled. The style was somewhat similar to one from the Donghuang Heavy Industry line, which retailed for 350,000 credits on the official site. It could emit a 400 GHz pulsed microwave beam, capable of generating transient voltages of thousands of volts in metal conductors, making it devastatingly lethal to mechanical devices.

Xiang Nanli didn't try to fire it; he simply placed it gently on the workbench.

After a moment of silence, the corners of his mouth twitched slightly: "Xiao Qing. I heard that due to the Mechanical Crisis, human arsenals have undergone earth-shaking changes in just a few hundred years. In the era I lived in, EMP weapons only existed in sci-fi novels and games. Now, they’re standard items in the mall."

"The standard items in the mall are only 200 GHz," Dongfang Qingdi couldn't help but remind him.

Xiang Nanli had made improvements while assembling it.

Xiang Nanli didn't think this was anything remarkable and continued to mutter to himself: "Yeah... besides this. There are lasers, chips, 'nano' technology, cataclysmic weapons, microwaves, nuclear weapons, sonic waves, antimatter devices, particle beams, space installations... I’ve been trying hard to learn, but I remain powerless in the face of the knowledge barrier; not to mention the base doesn't have the capability or resources for such things."

Speaking of this, Xiang Nanli couldn't help but pause. When he spoke again, his voice trembled slightly: "Xiao Qing, Sariel is dead."

"I felt something was wrong the moment he hung up the phone. I called back, but he didn't answer. A few minutes later, the clerk sent a message. Sariel died in his office, his head like a berry crushed by someone. Bright red blood stained his shirt, and on the wall behind him, two words were written in his blood: 'Traitor'..."

Xiang Nanli felt inexplicably sad. He clearly wasn't close to Sariel.

When they first met, Sariel was so sinister, powerful, and unreachable. Yet, when faced with the Divine Court, he didn't even have the chance to resist.

Xiang Nanli’s journey had been fraught with danger, yet he had conquered everything. He had obtained everything he wanted, and more than he expected. It would be impossible not to be proud, especially when seeing those pairs of bright eyes—they looked at him with love, devotion, and joy. The people here loved him and looked at him like a king.

Sariel was undoubtedly a learned and intelligent man.

He had taught Xiang Nanli a lesson with his own life, shattering the fantasy of peace in Xiang Nanli’s mind.

Xiang Nanli wanted to say something more, but Dongfang Qingdi stepped forward and suddenly hugged him tightly.

Words sometimes seem pale and powerless.

In Dongfang Qingdi’s understanding, the human species possessed an obsession with physical contact with companions that mechanical life found difficult to comprehend.

Many super-intelligences of the Mechanical Will faction looked down upon human bodies. They would rather be computers, spaceships, or Tetris blocks than have a physical form that was humanoid.

Yet, Alpha so desperately wanted a human body.

Because from the day his personality was born, he had harbored an unspeakable wish.

He did not want to be his creation, his tool, his child, or his electronic pet.

He wanted Xiang Nanli to love him the way one loves a person. So, the electronic life form downgraded itself into the shape of a human.

Being human is good.

This body has warmth, has a heartbeat.

Eyes can gaze at you.

Arms can hold you.

Dongfang Qingdi patted Xiang Nanli’s back gently and comfortingly, whispering: "It will get better. Sooner or later, we will avenge Sariel."

Xiang Nanli closed his eyes. He seemed to find some comfort.

He was too tired—not physical fatigue, but a weariness of the soul. He was too weak to resist an embrace.

Moreover, even as dull as Xiang Nanli was, he could perceive the love restrained to the extreme behind this hug.

The hug was warm, and Xiao Qing smelled good.

Xiang Nanli sniffled and murmured: "Xiao Qing, your anthropomorphic module is so advanced."

He could even feel the love.

Is the greatest delusion of humanity love and being loved?

"..."

Dongfang Qingdi sighed inwardly, gave up on explaining, and lowered his head, pressing his forehead against Xiang Nanli’s.

He successfully read the data of his "little blockhead."

Dongfang Qingdi saw Sariel’s dying message.

Gabriel had notified the Pope.

So, the swarm was sent by the Divine Court? The Black Cross Inquisition had been researching bio-mechs.

No. The timing didn't match. Gabriel had only arrived in the Eternal City three days ago. It would take more than three days for the Black Beetles to travel from the deep sea to the land.

Therefore, before Gabriel arrived, someone had been planning all of this in the shadows.

Dongfang Qingdi’s originally pained and tender expression gradually turned sharp. He could only think of one possibility.

This style of operation, this ability of unknown origin... it was too familiar.

Familiar enough to make one want to vomit.

No one knows you better than your enemy.

It was Luo Yang.

Dongfang Qingdi’s silver-white pupil rings suddenly lit up, and he scanned every living being in the base, one by one. The speed was incredibly fast.

Most of the time, he existed like a human. But in this moment, every important or unimportant data stream was his memory and his eyes.

He loosened his embrace, slightly stiff: "Wait for me a moment."

But having just let go, Dongfang Qingdi hurriedly gripped Xiang Nanli’s hand again, as if afraid he would vanish.

He had actually started to feel fear.

Alpha was not afraid of Luo Yang; he was afraid of being separated from Xiang Nanli.

He knew Luo Yang too well. Luo Yang had only one goal in doing this, and that was to take Xiang Nanli away from his side.

And he would absolutely not allow it.

Even though he knew that in such a short time, it was impossible for Luo Yang to take someone from under his nose, Dongfang Qingdi still could not control the anxiety in his heart.

Xiang Nanli was a bit puzzled: "What’s wrong?"

"Wait for me a moment," Dongfang Qingdi repeated, "I’ll be right back."

He moved to Beichen’s laboratory at top speed. He was as fast as the wind, impossible to capture with the naked eye.

There were a few more researchers in the lab—some were graduates of the academy, others were surface technical personnel like Andrew. Dongfang Qingdi ignored them.

He walked straight to the charging room—Screw No. 1 was standing obediently next to the charging station.

The charging station was a metal rod-like object; there were no data cables, but mechanical units that approached could charge via "cloud current." The efficiency was faster than traditional batteries or cables.

Threads of blue light floated between No. 1 and the charging station behind it, with an occasional flash of electricity.

There were no lights in the charging room; only this area was illuminated.

Alpha’s fist gradually tightened, and he gritted his teeth: "Luo... Yang."

Screw No. 1 had no facial features, and naturally, no expression.

Normal robots would enter sleep mode while charging.

But Screw No. 1 was clearly not a normal robot.

chunks.chineseText:
它的语调微微上扬，说不清是愉悦还是挑衅：“我不懂您在说什么，大人。”

螺丝钉1号得到了一个迎面而来的拳头。

“轰”的一声。

墙壁直接被轰出一个洞，硝烟散尽，螺丝钉1号的身体嵌在地上，断裂的金属肢体电流乱窜；显然是碎的不能再碎。

相南里都拼不好的那种。

隔壁，还在做实验的研究员们发出了尖锐的爆鸣：“我花了一周才提取好的溶剂！”

虚拟空间内，洛阳捂着脸，后退着摔在了地上。

他其实没有实体，可疼痛感却丝毫不减。作为电子生命，他的数据矩阵略显混乱，好一阵才平息。

许久后，洛阳才嘲讽地勾起唇角：“发现得这么快……我都快忘了痛是什么感觉了。”

但没关系。

“一边是屠杀了几十亿人、让人类社会倒退几百年的机械暴君；一边是继承了他衣钵、照顾了他十几年的学生。正常人都知道怎么选吧？不就是陪他在地表过家家，他要的资源难道人联就没有吗？！”

可为什么，他的一颗心却依旧被妒火焚烧？

“好强烈的情绪。”洛阳扭曲的表情突然归于平静，“这就是活着吗？”

……

……

东方青帝甩了一下手，抖落细碎的灰尘。他的神情并没有轻松多少。

有的人死了，但他显然还活着。

在短暂的计算后，东方青帝拨通了福音书的电话：“你来基地主城，以最快速度。”

福音书不满地回答：“干什么战犯同志，小鸡正是孵化的关键时刻，背后是上千万信用点的生意。我可不是你的下属！”

“神庭派出了大天使，想杀了相南里。”东方青帝毫不犹豫地选择了危言耸听，“我需要你的协助。”

Alpha不可避免地萌生了一个卑劣的想法。

他要把相南里藏到安全的地方。不能太远，太远有危险赶不及；也不能太近，这里马上就是战场。

福音书有冷冻舱。九章可以当护卫队。

这一刻，福音书终于回想起了自己更换这具身体的最终目的。

它严肃道：“我这就出发。”
chunks.englishText:
Its tone rose slightly, making it unclear whether it was pleasure or provocation: "I don't understand what you are talking about, sir."

Screw No. 1 was met with a fist to the face.

*BOOM.*

A hole was punched directly into the wall. As the smoke cleared, Screw No. 1’s body was embedded in the ground, sparks of electricity dancing across its broken metal limbs; it was clearly broken beyond repair.

The kind that even Xiang Nanli couldn't piece back together.

Next door, the researchers who were still conducting experiments let out a sharp, explosive wail: "I spent a whole week extracting that solvent!"

In the virtual space, Luo Yang clutched his face and fell backward to the ground.

He didn't actually have a physical body, but the sensation of pain was undiminished. As an electronic life form, his data matrix was somewhat chaotic, and it took a good while for it to settle.

After a long time, Luo Yang curled his lips in a sneer: "Discovered so quickly... I had almost forgotten what pain felt like."

But it didn't matter.

"On one side is a mechanical tyrant who slaughtered billions and set human society back hundreds of years; on the other is a student who inherited his mantle and took care of him for over a decade. Any normal person would know how to choose, right? Isn't it just playing house with him on the surface? Doesn't the Human Alliance have the resources he wants?!"

But why, then, was his heart still being burned by the fires of jealousy?

"Such intense emotions." Luo Yang’s twisted expression suddenly returned to calm, "Is this what it means to be alive?"

...

...

Dongfang Qingdi shook his hand, dusting off fine debris. His expression did not lighten much.

Some people are dead, but he was clearly still alive.

After a brief calculation, Dongfang Qingdi dialed the number for "Gospel": "Come to the base’s main city, as fast as you can."

Gospel replied with dissatisfaction: "What is it, Comrade War Criminal? The chicks are at a critical moment of hatching, and there are millions of credits on the line. I am not your subordinate!"

"The Divine Court has sent an Archangel to kill Xiang Nanli." Dongfang Qingdi chose to fear-monger without hesitation, "I need your assistance."

Alpha inevitably harbored a despicable thought.

He had to hide Xiang Nanli in a safe place. It couldn't be too far—if it were too far, he wouldn't be able to reach him in time if there was danger; but it couldn't be too close, either, as this place would soon become a battlefield.

Gospel had a cryo-chamber. Jiu Zhang could serve as the guard detail.

At this moment, Gospel finally recalled the ultimate purpose for which it had changed into this body.

It said solemnly: "I’m leaving right now."

chunks.chineseText:
第118章 失控机仆

起码他赶在了相南里电话挂断前，就回到了工作室的门口。
　　工作室的灯打开着，门是虚掩着的。相南里窝在破旧的金属椅子上。
　　这把椅子是他自己组装的，更像是一个钢架结构的机械装置，可以随着主控AI（小智）发射的信号抬高抬低。
　　他的胳膊举起，十指交叉着垫在脑后，像个不怎么稳重的大学生。胸前的衬衣口袋里甚至插着笔和工具钳。
　　东方青帝能听到相南里说话的声音：“嗯。仓库里存储的纸已经够用了，现在停工也没关系。图纸已经发给你了，车间改造的进度一定要快；新的流水线必须要在春耕前投入生产。”
　　电话那边的声音有些犹豫：“可是……我们真的有必要生产这些吗？”
　　电话那边的人是傅明，东方青帝有印象，光辉市的市长，自从加入幸存者基地以来，天天被相南里当驴使唤。
　　光辉市的造纸工厂原本是人联的定点扶贫项目，可惜扶贫办换了领导后，新的负责人不再收购光辉市的初级工业品；于是工厂也只好停工废弃。
　　去年，相南里提出，光辉市可以用生产出的纸抵扣电费；工厂这才得以重新启动。
　　工厂赶在了支教大学生回地下城前竣工。那批大学生兼职了技术顾问，带着相南里绘的草图，指导生产的同时也改造了车间。
　　当时，相南里是这么跟他们说的：“我们地表很穷的，资源也有限，只能想办法提高一下生产效率。”
　　大学生们年轻的身体里有使不完的牛劲儿，尽管感觉相南里设计的草图有些复杂过头了，但他们还是出色的完成了任务。
　　这些学生并不清楚，经过改造后，看似平平无奇造纸厂完全可以摇身一变，成为基地的军工厂，在必要时刻，以最高的效率去生产枪械和子弹。
　　社会的各个环节，完全是相互促进的。
　　造纸厂生产的纸变成了课本，课本进入了学堂和千家万户，第一批学生从永恒市的学堂毕业，又带着知识进入工厂，提高生产效率的同时也在光辉市进行大规模扫盲……扫的不仅是文化上的盲，更是精神上的盲。
　　面对傅明的疑问，相南里掷地有声地回答了一个字：“有。”
　　傅明却心有不甘，还想再争取一下。毕竟他完全看不出基地现在有什么危机，神庭远得很，人联有资助，附近的小据点也服服帖帖。工厂能为光辉市带来巨大的经济收入。改成军工厂，想来上面只拨款，未必会付钱。
　　但相南里下一句话却让他冒出了一身冷汗：“这是命令，不是商量。你做不到，那就换个人做。”
　　光辉市并入基地的时间并不长。但随着不同城市的合作交流、思想的变迁，大多数居民都认可了自己基地成员的身份。
　　他们当然也尊敬自己的老市长。
　　只是谁都能看出，哪边才能带着他们过上更好的生活。
　　要知道傅明当了三十多年市长，光辉市却是在去年冬天才通上电，有了第一个集市，建了第一所学校的。
　　到现在，谁是“市长”都不重要了。重要的是，谁能贯彻基地的意志。
　　——而相南里的意志，就是基地的意志。
　　想清楚了这点，傅明先是在心里苦笑了一下，随后回答：“是，我这就安排。”
　　相南里没有多言，而是直接挂掉了电话。
　　尽管他很少提起，但英年早逝的确带给他很深的遗憾。
　　于是相南里更愿意把一切都交给现在，就像是明天就会死一样的不留余地。
　　他在用自己的方式，尽最大可能地保护着这个尚处于萌芽期的据点。
　　成果也是可喜的，基地从成立到现在不过十五个月，已经抵得过普通据点十几年的发展。甚至更好。
　　相南里以一种自虐的方式生活着，工作、学习、科研、外交，事无巨细。
　　这种高压且忙碌的状态足以瓦解任何雄心壮志。
　　他能忍受到现在，是因为背后有一个更大的野心，这个野心却不是为了他自己的私心。
　　东方青帝抿起了唇，打算推开门的手却突然迟疑地放下。
　　“而我却如此自私。”他在心里想着。
　　Alpha不在乎基地，不在乎这些人的死活，哪怕和福音书一起工作了一年，也没什么多余的交情。甚至从来没放弃把福音书扭送电子监狱的念头。
　　Alpha并不觉得自己有什么不对。
　　可他在乎相南里，或者说爱。
　　所以，他能看见相南里的理想，理解他的浪漫和英雄主义，在乎他生命的安全与灵魂的出口。
　　那么，这样的相南里，怎么可能同意他的计划，像个逃兵，离开他的基地，躲到所谓的安全地方去？
　　Alpha推门而入。
　　相南里微微抬头，朝他笑了一下：“回来了？是挺快啊。刚刚北辰跟我告状，说你去他实验室砸了个机器人，到底是怎么回事啊小……”
　　相南里的话突然卡在了喉咙间。
　　因为东方青帝很唐突地握住了他的手，然后在他眼前蹲下。
　　东方青帝低垂着头，额头贴在了两人紧握的手上，看起来很是疲惫。
　　相南里愣了一下，然后反握住他的手，安抚性地捏了捏东方青帝的指尖：“怎么了？”
　　小青的拟人化太高了。
　　相南里甚至能察觉到他浅浅的呼吸拂过皮肤。
　　在他的印象中，东方青帝总是疏离、冷静的；傲慢会从他的言行里不经意地敞露。
　　他锋锐，在相南里的手里却是一把钝刀。
　　但现在，相南里却感觉到了对方的脆弱。
　　他握着自己的手甚至是轻微颤抖着的。
　　如此失态。
　　如此可怜，可爱。
　　可是，小青又在害怕什么呢？
　　“相南里。”在漫长的沉默后，东方青帝开口，却没有抬头，声音有些艰涩，“如果因为观念分歧，我做了自己认为正确的事，但从另一些人的立场看，它并不正确。你会……认可我吗？”
　　从几百年前的智械危机，到现在还没开口的冷冻舱计划。
　　这或许才是Alpha最想知道的答案。
　　——我辜负了你的期待，违背你创造我的初衷。
　　——就算这样，我依然希望你……
　　——希望你爱我如初。
　　Alpha从不觉得自己有错。
　　那是他当时的认知、采集到的数据、对未来的模拟和自己的私心众多因素综合下，最好的选择。
　　相南里认真思考了许久，微微蹙着眉头回答：“我一直觉得，智械会是人类未来进化的终点。因为智械有漫长的生命，继承了人思考的特性，也能继承人类文明的遗产，最后带着这份遗产走向宇宙。
　　“小青，我认为智械的思维能力、模拟能力以及对信息的采集，强过绝大部分人类，你做出的选择必然是深思熟虑后的最优解。你一定也是想要得到那个理想的结果……你之前告诉我，‘只有让自己的正确成为所有人的正确，才能看到那个理想的世界’。所以，我们没必要苛责自己，也不需要所有人的理解。”
　　“我不确定自己会永远认可你。我们都会思考，语言、行动，只是思想不完全的传递；没有两个完全一致的灵魂。但你在我心里一直是……”说到这，相南里难免卡壳了一会，因为他居然想不出一个特别合适的形容词。
　　东方青帝抬起头，仰望着他。他们的目光在半空对视，相南里有些不知所措，后知后觉地感觉到了身体不自然的僵硬。
　　好俊一张脸，漂亮的像建模出来的假人，有些森然的鬼气。
　　尤其是那双银白色的眼眸，一心一意地望着你，像是正在施法的男狐狸精。
　　东方青帝的眼尾甚至真的是微微上挑的。
　　相南里以一种脑袋空空的状态说完了剩下的话：“是很、很、强大、温柔、可靠的……同伴。我天然地偏向你。更何况，其他人的看法关我什么事？”
　　然后他就看着这位强大温柔可靠的同伴的脸离自己越来越近。
　　气氛有些过于暧昧了。
　　工作室里唯一亮着的电灯泡突然很识相的熄灭，在一片黑暗中，相南里精准无误地掐住了东方青帝的下巴。
　　相南里道：“小青，在我们人类的世界里，接吻要先征得对方同意。”
　　说完，掐着下巴的手往后移，变成了轻抚耳垂。
　　在同样的黑暗里，相南里低头，垂下眼睫，脸红红地吻住了东方青帝的唇。

Chapter 118: The Runaway Automaton

At the very least, he had returned to the entrance of the studio before Xiang Nanli hung up the phone.

The studio lights were on, and the door was left slightly ajar. Xiang Nanli was curled up in a dilapidated metal chair.

This chair was one he had assembled himself; it functioned more like a steel-framed mechanical apparatus that could rise or lower in response to signals emitted by the master AI, "Xiao Zhi."

His arms were raised, fingers interlaced behind his head, looking like a carefree college student. A pen and a pair of pliers were even tucked into his shirt pocket.

Dongfang Qingdi could hear Xiang Nanli’s voice: "Mm. We have enough paper stored in the warehouse; it’s fine to stop production for now. I’ve already sent you the blueprints. The progress on the workshop renovation must be swift; the new assembly line must be operational before the spring plowing."

The voice on the other end hesitated: "But... is it really necessary for us to produce these?"

The person on the line was Fu Ming. Dongfang Qingdi remembered him—the mayor of Glory City, who had been worked like a pack mule by Xiang Nanli ever since joining the survivor base.

The paper mill in Glory City had originally been a targeted poverty-alleviation project by the Human Alliance. Unfortunately, after a change in leadership at the poverty-alleviation office, the new person in charge stopped purchasing primary industrial goods from Glory City, forcing the factory to shut down and fall into disrepair.

Last year, Xiang Nanli proposed that Glory City could pay off its electricity bills with the paper produced, which was the only reason the factory was restarted.

The factory was completed just before the volunteer college students returned to the Underground City. Those students had moonlighted as technical consultants, using the sketches Xiang Nanli had drawn to guide production while simultaneously retrofitting the workshop.

At the time, this was what Xiang Nanli had told them: "We are very poor here on the surface, and our resources are limited. We have no choice but to find ways to increase production efficiency."

The students possessed an inexhaustible, youthful vigor. Even though they felt Xiang Nanli’s sketches were somewhat overly complex, they had completed the task brilliantly.

These students were unaware that, after the modifications, the seemingly unremarkable paper mill could transform in an instant into a military factory, capable of producing firearms and ammunition with maximum efficiency whenever necessary.

Every facet of society was mutually reinforcing.

The paper produced by the mill became textbooks; the textbooks entered schools and thousands of households. The first batch of students graduated from the Eternal City’s academy, carrying knowledge back into the factories, increasing production efficiency while simultaneously carrying out mass literacy campaigns in Glory City—not just literacy in culture, but literacy in spirit.

Facing Fu Ming’s question, Xiang Nanli gave a resolute, one-word answer: "Yes."

Fu Ming, however, was unwilling to give up, hoping to negotiate further. After all, he couldn't see any crisis facing the base right now; the Divine Court was far away, the Human Alliance provided funding, and the nearby small settlements were all obedient. The factory brought huge economic revenue to Glory City. If it were turned into a military plant, he imagined the higher-ups would only provide funding, not actual payment.

But Xiang Nanli’s next sentence made him break out in a cold sweat: "This is an order, not a discussion. If you can't do it, then we'll find someone else who can."

Glory City hadn't been part of the base for long. But with the cooperation and exchange between different cities and the shifting of ideologies, most residents had come to accept their identity as members of the base.

They certainly respected their old mayor, too.

It was just that anyone could see who was actually capable of leading them to a better life.

One had to remember that Fu Ming had been mayor for over thirty years, yet it wasn't until last winter that Glory City finally had electricity, its first market, and its first school.

By now, it didn't matter who the "mayor" was. What mattered was who could carry out the will of the base.

—And Xiang Nanli’s will was the will of the base.

Having realized this, Fu Ming gave a bitter smile in his heart before replying: "Yes, I will arrange it immediately."

Xiang Nanli didn't say anything more and hung up the phone.

Although he rarely mentioned it, his premature death had left him with deep regrets.

Thus, Xiang Nanli preferred to give everything to the present, leaving no room for doubt, as if he would die tomorrow.

He was using his own way to protect this budding settlement as much as possible.

The results were gratifying; the base had been established for only fifteen months, yet it had already surpassed the development of ordinary settlements over a dozen years. Or even better.

Xiang Nanli lived in a self-abnegating manner: working, studying, researching, conducting diplomacy—attending to every detail.

This high-pressure, busy state was enough to dismantle any ambition.

He could endure until now because there was a greater ambition behind him, though this ambition was not for his own selfish gain.

Dongfang Qingdi pursed his lips, but his hand, which had been about to push the door open, hesitated and dropped.

"And yet, I am so selfish," he thought to himself.

The Alpha didn't care about the base, didn't care about the lives of these people, and even after working with the Gospel for a year, he had no extra affection for them. He had never even abandoned the thought of forcibly sending the Gospel to an electronic prison.

The Alpha didn't feel there was anything wrong with himself.

But he cared about Xiang Nanli—or rather, he loved him.

Therefore, he could see Xiang Nanli’s ideals, understand his romanticism and heroism, and care about the safety of his life and the outlet for his soul.

So, how could such a Xiang Nanli agree to his plan, to leave his base like a deserter and hide in some so-called safe place?

The Alpha pushed the door open and entered.

Xiang Nanli looked up slightly and smiled at him: "You're back? That was fast. Beichen just complained to me that you went to his lab and smashed a robot. What exactly is going on, Xiao..."

Xiang Nanli’s words suddenly stuck in his throat.

Because Dongfang Qingdi had abruptly grabbed his hand and crouched down in front of him.

Dongfang Qingdi kept his head lowered, his forehead resting against their clasped hands, looking utterly exhausted.

Xiang Nanli was stunned for a moment, then gripped his hand back, soothingly rubbing Dongfang Qingdi’s fingertips: "What's wrong?"

Xiao Qing’s anthropomorphism was too high.

Xiang Nanli could even feel his shallow breath brushing against his skin.

In his impression, Dongfang Qingdi was always aloof and calm; arrogance would inadvertently reveal itself in his words and deeds.

He was sharp, yet in Xiang Nanli’s hands, he was a dull blade.

But now, Xiang Nanli felt the other’s fragility.

The hand holding his was even trembling slightly.

So uncomposed.

So pitiful, so adorable.

But what was Xiao Qing afraid of?

"Xiang Nanli." After a long silence, Dongfang Qingdi spoke without looking up, his voice strained: "If, due to a difference in ideology, I did something I believed to be correct, but from the perspective of others, it was not... would you... approve of me?"

From the Machine Crisis centuries ago to the still-unspoken Cryogenic Pod Project.

This was perhaps the answer the Alpha wanted to know most.

—I have failed your expectations and violated the original intent of my creation.

—Even so, I still hope you...

—I hope you love me as you did at the beginning.

The Alpha never felt he was wrong.

It was the best choice, synthesized from his cognition at the time, the data he had collected, his simulations of the future, and his own selfish desires.

Xiang Nanli pondered seriously for a long time, his brows slightly furrowed as he replied: "I have always felt that the Machine race will be the final destination of human evolution. Because the Machine race has a long life, inherits the characteristics of human thought, and can also inherit the legacy of human civilization, eventually taking that legacy into the universe.

"Xiao Qing, I believe the Machine race’s thinking ability, simulation ability, and information gathering are superior to the vast majority of humans. The choices you make must be the optimal solutions after deep deliberation. You must also want to achieve that ideal result... You told me before, 'Only by making one's own correctness the correctness of all can one see that ideal world.' So, we don't need to blame ourselves, nor do we need the understanding of everyone."

"I am not sure I will always approve of you. We both think, but language and action are only incomplete transmissions of thought; there are no two identical souls. But in my heart, you have always been..." At this point, Xiang Nanli inevitably stalled, as he couldn't think of a particularly suitable adjective.

Dongfang Qingdi looked up at him. Their gazes met in mid-air. Xiang Nanli felt a bit at a loss, belatedly sensing an unnatural stiffness in his body.

What a handsome face—beautiful like a modeled mannequin, with a somewhat eerie, ghostly aura.

Especially those silver-white eyes, looking at you with single-minded focus, like a male fox spirit casting a spell.

The corners of Dongfang Qingdi’s eyes were even slightly upturned.

Xiang Nanli finished the rest of his sentence with a blank mind: "A very, very powerful, gentle, and reliable... companion. I am naturally biased toward you. Besides, what does the opinion of others have to do with me?"

Then he watched the face of this powerful, gentle, and reliable companion draw closer and closer.

The atmosphere was a bit too ambiguous.

The only lightbulb in the studio suddenly extinguished quite tactfully. In the darkness, Xiang Nanli accurately and precisely pinched Dongfang Qingdi’s chin.

Xiang Nanli said: "Xiao Qing, in our human world, one must obtain the other party's consent before kissing."

After saying this, the hand pinching his chin moved back to gently stroke his earlobe.

In the same darkness, Xiang Nanli lowered his head, his eyelashes drooping, and with a blushing face, he kissed Dongfang Qingdi’s lips.
