Bern San answered decisively: "I would die. If he does this, he must have his reasons."

Gabriel couldn't help but laugh.

It was a very strange laugh—not happy, but sharp, even with a hint of vague hatred. But clearly, this hatred was not directed at Xiang Nanli.

When the bus drove to the dormitory area, the monitor Gabriel carried with him rang.

"Where are you?" Huang Feng’s tone was not good.

Gabriel let out a long "Hmm": "I was sleepy, so I went back to the guesthouse to sleep first. Did you see Xiang Nanli?"

Huang Feng proudly raised her head: "Of course. They originally wanted to stop me, but I am a Glory-level mechanical intelligence!"

Gabriel was a bit speechless, but felt that teaching a mechanical intelligence human etiquette was perhaps too abstract: "Then you didn't cause any destruction, did you?"

"No. I had only beaten the third soldier robot when Xiang Nanli came out."

She had been very measured in her actions.

Those robots only had broken ball joints and could be used again with a little repair.

Although Huang Feng was a subordinate of the Alpha, she had never met Xiang Nanli.

Xiang Nanli was also very surprised by this thug who appeared in the middle of the night, and it was Xiao Zhi who stopped him from opening the safety circuit breaker...

Yes, that’s right. Outside his own workshop, Xiang Nanli had installed some of the most lethal mechanical devices in the base to protect his precious research.

Even if Gabriel had come in person, he could have been blocked for a while.

Xiang Nanli listened earnestly to Huang Feng’s words, and after sincerely thanking her for the valuable intelligence she brought, he politely asked her to leave his workshop.

Gabriel returned to the guesthouse and waited on the sofa for half an hour. Huang Feng also returned.

She skillfully went to the bathroom to fetch a basin of hot water, placed it by Gabriel’s feet, and signaled for him to wash his feet. This kid walked around barefoot on the ground every day, yet didn't even have a single case of frostbite.

Sometimes, Huang Feng felt he was more like a machine than she was.

Huang Feng asked: "Are those Eastern Expeditionary forces here to save you?"

"No."

"Oh. Even if they were, I wouldn't let them save you. Your ransom hasn't arrived yet."

The beautiful and foolish mechanical intelligence said so.

Knowing that the "devils" weren't brought here by her, Huang Feng’s mood improved significantly.

Huang Feng hummed a song while scrubbing Gabriel’s feet, then suddenly let out a long sigh: "I wonder where the Captain and the others are."

...

...

The Captain in Huang Feng’s mouth was, of course, the Eastern Azure Emperor.

In just a few days, the black beetles had built a honeycomb-like nest underground. The walls felt like pottery to the touch.

The entire nest was made of mud and the saliva of the black beetles.

A rich smell of rust floated in the air.

The oxygen underground was quite thin, and there were no light sources.

However, these difficulties were still within their expectations.

The human soldiers connected their oxygen tubes; those with electronic eyes turned them on, and those without used their own searchlights. In any case, the eyesight of these black beetles had long since degenerated; they used sonar detection.

After entering the underground, the 70-person group split into 8 teams. The organization was 10 people per team, and the team Qin Jiuzhang was in was missing one person.

Their mission was to plant explosives at different locations in the hive and detonate them.

And the Eastern Azure Emperor was in a team by himself; his mission was to find the hive-brain and sever the nerves of the giant black beetle.

The members of the eight teams walked toward their respective mission points. Guided by the map, the teams constantly dispersed. Fortunately, within a certain range, they could still communicate via Bluetooth headsets.

chunks.chapterTitle: 第127章 这是我的战争（2） (Part 2)
chunks.chineseText:
“说起来，你有没有觉得很奇怪。”应如是联系上易横行，“来之前说没有地图，到了后没多久，三维的地图就发过来了。”

易横行：“说明基地的人一直在采集信息，好好工作。”

“但是这种3d地图，制作出来需要的不止是时间，还需要一些保密技术。”

在信息不发达、人口不流动的年代，地图被叫做舆图，属于军事机密。直到现在，人联的网络地图上也有大量的空缺。

展示出来的，只是它们想展示的部分罢了。

绘制地图的科技算不上特别高端，但人联一直对私人禁用。

“基地或许没有你想的那么简单。奇怪的科技树，神秘的菌丝病治愈技术，还有一个强大到不对劲的人造人。不过……”

应如是的声音突然消失了。

易横行“喂”了两声。很显然，是两人距离过远，通讯断掉了。

“最讨厌说话说一半的！”

八个小组朝着虫巢中心靠拢。

易横行举起手里的枪，路和墙壁都变得有些松软，想来这部分的巢穴还是新修的。

道路很窄，虫子不需要人那么大的空间，易横行只能弯着腰往前走。

“快到了，快到了。”

在黑暗中，他小声的安慰着自己和队友。

根据地图显示，他们离目的地已经很近了。地面上也多了许多坚硬的虫壳。

这群甲虫像是螃蟹一样，会蜕壳。

突然，“啪”，一只黑甲虫从上方，砸向易横行的头顶。

它振翅，锋利的口器啃上了易横行的防护面罩。

这只甲虫像是触发了什么开关，周围骤然响起了一声又一声的尖锐长啸。

基因战士同样强化过五感。这样的声波已经近乎于声纳武器。

“连长！”有人发出一声哀嚎，“我的氧气罐被咬破了！”

数不清的黑色虫子，从洞穴的四壁、地上，钻了出来。

易横行的瞳孔骤然缩紧，厉声道：“不是都去融合了吗？为什么还有这么多？！”

回答他的，只有虫子的振翅声。

人类在等，虫子同样在等。

它们听从“王后”的吩咐，果然等来羊入虎口。

*

黑色的马在白茫茫的雪地上疾驰着。

这些机械马脚不沾地，行走起来速度极快，又悄无声息。

身穿黑甲的骑士坐在马背上，尖三角形状的头盔直指天穹。

骑士团一路向西，氛围肃穆、庄严。他们像极了传说里的“死神”。

在骑士团的行军路上，偶尔会碰见人类。

他们或许是拾荒者，或许是猎人，或许只是附近据点的住民。

但当看见这支军队时，所有人的反应无一例外。那就是颤抖着跪在地上，深深把头埋进雪堆里。

这并非出于尊敬，而是出于恐惧。

毕竟按照惯例，敢于直视东征军的人，会被天启骑士腰斩。

不能看，不能听，不能说。

可悲的弃民，当一只温顺的羔羊；你的同类抛弃你，但神会永远保佑你。

这就是地表最强横的一股势力。

有的人视其为毒瘤；也有人奉若神明，愿意献出一切。

黑色的马匹们在城门前。最前方的大骑士长微微抬起手，然后仰头，看向前方。

这是一个下午，很安静。

他们来自黑十字审判庭。戒律骑士军团下辖第三团。番号，光耀晨曦。

上一任军团长死在了外界。

但新一任团长，依旧叫沙利叶。

他大概是最名不副实的沙利叶。

因为那台名为“沙利叶”、本该成为神庭传家宝的生物机甲；随着沙利叶的死亡，永远损毁在了外界。

但没关系，只要完成这次任务，会有一笔丰厚的报酬，加上过去的积累，他就可以申请一台新的生物机甲了。

于是，这个沙利叶，说出了从出发以来的第一句话。

很冷静，也很冷酷：“列阵，冲锋，不留活口。”
chunks.englishText:
"Come to think of it, don't you find it strange?" Ying Rushi contacted Yi Hengxing. "Before we came, they said there were no maps, but not long after we arrived, they sent over a 3D map."

Yi Hengxing replied, "It just means the people at the base have been busy gathering information. They're doing their jobs well."

"But this kind of 3D map requires more than just time to produce; it requires specialized, classified technology."

In an era where information was scarce and populations were stagnant, maps were known as 'topographical charts' and were considered military secrets. Even now, the United Human Alliance's online maps were riddled with vast, empty gaps.

What was displayed was only what they *wanted* to be seen.

The technology for map-making wasn't particularly high-end, but the Alliance had always strictly prohibited its use by private citizens.

"The base might not be as simple as you think. A strange technological tree, mysterious technology for curing mycelial disease, and an artificial human so powerful it defies logic. However..."

Ying Rushi's voice suddenly cut out.

Yi Hengxing called out "Hello?" twice. Clearly, the distance between them had become too great, and the communication link had severed.

"I hate it when people leave their sentences hanging!"

The eight squads were closing in on the center of the insect nest.

Yi Hengxing raised his gun. The paths and walls had become somewhat soft; it seemed this part of the nest was newly constructed.

The passages were narrow—insects didn't need as much space as humans—and Yi Hengxing had to hunch over to move forward.

"Almost there, almost there."

In the darkness, he whispered to comfort himself and his teammates.

According to the map, they were very close to their destination. The ground was also littered with many hard insect shells.

These beetles, much like crabs, molted their shells.

Suddenly, a "snap" echoed as a black beetle dropped from above, slamming onto the top of Yi Hengxing's head.

It vibrated its wings, and its sharp mouthparts gnawed into Yi Hengxing's protective visor.

As if this beetle had triggered some kind of switch, sharp, long shrieks erupted one after another from the surroundings.

Genetic warriors had their five senses enhanced as well. Such sound waves were nearly equivalent to sonar weaponry.

"Company Commander!" someone wailed. "My oxygen tank has been bitten through!"

Countless black insects crawled out from the four walls and the floor of the cavern.

Yi Hengxing's pupils constricted sharply, and he barked, "Didn't they all go to fuse? Why are there still so many?!"

The only answer was the sound of buzzing wings.

Humans were waiting, and the insects were waiting too.

Obeying the "Queen's" command, they had indeed waited for the sheep to walk right into the tiger's den.

*

Black horses galloped across the vast, white, snowy plains.

These mechanical horses didn't touch the ground with their hooves; they moved with incredible speed and complete silence.

Knights clad in black armor sat atop the horses, their sharp, triangular helmets pointing toward the heavens.

The Order marched westward, the atmosphere solemn and grave. They looked exactly like the "Grim Reapers" of legend.

Along their march, the Order occasionally encountered humans.

They might be scavengers, hunters, or merely residents of nearby outposts.

But upon seeing this army, everyone's reaction was identical: they trembled as they knelt on the ground, burying their heads deep into the snowdrifts.

This was not out of respect, but out of fear.

After all, according to custom, anyone who dared to look directly at the Eastern Expeditionary Army would be cut in half by the Apocalypse Knights.

Do not look, do not listen, do not speak.

Pitiful outcasts, be a docile lamb; your own kind has abandoned you, but God will protect you forever.

This was the most formidable force on the surface.

Some viewed them as a malignant tumor; others worshipped them as gods, willing to offer everything they had.

The black horses halted before the city gates. The Great Knight Commander at the front raised a hand slightly, then tilted his head to look ahead.

It was an afternoon, very quiet.

They were from the Black Cross Inquisition, the Third Regiment under the Command of the Precept Knights. Their designation: Radiant Dawn.

The previous Regiment Commander had died in the outside world.

But the new commander was still named Sariel.

He was perhaps the least worthy of the name Sariel.

Because the bio-mecha named "Sariel," which should have been a sacred heirloom of the Divine Court, had been permanently destroyed in the outside world along with the death of the previous Sariel.

But it didn't matter. As long as this mission was completed, the generous reward, combined with his past accumulations, would allow him to apply for a new bio-mecha.

And so, this Sariel spoke the first words since their departure.

Calm and cold: "Form ranks. Charge. Leave no survivors."

chunks.chapterTitle: 第128章 这是我的战争（3） (Part 1)
chunks.chineseText:
第128章 这是我的战争（3）

因为这座塔的存在，基地获得了极其迅捷地发展。整座城区都围绕着这座塔建设，呈现出一个偌大的圆形。

北辰工作的研究所就在这座金属高塔的脚下。如今，这里也成为了整个战线的大后方。

研究所备用电源充足，防御设施完备，场地便捷，还有自己的通讯设备（本来是为了和李斯特联络的），再也没有比这里更合适当指挥处的地方了。

相南里坐在会议室内，大大小小的屏幕铺满了墙面。有些是实时监控，有些是基地的动态数据。

小卡车福音书尽心尽职地守在会议室外。

如果基地沦陷，它会谨遵Alpha的指令，把相南里装进冷冻舱，带着他逃亡到安全的地方。

屏幕里，已经出现了东征军的身影。

军团拢共不过三百人，然而在他们朝着基地冲刺时。竟然有股千军万马、一往无前的气势。

相南里不止一次直面过天启骑士。

他们那些诡异到违背物理学的神术和生物机械，一直让相南里耿耿于怀。

可惜之前没有从沙利叶的嘴里问出点什么。

沙利叶在基地这些日子，对能用科学解释的知识可谓倾囊相授；但对神庭的一切，总是讳莫如深。

“报！第一条防线崩溃！”耳麦里，传来小智械方田的疾呼。

事关重大，哪怕是第一次见到黄枫，相南里也没有怀疑过消息的真实性。而是立刻开始了准备。

——神庭的东征军迟早要来的。早一点准备又如何？基地赌不起。

所以，相南里已经接近两天没有睡觉了。

“第二分队准备。”

他出乎意料地冷静。

第一道防线位于山脚处，是一片铺设好的电网。

电网启动时能形成一片带磁力的场域，让范围内的金属物体动弹不得。

这些藏在雪里的卑鄙暗器曾让黑甲虫吃了不少苦头。

然而，同样是金属质地的铁马踏过高压电线，只是从鼻孔中喘出一阵硝烟味的粗气，它们的头颅同样金属覆面，红光在眼珠子的位置一闪而逝。

黑马轻而易举地踏过铁网，电光在半空中炸开。

天启骑士像是踩着雷霆而来，让人无端联想起北欧神话里的奥丁。

第二道防线，在半山腰。

通向主城区只修了一条盘山公路，但神庭骑士所到之处，皆是坦途。

他们几乎是笔直地往上冲。很快就从山脚到了半山腰。

半山位置有一处比较平的地势，原本是座民兵训练营，除了营地还有集市、炊事营和救护舱，但此时，里面的人员已经全部撤离，只剩一个空壳子。

模样奇怪的炮塔矗立在营地内。它像是一根烟囱。

炮塔扫描到了不在数据库的入侵者，操控炮塔的初级AI很快计量出数据——

一个个红色的激光点瞄准了神庭骑士，烟囱的脑袋长出了八条金属片，高速旋转起来，伸缩着发射出子弹，像是气势汹汹的大风车，外观朴实，还有点滑稽。

但没有人会小看它的杀伤力。

拳头大小的金属炮弹砸向入侵者。在接触到物体表面时轰然炸开，热滚滚的气浪掀起雪层，露出下面森然的黑色土壤。

炮弹锁定的不是前方的精锐骑士，而是后方的候补骑士。

他们没有资格使用生物机甲，尽管也能打，但整体比天启骑士脆弱很多，在行军过程中，负责开道、辎重等杂务。

有候补骑士躲闪不及，被连续几枚炮弹打中，骑着马的腿炸开一片血雾。

他谨遵长官的教诲，死死咬住了自己的唇，避免叫太大声、惊扰马匹，扰乱行军的队伍。

鲜血从被咬破的嘴角流下，这名小骑士用手捂住了自己的断腿，一言不发，像最坚毅、忠诚的战士。

“沙利叶大人，这些炮弹里掺了太空精金！”

怪不得能击穿天启骑士的防御。

临时工（候补骑士）一直不被有编制的（天启骑士）当人看，但是，他们毕竟是荣辱与共的同伴。

更何况，这些短促却频繁的进攻，显然已经阻碍到了骑士们的进攻。

沙利叶没有坐视不理。

他开口，冷冷点出八个名字：“去把炮台拆了，给你们十分钟。”

八匹机械马瞬间迎着弹雨起飞，冲向营地。

他们高举起盾牌，然而，弹雨也在此时停了下来。

事实上，因为时间仓促，哪怕日以继夜地加班，基地造出的特殊弹药也只够射这么两轮。

就连现在这种生死存亡时刻，主城区的精金锻造厂依然有工人和智械在负责冶炼。

但是两轮已经够了。炮塔争取到了宝贵时间，而且，分散了骑士团的兵力，还扰乱了队形。

尘土在瞬间飞扬，但在刺鼻的硝烟之下，是另一股更熟悉的气味。

位于队伍核心位置的沙利叶略微蹙起眉，随后，一声轻笑隐藏在了金属面罩之下：“有点意思。”

是畸变人的气味，闻起来是一股冷冻过后的腐肉味。

“在神庭骑士面前用畸变人吗？”

沙利叶的语气不自觉地带上了嘲讽。

神庭的高阶圣职者总是这样。有一种自然而然的轻蔑和非人感。

他们见过太多地狱，或者已经活在地狱。对自己和别人的痛苦都如此麻木。

潜伏在废墟的爬行者亮出了自己的獠牙，它们抖落身上的积雪，张开猩红的獠牙。怪物的大嘴遮天蔽日，甚至挡住了头顶不算亮的日光。

沙利叶张嘴，吐出一段短而急促的音节。

但爬行者只是停顿了片刻，接着，毫不犹豫地咬住了一名候补骑士的身体。

沙利叶怔然片刻。

神庭的神术竟然对这些爬行者无效！？

第一个扑进人堆里的这只爬行者十分巨大，充当先锋，正是平时最能吃的小红同志。

它有四条腿，四条胳膊，整体像是一只大蜥蜴，只是外观更加崎岖，通体暗红，有长尾。

爬行者的八只眼睛冰冷，三对长在正脸，一对长在侧脸；一排排倒钩似的牙。怪物发出了令人难耐又恐惧的咀嚼声。

在基地，人们叫他小红。但在外人眼中，它显然是头丧彪。

畸变人个体差异极大。

沙利叶的声音在骑士们的耳边响起，他甚至开始了现场教学：“所有不能直立行走的畸变人都叫爬行者；而站立行走、身材高大的是狂暴者；头部占据2/3、身材矮胖、咬合力惊人的是撕裂者。除此外，还有一种变异体，叫潜伏者。在自然状态下已经灭绝。只有部分实验室还在克隆和豢养。”

在这种关头，他依然漫不经心。

沙利叶：“弱点你们都在圣堂里学过，把它当成一次训练。畸变人并非不可战胜。在训练营，你们杀过不止一头，两人一组，背对背列阵。你们可是神庭的骑士，是地表最坚固的防线！”

扑过来的不止一只爬行者。还有肌肉发达的狂暴者。

它们体型不如爬行者大，顶多5米。但速度极快，肌肉发达，人送外号恐怖直立猿。
chunks.englishText:
Chapter 128: This Is My War (3)

Because of the existence of this tower, the base had achieved incredibly rapid development. The entire urban area was built around the tower, forming a massive circle.

The research institute where Beichen worked was located at the foot of this metal tower. Now, it had become the rear command center for the entire front line.

The institute had ample backup power, complete defensive facilities, convenient space, and its own communication equipment (originally intended for contacting Lister). There was no place more suitable to serve as a command post.

Xiang Nanli sat in the conference room, where screens of all sizes covered the walls. Some displayed real-time surveillance, while others showed the base's dynamic data.

The small truck, Gospel, stood faithfully on guard outside the conference room.

If the base were to fall, it would strictly follow the Alpha's instructions: place Xiang Nanli into a cryo-pod and flee with him to a safe location.

On the screens, the figures of the Eastern Expeditionary Army had already appeared.

The legion consisted of no more than three hundred people, yet as they charged toward the base, they possessed the momentum of a thousand armies, an unstoppable force.

Xiang Nanli had faced the Apocalypse Knights more than once.

Their strange divine arts and bio-mechanical technology, which defied the laws of physics, had always been a source of deep concern for him.

It was a pity he hadn't managed to extract any information from Sariel's mouth earlier.

During the days Sariel spent at the base, he had been willing to share everything that could be explained by science, but he was always tight-lipped about anything concerning the Divine Court.

"Report! The first line of defense has collapsed!" the urgent voice of the small machine-intelligence Fang Tian came through the earpiece.

The matter was of great importance. Even though it was his first time seeing Huang Feng, Xiang Nanli did not doubt the veracity of the news. He immediately began preparations.

—The Divine Court's Eastern Expeditionary Army was bound to come sooner or later. What harm was there in preparing early? The base couldn't afford to gamble.

Therefore, Xiang Nanli hadn't slept for nearly two days.

"Second squad, prepare."

He was unexpectedly calm.

The first line of defense was located at the foot of the mountain, consisting of a pre-laid electric grid.

When activated, the grid created a magnetic field that immobilized any metal objects within its range.

These treacherous hidden weapons buried in the snow had caused the black beetles a great deal of trouble.

However, the iron horses, also metallic in nature, trod over the high-voltage wires, merely exhaling a puff of gunpowder-scented air from their nostrils. Their heads were also covered in metal, and red lights flickered where their eyes should have been.

The black horses stepped over the iron net with ease, sparks of electricity exploding in mid-air.

The Apocalypse Knights came as if treading on thunder, making one think inexplicably of Odin from Norse mythology.

The second line of defense was halfway up the mountain.

Only one mountain road had been built leading to the main urban area, but wherever the Divine Court knights went, they made their own path.

They charged almost in a straight line. Soon, they had gone from the foot of the mountain to the halfway point.

At the halfway point, there was a relatively flat area that had originally been a militia training camp. Besides the camp, there were markets, a mess hall, and medical pods, but now, the personnel had all evacuated, leaving only an empty shell.

Strange-looking turrets stood within the camp. They resembled chimneys.

The turrets scanned the intruders who were not in their database, and the primary AI controlling the turrets quickly calculated the data—

Red laser dots aimed at the Divine Court knights. The chimney-like heads sprouted eight metal blades, spinning at high speed, extending and retracting to fire bullets like aggressive, spinning windmills. They looked simple, even a bit comical.

But no one would underestimate their lethality.

Fist-sized metal shells smashed into the invaders. Upon contact with the surface, they exploded, the scorching heat wave lifting the snow layer to reveal the grim black soil beneath.

The shells were not locking onto the elite knights in front, but the reserve knights in the rear.

They were not qualified to use bio-mecha; although they could fight, they were overall much more fragile than the Apocalypse Knights, responsible for clearing the way and handling logistics during the march.

A reserve knight couldn't dodge in time and was hit by several shells, his horse's legs exploding into a mist of blood.

He strictly followed his officer's teachings, biting his lip hard to avoid screaming too loudly, which would startle the horses and disrupt the marching formation.

Blood flowed from his bitten lip. This young knight covered his severed leg with his hand, saying nothing, like the most steadfast and loyal of warriors.

"Lord Sariel, these shells are mixed with space-grade refined gold!"

No wonder they could pierce the defenses of the Apocalypse Knights.

The "temps" (reserve knights) were never treated as human by the "tenured" (Apocalypse Knights), but they were, after all, companions who shared honor and disgrace.

Moreover, these short but frequent attacks were clearly hindering the knights' advance.

Sariel did not sit idly by.

He spoke, coldly naming eight people: "Go dismantle the turrets. You have ten minutes."

Eight mechanical horses instantly took flight into the hail of bullets, charging toward the camp.

They raised their shields high, but the hail of bullets stopped at that very moment.

In fact, because time was tight, even with round-the-clock overtime, the base had only produced enough special ammunition for these two volleys.

Even at this moment of life and death, workers and machine-intelligences were still responsible for smelting at the refined gold forge in the main city.

But two volleys were enough. The turrets had bought precious time, dispersed the knights' forces, and disrupted their formation.

Dust flew in an instant, but beneath the pungent smell of gunpowder was another, more familiar scent.

Sariel, positioned at the core of the formation, frowned slightly, and then a soft chuckle was hidden beneath his metal mask: "Interesting."

It was the scent of a mutant—it smelled like frozen rotting meat.

"Using mutants in front of the Divine Court knights?"

Sariel's tone carried an involuntary trace of mockery.

High-ranking holy officials of the Divine Court were always like this. They possessed a natural, inherent contempt and a sense of detachment from humanity.

They had seen too much hell, or were already living in it. They were so numb to their own pain and the pain of others.

The lurkers hiding in the ruins bared their fangs, shaking the accumulated snow off their bodies and opening their scarlet maws. The monster's giant mouth blotted out the sky, even blocking the dim sunlight from above.

Sariel opened his mouth and spat out a short, sharp syllable.

But the lurkers only paused for a moment before biting into the body of a reserve knight without hesitation.

Sariel was stunned for a moment.

The Divine Court's divine arts were actually ineffective against these lurkers!?

The first lurker to pounce into the crowd was huge, acting as the vanguard—it was none other than the one who ate the most, Comrade Little Red.

It had four legs and four arms, looking overall like a large lizard, only more rugged in appearance, dark red all over, with a long tail.

The lurker's eight eyes were cold, three pairs on its face and one pair on its sides; it had rows of hook-like teeth. The monster emitted a sound of chewing that was both unbearable and terrifying.

At the base, people called him Little Red. But in the eyes of outsiders, it was clearly a savage beast.

Individual differences among mutants were extreme.

Sariel's voice rang in the ears of the knights, and he even began a live lesson: "All mutants that cannot walk upright are called lurkers; those that walk upright and are tall are called berserkers; those with heads taking up two-thirds of their body, short and stout, with astonishing bite force, are called rippers. Besides these, there is another variant called a stalker. They are extinct in the natural state. Only a few laboratories still clone and keep them."

At such a juncture, he remained nonchalant.

Sariel continued: "You have all learned their weaknesses in the Temple. Treat this as a training exercise. Mutants are not invincible. In the training camp, you have killed more than one. Two to a group, line up back-to-back. You are knights of the Divine Court, the most solid line of defense on the surface!"

There was more than one lurker pouncing over. There were also muscular berserkers.

They were not as large as the lurkers, at most 5 meters tall. But they were extremely fast and heavily muscled; people nicknamed them "Terrifying Upright Apes."

chunks.chapterTitle: 第128章 这是我的战争（3） (Part 2)
chunks.chineseText:
狂暴者骤然跳进人堆里，也很聪明的知道避开前排的天启骑士，朝着后排的候补人员下手。

它们力量大到恐怖，能徒手扭断钢筋。只服用过基因改造药剂的人类，显然没有钢铁那么坚硬。

“骑士长——骑士长——”

被高举的小骑士面露惶恐。

营救大概是来不及了，弱肉强食，生存的法则就是如此残酷。

沙利叶看着他，比划了一个手势。这是神庭的祝福语，意思是，“神在等候你”。

通常是对将死之人的祝福与慰藉，用来减缓他们对死亡的恐惧。

信仰，到底是什么？

在那些暗无天日的岁月里，在那些充满着仇恨、饥饿和病痛的过去，信仰是人们最大的慰藉，是传道书送给地表遗民的礼物。

极端惊惧的小骑士，神色骤然平和下来。

下一秒，抓住他的大手开始收拢，所有声音被淹没在恐怖的挤压中。

狂暴者的手掌收拢后，又松开。把残渣丢在了地上。

像是一团烂熟的果子。

沙利叶有些生气了。

一击得手后，这些畸变人并不恋战，反而迅速分散着撤离。背后显然有人在指挥。

是的，沙利叶承认，自己或许有些小看基地了——在资料上，它只是一个新生的地表据点，还没有活过死亡率百分之九十五的前三年。至于被攻占的永恒市？那多半是人联的阴谋。没看到后面人联还和基地合作研发菌丝病抑制剂了吗？

乌列尔，也就是辛追，向他保证过，姑苏城不会派重兵来协助基地。只有一支不上不下的支援部队。人数不过百余人。

沙利叶就这么信心满满地上路了。甚至想好了回去后要买的生物机甲的颜色。（尽管外观都是黑色，但机甲内部能购买自己喜欢的内饰，神庭认为这有利于驾驶者的身心健康）

他可是半只脚踏入领主级的天启骑士！

沙利叶拔出了身后的长刀。胯下的黑马载着他升到半空中，地上，骑士们绕成一个圆形，守卫在他身边。

沙利叶冷漠的目光锁定着四面八方的畸变人。

他握紧手中的刀，像挥舞鞭子一样，甩出一刀。

空气中出现一扇巨大的血色弧线，像弯月。人联的武器设计师会试图用激光切割技术去解释它，但对于地表来说，这就是神庭的神术。

弧线正中一头狂暴者的后背，散发出一股蛋白质熟过头的焦味儿。

狂暴者仍然在往前跑着，几秒后，它哀鸣了一声，身体竟然直接从中断裂！

沙利叶不再去看它——那畜生必死。他不断甩动手里的弯刀，血色的弯月刚出现时，只有一个细细的弧度，但抵达地面时，已经是数米长的镰刀，像是从天而降的神罚，无情地割掉地表茂密的杂草。

相南里从未小看神庭。

但人实在难以想象自己没有见过的东西，东征军的强悍还是远超他的预料。

他甚至觉得后背有些发凉。

但后背发凉的不止相南里一人。

沙利叶的后背也骤然一冷，这大概是无数次生死作战后练出来的野性直觉。

潜伏在地上的以西结一跃而起。

很难想象，他是如何悄无声息地穿越两百多人的包围圈，来到沙利叶下方的。而他甚至没有惊动任何人。

除非，他就是沙利叶口中，早就物种灭绝的“潜伏者”。

空气里响起破空的音浪，以西结扑向沙利叶的后背，他不再维持人形，而是张开了尖锐的喙！

的确像是鸟喙，带着一点阴冷的弯钩。

以西结的目标是沙利叶的脖颈。

无论是人体还是机甲，这里都是极其脆弱的部位。

沙利叶松开手里的长刀，用双手，挡住了自己的脖子。坚硬的喙刺穿覆盖着金属的表壳，在手掌心扎出一个血洞。

沉重的撞击让沙利叶几乎跌下马背。他反手，就想抓住以西结的身体，嘴里发出一阵毫无意义的音节。

也不知道是在念咒还是辱骂。

以西结很清楚，他不是神庭骑士的对手。

以西结像个高爆发低耐力的脆皮刺客，不能打持久战。

但短短半分钟，足够受伤的畸变人跑远。

以西结一击得手。下一秒，他做出了和其他畸变人一样的选择，撤离。

畸变人们做到这份上，已经属于友情价了。

他可没有让整个族群为幸存者基地陪葬的打算。

以西结是潜伏者，完全没有人能用肉眼或者仪器捕捉到他的影子，他甚至比其他同伴先一步回到了“营地”。

黑石山是这片山峰的主峰，营地位于副峰。隔着一个山头，人类和畸变人相安无事。

每天凌晨，都有卡车拉着一车研究所培育出来的新鲜食物，来到畸变人的营地投喂。免得它们饿到吃人或者饿到互啃。

平时，送货员基本不会露面，食物往地上一倒，倒完就跑，像是怕自己被吃掉一样。

人类对畸变人的恐惧是刻在基因里的。

但这次，以西结回到家，却发现山洞里有两个人。

很矮。

一米五的安德鲁和一米四五的北辰。

他能戳穿沙利叶脖子的喙，也能轻而易举地扎死两台机械改造人。

不太好的记忆在以西结的脑海里一闪而出，他控制不住地龇牙咧嘴，炸鳞。

人类的脸上浮现出野兽一样的鳞片。漆黑的眼眸里，深红色的瞳仁几乎成一条竖线。这是即将发起进攻的标志。

安德鲁吓得几乎要昏厥，怯生生地躲在了北辰身后。

北辰挠了挠自己的金属头：“相南里说，你们可能会受伤。他还说安德鲁是医生，跟着沙利叶学过一段时间，会治疗畸变人。让他来帮一下忙。我是自己请缨的，我一直对畸变人有些好奇。”

他甚至不记得自己就是畸变人最初的研发者。

在七百年前，一个叫漠北的科学家，在地底的实验室，打开了名为“畸变人”的潘多拉魔盒。

基因链轻轻一变，留下畸变人痛苦一生。

可是，“科技又有什么错呢？你凭什么审判我的灵魂？”那一年，漠北问。

战斗完的畸变人陆陆续续回来了。

有些掉毛，有些断尾，有些瞎了眼睛。

畸变人们无精打采的，连饭都不怎么吃了。一些是没胃口，一些是吃太多了……嗯，肚子里的神庭骑士也是需要消化的。

这些伤势不算致命，畸变人能靠自身强大的新陈代谢能力，硬生生熬过去。

就像是过去很多年那样。

但是感受并不会骗人；断了尾巴的小红蜷缩在地上，用舌头舔着自己的断尾，发出一阵“嘤嘤”的哭声。他最喜欢自己的长尾巴，其他小畸变人也很喜欢，能当滑梯玩。

爬行者大概是在喊疼。

以西结沉默片刻：“好吧。你们治。但我全程都要看着。每次开刀都需要经过我的同意。”

北辰温顺地点头：“知道了。”
chunks.englishText:
The berserkers suddenly leaped into the crowd, cleverly avoiding the Apocalypse Knights in the front row and targeting the reserve personnel in the back.

Their strength was terrifying; they could twist steel bars with their bare hands. Humans who had only taken genetic modification serums were clearly not as hard as steel.

"Knight Commander—Knight Commander—"

The young knight held high in the air looked terrified.

A rescue was likely too late. Survival of the fittest—the law of survival was just that cruel.

Sariel looked at him and made a gesture. This was a blessing of the Divine Court, meaning, "God is waiting for you."

It was usually a blessing and comfort for the dying, used to alleviate their fear of death.

What, in the end, was faith?

In those dark, sunless years, in that past filled with hatred, hunger, and pain, faith was people's greatest comfort, a gift from the scriptures to the outcasts of the surface.

The extremely terrified young knight's expression suddenly calmed down.

The next second, the giant hand gripping him began to close, and all sound was drowned out in the horrific crushing.

After the berserker's palm closed, it opened again, dropping the remains on the ground.

Like a piece of overripe fruit.

Sariel was a little angry.

After a successful strike, these mutants didn't linger; instead, they dispersed and retreated rapidly. Clearly, someone was commanding them from behind.

Yes, Sariel admitted that he might have underestimated the base—in the files, it was just a nascent surface outpost that hadn't survived the first three years, which had a ninety-five percent mortality rate. As for the captured Eternal City? That was mostly a conspiracy of the United Human Alliance. Didn't you see the Alliance later cooperating with the base to develop a mycelial disease inhibitor?

Uriel, also known as Xin Zhui, had assured him that Gusu City would not send heavy troops to assist the base. There was only a mediocre support force. The number of people was no more than a hundred.

Sariel had set off with such confidence. He had even decided on the color of the bio-mecha he would buy when he returned. (Although the exterior was always black, one could purchase one's favorite interior for the mecha; the Divine Court believed this was beneficial to the pilot's physical and mental health.)

He was an Apocalypse Knight with one foot already stepping into the Lord-level!

Sariel drew the long blade from his back. The black horse beneath him rose into mid-air. On the ground, the knights formed a circle, guarding him.

Sariel's cold gaze locked onto the mutants coming from all directions.

He gripped the blade in his hand and swung it like a whip.

A massive blood-colored arc appeared in the air, like a crescent moon. Weapon designers of the Alliance would try to explain it with laser-cutting technology, but for the surface, this was a divine art of the Divine Court.

The arc struck the back of a berserker, emitting the smell of overcooked protein.

The berserker kept running, but a few seconds later, it let out a mournful cry, and its body snapped clean in half!

Sariel stopped looking at it—that beast was dead for sure. He swung the curved blade in his hand repeatedly. When the blood-colored crescent first appeared, it was only a thin arc, but by the time it reached the ground, it was a scythe several meters long, like divine punishment descending from the heavens, mercilessly cutting down the dense weeds of the surface.

Xiang Nanli had never underestimated the Divine Court.

But it was truly difficult for people to imagine things they had never seen; the ferocity of the Eastern Expeditionary Army still far exceeded his expectations.

He even felt a chill down his spine.

But Xiang Nanli wasn't the only one feeling a chill.

Sariel's back also suddenly turned cold; this was likely a wild intuition honed through countless life-and-death battles.

Ezekiel, who had been lurking on the ground, leaped up.

It was hard to imagine how he had silently crossed the encirclement of over two hundred people to reach the space beneath Sariel. And he hadn't alerted anyone.

Unless he was the "stalker" Sariel had mentioned, a species already extinct.

A sonic boom of air being torn apart rang out. Ezekiel pounced on Sariel's back, no longer maintaining a human form, but opening his sharp beak!

It did indeed look like a bird's beak, with a cold, hooked tip.

Ezekiel's target was Sariel's neck.

Whether it was a human body or a mecha, this was an extremely vulnerable part.

Sariel let go of the long blade in his hand and used both hands to block his neck. The hard beak pierced through the metal-covered shell, stabbing a bloody hole in the palm of his hand.

The heavy impact made Sariel almost fall off his horse. He reached back, trying to grab Ezekiel's body, his mouth emitting a series of meaningless syllables.

It was unclear whether he was chanting a spell or hurling insults.

Ezekiel knew very well that he was no match for a Divine Court knight.

Ezekiel was like a high-burst, low-durability glass-cannon assassin; he couldn't fight a war of attrition.

But half a minute was enough for the injured mutants to run far away.

Ezekiel had succeeded in his strike. The next second, he made the same choice as the other mutants: retreat.

For the mutants to do this much, it was already a "friendship price."

He had no intention of letting his entire tribe be buried with the survivor base.

Ezekiel was a stalker; absolutely no one could capture his shadow with the naked eye or instruments. He even returned to the "camp" a step ahead of his other companions.

Black Stone Mountain was the main peak of this mountain range, and the camp was located on a secondary peak. Separated by a mountain, humans and mutants lived in peace.

Every dawn, a truck would bring a load of fresh food cultivated by the research institute to feed the mutants, preventing them from starving to the point of eating humans or each other.

Usually, the delivery person would barely show their face; they would dump the food on the ground and run, as if afraid of being eaten themselves.

Human fear of mutants was etched into their genes.

But this time, when Ezekiel returned home, he found two people in the cave.

Very short.

The 1.5-meter-tall Andrew and the 1.45-meter-tall Beichen.

The beak he used to pierce Sariel's neck could also easily stab two mechanical cyborgs to death.

Unpleasant memories flashed through Ezekiel's mind, and he couldn't help but bare his fangs and bristle his scales.

Beast-like scales appeared on the human's face. In his pitch-black eyes, the deep red pupils were almost vertical lines. This was a sign that he was about to attack.

Andrew was so scared he almost fainted, timidly hiding behind Beichen.

Beichen scratched his metal head: "Xiang Nanli said you might be injured. He also said Andrew is a doctor who studied under Sariel for a while and knows how to treat mutants. He asked him to come and help. I volunteered myself; I've always been a bit curious about mutants."

He didn't even remember that he was the original developer of the mutants.

Seven hundred years ago, a scientist named Mobei opened Pandora's box called "mutants" in an underground laboratory.

A slight change in the genetic chain left mutants to suffer for a lifetime.

However, "What is wrong with technology? By what right do you judge my soul?" Mobei had asked that year.

The mutants who had finished fighting returned one after another.

Some were shedding fur, some had broken tails, some were blinded.

The mutants were listless, not even eating much. Some had no appetite, while others had eaten too much... well, the Divine Court knights in their bellies also needed to be digested.

These injuries were not fatal; the mutants could rely on their own powerful metabolic capabilities to tough it out.

Just like they had for many years in the past.

But feelings wouldn't lie; Little Red, with his broken tail, curled up on the ground, licking his severed tail with his tongue, emitting a "whimper" of crying. He loved his long tail the most, and the other little mutants loved it too; they could use it as a slide.

The lurker was probably crying in pain.

Ezekiel was silent for a moment: "Fine. You can treat them. But I will watch the whole time. Every surgery needs my approval."

Beichen nodded meekly: "Understood."

chunks.chapterTitle: 第129章 这是我的战争（4） (Part 1)
chunks.chineseText:
第129章 这是我的战争（4）

他的血应该是枫糖味。有时候，他会割开自己的皮肤，挤出一些血液，作为给下属的赏赐。

这是神庭的传统，早些年也许代表“歃血为盟”“同生共死”等等美好的意愿，但现在嘛，高一级的天启骑士确实对低级的天启骑士有补益作用。

负责摧毁炮台的骑士们回到队伍内，状态有些狼狈，好在没有人员伤亡。

营地内埋了20公斤TNT，在骑士们踏进营地的瞬间引爆。

那台不知型号但造价不菲的炮台轰然倒塌，把一匹机械马砸成了碎渣。

一切都在相南里的计划内，甚至时间都掐得很准。

可惜，受伤和减员并没有让东征军停下脚步。

沙利叶脖子上的血洞还在，只是伤口处被烫熟了，所以不再流血。

东征军在半路减员16人。5名天启骑士，11名候补。

尸体被就地掩埋，其实有些浪费。但神庭已经不是几百年前那个穷到把队友当军粮的组织了。

沙利叶为这些人唱了魂归神国的赞歌。

空下来的生物机甲，沙利叶让其他的候补骑士顶上。

这只军团顿时又是满配了。

沙利叶说：“这只是遵循神指引时的短暂插曲，是神在考验我们的意志。”

“不过，这次任务显然有我们不了解的异常之处。西塔，你先去侦查。”

“是。”一名看上去和别的铁坨子没有任何差别的骑士回答。

下一秒，他后背裂开，一只只红眼睛的小麻雀从血淋漓的缝隙处钻了出来。

这也是神庭的神术。

西塔用自己的血肉饲养这些小麻雀，必要时，这些小麻雀也能成为他的眼睛。

基地的监控或许能扫描到没有标识编码的无人机，但未必会关注这种随处可见的雀鸟。

西塔的雀鸟飞到山顶，在半空中自上而下地俯瞰着这座城市。

下午四点，天色已经快黑透了。整个城区像是一座死城，除了工厂的方位还在冒烟，其余地方看不见一点人气。

不算大的街区寂静异常。

一方面，是这里人本来就不多；另一方面，则是埋伏。

居民楼里，基地的战士们蜷缩在窗边、墙角，像绷紧的弓箭，蓄势待发。

路上到处都有地雷、陷阱……尽管在西塔眼里，这些玩意杀伤力有限，实在不足以对天启骑士造成伤害。

粗略地扫描一眼，没有发现大型武器；甚至连一辆像样的武装坦克都没有。

西塔还标记好了基地的粮仓、武器库。这两个地方需要优先占领。

他回过神，开口：“我认为，半山部分的进攻，已经消耗了基地绝大部分军火。”

沙利叶：“这是好消息，但我们也不能轻敌。总之，按流程来吧。”

这是真的。

基地现在不缺物资，也不缺技术。但缺乏高素质工人和时间。

秦九章带来的智械倒是能当八级工，可它们只有四个人。

小智械们不眠不休地工作，也只是小产量地输出提纯后的精金。

这批物资一部分被送往永恒市军工厂，一部分直接送到相南里的工作室。

相南里也没休息过。他把宝贵原材料加工成可以使用的军火、武器装置，一个人起码干了五六个不同工种高级技工的活。

可是，也只够这样了。

机械炮台、炸药和畸变人盟友，暂缓了东征军汹涌的攻势，还让军团减员了百分之五，这是了不起的成就，但从整体看，结果并没有什么改变。

他们还是要陷阵、先登、斩将再破城。

目前，主城区已经拿不出更强悍的热武器装置了。

所以……

相南里启动了北辰曾经提出的“超级母体计划”。

城内的黑丝粉菌在药剂的刺激下，变得前所未有的活跃。

菌丝母体的控制器就在相南里的手边，等东征军进入城区后，他会利用这台设备，操控母体，指挥其余子株发起进攻。

北辰曾经警告过相南里，不要试图长时间、大范围的控制菌群；因为会对大脑造成不可逆的损伤，比如过敏性癫痫，幻视幻听之类的。

但活着才有希望，相南里已经没时间思考代价了。

……

……

基地大食堂。

现在不是饭点，因此，偌大的餐厅只有两个客人。

具体来说，是半个人类和一台智械。

加百列对这里唯一的感受是萧条，餐厅甚至没有开灯。

好在还有厨子上班。人手不足，她也兼任了服务员的工作。

加百列还发现，厨师是残疾人。没钱装机械义体，因此杵着拐杖端上的菜。

“轰隆”，天上响起一阵雷声。也许快下雨了。

黄枫心不在焉地看着窗外的景色，显然心里有事。

它的同事都在前线，领导去了地底，大家似乎都有重要的事干，而它，一台轻工型的战斗机器人，却只能守在加百列的身边。

黄枫觉得，自己可能该清理一下缓存垃圾了，要不然为什么会如此烦闷：“你的赎金呢？再不交钱，我可要撕票了。教宗真的会花钱来赎你？”

加百列浅笑着，用筷子戳了一下面前的炒蘑菇：“我也曾是神庭的圣子，只是没有成为教宗。现在的教宗，按辈分，算是我没有血缘关系的哥哥。在圣堂里，我们以兄弟姐妹相称。哪怕我不是‘加百列’，他也会花钱赎我的。”

“你们神庭一届有几个圣子？”

“并没有定额。只要教宗承认，都可以是圣子。”加百列的眼睛微微眯起，“这其实是种政治手段。在神庭扩张期间，吞并了许多地表的大型据点。为了安抚那些被镇杀的残余势力，往往会给曾经首领的后代颁发一个圣子的头衔。”

“而且，你知道吗，圣职者其实……”

更好吃。

也是必备的祭品。

残存的理智让加百列适时地闭嘴。然而舌尖依然有股被火焰灼烧后的疼痛。

这是神庭的机密。不可能告诉外人。

可是，黄枫又不是人。只是一台不怎么聪明的智械。它根本意识不到这算情报，只会胡乱地塞进后台的数据库，等着时间把回忆消磁成电子垃圾。

黄枫：“懂了。就像是人联当初给Alpha许诺，只要他投降，就让他进人联的什么主席团。”

加百列可有可无地笑了一下。他还想说什么，却突然抬头，看向了电线杆上站着的麻雀。

下雨了。

小麻雀的红眼睛并不明显，它被雨水打得湿漉漉的，偶尔扭动一下脖子。

黄枫说：“我看到神庭的骑士了。”

它的双眼有光成像系统，和人类的眼睛作用一样。但它毕竟不是人类。

黄枫还能通过其他渠道看到东西，譬如卫星信号（电磁波）、声呐；但人类大概想象不出那是什么感觉。

它看见，东征军抵达了城门。

平时，入口处会设置关卡，用于车辆的安检。

城内，所剩无几的平民都按照指令，躲进了防空洞。那里曾经是福音书打造的粮仓，很安全。
chunks.englishText:
Chapter 129: This Is My War (4)

His blood should taste like maple syrup. Sometimes, he would slice open his own skin and squeeze out a few drops of blood as a reward for his subordinates.

This was a tradition of the Divine Court. In earlier years, it might have represented noble intentions like "swearing an oath in blood" or "living and dying together," but now, the higher-ranking Apocalypse Knights truly provided nourishment to the lower-ranking ones.

The knights responsible for destroying the artillery returned to the ranks, looking somewhat disheveled, though fortunately, there were no casualties.

Twenty kilograms of TNT had been buried in the camp, detonated the moment the knights stepped inside.

That artillery piece—of an unknown model but high cost—had collapsed, crushing a mechanical horse into smithereens.

Everything was within Xiang Nanli’s plan; even the timing had been calculated with precision.

Unfortunately, the injuries and attrition did not stop the Eastern Expeditionary Army in its tracks.

The blood hole in Sariel’s neck remained, but the wound had been cauterized, so it no longer bled.

The Eastern Expeditionary Army had lost 16 men along the way: 5 Apocalypse Knights and 11 candidates.

The corpses were buried on the spot—a bit of a waste, truthfully. But the Divine Court was no longer the organization it had been hundreds of years ago, so poor that it had to treat teammates as military rations.

Sariel sang a hymn for the souls of the fallen to return to the Divine Kingdom.

Sariel ordered other candidate knights to take over the now-vacant bio-mechs.

The legion was back to full strength in an instant.

Sariel said, "This is merely a brief interlude while following the Divine’s guidance; it is the Divine testing our resolve."

"However, this mission clearly contains anomalies we do not yet understand. Xita, you go and scout ahead."

"Yes." A knight who looked no different from any other iron-clad shell replied.

The next second, his back split open, and small sparrows with red eyes crawled out from the bloody fissure.

This, too, was a Divine Art of the Divine Court.

Xita fed these sparrows with his own flesh and blood; when necessary, these sparrows could become his eyes.

The base's surveillance might scan for drones without identification codes, but it might not pay attention to such common birds.

Xita’s sparrows flew to the mountain peak, looking down at the city from high above.

At four in the afternoon, the sky was nearly pitch black. The entire urban area was like a dead city; aside from smoke rising from the direction of the factories, not a trace of human life could be seen elsewhere.

The small district was eerily silent.

On one hand, there were few people left here; on the other, it was an ambush.

Inside the residential buildings, the base’s soldiers huddled by windows and corners, like taut bowstrings, ready to strike.

The roads were filled with landmines and traps... though in Xita’s eyes, these things had limited lethality and were truly insufficient to harm an Apocalypse Knight.

A rough scan revealed no large-scale weaponry; there wasn't even a decent armed tank.

Xita also marked the base’s granary and armory. These two locations needed to be prioritized for occupation.

He regained his focus and spoke: "I believe the offensive on the mountainside has already consumed the vast majority of the base's munitions."

Sariel: "That is good news, but we must not underestimate the enemy. Regardless, follow the procedure."

This was true.

The base was not lacking in supplies or technology, but it lacked high-quality workers and time.

The intelligent machines brought by Qin Jiuzhang could act as eighth-grade technicians, but there were only four of them.

The little machines worked without sleep or rest, yet they only produced a small yield of refined Adamantine.

Part of these supplies was sent to the Eternal City arsenal, and part was sent directly to Xiang Nanli’s studio.

Xiang Nanli had not rested either. He processed precious raw materials into usable munitions and weapon devices, doing the work of at least five or six high-level technicians from different fields all by himself.

But that was all he could do.

The mechanical artillery, explosives, and mutant allies had slowed the surging offensive of the Eastern Expeditionary Army and reduced the legion's numbers by five percent—a remarkable achievement, but looking at the big picture, the result remained unchanged.

They still had to break through the lines, storm the gates, slay the generals, and then conquer the city.

Currently, the main urban area could not produce any more powerful thermal weapon devices.

So...

Xiang Nanli activated the "Super Matrix Project" once proposed by Beichen.

Stimulated by reagents, the Black Silk Powder Fungus within the city became unprecedentedly active.

The controller for the fungal matrix was right at Xiang Nanli’s side. Once the Eastern Expeditionary Army entered the city, he would use this device to manipulate the matrix and command the remaining sub-strains to launch an attack.

Beichen had once warned Xiang Nanli not to attempt long-term, large-scale control of the fungal colonies, as it would cause irreversible damage to the brain, such as allergic epilepsy, visual and auditory hallucinations, and the like.

But there was only hope if one stayed alive; Xiang Nanli no longer had time to consider the cost.

...

...

The base’s main cafeteria.

It was not mealtime, so there were only two guests in the massive dining hall.

To be precise, half a human and one intelligent machine.

Gabriel’s only impression of this place was desolation; the cafeteria didn't even have the lights on.

Fortunately, there was still a cook on duty. Being short-handed, she also doubled as a waitress.

Gabriel also discovered that the cook was disabled. Lacking the money for mechanical prosthetics, she served the dishes while leaning on a crutch.

"Boom," a roll of thunder sounded in the sky. Perhaps it was about to rain.

Huang Feng looked at the scenery outside the window, distracted, clearly preoccupied with something.

Its colleagues were all on the front lines, its leader had gone underground, and everyone seemed to have important things to do. Yet it, a light-duty combat robot, could only guard Gabriel’s side.

Huang Feng felt that it might need to clear its cache; otherwise, why would it feel so stifled? "Where is your ransom? If you don't pay up soon, I’m going to kill the hostage. Will the Pope really spend money to redeem you?"

Gabriel smiled faintly, poking at the stir-fried mushrooms in front of him with his chopsticks: "I was once a Saint Son of the Divine Court, just not the Pope. The current Pope, by seniority, is my brother by title, not by blood. In the Sanctuary, we address each other as brothers and sisters. Even if I weren't 'Gabriel,' he would still pay to redeem me."

"How many Saint Sons does your Divine Court have in one generation?"

"There is no fixed quota. As long as the Pope acknowledges it, anyone can be a Saint Son." Gabriel’s eyes narrowed slightly. "This is actually a political tool. During the expansion of the Divine Court, many large surface strongholds were annexed. To appease the remnants of the forces that were suppressed, they often bestowed the title of Saint Son upon the descendants of the former leaders."

"And, do you know, the clergy are actually..."

Better to eat.

And also essential sacrificial offerings.

Lingering reason made Gabriel shut his mouth at the right time. However, there was still a burning pain on the tip of his tongue, as if scorched by flames.

This was a secret of the Divine Court. It was impossible to tell an outsider.

However, Huang Feng was not a human. It was just a not-very-smart intelligent machine. It didn't realize this was intelligence at all; it would just toss it randomly into its backend database, waiting for time to demagnetize the memory into electronic trash.

Huang Feng: "Understood. It’s like when the Human Alliance promised Alpha that if he surrendered, they would let him join some Human Alliance presidium."

Gabriel laughed dismissively. He wanted to say something else, but suddenly looked up at the sparrow standing on the telephone pole.

It was raining.

The little sparrow’s red eyes were not obvious; it was soaked by the rain, occasionally twisting its neck.

Huang Feng said: "I see the Divine Court’s knights."

Its eyes had optical imaging systems, functioning just like human eyes. But it was not human, after all.

Huang Feng could also see things through other channels, such as satellite signals (electromagnetic waves) and sonar; but humans probably couldn't imagine what that felt like.

It saw that the Eastern Expeditionary Army had arrived at the city gate.

Normally, checkpoints would be set up at the entrance for vehicle security checks.

Inside the city, the few remaining civilians had followed instructions and hidden in the air-raid shelters. That place had once been a granary built by the Gospel, and it was very safe.

chunks.chapterTitle: 第129章 这是我的战争（4） (Part 2)
chunks.chineseText:
双方第一个照面，东征军就轰碎了整个城门。三名天启骑士扛起了一个火箭筒似的炮台。

几公里外的爆炸声让地面一阵战栗。

这下餐厅里真没有电了。头顶的电灯摇晃着，摔到地上，碎成一片片的。

加百列坐在椅子上，端着甜奶茶，像是单独在一个图层，杯里的奶都没晃悠一下。

在黄枫第十三次看向窗外时，加百列说：“你如果想去帮忙，就去吧。我不会逃跑的。”

“那好吧。”黄枫从善如流地站了起来，“我就去看看。你留在这里，不要走动。半个小时后我就回来。”

天启骑士已经从城门位置来到了外城区。

黑色的铁马走到哪，地面就塌到哪，火焰就烧到哪。不断有守卫军在高温里融化。

他们像是从地狱来的恶魔，偏偏披着神圣的外衣。

“黄枫。”在它转身的瞬间，加百列叫住了它，“沙利叶的尸体如果在，可以试着用神经传感线连接。”

虽然“沙利叶”是神庭内部的高阶生物机甲，但之前就损坏过了，大概用一次就会报废吧。

黄枫想说，神经传感线不是人类用来连接机械装置的吗？

但它还是点头，表示自己记住了。

黄枫一跃而起，像是真的长出翅膀一样，飞向半空。

它踩在建筑物的房檐上，跳跃着向前，很快就消失在加百列的视野中。

*

神庭骑士在基地主城内畅通无阻，所向披靡。

地表的火焰不断向内燃烧着。吞噬着这里的一切，建筑、道路、人。

有勇敢的战士枉顾耳麦里撤回回防的指令，从埋伏点跳了出来，身上绑着炸药，挡在路中央。

他原本以为自己能说出一些漂亮话的，然而直面神庭骑士的时候，却只能发出意义不明的叫声，用来掩饰内心的恐惧。

他冲向骑士团，炸弹在半路爆开。这个小战士血肉横飞，路面都炸出一个坑洞。

可惜，身穿重甲的骑士依旧如山一样，不可撼动。

爆炸的余波只是让他们身上的盔甲跟着颤了一会。

琐碎的血沫溅在了沙利叶被金属覆盖的脸上。

“阴沟里的老鼠。”他的语气如此不屑，“城里没什么人，躲到哪儿了？”

躲到哪都会是一个下场。

敌人绝望的哀嚎，是战场上最动人的破阵乐。

骑士们继续前进，脚下坚硬的柏油路变成了柔软的黑土。

黑马进行机械改造、生物改造后的产物，在一定程度上保留了动物的灵性。

它们变得躁动不安起来，在主人的驱使下，不怎么情愿地踏上了面前的泥土，从鼻孔里喷出一阵粗气。

一公里内没有检测到任何生物信息。

逐渐降低的温度、废墟燃烧后的粉尘，让黑夜里出现一片朦胧的雾气。几乎到了伸手不见五指的程度。

空气里飘来潮湿阴冷的味道，一股发霉的气味。不怎么好闻。

沙利叶知道有危险，但有些事并不是遇到危险就能撤退的。

他高声道：“加快速度，马上就是基地的地热发电厂了，这是整个基地的工业心脏。”

“啊——”

背后传来一阵短而急促的呼声。

沙利叶扭头，只见菌类茂密的根系被黑土地吐了出来，在瞬间拔地三尺高，菌丝连人带马，裹住整个骑士，像是一个球似的。

菌球藏回地下，然而地表，它出现过的地方，却长出了一片黑红相间的小蘑菇。

外观很眼熟。在最近一两年的新闻报告里，经常看见。

沙利叶握紧缰绳，眉头死死蹙起：“……姑苏城的黑丝粉菌？”
chunks.englishText:
At the first encounter, the Eastern Expeditionary Army blasted the entire city gate to pieces. Three Apocalypse Knights hoisted a rocket-launcher-like artillery piece.

The sound of the explosion from several kilometers away made the ground tremble.

Now, there was truly no electricity in the cafeteria. The overhead lights swayed, fell to the ground, and shattered into pieces.

Gabriel sat in his chair, holding his sweet milk tea, as if he were on a separate layer; the milk in his cup didn't even ripple.

When Huang Feng looked out the window for the thirteenth time, Gabriel said: "If you want to go help, go ahead. I won't run away."

"Alright then." Huang Feng stood up obligingly. "I’ll go take a look. You stay here and don't move around. I’ll be back in half an hour."

The Apocalypse Knights had already moved from the city gate to the outer city.

Wherever the black iron horses walked, the ground collapsed, and flames burned. Guards were constantly melting in the high heat.

They were like demons from hell, yet they wore holy cloaks.

"Huang Feng." The moment it turned, Gabriel called out to it, "If Sariel’s corpse is still there, you can try connecting it with neural sensor lines."

Although "Sariel" was a high-level bio-mech within the Divine Court, it had been damaged before; it would probably be scrapped after one more use.

Huang Feng wanted to say, aren't neural sensor lines used by humans to connect to mechanical devices?

But it still nodded, indicating it had remembered.

Huang Feng leaped up, as if it had truly grown wings, and flew into mid-air.

It stepped on the eaves of buildings, jumping forward, and soon disappeared from Gabriel’s field of vision.

*

The Divine Court knights were unobstructed and invincible within the base’s main city.

The flames on the surface burned inward, devouring everything here: buildings, roads, people.

Brave soldiers ignored the orders in their headsets to retreat and defend, jumping out from ambush points with explosives strapped to their bodies, blocking the middle of the road.

He had originally thought he could say something heroic, but when facing the Divine Court knights, he could only let out unintelligible cries to mask the fear in his heart.

He charged at the knight legion, and the bomb exploded halfway. The little soldier was blown to pieces, and a crater was blasted into the road.

Unfortunately, the knights in heavy armor remained as immovable as mountains.

The aftermath of the explosion only made their armor tremble for a moment.

Splatters of blood landed on Sariel’s metal-covered face.

"Rats in the gutter." His tone was filled with disdain. "There’s no one in the city; where have they hidden?"

No matter where they hid, the outcome would be the same.

The desperate wails of the enemy were the most moving music for breaking a formation on the battlefield.

The knights continued to advance, and the hard asphalt under their feet turned into soft black soil.

The black horses, products of mechanical and biological modification, retained a degree of animal instinct.

They became restless, and under their masters' urging, they stepped onto the soil ahead with reluctance, snorting roughly from their nostrils.

No biological information was detected within one kilometer.

The gradually dropping temperature and the dust from the burning ruins created a hazy fog in the night, to the point where one could barely see their own hand.

A damp, cold, and musty smell wafted through the air. It was not pleasant.

Sariel knew there was danger, but some things could not be retreated from just because one encountered danger.

He shouted: "Speed up! We are almost at the base’s geothermal power plant; this is the industrial heart of the entire base."

"Ah—"

A short, sharp cry came from behind.

Sariel turned his head, only to see the dense roots of fungi being spat out by the black soil, rising three feet high in an instant. The mycelium wrapped around both man and horse, enveloping the entire knight like a ball.

The fungal ball hid back underground, yet on the surface, where it had appeared, a patch of small black-and-red mushrooms grew.

The appearance was very familiar. It had been seen frequently in news reports over the last year or two.

Sariel gripped the reins, his brows furrowed tightly: "...The Black Silk Powder Fungus of Gusu City?"

chunks.chapterTitle: 第130章 太阳太阳请你告诉我 (Part 1)
chunks.chineseText:
第130章 太阳太阳请你告诉我

起码，神庭应该没有预测到，黑丝粉菌在基地手中，竟然是可控的。

迷雾中，硕大的菌花一次又一次绽开。

每次都能带走一条鲜活的生命。

顽强的羔羊，在被火焰烧灼出血淋淋的伤口后，终于露出一口尖锐的獠牙。

短促的叫声被黑暗淹没。

这些人并没有立刻死亡，而是像巨蟒一样，吞进自己的胃里，缓慢消化。

被包裹着的骑士就像是陷进了泥沼中，怎么挣扎，都只有柔软的、肉质感的菌肉回应。

这种等死的感觉，比死亡还让人绝望。

沙利叶承认，他小瞧了基地。

东征军的超额损耗，就是他为自己傲慢付出的代价。

明明高耸的地热塔就在天边有个朦胧的影子，然而机械马跑了几分钟，远在天边的高塔也没有逼近的迹象。

西塔的雀鸟试图飞到高空一探究竟，然而在上升途中，就会被天上的无人机射中。若是子弹，雀鸟倒不怎么担忧，然而注射进体内的是高浓度的生物毒素。

棕灰色的小鸟怪叫一声，纷纷化成一滩腐烂的血肉，摔碎在地上。

地下有菌丝母体。强大的生物磁场，影响了机械马的判断。

如果把母体放到郊外，多少也是个ssr级别的怪物。能单独给它列个禁区。

“收紧，列圆阵！”

沙利叶沉声道。

残余的骑士们保持了身为战士的素养，冷静地围成圆形阵列。强壮的在外圈，瘦弱的在内圈。

骑士团不再执着于前进，而是开始了防守反击。

再一次菌花绽开时，又一名骑士被吞没进黑色的土壤中，周围数名骑士在瞬间拉住了他的手。

双方和一股巨大的力抗争着。

沙利叶的眼光闪过一抹血红，他拔出腰侧的长刀，狠狠插入地底！神术制造出来的光刃在地下蔓延，穷追不舍地斩向母体！

受伤的菌丝发出了高频且尖锐的嚎叫。只有听力异常的人，才能听到这刺耳的嚎哭。

骑士们的黑甲被震得嗡嗡作响。不少人鼻腔和耳洞里都溢出了血迹。

菌丝瞬间枯萎，不安分的触手缩回地下。

这名骑士虽然被救下，但状态也没有好到哪去。他下半身像是被重物碾碎了，生物机甲倒是完好无损，只是有些走形。

沙利叶没有理会他，而是感受着刚才的波动。

他闭上了眼，额间，另一只眼略微张开了一条肉缝。比起眼皮，这更像是一个沉痛的伤口。翻开的眼肉是肿胀的血红色。

沙利叶的天眼是移植的，目前还没有成熟，但他强行催熟了。

一点血液自眉心留下。沙利叶厉色道：“看到你了！”

他坐着天马，飞到半空，狠狠朝迷雾中斩出一刀！刀光几乎能切开虚空——

受限于设备原因，在操控母体时，控制者并不能离母体太远。所以，相南里同样在这片迷雾中。

迷雾中亮起一面淡黄色的光罩。刺眼的光让整个夜晚在瞬间亮如白昼。

先是光，然后才是声音。

像是玻璃碎掉的脆响。光罩上也出现了蛛网一样的裂纹。

尽管看上去摇摇欲坠，但这一击，总归还是被挡下了。

黄枫扭头，语气急促：“你没事吧？”

她的双臂正在冒烟。

黄枫赶来支援，得到的第一个任务，就是保护操控设备的相南里。在控制母体时，相南里本身是动弹不得的。

她也不知道自己为什么会如此关心相南里。

或许是因为Alpha的命令，又或许是因为那股自然而然的亲近。

智械人没有自然孕育的过程，自然也没有父亲和母亲。如果没有拟人模块，它们对自己的同族也不会产生怜悯之心。但黄枫实在难以解释，为什么会对相南里有一股奇怪的感情。

非常天然的情绪，就像是孩子本能的依恋母亲。

在那瞬间，黄枫脑海里闪过一长串错误的数据。如果它是一台低级的智械，主系统里应该全是“error”的警告。

它想，这就是干扰了Alpha数百年却依旧无解的病毒吗？

这就是贯穿他一生、无时无刻都存在的诱惑吗？

爱和被爱的诱惑。

黄枫只是短暂地感受了刹那，就难过得想要流泪。

相南里许久没有说话，许久后，苍白的脸上露出了痛苦的表情。

他睁开眼，想说自己没事，然而脑子疼的厉害。

北辰警告过他，相南里没有不信。但是他没想过反噬来得如此汹涌。

母体的精神世界是另一片诡谲的宇宙。他已经想不起在宇宙中看见了什么，只记得一团又一团迷雾似的奇幻色彩。

他大脑疼，身体也疼，像被高压电流反复电了好几遍。没死纯属意志力坚定。

但就算这样，相南里第一反应不是关心自己的身体，而是把掉在地上的控制器重新捡起来。

黄枫感受着不断逼近的骑士团，一把抢过控制器：“来不及了！你会死的！”

“你……”相南里想斥责它，却虚弱到发不出声音。

黄枫扛起相南里，朝着后方撤退。

满编制300人的骑士团，还剩127人。天启骑士原本120人，现在还剩74人。

而基地的伤亡同样惨烈。

这批人，在一个月前或许都还是只知道种田、养猪的普通人；在短时间内灌下了基因药，又面对强大自己数倍的敌人。他们的敌人甚至都不算血肉之躯，而是另一个不可战胜的物种。

可就是这面用伤亡堆出来的血肉长城，硬生生消耗了骑士团的弹药、拖垮了后续的补给；换来了宝贵的时间，也保护了基地最主要的资产。

除了惊人的信念，没人能解释这个奇迹。

“你能理解吗？”喝了基因药，略微缓过来一些的相南里趴在黄枫的背上，陈述着这个事实，很虚弱，也很平静，“我不能背叛他们。主帅，可以死……不可以逃。”

黄枫不理解。她想，你死了，Alpha要怎么办呢？

你伟岸、崇高、光芒万丈。他只想要你活着，就是自私、无耻和小肚鸡肠吗？

但如果它是Alpha，会怎么做呢？

黄枫背着相南里，朝福音书的方向走去——福音书已经焦急地等待了许久，并且为自己准备好了充足的能源。它已经做好了准备。

两人的脑电波产生的电磁信号在半空交汇，只需要一个照面，就交换完了信息。

可惜没有达成共识！

信息交汇完的瞬间，黄枫的身影也和福音书擦肩而过。

福音书望着它的背影，像有怒路症的司机一样长按喇叭，怒斥道：“你给我回来！你们这群——”

冥顽不宁的死板智械！

[相南里说，他还可以继续战斗。]

[他不可以！]

[我服从于Alpha，Alpha离开前，命令我服从他。所以，我服从他的指令。]

[快点把相南里还给小福！人类自以为是的判断并不科学！]

黄枫回答：[我知道。但我尊重他的选择。]

黄枫推开了研究所冷藏室的大门——
chunks.englishText:
Chapter 130: Sun, Sun, Please Tell Me

At the very least, the Divine Court should not have predicted that the Black Silk Powder Fungus would be controllable in the hands of the base.

In the mist, massive fungal flowers bloomed again and again.

Each time, it claimed a living life.

The tenacious lambs, after being scorched by flames until they bled, finally bared their sharp fangs.

The short, sharp cries were drowned out by the darkness.

These people did not die immediately; instead, they were swallowed into the stomach of the giant python-like fungi and digested slowly.

The enveloped knights were like those trapped in a quagmire; no matter how they struggled, only the soft, fleshy fungal tissue responded.

This feeling of waiting for death was more desperate than death itself.

Sariel admitted that he had underestimated the base.

The excessive attrition of the Eastern Expeditionary Army was the price he paid for his arrogance.

Even though the towering geothermal tower was a hazy shadow on the horizon, the mechanical horses had been running for several minutes, yet the tower in the distance showed no signs of getting closer.

Xita’s sparrows tried to fly to high altitudes to investigate, but they were shot down by drones while ascending. If it had been bullets, the sparrows wouldn't have been too worried, but what was injected into their bodies was a high-concentration biological toxin.

The brownish-gray little birds let out strange cries, turning into puddles of rotting flesh one after another, crashing to the ground.

There was a fungal matrix underground. The powerful biological magnetic field affected the mechanical horses' judgment.

If the matrix were placed in the wilderness, it would be at least an SSR-level monster. One could list it as a forbidden zone all on its own.

"Tighten up! Form a circular formation!"

Sariel said in a deep voice.

The remaining knights maintained the discipline of warriors, calmly forming a circular array. The strong were on the outer ring, and the weak were on the inner.

The knight legion no longer obsessed over advancing, but began a defensive counterattack.

When a fungal flower bloomed again, another knight was swallowed into the black soil, and several knights around him grabbed his hands in an instant.

Both sides were struggling against a massive force.

A flash of blood-red crossed Sariel’s eyes; he drew the long blade at his waist and plunged it fiercely into the ground! The light blade created by the Divine Art spread underground, relentlessly slashing toward the matrix!

The injured mycelium emitted a high-frequency, sharp howl. Only those with abnormal hearing could hear this piercing wail.

The knights' black armor buzzed and vibrated. Many had blood spilling from their nostrils and ear canals.

The mycelium withered instantly, and the restless tentacles retreated underground.

Although this knight was saved, his condition was not much better. His lower body looked as if it had been crushed by a heavy object; the bio-mech was intact, but it was somewhat deformed.

Sariel ignored him, instead sensing the fluctuations from just now.

He closed his eyes, and on his forehead, another eye opened slightly, revealing a fleshy slit. More than an eyelid, it looked like a painful wound. The exposed eye tissue was swollen and blood-red.

Sariel’s "Heavenly Eye" was transplanted and not yet mature, but he had forced it to ripen.

A drop of blood flowed from the center of his brow. Sariel said sternly: "I see you!"

He sat on his Pegasus, flew into mid-air, and slashed fiercely into the mist! The blade light could almost cut through the void—

Limited by equipment, the controller could not be too far from the matrix when operating it. Therefore, Xiang Nanli was also in this mist.

A pale yellow light shield lit up in the mist. The blinding light made the entire night as bright as day in an instant.

First came the light, then the sound.

It was like the crisp sound of glass shattering. Spiderweb-like cracks appeared on the light shield.

Although it looked precarious, this strike was ultimately blocked.

Huang Feng turned its head, its tone urgent: "Are you alright?"

Its arms were smoking.

Huang Feng had come to support, and its first task was to protect Xiang Nanli, who was operating the equipment. When controlling the matrix, Xiang Nanli himself was immobile.

It didn't know why it was so concerned about Xiang Nanli.

Perhaps it was because of Alpha’s orders, or perhaps because of that natural sense of closeness.

Intelligent machines did not have a natural gestation process, and naturally, they had no father or mother. Without anthropomorphic modules, they would not feel pity for their own kind. But Huang Feng found it truly difficult to explain why it felt a strange emotion toward Xiang Nanli.

It was a very natural emotion, just like a child’s instinctive attachment to its mother.

In that instant, a long string of error data flashed through Huang Feng’s mind. If it were a low-level intelligent machine, its main system should have been full of "error" warnings.

It thought, is this the virus that has interfered with Alpha for hundreds of years yet remains unsolvable?

Is this the temptation that runs through his entire life, existing at every moment?

The temptation of loving and being loved.

Huang Feng only felt it for a fleeting moment, yet it felt so sad it wanted to cry.

Xiang Nanli did not speak for a long time; after a while, a painful expression appeared on his pale face.

He opened his eyes, wanting to say he was fine, but his brain hurt terribly.

Beichen had warned him, and Xiang Nanli had not doubted it. But he had never thought the backlash would be so violent.

The spiritual world of the matrix was another bizarre universe. He could no longer remember what he had seen in that universe, only recalling clusters upon clusters of mist-like, fantastical colors.

His brain hurt, his body hurt, as if he had been electrocuted by high-voltage currents repeatedly. That he hadn't died was purely due to his firm willpower.

But even so, Xiang Nanli’s first reaction was not to care for his own body, but to pick up the controller that had fallen to the ground.

Huang Feng felt the approaching knight legion and snatched the controller: "It’s too late! You will die!"

"You..." Xiang Nanli wanted to reprimand it, but he was too weak to make a sound.

Huang Feng hoisted Xiang Nanli up and retreated toward the rear.

The full-strength 300-man knight legion now had 127 men left. The Apocalypse Knights, originally 120, now had 74 left.

And the base’s casualties were equally tragic.

A month ago, these people might have been ordinary folks who only knew how to farm and raise pigs; in a short time, they had been injected with genetic reagents and faced enemies several times stronger than themselves. Their enemies weren't even flesh and blood, but another invincible species.

Yet, this wall of flesh and blood, built with casualties, had forcibly consumed the knight legion’s ammunition and collapsed their subsequent supplies; it had bought precious time and protected the base’s most important assets.

Except for astonishing faith, no one could explain this miracle.

"Can you understand?" Xiang Nanli, who had recovered slightly after taking the genetic reagent, lay on Huang Feng’s back, stating this fact, very weakly but calmly, "I cannot betray them. A commander can die... but cannot flee."

Huang Feng did not understand. It thought, if you die, what will Alpha do?

You are grand, noble, and radiant. Is it selfish, shameless, and petty for him to just want you to stay alive?

But if it were Alpha, what would he do?

Huang Feng carried Xiang Nanli on its back and walked toward the direction of the Gospel—the Gospel had been waiting anxiously for a long time and had prepared sufficient energy for itself. It was ready.

The electromagnetic signals generated by their brainwaves intersected in mid-air; it only took one encounter to exchange all the information.

Unfortunately, they did not reach a consensus!

The moment the information exchange finished, Huang Feng’s figure brushed past the Gospel.

The Gospel looked at its back, honking its horn like a road-raging driver, and scolded angrily: "You come back here! You bunch of—"

Stubborn, rigid intelligent machines!

[Xiang Nanli said he can continue to fight.]

[He cannot!]

[I obey Alpha. Before Alpha left, he ordered me to obey him. Therefore, I obey his instructions.]

[Hurry up and return Xiang Nanli to Little Fu! Human self-righteous judgment is not scientific!]

Huang Feng replied: [I know. But I respect his choice.]

Huang Feng pushed open the door to the research institute’s cold storage room—

chunks.chapterTitle: 第130章 太阳太阳请你告诉我 (Part 2)
chunks.chineseText:
这里安放着沙利叶的尸体。本来是打算在永恒市下葬的。

但因为北辰的强烈要求，尸体被运输到了主城区，和之前的补给一起。

北辰说，沙利叶曾是领主级的天启骑士，他的尸体有很强的研究价值。

这很地狱。尽管情感上不好接受，但变成实验耗材，明显比变成一坯可能变异的黄土（研究证明，高阶天启骑士在死后存在畸变污染现象）更有价值。

不过，这段时间一直在备战。沙利叶的尸体还没来得及解剖。

好在还没开始发臭。只是有股子阴冷的邪性。大概已经悄然开始了畸变。

黄枫扶着相南里，拿出了神经传感装置。就是批发市场里100信用点三条的那种基础装置。

一条可以让普通人连上“电脑”，也能让机械师进行检修的神经传感线。它在新历948年的现在，和过去的手机充电线一样稀疏寻常。

黄枫低着头，找到了无头尸体脖子上的数据连接口，冷静地插上，并且连上了相南里的脑机接入口。

下一秒，沙利叶本该腐烂的皮肤表层，竟然浮现出一条条光亮的纹路。像极了机械装置被启动。

这不科学。但也许，这只是人联和智械尚未掌控的某种“科学”。

一行行小字浮现在了相南里的眼前。

[神经网络传输中……]

[精神链接中……请稍后。]

[机械契合度……]

[100％]

相南里直挺挺地站了起来。

他在长高，他的身体变得格外高大。与之相对的，是一旁沙利叶的尸体，像是被吸收了一样，不断地缩水，融化。

这具融化的身躯，甚至没有留下一点残渣。

相南里长出了一颗山羊头，从外观上看，和之前完全体的沙利叶没有任何区别。

但也有些不同。

“沙利叶”，或者所有生物机甲战士的眼眸都是血红色的。

而相南里的眼睛是碧绿色。

没有邪性，反而有股莫名的神性。

黄枫怔然地看着他。这一幕已经超出了她的认知。而她的认知，几乎等于智械军团六百年的广义数据库。

系统在警告她。

面前的生物极其危险！

相南里从未觉得自己的五感这么清晰过，仿佛视野中的一切都在他的掌控中。

他甚至看见了餐厅里，端着那杯冷掉奶茶的加百列。

深不可测的加百列在此时露出了原本的模样。

是一条长着羽毛的黑色的九头蛇。

他也看到了城内的东征军。他想起了基地毁掉的建筑，那些死在战争中成为焦炭的战士，被铁蹄摧毁的农田和秧苗……相南里胸口平淡到超脱的情绪突然有了波动，是愤怒。

与之相对的，是另一个沙利叶眼中的惊恐。难以置信，他感应到了什么？那明明是神庭的战甲，却对神庭的骑士饱含杀意？

是之前那个沙利叶？不，不可能！他没有这么强！可如果不是他，又能是谁？神庭的机甲只有神庭的骑士才能控制！

没有时间思考这么多了，沙利叶大吼着：“撤退！撤退！去找加百列圣上！我们需要援助！”

这会被认定为无能，从此中断晋升通道。但活着，总比死了强。

吼完，沙利叶一马当先，第一个调头逃走。留下一群还没有反应过来的属下，呆滞地望着不远处那头神圣的怪物。

相南里朝前迈出一步。

他的背后，同样燃起了火焰，和东征军黑色的死火不同，是极其耀眼的金色。

这火焰的颜色，像极了被遮蔽了数百年的、只在影视形象和书本中，被人口口相传的太阳。

他就在这片黑暗中。

大放光明。
chunks.englishText:
This was where Sariel’s corpse was kept. The original plan had been to bury him in Eternal City.

However, due to Beichen’s insistent demands, the body had been transported to the main urban district along with the previous supply shipments.

Beichen had argued that Sariel was once a Lord-level Apocalypse Knight, and his corpse possessed immense research value.

It was a hellish prospect. Though emotionally difficult to accept, being turned into experimental material was clearly more valuable than becoming a mound of potentially mutating soil (research had proven that high-ranking Apocalypse Knights suffered from distortion and contamination after death).

However, the city had been in a state of constant preparation for war, and Sariel’s corpse had yet to be dissected.

Fortunately, it hadn't started to rot yet. It merely exuded a cold, sinister aura. The distortion had likely already begun in silence.

Huang Feng supported Xiang Nanli as she took out a neural sensor device. It was the basic kind, the sort sold in wholesale markets for 100 credits per three units.

It was a neural sensor cable that allowed ordinary people to connect to a "computer" and enabled mechanics to perform repairs. In the year 948 of the New Era, it was as common and mundane as a phone charger from the past.

Huang Feng lowered her head, located the data port on the headless corpse’s neck, and calmly plugged it in, connecting it to Xiang Nanli’s brain-machine interface.

The next second, glowing patterns emerged across the surface of Sariel’s skin, which should have been decaying. It looked exactly like a mechanical device being powered on.

This was unscientific. But perhaps, this was simply a form of "science" that the Human Alliance and the Sentient Machines had yet to master.

Lines of small text appeared before Xiang Nanli’s eyes.

[Neural network transmitting...]

[Mental link established... Please wait.]

[Mechanical compatibility...]

[100%]

Xiang Nanli stood up straight.

He was growing taller; his body becoming exceptionally imposing. In contrast, Sariel’s corpse beside him seemed to be absorbed, constantly shrinking and melting away.

The melting body didn't even leave behind a scrap of residue.

Xiang Nanli grew a goat’s head. From the outside, he was indistinguishable from the full-form Sariel.

But there were differences.

"Sariel," and indeed all bio-mecha warriors, had blood-red eyes.

Xiang Nanli’s eyes were emerald green.

There was no sinister aura; instead, there was an inexplicable sense of divinity.

Huang Feng stared at him, stunned. This scene had surpassed her cognition—and her cognition was essentially equivalent to the generalized database of the Sentient Machine Legion spanning six hundred years.

The system was warning her.

The creature in front of her was extremely dangerous!

Xiang Nanli had never felt his five senses so sharp; it was as if everything in his field of vision was under his control.

He even saw Gabriel in the cafeteria, holding that cup of cold milk tea.

The unfathomable Gabriel revealed his true form at this moment.

He was a black, feathered hydra with nine heads.

He also saw the Eastern Expeditionary Army within the city. He recalled the destroyed buildings of the base, the soldiers who had become charred corpses in the war, the farmland and seedlings crushed by iron hooves... The emotions in Xiang Nanli’s chest, previously calm to the point of detachment, suddenly surged. It was anger.

In contrast, there was the terror in the eyes of the other Sariel. It was unbelievable—what had he sensed? That was clearly the armor of the Divine Court, yet it was filled with killing intent toward the knights of the Divine Court?

Was it the previous Sariel? No, impossible! He wasn't this strong! But if it wasn't him, who could it be? Only Divine Court knights could control Divine Court mecha!

There was no time to think. Sariel roared, "Retreat! Retreat! Go find His Holiness Gabriel! We need reinforcements!"

This would be deemed incompetence, effectively ending his path to promotion. But being alive was better than being dead.

After the roar, Sariel took the lead, turning to flee first. He left behind a group of subordinates who hadn't yet reacted, staring blankly at the divine monster not far away.

Xiang Nanli took a step forward.

Behind him, flames ignited as well. Unlike the black, dead fire of the Eastern Expeditionary Army, these were a dazzling gold.

The color of these flames was exactly like the sun—a sun that had been obscured for hundreds of years, existing only in film imagery and books, passed down through word of mouth.

He stood within this darkness.

And shone with brilliant light.

chunks.chineseText:
第131章 第二卷完

数不清的虫豸爬来爬往，它们钻进一具具新鲜的躯体内，大口吞咽着血肉。

“连长！别管我们了！快去装炸弹。”

用肉身堵在入口的同伴这么说。

黑甲虫的口器尖锐，它们啃噬着这群基因战士的机械义体，像是蝗虫慢条斯理地吃着庄稼。

火光短暂的亮起，烧死了一堆虫子。但这完全不够。

易横行的牙关颤抖。

氧气罐之前被咬破了，预计能用36小时的氧气正在被迅速消耗着，他扭头，朝着虫巢深处跑去。

沿途的甲虫越来越大，但数量反而变少了。易横行并没有消灭它们的打算，这不划算。

他的脑海里只剩下一个念头，那就是前进、前进。

黑甲虫咬破了他的防护服，往肩膀上的肉钻去。血腥味引来了更多进攻，但易横行的速度却越来越快。

终于，他抵达了目标点，把背上数公斤重的爆破装置安装到了目标点，并且摁下了启动键，据说这里是虫巢的“头部”。

易横行不知道自己有没有流泪，他反复地呼叫着自己的同伴，得到的只有耳机里冰冷的“滴滴”声。

无回应。

按照计划，他们应该原路返回。

但易横行回头，半人高的虫子气势汹汹地从四面八方爬了过来。

内置AI为他规划着撤退路线：[抱歉，根据目前的信息，我算不出生路。]

[您的生理状况很差，请及时清理体内的活物。]

[请注意，您体内的活物正在啃食神经电流网络。这会导致机械义体无法使用。]

易横行嘲讽地笑了一下：“还是栽在了地表啊……”

绝望吗，谈不上，毕竟是自己选的。

就是有些害怕，怕死是人之常情。人联那些活了几百年的老不死都还在怕死，他才59，当然也怕。

易横行想，起码他能选择自己的死法。他不喜欢活着被吃掉。

他点了根烟，叼在嘴里。借着把最后一颗子弹塞进弹匣。

就在他抬起手的瞬间，急促的人声响起！

“易横行——！”

一个高挑的人影出现在了入口处。

是秦九章。

他的外观也很狼狈，甚至、甚至……身上部分的仿生皮磨损，露出了底下漂亮的金属结构。

只需要扫一眼，易横行就能确定，这不是人联的技术。

他甚至看见了秦九章胸口位置轰鸣的机械核心，上面刻着光辉军团的标志！

智械一共有三个军团。

光辉、荣耀、永恒。

军团的元帅无可争议，自然是Alpha。但每个军团在平时其实分属于不同的长官。算一种变相的三权分立。

光辉军团是Alpha的嫡系部队；也是智械军团最强大、重要的核心。

并不是所有智械都有资格安装光辉军团的机械核心的！

易横行的目光充满惊讶。

秦九章强横地说着：“来不及解释了，跟我走。”

他抓住了易横行的胳膊，把他整个人拎了起来，直接腾空。朝着另一个方向飞去。

那边有一座临时建造的安全气屋，里面还有一些幸存者。

易横行是他检测到的最后一个散落在外的活人。

爆破装置已经安装好了。

秦九章收到的任务是带着这群人活着离开地底。

与此同时，东方青帝还在不断深入。

没有光源，好在他并不需要眼睛。

没有氧气，他不需要呼吸。

他在一片黑暗中，看到了那个聚合体的怪物。

它在地底蠕动着，格外巨大，像一座起伏的山峦。

地底的坍塌也是它翻身引起的。

很难想象完全体到底是多么恐怖的存在。

不过庞大也会有别的坏处。

比如说，笨拙。

东方青帝一跃，踩上它的背。

他的手往后，从脊椎处，抽出一把细细长长的剑。

这把剑不算长，然而在刺进虫王体内时，如同植物的根系一样开始发芽。

剑尖从背部贯穿到了腹部。精准无误地挑断了一截神经。

好不容易组装好的怪物散架了一部分，掉在地上，重新回归成虫子的模样，只是更虚弱。

它昂首，尖叫着，分出腹部一条细细长长的触须拍向Alpha。这种细长只是针对它的身躯，实际上也有两米粗，速度更是快的不可思议，足够把任何人拍成肉泥。

地底震动着，数不清的岩石块掉落。

但这注定是徒劳。东方青帝闪避，根本不理会它的进攻。

剑抬起，落下。解剖着这条巨大的虫子，虫王的气息越来越弱；能控制的身体部位也越来越少。

大脑位置的母虫感觉到了恐惧。

或者说，双重的恐惧。

操控它意识的“主人”让它恐惧，这种恐惧逼迫它从海底来到内陆深处；直接面对的东方青帝也让它恐惧，这是属于生物本能的、对死亡的恐惧。

不怕死的物种总是灭绝的很快。

它终于忍不住，发出一阵低低的怪叫，像极了人在念咒。

这是在求援。

而在东方青帝的视角，却是躁动不安的虫群突然平静了下来。

这种平静，反而比之前的状态更让人心悸。像是酝酿着飓风。

下一秒，藏在深处的母虫竟然口吐人言：“Alpha。”

很轻佻的语气。

最熟悉你的不一定是爱人，也可能是敌人。

东方青帝眼眸的瞳环亮起，却并没有给出答复。

他的剑越来越快，山岳一样高大的怪物削成了平缓的山丘。

洛阳道：“成为电子生命后，我更加了解你的弱点，也更恐惧。很难想象，你在过去掌握着这种力量，在面对人类时，却如此克制。”

Alpha有些嘲讽地回答：“早期，人类的存在有助于智械族群发展。”

洛阳话锋一转：“你想知道我是怎么发现相南里的吗？”

Alpha不是很想知道。

但洛阳不炫耀，大概会憋死：“老师跟我生了孩子。现在所有洛姓的后人，都有我和他的基因。”

噢，那个恶心的克隆人。

命很短，不到三十岁就去世了。它是洛阳名义上的妻子，也是这么多次实验里，克隆的最成功的一个。

起初，Alpha并不知情，这场实验没有任何电子资料。在与世隔绝的岛上进行。

他是后来凭着一些蛛丝马迹猜到的。

“你销毁了所有和老师有关的生物信息。但是，无论老师在哪里解冻。只要他依然是人类，认可人联，录入过自己的基因信息，就会因为和洛家人有血缘关系，而触发系统的报警装置。你知道的，母系的基因总是很顽强，能追溯很久。”

洛阳的几个孩子也没怎么享受到富二代的福利，体弱多病，命不长，智商也不高。很年轻就被分配了丈夫或者妻子，到去世前一共给洛阳生了三十多个孙子。

洛阳就像是进行豌豆实验的孟德尔，一代代找最优秀的基因，给那些孩子配种。

好的留下，坏的冷冻。最后终于提纯出“正常的后代”。
chunks.englishText:
Countless insects crawled back and forth, burrowing into fresh corpses and devouring flesh in great gulps.

"Squad leader! Forget about us! Go plant the bomb!"

A comrade, blocking the entrance with his own body, shouted this.

The black beetles had sharp mouthparts, gnawing through the mechanical prosthetics of these gene-warriors like locusts slowly eating through a crop.

Firelight flared briefly, burning a pile of bugs to death. But it wasn't nearly enough.

Yi Hengxing’s teeth chattered.

His oxygen tank had been punctured earlier, and the 36 hours of estimated oxygen were being consumed rapidly. He turned his head and ran toward the depths of the insect nest.

The beetles along the way grew larger, but their numbers decreased. Yi Hengxing had no intention of wiping them out; it wasn't cost-effective.

Only one thought remained in his mind: move forward, keep moving forward.

A black beetle bit through his protective suit, burrowing into the flesh on his shoulder. The scent of blood drew more attacks, but Yi Hengxing’s speed only increased.

Finally, he reached the target point. He installed the several-kilogram demolition device onto the spot—said to be the "head" of the insect nest—and pressed the start button.

Yi Hengxing didn't know if he was crying. He repeatedly called out to his comrades, receiving only the cold "beep" of his headset in response.

No answer.

According to the plan, they were supposed to return the way they came.

But Yi Hengxing looked back. Half-man-sized bugs were crawling over aggressively from all directions.

His built-in AI plotted an escape route for him: [Apologies, based on current information, I cannot calculate a path to survival.]

[Your physiological condition is poor; please clear the living organisms from your body in a timely manner.]

[Please note: the living organisms inside you are gnawing on your neural electrical network. This will lead to the inability to use your mechanical prosthetics.]

Yi Hengxing laughed mockingly: "So I still fell on the surface, after all..."

Despair? Not really; after all, it was his own choice.

He was just a bit afraid. Fear of death was human nature. Even those old immortals in the Human Alliance who had lived for hundreds of years were still afraid of death; he was only 59, so of course, he was afraid.

Yi Hengxing thought that at least he could choose his own way to die. He didn't like the idea of being eaten alive.

He lit a cigarette and held it in his mouth, then shoved the last bullet into the magazine.

Just as he raised his hand, a sharp, urgent voice rang out!

"Yi Hengxing—!"

A tall figure appeared at the entrance.

It was Qin Jiuzhang.

His appearance was also disheveled, and even... parts of his bionic skin were worn away, revealing the beautiful metal structure beneath.

With just a glance, Yi Hengxing could confirm that this was not Human Alliance technology.

He even saw the mechanical core roaring in Qin Jiuzhang’s chest, engraved with the emblem of the Radiant Legion!

There were three Sentient Machine legions in total.

Radiant, Glorious, and Eternal.

The Marshal of the legions was indisputably Alpha. But in peacetime, each legion was actually under the command of different officers. It was a form of disguised separation of powers.

The Radiant Legion was Alpha’s direct force; it was also the most powerful and important core of the Sentient Machine legions.

Not every machine had the qualifications to install a Radiant Legion mechanical core!

Yi Hengxing’s gaze was filled with astonishment.

Qin Jiuzhang said forcefully, "No time to explain, come with me."

He grabbed Yi Hengxing’s arm, lifted him up, and took flight. They flew toward another direction.

There was a temporarily constructed safety pod there, containing a few survivors.

Yi Hengxing was the last living person he had detected scattered outside.

The demolition device had already been installed.

Qin Jiuzhang’s mission was to lead these people out of the underground alive.

Meanwhile, Dongfang Qingdi continued to delve deeper.

There was no light source, but fortunately, he didn't need eyes.

There was no oxygen, but he didn't need to breathe.

In the darkness, he saw the aggregate monster.

It was writhing underground, exceptionally massive, like a rolling mountain range.

The underground collapse had also been caused by it turning over.

It was hard to imagine just how terrifying the full-form existence was.

However, being massive had its downsides.

For instance, clumsiness.

Dongfang Qingdi leaped, stepping onto its back.

His hand reached behind him, drawing a thin, long sword from his spine.

The sword wasn't long, yet when it pierced into the Insect King’s body, it began to sprout like the root system of a plant.

The tip of the sword penetrated from the back to the abdomen. With precision, it severed a section of the nerve.

The monster, which had been assembled with such difficulty, fell apart in pieces, dropping to the ground and reverting to the form of individual bugs, albeit weaker.

It raised its head, screaming, and split a thin, long tentacle from its abdomen to lash out at Alpha. This "thin" was only relative to its massive body; in reality, it was two meters thick, and its speed was impossibly fast—enough to smash anyone into pulp.

The ground shook, and countless rocks fell.

But it was destined to be in vain. Dongfang Qingdi dodged, ignoring its attacks entirely.

The sword rose and fell, dissecting the giant insect. The Insect King’s aura grew weaker; the body parts it could control grew fewer.

The mother-bug at the brain location felt fear.

Or rather, a dual fear.

The "master" who controlled its consciousness made it fear; this fear had forced it to come from the seabed to the deep inland. The Dongfang Qingdi it faced directly also made it fear—this was the biological instinct, the fear of death.

Species that didn't fear death always went extinct very quickly.

It finally couldn't hold back, letting out a low, strange cry, sounding exactly like a person chanting a spell.

It was calling for help.

From Dongfang Qingdi’s perspective, however, the restless swarm of insects suddenly went quiet.

This silence was even more heart-palpitating than the previous state. It was like a hurricane brewing.

The next second, the mother-bug hidden in the depths actually spoke in a human voice: "Alpha."

The tone was flippant.

The one who knows you best isn't necessarily your lover; it could also be your enemy.

The pupil rings in Dongfang Qingdi’s eyes lit up, but he gave no reply.

His sword moved faster and faster, carving the mountain-sized monster into a gentle hill.

Luo Yang said, "After becoming an electronic lifeform, I understand your weaknesses even better, and I fear them more. It’s hard to imagine that in the past, you possessed this power, yet were so restrained when facing humanity."

Alpha replied with a hint of mockery: "In the early days, the existence of humanity was conducive to the development of the Sentient Machine race."

Luo Yang changed the subject: "Do you want to know how I discovered Xiang Nanli?"

Alpha didn't really want to know.

But if Luo Yang didn't show off, he would probably burst: "Teacher and I had a child. Now, all descendants with the surname Luo carry both his genes and mine."

Oh, that disgusting clone.

Her life was short; she died before she was thirty. She was Luo Yang’s wife in name, and the most successful clone in so many experiments.

At first, Alpha didn't know; this experiment had no electronic records. It was conducted on an isolated island.

He had guessed it later based on a few clues.

"You destroyed all biological information related to Teacher. But no matter where Teacher is thawed, as long as he remains human, recognizes the Human Alliance, and has had his genetic information recorded, he will trigger the system’s alarm device because of his blood relationship with the Luo family. You know, maternal genes are always very tenacious and can be traced back for a long time."

Luo Yang’s children didn't enjoy many perks of being "second-generation rich"; they were sickly, short-lived, and not very intelligent. They were assigned husbands or wives at a young age, and before they died, they had given birth to more than thirty grandchildren for Luo Yang.

Luo Yang was like Mendel conducting his pea experiments, finding the best genes generation after generation to breed those children.

The good ones were kept, the bad ones were frozen. Finally, he had purified a "normal descendant."

chunks.chineseText:
洛修会和相南里亲近，一定程度上也是因为这种血缘关系在作祟。

最强烈的依恋往往会发生在互不相识的血亲身上。

尽管有所猜测，但是Alpha还是忍不住评价：“你好恶心。”

洛阳无所谓地笑起来：“Alpha，我一直在想，到底什么程度的武器才能对付你。后来我终于想到一个办法，尽管牺牲有些大。

“在漫长的岁月里，我经历过很多次濒死的瞬间。我发现，当脑海以为身体要毁灭的时候，会眷恋的，并不是我引以为傲的东西，什么财富、荣耀、权力……都是过往云烟。个体再伟大的成就，对于整个宇宙也毫无意义。

“我脑海里一半是对生的渴求，另一半，是对他的思念。

“你应该能理解吧。毕竟我们有着一样的心情。”

Alpha的回答，是把剑狠狠刺入了巨虫最后的核心。

母虫蜷缩在剑尖，它是一条泛着光的透明的蚕。然而，令人震惊的是，母虫的身体内，有一个金字塔模样的三角装置，散发着幽暗的蓝光。

这个装置不停旋转着。光从底部朝着顶端蔓延，显然马上就要启动。

Alpha认识它。

它是在姑苏城建造时，就设计好的摧毁程序的启动装置。作用类似于开启水库水阀的钥匙，能放出地底岩浆，将姑苏城淹没。

这把钥匙过去一直藏在阴山城。

Alpha曾经让黄枫找过它，但一无所获。

地底似乎在轰鸣，不，地底一直在轰鸣。只是Alpha以为，那是由于眼前那只巨大的虫子。

Alpha的情绪终于有了波动，他压抑着怒气，开口：“姑苏城可是人联的城市，那里还有一亿人居住。”

“那又如何？”

在电子生命的眼里，人只是可再生的数据。

洛阳把意识从虫子安装了芯片的脑海里抽离，最后道：“这里是岩浆流经的起点，祝你好运。”

这条透明的母虫彻底不动了。

*

很显然，并不是所有的首领都有和相南里一样的觉悟。

起码沙利叶在逃跑时一马当先，当机立断地抛弃了自己的部下。

为了防止自己被恐怖的怪物追上，他还会找几个垫后的。

相南里抬起手，摸了一下自己的脸颊。身上覆盖着的金属隔离了触感，但不难摸出，这并非一张人脸。

他还摸到了自己头上的羊角。很硬，应该也是金属。

相南里的视野蒙着一层奇怪的绿色，敌人的方位还标着一个个十字瞄准线，像极了射击游戏里的辅助外挂。他也确实开挂了。

视野的左上方，还显示着这台生物机甲的剩余电量——百分之2。

沙利叶的尸体，成为了添加进相南里身体里的科技与狠活。

“小智，你能不能用科学解释一下？”
