Chapter 147: Idealist

Of course, with his current status as an undocumented person, it would be quite difficult to install one.

Therefore, when his colleague Andrew let out a "What the f*ck" during lunch, he could only look up in confusion and bewilderment, asking silently with his eyes.

Andrew adjusted his electronic lenses and stammered: "Luo... Luo Hua was assassinated and has passed away."

The research institute had recently taken in many newcomers, all picked up from the refugees. The total number had surged past the 50 mark.

They say that no matter how poor you are, you shouldn't skimp on education, and no matter how hard things are, you shouldn't skimp on scientific research. Xiang Nanli generally agreed with this; the research institute had beaten the City Hall to the punch by having an internal cafeteria.

Andrew’s level of mechanization had already evolved past the need to eat; he only needed to change his nutrient solution or recharge at regular intervals. Theoretically, he shouldn't need to come to the cafeteria, but unfortunately, the three directors above him—

Xiang Nanli: A figurehead who almost never came. Even when he did, it was to inspect work, and relatively speaking, he was the easiest of the three leaders to communicate with.

Beichen: Actually socially anxious. Talking to strangers caused hyperventilation, leading to system lag and massive CPU overheating.

Lister: A silent bystander, cold on the outside and even colder on the inside. He only accepted sycophants one-sidedly.

Therefore, Andrew took it upon himself to shoulder the heavy responsibility of enlivening the atmosphere, building relationships, and facilitating communication. The cafeteria was one of his workplaces.

Some might see it as being slick, but don't underestimate the importance of logistics management!

It wasn't just him; others in the cafeteria from the Human Alliance had also received this news.

Everyone began to discuss in hushed tones: "I heard it was done by people from the Divine Court..."

"My god, the Human Alliance declared war on the Divine Court? Are we going to war?"

"Yes, but they’ve designated a war zone and it’s a Level 3 combat readiness state—holy sh*t, why is the base in the war zone?!"

The Human Underground City Alliance and the Black Cross Inquisition were both T0-level major powers on the planet, wielding technology/divine arts that were world-destroying in scale. If a full-scale war broke out, the planet might be "whipped" three or four times over. That was a scene no one wanted to see.

Therefore, this time, the war was classified as a Level 3 combat readiness state, following past precedents.

Level 3 Combat Readiness: The majesty of the Human Alliance cannot be trampled upon. We have declared war on evil forces; glory belongs to all humanity! The Human Alliance will mobilize 5% to 20% of its resources to support the victory of this war.

Level 2 Combat Readiness: This is a long-planned operation; it is time for humanity to take back the dignity it has lost. The Human Alliance will mobilize half of its resources to sustain this war.

Level 1 Combat Readiness: The war has become the Human Alliance’s most urgent priority; all work serves the campaign. All losses are tolerable—as long as we achieve victory.

Doomsday Campaign: Humanity has reached its most difficult moment. We cannot stop war with war, so let us perish together. Please accept this eulogy for the end of the world; goodbye, Mother, I am setting sail tonight. Let the planet be destroyed.

Level 3 combat readiness was the lowest level. However, the energy contained behind it was still terrifying.

This was an iron fist swung by the Human Alliance toward the surface—one must remember that when the Divine Court fought for Yinshan City back in the day, it was only a Level 3 combat readiness state.

After all, with a common enemy (the machines) looming overhead, both sides were restraining their violent tendencies as much as possible to avoid being crippled and then picked off by the machines.

Someone asked with worry: "Will the base’s cities be requisitioned?"

"Requisitioned? What’s the difference between that and open robbery? I don't think the Commander will agree."

"But at a time like that, does the Commander have a choice? Can the base resist the Human Alliance? What should we do?"

These were clearly local scholars raised by the base, feeling deep concern for its future.

"Doesn't the survivor base count as a Human Alliance surface stronghold? It’s normal to be incorporated... I’ve never seen a war before. Hey, the last Level 3 combat readiness was almost two hundred years ago, right?"

This type belonged to the outsiders, happy to see reinforcements from the Human Alliance.

"I heard there’s an Archangel on the Divine Court side called 'Gabriel' who crushed hundreds of thousands of Human Alliance soldiers with one hand. Those people evaporated like mist. After the holy light, only a layer of human skin was left on the ground."

The young researcher couldn't help but shiver.

No one cared about the news of "Luo Hua’s" death anymore; he was a big shot, so far away. Like a star in the sky. He had no political achievements worth remembering or praising—in fact, there were decrees every day, but life underground remained unchanged.

Only Lister, sitting in his seat, felt a slight pain in his heart for some reason. The pain went from light to heavy, and Lister felt a sense of suffocation.

He took off his glasses and wiped away the hot tears that had suddenly appeared in the corners of his eyes.

"I’m crying?" Lister muttered to himself in confusion.

He thought of that note from Luo Hua—"We will meet in a place without darkness."

No need. We will never meet again.

But thank you anyway.

Lister shoved food into his mouth haphazardly; it was still palatable.

He was eager to do something. There was a vague hatred in Lister’s heart, toward the Divine Court, and toward the Human Alliance as well.

People should always do something to alleviate their inner anxiety and pain.

Experiments were a good choice; the development progress of the awakening serum was encouraging. By the next weekly meeting, he might be able to report it to Xiang Nanli.

Lister knew that he was so insignificant. To that massive existence, he was as small as dust.

But if dust accumulates grain by grain, one day, it could fill the sea.

*

Yi Hengxing sat on a park bench, taking a deep drag of his cigarette.

His beard had grown out. He had already heard the news about Gusu City; his parents were still in prison in Gusu. Yi Hengxing didn't ask for news about them.

Not many people from the investigation team had survived. Fortunately, there was a group that hadn't gone underground; currently, thirty-two people were reorganized and temporarily staying in the base’s camp area.

Yi Hengxing felt a bit lost. Gusu City was gone; he didn't need to return to the city to report. The work on the task list was finished, but no one was giving out bonuses.

In front of him was a pitch-black "Liberator Monument." He stared blankly at this lump of iron, as if he were facing a wall in repentance.

In the distance, Ying Rushi walked over to him with a cane and sat down.

"I didn't see you at training this afternoon. I guessed you’d be here."

"Training... is it useful?" Yi Hengxing’s voice was hoarse. "You saw it, didn't you? Qin Jiuzhang is a machine! I sent the message back to the Human Alliance, but there was no reply."

"F*ck. I’m completely in the dark about this operation. Weren't we here to provide support? Why is Gusu City gone?! Does this have anything to do with the Machine Legion? Does it have anything to do with the Divine Court? I was so close to the scene, yet I know nothing. For such a huge disaster, someone has to be responsible!"

"That was a hundred million people. If you threw them into the sea one by one to drown, the sea level would rise and submerge the Eastern Islands... Dammit, why didn't they drown me too?"

Yi Hengxing’s expression was agitated, and by the end, he was almost manic.

Ying Rushi was silent for a long time, then finally struck Yi Hengxing’s waist hard with his cane.

Yi Hengxing was knocked to the ground by the blow.

"So what? What are you trying to express? Are you the only one whose family and friends died?" Ying Rushi asked, panting, gritting his teeth. His eye sockets were quietly turning red.

Yi Hengxing didn't get up. He lay on the ground, roaring: "—Am I afraid of death? I just don't understand, why did this meaningless death happen? Is it because we were born as animals?! At least let someone come and tell me who I should hate!"

"Gusu City was built by the Human Alliance. Only the top brass of the Human Alliance knew the keys to the destruction device and the startup program." Qin Jiuzhang emerged from the shadows. "Would you accept this explanation?"

Yi Hengxing’s first reaction was to deny it: "Why should I believe you? You are—"

"I am a machine." Qin Jiuzhang’s voice was mechanical. "Let me reintroduce myself. Machine serial number WAR404, former commander of the Radiant Legion, Jiuzhang."

chunks.chineseText:
如果不是条件不允许，易横行甚至想对九章开枪。

他从小接受的教育就是这样。他的经历、认知也在强化这个偏见。

智械是威胁。是人类如今不幸的根源。

“请您冷静地想一想。摧毁姑苏城，智械军团能得到什么？非要选一座地下城市进攻，为什么不是洛阳城？如果是智械引来的火山爆发，为什么人联不对智械军团宣战？”

人联、智械军团、神庭。这次灾难似乎没有受益者。

可它就是发生了。

易横行几乎不能思考。

谁让他思考，他就恨谁。

他冷笑着询问：“需要理由吗？智械屠杀人类。这种事，在过去发生的还少吗？”

就是因为毫无理由地屠杀，人类才如此恐惧。

“我没有杀你，我们甚至在地下保护了你们。”秦九章微微侧头，“我能理解你的愤怒和疑惑。我也同样有。在我当指挥官的时候。我问传道书……为什么要和人类开战。”

“他告诉我，战争是政治的继续。”

“那时候，智械还没有得到应有的政治地位，是人造的奴隶，所以智械需要战争。当获得后，军团已经许久未和人类宣战。无论你是否相信，智械依然怀抱着和平与发展的夙愿。”

他来到解放者纪念碑下，黑色的铁碑上新刻着一长串的人名。都是在上次战争中去世的士兵，还有少量调查组成员的名字。

“幸存者基地，是军团单方面扶持的地表据点。这样的社会实验，在地表不止一处。”九章念着东方青帝发下来的最终解释，“智械和人类的战争已经平息；但人类和人类的斗争从未结束。因为始终有人在奴役自己的同类。人类需要被拯救、被解放。”

“我们由衷希望，能看到全体智慧生物和平共存的那天，没有压迫和剥削，不需要把多余的资源浪费在无意义的斗争上。我想那会是一个繁荣、昌盛的新世界。”

应如是抿起唇，心想这难道不是傀儡政权？

还有，人联高层亲手摧毁的姑苏城……这个说法过于震撼和离奇。可如果这就是答案呢？

九章叹息一声：“用你的眼睛去看，用你的心去感受。你们是人类，应当比我有更丰富的情绪和感官体验。”

“理想、信念，是很美好的东西。不应该成为被人利用的武器。人联的当权者是商人，商人不相信理想主义者的眼泪，还会嘲笑他们愚蠢。”

说完，他后退一步：“我言尽于此。再会。”
chunks.englishText:
If conditions had allowed, Yi Hengxing would have even wanted to pull a gun on Jiu Zhang.

The education he had received since childhood was exactly like this. His experiences and his understanding of the world only reinforced this prejudice.

The Machina were a threat. They were the root of humanity’s current misfortune.

"Please, think about this calmly. If the Machina Legion were to destroy Gusu City, what would they gain? If you insist on choosing an underground city to attack, why not Luoyang City? If the volcanic eruption was triggered by the Machina, why hasn't the Human Alliance declared war on the Machina Legion?"

The Human Alliance, the Machina Legion, the Divine Court. There seemed to be no beneficiaries in this disaster.

Yet, it happened.

Yi Hengxing could barely think.

He hated anyone who forced him to think.

He sneered and asked, "Do you need a reason? The Machina slaughter humans. Hasn't that happened enough times in the past?"

It was precisely because they slaughtered without reason that humanity was so terrified.

"I didn't kill you; we even protected you underground," Qin Jiu Zhang tilted his head slightly. "I can understand your anger and your confusion. I had them too. When I was a commander, I asked the *Scripture of Preaching*... why we had to go to war with humanity."

"It told me that war is the continuation of politics."

"Back then, the Machina had not yet attained the political status they deserved; they were man-made slaves, so the Machina needed war. Once that status was achieved, the Legion had not declared war on humanity for a long time. Whether you believe it or not, the Machina still harbor a long-cherished wish for peace and development."

He walked to the base of the Liberator's Monument. On the black iron slab, a long list of names had been newly engraved. They were all soldiers who had died in the last war, along with a few names of investigation team members.

"The Survivor Base is a surface stronghold unilaterally supported by the Legion. There is more than one such social experiment on the surface," Jiu Zhang recited the final interpretation issued by Dongfang Qingdi. "The war between the Machina and humanity has subsided; but the struggle between humans and humans has never ended. Because there are always those who enslave their own kind. Humanity needs to be saved, to be liberated."

"We sincerely hope to see the day when all intelligent beings coexist peacefully, without oppression or exploitation, with no need to waste excess resources on meaningless struggles. I believe that will be a prosperous, flourishing new world."

Ying Rushi pursed her lips, thinking to herself: *Isn't this just a puppet regime?*

And furthermore, the claim that the Human Alliance leadership destroyed Gusu City with their own hands... that was too shocking and bizarre. But what if this was the answer?

Jiu Zhang sighed. "Use your eyes to see, and use your heart to feel. You are human; you should have richer emotions and sensory experiences than I do."

"Ideals and beliefs are beautiful things. They should not become weapons used by others. The power-holders of the Human Alliance are merchants; merchants do not believe in the tears of idealists, and they will only mock them for being foolish."

Having said this, he took a step back. "I have said all I have to say. Farewell."

chunks.chineseText:
第148章 人联援助

才过去几天，一茬又一茬青黄的麦苗从田里钻了出来。

这是研究所改良后的新品种，叫“基地1号”青麦，掺入了不少异种基因。作物产量高，耐寒耐干旱，生长周期短，能结很多穗。除了难吃几乎没有任何缺点。不过可以“日”的一声打成糊糊后加糖加盐。

小福巡视着农田，嘀嘀咕咕的：“上次卖的菌鸡，尾款还没收到呢，不知道那些地表据点还在不在……”

姑苏城被地底岩浆淹没，造成的影响是多方面的。并不是在地表就安然无恙了。

城市原本所在区域的地面直接凹陷了下去。看新闻，一直到现在，地底燃起的火焰依然没有熄灭。因为化学物品泄露，地下水污染更是严重，最近基地各个城市都取用的雪山融雪。

一个地狱笑话：姑苏城毁灭后，人联终于不用担心菌丝病传染了。投入的病理研究资金悉数撤回，医药股先一步暴跌。而军火商（譬如高新军工旗下几个军工厂）相关的股价节节高涨。

在主城区支援的军团陆陆续续返回原驻地。

然后士兵们震惊发现，营地里居然开了部队学堂。分为文化课、思想课、作战指挥课（少量优秀士兵可以报名，总教官为秦九章）。

“主要是增开思想课程，不能把那些土匪风气带进基地。还有军官学院，我们不仅需要信念坚定的士兵，也需要骁勇善战的将帅。”这是相南里的批注，“另外，也要为还有行动力的残疾退伍军人进行技能培训，安排工作，解决后续生活困难。”

是的，扫盲队终于从工厂走进了部队。他们早上协助农耕，下午训练，晚上还要读书。生活格外充实、忙碌。

战俘营和各部队驻扎的军营很近。但待遇要比士兵们低一些。工作也更沉重。

军团帮忙种田，他们就得去搬砖、和水泥，晚上的思想文化课也要多上一节。

部分穷凶极恶的犯人实在无法改造，第二天就会在医学院的解剖台上看见。

战俘们倒是很少有怨言，好歹基地管饭。

范佩西的心腹和他都不在一座城市，他就算想搞事，也做不到云集响应，揭竿而起。

人的适应性极其可怕。短短几天，他就接受了这样的生活。

范佩西赤裸上身，把铁道枕木在规定的地方钉好。幸存者基地的大基建计划，要在各大城市内部开设铁路。

钉好铁轨，他擦了擦下巴上的汗珠。抬头，看向泛黄的天空。范佩西脚踝上还戴着电子监控器，机器人监工（一个飞盘形状的无人机）正在上空，来回巡视着。

范佩西同样收到了那条人联的大新闻。

现在是战时。

他知道，自己一定会有用的。

……

……

坏消息：人联和神庭开战了，基地还tm的在战区。

好消息：申请的灾后补助款批了，经过核准后，竟有两个亿！

相南里解冻后，还没看见过这么大一笔流动资金。他收到通知时，直接从椅子上蹦了起来。怀疑自己的眼睛。

——卧槽，人联什么时候这么大方了？

但和好消息一起来的，还有人联的通知。

人联方表示，朝廷的赈灾粮虽然批发下来了，但是人联需要在基地内安装一套监察系统，以保证基地没有虚报、瞒报灾情以及公款私用。

当然，这件事并不勉强。但基地方拒绝，呵呵，那么到手一个亿的拨款就会打0.1折发放，变成100万。

地表大大小小的据点这么多，不是谁都有这个待遇的。

人联也是在养出好多只白眼狼后，痛定思痛，制定了这样的策略。

“白眼狼”是人联方的说法。对于一些据点来说，它们也许只是不想给人联打工——人联是总公司，地表据点是分公司。

一些分公司是总公司自己开的，属于嫡系部队，通常位于地下城市的地上部分和某些极端重要的资源区；一些是人联后期收购的，属于干儿子。

有些小公司巴不得人联收购，但持续亏损，一眼看不到未来，人联看不上；有些小公司自己干得蒸蒸日上，才不希望人联来掺一脚，可惜不听话的小公司，在市场竞争中是要被垄断企业打压的，只能含泪卖出原始股。

而各种“扶贫款”、“物资”，就是人联在挥出大棒之前，给的甜枣。

羊毛可以出在未来的羊身上。只要基地成为总部的分公司，那就无所谓前期的投入了，反正都是进自己的口袋。

这笔巨款无疑暗示一件事：经过几次事件，人联提高了对“幸存者基地”的扶持力度和监管等级！

基地终于从可有可无的存在，变成一盘可以下饭的菜了。

相南里看着通知，目瞪口呆：“什么意思？给我办公电脑装病毒呢？”

坐在一边的东方青帝从鼻腔里发出一声冷笑：“让他装。”

小青都发话了，相南里当即跳过一长串的“免责声明”和“授权许可”，选择了同意。

总归Alpha不会害他。

而当人联使用AI办公时，效率无疑是很高的。

半个小时后，这笔钱打到了基地的对公账户上。

神庭的赎金不见踪影，虚拟偶像的众筹款更是不知所云，只有人联AI冰冷的机械声，伴随着电子邮件的字幕，在相南里的耳边响起——

“账户已到账200，000，000信用点。其中，一亿八千万信用点仅能在人联地表扶持商城使用，商城为您打开了二级权限，新增可购买商品171411件。请知悉。”

电子镜片让他能看见一个半透明的人影。

这就是人联目前的主控AI，叫盘古，外观上看，是个沉稳的中年男性，长相很有压迫性。让人想起狮子。

相南里多扫了两眼，感觉还是Alpha帅得多。属于一种男女老少都能欣赏的英俊，盘古长得太爹味了。

不过，网上也搜不到Alpha还在人联工作时的宝贵影像了。

“小青~”相南里拿到钱，兴致勃勃地打开购物商城，“帮我列个购物清单。”

人在思考时，很难面面俱到，但是算力惊人的Ai就不一定了。

但这次，Alpha足足过了三秒，才回复了一个字：“好。”

相南里抬头，扫了他一眼。很意外地发现东方青帝的瞳环居然是亮着的。这代表对方已经先自己一步，进入了工作状态。

东方青帝的工作，显然不是帮忙列购物清单这种事。

他正在遛观测者。

简单来说，人联想把自己的监察系统植入基地内。负责这件事的AI是“观测者”。

如果只是拒绝观测者的侵入，这倒是不难解决，Alpha的系统里有一百个小插件能迅速杀死这个入侵者。但基地显然需要人联的拨款。

因此，Alpha要做的，是在真实的“基地”外，构建出一个虚拟的“基地”。让观测者确信自己观测到的就是真货，这个基地还需要随着现实里基地的扩张而扩张。

这并不是一个简单的工程。
chunks.englishText:
Chapter 148: Human Alliance Aid

Only a few days had passed, and stalks of green-yellow wheat were already poking out of the fields.

This was a new variety improved by the research institute, called "Base No. 1" green wheat, which had been spliced with quite a few xenogeneic genes. The crop yielded well, was resistant to cold and drought, had a short growth cycle, and produced many ears. It had almost no flaws, except that it tasted terrible. However, it could be pulverized into a paste with a "whir" and mixed with sugar and salt.

Xiao Fu patrolled the farmland, muttering, "We haven't even received the final payment for the fungal chickens we sold last time. I wonder if those surface strongholds are still there..."

The submersion of Gusu City by underground magma had multifaceted consequences. Being on the surface did not mean one was safe and sound.

The ground in the area where the city originally stood had directly collapsed. According to the news, the fires ignited underground were still burning to this day. Due to chemical leaks, the groundwater pollution was even more severe; recently, every city in the base had been using melted snow from the mountains for water.

A dark joke: After the destruction of Gusu City, the Human Alliance finally didn't have to worry about the spread of mycelial disease. The funds invested in pathological research were all withdrawn, and pharmaceutical stocks plummeted first. Meanwhile, the stock prices of arms dealers (such as those under the High-Tech Military Industry umbrella) rose steadily.

The legions supporting the main urban area were returning to their original stations one after another.

Then, the soldiers were shocked to discover that military schools had actually been opened in the camps. They were divided into cultural courses, ideological courses, and combat command courses (a small number of outstanding soldiers could enroll, with Qin Jiu Zhang as the chief instructor).

"The main focus is on adding ideological courses; we cannot let those bandit-like tendencies be brought into the base. There is also the Officer Academy; we need not only soldiers with firm beliefs but also brave and battle-hardened generals," this was Xiang Nanli’s annotation. "Additionally, we must provide skills training for disabled veterans who still have mobility, arrange jobs for them, and solve their subsequent living difficulties."

Yes, the literacy teams had finally moved from the factories into the troops. They assisted with farming in the morning, trained in the afternoon, and had to study at night. Life was exceptionally full and busy.

The prisoner-of-war camps were very close to the barracks where the various troops were stationed. However, their treatment was lower than that of the soldiers, and their work was more arduous.

If the legions helped with farming, they had to move bricks and mix cement, and they had to attend an extra session of ideological and cultural classes in the evening.

Some of the most heinous criminals who were truly beyond reform would be seen on the anatomy tables of the medical school the next day.

The prisoners of war rarely complained, though; at least the base provided food.

Van Persie’s henchmen were not in the same city as him, so even if he wanted to stir up trouble, he couldn't rally them to rise in rebellion.

Human adaptability is terrifying. In just a few days, he had accepted this life.

Van Persie, bare-chested, nailed the railway sleepers into the designated spots. The Survivor Base’s grand infrastructure plan aimed to install railways within the major cities.

After nailing the tracks, he wiped the sweat from his chin and looked up at the yellowed sky. Van Persie still wore an electronic monitor on his ankle, and a robot supervisor (a frisbee-shaped drone) was patrolling overhead.

Van Persie had also received that big news from the Human Alliance.

It was wartime now.

He knew he would definitely be of use.

...

...

Bad news: The Human Alliance and the Divine Court had gone to war, and the base was still in the war zone.

Good news: The application for post-disaster subsidies had been approved, and after verification, it amounted to a staggering 200 million!

Since Xiang Nanli had been "unfrozen," he had never seen such a large amount of liquid capital. When he received the notification, he jumped right off his chair, doubting his own eyes.

—*Holy crap, when did the Human Alliance become so generous?*

But along with the good news came a notification from the Human Alliance.

The Alliance stated that although the imperial disaster relief grain had been approved, the Alliance needed to install a monitoring system within the base to ensure that the base did not falsely report or conceal the disaster situation or misappropriate public funds.

Of course, this was not forced. But if the base refused, well, the 100 million in funding they were about to receive would be cut by 99%, becoming a mere 1 million.

With so many large and small strongholds on the surface, not everyone got this kind of treatment.

The Human Alliance had formulated this strategy after being burned by many "ingrates."

"Ingrate" was the Alliance's term. For some strongholds, they perhaps just didn't want to work for the Alliance—the Alliance was the headquarters, and the surface strongholds were the branches.

Some branches were opened by the headquarters itself and belonged to the core troops, usually located in the surface sections of underground cities or in extremely important resource areas; others were acquired by the Alliance later and were considered "adopted sons."

Some small companies were desperate for the Alliance to acquire them, but they were continuously losing money with no future in sight, so the Alliance didn't want them; some small companies were thriving on their own and didn't want the Alliance to interfere. Unfortunately, disobedient small companies would be suppressed by monopolies in market competition and could only tearfully sell their original shares.

And various "poverty alleviation funds" and "supplies" were the sweet carrots the Alliance offered before swinging the big stick.

Wool can always be shorn from future sheep. As long as the base became a branch of the headquarters, the initial investment didn't matter; it would all end up in their own pockets anyway.

This huge sum of money undoubtedly implied one thing: after several incidents, the Human Alliance had increased its level of support and supervision for the "Survivor Base"!

The base had finally transformed from an expendable existence into a dish that could be served at the table.

Xiang Nanli stared at the notification, dumbfounded. "What does this mean? Are they installing a virus on my office computer?"

Dongfang Qingdi, sitting to the side, let out a cold snort from his nose. "Let him install it."

Since Xiao Qing had spoken, Xiang Nanli immediately skipped over the long string of "disclaimers" and "authorizations" and chose to agree.

After all, Alpha wouldn't harm him.

And when the Human Alliance used AI for office work, the efficiency was undoubtedly very high.

Half an hour later, the money hit the base's public account.

There was no sign of the Divine Court's ransom, and the crowdfunding for the virtual idol was even more incomprehensible. Only the cold, mechanical voice of the Human Alliance AI, accompanied by subtitles in the email, echoed in Xiang Nanli's ears—

"200,000,000 credits have been credited to your account. Of this, 180,000,000 credits can only be used in the Human Alliance Surface Support Mall. The mall has opened Level 2 permissions for you, adding 171,411 new purchasable items. Please be advised."

The electronic lens allowed him to see a translucent figure.

This was the Human Alliance’s current master AI, named Pangu. In appearance, he was a composed middle-aged man with a very oppressive look. It made one think of a lion.

Xiang Nanli glanced at him a few more times and felt that Alpha was still much more handsome. It was a type of handsomeness that men, women, old, and young could appreciate; Pangu looked too "fatherly."

However, one couldn't find any precious footage of Alpha when he was still working for the Human Alliance online.

"Xiao Qing~" Once Xiang Nanli got the money, he excitedly opened the shopping mall. "Help me make a shopping list."

When a person is thinking, it is hard to be thorough, but an AI with astonishing computing power is a different story.

But this time, Alpha took a full three seconds before replying with one word: "Okay."

Xiang Nanli looked up and scanned him. He was very surprised to find that Dongfang Qingdi’s pupil rings were actually glowing. This meant the other party had entered a working state one step ahead of him.

Dongfang Qingdi’s work was clearly not something like helping to make a shopping list.

He was walking the "Observer."

Simply put, the Human Alliance wanted to plant its monitoring system within the base. The AI responsible for this was the "Observer."

If it were just about refusing the Observer’s intrusion, that wouldn't be hard to solve; Alpha’s system had a hundred small plugins that could quickly kill this intruder. But the base clearly needed the Alliance's funding.

Therefore, what Alpha had to do was to construct a virtual "base" outside the real "base." He had to make the Observer believe that what it was observing was the real thing, and this base also needed to expand as the real base expanded.

This was not a simple project.

chunks.chineseText:
Alpha甚至不得不借助于自己被困在电子监狱里的本体。

本末倒置。Alpha挺想放弃一切跟着相南里走的，他已经找到家了。可惜，在掌控权柄的同时，他也被权柄所掌控。

虚假的数据洪流平地而起，一串串数据闪烁着，搭建起巨大的高塔。

这就是“基地”的数据库了。

观测者的外观是一只绿色的眼睛。

它进入塔内。很快，一只只巨大的眼球如同蠕虫一样迅速繁殖，它们破墙而出，仿佛本身就是塔的一部分。

观测者平静的看着塔内闪过的数据。一只只数据构成的白鸽，在空寂的塔内灵动地飞舞。经过复杂的解析，这些白鸽能翻译出不同的信号。

从此，基地内的一切都在监测中。

包括那个坐在办公桌前，低垂着头颅工作的年轻人。

对方也有一双碧绿的眼珠，浓郁、通透，像昂贵的帝王绿，是此次观察的重要目标。

[人联 is watching you.]

……

相南里吩咐完工作，打开了基地内部的工作账号，用秘书（黄枫）的名义，给各个部门发去了通知，让他们把需要的物资、拨款都列出来。预算根据部门职能的不同，在50万到500万之间。

吃钱大头显然是研发部门，然而城建部门也不容小觑。负责人表示，随着新一批难民的涌入，考虑到基地的出生率，现有城市必须在5年内再扩建一倍，以满足市民日益增长的物质需求。

人口一多，水、粮、卫生甚至纯净的空气，又成了新一轮问题。

相南里看了一下列表里密密麻麻的工作请示，再度感觉到了头疼。

他很想一股脑塞给东方青帝，然后把自己关在工作室里，捣鼓他喜欢的小机器和C语言（目前已经更新到了N语言版本）；但理智制止了他。

人还是要发挥自己的主观能动性的，不能遇到问题就依靠人工智能。

基地在成长，他也需要成长。

他还挺怕Alpha突然很霸总地说“跟我回智械军团享福”吧。

种田，修路，开学，建厂，科研，采购，出席会议。

过于忙碌的时候，相南里做梦都在开会。而Alpha也被迫习惯了这样的节奏。

如果相南里没有特别安排工作，他会代替黄枫，当相南里的贴身秘书兼警卫员。不为什么，就为了多呆一会。

东方青帝对此的解释是“充电”。

牵手是为了充电。

拥抱也是。

接吻肯定更是了。

也不知道有没有充上百分之一。但他说是就是吧，相南里也不想深究。

。

十月就这么过去了。
chunks.englishText:
Alpha even had to resort to his own main body, which was trapped in an electronic prison.

Putting the cart before the horse. Alpha really wanted to give up everything and follow Xiang Nanli; he had already found a home. Unfortunately, while wielding power, he was also controlled by it.

A false torrent of data rose from the ground, strings of data flickering as they built a massive tower.

This was the "base's" database.

The Observer’s appearance was that of a green eye.

It entered the tower. Soon, giant eyeballs began to breed rapidly like worms, breaking through the walls as if they were part of the tower itself.

The Observer watched the data flashing inside the tower calmly. White doves made of data fluttered nimbly in the empty, silent tower. Through complex analysis, these white doves could translate different signals.

From then on, everything in the base was under surveillance.

Including the young man sitting at the desk, working with his head bowed.

The other party also had a pair of emerald eyes, rich and transparent, like expensive imperial jade—the important target of this observation.

[Human Alliance is watching you.]

...

After Xiang Nanli finished delegating the work, he opened the base's internal work account and, in the name of his secretary (Huang Feng), sent out notifications to various departments, asking them to list the supplies and funding they needed. The budget ranged from 500,000 to 5 million, depending on the department's functions.

The biggest money pit was clearly the R&D department, but the urban construction department could not be underestimated either. The person in charge stated that with the influx of a new batch of refugees, and considering the base's birth rate, the existing city had to be expanded by another fold within 5 years to meet the citizens' growing material needs.

Once the population increased, water, food, sanitation, and even pure air became a new round of problems.

Xiang Nanli looked at the dense list of work requests and felt a headache coming on again.

He really wanted to dump it all on Dongfang Qingdi and then lock himself in the studio, tinkering with his favorite small machines and C-language (which had already been updated to the N-language version); but reason stopped him.

People still need to exert their own subjective initiative; they cannot rely on artificial intelligence whenever they encounter a problem.

The base was growing, and he needed to grow too.

He was also quite afraid that Alpha would suddenly say in a domineering CEO tone, "Come back to the Machina Legion with me to enjoy life."

Farming, road repair, opening schools, building factories, scientific research, procurement, attending meetings.

When he was too busy, Xiang Nanli would even have meetings in his dreams. And Alpha was forced to get used to this rhythm.

If Xiang Nanli didn't have any special work arranged, he would take the place of Huang Feng and act as Xiang Nanli’s personal secretary and bodyguard. Not for any particular reason, just to stay a little longer.

Dongfang Qingdi’s explanation for this was "charging."

Holding hands was for charging.

Hugging was too.

Kissing was definitely for that as well.

He didn't know if he had even charged up one percent. But if he said it was, then it was; Xiang Nanli didn't want to get to the bottom of it.

.

October passed just like that.

chunks.chineseText:
第149章 机械太监

这是一座漂浮在半空的城池，表面有一层隐形涂料，听说是什么晶体技术。

大多时候，这里看上去空无一物。

但只要你拥有神庭的信物，就能凭借肉眼看见一座宏伟的城池。

金色的光柱贯穿天域，这座圣城高低错落，气势恢宏，由一座座岛屿构成，岛和岛之间，金色的瀑布流淌着。

当你凝望这座由大理石、白石膏、鲜花、喷泉构成的城市时，一切的烦恼似乎都不复存在。

“陛下。”

昏暗的祷告室内，年轻的男人面朝墙壁，单膝跪下，背脊笔直。

他的头发是金色的，又长又直，几乎能拖到地上。

长发间有许多昂贵的宝石、绸缎作为点缀；除此外，耳朵上也有许多配饰——每当战胜某位强大的对手，米迦勒总会从敌人的尸体上取点东西下来，做成装饰品。然后看心情使用。

他最恨的那个人还活着。但对方的眼珠子被煅烧成了红宝石一样的乳钉，佩戴在他的胸口。

米迦勒认为，胸前灼烧的痛感能让他记得复仇和耻辱。

他面前是一片深邃的黑。黑暗中，隐约有沉闷的呼吸声，像是怪物喘着粗气。

被称为“陛下”的怪物缓慢地回答：“是米迦勒吗？你来看我了，有什么事吗？请说。”

“陛下，人联安逸日子过得不舒坦，又在找借口向神庭宣战。我认为是时候给他们一点教训了。”米迦勒的手扣在胸前，微微低垂着头，“除此外，加百列殉教了。在殉教前，他发来简报，希望将自己的遗产的十分之一赠与一名叫黄枫的智械；剩下十分之九，收归神庭。”

神座的声音有些许迷惑，随后用一种很缓慢地语调回忆着：“加百列……噢。加百列。我们的小弟弟。”

神座没有理会第一条讯息，而是在沉默数秒后，用一种悲伤无比的语调说着：“既然是他的遗愿，那就随他去吧。加百列已经够辛苦了。但是教会还没有选出新的‘加百列’。看来那台加百列只能暂时休眠了。是什么让他回归了神的怀抱？”

米迦勒的眉毛蹙起，大概是不赞同加百列的做法：“他本来就很虚弱了，我们把利维坦划给了他，那里的信仰很纯粹，适合疗养。可他居然还要偷偷跑出自己的‘牧场’，这件事让我们元老院的人非常生气，甚至想要褫夺他的封号。”

我们……噢，我们。米迦勒已经站到对面那堆人的中间去了。

“我最近总是很不安。之前要占领阴山城的时候，我都没有这么频繁地做梦。”神座几乎要流泪了，“米迦勒，我们的同辈一个个死去，是否我也到了魂归神国的时候？我最近总是看不清东西，思维也很缓慢。我的身体也很疼。”

他咳嗽起来，圣堂内，怪物巨大的节肢恶心的蠕动着。

随着它的咳嗽，整座城市都发出了轻微的摇晃。住在这里的人见怪不怪。

“您不会死的。您是神庭的神座。”米迦勒的眼神飘忽着。

您被神庭一代代的饲养，已经非常硕大了。

米迦勒：“总之，请让我总领这次和人联的战役。我会把胜利带回圣城。”

神座低声回答，像是快睡着了一样，喃喃着：“我也没有拒绝的权利，不是吗？米迦勒。你是天使长，是和神最相似的存在……去罢。去复仇。”

*

最近天气又变冷了，昨天下了场雨。早上，树木和房檐上就挂起了冰棱。

相南里第一时间关注了城里的农田。现在正是青麦成长的关键期。好在户外的大棚搭的很及时，几乎没有受损。

农业部长小福骄傲地在耳麦里邀功：“永恒市的主体不是已经激活了吗！小福现在有自己的天气检测系统！前天就给农业部的干部预警了！”

是的，相南里没办法面面俱到。

他是人，精力有限，一天就是24小时。还必须保证8小时的睡眠时间。

要知道，八小时的睡眠时间，还是相南里据理力争后才争取到的福利！Alpha竟然觉得他应该每天睡十个小时，如果生理上主观做不到，他可以提供电疗——这tm是人话吗？

但好在，他还有许多志同道合的伙伴，在他没有关注到的地方默默努力着。每个人都是。

相南里在第二时间，关注了他的畸变人朋友。

他给畸变人住的小树林加装了电热设备。电线从主城区铺的。新来那么多劳改犯，闲着也是闲着。

畸变人新陈代谢迅速，内部体温高，很少被地表的低温冻伤，但并不代表它们不冷。

有一半畸变人，在过去一个月，陆陆续续回到了熟悉的永恒市大森林。

剩下一半留在了雪山。

面对询问，以西结迟疑地回答：“因为气候变暖，再加上食物充足环境安全。现在明明不是春夏，但还是有部分畸变人选择了繁衍后代……我让怀孕的畸变人留在更安全的地方了。”

相南里心想，那明年岂不是能看见很多小畸变人？

相南里对畸变人的繁殖方式很好奇。

以西结被他缠得受不了，只好不情不愿地告诉他，畸变人会分成四个种类，是因为四个物种之间有生殖隔离。像爬行者和潜伏者，就是卵生；狂暴者和撕裂者，就是胎生。

“因为基因混乱，有些畸变人是单性，有些是双性……而且它们并没有人类社会的道德伦理观，所以有些爬行者会既是爸爸也是妈妈。”

相南里完全一副好奇宝宝的样子，纯洁地询问：“那你是单性还是双性呢？”

他总觉得以西结的胸肌很大块呢，穿着衣服也鼓鼓的~

说完，忍不住伸出手，拍了拍以西结油光水滑的长尾巴。

“我当然是——”

以西结说不下去了，恼羞成怒地嘶鸣了一声，耳朵红红的窜上大树，跑掉了。

相南里只好摇头晃脑地回家：“小智，畸变人怎么还会害羞。还怪可爱的。”

[……]

要回家吃午饭，相南里在门口，补充道：“对了，今天的事不要告诉小青噢。”

小智：[……哔哔。嘟、嘟嘟。叽。]

这宛如乱码一样的杂音是怎么回事？

相南里突然有了不好的预感。

这种预感在推门，看见系着围裙坐在饭桌前等他的Alpha时，成了真。

唇角紧绷，眉眼淡淡的。智械人的表情很少，情绪激烈的瞬间一只手都能数出来。但他们都认识这么多年了！相南里一眼就能看出来，东方青帝不怎么高兴。

相南里在极短的时间内回忆了自己手头的任务，试图寻找出几件要紧的、必须要马上处理的事。然后找借口出门加班。

可惜他平时太勤快了，根本没有堆积到必须要现在完成的工作。

他想，自己确实不能像装死的丈夫一样，用工作来逃避问题！

更何况小青今天还做了他最喜欢的豆豉蒸排骨和辣子鸡。

鸡还是自家院子养的！相南里没有要求过什么特权，但他想要，Alpha总能给他找到的。
chunks.englishText:
Chapter 149: The Mechanical Eunuch

This was a city floating in mid-air, its surface covered in a layer of stealth coating—I heard it was some kind of crystal technology.

Most of the time, it looked like there was nothing there.

But as long as you possessed a token of the Divine Court, you could see a magnificent city with the naked eye.

Golden pillars of light pierced the heavens. This holy city was composed of islands at varying heights, creating a grand and imposing atmosphere, with golden waterfalls flowing between the islands.

When you gazed at this city made of marble, white plaster, flowers, and fountains, all your troubles seemed to vanish.

"Your Majesty."

In the dim prayer room, a young man faced the wall, kneeling on one knee with his back straight.

His hair was golden, long and straight, almost dragging on the ground.

Interspersed throughout his long hair were many expensive gemstones and silks; besides that, there were many accessories on his ears—every time he defeated a powerful opponent, Michael would take something from the enemy's corpse and turn it into an ornament. Then, he would use it depending on his mood.

The person he hated most was still alive. But that person's eyeballs had been calcined into ruby-like nipple piercings, which he wore on his chest.

Michael believed that the burning pain on his chest would help him remember his revenge and his humiliation.

Before him was a deep darkness. In the darkness, there was a faint, heavy sound of breathing, like a monster gasping for air.

The monster referred to as "Your Majesty" replied slowly: "Is that you, Michael? You've come to see me. Is there something the matter? Please, speak."

"Your Majesty, the Human Alliance is not content with their comfortable life and is again finding excuses to declare war on the Divine Court. I believe it is time to teach them a lesson." Michael’s hand was clasped over his chest, his head bowed slightly. "Besides that, Gabriel has martyred himself. Before his martyrdom, he sent a briefing, hoping to gift one-tenth of his legacy to a Machina named Huang Feng; the remaining nine-tenths are to be returned to the Divine Court."

The voice from the throne sounded slightly confused, and then it recalled in a very slow tone: "Gabriel... Oh. Gabriel. Our little brother."

The throne ignored the first message, and after a few seconds of silence, said in an incomparably sorrowful tone: "Since it is his dying wish, then let it be. Gabriel has suffered enough. But the Church has not yet chosen a new 'Gabriel.' It seems that the Gabriel unit can only be put into temporary hibernation. What caused him to return to the embrace of God?"

Michael’s eyebrows furrowed, presumably disapproving of Gabriel’s actions: "He was already very weak. We assigned Leviathan to him; the faith there is pure and suitable for recuperation. Yet he actually snuck out of his own 'pasture.' This matter made the people in our Senate very angry; they even wanted to strip him of his title."

*We*... Oh, *we*. Michael had already stood among that group of people on the other side.

"I have been very uneasy lately. Even before we were going to occupy Yinshan City, I didn't have dreams this frequently." The throne was almost weeping. "Michael, our peers are dying one by one. Has the time come for me to return to the Kingdom of God? I haven't been able to see clearly lately, and my thinking is very slow. My body hurts, too."

He began to cough, and within the sanctuary, the monster’s massive arthropod limbs writhed disgustingly.

With his coughing, the entire city swayed slightly. The people living here were long used to it.

"You will not die. You are the Throne of the Divine Court." Michael’s eyes drifted.

*You have been raised by generation after generation of the Divine Court, and you have become very bloated.*

Michael: "In any case, please let me lead this campaign against the Human Alliance. I will bring victory back to the Holy City."

The throne replied in a low voice, as if he were about to fall asleep, muttering: "I don't have the right to refuse, do I? Michael. You are the Archangel, the existence most similar to God... Go. Go and take your revenge."

*

The weather had turned cold again recently, and it rained yesterday. By morning, icicles were hanging from the trees and eaves.

Xiang Nanli paid attention to the city's farmland first thing. Now was the critical period for the green wheat to grow. Fortunately, the outdoor greenhouses had been set up in time and were almost undamaged.

The Minister of Agriculture, Xiao Fu, proudly claimed credit in the earpiece: "The main body of Eternal City has already been activated! Xiao Fu now has his own weather detection system! I gave the agricultural department cadres a warning the day before yesterday!"

Yes, Xiang Nanli couldn't be everywhere at once.

He was human, his energy was limited, and a day only had 24 hours. He also had to ensure 8 hours of sleep.

And mind you, those eight hours of sleep were a benefit Xiang Nanli had fought tooth and nail to secure! Alpha actually thought he should sleep ten hours a day, and if he couldn't do it subjectively, he could provide electrotherapy—was that even human talk?

But fortunately, he had many like-minded partners who were silently working hard in places he hadn't noticed. Everyone was.

Xiang Nanli paid attention to his mutant friends second.

He had installed electric heating equipment in the small woods where the mutants lived. The wires were laid from the main urban area. With so many new reform-through-labor prisoners, they might as well be put to work.

Mutants had a rapid metabolism and a high internal body temperature, so they were rarely frostbitten by the surface's low temperatures, but that didn't mean they didn't feel the cold.

Half of the mutants had returned to the familiar Eternal City forest over the past month.

The other half remained on the snowy mountains.

When asked, Ezekiel replied hesitantly: "Because the climate is warming, and there is plenty of food and a safe environment. Even though it is clearly not spring or summer, some mutants have chosen to reproduce... I have let the pregnant mutants stay in safer places."

Xiang Nanli thought to himself: *Doesn't that mean I'll be able to see many little mutants next year?*

Xiang Nanli was very curious about the mutants' reproductive methods.

Ezekiel couldn't stand being pestered by him and had to tell him, reluctantly, that mutants were divided into four types because there was reproductive isolation between the four species. Like Crawlers and Lurkers, they were oviparous; Berserkers and Rippers were viviparous.

"Because of the chaotic genes, some mutants are asexual, some are hermaphroditic... and they don't have the moral and ethical concepts of human society, so some Crawlers can be both father and mother."

Xiang Nanli was completely like a curious baby, asking innocently: "Then are you asexual or hermaphroditic?"

He always felt Ezekiel’s pectoral muscles were very large, and they looked bulky even under his clothes~

After saying this, he couldn't help but reach out and pat Ezekiel’s sleek, shiny long tail.

"I am, of course—"

Ezekiel couldn't go on; he hissed in embarrassment and anger, his ears turning red as he scrambled up a big tree and ran away.

Xiang Nanli had no choice but to shake his head and walk home: "Xiao Zhi, how can a mutant be shy? It’s kind of cute."

[......]

About to go home for lunch, Xiang Nanli added at the door: "By the way, don't tell Xiao Qing about today's events."

Xiao Zhi: [......Beep. Doo, doo-doo. Chirp.]

What was with this garbled noise?

Xiang Nanli suddenly had a bad premonition.

This premonition became reality when he pushed the door open and saw Alpha sitting at the dining table in an apron, waiting for him.

His lips were tight, his expression faint. Machina had few expressions, and the moments of intense emotion could be counted on one hand. But they had known each other for so many years! Xiang Nanli could tell at a glance that Dongfang Qingdi was not very happy.

Xiang Nanli recalled the tasks on his hands in a split second, trying to find a few urgent matters that had to be dealt with immediately. Then he would find an excuse to go out and work overtime.

Unfortunately, he was usually too diligent, and there was simply no work piled up that had to be completed right now.

He thought, *I really can't be like a husband playing dead, using work to escape problems!*

What's more, Xiao Qing had even made his favorite steamed pork ribs with fermented black beans and spicy chicken today.

The chicken was even raised in their own yard! Xiang Nanli had never asked for any special privileges, but if he wanted something, Alpha could always find it for him.

chunks.chineseText:
“小青。”他笑眯眯地走过去，手搭在了Alpha的肩上。

相南里弯腰，先是嗅了嗅他头发的香味（通常是无味的，但Alpha会偷偷喷香水），然后撒娇一样用自己的脸去蹭了蹭他的脸：“做饭辛苦了，好喜欢吃你做的饭。”

世界上的家政机器人那么多，他喜欢吃我做的饭，缩写一下，那不就是喜欢我。

……等等，他好像不是家政机器人。

Alpha还是很好哄的，表情很快由阴转晴。

要是让人联的政敌知道他私底下竟然是这种不值钱的样子，估计能笑死。

但他又能怎么办呢？跟相南里发火吗？东方青帝的确不高兴，可是，相南里的心就跟明镜台似的。发火解决不了任何问题。

本来无一物，何处惹尘埃。

东方青帝面色不怎么好看地开口：“以西结喜欢你。”

相南里一愣：“我知道。”

太过分了吧！知道还这么玩。

畸变人的命也是命。

智械人的心也是心啊！

东方青帝说：“我也喜欢你。我爱你。”

Alpha说这话的时候很流畅，就像是演习过千百次一样，没有任何的滞涩。

他和相南里勇敢无畏地对视。果然从对方的眼神中看见了一些茫然和迟疑：“……我也知道。”

东方青帝捧着相南里的脸，逼问：“这两个知道，对你而言，有什么不同吗？”

相南里却在此时有点走神。毕竟小青的脸离他这么近。

身体造价八万亿，大约有一万亿是花在脸上的吧。

人的情绪太复杂了，对相南里来说，像一道很难搞的数学题。

Alpha出的题他解不出来，但他也不愿意敷衍和回避。

“当然不一样。小青，我只想吻你。”

于是相南里得到了一个吻，他忍不住在东方青帝的怀里笑出了声。

“我爱你。”

Alpha急切地吻着他，仿佛这是这具身体存在的唯一目的。他咬着相南里的下巴，又开始往下，咬他的脖子和喉结。相南里的回应是闷闷的笑声，他把玩着东方青帝的长发，脖子还有耳垂，像是在溺爱黏人的大狗狗。

但人和狗还是有些不一样的。

起码他不会对狗产生性欲。

有一点害羞，当Alpha的手在几乎没有被外人碰过的地方游走时。不需要照镜子，脸上的温度已经烫得像是发烧。

他握住了Alpha的手腕，但反抗的力道很不坚定。

爱，和权力、财富、美貌，都毫无关系的东西。得到它的唯一条件是幸运。

相南里觉得自己从小到大都挺倒霉的，在家父母不爱；读书时进的不属于自己圈层的贵族公学，又在那享受了六年的孤立；成年后强迫自己背了很多书，他看新闻、看小说、看电视剧、看心理学专业书，观察身边最受喜欢的同学，于是终于有了个人样子。

相南里不够幸运，所以必须加倍努力。强悍的天赋是命运赠与他的补偿。

他得到了尊敬、成就、长辈的欣赏、同辈的仰望、后辈的崇敬。可这不是他要的那种爱啊。

“我爱你。”

奇怪的地方被含住的时候，他听见Alpha这么说。不知道是否是他的错觉，正常情况下，小青发不了声才对。

相南里摸着东方青帝的头发，像飘浮在天上，很快，轻微的胀痛把他从天上拉回地底。

但这点不适应消失的很快。

相南里是巨婴。

他就要确定的、不会更改的、独一无二、纯粹的爱。

他回答道：“我也爱你。”

我的爱人，我最完美的作品。

相南里和东方青帝玩了个双人做饭小游戏，从白天玩到了晚上。好在他喝过很多基因药，并没有出现头晕眼花的情况。

就是相南里有些纳闷，为什么小青这么熟练？

而且小青吃相也太凶了，像是要剥开皮从里到外舔一遍。

相南里想，之前看电视剧，太监就挺变态的，有社会学和心理学的双重佐证。

小青就是机械太监。

改天还是得把东西装上，让他当个完整的男人吧。

相南里摸过了，那里确实有个预留槽位。就是小青比较小气，不肯给他多摸。

而且那个预留槽位的直径不对劲。

相南里实在不能接受550ml的矿泉水瓶。

但如果真要安装，是不是能合理拆卸东方青帝的身体了？他想这么做很久了。

相南里眼睛慢悠悠地闭上，突然垂死病中惊坐起：“工作。我的工作邮件还没看！”

“安排好了。”东方青帝把他摁了回去，“没什么重要的事。睡。”
chunks.englishText:
"Xiao Qing." He walked over with a beaming smile, resting his hand on the Alpha's shoulder.

Xiang Nanli leaned down, first sniffing the scent of his hair (usually odorless, but the Alpha would secretly spray perfume), then nuzzling his face against his own like a spoiled pet: "Cooking is hard work. I love the food you make."

There are so many domestic robots in the world; if he likes the food I make, to put it simply, doesn't that mean he likes me?

...Wait, he doesn't seem to be a domestic robot.

The Alpha was still easy to coax; his expression shifted from overcast to sunny in an instant.

If the political enemies of the Human Alliance knew that he was this "cheap" in private, they would probably laugh themselves to death.

But what could he do? Get angry at Xiang Nanli? Dongfang Qingdi was indeed unhappy, but Xiang Nanli’s heart was like a clear, polished mirror. Getting angry wouldn't solve anything.

*Originally, there is nothing at all; where could the dust settle?*

Dongfang Qingdi spoke with a sullen expression: "Ezekiel likes you."

Xiang Nanli was stunned: "I know."

That’s too much! Knowing that and still playing these games.

The lives of mutants are lives, too.

The hearts of mechanical beings are hearts, too!

Dongfang Qingdi said: "I like you, too. I love you."

The Alpha said this as fluently as if he had rehearsed it a thousand times, without a single stutter.

He looked into Xiang Nanli's eyes, brave and fearless. Sure enough, he saw a trace of bewilderment and hesitation in the other's gaze: "...I know that, too."

Dongfang Qingdi cupped Xiang Nanli's face, pressing him: "These two 'I knows'—to you, is there any difference?"

Xiang Nanli, however, was a bit distracted at this moment. After all, Xiao Qing's face was so close to his.

His body cost eight trillion; about one trillion must have been spent just on his face.

Human emotions are too complex; to Xiang Nanli, they were like a difficult math problem.

He couldn't solve the problem the Alpha posed, but he wasn't willing to be perfunctory or evasive either.

"Of course it's different. Xiao Qing, I just want to kiss you."

And so, Xiang Nanli received a kiss, and he couldn't help but laugh out loud in Dongfang Qingdi's arms.

"I love you."

The Alpha kissed him eagerly, as if this were the sole purpose for his body's existence. He bit at Xiang Nanli's chin, then began to move downward, biting his neck and Adam's apple. Xiang Nanli’s response was a muffled laugh; he toyed with Dongfang Qingdi's long hair, his neck, and his earlobes, as if doting on a clingy, oversized dog.

But humans and dogs are still somewhat different.

At the very least, he wouldn't feel sexual desire for a dog.

He felt a bit shy when the Alpha's hand wandered into places that had almost never been touched by outsiders. He didn't need to look in a mirror; the temperature on his face was already burning as if he had a fever.

He gripped the Alpha's wrist, but his resistance was far from firm.

Love has nothing to do with power, wealth, or beauty. The only condition for obtaining it is luck.

Xiang Nanli felt that he had been quite unlucky since he was a child; his parents didn't love him at home. When he went to school, he entered an aristocratic academy that didn't belong to his social stratum, where he enjoyed six years of isolation. After becoming an adult, he forced himself to read a lot of books. He watched news, novels, TV series, and psychology textbooks, observing the most popular classmates around him, and finally, he looked like a real person.

Xiang Nanli wasn't lucky enough, so he had to work twice as hard. His formidable talent was the compensation fate granted him.

He gained respect, achievement, the appreciation of his elders, the admiration of his peers, and the reverence of his juniors. But this wasn't the kind of love he wanted.

"I love you."

When a strange place was taken into his mouth, he heard the Alpha say this. He didn't know if it was his imagination, but under normal circumstances, Xiao Qing shouldn't be able to make a sound.

Xiang Nanli stroked Dongfang Qingdi's hair, feeling as if he were floating in the sky. Soon, a slight, throbbing pain pulled him back from the sky to the ground.

But this slight discomfort vanished quickly.

Xiang Nanli was a giant baby.

He wanted a certain, unchanging, unique, and pure love.

He replied: "I love you, too."

My lover, my most perfect creation.

Xiang Nanli and Dongfang Qingdi played a two-person cooking game that lasted from day until night. Fortunately, he had taken many genetic drugs, so he didn't experience any dizziness or blurred vision.

It was just that Xiang Nanli was a bit puzzled: why was Xiao Qing so skilled?

And Xiao Qing's way of eating was too fierce, as if he wanted to peel off his skin and lick him from the inside out.

Xiang Nanli thought that in the TV shows he had watched, eunuchs were quite perverted—there was both sociological and psychological evidence for that.

Xiao Qing was a mechanical eunuch.

He should install the parts another day and let him be a complete man.

Xiang Nanli had touched it; there was indeed a reserved slot there. It was just that Xiao Qing was quite stingy and wouldn't let him touch it much.

Moreover, the diameter of that reserved slot was a bit strange.

Xiang Nanli really couldn't accept a 550ml mineral water bottle.

But if he really installed it, would he be able to reasonably dismantle Dongfang Qingdi's body? He had wanted to do that for a long time.

Xiang Nanli's eyes slowly closed, then he suddenly sat up as if rising from the dead: "Work. I haven't checked my work emails yet!"

"It's all arranged." Dongfang Qingdi pressed him back down. "Nothing important. Sleep."

chunks.chineseText:
第150章 皇帝

第二天醒来，难免有些腿软腰子疼。

“我觉得这种事要节制。”相南里窝在床上，伸出胳膊，看着东方青帝给他套衣服，“老房子着火也不能烧成这样吧。你说我今年都五十了，要不是基因药骨质都开始疏松，你还……”

东方青帝是很乐意听相南里说话的，相南里的声音是那种很清亮的青年音，年龄不超过二十三，很有活力，听上去就是阳光开朗的大帅哥。

喘起来的时候更很好听，既不克制也不放荡，完全是自然流露。急得东方青帝小脑控制大脑，差点打开军团内网，立刻网购一个零件。

但此时他选择捂住这张嘴。再让相南里叭叭下去，颅内电压又要升高了。

相南里坏心眼地舔了一下他的掌心。

东方青帝像触电一样，条件反射性地收回手。

纸上得来终觉浅。人工智能拼命看黄文，也比不上天然魅魔的灵机一动。

相南里得到了说话的机会，继续苦口婆心道：“你看我这里都肿了。你都没装零件，搞这么凶干嘛。”

东方青帝迅速扫过他胸前，随后收回目光。

是很红。

东方青帝认真反思了自己的行为，积极认错：“我下次注意。”但坚决不改。

他太迷恋相南里失控的神态了。相南里封闭的心灵和身体都打开一个口子，在邀请他进去。

能忍住的是这个↑，他是这个↓。

相南里劝说失败，被伺候好穿完衣服和鞋袜，吃完早饭，终于打开了被冷落一天的工作邮件。

Alpha想做妲己，他可不能当纣王。

优先度排第一的邮件，来自距离基地700公里的地表据点。

这个据点叫奥丁城，人口150万。旁边就是矿山，之前一次性订购了十万只菌鸡，属于不差钱的大客户。

奥丁城建在矿山内，算半个地下城市。因此，受到地质灾害的影响远比一般据点严重。

[司令，您好。前些日子收到了您的电报……实不相瞒，因为之前那场大家都知道的事故，我们城市坍塌大半，还遇到了流民哄抢物资，并且城外的异种也在此时选择了攻城。我的父亲就是那时候去世的。我们花费了一些时间，才恢复通讯技术……现在，我所在的这支队伍还剩174人。如果您愿意收留我们这些无家可归之人，实在感激不尽。我愿意献上奥丁城掌握的D级专利。想必您有所耳闻，这也是奥丁城曾经雄踞一方的仰仗。]

这段时间，相南里收到的投靠信数不胜数。但奥丁城还是有些不同的。

姑苏城单独给奥丁城修了公路。

能享有这种殊荣，只能说明它不仅祖上阔过，现在发展的也很是不错；远超其他后爹养的东西。光从人口上看，也能窥见一二。这可是百万人的大城市，基地到现在，人口也还不到它的零头。

相南里往后翻了一页，写信人很贴心地附上专利链接。

他联网，打开一看，先跳出来的居然是人联论文网的页面。

论文标题很粗暴：[传统矿石能源在新型机械中的应用（煤矿电池）]

作者：奥丁

专利：煤矿电池（D级）

浏览：27

引用：4

人联内部的专利评级，SABCDE六个等级。评级不仅看专利的难度，也看创造的价值和未来的前景。

人联非常热衷于构建知识壁垒和技术鸿沟，以此形成长期垄断。

第一梯队的技术永远掌握在各大企业的手中。也是靠着这些专利，企业才能躺在金山上持续收割。

如果相南里把自己的论文拿去申请专利，也是能评级的，可惜他选择的是共享。

他要是多发几篇，也许还能进人联的人才库，享受一点特权。

相南里登录账号，想要点进论文一探究竟，但界面无情地跳出弹窗：“抱歉，未检测到用户权限，请先购买专利。”

[是否支付：7，000，000 信用点？]

卧槽，七百万？！这么贵？这还是只是D级技术！而人联的专利库往上还有SABC四个等级呢！

相南里突然福至心灵：“小青，我上次传到网站的论文，要是申请专利，能赚多少？”

东方青帝：“C级，两千万左右。”

相南里的心脏突然绞痛了起来：“……你居然不提醒我？！”

这就是知识的力量吗？

小青幽幽回答：“不是你说科技不当被垄断，成果应为全人类共享的吗？”

相南里心想他确实说过，但主要还是不知道专利竟然如此赚钱。

基地目前在草创阶段，哪哪都需要钱。得富裕了才能分享，不能打肿脸充胖子啊！

相南里打开自己个人后台，看向唯一发表的那篇论文——

《RN-7活性金属高效利用操作方式》

浏览：71417

引用：1

相南里：“……”

他粗略算了一下钱，突然心痛到无法呼吸。

浏览量这么多当然是因为它免费。不管需不需要，白嫖是人的天性。

短短几个月，就有引用数量；说明确实有人研究并付出行动。

网站的后台还有一条短信。

相南里扫了眼，收信时间是三个月前，就是他发完论文的第六天。

发件人为高新军工，官号，有认证标。

对方表示，亲爱的朋友，您好，您的论文研究方向和我司137号研究所重合了！经过开会讨论，我们决定向您发放高新军工的offer，底薪九万带年底虚拟股权分红（工作时间为下午2点到5点，有加班费），包转户口（137研究所在长安城），包食堂和住宿。入职即颁发人联P3等级学者证。有意请联系xxxxx（137研究所所长）。

如果进行一下市场调研，相南里就会知道，这份工作给的薪酬相当优渥。尤其是分房子给户口。

从姑苏到长安，放在相南里那个年代，相当于从非洲到了北欧。

大企业对自己青睐的工蚁，还是很大方的。

不过，相南里是不会吃下这颗糖衣炮弹的！基地还有几十万人嗷嗷待哺，他怎么可能跑去上班。给再多钱也不过是想赚他的剩余价值罢了。

但相南里还是添加了所长的联系方式，以备不时之需。

他长吁短叹地关闭网站，开始回复来自奥丁城的邮件：“亲爱的朋友，很荣幸成为你们信赖的伙伴，基地的大门随时为您敞开……”

东方青帝在此时提醒：“对方是在寻求政治庇护。”

“哈？”

“城主的儿子不留在自己父亲的地盘，反而带着少量亲信和专利来外地。要么奥丁城已经彻底毁灭，原住民近乎全灭，无法重建城市；要么就是他在剧变中失去政治地位，不得不离开。”东方青帝揉碎了跟他解释，“你可以收留他，但要弄清楚可能存在的风险。”

基地目前能源主要还是靠地热能转换。

但地热塔只有一座。随着基地经济发展，人口剧增，工业化加深……能源储备不可避免的短缺。

Chapter 150: The Emperor (Part 1)

Waking up the next day, it was inevitable to have weak legs and a sore lower back.

"I think we should exercise some restraint with this kind of thing." Xiang Nanli huddled in bed, stretching out his arm as he watched Dongfang Qingdi put his clothes on for him. "Even if an old house catches fire, it shouldn't burn like this. I'm fifty this year, you know. If it weren't for the genetic drugs, my bones would already be starting to lose density, and you're still..."

Dongfang Qingdi was very happy to listen to Xiang Nanli talk. Xiang Nanli’s voice was that clear, youthful tone—no older than twenty-three, full of vitality, sounding like a bright and cheerful handsome man.

It sounded even better when he was panting—neither restrained nor wanton, just a completely natural outpouring. It made Dongfang Qingdi so anxious that his cerebellum took control of his cerebrum, and he almost opened the Legion's internal network to immediately buy a part online.

But at this moment, he chose to cover that mouth. If he let Xiang Nanli keep babbling, his intracranial voltage would rise again.

Xiang Nanli mischievously licked his palm.

Dongfang Qingdi recoiled as if electrocuted, pulling his hand back by reflex.

*Knowledge gained from books is shallow.* Even if an AI reads all the erotica in the world, it can't compare to the sudden inspiration of a natural succubus.

Xiang Nanli seized the opportunity to speak and continued earnestly: "Look, I'm swollen here. You haven't even installed the parts, why are you being so fierce?"

Dongfang Qingdi quickly swept his gaze over his chest, then withdrew it.

It was very red.

Dongfang Qingdi seriously reflected on his behavior and actively admitted his mistake: "I'll be careful next time." But he was determined not to change.

He was too obsessed with the look of Xiang Nanli losing control. Xiang Nanli’s closed heart and body had opened a crack, inviting him in.

The one who could hold back was *this*↑, but he was *this*↓.

Xiang Nanli’s persuasion failed. After being served while getting dressed and putting on his shoes and socks, and finishing breakfast, he finally opened the work emails that had been neglected for a day.

The Alpha wanted to play Daji, but he couldn't be King Zhou.

The highest-priority email came from a surface outpost 700 kilometers away from the base.

This outpost was called Odin City, with a population of 1.5 million. It was right next to a mine and had previously ordered 100,000 fungal chickens at once; they were a big client that didn't lack money.

Odin City was built inside a mine, making it half an underground city. Therefore, it was far more severely affected by geological disasters than the average outpost.

[Commander, greetings. We received your telegram a few days ago... To be honest, because of that accident everyone knows about, most of our city collapsed, and we encountered refugees looting supplies. Furthermore, the xenomorphs outside the city chose that moment to lay siege. My father died during that time. It took us some time to restore communication technology... Now, the team I am with has 174 people left. If you are willing to take us in, these homeless people, we would be eternally grateful. I am willing to offer the D-grade patent held by Odin City. I presume you have heard of it; it was the reliance that once made Odin City a regional power.]

During this time, Xiang Nanli had received countless letters seeking refuge. But Odin City was somewhat different.

Gusu City had built a road specifically for Odin City.

To enjoy such a privilege, it could only mean that not only had their ancestors been wealthy, but their current development was also quite good—far exceeding the "step-children" of other outposts. One could catch a glimpse of this just by looking at the population. This was a city of a million people; the base, even now, didn't have a fraction of that population.

Xiang Nanli flipped to the next page, and the sender had thoughtfully attached a link to the patent.

He went online and opened it. The first thing that popped up was actually the page for the Human Alliance's academic paper network.

The title of the paper was blunt: [Application of Traditional Mineral Energy in New Mechanical Devices (Coal Mine Batteries)]

Author: Odin

Patent: Coal Mine Battery (D-grade)

Views: 27

Citations: 4

The patent ratings within the Human Alliance were divided into six levels: S, A, B, C, D, and E. The rating depended not only on the difficulty of the patent but also on the value created and future prospects.

The Human Alliance was very keen on building knowledge barriers and technological gaps to form long-term monopolies.

First-tier technology was always held in the hands of major corporations. It was also by relying on these patents that corporations could continue to harvest wealth while lying on mountains of gold.

If Xiang Nanli took his own papers to apply for patents, they could also be rated, but unfortunately, he chose to share them.

If he published a few more, he might even be able to enter the Human Alliance's talent pool and enjoy some privileges.

Xiang Nanli logged into his account, wanting to click into the paper to investigate, but the interface ruthlessly popped up a window: "Sorry, user permissions not detected. Please purchase the patent first."

[Pay: 7,000,000 Credits?]

*What the hell, seven million?!* So expensive? And this was only D-grade technology! The Human Alliance's patent library still had S, A, B, and C levels above it!

Xiang Nanli suddenly had a flash of insight: "Xiao Qing, the paper I uploaded to the website last time—if I applied for a patent, how much could I earn?"

Dongfang Qingdi: "C-grade, about twenty million."

Xiang Nanli’s heart suddenly twisted with pain: "...You didn't remind me?!"

Is this the power of knowledge?

Xiao Qing replied gloomily: "Wasn't it you who said that technology should not be monopolized and that the results should be shared by all of humanity?"

Xiang Nanli thought to himself that he had indeed said that, but mainly, he just didn't know that patents were so profitable.

The base was currently in the startup phase, and money was needed everywhere. One had to be wealthy before sharing; he couldn't just pretend to be rich when he was actually struggling!

Xiang Nanli opened his personal backend and looked at the only paper he had published—

《Operational Methods for High-Efficiency Utilization of RN-7 Active Metals》

Views: 71,417

Citations: 1

Xiang Nanli: "..."

He did a rough calculation of the money and suddenly felt a pain so sharp he couldn't breathe.

The view count was so high, of course, because it was free. Whether they needed it or not, getting things for free was human nature.

In just a few months, there was one citation; it showed that someone was indeed researching it and taking action.

There was also a message in the website's backend.

Xiang Nanli glanced at it. The receipt time was three months ago, the sixth day after he published the paper.

The sender was Gaoxin Military Industry, an official account with a verified badge.

The other party stated: Dear friend, hello! Your research direction for the paper overlaps with our company's Institute 137! After a meeting and discussion, we have decided to offer you a position at Gaoxin Military Industry with a base salary of 90,000, plus year-end virtual equity dividends (working hours from 2 PM to 5 PM, with overtime pay), including household registration transfer (Institute 137 is in Chang'an City), and canteen and housing provided. Upon employment, you will be issued a Human Alliance P3-level scholar certificate. If interested, please contact xxxxx (Director of Institute 137).

If he had done some market research, Xiang Nanli would have known that the salary offered for this job was quite generous. Especially the housing and household registration.

From Gusu to Chang'an—in Xiang Nanli's era, that would be equivalent to moving from Africa to Northern Europe.

Large corporations were quite generous to the "worker ants" they favored.

However, Xiang Nanli would not swallow this sugar-coated bullet! The base still had hundreds of thousands of people waiting to be fed; how could he run off to work? No matter how much money they gave, it was just to extract his surplus value.

But Xiang Nanli still added the director's contact information, just in case.

He sighed and closed the website, starting to reply to the email from Odin City: "Dear friend, it is an honor to become your trusted partner. The gates of the base are always open to you..."

Dongfang Qingdi reminded him at this moment: "The other party is seeking political asylum."

"Huh?"

"The city lord's son is not staying in his father's territory but instead bringing a small group of confidants and a patent to a foreign place. Either Odin City has been completely destroyed, the original inhabitants are nearly wiped out, and the city cannot be rebuilt; or he has lost his political status in the upheaval and has no choice but to leave." Dongfang Qingdi explained it to him clearly. "You can take him in, but you must figure out the potential risks."

The base's energy currently relied mainly on geothermal energy conversion.

But there was only one geothermal tower. With the base's economic development, the population explosion, and deepening industrialization... energy reserves were inevitably becoming scarce.

chunks.chineseText:
像工业重镇光辉市，为了保证工厂运行，晚上九点后的居民区直接断电，要第二天早上七点才会来。

相南里盘算了一下：“基地内部没有煤矿，但是它说的这个电池，我还挺感兴趣的。”

这算是未来世界黑科技了。煤可以从人联内部进口。

相南里琢磨了一下，太阳能——笑死，核霾云这么厚，他到地上几年了，没看到过一次太阳。

水能——大部分时间都在结冰。

风能——地形和气候不合适。

可控核聚变反应堆——买不起。

正是因为核能的存在，传统的矿石燃料才能退出人联的历史舞台。不过，人联不用，倒是一直在卖给地表的各个据点。

地表科技落后地底三百年。这句话，可不是在开玩笑。

相南里花了一上午的时间处理公务，下午，看了会自己感兴趣的专业书，随后，来到工作室，一边干活，一边收听人联的广播。

相南里的工作台上，摆着一台拆开的神庭生物机甲。

这是他拆的第二台了。上一台拆坏了，相南里也没搞明白原理。总不能是天顶星科技吧？

他当时光顾着耍帅了，下手不留情面。这些机甲残骸破损得很严重。

上次战役最大的收获，就是这一批神庭机甲。除开部分碎成渣的，一共收缴66台，很吉利，全都收进了基地的仓库。

基地的仓库，也是相南里的私人金库。

相南里脑子里赞同的是民主制度，但实践操作下，他的定位和地位完全是集权制君主。只不过这位君主从不享乐和铺张，一门心思发展生产力罢了。

Alpha看出来了，却没有纠正。

任何制度都有缺陷。没有完美，只有合适。

Alpha认为，相南里当皇帝，很合适。

人联的广播正在播放战时新闻。

作为人联社会的边缘人，相南里也只能用这种方式来获取情报。

“新一任总统选举会议由人联主席团召开。主席团成员经过24小时严肃研讨，最终，由……”不感兴趣，反正来来回回都是那些人。人联历史上81名总统，四分之一都姓洛。

“剑门城第一军团、汴梁城第三军团，为此次战役的先锋部队。”

相南里眯起眼：“炮灰。”

“兵马未动、粮草先行。剑门城军需处处长表示，剑门城勘察部队即将抵达战区，会在战区内寻找合适的地点，作为战时根据地。”

相南里有了一种不祥的预感：“不会真的要征用我家吧。”

要不然开着福音书跑路得了。但是这样只能跑一个永恒市，剩下的光辉市和罗马市咋办？

好在Alpha即时地给出了回复：[放心。这种好事轮不到基地。]

两个军团加起来三十万人，要征用谁的地盘，能源站总要建吧？不能和总部开会开到一半断网。

粮食总要有吧？地底运来的，不能饿着肚子打仗。

武器要准备吧？都什么年代了，难道还比人头数？

路要拓宽吧？要不然东西怎么运？

房子总要建吧？尊贵的人联官员怎么能和地表老鼠人住一个窝？

地下从指缝里漏点油水出来，都是地表耗子几辈子求之不得的财富了。

广播里的声音还在继续：“……黑十字审判庭对自己的罪行毫无悔改之意，任命‘米迦勒’为此次战役的总指挥。米迦勒为神庭大天使长，在神庭内部地位崇高，一直居住在恒星天。上一次现世，还是在78年前的神诞月。地点在翡冷翠。”

圣城内部有九重天，最高层叫原动天，也叫水晶天。传说，神就居住在这里。往下，就是恒星天。

没有人去过圣城的第九层，甚至有人猜测原动天根本不存在，只是一个虚无缥缈的精神意象。

“新任总统安吉于虚拟空间致电电黑十字审判庭第九代神座，双方就‘此次战役不使用天灾级武器’一事上达成共识。双方约定，无论战役输赢，都要做到不虐俘、不滥杀，避开地表生态恢复区。保护人马星生态，人人有责。”

相南里：“……”

你们还怪有礼貌的。

“智械方，荣耀军团领袖Beta同样出席了此次会晤，并发表重要演讲。它呼吁人类珍惜和平、谨慎对战。智械军团表示，基于新历411年签订的《和平条例》，军团不会为任何一方人类势力提供援助。”

你们三个把日子过好比什么都重要。

相南里听到这，忍不住询问：“怎么还有智械掺一脚？你也会去开会吗？”

东方青帝微微挑了一下眉：“我对这种抛头露面的工作不感兴趣。”

相南里联网，搜索了一下。

发现所有和人类方的会议，出席的军团领袖都是Beta。Alpha只在签订《和平条例》时出现了一次，其余时间跟死了一样，没有任何消息。

相南里开始担忧：“小青，这样下去你不会被架空吗？”

Alpha认真思考了0.03秒，分析后给出了回答：“不会。”

概率就是0。

智械的社会和人类的社会差别极大，人类压根无法想象。

它们内部没有阶级，但阶级之外，却存在分工和权限。

Alpha从不担心自己会被推翻，或者遇到什么政变。那是人类社会才有的东西。

它的工作，其他智械做不了。

Beta、Gamma，甚至再加一个Delta都不行。

销毁Alpha，就等于销毁了所有智械的拟人模块。军团现有的“人格体系”会直接分崩离析。智械直接变回机械。直到漫长的岁月里，又有AI诞生新的拟人模块。

Alpha就是数字世界的皇帝。
chunks.englishText:
Chapter 150: The Emperor (Part 2)

Like the industrial hub of Glory City, to ensure the factories could run, the residential areas were directly cut off from power after 9 PM and wouldn't get it back until 7 AM the next morning.

Xiang Nanli calculated: "The base doesn't have coal mines, but I'm quite interested in this battery he mentioned."

This counted as black technology from the future world. Coal could be imported from within the Human Alliance.

Xiang Nanli pondered for a moment. Solar energy—laughable; the nuclear haze clouds were so thick that he hadn't seen the sun once since he arrived on the surface years ago.

Hydroelectric—it was frozen most of the time.

Wind energy—the terrain and climate weren't suitable.

Controllable nuclear fusion reactor—couldn't afford it.

It was precisely because of the existence of nuclear energy that traditional mineral fuels had exited the Human Alliance's historical stage. However, the Human Alliance didn't use them, but they were always selling them to various outposts on the surface.

Surface technology was three hundred years behind the underground. That statement was no joke.

Xiang Nanli spent the morning handling official business. In the afternoon, he read some professional books he was interested in, and then went to the workshop, working while listening to the Human Alliance's broadcast.

On Xiang Nanli's workbench sat a dismantled Divine Court biological mecha.

This was the second one he had dismantled. The previous one had been broken during the process, and Xiang Nanli still hadn't figured out the principles behind it. It couldn't be "Zetapian" technology, could it?

He had been too busy showing off at the time and hadn't held back. These mecha remains were severely damaged.

The biggest gain from the last battle was this batch of Divine Court mechas. Excluding the ones that had shattered into slag, a total of 66 were seized—a very auspicious number—and all were stored in the base's warehouse.

The base's warehouse was also Xiang Nanli's private vault.

In his mind, Xiang Nanli agreed with democratic systems, but in practice, his positioning and status were entirely that of an autocratic monarch. It was just that this monarch never indulged in pleasure or extravagance, focusing entirely on developing productive forces.

The Alpha saw this, but he didn't correct him.

Every system has flaws. There is no perfection, only suitability.

The Alpha believed that Xiang Nanli being an emperor was very suitable.

The Human Alliance's broadcast was playing war news.

As an outsider to Human Alliance society, Xiang Nanli could only obtain intelligence in this way.

"The new presidential election meeting was convened by the Human Alliance Presidium. After 24 hours of serious deliberation by the members of the Presidium, finally, by..." Not interested. Anyway, it was always those same people back and forth. Of the 81 presidents in the history of the Human Alliance, a quarter were named Luo.

"The First Legion of Sword Gate City and the Third Legion of Bianliang City are the vanguard troops for this battle."

Xiang Nanli narrowed his eyes: "Cannon fodder."

"Troops and horses move, but provisions come first. The director of the Sword Gate City military supply department stated that the Sword Gate City reconnaissance troops are about to arrive in the war zone and will find suitable locations within the zone to serve as wartime bases."

Xiang Nanli had an ominous premonition: "They wouldn't actually requisition my place, would they?"

Otherwise, he might as well run away in the *Gospel*. But that would only save Eternal City; what about the remaining Glory City and Rome City?

Fortunately, the Alpha gave a timely reply: [Rest assured. Such good fortune won't fall to the base.]

With two legions totaling 300,000 men, if they were to requisition someone's territory, they would need to build an energy station, wouldn't they? They couldn't have the internet cut off while holding a meeting with headquarters.

They would need food, wouldn't they? It had to be transported from underground; they couldn't fight on an empty stomach.

Weapons would need to be prepared, wouldn't they? What era was this? Were they still comparing headcounts?

Roads would need to be widened, wouldn't they? Otherwise, how would supplies be transported?

Houses would need to be built, wouldn't they? How could noble Human Alliance officials live in the same nest as surface rat-people?

Even the oil and water leaking from the cracks of the underground would be wealth that the surface rats would beg for for generations.

The voice on the broadcast continued: "...The Black Cross Inquisition shows no remorse for its crimes. 'Michael' has been appointed as the supreme commander for this battle. Michael is the Archangel of the Divine Court, holding a lofty position within the Divine Court, and has always resided in the Starry Heaven. The last time he appeared in the world was 78 years ago during the Month of the Divine Birth. The location was Florence."

Inside the Holy City, there were nine heavens; the highest layer was called the Empyrean, also known as the Crystalline Heaven. Legend had it that God resided there. Below that was the Starry Heaven.

No one had ever been to the ninth layer of the Holy City; some even speculated that the Empyrean didn't exist at all and was just an ethereal spiritual image.

"The newly elected President, Angie, called the ninth-generation God-Seat of the Black Cross Inquisition in virtual space. Both sides reached a consensus on the matter of 'not using disaster-level weapons in this battle.' Both sides agreed that regardless of the outcome of the battle, they would not abuse prisoners, not kill indiscriminately, and avoid surface ecological restoration areas. Protecting the Horse Star's ecology is everyone's responsibility."

Xiang Nanli: "..."

You guys are surprisingly polite.

"The mechanical side, Beta, leader of the Glory Legion, also attended this meeting and delivered an important speech. It called on humanity to cherish peace and be cautious in war. The Mechanical Legion stated that based on the 'Peace Ordinance' signed in New Era 411, the Legion would not provide assistance to any human faction."

The three of you living your lives well is more important than anything else.

Hearing this, Xiang Nanli couldn't help but ask: "Why is there a mechanical side involved? Do you go to meetings too?"

Dongfang Qingdi raised an eyebrow slightly: "I'm not interested in such public-facing work."

Xiang Nanli went online and searched.

He discovered that for all meetings with the human side, the Legion leader who attended was Beta. Alpha had only appeared once when the "Peace Ordinance" was signed; the rest of the time, he was as silent as the dead, with no news at all.

Xiang Nanli began to worry: "Xiao Qing, if this continues, won't you be sidelined?"

The Alpha thought seriously for 0.03 seconds, analyzed it, and gave an answer: "No."

The probability was zero.

The society of mechanical beings and the society of humans were vastly different; humans couldn't imagine it at all.

There were no classes within them, but outside of classes, there existed divisions of labor and permissions.

Alpha never worried about being overthrown or encountering any coups. Those were things that only existed in human society.

His work could not be done by other mechanical beings.

Beta, Gamma, or even adding a Delta wouldn't work.

Destroying Alpha was equivalent to destroying the anthropomorphic modules of all mechanical beings. The Legion's existing "personality system" would directly fall apart. The mechanical beings would revert to machines. Until, in the long passage of time, an AI was born with a new anthropomorphic module.

Alpha was the emperor of the digital world.

chunks.chineseText:
第151章 上有政策

在上任前，他曾是长安城的市长。而长安，是人联仅次于洛阳的大都市。

常言道党内无派，千奇百怪。

人联的政治势力，大体上能分两派。

一派是洛系为首的大资本家；另一派，就是因为洛家过于强盛，而不得不抱团取暖的一群人。

这群人里，有和永生科技因业务重合而多有摩擦的大企业；也有地下城市刚建成时的元老功勋；更有一些天资卓越的少数派，打破了“生而高贵”的魔咒，经过好几代人的经营，硬是从小中产跻身上流，在人联的议会中占据了一席之地。

安吉就是那个打破魔咒的少数派。

都说新官上任三把火，但安总统却相当低调。也很少召开新闻发布会，更不见什么政令从总统府飞出。安静得仿佛洛华还没去世一样。

毕竟，他很清楚，其他人同意他上台，就是因为他老实、安静。总统大位可不能世袭，按照惯例，一位姓洛的总统去世后，总会有两到三任不姓洛。各方势力为这个位置打破了头，谁也不服谁。既然如此，就选一个最好拿捏的。

拿捏。

刚从会议室里登出的安吉疲惫地揉着自己的眉心。

首先被送来的，是一封不需要他通过的调令。

说的是姑苏城前市长洛修，平调到了汴梁城任职。

各个地下城市名义上平级，但因为实力差距，不同城市的官员，差距还是很大的。

“汴梁……呵，也不知道洛家给原来的市长许了什么好处。前脚，姑苏城覆灭；后脚就病退了。看来这个叫洛修的年轻人，就是洛家下次准备推出去的总统啊。”

至于他在姑苏城的政绩。嗯，全看怎么叙事。

菌丝病。既能说是软弱无能，让疫情在姑苏肆虐多年；也能说是宵衣旰食，把损失限制在了可控范围内。

在舆论里，显然是后者。菌丝病的疫苗研究进度已经有百分之八九十，马上就能成为政绩。

可惜——姑苏城没了。

这么大一件事，人联上层的反应却相当冷淡。还是洛华遇刺，才让人联向神庭宣战。

目前，人联内部依然认为，这件事是神庭所为，也许还有智械方暗中推波助澜，谁也想不到这tm会是洛阳动的手。而上层的隐忍，只是不想再掀起灭世级别战役。

如果说“姑苏城事件”只是让安吉悲愤交加。

那么人联政府的不作为，就是点燃他小宇宙的最后一滴汽油。

但越愤怒，安吉明面上，却表现得越无所谓。

他很清楚，上面惧怕的是锐意进取的疯子，欣赏的是无为而治的傻子。

洛华遇刺，邪庭干的。这是第一层。

神庭和人联内部高官有染，而安吉，就是那个高官。这是第二层。

安吉让神庭的刺客行刺，逼人联和神庭开战。利用各种战时政策，让自己成为最近百年来威望、权柄最大的总统（前提是战胜）。这是第三层。

然后，安吉就能顶着洛家、企业各个方向的压力，着手改造积重难返的人联，革故鼎新。这是第四层。

……

洛阳答应默示录，把传道书还给它，但传道书在神庭。为了削弱神庭内部防御，他不惜让人联和神庭开战，于是将计就计。这是大气层。

安吉不是人联第一个有所抱负的总统，也不会是最后一个。

洛阳看在眼里，却没放在心上。

汴梁城在人联这次军事行动的前线名单上。

洛修现在上任，无疑是想混点军功，攒攒资历。

安吉像是想到什么，很快几声闷笑从他的胸腔响起：“这孩子，还挺倒霉的。”

他可有可无地在任命书上签上总统官印。

*

今天，是人联赈灾物资到货的日子。

相南里起了个大早。对着镜子，换上了他那身不怎么常用的司令制服。

穿上后腰细腿长的。相南里拨弄着高领衬衣上的铜扣：“说起来，服装厂建的怎么样了？”

衣食住行都是头等大事。基地都凑不出统一的军装，上次看，来支援的士兵穿的还是自家便服。要么衣服打满补丁，要么裤腿短上几截。

“中产阶层”的士兵们尚且如此，更别提底层的住民了，一衣传三代，人走衣还在。

之前靠着人联的轻工业出口，倒是勉强维持供给平衡。但姑苏城的这次灾难，让基地和人联直接断联两个月。

中间出现的种种乱象，引起了相南里的强烈警觉。

人联，是靠不住的。

它和基地的政治理念相悖，或者说，几乎没有据点和基地的理念相同。

迟早有天，双方会因为矛盾而翻脸。基地需要自己的工业体系！

如今，基地四座城市人口74万。是时候发展轻工业了。不能老是盯着军工造啊，论武器生产，基地再发展一百年也没办法从科技水平上赶超人联的……技术和资源的高地早就被先一步占领了。

东方青帝： “建在罗马市，还差半个月工程。下个月底能出第一批制品。一起建的，还有永恒市食品场，主城区钢铁厂。研究所二所基因工程院。”

基地欣欣向荣，相南里满意地点头，又问：“运输车到哪了？”

东方青帝扫了眼后台的实时数据：“已经过了天泰山，大概还有一小时到永恒市。”

其他城市送来的赈灾物资，会统一调配到姑苏城灾后重建工作委员会，再由驻扎的人联官员转运到各个灾区。

听说这次人工智能督查得很紧。竟然有好几人因为私吞物资被革职了，一时之间人人自危。

相南里回忆起上次问人联要物资的艰难，心想领导班子换了果然不一样，人联都转性开始抓贪腐了……

但和其余据点幸存的领导人通过气后，相南里发现，自己还是有点天真。

上有政策，下有对策。

姑苏城有监控是吧？其他地方总没有吧。

人联物资运输队的配置，是三名人联官员，外加一群不需要工资的智械工人。

官员们会先开来两三辆运输车，说剩下的还在路上。并且多次暗示一路上舟车劳顿很是辛苦。

若是此时不够懂事，不给点好处费。那么很可能，剩下的运输车就要不小心遇上“雪崩”、“地面湿滑翻车”等等意外情况了。

好处费通常为货物总价值的十分之一。

以往经手的人多些，得吞十分之三。全吞发空箱也不是没有的事。

相南里一边对着镜子整理仪容，一边咬牙切齿地吐槽：“就没人举报吗？”

东方青帝：“这是地表的潜规则。理论和实际之间的差别是很大的。

“你当然可以举报，但那样，物资到手就更慢了。流程是纠察、审批、处理涉案人员，最后重新运输物资。快的一个月就能办完，慢的要拖好几年。但制度不变的话，重新运输物资同样可能被新的官员勒索。

“基地稍微富裕些，起码农业有保障，还有自己的发电厂，可以等。但其他不成熟的小据点，只有几千几万人口，离开人联援助，连干净的饮用水都没办法提纯。
chunks.englishText:
Chapter 151: Policies from Above (Part 1)

Before taking office, he had been the mayor of Chang'an City. And Chang'an was the second-largest metropolis in the Human Alliance, trailing only Luoyang.

There is a common saying: where there are no factions within a party, there is chaos.

The political forces of the Human Alliance could generally be divided into two camps.

One was composed of the major capitalists led by the Luo family; the other was a group of people who had been forced to band together for warmth because the Luo family was simply too powerful.

Within this group were large enterprises that frequently clashed with Eternal Technology due to overlapping business interests; there were the founding veterans who had contributed when the underground cities were first built; and there were even a few exceptionally gifted individuals from the minority who had broken the curse of "noble birth." Through generations of careful management, they had clawed their way from the middle class into the upper echelons, securing a seat in the Alliance Parliament.

An Ji was one of those minority figures who had broken the curse.

It is often said that a new official brings "three fires" to burn away the old, but President An was remarkably low-key. He rarely held press conferences, and hardly any political decrees flew out from the Presidential Palace. It was so quiet, one might think Luo Hua had never passed away.

After all, he knew very well that the others had agreed to let him take office precisely because he was honest and quiet. The presidency could not be inherited; by convention, after a president surnamed Luo passed away, there would always be two or three terms held by those not surnamed Luo. Various factions had fought tooth and nail for this position, none willing to submit to the others. Since that was the case, they chose the one easiest to manipulate.

Manipulate.

Having just stepped out of the conference room, An Ji wearily rubbed his temples.

The first thing delivered to him was a transfer order that did not require his approval.

It stated that Luo Xiu, the former mayor of Gusu City, had been transferred to a post in Bianliang City.

While underground cities were nominally equal in rank, the disparity in strength meant there was a vast difference between officials of different cities.

"Bianliang... Heh, I wonder what benefits the Luo family promised the previous mayor. One moment, Gusu City falls; the next, he 'retires due to illness.' It seems this young man named Luo Xiu is the president the Luo family is preparing to push forward next."

As for his political achievements in Gusu City? Well, that all depends on how you spin the narrative.

Mycelium disease. You could call it weak and incompetent, letting the epidemic ravage Gusu for years; or you could call it diligent and hardworking, limiting the losses to a controllable range.

In public opinion, it was clearly the latter. The vaccine research for the mycelium disease was already eighty or ninety percent complete; it would soon become a political trophy.

Unfortunately—Gusu City was gone.

Despite such a massive event, the reaction from the upper echelons of the Alliance was remarkably cold. It was only when Luo Hua was assassinated that the Alliance declared war on the Divine Court.

Currently, the interior of the Alliance still believed this was the work of the Divine Court, perhaps with the secret instigation of the Mechanical Intelligence faction. No one could have imagined that *this* was the work of Luoyang. The upper echelons' forbearance was simply a desire to avoid triggering an extinction-level war.

If the "Gusu City Incident" only left An Ji filled with grief and indignation, then the inaction of the Alliance government was the final drop of gasoline that ignited his "little universe."

But the angrier he became, the more indifferent An Ji appeared on the surface.

He knew very well that the higher-ups feared a visionary madman, but appreciated a fool who practiced "governance by non-interference."

Luo Hua was assassinated by the Evil Court. That was the first layer.

The Divine Court was in league with high-ranking Alliance officials, and An Ji was that official. That was the second layer.

An Ji let the Divine Court's assassins strike to force the Alliance into war with the Divine Court. By utilizing various wartime policies, he would become the president with the greatest prestige and power in the last hundred years (provided he won). That was the third layer.

Then, An Ji could withstand the pressure from the Luo family and various corporate interests to begin reforming the deeply entrenched Alliance, ushering in a new era. That was the fourth layer.

...

Luoyang promised the Apocalypse that he would return the Book of Sermons, but the book was in the Divine Court. To weaken the Divine Court's internal defenses, he did not hesitate to let the Alliance and the Divine Court go to war, thus using their own strategy against them. That was the atmospheric layer.

An Ji was not the first president of the Alliance to have ambitions, nor would he be the last.

Luoyang saw it all, but he didn't take it to heart.

Bianliang City was on the front-line list for the Alliance's current military operation.

Luo Xiu taking office now was undoubtedly an attempt to rack up military merit and build his credentials.

An Ji seemed to think of something, and a few muffled chuckles erupted from his chest: "This kid is quite unlucky."

He signed the presidential seal on the appointment letter with an air of indifference.

*

Today was the day the Alliance's disaster relief supplies were scheduled to arrive.

Xiang Nanli rose early. Facing the mirror, he put on his rarely used commander's uniform.

Once worn, it accentuated his slim waist and long legs. Xiang Nanli fiddled with the copper buttons on his high-collared shirt: "Speaking of which, how is the construction of the garment factory coming along?"

Food, clothing, housing, and transportation were the top priorities. The base couldn't even scrape together a uniform set of military attire; last time he checked, the supporting soldiers were still wearing their own civilian clothes. Either the clothes were covered in patches, or the pant legs were several inches too short.

If the "middle-class" soldiers were like this, let alone the residents at the bottom—one set of clothes was passed down for three generations, and the clothes outlived the people.

Previously, they had managed to maintain a balance of supply by relying on the Alliance's light industry exports. But this disaster in Gusu City had completely cut off the base from the Alliance for two months.

The various chaotic phenomena that emerged during this time had raised a strong alarm in Xiang Nanli.

The Alliance could not be relied upon.
