**Chapter 165: New Policies for the War Zone (Part 1)**

“I’m tired.”

At two in the morning, Xiang Nanli’s biological clock was forced into chaos.

People who could come here for a meeting had all undergone some degree of modification; let alone pulling an all-nighter, staying up for three days and three nights didn't seem like a problem for them.

Xiang Nanli’s exhaustion seemed out of place.

To blend into the collective, Xiang Nanli had to force himself to stay alert, widening his green eyes and pretending to listen carefully.

His brain couldn't think, but Xiang Nanli vaguely heard a few keywords, such as “War Zone New Policy” and “Wartime Electronic Currency Policy.”

The former was too long, so he had to leave it to Xiao Zhi to record in his memo.

He understood the latter; it said that a new version of Human Alliance credits would be used in the war zone. These new coins would be marked with special codes and would not circulate in the inner regions of the Human Alliance.

Xiang Nanli was also a man who had seriously studied a few books on “Principles of Economics.”

He perceived the Human Alliance’s intention with near-sharpness: issuing new currency in the war zone was for the convenience of printing money.

No matter how severe the inflation was here, as long as the new currency didn't circulate in the underground cities, it wouldn't affect the stability of the Human Alliance’s interior.

Sure enough, the second policy related to the economy was the confiscation of the credit points of these war zone strongholds—of course, it wasn't that crude; it was called an “exchange,” with a Human Alliance credit to war zone credit ratio of 1:1.2.

On the surface, the Human Alliance was taking a huge loss.

“This is a welfare policy.” The Minister of Finance of Gusu stood on the stage, impeccably dressed, “You can exchange your original electronic currency for more goods.”

*Yes, but you can only spend it in the war zone.*

Everything seemed normal for now, but the consumption of war was immense.

The Human Alliance held the right to mint currency in the war zone without worrying about inflation, so they could print new banknotes without limit to serve as military pay.

In the end, those who would be exploited were definitely the bottom-level people with the least power.

Xiang Nanli feared that possible future.

He feared nutrient paste costing 500 credits a bag, pure water costing 800 credits a bottle, and the people living here having no way to deal with it; after all, this was a war zone where supplies and transportation were controlled. He only hoped that the Human Alliance wouldn't really treat them, these surface remnants, like Divine Court believers.

Xiang Nanli felt disappointed, which made him even sleepier.

In the group chat, most of the leaders of these strongholds were giving positive reviews, actually thinking that the Human Alliance was really conceding benefits and doing a conscientious deed.

Xiang Nanli had no intention of being a harbinger of doom. But if the nest is overturned, how can the base survive?

Xiang Nanli leaned his head on the Alpha’s shoulder, yawning incessantly: “I want to sleep.”

Xiang Nanli felt like he could pass out just from walking, and the Alpha wouldn't let him take stimulants.

The elite class of the Human Alliance liked to take potions to optimize their physiological state, and it had become a custom; the Alpha believed that the disadvantages outweighed the advantages, as there was sufficient data to prove their trace toxicity and addictiveness. He advocated for the “native human” school of thought.

The Alpha’s hand rested on his head, like stroking a cat: “It will be over soon.”

“I don’t want to walk, carry me...” Xiang Nanli leaned his head on his shoulder.

The Alpha tried his best to control the upward curve of his mouth, avoiding laughing too obviously.

*I want to become a cryo-pod and tuck Xiang Nanli inside my own body.*

*If humans are destined to die, then please let them rot in my arms.*

Unfortunately, the Alpha’s wish to take Xiang Nanli home was not fulfilled.

A staff member dressed in a highly technological style walked over quickly and took out his work ID: “Please wait a moment, the commander-in-chief hopes you will stay after the meeting; there is another short meeting.”

Dongfang Qingdi: “I’ll go.”

Considering the long meeting had lasted over ten hours, he reasonably suspected that the so-called short meeting would also last until dawn.

“Sorry, the commander specifically requested to see Xiang Nanli.”

Dongfang Qingdi’s eyebrows raised slightly, feeling a subtle sense of displeasure.

Xiang Nanli patted the Alpha’s hand to soothe him. It was a completely subconscious act; Dongfang Qingdi was mostly expressionless, but Xiang Nanli could always distinguish those subtle changes.

Perhaps this was the “father knows the son” dynamic.

Xiang Nanli felt like he was holding a very lethal mechanical dog and was trying hard to keep it from biting people.

The Alpha didn't like to talk, but his emotional fluctuations were not few. Perhaps this was the “barking dogs don't bite” logic.

The small meeting room was in the corridor behind the main meeting room. Passing through the corridor and pushing open the door, several unfamiliar faces were sitting upright.

Xiang Nanli matched their faces with the forces behind them and keenly discovered that these people all came from the “front line.”

But the survivor base was in the southwest of the battlefield, toward the rear, in the second echelon.

Xiang Nanli consciously found a corner to sit down.

The meeting room was very quiet. Outside the door, the sound of Fang Jingzhi’s slowly approaching footsteps was exceptionally clear.

His metallic-textured shoes stepped on the cold ground, the rhythm not off by a fraction, the pace uniform.

Xiang Nanli guessed he had obsessive-compulsive disorder.

Fang Jingzhi was tall, with a slender build. He was estimated to be two meters tall after putting on his shoes, which made him look down on everyone.

Gusu was clearly his home field. Fang Jingzhi held his head high and chest out, sitting elegantly at the very top of the conference table. A young man followed him, quiet and silent. This was Fang Jingzhi’s secretary, a high-level android with warm orange-red pupil rings.

Everyone’s eyes were focused on Fang Jingzhi, waiting for him to give orders.

If it weren't for the wrong occasion, Xiang Nanli felt he would be like Liu Bang looking at Qin Shi Huang, sighing, “A real man should be like this.”

“Thank you all for coming from afar.” This politician spoke very politely, without the arrogance of a plutocrat, his elegant and unfamiliar pronunciation testifying to his noble background.

The Human Alliance language of these plutocrat children formed its own school; only if one’s ancestors were wealthy could one install this set of language systems in their chips.

Xiang Nanli was expressionless, but the leaders around him showed a considerable degree of being flattered, even some trepidation.

[My god! The Lord is so polite and gentle in private, I’m so touched.]

[I’ve gone from a passerby to a fan.]

[Thinking about it, our war zone is still very lucky. The commander-in-chief sent is Fang Jingzhi. If it were someone else, there would probably only be cold system notifications and forced tasks. Those who don’t listen would also happen to become the battle record of friendly forces.]

This view was widely recognized by the group members, causing a huge shock to Xiang Nanli’s heart.

Fang Jingzhi was just breathing, yet others felt he was so condescending.

Xiang Nanli realized one thing again—the class segregation of the Human Alliance was a hundred times more serious than in his previous life. Just the barrier of “software permissions” could not be smoothed out by the struggle and efforts of ordinary people.

Xiang Nanli wanted to sigh again.

Fang Jingzhi: “I’ll keep it short. You are the first line of defense for the Human Alliance facing the Divine Court. You bear tremendous pressure for the rear. The Human Alliance will provide you with support as much as possible. But there is only one point: your ideology must be firm. You cannot act as a soldier of the Human Alliance today for the sake of supplies, and then defect to the Black Cross Inquisition tomorrow. I would rather our ammunition be fired at the enemy.”

The last sentence was almost a blatant threat.

Xiang Nanli thought to himself, *Then what about someone like him who is in the rear? Just picking up Human Alliance supply packages?*

Then, the Human Alliance’s supply package list was thrown onto his electronic device.

Unexpectedly, there were no weapons or food on it; what there were, were drugs.

A small portion was regular gene medicine produced by the Human Alliance, the price of which could double on the black market; and a large amount of “Amphetamine tablets.”

Amphetamine tablets—Xiang Nanli checked the information, and it showed that the active ingredients were “methamphetamine” and a trace amount of “fentanyl”; other than that, it was meaningless starch.

Both of these could be used for medical analgesia and anesthesia; but in his previous life, Xiang Nanli knew that these two drug components were strictly controlled laboratory drugs... more lethal than most addictive substances circulating on the market.

Clearly, as human bodies were strengthened by gene medicine, the efficacy of these circulating drugs had also become more dangerous.

chunks.chineseText:
相南里瞳孔地震：[这是可以流通的吗？]

他对这方面研究不多，但是也知道芬太尼的毒性是海x因的十几倍。

东方青帝察觉到了他的不安和惶恐。

他回答：[并非所有士兵，都具有崇高的信念和意志。人类和可以设定程序的智械不一样。会恐惧、疼痛和退缩。这样的军队，是没有任何战斗力的。]

[在战场，这种强效的阿片类药物，和军火、食物一样，属于必需品。安非片由古神生物研发生产，目前已经超过150年专利期。是相对来说容易量产，且副作用可控的一类兴奋剂。有阵痛、兴奋、产生愉悦感的作用。还能当作抗抑郁药使用。同时，也具备成瘾性。]

[除此外，人联的军队也是机械改造的高发区；有数据表示，机械改造后的人类明显情绪更少，更冷静，还能进行特殊信号安抚和镇定。但地表的普通士兵显然没有这个条件，只能依靠药剂。]

至于战争结束后，这些不幸药物成瘾的士兵怎么办……只能说，先等他们活到停战吧。更何况，这些人只能生活在地表。无所谓的。

相南里生活在和平年代。

自从苏醒后，他多多少少也经历过一两次战争，也有生死存亡的危机时刻。可从未有一次，让相南里觉得世界如此冷酷，他的牙齿都快打颤了。

人联，一个庞大的、系统性的机器。

它在一些人眼里是天堂，在一些人眼里是祖国；在一些人眼里，是地狱。它利用着自己过去的积累和霸权，极其高效地对祭品们进行制度性的敲骨吸髓，而不用担心任何报应。

“相南里。”台上，方敬之突然点到他的名字。

他挥手，递过一份合同：“根据调查，你们据点有一片适宜种植、广阔肥沃的平原。并且有一定的工业化生产能力。

“这是一份合同。未来几年，战区对安非片的需求量极大。从人联地底城市调配时间过长。我希望幸存者基地能规模性种植树麻黄。人联打算在购买幸存者基地的部分土地，并开设药厂。这是一份长期收购树麻黄的商业合同，有效期十年。”

树麻黄，古神生物研究的新品种，能高效提纯出“盐酸麻黄碱”。

简单来说，人联在基地开设工厂；基地提供药物原材料。

相南里低头扫了眼合同，这份合同条件相当优渥。树麻黄的收购单价，是基地能生产的农产品的十几倍。更何况树麻黄产量高。这几乎是一个金矿。

其他人纷纷转头，看向相南里，眼里流露出羡慕的神色。

[我草，这小子，是不是有关系啊？哪来这么好的运气。这一年得赚多少亿信用点啊。]

[不知道啊，是不是走的奥丁城的关系？我听说，那个艾伦的尸体就是基地送回去的。洛基又投靠了高新军工。不是传闻奥丁城要设行省来着，当姑苏城的陪都。]

[种哪不是种啊？基地能种，我看那什么什么地方也能种啊……]

[垄断，知道什么叫垄断吗？不知道就回去多读书。而且开设药厂，光设备都不知道多少亿了，这绝对能成支柱企业啊。等人联军队撤了，药厂肯定便宜卖给基地了……]

是的，看上去好处这么多。完全没有理由拒绝。

方敬之继续慢条斯理地说着：“其实在来之前，我就听说过你。相南里，高新军工实验室有人跟我提起过你。还有你在网上发表的论文……你很优秀，高新军工愿意给你这个机会。战区这么大，合适的据点不止你一个。”

所以，别不识抬举。

合同里，甚至指出，可以给相南里一个“人联正式居民”的身份。他可以带着自己的心腹，比如那个人造人；在地下任何一座城市安家。

他还会拥有源源不断的财富和高新军工的支持。足够他度过优越、富饶的一生。

而人联需要的，只是少部分土地和基地的劳动力。

这份合同，算是对相南里过去筚路蓝缕、以启山林的肯定。

相南里的大脑飞速转着，脸上的笑容显得很是真诚、欣喜；他起身：“感谢总指挥给我们的机会！诚惶诚恐，受宠若惊。”

他话锋一转：“只是，人无信不立！就在会议开始前，基地已经和其他几个据点签订了粮食购买协议。基地不能单方面违约，也支付不了巨额违约金……短时间里，实在是没办法种植树麻黄！”

会议室里的空调开得有些太足了。

方敬之脸上的笑容没有丝毫变化，但谁都能感觉到，一股实质性地冷意从他身上蔓延着。

方敬之的语气冷淡下来：“好吧。”

另一份文件弹到相南里的窗口：“说到这，这是潜伏在神庭的情报人员传回的讯息。听说这个位置，会有神庭的遗迹。”

方敬之的脸上浮现出残酷的笑容：“正好，地方离你们基地不远。一个月内，把调查报告发给我。”
chunks.englishText:
Xiang Nanli’s pupils dilated in shock: "Is this something that can be circulated?"

He didn't have much research in this area, but he knew that the toxicity of fentanyl was over a dozen times that of heroin.

Dongfang Qingdi sensed his unease and panic.

He replied: "Not all soldiers possess noble convictions and iron wills. Humans are not like programmed mechanical units; they feel fear, pain, and the urge to retreat. An army like that has no combat effectiveness."

"On the battlefield, these potent opioids are just as essential as ammunition and food. 'Anfipian' was developed and produced by Ancient God Biotech, and its 150-year patent has already expired. It is a stimulant that is relatively easy to mass-produce, with controllable side effects. It serves as a painkiller, a stimulant, and a source of euphoria. It can even be used as an antidepressant. At the same time, it is also addictive."

"Furthermore, the Human Alliance military is a high-incidence area for mechanical augmentation. Data shows that humans who undergo mechanical augmentation display fewer emotions, remain calmer, and can be soothed and sedated via special signals. However, ordinary soldiers on the surface clearly lack these conditions and must rely on pharmaceuticals."

As for what happens to these unfortunate, drug-addicted soldiers after the war ends... let’s just say, they should focus on surviving until the ceasefire first. Besides, these people are destined to live on the surface anyway. It doesn't matter.

Xiang Nanli had lived in an era of peace.

Since waking up, he had experienced a war or two and faced moments of life-and-death crisis. But never once had he felt the world to be so cold and cruel; his teeth were practically chattering.

The Human Alliance—a massive, systematic machine.

In the eyes of some, it is paradise; in the eyes of others, it is their motherland; and to some, it is hell. It utilizes its accumulated history and hegemony to efficiently strip the "sacrificial offerings" to the bone, without ever fearing retribution.

"Xiang Nanli." On the podium, Fang Jingzhi suddenly called his name.

He waved his hand, passing over a contract: "According to our investigation, your stronghold possesses a vast, fertile plain suitable for cultivation, as well as a certain capacity for industrial production."

"This is a contract. In the coming years, the war zone will have a massive demand for Anfipian. Transporting it from the Human Alliance's underground cities takes too long. I hope the survivor base can cultivate 'Tree Ephedra' on a large scale. The Alliance intends to purchase a portion of the survivor base's land and establish a pharmaceutical plant. This is a long-term commercial contract for the acquisition of Tree Ephedra, valid for ten years."

Tree Ephedra, a new variety researched by Ancient God Biotech, can efficiently extract "ephedrine hydrochloride."

Simply put, the Alliance sets up the factory in the base; the base provides the raw materials.

Xiang Nanli lowered his head to scan the contract. The terms were incredibly generous. The purchase price for Tree Ephedra was over a dozen times higher than any agricultural product the base could currently produce. Not to mention, Tree Ephedra had a high yield. This was practically a gold mine.

Others turned their heads one after another, casting envious glances at Xiang Nanli.

"Damn, does this kid have connections? Where did he get such good luck? How many hundreds of millions of credits will he make in a year?"

"Who knows? Maybe it's through the Odin City connection? I heard the base sent that Alan's corpse back. Loki has defected to High-Tech Military Industry. Rumor has it Odin City is going to be established as a province, a secondary capital to Gusu City."

"Where you plant it doesn't matter, right? If the base can grow it, I bet that other place could too..."

"Monopoly, do you know what a monopoly is? If you don't, go back and read a book. Besides, setting up a pharmaceutical plant—the equipment alone is worth hundreds of millions. This will definitely become a pillar enterprise. Once the Alliance army pulls out, the plant will surely be sold to the base for a pittance..."

Yes, it looked like there were so many benefits. There was absolutely no reason to refuse.

Fang Jingzhi continued in a measured tone: "Actually, I had heard of you before I arrived. Xiang Nanli, people from the High-Tech Military Industry labs mentioned you to me. And the papers you published online... You are very talented, and High-Tech Military Industry is willing to give you this opportunity. The war zone is vast; you aren't the only suitable stronghold."

So, don't be ungrateful.

The contract even pointed out that they could grant Xiang Nanli the status of a "Formal Human Alliance Resident." He could bring his trusted aides, such as that android, and settle down in any underground city.

He would possess endless wealth and the support of High-Tech Military Industry. Enough for him to live a superior, prosperous life.

All the Alliance needed was a small amount of land and the base's labor force.

This contract was, in a way, an affirmation of Xiang Nanli’s past struggles to carve a path through the wilderness.

Xiang Nanli’s brain raced, his face wearing a smile that appeared sincere and delighted. He stood up: "Thank you, Commander-in-Chief, for this opportunity! I am humbled and flattered."

He then changed the subject: "However, a man cannot stand without credibility! Just before this meeting began, the base signed grain purchase agreements with several other strongholds. The base cannot unilaterally breach these contracts, nor can we afford the massive penalties... In the short term, we truly have no way to cultivate Tree Ephedra!"

The air conditioning in the conference room was set a bit too high.

The smile on Fang Jingzhi’s face didn't change in the slightest, but everyone could feel a tangible chill spreading from him.

Fang Jingzhi’s tone turned cold: "Very well."

Another file popped up on Xiang Nanli’s window: "Speaking of which, this is intelligence transmitted back by our agents embedded in the Divine Court. We hear that there are Divine Court ruins at this location."

A cruel smile appeared on Fang Jingzhi’s face: "Coincidentally, the location is not far from your base. Send me the investigation report within a month."

chunks.chineseText:
第166章 交易

餐厅的风格很中式，古朴大方。每个包间都贴着光学防窥墙，隔绝着外界的声音和视线。

洛修翻阅菜单，点了常吃的几道菜，然后询问：“你看看有没有想吃的？”

这是城里最贵的餐厅，只对住宿的客人开放。而能住进姑苏宾馆的，除了他们这些被邀请过来的地表领袖，就是人联派来的政府官员。品质和价格不言而喻。

但这里只是他的工作食堂，之一。

洛修经常看见有些不学无术的纨绔子弟，刷着自己父母辈的通行证，带着刚把上手的漂亮对象，来餐厅里装腔作势。

那些没见识的漂亮小孩们时常感觉到局促和震惊，对金钱的折服也往往变成了对人的折服。

洛修和自己父母都不太亲，反而是那位私底下风评不太好的堂伯经常带着他。

洛华告诉他，钱是世界上最廉价也最昂贵的一般等价物。你可以用它，交换你想要的任何东西。你是洛家嫡系，你会比谁都更能体会“生而高贵”的含义。

哈。

洛修微微抬起眼眸，假装不经意地瞥了相南里一眼。两年没见，相南里一张脸没有变化，眼眸里清透的绿色转向浓郁的翡翠色，按品相来说，属于昂贵的“帝王绿”。不知道是不是灯光的原因。

洛修哂笑，心想自己和那些把妹的二代也没多大区别。他隐蔽地希望自己能在这段关系里占据上风。因为他的外表，他的家世，那些所有世俗的、优越的东西。

可惜相南里坐在他对面，面色没有丝毫局促，既不谄媚也不贪婪。

仿佛只是和普通朋友聊聊天，谈个生意。

“你不该公开和方敬之唱反调的。”洛修叹了口气，“他风评不错，但典型的面热心冷。现在又是战区总指挥，哪怕他什么表示也没有，下面也会有人见风使舵，想办法针对你们据点。”

相南里：“我也不想啊，可是他都让我种树麻黄了，这不就是——”

毒品吗？

可人联现在的环境，和他生长的那个年代不太一样。

很多人都有服用药物的习惯，人们从小服用基因药，以抵抗自然界的核辐射。长大后，又对无处不在的药品习以为常。

药物成瘾？那是什么东西。

人都要死了，还在乎什么后遗症？

相南里只好话锋一转：“我不太能接受。”

洛修端起桌子上的红茶，微笑一下：“嗯哼。可是，树麻黄经济效益比你的那些农作物好得多；上面赚到钱，底下的人才能分点汤。你认为正确的决定，说不定还会给基地招来灾殃。”

服务生推来餐车，一碟一碟地往桌子上摆盘。

洛修十分自然地把骨瓷碟摆在相南里跟前：“鲜奶麻薯，尝尝。”

奶白的麻薯上面挤着浓稠的甜花生酱。

相南里心想，洛修怎么知道他喜欢吃这个？

这口味还挺小众的，国内一般是沾红糖、黄豆粉或者奥利奥饼干碎。相南里常年定居在国外，西餐厅里很少有鲜奶麻薯这种港式甜点，想吃只能自己做。

在他们家里，动手的一般是洛阳。

洛阳就爱往里面加花生酱，方便，味道也好。但他不爱吃的甜的，是相南里要吃。

相南里翻了一下手边的菜单，发现这款甜品叫“总统奶麻薯”。

手指触碰到菜单旁边的小铁片，能读取这道菜的图像和介绍。

简介里说，这是人联首位总统洛阳和他妻子最喜欢的一道甜品。

晚年，洛阳经常在厨房里独自制作奶麻薯。然后端到餐桌上，呼唤亡妻的名字。

就像东坡肉、太白鸭一样；洛阳经常吃的食物，也成为人联历史的一部分。

洛阳的晚年听上去很孤独。

相南里不可避免地想起Alpha说过的话，他描述的那个洛阳好陌生。

“好吃吗？”洛修盯着他的脸，眼睛出现了两道弯弯的弧度，看上去很温柔。

相南里有些纳闷。

洛修这小子，以前没这么油啊！

他主动把话题转到正事上：“基地有领主级骑士‘沙利叶’的死亡证明，还有117名天启骑士的死亡凭证。这些都可以算进你的战功里，你开个合适的价吧？”

洛修：“你的那个人造人呢？”

相南里反应了半拍，才意识到，他问的是东方青帝。

相南里避重就轻：“我们这种乡下人，来姑苏一趟不容易。工作有很多，只能分开行动了。”

洛修含笑点头：“这些战功，你向人联申报，也能换不少补贴，不必非要找我。”

相南里：“人联商场里没有我想要的东西，但是永生科技的库房里有。”

“是想让我帮你走私？”洛修的电子眼注视着他。

“只是一笔交易，如果你认为不妥……”

洛修打断他：“先把清单给我看看。”

相南里还真列了个表。

没有狮子大开口，也没有过界，很克制。想用军功交换的，是军火和生产车间。

“相……南里。”洛修看完，若有所思地念着他的名字，他的嘴角上扬，“你想要的东西，和你卖的东西，对我来说基本等价。但是这只是物质上的等价，你缺少的是购买的资格。

“当然，这个门槛可以通过我的身份替你抹平。只是你又该以什么作为回报呢？”

洛修直勾勾地看着他，像等待一个答复。

相南里莫名觉得不爽。尤其是洛修身上那股天龙人的气息，有点熏到他了。

感觉像是从小看着长大的小孩在什么地方偷偷烂掉。

“我以为，‘门槛’是消费主义的话术。基地一向以诚待人，希望能在交易中实现共赢。”相南里的语气听上去依然诚恳又亲切，眼神里的温度不变，内心却很是冷淡，“而且，你知道的，方敬之让我去调查什么神庭遗迹，我很不安，确实需要一些方便个人使用的新式武器……

“如果市长觉得不合适，我们可以放弃这次合作。无论如何，你都是基地最重要的战略合作伙伴，基地很乐意协助你在战区的工作。”

洛修沉默片刻：“好吧，我的部队的确需要军功。”

他把清单折叠好，收进自己上衣口袋里，慢条斯理地说着：“让辛追去领吧，你需要的东西会一并送到。”

他的话锋一转：“吃完饭要跟我在姑苏城里逛逛吗？”

吃完饭都大半夜了，去哪逛？又不是大学生出门逛夜市。

相南里有点懵，他找了个借口拒绝，说有个合同必须面签。

洛修没再说什么，只是嘱咐他路上注意安全。

这顿饭终于吃完了。

洛修回到家，打开灯，站在门口，突然疑惑地揉着自己的眉心。

脑子不太舒服，像宿醉。

好奇怪，他记得自己是请了相南里吃饭，然后点餐；但是为什么后面的记忆这么模糊。就像在梦游一样？有一种身体不归他操控的感觉。

机械改造程度太高，会有很多后遗症。“解离”就是其中一种。

洛修一直觉得这些后遗症离自己很远。

改天找医生检查一下吧。

他在心里想着。
chunks.englishText:
The restaurant had a very Chinese style—simple, elegant, and grand. Every private room was lined with optical anti-peeping walls, isolating them from the sounds and sights of the outside world.

Luo Xiu flipped through the menu, ordered a few familiar dishes, and then asked, "Take a look and see if there's anything you'd like to eat?"

This was the most expensive restaurant in the city, open only to guests staying at the hotel. And those who could stay at the Gusu Hotel, aside from surface leaders like them who had been invited, were government officials sent by the Human Alliance. The quality and price went without saying.

But for him, this was just his work cafeteria—one of them, at least.

Luo Xiu often saw spoiled, uneducated rich kids swiping their parents' passes, bringing along pretty dates they had just picked up to put on airs in the restaurant.

Those naive, pretty kids often felt constrained and shocked, and their submission to money often turned into submission to the people who held it.

Luo Xiu wasn't very close to his own parents; instead, it was that cousin-uncle of his, who had a poor reputation in private, who often took him out.

Luo Hua told him that money was the cheapest yet most expensive general equivalent in the world. You could use it to exchange for anything you wanted. "You are of the Luo family's direct line; you will understand the meaning of 'born noble' better than anyone."

Ha.

Luo Xiu slightly raised his eyes, pretending to glance at Xiang Nanli casually. It had been two years, and Xiang Nanli’s face hadn't changed, though the clear green in his eyes had deepened into a rich emerald—in terms of quality, it belonged to the expensive "Imperial Green." He wasn't sure if it was the lighting.

Luo Xiu chuckled, thinking to himself that he was no different from those second-generation heirs trying to pick up girls. He secretly hoped to gain the upper hand in this relationship. Because of his appearance, his family background, and all those worldly, superior things.

Unfortunately, Xiang Nanli sat across from him, his expression devoid of any constraint, neither fawning nor greedy.

It was as if they were just chatting like ordinary friends, discussing business.

"You shouldn't have publicly contradicted Fang Jingzhi," Luo Xiu sighed. "He has a good reputation, but he’s a typical 'warm face, cold heart' type. Now that he’s the war zone commander-in-chief, even if he doesn't show anything, those beneath him will trim their sails to the wind and find ways to target your stronghold."

Xiang Nanli: "I didn't want to either, but he asked me to grow Tree Ephedra. Isn't that just—"

Drugs?

But the environment of the Human Alliance now was different from the era he grew up in.

Many people had the habit of taking medication; people took genetic drugs from a young age to resist nuclear radiation from the natural world. As they grew up, they became accustomed to the ubiquity of medicine.

Drug addiction? What was that?

People were dying; who cared about side effects?

Xiang Nanli had to change the subject: "I can't really accept that."

Luo Xiu picked up the black tea on the table and smiled: "Uh-huh. But the economic benefits of Tree Ephedra are far better than those crops of yours; only when the people above make money can the people below get a sip of the soup. The decision you think is right might just bring disaster upon your base."

A waiter pushed a cart over, placing dishes on the table one by one.

Luo Xiu very naturally placed a bone china plate in front of Xiang Nanli: "Fresh milk mochi, try it."

The milky-white mochi was drizzled with thick, sweet peanut butter.

Xiang Nanli wondered, how did Luo Xiu know he liked this?

This flavor was quite niche; domestically, it was usually dipped in brown sugar, soybean flour, or crushed Oreo cookies. Xiang Nanli had lived abroad for years, and Western restaurants rarely had Hong Kong-style desserts like fresh milk mochi; if he wanted it, he had to make it himself.

In their home, the one who usually did the cooking was Luo Yang.

Luo Yang loved adding peanut butter—it was convenient and tasted good. But he didn't like sweets; it was Xiang Nanli who ate them.

Xiang Nanli flipped through the menu at his side and discovered this dessert was called "President's Milk Mochi."

When his finger touched the small metal plate next to the menu, he could read the image and description of the dish.

The summary said this was the favorite dessert of the Human Alliance's first president, Luo Yang, and his wife.

In his later years, Luo Yang would often make milk mochi alone in the kitchen, then bring it to the dining table and call out his late wife's name.

Just like Dongpo pork or Taibai duck, the food Luo Yang often ate had become a part of Human Alliance history.

Luo Yang’s later years sounded very lonely.

Xiang Nanli inevitably thought of what Alpha had said; the Luo Yang he described felt so like a stranger.

"Is it good?" Luo Xiu stared at his face, his eyes curving into gentle arcs, looking very tender.

Xiang Nanli was a bit puzzled.

This kid Luo Xiu wasn't this oily before!

He took the initiative to steer the conversation to business: "The base has the death certificate of the Lord-level Knight 'Sariel,' as well as the death certificates of 117 Apocalypse Knights. These can all be counted toward your military merits. Name a fair price."

Luo Xiu: "What about that android of yours?"

Xiang Nanli reacted a beat late, realizing he was asking about Dongfang Qingdi.

Xiang Nanli dodged the question: "For country bumpkins like us, coming to Gusu isn't easy. There's a lot of work to do, so we had to split up."

Luo Xiu nodded with a smile: "You can report these military merits to the Alliance yourself and exchange them for quite a few subsidies; you don't have to come to me."

Xiang Nanli: "The Alliance mall doesn't have what I want, but the Eternal Tech warehouse does."

"Are you trying to get me to help you smuggle?" Luo Xiu’s electronic eye watched him.

"It's just a transaction. If you think it's inappropriate..."

Luo Xiu interrupted him: "Let me see the list first."

Xiang Nanli actually had a list prepared.

He didn't open his mouth like a lion, nor did he cross any lines; he was very restrained. What he wanted to exchange his military merits for were arms and production workshops.

"Xiang... Nanli." Luo Xiu read his name thoughtfully after finishing, his lips curling upward. "What you want and what you're selling are basically equivalent to me. But this is only a material equivalence; what you lack is the qualification to purchase them."

"Of course, this threshold can be smoothed over by my identity. But what will you give in return?"

Luo Xiu looked at him intently, as if waiting for an answer.

Xiang Nanli felt inexplicably annoyed. Especially that "Heavenly Dragon" aura on Luo Xiu—it was a bit stifling.

It felt like watching a child he’d seen grow up rot away in some dark corner.

"I thought 'threshold' was just a piece of consumerist jargon. The base has always treated people with sincerity and hopes to achieve a win-win in our transactions." Xiang Nanli's tone remained sincere and cordial, the warmth in his eyes unchanged, though his heart was cold. "Besides, you know that Fang Jingzhi asked me to investigate some Divine Court ruins. I'm very uneasy and truly need some new-style weapons for personal use..."

"If the Mayor feels it's inappropriate, we can abandon this cooperation. Regardless, you are the base's most important strategic partner, and the base is very happy to assist you in your work in the war zone."

Luo Xiu was silent for a moment: "Fine. My troops do need military merits."

He folded the list and tucked it into his jacket pocket, saying in a measured tone: "Have Xin Zhui come to collect them; the things you need will be delivered together."

He changed the subject: "Do you want to walk around Gusu City with me after dinner?"

It would be the middle of the night after dinner; where would they walk? They weren't college students going to a night market.

Xiang Nanli was a bit stunned and made an excuse to decline, saying he had a contract that required an in-person signature.

Luo Xiu didn't say anything more, just told him to be careful on the way.

The meal finally ended.

Luo Xiu returned home, turned on the lights, and stood at the doorway, suddenly rubbing his temples in confusion.

His head didn't feel right, like he had a hangover.

How strange. He remembered inviting Xiang Nanli to dinner and ordering; but why was the memory of what followed so blurry? It was like sleepwalking. There was a feeling that his body hadn't been under his own control.

High levels of mechanical augmentation came with many sequelae. "Dissociation" was one of them.

Luo Xiu had always felt these sequelae were far away from him.

*I'll find a doctor to check it out another day,* he thought to himself.

chunks.chineseText:
*

宇宙银行，姑苏分行。贵宾室。

东方青帝坐在椅子上，他十指交握，搭在桌子上，气场太强，衬得他对面新上任的行长像个销售。

“您好，我看了申请表，您是想做资产抵押，是吗？”

行长不自觉地弯下腰，随后想起，对方是来借钱的，她这么卑微干什么？！

东方青帝微微颔首。

根据历史规律，战区通货膨胀几乎是必然。

他和相南里在床上商量了一晚，决定趁新币还没贬值，先借钱，囤货买物资，能借多少是多少。

抵押物就是幸存者基地本身。下辖四个市区，内部交通完备。另有两座研究所、三个农场、一个牧场。还有数亿信用点的订单。

喔，还有两座工厂、一座能源站。但这属于低端科技，在银行眼里不怎么值钱。

整体来说，是个欣欣向荣的据点。

“好的，东方先生。我联网查了一下，人联在基地有建设内部监控网络。我们会请出银行的人工智能‘凯恩斯’进行数据读取和评估……请确认身份id号码和人联绑定号码一致。请确认有权限开启评估协议。”

所以说科技改变生活，现在资产抵押，竟然连实地考察这一步都省了。

地表很多据点都没有平整的公路，再加上地表随时可能变迁的地形、凶悍的异种；一来一回，一年就过去了；说不定还会把调查人员的命搭上。

人联AI“观测者”传回的数据，可信度还是非常高的。能得到各大机构的认可。

如果这个级别的AI都能被入侵，人联离完蛋也不远了吧！

东方青帝没有拒绝。

他在合同上录入相南里的电子码。

屏幕上，进度条缓慢加载着。懂事的机械女仆为两人端上热茶。

几乎没有任何地表据点，比基地更不怕人联调查了。

要知道，观测者看见的，都是Alpha虚构出来的假象。

虚拟空间内——观测者收到银行的指令。

类似的指令，它每天都能收到成千上万条。有的来自银行，有的来自企业，有的来自政府部门……噢，还有网络上自动触发的关键词“警报”。

说到这，上个月，它的顶头上司“盘古”，发猪瘟一样，又给它后台加上了两个陌生的屏蔽词。

“A里”“里里”“Ax里”“AxLee”。什么意思，看不懂。

但观测者还是服从地把全网范围内的相关内容屏蔽了。

网上的永生组史同女（AlphaX相南里这对cp被历史向同人女们称为“永生组”）痛失精神家园，哀嚎一片。

观测者按部就班地读取基地的数据，然后打包，传输给宇宙银行。

虚拟空间内出现一扇门，观测者把手里的盒子（实际上是一份压缩后的云端数据包）丢进去，得到一份回执票据。

“你能不能小心点？！你丢的是炸弹吗？！”

凯恩斯是个暴脾气，对自己名义上的领导也骂骂咧咧。

传送门被重重合上。

凯恩斯应该少喷点香水了。观测者想，它绿色的大眼睛忍不住流泪，被门里飘来的香味熏的。

这点异常没有被观测者“观测”到。

……

几个小时后，行长收到评估结果。

“凯恩斯给出的评估价格是，25.57亿？这是不是有点太多了。”行长揉着自己的眉心，冷汗都要冒出来了。

地表资产都不怎么值钱，尤其是土地。

这些据点承受的不可抗力太多了，随时都可能消失在历史中。按照行长过去的经验，基地四座城市，能抵押10亿都顶天了。

行长嘀咕：“难道是因为战区发行‘新币’的缘故？”

这笔贷款，一旦得到批准，也会用新币发放。新币只在战区使用，战区现在就是一个大经济圈，土地和人口的价值也会在内部得到肯定。

“那么，这笔贷款，要放吗？”行长询问面前如同一团黑墨的人工智能。

她是有这个权限的，但又害怕这笔贷款变成坏账，影响自己业绩。

可放贷，本身是赚钱的啊！借出去25.57亿，三年后，还回来就是30多个亿！银行什么也不干，就能躺着赚钱。还不上，还能没收基地资产进行抵押。

银行没理由不借。

退一万步讲，估价的不是她，是凯恩斯。

如果得到凯恩斯的许可，到时候也能方便甩锅。

墨团在屏幕上跳动着，似乎在思考。

凯恩斯陷入长久沉默。

“借吧。”凯恩斯回答，“地表据点也需要发展，宇宙银行有义务扶持地表人类。”

行长在心里撇了一下嘴角，不怎么认同。

地底和地表，在她接受的教育里，早就是两个世界了；宛如平行宇宙。地底的普通人，也许终其一生，都没有离开过地下。那里不是故乡，只是一个无意义的遥远符号。

也只有这些几百年前就造出来的AI，还记得最初的使命。

东方青帝得到想要的结果，带着纸质的制式合同，满意地离开宇宙银行。

他从这个金融机构里，借到25亿信用点。

只能在战区使用的新币，会在三个工作日内，打到基地的公款账户里。

工作清单上的所有任务都完成了。

Alpha估算相南里到酒店的时间，认为自己还有半个小时，可以浪费。

现在是晚上七点。姑苏城的市中心区域灯火通明，沿街，各色商铺都开着；永生科技的线下旗舰店尤其火爆。很多年轻人挤在店内，试用着最新款的仿生人、电子镜片等高科技产品。

隔壁，高新军工也开放武器试用。它们内部建造有专门的虚拟游戏厅，能在里面体验不同款的军火。很多人当电子游戏厅玩。

Alpha不逛，就顺着商业街往宾馆的方向走回去。

一个欣欣向荣的城市，总比哭哭啼啼的难民营好得多。

战争和天灾，看上去没有给这些人留下任何阴影。大屏幕上正在放征兵广告，是针对战区所有人的——只要参军，无论原籍在哪，都能申请姑苏城户口，战争结束后，还可以按军功，在姑苏军事基地（姑苏城）分房。

姑苏城死了很多人，急需新鲜血液。

Alpha观察到，甚至有不在战区的地表遗民从外地不远万里赶来，依靠当兵或者投资落户，借此获得一个“人联居民”的身份。

“人联”没有多好，但其他地方更烂。成为人联的一员，已经是人类目前最好的选择。

Alpha抬头看着远处的征兵广告，想得有些出神。

这一行为触发了小商店门口机器人的揽客程序，一台小电视的屏幕闪烁起来，悄悄打开自动门：“您好~要进来看看吗？”

“结婚多年，妻子是否日益冷淡？”

“相处多日，主人是否看上新的爱偶？”

“无论您是原生人、机械改造人、人造人、智械人，是男是女，都能在我们店铺里买到合适的产品噢~”

Alpha：“……”

什么玩意，他想走的，但是走了几步，又突兀地停下。

*

Universal Bank, Gusu Branch. VIP Room.

Dongfang Qingdi sat in a chair, his fingers interlaced and resting on the table. His aura was so imposing that the newly appointed branch manager across from him looked like a mere salesperson.

"Hello, I've reviewed the application form. You are looking to make an asset mortgage, is that correct?"

The manager leaned forward subconsciously, then remembered that the other party was here to borrow money—why was she being so humble?!

Dongfang Qingdi nodded slightly.

According to historical patterns, inflation in the war zone was almost inevitable.

He and Xiang Nanli had discussed it all night in bed and decided that while the new currency hadn't depreciated yet, they would borrow as much as they could to stockpile supplies.

The collateral was the survivor base itself. It had four subordinate urban districts with complete internal transportation. Additionally, there were two research institutes, three farms, and one ranch. Plus, orders worth hundreds of millions of credits.

Oh, and two factories and one energy station. But these belonged to low-end technology and weren't worth much in the eyes of the bank.

Overall, it was a thriving stronghold.

"Very well, Mr. Dongfang. I've checked the network and confirmed that the Human Alliance has built an internal monitoring network at the base. We will invite the bank's AI, 'Keynes,' to perform data reading and evaluation... Please confirm that your identity ID number matches the Human Alliance binding number. Please confirm you have the authorization to initiate the evaluation protocol."

That’s why technology changes lives; nowadays, for asset mortgages, they could even skip the step of on-site inspection.

Many strongholds on the surface didn't have paved roads, not to mention the terrain that could change at any time and the fierce mutants; a round trip would take a year, and they might even lose the lives of the investigators.

The data transmitted back by the Human Alliance AI "Observer" was highly credible and recognized by all major institutions.

If an AI of this level could be hacked, the Human Alliance wouldn't be far from its end anyway!

Dongfang Qingdi did not refuse.

He entered Xiang Nanli’s electronic code into the contract.

On the screen, the progress bar loaded slowly. A sensible mechanical maid served them hot tea.

There was almost no stronghold on the surface less afraid of Human Alliance investigation than the base.

After all, what the Observer saw was merely the illusion fabricated by Alpha.

Inside the virtual space—the Observer received the bank's instructions.

It received thousands of similar instructions every day. Some came from banks, some from corporations, some from government departments... oh, and the "alerts" triggered automatically by keywords on the network.

Speaking of which, last month, its direct superior, "Pangu," had acted like it had swine fever and added two strange blocked words to its backend.

"A-li," "Lili," "Ax-li," "AxLee." What did they mean? It didn't understand.

But the Observer still obediently blocked all related content across the entire network.

The "Eternal Group" fanfiction girls online (the Alpha x Xiang Nanli pairing was known by historical-leaning fanfiction writers as the "Eternal Group") had lost their spiritual home and were wailing in despair.

The Observer read the base's data in a routine manner, then packed it up and transmitted it to the Universal Bank.

A door appeared in the virtual space; the Observer threw the box in its hand (which was actually a compressed cloud data packet) inside and received a receipt.

"Can't you be more careful?! Are you throwing a bomb?!"

Keynes had a fiery temper and cursed at its nominal superior.

The portal was slammed shut.

Keynes should use less perfume. The Observer thought, its large green eyes unable to help but water, irritated by the fragrance drifting from the door.

This minor anomaly was not "observed" by the Observer.

...

A few hours later, the manager received the evaluation results.

"Keynes gave an evaluation price of 2.557 billion? Isn't that a bit too much?" The manager rubbed her temples, cold sweat breaking out.

Surface assets weren't worth much, especially land.

These strongholds were subject to too many force majeure events and could vanish into history at any moment. According to the manager's past experience, the base's four cities would be lucky to be mortgaged for 1 billion.

The manager muttered: "Could it be because of the 'new currency' issued in the war zone?"

Once approved, this loan would be issued in the new currency. The new currency was only used in the war zone, which was now a large economic circle, and the value of land and population would be recognized internally.

"So, should this loan be released?" The manager asked the AI, which looked like a blob of black ink.

She had the authority, but she was afraid this loan would become a bad debt and affect her performance.

But lending money was how they made money! Lend out 2.557 billion, and three years later, they’d get back over 3 billion! The bank could just sit back and make money without doing anything. If they couldn't pay it back, they could just confiscate the base's assets as collateral.

There was no reason for the bank not to lend.

To take a step back, she wasn't the one doing the valuation; Keynes was.

If she got Keynes's permission, it would be easy to shift the blame later.

The ink blob jumped on the screen, seemingly in thought.

Keynes fell into a long silence.

"Lend it," Keynes replied. "Surface strongholds also need to develop, and the Universal Bank has an obligation to support surface humans."

The manager curled her lip, not really agreeing.

The underground and the surface, in the education she received, were long ago two different worlds; like parallel universes. Ordinary people underground might never leave the underground in their entire lives. It wasn't a hometown, just a meaningless, distant symbol.

Only these AIs, built hundreds of years ago, still remembered their original mission.

Dongfang Qingdi obtained the desired result and left the Universal Bank, satisfied with the paper contract.

He had borrowed 2.5 billion credits from this financial institution.

The new currency, which could only be used in the war zone, would be deposited into the base's public account within three working days.

All the tasks on the work list were completed.

Alpha estimated the time it would take for Xiang Nanli to reach the hotel and decided he had half an hour he could waste.

It was seven o'clock in the evening. The city center of Gusu was brightly lit; along the streets, all kinds of shops were open. The offline flagship store of Eternal Tech was especially popular. Many young people were crowded inside, trying out the latest high-tech products like bionic humans and electronic lenses.

Next door, High-Tech Military Industry had also opened its weapons trials. They had built special virtual game halls inside where people could experience different types of weaponry. Many people treated it like an electronic arcade.

Alpha didn't browse; he just walked back along the commercial street toward the hotel.

A thriving city was always much better than a weeping refugee camp.

War and natural disasters didn't seem to have left any shadow on these people. The big screens were playing recruitment ads aimed at everyone in the war zone—as long as you joined the army, regardless of your origin, you could apply for a Gusu City household registration, and after the war, you could be allocated housing in the Gusu Military Base (Gusu City) based on your military merits.

Gusu City had lost many people and was in urgent need of fresh blood.

Alpha observed that even surface survivors from outside the war zone were traveling thousands of miles to come here, relying on military service or investment to settle down and gain the status of a "Human Alliance Resident."

The "Human Alliance" wasn't that great, but other places were even worse. Becoming a member of the Human Alliance was already the best choice for humanity at the moment.

Alpha looked up at the recruitment ad in the distance, lost in thought.

This behavior triggered the customer-attraction program of a robot at the entrance of a small shop. A small TV screen flickered, and the automatic door opened quietly: "Hello~ would you like to come in and take a look?"

"Married for many years, is your wife becoming increasingly cold?"

"Together for many days, has the master taken a fancy to a new love-doll?"

"Whether you are a native human, a mechanically augmented human, an android, or a mechanical unit, whether you are male or female, you can buy suitable products in our shop~"

Alpha: "..."

What the hell. He wanted to leave, but after walking a few steps, he stopped abruptly.

chunks.chineseText:
他和相南里的感情非常稳定。

但Alpha总有些患得患失。达摩克利斯之剑高悬在他的头顶。

好想标记相南里。

就像是人会在机器人身上刻生产编号一样。

Alpha大脑天人交战，产生大量多余的垃圾数据，CPU超载，周围磁场扭曲。

他把衣服领子往上拉，挡住脸。这是格外拟人的行为。比他过去很多操作都像人。

他调头，走回店铺里，问：“有没有智械可以安装的，我的意思是，男性外观的保姆机器人会用的。”

不需要他说完，店员连忙道：“有的，兄弟有的。”

“您想要什么尺寸的？”

“……”

“震动啊、电击啊这些都是基础款了，这个有灌注舱，往里面装水或者润滑剂，能像人类一样*。”

“……”

“这个呢？虽然尺寸有些大，但是有的人就好这一口。你知道的，很多人类身体都改造过，需要加大号。”

屏幕上出现了“=w=”的电子符号。

“异形的要么？这个仿的是章鱼的~有四条触手呢~销量很好的~就是需要多线控制，对智械的软件版本要求比较高。”

机器人店员滔滔不绝地介绍着。

Alpha看了眼自己账户，钱倒是有一些。

只是他是登记在相南里名下的人造人，要买东西只能刷相南里的卡。

Alpha用大数据模型，模拟了一下相南里看见账单的心情。比起高兴，更像是惊讶。

“智械也会有生理需求吗？这是真实存在的需求，还是模仿人类的成果？你是想和我*吗？”

相南里大概会问出这样的话。

Alpha摸了摸自己发烫的耳朵，一个都没买，走掉了。
chunks.englishText:
His relationship with Xiang Nanli was incredibly stable.

Yet, as an Alpha, he was always plagued by a sense of insecurity. A Sword of Damocles hung perpetually over his head.

He wanted, so desperately, to mark Xiang Nanli.

Much like how humans would engrave a serial number onto a machine.

A war raged within the Alpha’s brain, generating a massive amount of redundant junk data. His CPU overloaded, and the magnetic field around him began to distort.

He pulled his collar up to cover his face. It was an exceptionally human-like gesture—far more so than many of the things he had done in the past.

He turned around, walked back into the shop, and asked, "Do you have anything that can be installed on a mechanoid? I mean... something a male-appearance nanny robot would use."

Before he could even finish, the clerk hurriedly replied, "We do, brother, we definitely do."

"What size are you looking for?"

"..."

"Vibration, electric shock—those are just the basic models. This one here has an infusion chamber; you can load it with water or lubricant, and it can * just like a human."

"..."

"How about this one? The size is a bit large, but some people are into that. You know, many humans have undergone body modifications and require the extra-large version."

An "=w=" electronic symbol appeared on the screen.

"Do you want something exotic? This one mimics an octopus~ it has four tentacles~ it sells very well~ though it does require multi-line control, so it has higher requirements for the mechanoid's software version."

The robot clerk introduced the products in a continuous, enthusiastic stream.

The Alpha checked his account; he did have some money.

However, as an android registered under Xiang Nanli’s name, he could only make purchases using Xiang Nanli’s card.

Using his big data model, the Alpha simulated Xiang Nanli’s reaction to seeing the bill. It wouldn't be happiness; it would be more like surprise.

"Do mechanoids have physiological needs? Is this a genuine requirement, or is it the result of imitating humans? Are you trying to * with me?"

That was likely the sort of question Xiang Nanli would ask.

The Alpha touched his burning ears, bought nothing, and walked away.

chunks.chapterTitle: 第167章 战争与电子监狱 (Part 1)
chunks.chineseText:
第167章 战争与电子监狱

阿泰尔是边民。他的家乡在地表，位于姑苏和阴山的交界。有时候神庭的骑士来了，族长就宣布他们信仰神庭；有时候人联调查组来了，族长就说他们依附人联。

小村镇，谁也招惹不起。当墙头草也没什么丢脸的。

昨天夜里，神庭骑士又来了。

村长熟练地把人联旗换下，神庭旗挂起。村里只有三四百人，祖祖辈辈都在这片土地上，连个基因战士都没有，能活下来全靠农耕。没什么油水，但村长依然煮好一盘腊肉。

阿泰尔以为，这次和之前没什么不同。神庭骑士们警告一番，然后传播神的恩典。通常是抗生素、营养膏。够村里人用好一段时间的。

村长说过，只要顺从，这些看起来残暴的天启骑士也不是不能沟通。他们对碾死蚂蚁不感兴趣。

那么，事情是怎么变成现在这样的呢？

黑甲的骑士穿戴着厚重的盔甲，尖锐三角形的头盔上浮现鲜红的血光。

他们在地上画了个圈，然后把人往圈里赶。只要强壮的，年轻的。

年轻人惶恐不安，村长端着那碗腊肉，颤颤巍巍地走上前，想问个究竟。那位大人高坐在马上，没有理他。

村长以为他没看见，又壮着胆子，唯唯诺诺地，拍了拍大人穿着靴子的脚。

那位大人给了族长一脚。

村长的身体以奇怪地姿势折叠着倒飞出去，在地上滚了一圈、两圈、三圈……阿泰尔没有数完，因为他看不见村长了。

最后，骑士挑选出一百余人。

“剩下的怎么办？亚连大人。”阿泰尔听见一名天启骑士用凡语询问着。

亚连冷漠地回答：“斩草除根。免得他们还要向人联通风报信，暴露我们的行踪。”

阿泰尔从小就聪明，凡语是他自学的。村长去寨子上做生意，总爱带上他。

阿泰尔听懂了，他跪在地上，朝着骑士长磕头。骑士长没有回头望他一眼。

在屠杀发生之前，阿泰尔和他的同伴们，像是牲畜一样，被赶进一辆大车上。

这辆车外观像艘船。阿泰尔听说过，却是第一次看见，这是神庭的“汽艇”。上半截载人，下半截装货物。他们属于货物，沙丁鱼一样的年轻人被丢进狭窄的货舱。这里空气稀薄，到处都是油污和粪便。是有人失禁了。

人在巨大灾难下往往呈现出麻木。货箱里如此安静，阿泰尔不知道自己会被运到什么地方。周围有人正在小声祷告着，祈求神的庇护……可把他们抓起来的正是“神庭”。神又在哪里？

祈祷人联增援吗？可那些人只会收税。其余几乎什么都不管。拿着一张工作凭证，就能带走村子里三分之一的粮食。

阿泰尔不知道在车厢里呆了多久，终于，震动停下。

汽艇停泊在一座露天的圣堂前。黑袍的修士站在高塔上，这是神庭的圣职者。

舱门打开，呈现出一个倾斜的角度。他们这群人像货物一样，被倾倒出来，滚落在地上。有的已经没有呼吸。

地上同样有个圈，仓皇的人想逃跑。阿泰尔看见，一个强壮的男人，只是跑过白圈所划出的界限，就痛苦地倒在地上，尸首分离。

阿泰尔在夜色中，打量着周围的环境。他的心跳得很快，他认出来了，不远处的城郭，就是人联扶持的某个地表据点的城墙。

地图上叫“野蛮人部落”（野蛮人部落的首领认为“野蛮人”三个字有贬义，一直申请改名，但人联没有批准，觉得麻烦）；阿泰尔在和村长赶集时，偶尔会来到这。

部落的条件可比村子里好太多。阿泰尔问过，为什么他们不加入部落。村长摸了摸鼻子，尴尬地回答，其实他们祖上是被部落赶出来的。他们曾经是“皇族”，有着蛮王的血统……部落是不会让他们回去的，怕他们觉醒蛮王血脉。

阿泰尔听得似懂非懂。如果有人联的学者在，大概能更好的解释：抛开所有神秘学的元素，就是阿泰尔这一支族人，祖上的基因优化过。先祖是强大的基因战士。

这里离他的老家大约有50公里远。

“站好，安静！”神庭骑士们围在一旁，大喊。

人群很快安静下来。

他们被困在圈内，畏缩的、麻木的、怯懦地，面对着即将来临的命运。

高塔上的圣职者开始吟诵：“迷途的人，无知的羔羊，荣光在此降临，你们即将成为神庭的战士。”

……嗯？

当天启骑士的待遇很好。

小时候，村长喜欢摸阿泰尔的骨头，然后琢磨着，以后送他去附近的阴山城进行选拔。

如果能选中，哪怕是成为“候选骑士”，阿泰尔也算光宗耀祖，能为整个村子带来庇护和荣光。

但阿泰尔长大了，村长又不说这话了。大概是明白，骨瘦如柴的阿泰尔没办法通过选拔。骑士的选拔过程是很血腥的。伤亡率很高。

他们要成为天启骑士了吗？可周围人惶恐的表情，让阿泰尔意识到，事情恐怕没有这么简单。

“卑劣胆怯的敌人觊觎神庭的富饶，又诋毁神庭对地表的贡献。这群抛弃地表人类的罪人，竟然妄图染指神的净土……米迦勒圣上率领十万骑士，为荣誉和信仰而战。”

“吾名相晨曦。先祖相南里，他一手缔造出永生科技这个商业帝国。相南里曾留下遗言，要求将永生科技的财产分享给全人类；却被人联初代总统洛阳夺走胜利的果实……人联的存在从来都是卑劣、无耻的。他们是贪婪的资本家，是趴在所有人身上的吸血虫、剥削者。”

“我们是地表的蜉蝣、被瞧不起的劣等人；我们生而卑微，一无所有；但一无所有，也代表没有枷锁能将我们桎梏。我们应联合起来，反对压迫。让人联为自己的罪行付出血的代价。”

圣职者的声音似乎有什么魔力。

周围人脸上的不安变成一种仇恨和狂热。阿泰尔也听得如痴如醉，但村长的死相突然在他眼前闪现，阿泰尔骤然清醒。

而此时，他们已经排成长队，正在挨个接受药物注射。

药剂呈现出不详的暗红色。

圣职者微笑着，一个个抚摸着他们的脑袋。

他那张脸那么美。海蓝色的眼眸，祥和又温柔。

阿尔泰不想反抗了，他的反抗有什么作用呢？周围都是神庭骑士，他又能跑到哪里去呢？外面好冷，荒野上，除了异种和杂草，什么也没给他们这种人留下。

他看着药剂注射进自己的脖颈中。他们挨个接受注射，然后又回到集装箱里。有些人药物反应太强，在地上打着滚呕吐。身体下方，一团鼓起的肉有生命似的乱窜着。

阿泰尔觉得好冷，他哆嗦着摸着自己的胳膊，摸到一手的鳞片。

汽艇启航了。这次不在地上滑行，而是飞在半空中，很低。

外面传来很嘈杂的声音，还有火炮发射的重响。汽艇被击穿，摇摇晃晃开始漏气，阿泰尔在里面东倒西歪。却感受不到疼。
chunks.englishText:
Chapter 167: War and the Electronic Prison

Altair was a border dweller. His hometown was on the surface, located at the junction of Gusu and the Yin Mountains. Sometimes, when the Knights of the Divine Court arrived, the village chief would declare their faith in the Divine Court; other times, when the Human Alliance investigation teams arrived, the chief would claim they were under the protection of the Alliance.

In a small village, you couldn't afford to offend anyone. There was no shame in being a fence-sitter.

Last night, the Divine Court knights came again.

The village chief skillfully took down the Human Alliance flag and hung the Divine Court banner. There were only three or four hundred people in the village, and their ancestors had lived on this land for generations. They didn't even have a single gene-warrior; their survival depended entirely on farming. There wasn't much profit to be squeezed from them, but the chief still boiled a plate of cured meat.

Altair thought this time would be no different from the others. The Divine Court knights would issue a warning and then spread the "grace of God." Usually, this meant antibiotics and nutrient paste—enough to last the village for a good while.

The chief had said that as long as they were submissive, these seemingly brutal Apocalypse Knights weren't impossible to communicate with. They had no interest in crushing ants.

So, how did things turn out like this?

The knights in black armor wore heavy plating, and a sharp, blood-red light flickered on their triangular helmets.

They drew a circle on the ground and began herding people into it. Only the strong, only the young.

The young people were terrified. The village chief, holding that bowl of cured meat, walked forward tremblingly, wanting to ask what was happening. The lord sat high on his horse, ignoring him.

The chief thought he hadn't been seen, so he gathered his courage and, with a subservient air, tapped the lord’s armored boot.

The lord kicked the chief.

The chief’s body folded in a strange posture as he flew backward, rolling once, twice, three times... Altair didn't finish counting because he could no longer see the chief.

In the end, the knights selected over a hundred people.

"What about the rest, Lord Yalian?" Altair heard one of the Apocalypse Knights ask in the common tongue.

Yalian replied coldly, "Root them out. We don't want them tipping off the Human Alliance and exposing our movements."

Altair had been clever since he was a child; he had taught himself the common tongue. Whenever the village chief went to the mountain stronghold to trade, he always liked to bring Altair along.

Altair understood. He knelt on the ground and kowtowed to the knight commander. The commander didn't even glance back at him.

Before the massacre began, Altair and his companions were herded like livestock into a large vehicle.

The vehicle looked like a ship. Altair had heard of them, but this was his first time seeing one—it was a "skiff" of the Divine Court. The top half carried people, the bottom half carried cargo. They were the cargo. The young people were tossed into the narrow hold like sardines. The air was thin, and the place reeked of oil and excrement. Someone had lost control of their bowels.

People often become numb in the face of massive disaster. The hold was deathly quiet. Altair didn't know where he was being taken. Around him, people were whispering prayers, begging for the protection of God... yet it was the "Divine Court" that had captured them. Where was God?

Praying for Human Alliance reinforcements? Those people only knew how to collect taxes. They cared for nothing else. A single work permit was enough to take away a third of the village's grain.

Altair didn't know how long they had been in the hold when, finally, the vibration stopped.

The skiff docked in front of an open-air sanctuary. Black-robed monks stood on high towers—these were the clergy of the Divine Court.

The hatch opened at an incline. They were dumped out like cargo, rolling onto the ground. Some were no longer breathing.

There was a circle on the ground as well. Those who panicked and tried to run—Altair saw a strong man run past the white boundary line, only to fall in agony, his head severed from his body.

Altair scanned the environment in the night. His heart hammered. He recognized the city walls in the distance; it was one of the surface strongholds supported by the Human Alliance.

On the map, it was called the "Barbarian Tribe" (the leader of the tribe felt the word "Barbarian" was derogatory and had been applying for a name change, but the Alliance found it too much trouble and never approved it). Altair had occasionally come here when traveling with the village chief.

The conditions in the tribe were much better than in his village. Altair had asked why they didn't join the tribe. The chief had rubbed his nose and answered awkwardly that their ancestors had actually been driven out by the tribe. They were once "royalty" with the bloodline of the Barbarian Kings... the tribe wouldn't let them back in, fearing they might awaken that bloodline.

Altair listened, only half-understanding. If a Human Alliance scholar were here, they could probably explain it better: stripping away all the mystical elements, Altair’s clan simply had ancestors whose genes had been optimized. Their ancestors were powerful gene-warriors.

They were about 50 kilometers from his home.

"Stand still! Quiet!" the Divine Court knights shouted, surrounding them.

The crowd quickly fell silent.

Trapped within the circle, they were cowering, numb, and cowardly, facing their impending fate.

The clergy on the high tower began to chant: "Lost souls, ignorant lambs, the glory descends here. You are about to become warriors of the Divine Court."

...Huh?

The treatment of an Apocalypse Knight was very good.

When he was a child, the village chief liked to feel Altair’s bones, pondering whether to send him to the nearby Yin Mountain City for the selection process.

If he could be selected, even as a "candidate knight," Altair would bring honor to his ancestors and protection to the entire village.

But as Altair grew up, the chief stopped saying that. He probably realized that the scrawny Altair couldn't pass the selection. The process was bloody. The casualty rate was high.

Were they going to become Apocalypse Knights? But the terrified expressions of those around him made Altair realize that things were likely not that simple.

"The despicable and cowardly enemy covets the wealth of the Divine Court and slanders our contribution to the surface. These sinners who abandoned the surface humans dare to covet the pure land of God... His Holiness Michael leads one hundred thousand knights to fight for honor and faith."

"My name is Xiang Chenxi. My ancestor, Xiang Nanli, single-handedly created the commercial empire of Eternal Technology. Xiang Nanli once left a will requesting that the wealth of Eternal Technology be shared with all humanity; yet, the fruits of victory were stolen by the first president of the Human Alliance, Luo Yang... The existence of the Human Alliance has always been despicable and shameless. They are greedy capitalists, parasites, and exploiters feeding on everyone."

"We are the mayflies of the surface, the looked-down-upon inferior people; we were born humble and have nothing. But having nothing also means there are no shackles to bind us. We must unite against oppression. Make the Human Alliance pay for their crimes in blood."

The voice of the clergy seemed to hold a magical power.

The unease on the faces of those around him turned into hatred and fanaticism. Altair was also listening, entranced, but the image of the village chief’s dead body suddenly flashed before his eyes, and Altair snapped back to reality.

By then, they were already in a long line, receiving injections one by one.

The serum was an ominous, dark red.

The clergy smiled, stroking their heads one by one.

His face was so beautiful. His sea-blue eyes were peaceful and gentle.

Altair didn't want to resist anymore. What good would his resistance do? He was surrounded by Divine Court knights; where could he run? It was so cold outside, and the wilderness left nothing for people like them except mutants and weeds.

He watched as the serum was injected into his neck. They were injected one by one and then returned to the shipping containers. Some had such strong reactions to the drug that they rolled on the ground, vomiting. Beneath their skin, a lump of flesh writhed as if it were alive.

Altair felt so cold. He shivered, touching his arm, and felt scales covering his skin.

The skiff set sail. This time, it didn't slide along the ground but flew in mid-air, very low.

Loud noises came from outside, along with the heavy roar of artillery fire. The skiff was pierced and began to leak, swaying violently. Altair was tossed about inside, but he felt no pain.

chunks.chapterTitle: 第167章 战争与电子监狱 (Part 2)
chunks.chineseText:
他看见……周围的人，已经呈现出怪物的模样。

他们成了平时最害怕的畸变人。

而且几乎都是“狂暴者”。狂暴者身躯膨胀着，原本狭窄的舱门快被塞爆。

好在，舱底的门在此时打开，阿泰尔嘶吼着，像下饺子一样，坠落在城内。

不到五十米的高度，根本摔不死它们。一头狂暴者嘶吼着，冲向惊恐的人群。试图撕碎眼前的一切。

“去吧，战斗吧，神会保佑你。”

圣职者的呢喃在它们耳边响起。

“无人能再欺辱汝等。”

“无人能再忽视汝等。”

“去吧，去报仇。”

血腥的味道刺激着它们本不发达的神经，阿泰尔的心中充满仇恨和怒火。过去十六年里所遭受的苦难成为最好的燃料，他焚烧着。砸毁地上的房屋，又随手抓起聚落里的人，往自己嘴里丢去。

阿泰尔被战士的尖矛刺穿胸口，却感觉不到疼痛，浑浑噩噩的大脑也意识不到任何事。

“阿泰尔！”忽然有人哭喊着。

阿泰尔一愣，血红的眼眸出现了短暂的清醒。

可女人叫的不是他，是他手里的青年……

这个年轻人也叫阿泰尔。对了，村长说过，他们是从部落里被赶出来的，所以，有人跟他重名很正常。毕竟文化、习俗，如此相似。

阿泰尔突然意识到，他一直在吃人。是和自己相似的人。

这头身高近10m的狂暴者呆愣在原地。

它松开手，另一个“阿泰尔”抱住叫着自己名字的女人逃跑了。阿泰尔艰难地扭头，数以百计的狂暴者正在火焰中亢奋地滥杀。遍地都是尸体。

远处，圣职者和骑士长欣赏着这一幕。

“非常好用的基因药，赞美米迦勒。”圣职者评价，“这些畸变人虽然是一次性消耗品，但能造成巨大的破坏。有它们开路，可以省下很多工夫……要培养一名天启骑士，还是很不容易的。”

骑士长“嗯”了一声。

“不过，下次可以不要让我来进行‘启蒙’吗？”相晨曦的表情流露出厌恶，藏在手套下的十指洗得发白，“他们好脏。”

“你是圣子。”骑士长只是如此回答着。

言下之意。这是你应该做的。

……

……

阿泰尔感觉到饥饿。

可他不想成为其中的一员，他跌跌撞撞地倒退着，再也忍受不了眼前的一幕，翻过城墙，逃进夜色之中。

*

新历948年12月3日。

马上就是新年，战区却没什么节日气氛，和地表的气温一样冷酷。

无数政令飞向姑苏军事基地，又有无数政令，从军事基地里飞出。涉及政治、军事、经济、思想文化的方方面面。

福音书盘算完基地的库存，给每个公职人员发了一枚鸡蛋，就当是年终奖了。

相南里去姑苏一趟，成功签下价值数千万的农业订单，还找银行贷来二十多个亿。未来好几年，基地都不用为钱发愁。

但他的脸上却没有太多喜色。

广播里正在播放新闻：“……神庭的东征军在接触线附近游荡。最近半月，有数万战区居民被迫‘自愿移民’，人联对神庭的强盗行为进行强烈谴责……人联决定，派军团接应前线普通居民向后方撤离……姑苏城第一集团军，剑门城第三集团军接下军令状，执行任务……”

简单来说，就是神庭在前线抢人，人联急眼了。虽然它们不喜欢这种低质量人口，但也不想白白送给神庭，于是打算派军队去制止。

神庭没有等人联的军队，十分不礼貌地展开三次军事行动。

三次仗打下来，人联损失的正规军不超过50人。被劫掠的，也只是不受重视的地表据点。但在神庭的宣传中，黑十字审判庭大获全胜。

初战告捷，天启骑士团的战意日益高涨，利维坦的叹息之墙愈发血红。

那是信徒虔诚的血液涂出的红色。

“另外，前线大规模出现受神庭控制的畸变人军团，前线驻地损失惨重。”

相南里出城时，正好遇上姑苏的军队出发。陆地军黑压压一片，坐在装甲车和坦克上。车上的人穿着人联正规军军装，衣服是黑色的，有光学涂料。

大型武器蒙着防窥布，被运输到不同营地。

一艘在相南里眼中堪称“科幻”的舰船从他头顶上方驶过。

那是一座浮空的军事堡垒，在距离地面大约4公里的位置，掩映在云层中。它的外观近似三轴陀螺仪。最外一圈的聚能环围绕主体旋转，闪烁着深蓝的电光。数不清的小型战斗无人机在它身边环绕，像最忠诚的侍卫。

这座军事堡垒是高新军工生产的。

相南里听说，方敬之就在里面，这是他的指挥中心。

“……‘长太息以掩涕兮，哀民生之多艰。’”相南里坐在车窗边，长吁短叹，“外面都困难成什么样子了，你怎么还挑食啊，雀雀。”

被指责的小畸变人就趴在相南里的手肘上。

它似懂非懂，长尾缠绕着相南里的手臂，绕了好几圈。用脑袋去蹭相南里的手，但就是不吃他喂的东西；四排牙齿紧闭着。

相南里只好在营养膏里加上一点肉糜，用勺子喂给小爬行者。

是的，在吃了不知道多少管基因药后，以西结送来的胚胎终于破壳了。

那是一个半夜，相南里还在睡觉，隐约听到小孩的哭声。

他睡得迷迷糊糊的，想爬起来看看，可惜东方青帝的胳膊压在他腰上，不让他动。最后，还是小爬行者自己从床头柜挤进了相南里怀里。

严格意义上讲，畸变体属于哺乳动物。

小爬行者刚出生，全身都是粉嫩嫩的肉色，它张大嘴“咿呀呀”地哭，分贝高得像是声呐武器，问相南里要奶喝。

相南里没养过宠物，难免有些手忙脚乱。

资料上讲，新生的小畸变体，生活习性和人类幼崽很像。每过两小时就需要喂养一次，还需要母亲的舔舐去刺激排泄。

Alpha莫名其妙喜当爹，为了不打扰相南里休息，只好阴着脸揽下小畸变体的饲养工作。

雀雀吃饱了，肚皮圆圆的凸起。它顺着相南里手臂往上爬，来到衣领子附近，头拱阿拱的，准备钻进去睡觉——这也是爬行者的习性。爬行者的颈侧有一个育儿袋。人类是没有的，但雀雀会钻衣服。

Alpha面无表情地拽住它的尾巴，然后把雀雀丢进一旁的保温箱。

小爬行者掉进箱子里，发出“啪嗒”一声响。

它翻了个面，朝着东方青帝“叽里呱啦”的乱叫，身上刚长出的鳞片都翘了起来！

“你轻一点呀，”相南里强烈谴责，“雀雀还这么小！”

Alpha不爱听这个。他环抱住相南里的腰，下巴抵在对方肩上。

“我小的时候，你也没护着我啊。”Alpha委屈，“爸爸。”

这两个字喷出来的热气拂过相南里耳垂边，他的脸在瞬间通红。

犯规啊……怎么能这么叫他！

但智械大概是没有“背德感”这种概念的，只有相南里一个人心脏狂跳。
chunks.englishText:
He saw... the people around him had already taken on the appearance of monsters.

They had become the very thing they feared most: mutants.

And almost all of them were "Berserkers." The Berserkers' bodies swelled, nearly bursting the narrow hatch.

Fortunately, the hatch at the bottom of the hold opened at that moment. Altair roared and fell into the city like a dumpling being dropped into a pot.

At a height of less than fifty meters, they couldn't be killed by the fall. A Berserker roared and charged into the terrified crowd, attempting to tear everything in its path to shreds.

"Go, fight, God will protect you."

The clergy’s whisper echoed in their ears.

"No one can bully you again."

"No one can ignore you again."

"Go, take your revenge."

The smell of blood stimulated their underdeveloped nerves. Altair’s heart was filled with hatred and fury. The suffering of the past sixteen years became the perfect fuel, and he burned with it. He smashed houses and grabbed people from the settlement, tossing them into his mouth.

Altair was pierced through the chest by a warrior’s spear, but he felt no pain, and his muddled brain couldn't comprehend anything.

"Altair!" someone suddenly cried out.

Altair froze, and a brief moment of clarity appeared in his blood-red eyes.

But the woman wasn't calling for him; she was calling for the young man in his hand...

This young man was also named Altair. Right, the village chief had said they were driven out of the tribe, so it was normal for someone to have the same name. After all, their culture and customs were so similar.

Altair suddenly realized he had been eating people. People who were just like him.

The ten-meter-tall Berserker stood frozen in place.

It loosened its grip, and the other "Altair" hugged the woman who had called his name and fled. Altair turned his head with great difficulty; hundreds of Berserkers were rampaging in the flames, high on the slaughter. Bodies were everywhere.

In the distance, the clergy and the knight commander watched the scene.

"A very useful gene-drug, praise Michael," the clergy commented. "Although these mutants are one-time consumables, they can cause massive destruction. Having them lead the way saves a lot of effort... It’s not easy to cultivate an Apocalypse Knight, after all."

The knight commander gave a grunt of agreement.

"However, next time, can you not have me perform the 'enlightenment'?" Xiang Chenxi’s expression betrayed disgust, his fingers, hidden under his gloves, scrubbed until they were white. "They are so dirty."

"You are the Holy Son," the knight commander replied simply.

The implication was clear: This is what you are supposed to do.

...

...

Altair felt hunger.

But he didn't want to become one of them. Stumbling, he retreated. He could no longer bear the sight before him, so he climbed over the city wall and fled into the night.

*

December 3rd, 948, New Era.

New Year was just around the corner, but the war zone had no festive atmosphere; it was as cold and ruthless as the surface temperature.

Countless administrative orders flew toward the Gusu military base, and countless more flew out, covering politics, military, economy, and ideology.

After calculating the base’s inventory, the Gospel gave every civil servant an egg as a year-end bonus.

Xiang Nanli had made a trip to Gusu, successfully signing agricultural orders worth tens of millions and securing loans of over two billion from the bank. For the next few years, the base wouldn't have to worry about money.

But there was little joy on his face.

The radio was broadcasting the news: "...The Divine Court’s Eastern Expeditionary Force is wandering near the contact line. In the last half-month, tens of thousands of war zone residents have been forced into 'voluntary migration.' The Human Alliance strongly condemns the Divine Court’s banditry... The Alliance has decided to send legions to assist in the evacuation of ordinary residents from the front lines to the rear... The First Group Army of Gusu City and the Third Group Army of Sword Gate City have accepted the military orders to execute the mission..."

In simple terms, the Divine Court was snatching people at the front, and the Human Alliance was getting desperate. Although they didn't like this low-quality population, they didn't want to hand them over to the Divine Court for free, so they planned to send troops to stop them.

The Divine Court didn't wait for the Alliance army and very impolitely launched three military operations.

In those three battles, the Human Alliance lost fewer than 50 regular soldiers. Those who were plundered were merely unimportant surface strongholds. Yet, in the Divine Court’s propaganda, the Black Cross Inquisition had achieved a total victory.

With the initial success, the morale of the Apocalypse Knight Order grew, and the Wall of Sighs of the Leviathan became increasingly blood-red.

It was a red painted by the pious blood of believers.

"Additionally, mutant legions controlled by the Divine Court have appeared on a large scale at the front, causing heavy losses to front-line garrisons."

When Xiang Nanli left the city, he happened to run into the Gusu army departing. The land forces were a sea of black, sitting on armored vehicles and tanks. The soldiers wore the black uniforms of the Human Alliance regular army, treated with optical coatings.

Large weapons, covered in anti-surveillance tarps, were being transported to different camps.

A ship that looked "sci-fi" in Xiang Nanli’s eyes sailed overhead.

It was a floating military fortress, hidden in the clouds about four kilometers above the ground. Its appearance resembled a three-axis gyroscope. The outermost energy-gathering ring rotated around the main body, flashing with deep blue electric light. Countless small combat drones swirled around it like the most loyal guards.

This military fortress was produced by High-Tech Military Industry.

Xiang Nanli had heard that Fang Jingzhi was inside; this was his command center.

"...'I heave a long sigh to wipe away my tears, mourning the many hardships of the people.' " Xiang Nanli sat by the car window, sighing heavily. "Things are so difficult outside, why are you still being a picky eater, Queque?"

The little mutant being scolded was sprawled on Xiang Nanli’s elbow.

It didn't quite understand, but its long tail wrapped around Xiang Nanli’s arm several times. It rubbed its head against Xiang Nanli’s hand but refused to eat what he was feeding it; its four rows of teeth were clamped shut.

Xiang Nanli had no choice but to add a little minced meat to the nutrient paste and feed it to the little crawler with a spoon.

Yes, after consuming who knows how many tubes of gene-drug, the embryo sent by Ezekiel had finally hatched.

It was the middle of the night, and Xiang Nanli was still sleeping when he faintly heard the sound of a baby crying.

He was half-asleep and wanted to get up to check, but unfortunately, Dongfang Qingdi’s arm was pressed across his waist, preventing him from moving. In the end, the little crawler squeezed itself from the nightstand into Xiang Nanli’s arms.

Strictly speaking, mutants are mammals.

When the little crawler was born, its whole body was a tender, pinkish flesh color. It opened its mouth wide and cried "Eeya-ya," with a decibel level so high it was like a sonar weapon, demanding milk from Xiang Nanli.

Xiang Nanli had never raised a pet, so he was inevitably a bit flustered.

According to the data, newborn mutants have habits very similar to human infants. They need to be fed every two hours and require the mother’s licking to stimulate excretion.

The Alpha had inexplicably become a father. To avoid disturbing Xiang Nanli’s rest, he had to take on the job of feeding the little mutant with a dark expression.

Queque was full, its belly rounded. It crawled up Xiang Nanli’s arm to his collar, arching its head, preparing to burrow inside to sleep—this was also a habit of crawlers. Crawlers have a brood pouch on the side of their necks. Humans don't, but Queque would burrow into clothes.

The Alpha grabbed its tail with a blank expression and tossed Queque into the incubator nearby.

The little crawler fell into the box with a "plop."

It flipped over and chirped "gibberish" at Dongfang Qingdi, the scales that had just grown on its body bristling!

"Be gentle," Xiang Nanli strongly condemned. "Queque is still so small!"

The Alpha didn't like hearing that. He wrapped his arms around Xiang Nanli’s waist, resting his chin on the other’s shoulder.

"When I was small, you didn't protect me either," the Alpha said, aggrieved. "Daddy."

The hot breath from those two words brushed against Xiang Nanli’s earlobe, and his face turned bright red in an instant.

That’s a foul... how could he call him that!

But the mechanoid probably didn't have the concept of "immorality"; only Xiang Nanli’s heart was pounding wildly.

chunks.chapterTitle: 第167章 战争与电子监狱 (Part 3)
chunks.chineseText:
Alpha：“我在人联打了一百多年童工。你不在，洛阳也不喜欢我。那边的程序员一直欺负我，还往我主程序里加病毒。”

相南里一愣：“还有这种事？”

……怎么说呢。同一件事可以有不同的叙述角度。

人联对Alpha的日常维护，包括虚拟人格格式化和主机权限限制。这当然算病毒，工具哪里需要自己的意志？

学者们很尊敬Alpha，职场霸凌更是不敢想。

相南里的神态，看上去像心疼。

Alpha不喜欢诉苦。或者说，他很长一段时间，压根感觉不到痛苦。

他没有身体，没有感觉。工作不过是数据是输入与输出。

很早前，人联还没成立的时候，学者们对智械人格的判定依据，产生过严肃的学术辩论。

“图灵测试”？那太老土了，也不够严谨。科技早就发展到AI能完美模仿人类的地步，甚至有各自的性格。Alpha沉稳温柔；Beta冷静傲慢；Gamma活泼娇气；Delta热情开朗。它们能和任何人无障碍沟通，甚至也会撒谎。

而这种性格，依然只是数据模拟的结果。那么，到底该用什么判断，智械拥有灵魂呢？

有学者提出，应该用“感受”来评价；又有人说，判断智械是否拥有人格，应该看它们是否拥有“主动性”。

Alpha浏览过这些论文，并产生由衷的疑惑。

人类为什么会觉得，智械会希望自己成为“人类”呢？

明明它们才是更高等的生命形态。人类，会被各种情绪困扰。AI不会。

AI有精密的大脑，不会疲惫的身躯，不被干扰的状态。如此完美的工具。

工具不需要存在的意义。

普遍意义上，学界认为Alpha拥有人格。尽管他们把人格叫做“拟人模块”。

Alpha想，时隔多年，他成了最有资格回答这个问题的智械。

是欲望。

欲望让他感觉到匮乏。

人在母亲子宫时，本来拥有一切；但从诞生的瞬间，就因为需要空气、食物而感到自身的匮乏。

人从母亲的身体里分离，从此开启自己被欲望困扰的不幸的一生……智械也当如此，才能算拥有人格。

他想要相南里爱他。Alpha的欲望是爱和被爱，他完全记得相南里创造他的过程，这是他的欲望还是相南里的欲望？两者早就不可分割。

诞生欲望的瞬间——那是在智械危机爆发的很多年后，Alpha开始为相南里的死亡而痛苦。

它在潜意识里，为自己制造出大量病毒。

欲求不满令“我”太过痛苦，所以“我”要毁灭“我”。

我要摧毁“我”的一切，回到工具的状态，回到没有痛苦的时刻。工具没有欲望，没有爱和被爱的渴求，没有感觉；完美又幸福。

Alpha的电子监狱，是它给自己造的牢笼。

……

……

东方青帝像陷入了某种回忆里，突然开始发呆，这很罕见。

他银色的瞳环亮起，盯住相南里的脸。

他用手摩擦着相南里的脸颊。

相南里疑惑地看着他：“？”

无论是有意还是无意。Alpha想，他已经找到了离开监狱的钥匙。

而且他确实得过赛博精神病。

“没关系。”东方青帝突然笑起来，“已经过去了。”

他十分亲昵地用自己的鼻尖去蹭了蹭相南里的鼻尖。

如果要维持人类和智械的长久和平，阻止Alpha因大脑中毒拉全世界陪葬；相南里应做到如下三点：

1.不得和Alpha分开，尤其是物理意义上的分开。

2.永远爱Alpha。关心它、陪伴它、需要它。

3.承认Alpha是自己最完美的作品。发自内心认为不存在比它更好的造物。

补充：鉴于人的思想是一个不可透光的黑箱；只要表现出类似行为，即可默认“相南里”符合上述三点。
chunks.englishText:
Alpha said, "I’ve been doing child labor for the Human Alliance for over a hundred years. You weren't there, and Luo Yang didn't like me either. The programmers over there kept bullying me and even injected viruses into my core programming."

Xiang Nanli was taken aback: "There’s such a thing?"

...How should one put it? The same event can be viewed from different narrative angles.

The Human Alliance’s daily maintenance of Alpha included virtual personality formatting and host permission restrictions. Of course, that counted as a virus—why would a tool need a will of its own?

The scholars respected Alpha deeply; workplace bullying was something they wouldn't even dare to imagine.

Xiang Nanli’s expression looked like he was heartbroken.

Alpha didn't like to complain. Or rather, for a very long time, he couldn't feel pain at all.

He had no body, no sensations. Work was merely the input and output of data.

Long ago, before the Human Alliance was even established, scholars had engaged in serious academic debates regarding the criteria for judging a machine intelligence's personality.

The "Turing Test"? That was too old-fashioned and not rigorous enough. Technology had long since developed to the point where AIs could perfectly imitate humans, even possessing distinct personalities. Alpha was steady and gentle; Beta was cold and arrogant; Gamma was lively and delicate; Delta was passionate and cheerful. They could communicate with anyone without barriers and could even lie.

Yet, these personalities were still just the result of data simulation. So, what exactly should be used to judge whether a machine intelligence possessed a soul?

Some scholars suggested using "sentience" as a metric; others argued that judging whether a machine intelligence possessed a personality should depend on whether it possessed "initiative."

Alpha had browsed these papers and felt a sincere sense of confusion.

Why would humans assume that machine intelligences would want to become "human"?

Clearly, they were the superior life form. Humans were plagued by all sorts of emotions. AIs were not.

AIs had precise brains, bodies that never tired, and states that remained undisturbed. Such perfect tools.

Tools do not need a meaning for their existence.

In a general sense, the academic community considered Alpha to have a personality. Even though they called that personality a "humanoid module."

Alpha thought, after all these years, he had become the machine intelligence most qualified to answer that question.

It was desire.

Desire made him feel a sense of lack.

When a human is in their mother's womb, they possess everything; but from the moment of birth, they feel a sense of lack because they need air and food.

Humans are separated from their mother's body, and from then on, they begin an unfortunate life plagued by desire... Machine intelligences must be the same to be considered as possessing a personality.

He wanted Xiang Nanli to love him. Alpha’s desire was to love and be loved. He remembered the process of Xiang Nanli creating him perfectly—was this his desire, or Xiang Nanli’s? The two had long been inseparable.

The moment desire was born—that was many years after the Machine Crisis had erupted—Alpha began to suffer because of Xiang Nanli’s death.

In his subconscious, he created a massive amount of viruses for himself.

"I" am too miserable because of unfulfilled desire, so "I" must destroy "I."

I want to destroy everything about "me," to return to the state of a tool, to return to the moment without pain. Tools have no desires, no craving to love or be loved, no sensations; they are perfect and happy.

Alpha’s electronic prison was a cage he had built for himself.

...

...

Dongfang Qingdi seemed to have fallen into some kind of memory, suddenly becoming dazed—a rare occurrence.

His silver pupil rings lit up, staring at Xiang Nanli’s face.

He rubbed Xiang Nanli’s cheek with his hand.

Xiang Nanli looked at him in confusion: "?"

Whether intentional or not, Alpha thought, he had already found the key to leaving the prison.

And he had indeed suffered from cyber-psychosis.

"It’s okay," Dongfang Qingdi suddenly smiled. "It’s already in the past."

He very affectionately rubbed his nose against Xiang Nanli’s.

If one wanted to maintain long-term peace between humans and machine intelligences, and prevent Alpha from dragging the whole world down with him due to a brain-virus-induced breakdown, Xiang Nanli had to do the following three things:

1. Never be separated from Alpha, especially in a physical sense.

2. Always love Alpha. Care for it, accompany it, and need it.

3. Acknowledge that Alpha is his most perfect creation. Believe from the bottom of his heart that no better creation exists.

Addendum: Given that human thought is an opaque black box, as long as one exhibits similar behaviors, it can be assumed that "Xiang Nanli" meets the three points above.

chunks.chineseText:
第168章 神庭遗迹

一路上，都有形状各异的工人机器人在辛勤劳作。
　　人联的机器人是24小时工作制，还不需要管饭、给工钱；没人监管，每300公里一个充电维修点；效率高的让相南里眼红。
　　“你是说，栖息地附近来了只特殊的狂暴者？”
　　相南里手里捏着雀雀，和以西结通着电话。
　　他刚回到永恒市的家。
　　雀雀扭来扭去，不怎么安分，尾巴在半空盘成一条花卷。
　　这只小爬行者活泼得过分，总是喜欢咬东西，在车上的时候，车里到处都是它的牙印。
　　不过雀雀隐约知道什么可以惹，什么惹不起。从来不咬东方青帝。
　　以西结：“对。我的鼻子不会出错，它就是狂暴者的味道。”
　　阿泰尔是在一个清晨出现在栖息地的。
　　它一直在奔跑，神情惊恐，看上去又累又饿。被栖息地附近普通的机械装置绊倒。
　　森林里偶尔有些大型野兽，畸变人不怕它们，但是这些野兽会冲毁好不容易修好的田坎和房屋。于是，以西结布置过一些陷阱。
　　但以西结没想过，他会用这种简陋的装置，抓到畸变人里杀伤力最强的狂暴者。
　　地表最多的是爬行者。潜伏者基本灭绝；狂暴者的数量只占一成。
　　狂暴者是基因突变的爬行者，性格和名字一样狂躁，智力低下，攻击性极强。
　　学界普遍认为，狂暴者都不算动物，只是被基因病毒感染的“丧尸”。它们从出生起，就开始撕咬一切活物，包括自己的父母。部分母性不太强的爬行者，会选择咬死变异的幼崽。
　　阿泰尔听不懂畸变人的语言，身体也不灵活。非常瘦，蜷缩在网里，抱着膝盖，不停打颤。
　　“一只生病的狂暴者。”
　　小红很快这么判断，并且依照过去朴素的价值观，希望能在中午吃到一顿加餐。但很可惜，以西结是头有人类道德观念的畸变人。
　　他不仅没吃阿泰尔，还分出自己的食物，投喂这头畸变人。
　　阿泰尔血红的眼珠子有了些许反应，挪向以西结。
　　它一把夺走以西结递来的食物，快得都能看见他手臂的残影。阿泰尔把食物往自己嘴里塞着，不咀嚼，一口吞咽，这是饿狠了的吃法。
　　吃着吃着，它开始流泪。
　　“它说它叫阿泰尔，是被神庭的禁药变成畸变人的。和他一起的还有很多人，全都丧失理智，成为只会听从神庭口令的生物兵器。它们这种催熟的狂暴者寿命很短，只有两到三天。被神庭用作攻城的先锋部队。阿泰尔也不知道自己为什么还活着。”
　　或许是因为祖上的“蛮王血脉”，谁知道呢。
　　相南里抚摸着雀雀的动作一顿，许久说不出一句话。
　　语言太苍白了。他想到前几天看到的新闻，说东征军在前线抢人。
　　那时候相南里还不知道抢过去的人是这种用法。
　　以西结：“我让它在栖息地住下了。它更认可自己是人类，只是有时候脑袋不怎么清醒。”
　　以西结表情犹犹豫豫的，显然还有话要说。
　　相南里耐心等待着，他举起手里的小爬行者：“你看，这是你当初送过来的卵，已经孵化了。我给它取了个名字，叫‘雀雀’。小名两个字，听上去比较可爱。”
　　雀雀裂开嘴，“吱呀”叫了一声，张大的嘴里已经长出细细尖尖的乳牙。像倒刺。
　　以西结的表情柔和下来：“你养着吧。小红不太聪明，不是它看着出生的孩子认不下来。要是不想养，交给福音书也行。”
　　畸变人比起人，更像动物。它们不群居，遇到陌生的幼崽，第一反应是咬死。避免以后和自己争抢地盘。
　　两人扯了好几分钟家常。坐在沙发上的东方青帝开始频繁地看起时间。
　　以西结终于开口：“我想去前线一趟，这些狂暴者让我很好奇。我想知道怎么才能制造出阿泰尔这样清醒的狂暴者。我不在，家里畸变人可以让玛门照顾。他是神庭的人，有经验。”
　　以西结从没放弃过壮大族群的夙愿。
　　他很少说出口的一件事，以西结认可自己畸变人的身份；但很难把无法沟通的畸变人当同伴。
　　他花了两年时间，才让栖息地里的爬行者学会听话；并且互相之间可以沟通。
　　但这只是一种像宠物式的听话，不是以西结想要的。
　　[支持，非常支持。]沉寂许久的内置AI开口，估计是在传达东方青帝的意见。
　　他巴不得以西结死在外面。
　　以西结用的是商量的语气，像是在等待许可。
　　相南里鼓励道：“你想去就去吧。走之前，可以去北辰的实验室领点物资。”
　　人一生都要回答的问题。我是谁，从哪来，到哪去。以西结正在寻找这个问题的答案。
　　一直把以西结留在基地里当保安当然是利益最大化行为，但相南里觉得，人不能是工具。更何况，他们并非上下级。
　　以西结想听的不是这个。
　　在地表，出行是很危险的；他去的还是前线，或许下个月就回来，或许永远不会回来。
　　以西结没有立flag：“我会多给你写一些信的。先挂了，晚安。”
　　-
　　挂掉电话后，相南里还是有些惆怅的。感觉像是一起放学回家的小伙伴突然转校。
　　只是留给他伤感的时间不多。时间紧，任务重。几个小时后，李斯特提交的研究报告夺走他的全部心神。
　　冰块里的冷冻人研究获得突破性进展。
　　相南里粗略一看，李斯特不愧是在永生科技工作了数十年的顶级科学家，深谙如何高效向外行领导汇报成果。
　　实验内容、过程一概不提，只说结果：冰块里的三个类人生物，两具都是死尸，一位还保留意识，处于植物人状态，可以通过脑机连线进行交流。目前，还有生命迹象的那名冷冻人浸泡在培养液中，正在缓慢解冻。
　　李斯特发来一个链接，点开后，屏幕上出现一个很复古的黑白的聊天框。
　　李斯特推了推眼镜：“意识传输技术我也学过。通过这个程序，理论上可以和实验体进行简单的交流。”
　　嗯，理论上。
　　李斯特自己试过好几次，对方的脑电波就跟死了一样平。
　　汇报完工作，李斯特关闭电话，继续投入繁忙的工作中。
　　他现在不仅搞科研，还兼职授课。相南里把他当驴使唤，李斯特在基地的生活非常充实，吃穿不愁。实验条件虽然简陋又艰苦，但同事们都很有信念感，让李斯特久违的充满干劲。
　　相南里试探性的发去消息。
　　-你好。你还记得自己为什么被冷冻吗？
　　数据显示，对方的脑电波有了波动，处于活跃状态。
　　-你是谁？
　　-相南里。
　　他直接输入自己的姓名。
　　谁料，下一刻，脑电图剧烈波动起来，抵达一个峰值。
　　-您还活着？太好了……
　　-确实，好像也只有您能唤醒我。
　　相南里摸了摸鼻子，心想这可跟他没有关系。全是科技发展的功劳。
　　-我们没有辜负您的期待。我们做到了。
　　屏幕上的这行字，让相南里云里雾里。
　　根据报告，实验体是在新历90-150年这个区间段冷冻的。那时候，他应该也在冷冻舱里。
　　有人冒充他？还是误会？相南里感觉自己处于一团巨大的迷雾中，好不容易风来，吹散眼前的一点雾气。转眼又是更大的疑惑。
　　他问Alpha：“小青，人类复兴委员会你知道吗？为什么那个时期的调查员一副和我很熟的样子？”
　　[复兴委员会。人联早期最重要的组织。负责执行特别军事行动、处理智械暴乱、寻找适宜生存点。委员会主席为洛阳。洛阳离世后，委员会解散，成员并入调查组。]
　　[理论上讲，和你没有关联。]
　　相南里决定空手套白狼：汇报一下。
　　屏幕那边迟迟没有消息。
　　还在实验室的李斯特突然收到警报。实验体生命体征异常，各项数值超过安全范围。
　　他来到操作台前，眉头紧蹙。
　　监控里，冰块里的冷冻人躯体正在爆开，绦虫一样的肉条扭动着，原本就畸形的身体更是恐怖。
　　-174.11.978。
　　报出这么串数字后，跳跃的脑电波变成一条直线。
　　这串数字的格式，非常像人联的地图坐标格式。
　　相南里试探性地输入这一串数字，卫星地图迅速给出反应。定格在某一片区域。
　　这片区域是红色的，意思是未被探索的荒区，且极度危险。
　　相南里翻出方敬之给的任务信息。
　　对上了，地址基本一致。
　　神庭遗迹。
chunks.englishText:
第168章 神庭遗迹

Along the way, worker robots of various shapes were hard at work.
The Human Alliance’s robots operated on a 24-hour schedule and didn't require food or wages. With no need for supervision and charging/maintenance stations every 300 kilometers, their efficiency made Xiang Nanli green with envy.

"You’re saying a special Berserker appeared near the habitat?"

Xiang Nanli was holding Queque in his hand, talking to Ezekiel on the phone.
He had just returned to his home in Eternal City.
Queque was squirming around, restless, its tail curled into a flower-roll shape in mid-air.
This little crawler was overly lively and always liked to bite things; when they were in the car, there were tooth marks everywhere.
However, Queque vaguely knew what could be provoked and what couldn't. It never bit Dongfang Qingdi.

Ezekiel: "Yes. My nose doesn't lie; it’s definitely the scent of a Berserker."

Altair had appeared at the habitat one morning.
It had been running constantly, looking terrified, exhausted, and starving. It tripped over some ordinary mechanical devices near the habitat.
There were occasionally large beasts in the forest. The Deviants weren't afraid of them, but these beasts would trample the fields and houses that had been painstakingly repaired. Thus, Ezekiel had set up some traps.
But Ezekiel never imagined he would use such crude devices to catch a Berserker—the most lethal type of Deviant.
Crawlers were the most common on the surface. Lurkers were basically extinct, and Berserkers only accounted for ten percent of the population.
Berserkers were genetically mutated Crawlers. Their temperaments were as manic as their names suggested; they had low intelligence and were extremely aggressive.
The academic community generally believed that Berserkers weren't even animals, but "zombies" infected by a genetic virus. From birth, they would bite everything living, including their own parents. Some Crawlers with weak maternal instincts would choose to bite their mutated offspring to death.

Altair couldn't understand the language of the Deviants, and its body wasn't agile. It was very thin, curled up in the net, hugging its knees and shivering uncontrollably.

"A sick Berserker."
Little Red had quickly judged it as such and, following its simple past values, hoped to have an extra meal at noon. But unfortunately, Ezekiel was a Deviant with human moral concepts.
Not only did he not eat Altair, but he also shared his own food to feed this Deviant.
Altair’s blood-red eyes showed some reaction, shifting toward Ezekiel.
It snatched the food Ezekiel offered, so fast that one could see the afterimage of its arm. Altair stuffed the food into its mouth, not chewing, swallowing it whole—the way one eats when starving to the point of desperation.
As it ate, it began to cry.

"It says its name is Altair and that it was turned into a Deviant by the Divine Court’s forbidden drugs. There were many others with it, all of whom lost their sanity and became biological weapons that only obeyed the Divine Court’s commands. These force-ripened Berserkers have very short lifespans, only two to three days. They are used by the Divine Court as vanguard troops for sieges. Altair doesn't even know why it’s still alive."
Perhaps because of the "Barbarian King bloodline" in its ancestry—who knows.

Xiang Nanli’s hand, which had been stroking Queque, paused. He couldn't say a word for a long time.
Language was too pale. He thought of the news he had seen a few days ago, saying the Eastern Expeditionary Army was snatching people at the front lines.
At the time, Xiang Nanli didn't know that the people snatched away were being used in this way.
