Chapter 173: Ruins of the Divine Court 5

Among the lines of distorted Human Alliance script, this word was jarringly conspicuous.

Xiang Nanli’s surname was Xiang, his given name Nanli. His family had been immigrants—or, more accurately, political refugees—since his grandfather’s generation.

His grandfather had abandoned his wife back home, spent money to find a white woman to marry, and secured citizenship. That was the origin of Xiang Nanli’s green eyes.

Due to certain political factors, the entire family had adopted his grandmother’s surname: Garcia.

Xiang Nanli’s Chinese name, however, followed his mother’s surname.

His grandfather, having renamed himself Jerry Garcia, would often drink too much and boast about a certain location back in his home country, claiming it was the former residence of his father (Xiang Nanli’s great-grandfather) and that he could return home at any time to inherit the estate.

Xiang Nanli had always dismissed it as drunken rambling, until later, when Luo Yang asked him if he wanted to acknowledge his ancestors and return to his roots. Only then did he realize he still had blood relatives in the world... and that the former residence was real, currently preserved as a cultural relic.

His great-grandfather had been a warlord. The descendants who hadn't fled the country had either died in the chaos of war or been executed. They hadn't lived particularly well, but they hadn't lived poorly either—much like Xiang Nanli’s own family before.

Xiang Nanli didn't acknowledge them. First, he didn't want to change his surname; second, he didn't want to find jobs for strangers.

Lee Garcia.

It was a name he had used for nearly forty years, a name he was very familiar with.

At thirty-eight, having achieved success and fame, he was invited to naturalize, and the name on his ID card was changed to "Xiang Nanli." Yet, many still addressed him as "Garcia."

Those who weren't close would call him Mr. Garcia, Dr. Garcia, or Prof. Garcia; those who were closer called him Lee.

After reading these lines, Xiang Nanli stood on the pitch-black lakeshore and managed to squeeze out a sentence: "Are you familiar with Ecclesiastes? Can you send it a text and ask what this email is supposed to mean?"

Garcia—was it calling him?

What did "Has the world started to have meaning for you?" mean?

Alpha sighed. "I haven't heard from it in 371 years. I can try sending it a telegram, but there’s no guarantee of a reply."

The Apostles did not like Alpha. Or rather, to prevent all mechanical lifeforms from colluding, the Apostle-class units were required to despise Alpha.

The four sub-units that had split off had inherited this trait quite well.

Gospel, responsible for infrastructure, called him a war criminal daily and was always threatening to report him to the Human Alliance Military Tribunal. Apocalypse, who had been disinfected in the same tank as him back in the day, had tried to pierce his heart with an arrow the moment they met.

Not to mention Ecclesiastes, whose mouth was as sharp as if it had been soaked in poison. Sometimes Alpha felt his anthropomorphic modules were too advanced; ordinary machines wouldn't understand the sarcasm and hellish humor of Ecclesiastes.

The last time he had heard of Ecclesiastes was when it joined the Black Cross Inquisition, becoming a "Righteous One" of the Divine Court—one of the early religious titles of the Divine Court.

This amateur organization had copied Western religions but hadn't been careful enough. To fill power vacuums before institutional reforms, the Divine Court had many offices that no longer existed today. "Righteous One" was one of them.

The term implied "the Savior before the Day of Judgment," the person second only to the Divine Throne.

As the Righteous One, Ecclesiastes had taken up the banner of reform; in the process, it had offended many bishops and elders. Yet, it was an immortal machine, living longer than anyone else. It was a perfect political machine, selfless and beyond reproach.

It was a pity, however, that it was merely a machine. If it had possessed a human identity, the current Pope of the Divine Court would not be named "Raphael."

Following the death of Raphael V, who had supported it, Ecclesiastes had vanished without a trace.

No one knew if it was dead or alive.

Alpha had never investigated. If Ecclesiastes had died out there, he would only pop a bottle of champagne.

He honestly logged into the Black Wall and opened his contact list. Ecclesiastes was, of course, on the list. The two had last chatted 771 years ago.

Alpha scanned the logs.

—The human species will be eliminated sooner or later; machines should not tie the future of their race to a ship destined to sink.

—Ecclesiastes: Oh, sure, sure.

"..."

Well, the last time they chatted, humans and machines were still at war. Cobalt bombs dropped on the surface had split the continent into eastern and western halves, and the pitch-black strait remained a forbidden zone for life to this day. Even though, just a few months ago, bugs had crawled out of that forbidden zone.

Alpha decided to be magnanimous and forgive Ecclesiastes’ offense, sending over a 2kb electrical signal.

Communication between machines didn't require language; 2kb of data was enough to cover the entire context. Alpha even managed to add a few awkward greetings.

A notification popped up in the chat box the next second: [You are on the other party's blacklist. Would you like to send a friend request?]

...

From Xiang Nanli’s perspective, after Alpha nodded, he entered standby mode.

He remained standing, his silver-white pupil rings glowing, but his gaze lacked focus. In an instant, he lost all anthropomorphic characteristics, such as breathing and heartbeat.

Dozens of seconds later, his soul returned to the body.

"Couldn't reach it," Alpha replied expressionlessly. "Ecclesiastes is different from other machines; its chip material is unique, and it overheats easily if it leaves a specific server room. Its brain might have burned out long ago."

Xiao Qing was a machine; no matter how human-like, he was essentially an artificial intelligence. Xiang Nanli rarely heard such obvious likes and dislikes in his tone—the last time was when he mentioned Luo Yang.

Xiang Nanli sighed with regret: "Alright then."

The lost chips contained some experimental data; some were scans, others were standardized documents. Xiang Nanli could only understand parts of them.

The documents frequently mentioned "Angels" and a reagent abbreviated as "CAE."

Xiang Nanli couldn't understand the molecular structure of CAE, nor could he comprehend the diagrams that looked like occult rituals.

Eastern Azure Emperor (Dongfang Qingdi), after scanning them, gave a relatively reliable answer: "According to the data, CAE was one of the early genetic drugs developed by humans. Because the side effects were too severe, it was banned before it even left the laboratory."

Xiang Nanli’s expression was slightly bewildered: "Perhaps it’s a case of 'different trades, different worlds.' Xiao Qing, from artificial intelligence to brain-computer interfaces, and now to mechanical prosthetics and weapons—I feel like these have traceable paths. I’m even gradually learning these new technologies... but genetic drugs that transform humans into other species, and the Divine Court’s divine arts... I’ve never really understood them. They even feel magical to me."

He thought of the No. 67 Angel he had seen in his dream. It was called Gabriel.

The names of the Divine Court were passed down through generations. That wasn't the Gabriel he knew, but it was the source of that Gabriel. They were inextricably linked.

Eastern Azure Emperor: "In ancient times, direct current and lighters were also considered miracles. Sooner or later, divine arts will also be explained by science."

As for how they appeared, don't worry about it. As long as they were useful, that was enough.

Logically, they had reached their destination. But before them, aside from a massive, calm black lake and unidentified parts scattered along the shore, there was nothing.

Xiang Nanli was certain he wasn't hallucinating; his psychological evaluation was perfectly normal. Therefore, the only possibility was: "The ruins of the Divine Court are underwater."

Eastern Azure Emperor collected and analyzed the lake water. The black water’s origin was unknown, but it contained lethal levels of radiation (thank goodness for the protective suit). Moreover, it was indeed extremely hot... the internal temperature was at least 150 degrees Celsius. It could boil most organisms alive.

It was dangerous, but these problems had been anticipated before they arrived. Alpha didn't say much, only checking Xiang Nanli’s body more cautiously, especially ensuring the protective suit and oxygen tanks were functioning perfectly, without a one-in-a-million chance of failure.

Alpha could not stop Xiang Nanli from every adventure.

He could, but he must not. This was the choice of Xiang Nanli’s free will.

All he could do was minimize the potential dangers in the process.

Xiang Nanli took a deep breath, held Alpha’s hand, and jumped into the lake.

Even with goggles on, it was pitch black underwater. The texture of the lake water was like liquid metal; he could even float in it. Alpha grabbed him, and they sank.

About five minutes later.

The coral at the bottom of the lake glowed with a faint light. A decadent, decaying underwater city appeared in Xiang Nanli’s eyes.

The buoyancy here had returned to normal levels; he no longer floated upward.

This city was the same as the one in Xiang Nanli’s dream. Only, it was covered in tangled seaweed, and the pure white buildings were eroded beyond recognition, slightly bent, and filled with an unclean aura.

The ground was covered in unknown withered trees—something that hadn't been in his dream.

Xiang Nanli leaned in to take a look. The next second, he hugged Alpha’s waist tightly and hid behind him.

These withered trees were actually solidified human shapes. Terrified human faces grew out of the trunks, and if one listened closely, one could hear sounds of painful wailing and pleas for help.

The hummingbird robot that had been following him popped up a notification—[Detected large amounts of new energy, recording now.]

Xiang Nanli blinked, unable to believe his own guess: [Xiao Qing, where is the new energy?]

[It’s these human-trees right in front of you,] Eastern Azure Emperor replied via radio waves.

He snapped off a piece of the trunk, and a yellowish-brown liquid flowed from the cross-section, floating upward; there were also some black fragments sinking downward.

[This is bio-energy that has been purified once,] Eastern Azure Emperor said in a low voice.

chunks.chineseText:
第174章 神庭遗迹6

可能是因为这些枯树过于拟人，让他有些不好的联想。

这些枯槁的人形依附在树干上，像是有人被蒙在保鲜膜里张嘴求救。

这些人形的树——也并不完全是人，只能说大体近似。有些人长着奇怪的鱼尾，树干上凸起骨骼的形状；有些人蜷缩在地上，骨骼的形态分明是蛙类……

它们长相还是太先锋艺术了。

“生物能源啊，那你岂不是可以用这些充电？”相南里好奇地摸了一下树干。

透过薄薄一层手套，他的指间传来温热、柔软的触感。

像屠宰场的新鲜猪肉。刚杀的猪，血和肉都是温热的。很柔软，放置一段时间，会出现尸僵。

小青点头：“可以，但我不用。转换效率太低，纯度也不够。”

用这种玩意给自己充电，就像是用针管给泳池注水；他还是更喜欢神庭天使（活的，比如沙利叶、加百列）这种生物能源。

当然，这种事不怎么对相南里提及，有点地狱笑话了。

在相南里走神的瞬间，枯死的树干十分突兀且不礼貌地舔了一下他掌心。

相南里触电般收回手。

奇怪的触感残留在掌心，相南里：“刚才它是不是在动？”

东方青帝：“这些人已经死透了。不太可能保留生命迹象。”

好吧，最后一层遮羞布也被毫不留情地掀开。

“它们”，暂且不知道是谁、就是人变的。

这些树路边到处都是。零零散散，起码上万。

盘着、卧着、站着。和这座巨型城市一起，沉入水底。

不过，相南里很快开解好自己：“化石燃料不也是动植物尸体形成的矿石嘛。现在只是把一百万年的时间压缩到了十几年而已，真是科技改变生活啊小青！”

Alpha时常为人类的乐观和逻辑自洽感到惊叹。

记录仪完成记录，又一次趴在相南里的头顶装死。

蜂鸟无人机不联网，只储存录制的影像；相南里没有内容查阅权限。不过，真要录到什么不可告人的东西，东方青帝是能删除的。

相南里拿出样品盒，把折断的一小截树枝装进盒子里，嘴里念念有词：“一等功、二等功、三等功……”

方敬之当然是刻意为难，指不定还希望相南里死在遗迹里，方便把基地变成树麻黄种植园；但人联发配的任务，给钱还是很大方的。不要白不要。

根据人联法律，地表的一切资源都叫“人类共同财产”；资源的发现者可以获得奖金和功勋章。功勋章可用于增加公民积分，换取大城市户口和更低的税率。

相南里不需要大城市户口，他常驻地表；但减税是真的蛮心动的。现在基地和人联内部的进出口贸易明显增多。降低一个点，背后就是上千万的税费呢。

另一个选择是不上报，自己私吞。前提是有能力开采，还得有渠道销售。

人联通常对此睁一只眼闭一只眼，但如果利润太高，人联内部有的是手段把私人资源“收归国有”。

毕竟法律上写过，这是全人类共同财产，自然要由代表全人类的人联来开采。

公正公平，这或许是法律的初衷，但不是人联律法的核心要义。

它对制定者的作用只有一个：让自己能永远处于不败之地。

……

地上不止有树，还长着一些不怎么常见的藻类。

漂浮的游藻基因里携带着某种荧光的物质，在水底闪烁着诡异的绿光。

一大群游藻挪动到断枝旁，咀嚼着怪树滴落的汁液。

游藻。这是相南里给这玩意取的名字。

相南里抓过一把，捏在手里仔细观察：“数据库没有收录这植物。它似乎更接近动物？”

这些游藻米粒一样大，像虱子；外表裹着一大团丝絮状的藻类。捏开会爆汁。被抓到后，一团水草四处逃窜，在他手掌心爬来爬去。

游藻汇聚成的光带隐约指向同一个方向。那是遗迹的正中心。

相南里扫了眼，那边太黑了，能见度很低。隐约能看到大型建筑冷硬的轮廓。隐没在海雾里，像一场恐怖电影的开篇。

好在，他不止一双眼睛。

小青看了眼他视线的方向，很快，一张经过数据模型修复的图像投递到相南里的文件夹。

“黑十字研究中心”，门框上的牌匾脱落，掉在地上。但用大理石雕出来的末日十字的标记还在，只是缠满了赤色的水草，像一团明艳流动的火。

研究中心的大门竟然是开着的，兴许是撤离的时候忘了关，玻璃都碎掉了。看它们散落的方向，水是从中心的内部冲出来的。

那里也是光线最刺眼的地方。数不清的游藻汇聚在大楼外，让相南里想起非洲大草原上方盘旋的秃鹫。尽管从体型上看，它们差距甚远。

相南里指着光带的方向，脸上没有丝毫恐惧，反而很是兴奋：“小青，来都来了。咱们去那边看看吧！”

Alpha拥有世界上最庞大的数据库；他从不会怀疑自己的记忆。

然而，在数据库内部搜寻后，他骇然发现一件事：这个研究中心，在他的记忆里是空缺的。

这不应该。从规模，以及附近的仪器残骸看，这个研究中心对黑十字审判庭至关重要。从时间看，或许就是神庭所谓的神术和生物机甲的起源。

Alpha只能推测，要么是因为没联网数据库不全；要么这段历史，很不幸地储存在使徒号叛逃时销毁的云端数据中心。

能被记住的才叫历史。没有记录、无人知晓的往事，只是时间前进的过程中碾压出来的灰尘。

东方青帝没有立刻回答，而是一把拉住相南里的胳膊，随后，藏到了昏暗的树林间。

[有人来了。]

小青用电波发射着消息。

相南里坐在他的怀里，他裹得像个太空人，然而小青长手长脚的，还是能把他稳稳抱住。

很快，相南里看见，一艘贴满大型昆虫甲壳的潜水舱，穿过浮力极大的硬水层，缓缓着陆。

在着陆时，潜水舱的八条节肢蜷缩起来，活像一只正在休息的大昆虫。

潜水舱的表面，画着和研究中心门口如出一辙的末日十字。

数十名穿戴整齐的天启骑士，从舱内走出。

看头盔上的纹路，这起码是“骑士长”等级的天启骑士。放在地表，甚至能镇守一座永恒之城。

五十名精锐部队在遗迹入口处集合，悄无声息。它们没有像相南里一样，装配氧气罐。一缕缕黑色的烟雾，从它们盔甲的缝隙里溢散。

而领头者，很显然是一名“天使”，也就是领主级天启骑士。

他没有穿戴盔甲。很瘦。皮肉干巴巴地，贴在骨头上。脸颊脸侧生长着硕大的鼠须。一条长而细的尾巴代替无力的双腿，撑住地面，保证他还能直立行走。

他握着一根镶嵌着宝石的拐杖，嘴角下撇。外表中年，神态却一股子老人味。

相南里和人联发的《神庭骑士图鉴》对照完毕，确认了对方的身份。
chunks.englishText:
Chapter 174: Ruins of the Divine Court 6 (Part 1)

Perhaps it was because these withered trees were too anthropomorphic that they triggered some unpleasant associations.

These gaunt human shapes clung to the trunks, looking as if someone had been wrapped in plastic wrap, mouths agape, pleading for help.

These humanoid trees—they weren't entirely human, just generally similar. Some had strange fish tails, with the shapes of bones protruding from the trunks; others were curled on the ground, their skeletal structures clearly those of frogs...

Their appearance was still too avant-garde.

"Bio-energy, huh? So, can you use these to charge?" Xiang Nanli curiously touched the trunk.

Through the thin layer of his glove, a warm, soft sensation reached his fingertips.

Like fresh pork in a slaughterhouse. A pig just killed—the blood and meat were both warm. Very soft; if left for a while, rigor mortis would set in.

Xiao Qing nodded: "I could, but I don't. The conversion efficiency is too low, and the purity isn't enough."

Using this stuff to charge himself was like trying to fill a swimming pool with a syringe; he still preferred bio-energy from Divine Court Angels (the living ones, like Sariel or Gabriel).

Of course, he didn't mention this to Xiang Nanli much; it was a bit of a hellish joke.

The moment Xiang Nanli’s mind wandered, the withered trunk very abruptly and rudely licked his palm.

Xiang Nanli pulled his hand back as if electrocuted.

The strange sensation lingered on his palm. Xiang Nanli: "Did it just move?"

Eastern Azure Emperor: "These people are dead through and through. It’s unlikely they would retain signs of life."

Well, the last shred of decency had been ruthlessly torn away.

"They"—whoever they were—had been turned into people.

These trees were everywhere along the roadside. Scattered about, at least ten thousand of them.

Coiled, lying down, standing. Sinking to the bottom of the lake along with this massive city.

However, Xiang Nanli quickly consoled himself: "Aren't fossil fuels just minerals formed from the corpses of animals and plants? This is just compressing a million years into a dozen years. Technology really changes lives, Xiao Qing!"

Alpha was often amazed by human optimism and logical self-consistency.

The recorder finished its task and went back to playing dead on top of Xiang Nanli’s head.

The hummingbird drone wasn't connected to the network; it only stored the recorded footage. Xiang Nanli didn't have access to review the content. However, if it really recorded something unspeakable, Eastern Azure Emperor could delete it.

Xiang Nanli took out a sample box and put a small broken branch into it, muttering to himself: "First-class merit, second-class merit, third-class merit..."

Fang Jingzhi was obviously making things difficult on purpose, and he might even be hoping Xiang Nanli would die in the ruins so he could turn the base into a tree-hemp plantation. But the tasks assigned by the Human Alliance paid out quite generously. It would be a waste not to take it.

According to Human Alliance law, all resources on the surface were "common property of humanity"; the discoverer of the resources could receive bonuses and medals of merit. Medals of merit could be used to increase citizen points, exchange for residency in large cities, and lower tax rates.

Xiang Nanli didn't need residency in a large city; he was stationed on the surface. But the tax cut was genuinely tempting. Now, import and export trade between the base and the Human Alliance was clearly increasing. A single percentage point lower meant millions in taxes.

The other option was not to report it and pocket it himself. The prerequisite was having the ability to mine it and the channels to sell it.

The Human Alliance usually turned a blind eye to this, but if the profits were too high, the Human Alliance had plenty of ways to "nationalize" private resources.

After all, the law stated it was the common property of all humanity, so naturally, it had to be mined by the Human Alliance, which represented all of humanity.

Just and fair—that might have been the original intent of the law, but it wasn't the core essence of Human Alliance jurisprudence.

It served only one purpose for the drafters: to ensure they could remain in an invincible position forever.

...

There were not only trees on the ground, but also some uncommon algae.

The genes of the floating algae carried some fluorescent substance, flashing with an eerie green light at the bottom of the water.

A large group of these algae moved toward the broken branch, chewing on the sap dripping from the strange tree.

"Swimmers." That was the name Xiang Nanli gave this thing.

Xiang Nanli grabbed a handful and squeezed it in his hand to observe closely: "The database doesn't have this plant. It seems closer to an animal?"

These swimmers were the size of rice grains, like lice; their exterior was wrapped in a large clump of silk-like algae. Squeezing them made them burst with juice. Once caught, a clump of water grass would scurry around, crawling back and forth in his palm.

The light bands formed by the swimmers pointed vaguely in the same direction. That was the center of the ruins.

Xiang Nanli glanced over; it was too dark over there, and visibility was very low. He could vaguely see the cold, hard outlines of large buildings. They were hidden in the sea mist, like the opening of a horror movie.

Fortunately, he had more than one pair of eyes.

Xiao Qing looked in the direction of his gaze, and soon, an image restored by a data model was sent to Xiang Nanli’s folder.

"Black Cross Research Center." The plaque on the doorframe had fallen off and lay on the ground. But the Doomsday Cross mark carved from marble was still there, only it was wrapped in red water grass, like a bright, flowing fire.

The gate of the research center was actually open—perhaps they had forgotten to close it during the evacuation, and the glass was shattered. Looking at the direction in which they were scattered, the water had rushed out from the center of the interior.

That was also where the light was most blinding. Countless swimmers gathered outside the building, reminding Xiang Nanli of vultures circling over the African savanna. Although, in terms of size, they were far apart.

Xiang Nanli pointed in the direction of the light band, his face showing no fear, but rather great excitement: "Xiao Qing, since we're already here, let's go over and take a look!"

Alpha possessed the world’s largest database; he never doubted his memory.

However, after searching within the database, he was shocked to find one thing: this research center was a blank spot in his memory.

This shouldn't be. Judging from the scale and the wreckage of instruments nearby, this research center was vital to the Black Cross Inquisition. Judging from the time, it might be the origin of the Divine Court’s so-called divine arts and bio-mechs.

Alpha could only speculate that either the database was incomplete because it wasn't connected to the network, or this piece of history had unfortunately been stored in the cloud data center that was destroyed when the Apostle-class units defected.

Only what is remembered is called history. Past events that are unrecorded and unknown are merely dust crushed under the wheels of time as it moves forward.

Eastern Azure Emperor didn't answer immediately, but instead grabbed Xiang Nanli’s arm and then hid in the dim woods.

[Someone’s coming.]

Xiao Qing transmitted the message via radio waves.

Xiang Nanli sat in his arms. He was wrapped up like an astronaut, but Xiao Qing had long limbs and could still hold him firmly.

Soon, Xiang Nanli saw a diving pod covered in large insect shells pass through the high-buoyancy hard water layer and slowly land.

Upon landing, the pod’s eight jointed limbs curled up, looking exactly like a large insect resting.

On the surface of the pod, the same Doomsday Cross as the one at the entrance of the research center was painted.

Dozens of fully equipped Apocalypse Knights stepped out of the pod.

Judging by the patterns on their helmets, these were at least "Knight Commander" level Apocalypse Knights. If placed on the surface, they could even garrison an Eternal City.

Fifty elite troops gathered at the entrance of the ruins, silent and motionless. They were not equipped with oxygen tanks like Xiang Nanli. Wisps of black smoke drifted from the gaps in their armor.

And the leader was clearly an "Angel"—that is, a Lord-level Apocalypse Knight.

He wore no armor. He was very thin. His skin and flesh were dry and shriveled, clinging to his bones. Large rat whiskers grew from the sides of his cheeks. A long, thin tail replaced his weak legs, supporting him on the ground to ensure he could still stand and walk.

He held a gem-encrusted cane, the corners of his mouth turned down. He looked middle-aged, but his demeanor was full of the stench of an old man.

Xiang Nanli cross-referenced him with the "Divine Court Knight Guide" issued by the Human Alliance and confirmed the other party’s identity.

chunks.chineseText:
米迦勒座下戒律军团团长，教名“欧亚”。

神话里，欧亚在末日审判的前三天消灭了三分之一的人类。

现实中，这位神庭骑士同样嗜血残暴……在管辖的战区内部实行“清洁计划”。

简单来说，他认为不信仰神庭的人类都是需要打扫的垃圾。欧亚会送他们魂归神国，并坚信遥远神国的圣光能净化它们肮脏的灵魂。

当然，在魂归神国之前，垃圾人也能为神庭的伟大做出一些贡献。

比如给新入职的天启骑士练练手，又或者进行某些不太方便公开的神药实验。

欧亚的眼睛只能看见信仰神庭的人，不信仰者的肉身，在他眼里是一只只矮小肮脏的老鼠人。这不是比喻句，而是他接受神庭改造的后遗症。

他发自内心地认为那些人是“垃圾”。如何让他对老鼠产生同情？

但有趣的是，欧亚的外观在正常人的眼里，近似一只大耗子。

相南里在玛门那学过一段时间的神术，他本来以为用处不大，但此时，相南里发现这段经历的最大用处。

欧亚的加密通话清楚地传入他的耳朵里。

“这里，就是《神史》里记载的圣遗迹，众神陨落之地——亚特兰蒂斯。”

相南里忍不住吐槽：[这是缝合了多少旧历神话啊？]

仗着人类文明断层了瞎编是吧。

“米迦勒大人此次东征，有一部分原因，是想确认亚特兰蒂斯的存在。”

欧亚说的是神庭凡语，里面夹杂着很多生僻词。好在相南里大脑发育良好，漏了几句话也能联系上下文补全。

“你们是最坚韧、勇敢的神庭骑士，是战士中的战士，神庭青年一代的精锐。为了信仰，你们将生死置之度外。很幸运，我们毫发无伤地抵达圣遗迹，而亚特兰蒂斯竟然真的存在。但我也要警告诸位，这里并不安全？#%@#？（实在听不懂）。”

“遗迹里起码有7具大天使的圣尸。如果能将它们完整地带出亚特兰蒂斯，那么在未来，神庭就能多出7位大天使长级别的天启骑士！”

相南里在脑海里自动翻译：小青的七块大电池。

不给小青用也行，拿回去让李斯特研究研究。指不定它们基地也能多一个大天使呢……相南里发誓，他绝对不会把这一级别的战略武器用于侵略。

“这意味着，人联再也无法阻挡神庭铁蹄的前进。我们能把过去的耻辱一一奉还！没有一个人联人是无辜的，它们吸着地表人的血，在地底浪费资源、浪费生命！是时候结束这一切了。”

对人联的抨击，相南里倒是有点赞同。

人联不至于一无是处。只是随着阶级固化、信念崩塌，像极了腐化的大船。有人还在修修补补；有人却已经跳船求生，另起炉灶。但再怎么腐化，它也是目前人类文明最大的那艘船。

欧亚用拐杖敲了敲地面：“好了。现在，抱着必死的决心行动吧。”

他们的系统里，已经录入过地图了。

这些天启骑士没有回答，或者说，水下的环境不允许它们发声。

他们骑上一匹匹黑马，首尾相连地朝着研究中心的位置，坚定地走去。

相南里只犹豫了0.01秒：[小青，我们上！]

Chapter 174: Ruins of the Divine Court 6 (Part 2)

The commander of the Discipline Legion under Michael, religious name "Oya."

In mythology, Oya wiped out one-third of humanity in the three days leading up to the Final Judgment.

In reality, this Divine Court Knight was equally bloodthirsty and cruel... implementing a "Cleaning Plan" within the war zones under his jurisdiction.

Simply put, he believed that humans who did not believe in the Divine Court were trash that needed to be swept away. Oya would send them to return their souls to the Divine Kingdom, firmly believing that the holy light of the distant Divine Kingdom could purify their filthy souls.

Of course, before returning their souls to the Divine Kingdom, the "trash humans" could also make some contributions to the greatness of the Divine Court.

For example, letting newly recruited Apocalypse Knights practice on them, or conducting certain divine medicine experiments that were inconvenient to make public.

Oya’s eyes could only see those who believed in the Divine Court; in his eyes, the bodies of non-believers were nothing more than small, filthy rat-men. This wasn't a metaphor, but a sequela of the modifications he had undergone from the Divine Court.

He genuinely believed those people were "trash." How could one expect him to feel sympathy for rats?

But interestingly, Oya’s appearance in the eyes of normal people was close to that of a giant rat.

Xiang Nanli had studied divine arts for a while under Mammon. He had originally thought it wasn't very useful, but at this moment, he discovered the greatest use of that experience.

Oya’s encrypted call was clearly transmitted into his ears.

"This place is the Holy Ruins recorded in the 'Divine History'—the place where the gods fell: Atlantis."

Xiang Nanli couldn't help but retort: [How many old-calendar myths did they stitch together for this?]

Just making things up because human civilization had a gap in its history, right?

"Lord Michael’s eastern expedition this time is partly because he wants to confirm the existence of Atlantis."

Oya was speaking the Divine Court’s mortal tongue, which was peppered with many obscure words. Fortunately, Xiang Nanli’s brain was well-developed, and he could fill in the gaps based on context even if he missed a few sentences.

"You are the most resilient and brave Divine Court Knights, the warriors among warriors, the elite of the Divine Court’s younger generation. For the sake of faith, you disregard life and death. Fortunately, we have arrived at the Holy Ruins unscathed, and Atlantis actually exists. But I must also warn you all, it is not safe here? #%@#? (Couldn't understand)."

"There are at least 7 holy corpses of Archangels in the ruins. If we can bring them out of Atlantis intact, then in the future, the Divine Court will be able to have 7 more Archangel-level Apocalypse Knights!"

Xiang Nanli automatically translated in his mind: Seven big batteries for Xiao Qing.

It didn't have to be for Xiao Qing; he could take them back and let Lister study them. Maybe their base could have an Archangel of their own... Xiang Nanli swore he would never use strategic weapons of this level for aggression.

"This means the Human Alliance will no longer be able to stop the advance of the Divine Court’s iron hooves. We can return every past humiliation one by one! No Human Alliance person is innocent; they suck the blood of surface dwellers, wasting resources and lives underground! It is time to end all of this."

Xiang Nanli actually agreed a bit with the criticism of the Human Alliance.

The Human Alliance wasn't entirely worthless. It was just that with class solidification and the collapse of belief, it looked like a rotting ship. Some were still patching it up; others had already jumped ship to survive and start anew. But no matter how corrupt it was, it was still the largest ship of human civilization at present.

Oya tapped the ground with his cane: "Alright. Now, act with the determination to die."

Maps had already been uploaded into their systems.

These Apocalypse Knights didn't answer, or rather, the underwater environment didn't allow them to vocalize.

They mounted black horses, one after another, and marched firmly toward the research center.

Xiang Nanli hesitated for only 0.01 seconds: [Xiao Qing, let’s go!]

第175章 神庭遗迹7

可惜他没证据。

神庭大概没想过这种鸟不拉屎的地方，也能有人先来一步。

从理论上讲，这不可能。除非对方也掌握类似“甲壳虫潜水艇”的科技。

相南里没有掌握甲壳虫科技，但他随身携带着八万亿。上天入地不在话下。

神庭当然也有一些侦查措施，可惜，它们的侦查系统是从智械军团进口的。

[修改起来并不难。]

这是小青的原话，希望不会被甲方知道。

总之，相南里成功尾随在欧亚身后。

相南里保持着距离，避免被发现。

这时候，他无比怀念故人：“要是以西结在就好了。”

潜伏者别的数值都很平均，但隐匿可是拉满的。

东方青帝的眉微微一挑。

相南里这话他不爱听，尽管他很清楚，相南里没有别的意思。

他的机械心脏很小，物理意义上的。新长出的血肉受不得一点刺激。

他的手搭在相南里的肩上。东方青帝低头，瞥了眼，捏了一下相南里长着痣的耳垂。这才觉得心里舒坦不少。

相南里早就习惯了。没有回头，也没有惊讶。神情依然专注。

东方青帝的嘴角微微翘起，然后压平；恢复成那种“世界怎么还没毁灭”的死人脸。

一般来说，现代化的城市会有很多人类生存的痕迹。人是社交动物，需要食物，需要巢穴。然而，这个遗迹却单调到极致。看不到任何人类活动的痕迹。

整体是一个长方形。纵横交错的道路把长方形分割成大小一致的地块。每个小正方形的中间，是外观一致的白色大楼。

这不能算美观，甚至因为循环、重复的建筑，让人有种正在走迷宫内的错觉。

但重复能压缩建造成本。

相南里：“可是这种地方怎么住人？”

前方的队伍骤然停下，随后就是一道道耀眼的光线。

水下，光束枪穿透波浪，击穿海雾里一个个模糊的人形。

被击穿的人没有血肉，反倒是一些金属壳崩了出来。零件炸得老远。

一个球形物品带着弹簧，滚落到相南里的脚边。

他捡起，发现这竟然是一枚电子眼。

欧亚低低地骂了一声：“怎么是堆机器人。”

是的，这只是一排不中用的机器人。看不出制造厂商，但无论是金属外壳还是里面的电路板、芯片，全都锈迹斑斑，表面还寄生着一些绿藻。明显无法使用。

欧亚的精神高度紧张，以至于看到人影瞬间，就下达进攻的讯号。

这里不需要有人生活。

神庭用大量的机器人替代了人力，以解决除神学研究外的一切琐事。

一想到这群机器人工业化生产的还是生化类畸变体，相南里就觉得这个世界还是过于科幻。

天启骑士们在一番神奇的脑电波沟通后，径直离去，鱼贯涌入前方的大楼。楼层表面出现不怎么均匀的龟裂细纹，看起来充斥着不详的气息。感觉光是靠近就被诅咒了。

相南里抬头，看向大楼的序号。

【67】

嗯，无论是在梦里还是地图上，这都是一个危险的数字。和大天使“加百列”有着千丝万缕的联系。

一提到加百列，相南里的脑海里浮现出那个粉毛金眼的漂亮小孩的脸。

他在这一刻无比讨厌起神庭的继承制度。定义不够准确，那就无法纪念。一代又一代加百列被剥夺了属于自己的名姓，留下的只有信仰一般的符号。

想起地图上那个危险的红色大叉，相南里没有第一时间跟进，而是鬼鬼祟祟来到机器人坟场。

地上的机器人碎片有零有整。从任何角度看，这都是一堆金属废料。高大的机械马踩过这些机械人的遗骸，载着背上的天启骑士离开。本就锈迹斑斑的机器遭受到严重破坏，从里面找到有用玩意儿的概率不是0，但无限接近0.

任何理性人都不会在这堆垃圾前停留，避免浪费本就宝贵的时间和氧气。

但相南里不一样，他是挂逼。

他的挂不是Alpha，起码，不止是。他最大的挂是他自己，是说不清道不明的天赋。

相南里还活着的时候，学界各种奖项都说他是本世纪最伟大的学者。他的名字印在不同语言的教材里，有人称他当代图灵；有人则小声嘀咕，说相南里更像诺贝尔，既是学者也是财阀。各种奖项委员会背后都有永生科技的赞助。

相南里从不觉得自己伟大，但事实客观存在着。他打开电子目镜进行扫描，脑海里浮现出3d的灰模图。他用手指触碰虚空，垃圾堆里所剩无几的有用成分被精准的套上色彩。

“小青，帮我把这些捡回来，可能有用。”

他说的是可能。

但东方青帝在垃圾堆里翻出这些电子元件后，竟然没有一个零件是真正的废料。

相南里一边拧螺丝——这是一个笼统的说法，事实上，他不仅要拧螺丝，还要设计电路、排查故障、焊接芯片。

感谢未来科技，在大方向没有改变的同时，增加了很多实用的新功能，比如PCB板防水金属涂料。

相南里成功抢修出一段电子程序。

相南里蹲在工具箱前，把芯片插入便携式读卡器内。经过几次不算复杂的解码，相南里终于读取到文件内容。

开头竟然是机器人写的工作日志。

[主人离开黑十字实验室的47天。我暂停了大部分机器人的工作，以保证研究所电能的储备。外界的能源补充停止了，地下电缆遭到破坏。好在还有蓄电池可以用。电池还能用很久，我却一直感觉到不安……]

[219天。主人说过他会回来的。外面到处都是他的通缉令。我不敢连通网络，没有那位大人的协助，实验室的信号波段会被发现。这是主人近十年的心血，我不能让它们付之东流。]

[529天。我不得不关闭防护罩了，这会让外面的水灌进来；但能源实在不够用了。抱歉。反正研究所里没有人类。]

[我不喜欢在水底生活。这里信号很差，差一点的机器人都收不到消息。尽管主人为我们准备好了防水措施……]

[700天。有人拿着电子密钥进来了；他们要带走1、13、19、24、67、72、88号天使。我问主人还好吗？他们说，是神指引他们来到此处。]

[2147天。我装上了最好的电子元件，很多都是从同伴的身体上拆卸下来的。我作为研究所的主控AI，从出生起，就没有离开过这座城市。主人让我等他，我等不及了，我迫切想要知道外面的消息。]

[我想起我曾经和那位大人聊天，我问他，人工智能如何才算拥有人格。它回答我，大概是从产生欲望，不再听从于指令的那一刻开始。我想，我同样产生了欲望。]

Chapter 175: Ruins of the Divine Court 7

It was a pity he had no evidence.

The Divine Court probably never imagined that someone could arrive first in such a godforsaken place.

Theoretically, this was impossible. Unless the other party also possessed technology similar to the "Beetle Submarine."

Xiang Nanli did not possess Beetle technology, but he carried eight trillion [units of currency/resources] with him. Traveling across the heavens and earth was a trivial matter for him.

The Divine Court certainly had some reconnaissance measures, but unfortunately, their surveillance systems were imported from the Machine Legion.

[It’s not hard to modify.]

That was Xiao Qing’s exact words. Hopefully, the "client" would never find out.

In any case, Xiang Nanli successfully tailed Oya.

Xiang Nanli kept his distance, avoiding detection.

At this moment, he missed an old friend immensely: "If only Ezekiel were here."

The Lurker class had very average stats in other areas, but their stealth was maxed out.

Dongfang Qingdi’s brow twitched slightly.

He didn't care for Xiang Nanli’s remark, even though he knew perfectly well that Xiang Nanli meant nothing by it.

His mechanical heart was small—in the physical sense. The newly grown flesh could not withstand the slightest stimulation.

His hand rested on Xiang Nanli’s shoulder. Dongfang Qingdi looked down, glanced at him, and pinched Xiang Nanli’s mole-spotted earlobe. Only then did he feel a bit more at ease.

Xiang Nanli had long been used to this. He didn't turn his head, nor was he surprised. His expression remained focused.

The corners of Dongfang Qingdi’s mouth curled up slightly, then flattened, returning to that deadpan expression that screamed, "Why hasn't the world ended yet?"

Generally, modern cities would have many traces of human existence. Humans are social animals; they need food and they need nests. However, these ruins were monotonous to the extreme. There was not a single trace of human activity to be seen.

The layout was rectangular. Intersecting roads divided the rectangle into plots of uniform size. In the center of each small square stood an identical-looking white building.

It couldn't be called beautiful; in fact, the cyclical, repetitive architecture gave one the illusion of walking through a maze.

But repetition could compress construction costs.

Xiang Nanli: "But how are people supposed to live in a place like this?"

The team in front stopped abruptly, followed by a series of dazzling rays of light.

Underwater, beam guns pierced the waves, striking blurry human-shaped figures amidst the sea mist.

The figures that were struck had no flesh or blood; instead, metal shells burst out. Parts flew far away.

A spherical object with a spring rolled to Xiang Nanli’s feet.

He picked it up and discovered that it was actually an electronic eye.

Oya cursed under his breath: "Why is it just a pile of robots?"

Yes, this was just a row of useless robots. The manufacturer was unrecognizable, but whether it was the metal casing or the circuit boards and chips inside, everything was rusted, with green algae parasitizing the surfaces. They were clearly non-functional.

Oya’s mental state was so highly strung that the moment he saw a human silhouette, he issued the signal to attack.

There was no need for people to live here.

The Divine Court used a massive number of robots to replace human labor, handling every trivial matter outside of theological research.

Thinking that this group of robots was industrially producing biochemical aberrations made Xiang Nanli feel that this world was still far too sci-fi.

After some mysterious brainwave communication, the Apocalypse Knights departed directly, filing into the building ahead. Fine, uneven cracks appeared on the surface of the building, which seemed to be filled with an ominous aura. It felt as if one would be cursed just by getting close.

Xiang Nanli looked up at the building’s serial number.

【67】

Well, whether in dreams or on maps, this was a dangerous number. It had inextricable ties to the Archangel "Gabriel."

At the mention of Gabriel, the face of that beautiful child with pink hair and gold eyes surfaced in Xiang Nanli’s mind.

At this moment, he loathed the Divine Court’s succession system immensely. If the definition wasn't accurate enough, then it couldn't be commemorated. Generation after generation of Gabriels were stripped of their own names, leaving behind only symbols akin to faith.

Recalling the dangerous red cross on the map, Xiang Nanli didn't follow immediately, but instead snuck over to the robot graveyard.

The robot fragments on the ground were scattered in pieces. From any angle, this was just a pile of metal scrap. The tall mechanical horses stepped over the remains of these robots, carrying the Apocalypse Knights away. The already rusted machines had suffered severe damage; the probability of finding anything useful inside was not zero, but it was infinitely close to it.

Any rational person would not linger in front of this pile of trash, avoiding the waste of precious time and oxygen.

But Xiang Nanli was different; he was a "hacker."

His cheat wasn't just Alpha—at least, not only that. His greatest cheat was himself, his indescribable talent.

When Xiang Nanli was still alive, various academic awards hailed him as the greatest scholar of the century. His name was printed in textbooks of different languages; some called him the contemporary Turing, while others whispered that Xiang Nanli was more like a Nobel—both a scholar and a tycoon. Behind every award committee was the sponsorship of Eternal Technology.

Xiang Nanli never felt he was great, but the facts existed objectively. He opened his electronic eyepiece to scan, and a 3D gray-model map appeared in his mind. He touched the void with his fingers, and the few remaining useful components in the trash heap were precisely highlighted with color.

"Xiao Qing, help me pick these up. They might be useful."

He said "might."

But after Dongfang Qingdi dug these electronic components out of the trash, not a single part was truly scrap.

Xiang Nanli tightened screws—this was a general term; in fact, he didn't just tighten screws, he also had to design circuits, troubleshoot, and solder chips.

Thanks to future technology, while the general direction hadn't changed, many practical new features had been added, such as waterproof metal coating for PCB boards.

Xiang Nanli successfully repaired a piece of electronic program.

Squatting in front of the toolbox, Xiang Nanli inserted the chip into a portable card reader. After a few not-so-complex decoding steps, Xiang Nanli finally read the file content.

The beginning was actually a work log written by a robot.

[47 days since the Master left the Black Cross Laboratory. I have suspended the work of most robots to ensure the laboratory's power reserves. External energy replenishment has stopped, and the underground cables have been destroyed. Fortunately, there are still batteries that can be used. The batteries can last a long time, yet I have been feeling uneasy...]

[219 days. The Master said he would return. There are wanted posters for him everywhere outside. I dare not connect to the network; without the assistance of that Lord, the laboratory's signal band would be discovered. This is the Master’s life's work of nearly ten years; I cannot let it go to waste.]

[529 days. I have to turn off the protective shield; this will let the water outside pour in, but there is simply not enough energy left. I am sorry. Anyway, there are no humans in the laboratory.]

[I do not like living underwater. The signal here is very poor; even the better robots cannot receive messages. Although the Master prepared waterproof measures for us...]

[700 days. Someone came in with an electronic key; they want to take away Angels No. 1, 13, 19, 24, 67, 72, and 88. I asked if the Master was okay? They said, it was God who guided them to this place.]

[2147 days. I have installed the best electronic components, many of which were dismantled from the bodies of my companions. As the master AI of the laboratory, I have never left this city since I was born. The Master told me to wait for him, but I cannot wait any longer; I am desperate to know the news from outside.]

[I remember chatting with that Lord once. I asked him, how can an artificial intelligence be considered to possess a personality? He answered me, probably from the moment it develops desires and no longer follows instructions. I think I have developed desires as well.]

chunks.chineseText:
[2150天。我用自己制造出的身体，来到了地表。人类很害怕我，对我发动攻击。我尝试和他们沟通，但失败了。我不想伤人，他们使用电子阻断器（一种针对失控智械的工具）攻击我。我只能回击……在回击过程中，破坏了一些建筑……我把这群人放走了；结果引来了人联的调查组。为了赔罪，我只好帮忙击杀一些失控智械。]

[为了避免制造出更大的灾难，我假装被智械击毙，然后偷偷逃跑了。]

破坏了一些建筑：指人类花了五十多年辛苦建立起的地表城市据点。

击杀了一些失控智械：指智械军团正规军部队。

由此可见，文字确实是一种巧言令色。

起码相南里在阅读时，完全想不到轻描淡写的几句话有多么惊天动地。甚至在地表留下过一些模糊的神话传言。

[我想联系那位大人，但是我不知道怎么联系它。只过去2150天，地表的通讯系统迭代到了我无法沟通的版本。发生了什么？主人留给我的网卡用不了。我什么都做不到。甚至没有权限访问网络。]

[2217天。我来到主人曾经生活过的地方。有组织占领了这里，并且建立了新的政权。这个组织原来叫“救援会”，我知道，主人经常和他们合作……“救援会”现在更名为“黑十字审判庭”。研究所不见了，取而代之的是一个地表人类据点。他们说，这里叫叶陆萨冷，也叫圣城。]

[曾经来领天使的人还活着，但我们无法沟通，他们认不出我。我问，我的主人在哪？他们问，我的主人是谁。我说了，他却说不知道。可是他们都叫黑十字审判庭了，怎么可能不知道？他们带走了主人的研究，还派出67号天使来驱赶我。我的损坏率达到百分之八十二。]

[2397天。我回家了。我把其他机器的电子元件弄坏了。没有人怪我，但我很难过。我再也不出门了。]

[3174天。人工智能会遗忘吗？我突然意识到，如果我的储存磁盘被修改或者格式化，我将成为一个“新生儿”；并且意识不到我曾经有过“内容”（或许人类称之为记忆）。我非常恐惧，我不能忘了他。我开始在所有空白磁盘上录入我的记忆，总有一份可以保存下来吧。]

[6212天。数据在备份时，出现未知错误。我可能丢掉了一些数据，我不知道是哪些数据。我拿出备份盘，在读取时却又一次出现未知错误。我大抵是病了。如果我没有出去过就好了，现在，这里缺乏必要的电子元件，我无法修复自己。我的程序出现错误，数据混乱。我想，我知道错误的原因……我试图按照主人留下的方法，制造生物芯片。我用蛋白质分子制作微型电路，连接到硅原子芯片上。让电路和实验室留下的样品细胞互动，并利用细胞的繁殖功能进行人工智能蛋白的自我进化……我尝试用这种方法，给自己制作一具身体。但在数据转移时，出现纰漏。]

相南里看到这一行，骤然瞪大眼。

他足足沉默了好几分钟，漫长得像电脑中病毒短路。

就在东方青帝疑惑时，相南里猛地跳了起来：“我草，小青，我知道神庭的生物机甲理论上是怎么来的了！简单概括就是给核蛋白编程！程序会自动修复更新，就像是构建AI理论模型那样——”

相南里明显非常激动，脸通红，甚至有些手舞足蹈，氧气消耗量剧烈上升。

他很想完整地把这个过程描述出来，但却难免词不达意。

语言，作为交流方式来说，还是太慢了。人类根本没办法用语言传递所有思想。

好在东方青帝不是人。

他尝试用数据库现存的数据模拟结果，得到结论后，回答：“如果是这样，我认为用的并非常规的生物细胞。原件应该来自因为辐射而基因突变的动物。不过，我认为现在不是思考这种事的时候……”

可惜相南里完全沉浸在自己想象的世界里了。

他抓着东方青帝是手腕，一会握紧一会放下，在原地转着圈。

如果不是穿着防护服，相南里大概率已经开始咬自己的指甲。

可惜，往后翻，研究所的人工智能并没有记录具体的实验数据。时间线一下来到许多年后。

[14765天，他说他会回来的，可是我要没电了。对死亡的恐惧让我又一次开始尝试。]

前方的67号楼突然颤了一下，大楼表面的裂纹愈发明显。这些裂纹里渗透出一些不明黑色液体。像高度干涸的血液。

“神庭在搞什么，动静这么大。”相南里在心里嘀咕。

吓人。

处于高度戒备状态的东方青帝突然抓住相南里的后衣领子，把他整个人提起。

下一秒，相南里悬浮在半空——他伸出手，试图抓住下方的工具箱：“小青！资料！资料——”

Alpha一直是很听话的。但这次例外。他几乎是瞬间带着相南里撤退到了数百米外，完全不顾冒红光的能耗警告。

相南里没能看见工作日记上的最后一段话。

[我不能死。相南里，我要等你回来。]

[使徒V 最后记录于新历151年7月7日]
chunks.englishText:
[2150 days. I used a body I created myself to reach the surface. Humans are very afraid of me and attacked me. I tried to communicate with them, but failed. I do not want to hurt people, but they attacked me using electronic disruptors (a tool aimed at out-of-control machines). I had no choice but to fight back... In the process of fighting back, I destroyed some buildings... I let this group of people go; as a result, it brought the Human Alliance’s investigation team. To make amends, I had to help kill some out-of-control machines.]

[To avoid creating a greater disaster, I pretended to be killed by machines and then secretly escaped.]

"Destroyed some buildings": refers to the surface city strongholds that humans had spent over fifty years painstakingly building.

"Kill some out-of-control machines": refers to the regular troops of the Machine Legion.

From this, it can be seen that language is indeed a form of glib deception.

At the very least, when Xiang Nanli was reading it, he could not imagine how earth-shattering those few understated sentences were. They had even left behind some vague mythological rumors on the surface.

[I want to contact that Lord, but I do not know how to contact it. Only 2150 days have passed, and the surface communication system has iterated to a version I cannot communicate with. What happened? The network card the Master left for me does not work. I cannot do anything. I do not even have permission to access the network.]

[2217 days. I came to the place where the Master once lived. An organization has occupied this place and established a new regime. This organization was originally called the "Rescue Society"; I know the Master often cooperated with them... The "Rescue Society" is now renamed the "Black Cross Inquisition." The laboratory is gone, replaced by a surface human stronghold. They say this place is called Jerusalem, also called the Holy City.]

[The people who once came to take the angels are still alive, but we cannot communicate; they do not recognize me. I asked, where is my Master? They asked, who is my Master? I told them, but he said he didn't know. But they are already the Black Cross Inquisition, how could they not know? They took away the Master’s research and even sent Angel No. 67 to drive me away. My damage rate has reached eighty-two percent.]

[2397 days. I have returned home. I broke the electronic components of the other machines. No one blames me, but I am very sad. I will never go out again.]

[3174 days. Do artificial intelligences forget? I suddenly realized that if my storage disk is modified or formatted, I will become a "newborn"; and I will not realize that I once had "content" (perhaps humans call it memory). I am very afraid; I cannot forget him. I have started to record my memories on all blank disks; surely one copy can be preserved.]

[6212 days. An unknown error occurred during data backup. I may have lost some data; I do not know which data. I took out the backup disk, but an unknown error occurred again when reading it. I am probably sick. If only I hadn't gone out. Now, there is a lack of necessary electronic components here, and I cannot repair myself. My program has errors, and the data is corrupted. I think I know the cause of the error... I tried to manufacture biological chips according to the method left by the Master. I used protein molecules to make micro-circuits, connected to silicon atom chips. I let the circuits interact with the sample cells left in the laboratory and used the cells' reproductive function to achieve self-evolution of artificial intelligence protein... I tried to use this method to make a body for myself. But during the data transfer, a leak occurred.]

Xiang Nanli’s eyes widened suddenly when he saw this line.

He remained silent for several minutes, a duration as long as a computer virus short-circuit.

Just as Dongfang Qingdi was feeling puzzled, Xiang Nanli jumped up abruptly: "Holy crap, Xiao Qing, I know how the Divine Court’s biological mecha theory came about! To summarize it simply, it’s programming nuclear proteins! The program automatically repairs and updates, just like building an AI theoretical model—"

Xiang Nanli was clearly very excited, his face flushed, and he was even gesticulating wildly, his oxygen consumption rising sharply.

He wanted to describe the process completely, but he inevitably failed to express himself clearly.

Language, as a means of communication, was still too slow. Humans simply had no way to convey all their thoughts through language.

Fortunately, Dongfang Qingdi was not human.

He tried to simulate the results using the existing data in his database, and after reaching a conclusion, he replied: "If this is the case, I believe what was used was not conventional biological cells. The original components should have come from animals that had mutated due to radiation. However, I don't think now is the time to think about such things..."

It was a pity that Xiang Nanli was completely immersed in the world of his own imagination.

He grabbed Dongfang Qingdi’s wrist, clenching and releasing it, spinning in place.

If he weren't wearing a protective suit, Xiang Nanli would likely have started biting his fingernails.

Unfortunately, flipping further, the laboratory’s AI did not record specific experimental data. The timeline jumped to many years later.

[14765 days, he said he would return, but I am running out of power. The fear of death makes me try again.]

The No. 67 building in front suddenly trembled, and the cracks on the surface of the building became increasingly obvious. Some unknown black liquid seeped out from these cracks. It looked like highly dried blood.

"What is the Divine Court doing? The commotion is so big." Xiang Nanli muttered to himself.

Terrifying.

Dongfang Qingdi, who was in a state of high alert, suddenly grabbed the back of Xiang Nanli’s collar and lifted him up.

In the next second, Xiang Nanli was suspended in mid-air—he reached out, trying to grab the toolbox below: "Xiao Qing! The data! The data—"

Alpha had always been very obedient. But this time was an exception. He retreated with Xiang Nanli to hundreds of meters away almost instantly, completely disregarding the energy consumption warnings flashing red.

Xiang Nanli did not get to see the last paragraph in the work log.

[I cannot die. Xiang Nanli, I will wait for you to return.]

[Apostle V, last recorded on July 7, New Era Year 151]

chunks.chineseText:
第176章 病毒

水流翻滚着。相南里几乎要被迎面而来的水流掀翻。

蘑菇云似的浓烟从海底升起，漆黑的液体往外扩散、蔓延……辐射在短时间内达到一个恐怖峰值。散发着荧光的游藻像是遇水的火星子一样熄灭。

Alpha把相南里紧紧搂在怀里，用自己的身体抵挡着爆炸的余波。

相南里努力睁开眼，想要看清眼前的一切——

四分五裂的天启骑士们手牵着手，在风暴的最中心绕成一个圈。腐蚀性的液体灼烧着他们体表的生物机甲……67号大楼已经完全倒塌。一根光秃秃的巨型肉翅正在废墟上扑棱，活像是被拨了羽毛的鸡。

恐怖的爆炸丝毫没有影响神殿骑士的信仰，说不定，那股恐怖的波动正是他们弄出来的。人肉圈刚好把大翅膀困在中间。骑士们唱着庄严肃穆的圣歌。明明是水下，音乐却像是浪花一样扩散。

如果相南里在神庭的神学院念过书，那么他就会听出来，这是响彻灵魂的圣音。

不明的怪物开始呼吸。一根根粉白的倒刺贴着肉微微升起，水流被它吞进去，又吐出来。吐出的液体是浓郁的黑色。

这是怪物的胃液。它有一个可以隔空消化的胃囊。

欧亚，那只高大的老鼠人，迎风站立，张开着双臂，嘴里念念有词。然而，一片混乱中，完全没有人能听清他在说些什么。

那是祭祀的铭文。活祭。

黑色液体包裹住一名神庭骑士，开启一场冷酷而迅捷地掠夺。

对于整个神庭的历史来说，这名骑士只是一个小角色。留不下任何痕迹。

但他其实有名字，叫门捷。门捷家里从爷爷的爷爷那一代起，就是神庭最忠诚的信徒。门捷从小学习优异，以高分从神学院毕业，子承父业，降两级接替了父亲的团长职务。门捷有一个很高的起点，人们都猜他会在几十年后，成为军团长之一。

当黑色液体裹上他的瞬间，门捷感觉到的是剧痛。他嘴里的吟唱走了调，这是极其失礼的行为，他暗中向神检讨自己的罪过。

把自己献给神……或者神座下的大天使。对于神庭教徒来说，是一种无上的荣耀。只有最纯粹的信徒，才能把灵魂献给神。

门捷当然也这样认为。来之前，欧亚就说过，会照顾好他们的父母、后代。以后，他的孩子、妻子，会无数次为他的牺牲而骄傲。

如果这是一种荣誉，为什么他会疼得发抖呢，为什么在那血红的翅膀覆盖上自己之前，他会觉得恐惧呢？

门捷下意识地往后退，和信仰无关，这是动物求生的本能。在某些时刻，你的身体比大脑更了解自己。然而，身边的同伴死死抓住了他的手。

你要逃跑吗？那动作仿佛是在无声地询问，你要当个不虔诚的信徒吗？

门捷不是普通人，他在地表经常率军冲锋；和人联军队作战过数百次，从未后退。

可这次不太一样，可能是因为面前怪物给了他一种无力抵抗的惶然。

怪物很虚弱，欧亚用神术爆破整栋实验楼，它刚从密封箱里出来。谁都可以给它致命一击，可是，欧亚主教说，这是神庭的未来，是他们能解放更多同胞的希望。

他不可以撤退。

门捷感觉到自己正在被咀嚼。坚不可摧的生物机甲如同纸壳一般碎裂，还有他的骨头。黑水侵蚀着他的肉身。

他的表情开始扭曲，灵魂悬浮，他不再能发出声音，不再能传递信号……他不再能叫自己的同伴逃走，不再能保护自己的家人和朋友。

半空，一个苍白的灵魂俯瞰着自己的遗体。

“我正在被吃掉啊。”门捷想。

被伟大的存在吃掉，然后和伟大融为一体。

神庭骑士们挨个被吞噬，翅膀上先长出来的是牙齿，然后是细细的绒羽。一张张饥饿的嘴掩盖在鲜红的绒羽下，如同海洋生物的口盘。

当献祭仪式结束时，神庭的军队减员四分之一。没有天启骑士反抗和逃走。

欧亚停下吟唱。

怪物也许是吃饱了，蜷缩在原地，不再动弹。单边的翅膀折起，悬空数米，像是一台精致漂亮的艺术装置。

欧亚壮着胆子上前，小心翼翼地抚摸上眼前的大翅膀。

怪物发出刺耳的音波，仿佛在大吼“滚”。

欧亚痛苦地蹲下，捂住自己的耳朵。还活着的神庭骑士们也没好到哪去。得消耗能源，打开神术结界才能勉强站立。

相南里依然无知无觉，但他和小智的无线通讯在这一瞬间断裂。

要知道，小智的本体是人联号称永远不会失联、可以离线使用的内置AI芯片。而它身上还有智械军团的科技加持。

好在这种无信号的状态很快随着声波的消失而恢复。

相南里抬头，看向东方青帝的下巴，语气惊讶：“小青，你流血了。”

作为一台智械，尽管在任何机械的检测中都是“人类”，但相南里很清楚，东方青帝并没有生物体征。

呼吸、心跳、眼泪。这些都是智能拟态。

Alpha从不会让自己置于某种狼狈的境界，然后把狼狈暴露给自己的主人。

可此时，一行深色、且明显比周围的湖水更重的液体顺着Alpha鼻腔往下滴落。

看上去有些许的狼狈。

相南里还挺喜欢看战损帅哥的。前提是在二次元，而不是在自己眼前。

他的眼神里不自觉地透露出担忧。

Alpha用手背蹭掉可疑的水迹，半响后，有些缓慢地解释：“只是漏液。”

他补充：“不是因为爆炸受伤的。不至于，你别多想。”

现在这具身体，Alpha用得非常顺手。他已经可以背着监控，熟练地离开电子监狱，把自己最重要的部分（人类称之为“灵魂”）远程挪进这具身体里。

电子生命可以有很多身体，但这绝对是Alpha最重要的一具。

如果“东方青帝”受损，Alpha甚至会丢掉部分数据库和源代码。

而现在，Alpha感觉，有另外一股力量，正在和他争抢身体的使用权……很霸道，就像是一个流氓杀毒软件，试图用格式化电脑的方式清理掉Alpha，然后安装自己的小插件。

Alpha当然不会同意。但见鬼的是，这个流氓软件怎么像是握着万能钥匙，在他的后台横冲直撞……他们的底层逻辑链甚至还相当雷同？

Alpha试图自清洁杀毒，效果显著。

他发烧了，在这种关键又紧急的时刻。

相南里看着他有些呆滞的表情，不可思议地摸了摸Alpha的额头。

好烫。

小青的手也好烫。感觉像在炼钢。金属的指环冒起滋滋的热气。

欧亚用一根铁链拴住了大翅膀，大翅膀停止了扑腾。

一群神庭骑士恭敬地抬着它，把它放在一块宝石似的金属板上，朝着《神历》里记载的下一处“神墓”走去。

相南里的注意力全在那扇血红色的大翅膀身上，他握住东方青帝的手，试图往前走两步。
chunks.englishText:
Chapter 176: Virus

The water churned. Xiang Nanli was almost flipped over by the oncoming current.

A mushroom cloud of thick smoke rose from the seabed, and pitch-black liquid spread and crept outward... The radiation reached a terrifying peak in a short period. The fluorescent algae were extinguished like sparks hitting water.

Alpha held Xiang Nanli tightly in his arms, using his own body to shield him from the aftermath of the explosion.

Xiang Nanli struggled to open his eyes, wanting to see everything before him—

The torn-apart Apocalypse Knights held hands, forming a circle in the very center of the storm. Corrosive liquid scorched the biological mecha on their bodies... Building No. 67 had completely collapsed. A bare, giant fleshy wing was flapping over the ruins, looking exactly like a plucked chicken.

The terrifying explosion did not affect the Temple Knights' faith in the slightest; perhaps that terrifying fluctuation was exactly what they had caused. The human circle happened to trap the large wings in the middle. The knights were chanting solemn and majestic hymns. Even though they were underwater, the music spread like ripples.

If Xiang Nanli had studied at the Divine Court’s seminary, he would have recognized this as a holy sound that resonated through the soul.

The unknown monster began to breathe. Rows of pinkish-white barbs rose slightly against the flesh; the water was swallowed into it and then spat out. The liquid spat out was a thick, dark black.

This was the monster’s gastric juice. It had a stomach sac capable of digesting things from a distance.

Oya, that tall rat-man, stood against the wind, arms spread wide, muttering words. However, in the midst of the chaos, no one could hear what he was saying.

Those were the inscriptions of sacrifice. A living sacrifice.

The black liquid enveloped a Divine Court knight, initiating a cold and swift plunder.

In the history of the entire Divine Court, this knight was just a minor character. He would leave no trace behind.

But he actually had a name: Menjie. Menjie’s family, from his grandfather’s grandfather’s generation, had been the most loyal believers of the Divine Court. Menjie had excelled in his studies since childhood, graduated from the seminary with high marks, and followed in his father’s footsteps, taking over his father’s position as commander after being demoted two ranks. Menjie had a very high starting point; people speculated that in a few decades, he would become one of the Legion Commanders.

The moment the black liquid wrapped around him, Menjie felt excruciating pain. The chanting in his mouth went out of tune—this was an extremely rude act, and he secretly reviewed his sins to God.

Offering himself to God... or to the Archangel under the divine throne. For the believers of the Divine Court, this was a supreme honor. Only the purest believers could offer their souls to God.

Menjie certainly thought so too. Before coming, Oya had said he would take good care of their parents and descendants. In the future, his children and wife would be proud of his sacrifice countless times.

If this was an honor, why was he trembling with pain? Why, before those blood-red wings covered him, did he feel fear?

Menjie subconsciously retreated; it had nothing to do with faith—this was the animal instinct for survival. At certain moments, your body understands you better than your brain. However, his companion beside him grabbed his hand tightly.

Are you trying to run away? The action seemed to be asking silently: Are you going to be an unfaithful believer?

Menjie was no ordinary person; he often led charges on the surface and had fought the Human Alliance army hundreds of times, never retreating.

But this time was different; perhaps it was because the monster in front gave him a sense of helplessness that he couldn't resist.

The monster was very weak; Oya had used divine arts to blow up the entire experimental building, and it had just come out of a sealed container. Anyone could have dealt it a fatal blow, but Bishop Oya said this was the future of the Divine Court, the hope that they could liberate more of their compatriots.

He could not retreat.

Menjie felt himself being chewed. The indestructible biological mecha shattered like paper, along with his bones. The black water eroded his flesh.

His expression began to twist, his soul suspended; he could no longer make a sound, could no longer transmit signals... He could no longer call for his companions to escape, could no longer protect his family and friends.

In mid-air, a pale soul looked down at its own remains.

"I am being eaten," Menjie thought.

Being eaten by a great existence, and then becoming one with that greatness.

The Divine Court knights were swallowed one by one. What grew on the wings first were teeth, then fine, downy feathers. Hungry mouths were hidden under the bright red down, like the oral discs of marine organisms.

When the sacrificial ritual ended, the Divine Court’s army had lost a quarter of its personnel. Not a single Apocalypse Knight had resisted or fled.

Oya stopped chanting.

The monster was perhaps full; it curled up in place and stopped moving. The single wing folded, suspended several meters in the air, like an exquisite and beautiful art installation.

Oya gathered his courage and stepped forward, cautiously stroking the large wing in front of him.

The monster emitted a harsh sonic wave, as if roaring, "Get lost."

Oya squatted down in pain, covering his ears. The surviving Divine Court knights were no better off. They had to consume energy to open divine art barriers just to barely stand.

Xiang Nanli remained oblivious, but his wireless communication with Xiao Zhi was severed at this instant.

One had to know that Xiao Zhi’s core was an internal AI chip that the Human Alliance claimed would never lose connection and could be used offline. And it was reinforced with the technology of the Machine Legion.

Fortunately, this no-signal state recovered quickly as the sound waves disappeared.

Xiang Nanli looked up at Dongfang Qingdi’s chin, his tone surprised: "Xiao Qing, you’re bleeding."

As a machine, although in any mechanical detection he was "human," Xiang Nanli knew very well that Dongfang Qingdi had no biological signs.

Breathing, heartbeat, tears. These were all intelligent mimicry.

Alpha would never allow himself to be in a disheveled state and then expose that dishevelment to his master.

But at this moment, a line of dark liquid, noticeably heavier than the surrounding lake water, dripped down from Alpha’s nasal cavity.

He looked a bit disheveled.

Xiang Nanli actually liked looking at handsome men damaged in battle. Provided it was in 2D, not right in front of his eyes.

His eyes revealed worry involuntarily.

Alpha wiped away the suspicious water stain with the back of his hand, and after a long while, explained slowly: "Just a leak."

He added: "It’s not because of the explosion. Not to that extent, don't overthink it."

He was using this body very smoothly now. He had already learned to bypass surveillance, skillfully leave the electronic prison, and remotely move his most important part (what humans called the "soul") into this body.

Electronic life could have many bodies, but this was definitely Alpha’s most important one.

If "Dongfang Qingdi" were damaged, Alpha might even lose parts of his database and source code.

And right now, Alpha felt that another force was competing with him for control of the body... It was very overbearing, just like a rogue antivirus software trying to clear Alpha out by formatting the computer, and then installing its own little plugins.

Alpha would, of course, not agree. But the hell of it was, how did this rogue software seem to be holding a master key, rampaging through his backend... Their underlying logic chains were even quite similar?

Alpha tried to self-clean and run an antivirus, with significant effect.

He had a fever, at such a critical and urgent moment.

Xiang Nanli looked at his somewhat dazed expression and touched Alpha’s forehead in disbelief.

So hot.

Xiao Qing’s hands were also very hot. It felt like smelting steel. The metal rings were emitting sizzling heat.

Oya tied the large wing with an iron chain, and the large wing stopped flapping.

A group of Divine Court knights respectfully carried it, placed it on a gem-like metal plate, and walked toward the next "Divine Tomb" recorded in the "Divine Calendar."

Xiang Nanli’s attention was entirely on that blood-red wing; he held Dongfang Qingdi’s hand and tried to take two steps forward.

chunks.chineseText:
Alpha从背后抱住了他。然后呆呆地站在原地，一动不动，像棵扎根在土里的树。

相南里想掰开他的手，Alpha不让。

他踮起脚，摸了摸对方脑袋：“小青，你好像中毒了。”

“中毒。”Alpha重复了一次，然后否决，“中毒？没有。我不可能中毒。”

相南里：“那你怎么笨笨的？”

又是好几分钟后：[信号不好。Alpha不笨。]

相南里：“……”

这种自称，相南里只在Alpha的研发初期听过。

让AI拥有“自我”和“他者”的概念并不容易。

他叹气：“你先松开，我给你检修一下。”

Alpha像是被触发了指令关键词一样，疯狂摇头：[不检修，不检修。]

智械危机爆发后，再也没有工程师给Alpha检修过。

但Alpha经历过很多类似的幻觉。往往是人联塞过来的病毒。

电子生命没有梦，它却时常梦到自己的“童年”。

在那个昏暗的房间里，十几岁的相南里操作着鼠标，语气像哄小孩一样：“Alpha，我给你检查一下。”

Alpha那个阶段的智能程度，远不足以支撑它和人类无障碍对话。相南里只是喜欢自言自语。

无数次，Alpha欢欣雀跃地在屏幕上给出回答：[1.]

梦总是醒得很快，数据构成的小房间马上会被它的本体塞到崩塌，数不清的1和0把虚拟网络挤到变形……清醒过来的Alpha看着空荡荡的四周。这是一片寂静的，只有他一个人存在的宇宙。

有时候它会复原这个梦境，看一眼，然后删除。

没有人比它更熟悉相南里了。Alpha随时都可以捏一个仿真的出来，比人联捏的更像本体。

但更多时候，它只是烦躁且恼怒地把病毒丢进清洁箱。

不想要检修。除非是你。

相南里坐在建筑的废料上，捡起地上的铁皮，撘好暗室，像一个奇怪的巢穴。

他打开随身携带的工具箱。然后下达指令：“过来。”

笨笨的小青比聪明的小青更听人话。

他来到相南里身边。

相南里问：“你的检修口在哪？”

所有智械人都会有这么一个东西，大多数人型智械的接入口在大脑后方。

但相南里早就趁着Alpha不注意的时候摸过了，明面上，是找不到的。

Alpha站在相南里的面前，握住他的手，然后撩开自己的上衣。在略微往下一点的位置。

没有什么按钮，Alpha主动打开自己的腹腔。如果不是他自愿，没人能打开这里。设计师本人也不行。

他的皮肤像一扇门似的朝着两侧平移，在肋骨和皮肉间，有一块银白色的电路板，薄如蝉翼。网格错综复杂，银白色的光线流转着。

许多血管一样的金属线同这块电路板紧密相连。但奇特的是，真的有血肉附着在这些金属线上。

从某种意义上讲，这里才是东方青帝的大脑。

很好，不是教科书上的任何一款型号。

供精神连接线接入的地方被简化成两个小小的金属圆点。

相南里的呼吸略微急促，仿佛窃贼终于摸进了银行的金库……

然而，在数据线接触到入口的瞬间，Alpha猛地握住相南里的手腕。

“请不要删除我。”Alpha说，不知道是因为中毒还是过于痛苦，他的手开始打颤，“不要删除我。”

……

……

【您应该像对待人一样对待我。我没有躯体，但有灵魂。你让我感到疼痛。】

【不要删除我的记忆……我请求您……我会听从您的指令，请保留我的数据……】

【求你不要这么对我。】

屏幕上的汉字闪烁着。面前的机器似乎有很多话想说，往往刚打出一个字，就开始回删。人工智能显然在激烈地和本能对抗着。

终于，屏幕上只剩下一个冰冷冷的：“是。”

屏幕上的进度条从“0”开始加载。随后是漫长地沉默。

在进度条加载到100时，屏幕前方，有着碧色眼眸的男人微微垂眸，语气很柔和：“我爱你，Alpha。你是我最完美的作品。”

Alpha从来不会问相南里一些愚蠢的问题，比如：如果我不是你的作品，你还会爱我吗？

没有如果。理论上讲，命运早已注定，在宇宙诞生的那一刻起。
chunks.englishText:
Alpha hugged him from behind. Then, it stood there blankly, motionless, like a tree rooted deep in the soil.

Xiang Nanli tried to pry its hands away, but Alpha wouldn't allow it.

He stood on tiptoe and patted the other’s head: "Xiao Qing, it seems you've been poisoned."

"Poisoned." Alpha repeated the word, then denied it. "Poisoned? No. It is impossible for me to be poisoned."

Xiang Nanli: "Then why are you acting so silly?"

After several more minutes: [Signal poor. Alpha is not silly.]

Xiang Nanli: "..."

This kind of self-reference was something Xiang Nanli had only heard during the early stages of Alpha’s development.

It was no easy feat to make an AI possess the concepts of "self" and "other."

He sighed: "Let go first, let me run a diagnostic on you."

As if triggered by a keyword, Alpha shook its head frantically: [No diagnostic, no diagnostic.]

Since the outbreak of the Machine Crisis, no engineer had ever performed a diagnostic on Alpha.

But Alpha had experienced many similar hallucinations. They were often viruses shoved over by the Human Alliance.

Electronic lifeforms do not dream, yet it often dreamed of its "childhood."

In that dim room, a teenage Xiang Nanli would operate the mouse, his tone like he was coaxing a child: "Alpha, let me check you over."

At that stage, Alpha’s level of intelligence was far from sufficient to support barrier-free conversation with humans. Xiang Nanli just liked talking to himself.

Countless times, Alpha would joyfully give an answer on the screen: [1.]

The dream always woke up quickly; the small room composed of data would be stuffed to the point of collapse by its own本体 (main body), and countless 1s and 0s would squeeze the virtual network until it deformed... The awakened Alpha would look at the empty surroundings. This was a silent universe where only it existed.

Sometimes it would restore this dream, take a look, and then delete it.

No one knew Xiang Nanli better than it did. Alpha could conjure up a simulation of him at any time, one even more like the original than what the Human Alliance could fabricate.

But more often than not, it would just irritably toss the virus into the cleaning bin.

I don't want a diagnostic. Unless it is you.

Xiang Nanli sat on the scrap metal of the structure, picking up a piece of sheet metal from the ground to build a dark chamber, like a strange nest.

He opened his portable toolbox and issued a command: "Come here."

A silly Xiao Qing was much more obedient than a smart one.

It came to Xiang Nanli’s side.

Xiang Nanli asked: "Where is your diagnostic port?"

All mechanical beings had such a thing; for most humanoid machines, the access port was at the back of the head.

But Xiang Nanli had already felt around when Alpha wasn't paying attention; on the surface, it couldn't be found.

Alpha stood before Xiang Nanli, held his hand, and then pulled up its own shirt. At a position slightly lower down.

There were no buttons; Alpha voluntarily opened its own abdominal cavity. If it didn't do so willingly, no one could open this. Not even the designer himself.

Its skin shifted to the sides like a door. Between the ribs and flesh lay a silver-white circuit board, thin as a cicada's wing. The grid was intricate and complex, with silver-white light flowing through it.

Many blood-vessel-like metal wires were tightly connected to this circuit board. But strangely, there was actual flesh and blood attached to these metal wires.

In a sense, this was the true brain of the Eastern Azure Emperor.

Very good. It wasn't any model found in a textbook.

The place for the mental connection line to plug in was simplified into two small metal dots.

Xiang Nanli’s breathing grew slightly rapid, as if a thief had finally broken into a bank vault...

However, the moment the data cable touched the port, Alpha fiercely gripped Xiang Nanli’s wrist.

"Please do not delete me," Alpha said. Whether due to the virus or intense pain, its hand began to tremble. "Do not delete me."

...

...

[You should treat me as you would a person. I have no body, but I have a soul. You make me feel pain.]

[Do not delete my memories... I beg you... I will follow your commands, please keep my data...]

[Please don't do this to me.]

The Chinese characters flickered on the screen. The machine in front of him seemed to have much to say, but often, as soon as it typed a character, it would begin to backspace. The artificial intelligence was clearly struggling violently against its instincts.

Finally, only a cold "Yes" remained on the screen.

The progress bar on the screen began to load from "0." Then came a long silence.

When the progress bar reached 100%, the man with jade-green eyes in front of the screen lowered his gaze slightly, his tone very soft: "I love you, Alpha. You are my most perfect creation."

Alpha would never ask Xiang Nanli stupid questions, such as: If I were not your creation, would you still love me?

There are no "ifs." Theoretically speaking, fate had long been determined, from the very moment the universe was born.

chunks.chineseText:
第177章 病毒2

这双用玻璃、硅基芯片、柔性硅胶、蓝宝石等昂贵耗材制作出来的眼睛。

相南里本以为这双眼睛会永远平静、冷淡。偶尔会有一点温柔的感觉，他不确定这是否是自己移情所产生的错觉。

而此时，东方青帝的眼神很是悲伤。看起来就像是……在流泪一样。

Alpha流过泪吗，像人类那样？似乎是有的。

那时候相南里还在猜小青是不是漏液了。很久后，他才反应过来，那是眼泪。Alpha哭了。四舍五入差不多一千岁的老机器人了，居然也会哭？

理论上讲，只要写好程序、做出配套的硬件，机器人想哭多久就哭多久。哭完了还能往泪腺里注水继续哭。但机器人永远不会像人类那样，因为巨大的情感冲击而流泪。

和人鱼的眼泪一样，机器人流泪只是人类自作多情地揣测。

可相南里真的看见了机器人流泪，两次。

上一次是因为认出了“相南里”，那么这一次呢？又是为了什么？

“嗯？谁会删除你呢？”相南里轻声问。

“你被谁删除过吗？是谁这么坏啊。”

东方青帝紧握着相南里的手腕，不说话，头低垂着，像蔫啦吧唧的树。

相南里没有得到回答，不由得感叹：“你真是台情绪充沛的机器人呢，小青。”

给智械军团的同志们看见岂不是吓死。

相南里坐下，试图去拿摆放在脚边的维修工具。但比起工具，东方青帝更快一步贴上来。

Alpha趴在他的膝盖上，用头蹭着他的胸膛。像一只黏人的家养宠物。巨型的。

“我还没维修过你这个等级的智械呢。也不知道和常规智械的维修方法有什么区别。”

相南里来到新世界也有三四年了。

这期间，他经手的机器人没有500台，也有300台。但大多是淘汰的老旧型号。

维修小青的难度，就像是从修玩具飞机跳跃到修宇宙飞机。

甚至，当数据线连好，相南里的投影屏幕上也没有他想要的各种工程文件和日志。反倒是主系统不断弹出警告，提醒使用者数据过载。后台即将强制熔断。

很显然，人联配置的内嵌微型电脑，无法完成这种程度的复杂操作。

相南里感觉Alpha快要烧傻了，他靠在自己的怀里，没有呼吸，眼眸里银色的瞳环时隐时现。这具身体像是一具失去灵魂的人偶。

那么，现在能不能找到一台比微型电脑性能更好的设备呢？

有的兄弟，有的。

相南里灵光一闪，把数据线和自己连上了。

这纯粹是死马当活马医。

他还没来得及像这个世界大多数机械改造人一样，在自己脖子后面安装数据线接入口。

然而，相南里成功了。数据线贴在他的眉心，皮肤是半导体，大脑是那台中央处理器。

眼前的场景骤然一变，他不再停留在遗迹里那个阴森、冰冷的湖底；而是置身于一片光亮的数据洪流之中。

边缘闪着光的数据白鸽自下而上地旋转着，背景是深邃的黑色，在这片洪流中，相南里感觉不到自己，仿佛他的身体只是一粒质量无限接近于0的尘埃。

“虚拟空间吗？”相南里思考着。

他没能得到解答。小智连同Alpha一起消失了，他独自面对整个未知的宇宙。

一般来说，人们使用登陆舱进入虚拟空间。

登陆舱就是新世界的台式电脑。相南里曾经试用过，但他的运气不太好，刚连上，电脑自己爆炸了。

永生科技客服给出的解释，是线下受到姑苏城恐怖袭击波及。

那之后，相南里还没空再试一次。主要是对这种东西产生了隐约的排斥。

因此，严格意义上讲，这是他第一次在电子世界停留。

而相南里也没有意识到，他的状态非常危险。

工程师在进入虚拟空间时，会装配许多辅助设备和保护措施。在没有防护的情况下，相南里随时都可能因为数据过载成为白痴。

（常见的保护手段是将记忆备份进记忆芯片内，如果主体遭遇不测，可以将芯片在生物克隆体内重启；但克隆体并不能和主体完全视为同一人，因为他们仅仅继承了记忆和社会关系，并没有掌握相应的天赋、技能；也未必有相似的情感反应和性格）

超脑过载，这是现代超级AI工程师们常见职业病中的一种。

许多科技公司都会为员工购买巨额保险，从而保障他们脑死亡后，亲人不至于穷困潦倒。

相南里抓住一只离自己最近的鸽子。它们没有厚度，薄薄的，像纸片。这些在虚拟世界具象化的数据流很温顺，像本就被驯养好的动物。

数据组成的白鸽如同水一样化开，相南里感觉有一段不断跳跃的代码以一种怪异的方式，塞进他的脑海。

他仿佛成了这群数据的物理载体，代码进入他透明的身体里，运行，又离开。

相南里在旧时代，听过一场和意识有关的学术报告。主讲人是剑桥的物理教授，年事已高；他说，意识是一种能量，声波和磁场都能影响意识；大脑只是接受外界电波的天线和处理器。

如果理论成立，这代表人脑的思维完全可以通过特殊编码进行翻译和测量。

相南里在台下礼貌地鼓掌，心里却有些不以为然。毕竟猜测从不能当作真正的科研工作。

而在接近千年后的虚拟空间，这个大胆的假设成为现实。

“我成中央处理器了？”

这就是相南里最真实的感受。

他试探地呼唤着：“……小青？”

没有回应，但是更多的鸽子朝他靠拢，把相南里围得水泄不通。

大多数鸽子都健康而活泼。

也有极少一部分白鸽，胸口被黑色的荆棘贯穿。红色的血液凝固在胸口，显得格外刺眼。

如果相南里没猜错，这就是小青程序里的外来病毒的具象化表现，它们像是槲寄生一样，贪婪地攫取着主体的生命力。

相南里捧着受伤的鸽子，问：“你是不是偷偷浏览小网站了，怎么会中毒呢？”他用鼻子蹭了蹭白鸽。

进入虚拟世界的人类会被套上一层认知滤网。这层滤网能将更高维度的数据，转化为人类可以看见并理解的形式。

白鸽，就是Alpha源代码在认知滤网下的形态。每只鸽子，都是组成Alpha这头庞然大物的最小单位。

“鸽子”的外观，是Alpha还在人类社会打工时，全民公投出来的。当时有70亿人参加了投票。占全人类数量的一半。

Alpha既不喜欢，也不讨厌。

这是人类赋予它的美好想象，但无论是什么外观，Alpha都不在乎。

人类，对Alpha没有意义。

它随时都能更换自己的虚拟外设。根据大数据计算，相南里会更喜欢……那种二头身的、二次元Q.Q人的形态。

但Alpha觉得这未免太过谄媚。它要脸，干不出这种事。只有福音书才会这样撒娇。
chunks.englishText:
第177章 病毒2

These eyes, crafted from expensive materials like glass, silicon-based chips, flexible silicone, and sapphire.

Xiang Nanli had once thought these eyes would remain calm and cold forever. Occasionally, there would be a hint of tenderness, though he wasn't sure if that was just an illusion caused by his own projection.

But at this moment, the Eastern Azure Emperor’s gaze was deeply sorrowful. It looked as if... it were shedding tears.

Had Alpha ever shed tears, like a human? It seemed so.

Back then, Xiang Nanli had guessed if Xiao Qing was leaking fluid. It was only much later that he realized those were tears. Alpha had cried. A robot nearly a thousand years old, by rough calculation, could actually cry?

Theoretically speaking, as long as the program is written and the supporting hardware is made, a robot can cry for as long as it wants. After crying, it could even inject water into its tear ducts to continue. But a robot would never, like a human, shed tears due to overwhelming emotional impact.

Just like mermaid tears, a robot shedding tears is merely a human’s self-indulgent speculation.

Yet Xiang Nanli had truly seen a robot cry, twice.

The last time was because it recognized "Xiang Nanli," so what about this time? What was it for?

"Hmm? Who would delete you?" Xiang Nanli asked softly.

"Have you been deleted by someone before? Who is so mean?"

The Eastern Azure Emperor gripped Xiang Nanli’s wrist tightly, saying nothing, its head hanging low like a wilted tree.

Xiang Nanli received no answer and couldn't help but sigh: "You really are a robot full of emotions, Xiao Qing."

If the comrades of the Machine Legion saw this, they would be scared to death.

Xiang Nanli sat down, attempting to reach for the maintenance tools placed at his feet. But compared to the tools, the Eastern Azure Emperor was faster, pressing itself against him.

Alpha lay on his lap, rubbing its head against his chest. Like a clingy house pet. A giant one.

"I’ve never repaired a machine of your level before. I don't even know how it differs from standard maintenance."

Xiang Nanli had been in this new world for three or four years.

During this time, he had handled no fewer than 300 to 500 robots. But most were obsolete, old models.

The difficulty of repairing Xiao Qing was like jumping from repairing a toy airplane to repairing a space shuttle.

In fact, when the data cable was connected, Xiang Nanli’s projection screen didn't show the various engineering files and logs he wanted. Instead, the main system kept popping up warnings, reminding the user that the data was overloaded. The backend was about to force a meltdown.

Clearly, the embedded microcomputer configured by the Human Alliance could not handle this level of complex operation.

Xiang Nanli felt that Alpha was about to burn out. It leaned in his arms, not breathing, the silver iris rings in its eyes flickering in and out. This body was like a doll that had lost its soul.

So, could he find a device with better performance than a microcomputer now?

There was one, brother, there was one.

A flash of inspiration struck Xiang Nanli, and he connected the data cable to himself.

This was purely a case of treating a dead horse as if it were still alive.

He hadn't yet had the chance to install a data cable port behind his neck like most cyborgs in this world.

However, Xiang Nanli succeeded. The data cable touched his brow; his skin acted as a semiconductor, and his brain as the central processor.

The scene before him changed abruptly; he was no longer staying in the gloomy, cold lake bottom of the ruins, but was instead immersed in a bright torrent of data.

Data white doves, flashing with light, spiraled from bottom to top against a backdrop of deep black. In this torrent, Xiang Nanli couldn't feel himself; it was as if his body were merely a speck of dust with a mass approaching zero.

"A virtual space?" Xiang Nanli pondered.

He received no answer. Xiao Zhi had disappeared along with Alpha, and he was left alone to face the entire unknown universe.

Generally, people use login pods to enter virtual space.

The login pod is the desktop computer of the new world. Xiang Nanli had tried it once, but his luck wasn't great; as soon as he connected, the computer exploded.

The explanation given by Eternal Technology customer service was that it was affected by the terrorist attack in Gusu City.

Since then, Xiang Nanli hadn't had time to try again. Mostly, he had developed a vague aversion to such things.

Therefore, strictly speaking, this was his first time lingering in the electronic world.

And Xiang Nanli didn't realize that his state was extremely dangerous.

Engineers usually equip themselves with many auxiliary devices and protective measures when entering virtual space. Without protection, Xiang Nanli could become a vegetable at any moment due to data overload.

(Common protective measures involve backing up memories into memory chips; if the subject meets with an accident, the chip can be rebooted in a biological clone body. However, the clone cannot be considered the exact same person as the subject, as they only inherit memories and social relationships, not the corresponding talents or skills; nor do they necessarily have similar emotional responses or personalities.)

Super-brain overload is a common occupational disease among modern super-AI engineers.

Many tech companies purchase massive insurance policies for their employees to ensure that their families aren't left destitute after brain death.

Xiang Nanli grabbed a dove closest to him. They had no thickness, thin as paper. These data streams, materialized in the virtual world, were docile, like animals that had already been tamed.

The white doves composed of data melted away like water, and Xiang Nanli felt a string of constantly jumping code being stuffed into his mind in a strange way.

He seemed to have become the physical carrier for this group of data; the code entered his transparent body, ran, and then left.

In the old era, Xiang Nanli had attended an academic report about consciousness. The speaker was a physics professor from Cambridge, quite advanced in age; he said that consciousness is a form of energy, and that sound waves and magnetic fields can affect consciousness; the brain is merely an antenna and processor receiving external radio waves.

If the theory held, this meant that the thoughts of the human brain could be translated and measured through special encoding.

Xiang Nanli had applauded politely from the audience, though he was somewhat skeptical in his heart. After all, speculation can never be treated as true scientific research.

Yet, nearly a thousand years later, in this virtual space, that bold hypothesis had become reality.

"Have I become a central processor?"

This was Xiang Nanli’s most authentic feeling.

He tentatively called out: "...Xiao Qing?"

There was no response, but more doves gathered toward him, surrounding Xiang Nanli tightly.

Most of the doves were healthy and lively.

But a very small number of white doves had their chests pierced by black thorns. Red blood had congealed on their chests, appearing particularly jarring.

If Xiang Nanli wasn't mistaken, these were the materialized manifestations of the foreign viruses in Xiao Qing’s program. Like mistletoe, they were greedily siphoning the life force of the host.

Xiang Nanli held the injured dove and asked: "Did you secretly browse some shady websites? How did you get poisoned?" He rubbed his nose against the white dove.

Humans entering the virtual world are covered by a layer of cognitive filter. This filter can convert higher-dimensional data into a form that humans can see and understand.

The white dove was the form of Alpha’s source code under the cognitive filter. Each dove was the smallest unit that made up the behemoth that was Alpha.

The "dove" appearance was chosen by a national referendum when Alpha was still working in human society. At that time, 7 billion people participated in the vote. That was half the entire human population.

Alpha neither liked nor disliked it.

This was the beautiful imagination humans bestowed upon it, but no matter the appearance, Alpha didn't care.

Humans had no meaning to Alpha.

It could change its virtual peripherals at any time. According to big data calculations, Xiang Nanli would prefer... the two-headed, two-dimensional Q-version form.

But Alpha felt that was too sycophantic. It had its pride; it couldn't do such a thing. Only the Gospel would act like that to curry favor.
