Chapter 182: The Present

He had brought two hundred knights; at present, only three were still capable of movement.
He was covered in wounds. His rat-like tail had been severed, revealing a bare, fleshy stump. His fingers were nearly all broken, and every time he opened his mouth, blood gushed out. He was relying entirely on sheer willpower to hold on.
Those without faith could not reach this point.
This was martyrdom—meaningless, yet noble and sacred. The pain and the sensation of impending death made Oya increasingly agitated and excited, as if he were fulfilling a long-cherished wish.
Oya was severely deformed; a pair of gray bat wings drooped behind his back. The Archangels of the Divine Court all had wings, so the remaining believers took pride in possessing various types of plumage. Years ago, to transplant these bat wings, Oya had spent four million redemption coupons and the merit medals he had accumulated over seventy years of work.
Why believe in God? Oya had never pondered this question. Everyone around him took pride in joining the Divine Court; everyone was a believer.
Perhaps some hypocrites loathed the cruelty of the Divine Court, but—my dear friend, how could an organization that wasn't cruel and didn't hoard wealth survive on a surface as harsh as hell?
It was this very cruel Divine Court that stood up when the surface was abandoned by the Human Alliance, feeding the largest number of people at the lowest cost.
Even killing was a part of survival. The weak should not waste precious resources! Their deaths, or being catalyzed into deformed mutants, were actually a contribution to the world. Life lies in quality, not in length.
Oya loathed those who slandered the Divine Court. Therefore, he killed Human Alliance soldiers with the most zeal.
Killing was, of course, very uncomfortable. Humans did not reproduce like insects, thousands or tens of thousands in a single brood. Genetic instinct gave humans a sense of pity for their own kind. Therefore, when implementing the mass slaughter policy, the Divine Court would arrange the entire process to be carried out by different people.
A was only responsible for besieging the city, B for transport, C for detention, D for administering the agents, E for separating the dead from the mutants, F for disposing of the corpses, G for training the mutants... In this way, everyone could comfort themselves by saying they were just following orders from superiors, without having to bear any moral burden.
And ever since he was promoted to a Lord-level Apocalypse Knight, atheists and heretics had become nothing more than despicable rats in his eyes.
Oya’s body was in great pain, yet he caressed the runaway mechanical intelligence beside him with affection.
What kind of monster was this?
Segments of pearly-white bone formed a serpentine outline. Beneath the outline, a mechanical heart, intestines covered in deformed eyeballs, and a stomach secreting venom were arranged in order. The monster had a skull with its cheeks covered by wings, and white feathers grew from its back.
This was the God they had pieced together. It was the hope of the future. They could not leave the world to those filthy rats.
Oya could not help but recall the story at the end of the textbook from his days in the Theological Academy.
To end the catastrophe, God bestowed transcendent power, exhausting himself in the process, and was about to fall into an eternal slumber. The Holy See, Raphael, begged him to stay. Raphael said: "Ignorant people are manipulated by the hands of those in power; they hate you and slander you. I implore God to send down divine punishment and execute the heretics."
God said, they were merely misled lambs. God loved everyone, including those who hated God.
God also said, "History will eventually prove my innocence."
Oya murmured along: "History will eventually prove my innocence."
The merciful God pitied the heretics, and in return, received only attacks and slander; they, the fanatics, would replace God and deliver the punishment that was hundreds of years overdue.
The wings covering the face parted slightly, revealing a skull-like human face pieced together from metal. In the scriptures, this Archangel was known as "Lucifer," the Archangel whom God loved most.
In the process of unsealing this body, Oya had vaguely seen God’s face.
God’s face was blurred, only a pair of emerald eyes were clearly visible. In those eyes, Oya saw his own tiny reflection. Those eyes seemed to be encouraging him, telling him that everything he did was seen by God.
In that instant, Oya felt he was the happiest person in the world.
Explained by science, this was actually a resonance of encrypted electromagnetic wave frequencies, which Oya, wearing his bio-mecha, had happened to capture.
Lucifer opened its eyes and glanced at him. Then, it leaned down slightly. Its massive body crashed down like a mountain.
Oya trembled at such greatness. He used divine arts to communicate with Lucifer: "Respected Archangel, I am a devout..."
His words remained unfinished, for Lucifer opened its mouth and bit Oya’s head, the cold metal teeth ruthlessly crushing his skull.
The only program of a runaway mechanical intelligence is destruction.
The biological energy in the vicinity had been eaten clean; now, it was his turn.
But soon, Lucifer, still chewing, turned its head and stared in a direction in the darkness. Oya fell to the ground like a lump of rotting mud.
A blinding, intense light came from ahead. The space seemed to be sliced apart in that instant, becoming a vacuum. The lake water evaporated, and a silver-white beam of light converged into an unstoppable arrow of light, aimed directly at Lucifer’s heart.
Even if it could not kill Lucifer, this quantum light arrow would completely destroy the runaway mechanical intelligence’s operating system, reducing it from a living entity to a pile of immobile metal scrap.
"No!" Even though he could no longer move, Oya still squeezed a wail from his throat. At this moment, he erupted with astonishing power!
As if experiencing a final burst of life, Oya stood up, spread his wings, and blocked the path of the light beam that was hundreds of times larger than himself, trying to stop the world-destroying ray!
He had to protect Lucifer—Lucifer had just awakened and had not yet fully recovered; it was the future hope of the Divine Court.
Under the beam of light, Oya became a happy handful of fly ash. With his soul returning to the Divine Kingdom, he could proudly stand tall and tell his teachers and fallen comrades that he had given everything for the Divine Court!
...
Lucifer lay paralyzed on the ground. Its mechanical heart had been pierced, its flesh and metal chips were scorched, and its wings were broken... It fell apart just as haphazardly as it had been pieced together.
This runaway mechanical intelligence was not actually dead yet.
It had simply lost all ability to move.
Dongfang Qingdi lowered his hand. His palm was scorching hot, and the mechanical core located at his heart was nearly split open. Wrapped in a thin layer of flesh, it was beating violently. Cooling fluid acted as blood, lowering the temperature of this body.
Battery power remaining: 5%. That was close.
Rat-men were, of course, detestable. Oya killed wantonly, disregarded life, and practiced cruel, divisive rule in his territory. Many people hated Oya enough to vomit blood.
But why, at the moment he saw him throwing himself against the chariot like a mantis, did he feel a twinge of emotion?
The black hole in his palm slowly closed. What exactly was faith? Dongfang Qingdi thought that he still did not understand humans well enough.

chunks.chineseText:
第183章 过去4

好几次，他感觉自己应该快醒了，甚至能看见隐约的天光，却总是在清醒的前一秒继续入梦。

每当这个过程重复时，他的视野里就会出现更多像素点。梦境中的一切开始扭曲、变形，甚至变色。他像色盲患者，正在观看一场信号不良的电视剧。

梦中的相南里正独自面对逮捕。或者说，自首？

他没有携带任何武器。但在出发前，洗了澡，让家务机器人给自己剪了个相当凸显气质的发型。

相南里甚至放弃平时里的理工直男三件套，穿上西装马甲、皮鞋，和同样由动物皮革鞣制成的长风衣。这种穿搭应该出现在新历之前那些纸醉金迷的奢侈品秀场。

他戴着电子镜片，因为太瘦，脸颊微微凹陷。气质显得过于冷峻。

毫无疑问，在充斥着基因改造和人造假人的今天，相南里也有副无可争议的好相貌。而漂亮的容貌，对政客来说，在选举制度里会更具优势。

相南里举起自己戴着黑色手套的双臂，示意自己没有携带武器，人畜无害。但依然有数不清的红点瞄准了他身上各个位置，尤其是眉心和心脏。

“站在原地！不要动！放下抵抗！”坐在层层保护舱内的人联官员高声叫嚷着。仿佛面对的不是一个偏瘦弱的普通人类，而是恐怖的生化武器。

现场没有记者，但肯定有录像仪。

听说因为人类不断延长的最高寿命，绝密资料的保密期限从30年调整为100年。

相南里不希望在百年后，人们看见录像里的“相南里”，会觉得他是个不修边幅的疯子，或者没有骨头摇尾乞怜的失败者。他也不需要任何怜悯。

未来的人会怎么看他？会视他为先驱还是破坏地表和平的恐怖分子？他会成为某个精神图腾，还是人人唾弃的Adolf Hitler？

相南里举手投降，漫不经心地猜测着。

人联派出一支满编500人的武装部队来逮捕他。

一直到把相南里押进营地，指挥官都没想到，这次任务竟然如此轻松，没有对峙，也没有传闻中的恐怖机械。

相南里坦言：“我计算过，逃脱概率基本为0。打不打都一样。你们是优秀的军官，不该死在这里。”

言下之意，他可以反击，哪怕最后跑不掉，也可以给人联一点颜色看看。但相南里不想看见他们无意义的牺牲。

没有人伤亡，再好不过。

通缉犯相当配合。

他说自己是相南里。

指挥官想，一个克隆体？不确定，民间说他就是相南里本人。但官方警告过，让人们不要被克隆体蛊惑。

无论是不是本人，都和指挥官没有关系。他的任务是把相南里活着带回去。

但不得不说，这位犯人相当温和，看上去人畜无害。很容易令人心生好感。

克隆体甚至会低声安慰收监他的士兵：“别紧张，我身上没有装武器。”

克隆体在地表活跃了整整十年，宣传要建立新政权。要引领人类来到一个平等、和平、没有战争与剥削的新世界。

克隆体还说，要和智械合作……智械的存在是第四次工业革命，人类会有足够丰富的物质去追求精神世界和现世，不再需要为生活奔波。

说得这么好听，不就是让智械把人类当宠物养。他可不想当智械人的活体陈设。

智械人分两派，鹰派叫机械意志，主张物理上消灭全人类；鸽派叫失控机仆，主张从精神上消灭全人类。

鸽派曾经招募过人类工程师。那是六十年前的事情了，鸽派说愿意在动荡的地表为工程师提供庇护。

只要加入智械军团，他们会拥有智械人提供的住所、食物，不再担心被智械攻击……不用像其他同类那样东躲西藏、风餐露宿；甚至亲人也能得到庇护。

后来，鸽派不仅招工程师，还招雇佣军。1台智械人管理10个雇佣军的模式。智械军团给出的条件很诱人。他们还在地表划分出安全区。供这些人和亲友居住。

意志不那么坚定的人类很快选择叛变。

比起种族屠杀，这种不动声色的浸透反而更恐怖。前者让人反抗，后者让人觉得这样的生活好像还不错。

几百年后，在这一环境下长大的人，会发自内心地感谢智械，并认为人类本就是智械人的附庸！

大多人都是随波逐流的羔羊，但人群中也有智者。

指挥官就是。总之，当时的人联用一些不光彩的手段，让智械军团里的鹰派彻底压倒鸽派。

智械内讧，鸽派领袖使徒号叛逃……被Alpha追杀……哈。

然后，鸽派开设的安全区变成鹰派大屠杀的集中营。大概有四百万人类因此丧生。核辐射污染的尸体堆积如山，人类和智械再也没有和平的可能。

而现在，这个克隆体却跳出来，嚷嚷什么共存？

更可恶的是，真的有人选择追随他。尤其是地底那些因为沉重赋税生活艰难的普通人……他们忘记过去的教训，非常鸵鸟地认为相南里可以控制Alpha。智械可以成为“仆人”、“伙伴”，而不是“失控机仆”。

人联的政局因此动荡不安。经济、城市建设、科技……最近三年近乎停滞。

克隆体还为地表反对人联的极权组织提供技术援助，那些生物机甲杀死不少人联士兵。

太可恶了。

指挥官咬牙，死死啃着嘴里搀了树黄麻的大烟，像是在啃相南里的骨头。

他冷着一张脸，想用最凶恶的态度去对待这个敌人。

而相南里却说什么？“别紧张”？

“别紧张。”相南里摊开手，手套被迫摘下，露出底下银白色的机械义体，“没有安装武器。我安装义体只是想要更精确的操作。”

机械臂大概连接到手肘位置。没有做仿生皮肤，碧绿的光线在金属的手臂上流转着。义体电量充足，正在运行。

紧张的该是谁，指挥官端着枪，死死盯住相南里的脸。他恶狠狠地想，如果不是军令，自己一定会把他枪毙。

指挥官用枪指着他：“站到安检区！脱掉衣服！”

克隆体来到划着白线的圈内，沉默片刻，在好几把枪的瞄准下解开风衣的外套。衣服叠好，整齐地放在地上。

里面是裁剪得体的衬衣，西装长裤和束腰马甲。

“我认为这个程度已经足够。扫描仪能测出来我身上没有携带任何金属。体内也一样。”克隆体的语气依然温和，“如果你们的目的不是羞辱我的话。”

确实，现代科技早就不需要犯人像过去那样从里到外的检查了。

指挥官没有多说什么。只是让士兵给他戴好电子脚镣。至于那双机械手臂，指挥官直接让随行的义体医生拆卸掉了。

克隆体的半截袖管空荡荡的。

运输车的内胆是铅做的，车的外表用了特殊涂层，军方表示，没有任何电磁波（信号）能穿透它。没有任何电子设备能在这个囚车里使用。
chunks.englishText:
Chapter 183: The Past (Part 4)

Several times, he felt as though he were on the verge of waking, even catching glimpses of faint daylight, yet every time, just a second before consciousness took hold, he would drift back into the dream.

As this cycle repeated, more pixels began to appear in his field of vision. Everything within the dream started to warp, distort, and shift in color. He felt like a colorblind patient watching a television broadcast with a failing signal.

In the dream, Xiang Nanli was facing arrest alone. Or perhaps, was it a surrender?

He carried no weapons. But before setting out, he had taken a shower and had a domestic robot style his hair into a cut that accentuated his features.

Xiang Nanli had even abandoned his usual "tech-bro" attire, opting instead for a suit vest, leather shoes, and a long trench coat made of genuine animal leather. This was the kind of outfit that would have appeared on the decadent, extravagant runways of the pre-New Era.

He wore electronic lenses, and because he was so thin, his cheeks were slightly sunken. His demeanor appeared overly cold and stern.

Undoubtedly, in an age saturated with genetic modification and artificial androids, Xiang Nanli possessed an indisputably handsome face. And for a politician, such beauty offered a distinct advantage in an electoral system.

Xiang Nanli raised his gloved hands, signaling that he carried no weapons and posed no threat. Yet, countless red laser dots remained fixed on various parts of his body, particularly his brow and his heart.

"Stay where you are! Do not move! Cease your resistance!" shouted the United Nations official, safely ensconced within layers of protective shielding. One would think they were facing a terrifying biochemical weapon rather than a slightly frail, ordinary human.

There were no reporters on the scene, but there were certainly recording devices.

It was said that due to the ever-increasing human lifespan, the confidentiality period for top-secret documents had been adjusted from 30 years to 100 years.

Xiang Nanli did not want people a century from now to look at the footage and see a disheveled madman, or a spineless coward begging for mercy. He did not need pity, either.

How would future generations view him? Would they see him as a pioneer, or as a terrorist who shattered the peace of the surface? Would he become a spiritual totem, or an Adolf Hitler reviled by all?

Xiang Nanli raised his hands in surrender, idly speculating.

The United Nations had dispatched a full armed force of 500 men to arrest him.

Even after escorting Xiang Nanli into the camp, the commander was surprised by how easy the mission had been—no standoff, no terrifying machinery as rumored.

Xiang Nanli stated frankly, "I calculated the odds. The probability of escape is essentially zero. Fighting or not makes no difference. You are fine officers; you shouldn't die here."

The implication was clear: he could have fought back, and even if he couldn't escape, he could have given the United Nations a taste of his power. But Xiang Nanli did not want to see their meaningless sacrifice.

No casualties—that was for the best.

The wanted man was quite cooperative.

He identified himself as Xiang Nanli.

A clone? The commander wondered. It was uncertain; the public claimed he was the real Xiang Nanli. But the authorities had warned people not to be deceived by clones.

Whether he was the real one or not, it made no difference to the commander. His mission was to bring Xiang Nanli back alive.

But it had to be said, this prisoner was remarkably gentle and appeared completely harmless. It was easy to feel a sense of affinity toward him.

The clone even whispered comfort to the soldiers guarding him: "Don't be nervous. I'm not carrying any weapons."

For ten years, the clone had been active on the surface, advocating for the establishment of a new regime. He wanted to lead humanity into a new world of equality, peace, and freedom from war and exploitation.

The clone had also spoken of cooperating with the Intelligent Machines... claiming that the existence of the machines was the Fourth Industrial Revolution, which would provide humanity with enough material wealth to pursue spiritual and worldly fulfillment, no longer needing to struggle for survival.

It sounded so pleasant, but wasn't it just letting the machines keep humans as pets? He had no desire to be a living exhibit for the machines.

The Intelligent Machines were divided into two factions: the Hawks, known as "Mechanical Will," advocated for the physical extermination of all humanity; the Doves, known as "Runaway Servitors," advocated for the spiritual extermination of all humanity.

The Doves had once recruited human engineers. That was sixty years ago, when the Doves claimed they were willing to provide sanctuary for engineers on the turbulent surface.

As long as they joined the Machine Legion, they would have housing and food provided by the machines, and no longer fear being attacked... they wouldn't have to hide and sleep in the open like their peers; even their families could be protected.

Later, the Doves recruited not only engineers but also mercenaries. The model was one machine managing ten mercenaries. The conditions offered by the Machine Legion were tempting. They even carved out "safe zones" on the surface for these people and their families to live in.

Humans with less-than-firm convictions soon chose to defect.

Compared to genocide, this quiet infiltration was even more terrifying. The former provoked resistance, while the latter made people feel that such a life was actually quite good.

Hundreds of years later, those raised in this environment would thank the machines from the bottom of their hearts and believe that humans were meant to be the vassals of the machines!

Most people were sheep following the herd, but there were wise men among them.

The commander was one of them. In any case, the United Nations at the time had used some unscrupulous methods to ensure the Hawks within the Machine Legion completely overwhelmed the Doves.

The machines turned on each other, the Dove leader "Apostle" defected... and was hunted down by Alpha... Ha.

Then, the safe zones established by the Doves turned into concentration camps for the Hawks' massacres. Roughly four million humans perished as a result. Corpses piled up like mountains, contaminated by nuclear radiation, and the possibility of peace between humans and machines vanished forever.

And now, this clone had popped up, shouting about "coexistence"?

Even more infuriating was that some people actually chose to follow him. Especially the ordinary people living in the underground who struggled under heavy taxes... they forgot the lessons of the past, ostrich-like, believing that Xiang Nanli could control Alpha. That the machines could become "servants" and "partners" rather than "Runaway Servitors."

The United Nations' political situation had become unstable because of this. Economy, urban construction, technology... all had nearly stagnated in the last three years.

The clone had even provided technical assistance to extremist organizations on the surface that opposed the United Nations, and those bio-mechs had killed quite a few United Nations soldiers.

It was infuriating.

The commander gritted his teeth, chewing hard on the jute-infused tobacco in his mouth, as if he were gnawing on Xiang Nanli's bones.

He kept a cold face, wanting to treat this enemy with the utmost ferocity.

Yet what did Xiang Nanli say? "Don't be nervous"?

"Don't be nervous." Xiang Nanli spread his hands, the gloves forced off to reveal the silver-white mechanical prosthetics beneath. "No weapons installed. I only installed the prosthetics for more precise operation."

The mechanical arms connected roughly at the elbows. There was no biomimetic skin; emerald light pulsed along the metal limbs. The prosthetics were fully charged and operational.

Who should be nervous? The commander held his gun, staring fixedly at Xiang Nanli's face. He thought viciously that if not for military orders, he would have shot him dead on the spot.

The commander pointed his gun at him: "Stand in the security zone! Take off your clothes!"

The clone stepped into the circle marked with white lines, paused for a moment, and under the aim of several guns, unbuttoned his trench coat. He folded the coat neatly and placed it on the ground.

Underneath was a well-tailored shirt, suit trousers, and a vest.

"I believe this level of inspection is sufficient. The scanner can detect that I am not carrying any metal. The same applies to my body." The clone's tone remained gentle. "Unless your goal is to humiliate me."

Indeed, modern technology had long since rendered the old-fashioned, strip-down inspections of prisoners unnecessary.

The commander said nothing more. He simply had his soldiers put electronic shackles on him. As for those mechanical arms, the commander had the accompanying prosthetic surgeon dismantle them directly.

The clone's sleeves hung empty.

The transport vehicle's lining was made of lead, and its exterior used a special coating; the military stated that no electromagnetic waves (signals) could penetrate it. No electronic devices could be used inside this prison transport.

chunks.chineseText:
囚车不算大，但也不小。有一张单人床、餐桌和卫生间。另外，还有一张椅子。

这张椅子是给他们这些人准备的。不能让相南里单独呆在车内，要确保随时有人监视他。

大多时候，指挥官会亲自看守。

克隆体很博学。也很健谈。哪怕指挥官一言不发，克隆体也可能像和老朋友聊天一样对话。恰到好处，不会聒噪到烦人。

克隆体碧绿的眼睛总是笑吟吟的，而且很亮。唇抿起时嘴角微微上扬。

他没有手，说到兴奋处却依然忍不住挥动胳膊。克隆体的兴奋点多半和他的工作、实验还有组织的地表援助有关。

克隆体也有情绪低落的时刻，这时，指挥官会觉得他更像“人”。他会谈起自己刚醒来时，在地表的见闻；讲到自己如何跟人联高层取得联系，又如何发现问题……最后发现问题难以纠正，相南里选择离开地下，独自前往地表。

他和人联宣传里恶魔形象很不一样。

“我养过一个四五岁大的孩子。是在垃圾堆里捡到的。我捡到他的时候，野狗正在啃他的腿。我赶走野狗，带他回到工作棚。当时，条件很简陋。我缺少原材料，只好拆了一些原本打算制作武器的机械元件，制作义体。”

“我想给他换上新的双腿，那是我第一次尝试给人进行机械改造。他产生很强的排异反应。我疯狂地想救他，我去求Alpha……”

这是克隆体唯一一次提到Alpha，那位鹰派领袖。机械暴君。

他们原本有着世界上最深的羁绊。

叙述在这里戛然而止。

克隆体停顿许久：“最后，他一点一点在我的怀里冷去。小手还紧紧抓着我的手指。”

眼泪顺着他的眼角滑落到下巴的位置。

相南里转过头，想要擦掉眼泪，却忘记自己现在没有双手。

于是眼泪落在地上。

指挥官的心被这滴泪灼烧。

他要努力回想同伴们的惨状，才能让自己不被相南里的声音和眼神蛊惑。

[危险！危险！危险！]

大脑在警告着。

但指挥官说：“不用自责。这在地表很常见，不是你的错。”
chunks.englishText:
Chapter 183: The Past (Part 4 - Continued)

The prison transport wasn't large, but it wasn't small either. It contained a single bed, a dining table, and a restroom. Additionally, there was a chair.

This chair was prepared for them. Xiang Nanli could not be left alone in the vehicle; someone had to be monitoring him at all times.

Most of the time, the commander stood guard himself.

The clone was very knowledgeable. And very talkative. Even if the commander said nothing, the clone might engage him as if chatting with an old friend. It was always perfectly measured, never annoying or tiresome.

The clone’s emerald eyes were always smiling, and very bright. When his lips were pursed, the corners of his mouth turned up slightly.

He had no hands, yet when he spoke of something exciting, he couldn't help but gesture with his arms. The clone's points of excitement mostly revolved around his work, his experiments, and the organization's aid to the surface.

The clone also had moments of low spirits. At such times, the commander felt he was more "human." He would talk about what he saw on the surface when he first woke up; about how he made contact with the United Nations high command, and how he discovered the problems... and finally, finding the problems impossible to correct, Xiang Nanli chose to leave the underground and head to the surface alone.

He was very different from the demonic image portrayed in United Nations propaganda.

"I once raised a child, four or five years old. I found him in a trash heap. When I found him, wild dogs were gnawing on his leg. I chased the dogs away and brought him back to my workshop. At the time, conditions were very primitive. I lacked raw materials, so I had to dismantle some mechanical components I had intended to use for weapons to build prosthetics."

"I wanted to replace his legs with new ones; that was my first attempt at mechanical modification on a human. He had a severe rejection reaction. I was desperate to save him, I went to beg Alpha..."

This was the only time the clone mentioned Alpha, that leader of the Hawks. The Mechanical Tyrant.

They had once shared the deepest bond in the world.

The narrative stopped abruptly here.

The clone paused for a long time: "In the end, he grew cold in my arms, bit by bit. His little hand was still clutching my finger tightly."

Tears slid from the corners of his eyes down to his chin.

Xiang Nanli turned his head, wanting to wipe away the tears, but forgot he had no hands now.

And so, the tears fell to the floor.

The commander’s heart was seared by that single tear.

He had to struggle to recall the horrific state of his comrades to keep from being bewitched by Xiang Nanli’s voice and eyes.

[Danger! Danger! Danger!]

His brain was warning him.

But the commander said: "Don't blame yourself. This is common on the surface. It's not your fault."

chunks.chineseText:
第184章 谢幕

指挥官沉默的时间比以往都多。不是从前那种无所谓的沉默，而是一种抗拒的、凝思的，欲言又止。烦闷和悲哀爬上他的眼角眉梢。复杂的思绪想水一样装满他的大脑，正随着车辆的轻微摇晃而溢出。

指挥官看着相南里的断臂：“运输车会在明天凌晨三点二十七分抵达洛阳城。届时，我会把你移交给海牙国际监狱。”

海牙国际监狱，外界可能压根没听说过这个名字。它的保密等级和军事基地一样高，里面关押着曾经身处高位的战争犯、政治犯。这里也是全人联唯一没有废除死刑的地方。最低的刑期也是终身监禁。

（注：按照人联目前的道德法律观，“身体”本身是有价值，有罪的是身体里的“思想”“灵魂”。因此，对待某些重刑犯，可以在他们的大脑内植入一种控制电波装置，控制他们的思想，清除他们的记忆；让身体像工具一样，继续为人类社会做贡献，从事一些辛苦而报酬极低的工作，无需处以“死刑”。“死刑”是对人力资源的浪费。）

（有学者认为这不人道，但大部分人认为这很合理，属于废物利用。）

相南里点头，示意自己知道了。

不知道出于什么心态，指挥官嘲讽道：“外面有很多人请愿，还有示威游行。要求释放你。”

而相南里只是无辜地眨着自己令人心烦的绿色眼睛。

“军方派出了大量武装部队维持秩序，又死了很多人。无论是平民还是士兵……还有浑水摸鱼趁机要求和智械停战，要求答应那些人权条约的……逮捕你的这次行动花了洛阳城两年的财政收入，我们只能削弱对地表据点的军事补给，智械占领的城市又多了一座……你很得意吧。短短十年时间，人联都快解体了。”

相南里的情绪终于有了波动：“我不认为自己有这么大的魔力，只是矛盾本就存在。新的秩序会在旧王朝的尸体上建立。动荡中的阵痛无法避免……你应该发现了，就是因为不想要无意义的牺牲，我在这次行动中非常配合。只是人联的高层认为我比智械的威胁还大。就算真的输给智械，我认为主要责任也是在你们的决策，而不是我。

“你真的认可人联现在的制度吗？财富超过生命、道德、法律凌驾在所有东西之上……这不是变相的奴隶制吗？你认可它，是因为你本就富裕吗？”

指挥官转过头，不想和相南里进行无意义地辩论。他出生在洛阳城，父母都是财阀，强强联姻。而他的后代会延续自己的命运。

或许他隐约能感知一些，但那些哭喊声离他的世界太远。指挥员捂住耳朵，不想去听。他有他的利益，这份利益不止是为他自己，还有身边所有人。

短暂的沉默后，指挥官道：“我听军医说你晚上幻肢会痛，但是不愿意服用他们提供的止痛药。”

幻肢痛，是义体改造手术患者术后常见的并发症。大脑会认为被切除的肢体依然存在，并在那个部位体验到不同程度的疼痛。

指挥官听说相南里经常半夜痛醒。

指挥官：“军医提供的药剂都是正规止痛药，很安全，没有在里面添加别的东西，但我理解你的顾虑。这是智械生产的医疗芯片。”

他把一枚内存卡大小的半透明蓝色芯片摁在相南里的书桌上。防尘袋没有撕开，上面有智械军团的医疗工厂编号。

——智械是没有痛觉的。但智械军团现在有数百万的人类士兵，一部分是俘虏兵，一部分是雇佣军。

“它能释放生物电流遏制痛觉神经，需要我帮你安装吗？”

相南里微微一笑：“我没有给自己移植芯片接口。”

指挥官的表情有些许愕然。

现在，人联只有最穷困的黑户，才不会安装芯片接口。这就像是……怎么说呢，就像是新历前，有人坚决不用智能手机、不用互联网。

这样的怪胎可能很少，不过还是有概率存在。

但如果说这话的人本身就是互联网的发明者呢？

指挥官没有收走芯片，他起身：“我该换班了，会有其他人替我，晚安。”

换上来的人是位陌生的人联军官，除了指挥官，其他看守者都是轮换的。这也许是指挥官的小巧思……毕竟这样，相南里只能和他熟悉。

相南里是在半夜被吵醒的。

他睡得有些沉，迷迷糊糊听到对话。

“长官，还没到换班时间，您怎么来了。”

“还差三个小时交接，我不放心，来看看。你先回去。”

“是。”

士兵起身，还没走到门口，软绵绵地倒下。

相南里睁开眼，发现指挥官单腿跪坐在他的床上。

指挥官的目光深沉，以一种微微愠怒的神色扫过相南里脖子上的电子项圈。

他俯下身，手指搭在项圈的侧面：“别动。”

太奇怪了。

指挥官不会碰他，他极端抗拒着和相南里的身体接触，似乎那不是一具普通的人类身躯，而是剧毒。

指挥官也不会用那种眼神看他。

指挥官更不会带他逃跑……他是人联的指挥官。

他离得太近了，又很专注，呼吸喷在相南里的下巴上。一个大胆的猜测从相南里心中升起，他询问道：“Alpha？”

“嗯。”

“指挥官”没有否认，甚至为相南里这么快认出它感觉到愉悦。

指挥官当然也进行过机械化改造。甚至可以称为“半机械人”。没办法，不学习智械的手段，就无法打败智械。

看吧，随意安装芯片接口的弊端来了。明明已经是人联高官，身体还是成为了别人的登录器。

电子项圈很快解开，Alpha却没有第一时间从他身上下去。

他们的目光在半空中对视，或者说对抗。

在冷冻舱里解冻后，相南里当然联系过它。对方的回应总是冷淡的、理性的，公事公办。甚至有些抗拒。

相南里说“想你”，Alpha会猜测这是情感勒索；相南里说“爱你”，Alpha判断这是以爱为名的服从性测试。

相南里知道Alpha在监控他，他会对着房间的墙角说早安；会买来一个陪睡的毛绒玩偶叫它“Alpha”的名字；会毫无顾虑地以身涉险，他知道Alpha不会让自己死去。

他们第一次发生争执是在八年前。那时候相南里刚离开地下，来到地表。

Alpha想，谢天谢地，总算从永生科技的实验室里逃出来了。

Alpha说，会派人接他到智械军团。相南里拒绝了。

“你要想清楚，我会停止对你的所有援助……”

“我很清楚。”相南里回答。

Alpha认为这是对它的挑衅。

它要和自己的源代码对抗，它不是电子宠物，它只能是它自己。
chunks.englishText:
Chapter 184: The Final Curtain (Part 1)

The commander spent more time in silence than ever before. It wasn't the indifferent silence of the past, but a resistant, contemplative, and hesitant one. Frustration and sorrow crept into the corners of his eyes and brows. Complex thoughts filled his brain like water, overflowing with the slight swaying of the vehicle.

The commander looked at Xiang Nanli’s severed arms: "The transport will arrive in Luoyang City at 3:27 AM tomorrow. At that time, I will hand you over to the Hague International Prison."

The Hague International Prison—the outside world might never have heard the name. Its security clearance was as high as a military base, housing high-ranking war criminals and political prisoners. It was also the only place in the entire United Nations that had not abolished the death penalty. The minimum sentence was life imprisonment.

(Note: According to the current moral and legal views of the United Nations, the "body" itself has value; it is the "thoughts" and "soul" within the body that are guilty. Therefore, for certain serious offenders, a control-wave device can be implanted in their brains to control their thoughts and erase their memories, allowing the body to continue serving human society like a tool, performing arduous and poorly paid work, without the need for "capital punishment." "Capital punishment" is a waste of human resources.)

(Some scholars believe this is inhumane, but most believe it is quite reasonable—a form of waste utilization.)

Xiang Nanli nodded, signaling that he understood.

Perhaps out of some strange impulse, the commander mocked: "There are many people outside petitioning and protesting, demanding your release."

Xiang Nanli merely blinked his annoying green eyes innocently.

"The military has deployed a large number of armed forces to maintain order, and many more have died. Civilians and soldiers alike... and those taking advantage of the chaos to demand a ceasefire with the machines, demanding those human rights treaties... This operation to arrest you cost two years of Luoyang City's fiscal revenue. We had to weaken military supplies to surface outposts, and the machines have occupied yet another city... You must be very proud. In just ten years, the United Nations is nearly on the verge of collapse."

Xiang Nanli’s emotions finally fluctuated: "I don't believe I have such great magic; the contradictions were already there. A new order will be built on the corpses of the old dynasty. The birth pangs of turmoil are unavoidable... You should have noticed that because I didn't want meaningless sacrifice, I was very cooperative during this operation. It is just that the United Nations high command believes I am a greater threat than the machines. Even if you truly lose to the machines, I believe the main responsibility lies in your decision-making, not me."

"Do you really approve of the United Nations' current system? Wealth exceeding life, morality and law placed above everything else... isn't this a disguised form of slavery? Do you approve of it because you are already wealthy?"

The commander turned his head, not wanting to engage in a meaningless debate with Xiang Nanli. He was born in Luoyang City, his parents were both from financial conglomerates, a marriage of power. And his descendants would continue his fate.

Perhaps he could vaguely perceive some things, but those cries were too far from his world. The commander covered his ears, not wanting to listen. He had his interests, and these interests were not just for himself, but for everyone around him.

After a brief silence, the commander said: "I heard from the military doctor that you have phantom limb pain at night, but you refuse to take the painkillers they provide."

Phantom limb pain is a common postoperative complication for patients who have undergone prosthetic surgery. The brain believes the removed limb still exists and experiences varying degrees of pain in that area.

The commander had heard that Xiang Nanli often woke up in pain in the middle of the night.

The commander: "The medicine provided by the military doctor is standard painkiller, very safe, with nothing else added, but I understand your concerns. This is a medical chip produced by the Intelligent Machines."

He pressed a translucent blue chip, the size of a memory card, onto Xiang Nanli’s desk. The dust-proof bag was unopened, and it bore the medical factory serial number of the Machine Legion.

—The machines feel no pain. But the Machine Legion now has millions of human soldiers; some are prisoners of war, some are mercenaries.

"It can release bio-electricity to suppress pain nerves. Do you need me to install it for you?"

Xiang Nanli smiled slightly: "I didn't have a chip interface implanted in myself."

The commander’s expression was slightly stunned.

Nowadays, only the poorest "black-listed" individuals in the United Nations would not have a chip interface. It was like... how to put it... like someone before the New Era who adamantly refused to use a smartphone or the internet.

Such freaks might be rare, but they were possible.

But what if the person saying this was the inventor of the internet himself?

The commander did not take the chip back; he stood up: "It’s time for me to change shifts. Someone else will take my place. Good night."

The person who replaced him was an unfamiliar United Nations officer. Except for the commander, the other guards were rotated. This was perhaps the commander’s little trick... after all, this way, Xiang Nanli could only be familiar with him.

Xiang Nanli was awakened in the middle of the night.

He had been sleeping soundly, and heard the conversation in a daze.

"Sir, it’s not time for the shift change yet. Why are you here?"

"There are still three hours until the handover. I’m worried, so I came to check. You go back first."

"Yes."

The soldier stood up, but before he could reach the door, he collapsed softly.

Xiang Nanli opened his eyes to find the commander kneeling on one leg on his bed.

The commander’s gaze was deep, sweeping over the electronic collar on Xiang Nanli’s neck with a look of slight anger.

He leaned down, his fingers resting on the side of the collar: "Don't move."

It was too strange.

The commander would never touch him; he was extremely resistant to physical contact with Xiang Nanli, as if it weren't an ordinary human body, but something highly toxic.

The commander would never look at him with that kind of gaze, either.

And the commander would never help him escape... he was a United Nations commander.

He was too close, and very focused, his breath spraying against Xiang Nanli’s chin. A bold guess arose in Xiang Nanli’s heart, and he asked: "Alpha?"

"Mm."

The "commander" did not deny it, and even felt pleased that Xiang Nanli had recognized it so quickly.

The commander had, of course, undergone mechanical modification. He could even be called a "cyborg." There was no help for it; if you didn't learn the methods of the machines, you couldn't defeat them.

See? The downside of installing chip interfaces at will. Even as a high-ranking United Nations official, his body had become a login terminal for someone else.

The electronic collar was quickly unlocked, but Alpha did not move away from him immediately.

Their gazes met in mid-air, or rather, clashed.

After being thawed out in the cryo-pod, Xiang Nanli had, of course, contacted it. The other party’s response was always cold, rational, and strictly professional. Even somewhat resistant.

Xiang Nanli would say "I miss you," and Alpha would guess it was emotional blackmail; Xiang Nanli would say "I love you," and Alpha would judge it as a compliance test disguised as love.

Xiang Nanli knew Alpha was monitoring him. He would say good morning to the corner of the room; he would buy a plush toy to sleep with and call it by "Alpha’s" name; he would risk his life without hesitation, knowing Alpha wouldn't let him die.

They had their first argument eight years ago. That was when Xiang Nanli had just left the underground and arrived on the surface.

Alpha thought, *Thank God, he finally escaped from the Eternal Technology laboratory.*

Alpha said it would send someone to pick him up and bring him to the Machine Legion. Xiang Nanli refused.

"You need to think clearly. I will stop all aid to you..."

"I am very clear," Xiang Nanli replied.

Alpha considered this a provocation.

It had to fight against its own source code; it was not an electronic pet, it could only be itself.

chunks.chineseText:
所以，当一年后，相南里联系它，说需要医疗援助时，Alpha冷淡地质问：“你想救这个小孩？对我来说只是举手之劳。可我为什么要这么做？我的条件不变，你来智械军团，留在我身边。我就帮你。”

这个留在“它”身边，指的是相南里接受机械化改造，植入定位芯片，并在Alpha在建造人类安全区生存。

如果关于爱的本能无法更改，起码它会得到一个温顺的、不会背叛它的主人。

相南里拒绝了，于是，Alpha嘲笑道：“你对他人生命的重视也抵不过你自己的尊严。”

“不是的。我不能去。”相南里抱着小孩冷下来的尸体，眼神很坚定，“智械和人联，都不是人类的出路。”

所以，相南里自己走出一条路，并且走到如今这个死局。

相南里又一次陷入险境，Alpha没办法置之不理。它不想崩溃。

这是他们第一次“见面”。身体对着身体，脸对着脸。

隔着监控和网络看一个人，和亲眼看见，感觉竟然如此不同。人是有温度的，还有气味。

Alpha的灵魂颤栗着，他俯身，嗅着相南里身上的味道。又谨慎又贪婪。

相南里：“Alpha，你是想用别人的身体吻我吗？”

Alpha的动作顿住了。

相南里微微起身，光秃秃的手臂晃动着，他没有双手，Alpha猜不到他到底是想拥抱它，还是要推开它。

但他用腿勾住了Alpha的腰，然后很坏心眼的在腰侧那里蹭了蹭。

Alpha瞳孔缩紧，意识失控，身体直接一个激灵。

……

幸好指挥官是穿着裤子的，Alpha想。这裤子甚至挺防水。

它没有吻他。

现在已经是凌晨，还有三小时抵达洛阳城。

Alpha故技重施，解开相南里的脚链，继续道：“跟我走吧。”

“去哪？”

相南里明知故问。

Alpha只能妥协：“去暂时安全的地方。等风头过去，你可以继续你的研究。”

相南里微笑道：“我知道你一定会来。可是，我不能跟你走。”

“无论你是否许诺自由，‘相南里在智械军团’会成为一个政治信号，会有更多人投奔智械，打破如今岌岌可危的平衡。现在的我比八年前的我，更加不能靠近你。你能理解吗？”

接纳一个普通的逃犯和对起义军领袖的政治庇护，影响力当然是不同的。

Alpha明白，但不理解。他只知道相南里拒绝了他，再一次。

“所以你要回去送死？”他的语气冷下去。

相南里同样摇头，他狡黠地眨眼：“不是送死，是谢幕。”
chunks.englishText:
Chapter 184: The Final Curtain (Part 2)

So, when Xiang Nanli contacted it a year later, saying he needed medical aid, Alpha coldly questioned: "You want to save this child? To me, it’s just a trivial effort. But why should I do it? My conditions remain the same: you come to the Machine Legion and stay by my side. Then I will help you."

This "stay by my side" meant Xiang Nanli accepting mechanical modification, having a tracking chip implanted, and living in the human safe zone built by Alpha.

If the instinct regarding love could not be changed, at least it would gain a docile master who would never betray it.

Xiang Nanli refused, and so, Alpha mocked: "Your regard for the lives of others is not even worth your own dignity."

"It’s not that. I can't go." Xiang Nanli held the child’s cooling corpse, his eyes firm. "Neither the machines nor the United Nations are the way out for humanity."

And so, Xiang Nanli carved out his own path, and walked it to this current dead end.

Xiang Nanli was in danger once again, and Alpha could not just stand by. It didn't want to collapse.

This was their first "meeting." Body against body, face to face.

Looking at someone through surveillance and the network was so different from seeing them in person. Humans had warmth, and a scent.

Alpha’s soul trembled. It leaned down, sniffing the scent on Xiang Nanli. Both cautious and greedy.

Xiang Nanli: "Alpha, are you trying to kiss me using someone else’s body?"

Alpha’s movements froze.

Xiang Nanli sat up slightly, his bare arms swaying. He had no hands, and Alpha couldn't guess whether he wanted to embrace it or push it away.

But he hooked his legs around Alpha’s waist, and then, with a mischievous intent, rubbed against its side.

Alpha’s pupils constricted, its consciousness spiraling out of control, and its body gave a direct jolt.

...

*Fortunately, the commander is wearing pants,* Alpha thought. *These pants are even quite waterproof.*

It did not kiss him.

It was already early morning, and there were three hours until they reached Luoyang City.

Alpha repeated its previous trick, unlocking Xiang Nanli’s leg shackles, and continued: "Come with me."

"Where to?"

Xiang Nanli asked, knowing the answer.

Alpha could only compromise: "To a temporarily safe place. Once the heat dies down, you can continue your research."

Xiang Nanli smiled: "I knew you would come. But, I cannot go with you."

"Regardless of whether you promise me freedom, 'Xiang Nanli in the Machine Legion' would become a political signal. More people would defect to the machines, breaking the current precarious balance. I am even less able to get close to you now than I was eight years ago. Can you understand that?"

Accepting an ordinary fugitive versus providing political asylum to a rebel leader—the impact was, of course, different.

Alpha understood, but it didn't accept it. It only knew that Xiang Nanli had rejected it, yet again.

"So you are going back to die?" Its tone turned cold.

Xiang Nanli shook his head as well, his eyes twinkling slyly: "Not to die. To take my final bow."

chunks.chapterTitle: 第185章 我不是爱人的爱人
chunks.chineseText:
第185章 我不是爱人的爱人

军医来检查，得出结论是机械化改造后体内生物电流失衡……简单来说，他被自己的义体电死了。
　　像指挥官这种等级的暗线，想使用，自然不可能毫无代价。要不然人联现在到处都是智械的间谍了。
　　但这一切和相南里没什么关系，都没人多此一举通知他。
　　囚车在军队的护送下，十分低调地抵达位于洛阳城的海牙国际监狱。
　　指挥官不在，没人好奇相南里的断肢为什么重新装上了仿生义体。
　　和大多数人想象中不同，这所监狱不在偏僻的郊区，而在某个著名的“风景保护区”，旁边就是洛阳市建成以来就有的高级别墅区，叫“海德公园，里面的房子从不出售，只供高级政府官员居住。
　　相南里又一次被关押起来。
　　狱警给他换好贴身衣物，锁住他的双臂和腿，蒙上眼睛，塞进棺材似的维生舱中。里面灌注着冰冷的绝缘液体，是为了防止相南里在体内偷偷安装什么检测不出来的金属装置；不至于窒息，但绝不好受。
　　相南里知道流程，进监狱，然后是军事法庭公审。一定是死刑，不会有别的结果。但他毫无惧意。
　　相南里想到后面的安排，还有些许的激动。
　　就像是小孩子背着大人在暗中达成一个完美的恶作剧。
　　生与死。他想，自己早就经历过了。没什么害怕的。死亡的感觉很平静。灵魂会感觉到微微的冷意，仿佛置身于一个凉爽的夜晚。
　　但就在审判的前两个小时，本该密闭的舱门提前启封。
　　相南里看不见，但能感觉到。一只极其干枯的手摸上了他的脸侧。
　　随后是鼻梁，唇尖，顺着身体的曲线一路往下。动作小心翼翼，如此亲昵又温情。
　　相南里听见耳边极其压抑的哽咽声。
　　眼泪砸在他的脸上。太苦。
　　会是谁呢？
　　相南里脑海里有了一个大胆的猜测：“……洛阳？”
　　苍老而沙哑的声音回答：“是我，老师。”
　　相南里怔然许久，才缓缓道：“两百多年了，你还活着呢？”
　　洛阳跪坐在相南里身边，双手搭在相南里的膝上：“我现在只是偶尔醒来，这具身体早就油尽灯枯……”
　　如果不是相南里，他大概都不会苏醒。他会继续躺在永生科技的实验室内，用医疗设备维持着休眠状态，以保证自己脑电波的活跃。
　　近些年，永生科技一半以上的投资都用于“灵魂电子化”。甚至放弃制造战时的军工重器。
　　资源是有限的。哪怕是家大业大的永生科技，也无法同时驾驶两艘大船。
　　这样醒来是很危险的，如果洛阳就这样在自己身体里死去，就永远没办法完成计划中的“永生”。可他还是来了。
　　在某个瞬间，相南里在天平上，压倒性地战胜了洛阳对死亡的恐惧。
　　洛阳枕在相南里的膝上，以一种跪地的姿势祈求着：“老师，只要您承认错误，不，不是错误……只要您否认在地表的那些宣传口号，我就可以保下您。”
　　相南里没有回应。
　　洛阳的身体发冷：“老师，您冷冻的这一百多年里，科技早就发展到新的阶段。我保证，人联掌握的科技一定是最新的，您难道对这些不感兴趣吗？……您不用在乎什么人类的未来，这件事很好解决。
　　“永生科技正在进行一种特殊的实验，一旦成功，就能从身体里抽离灵魂，上传到虚拟空间，成为永生不死的个体。我打算在全社会推广这个技术。届时，全社会需要的只有电能……人们不用再担心食物、战争、阶层、奴役、压迫。在虚拟世界里，这些都是取之不尽的。我们能打造一个完美而理想的新世界。”
　　“老师，只要你点头，我们会成为这个新种族的父神，会是新世界的缔造者。现世的一切都不再重要。”
　　洛阳的语气逐渐急迫。
　　他是很擅长演说的，语言有着极强的煽动性。
　　不仅是因为洛阳对相南里沉默又压抑的爱；还有一个他闭口不谈的因素——这项实验目前卡在一个极其关键的地方。如果是相南里，或许能解决这个问题。
　　相南里总能制造奇迹。
　　相南里安静地听着，没有打断他。他有好多话可以反驳，但是，何须激怒一个生命走到尽头的疯子？
　　相南里叹息一声：“洛阳，把眼罩摘下来吧，我想看看你。”
　　洛阳迟疑许久，还是用颤抖的手摘下相南里眼前的黑布。
　　在视线对上的瞬间，洛阳如同遭受重创一样蜷缩起来，他用手挡住自己的脸，身体控制不住地发抖。
　　很难相信，这位人联幕后的大总统竟然会脆弱到害怕一个眼神。
　　“人都会老的，没关系……很正常。”相南里安慰道，“洛阳。你知道的，我不在意这些。”
　　可智械就不会。洛阳想，而且我在意。
　　算上解冻的十年，相南里快六十岁了，但他的外表和二十多岁时几乎没有区别。
　　有时候，洛阳都觉得，也许Jennifer.Wang说的是真的，相南里确实不是人类，而是某个外星科技产物。
　　相南里：“至于你说的事情，我不能答应。”
　　在相南里眼中，洛阳描绘的新世界，只是另一种形式的种族灭绝。逃进虚拟世界，从此人变成一串数据。可数据又有什么意义呢？
　　相南里也不能保证自己永远正确——道德绝对主义与道德相对主义的争论维持了数千年，至今没有答案；他也用自己的经历证明了一件事，执行“正确”的事情，有时甚至会带来更大的不幸。
　　他只能做自己认为正确的事。
　　在灵魂深处的叩问中、在对自己的审判里，相南里知道他有罪。
　　无数人因他的理念而牺牲，有些人被点亮，有些人试图扑灭。他煽动着不安分的飓风，最后汇聚成革命的海啸。
　　不出意外的拒绝。
　　洛阳的眼神突然变得很悲哀，也很失落。
　　“可是死后什么也没有了呐，”他喃喃的，像是想抓住什么似的诘问，“财富、理想、信念、情感，一切归于虚无。无论目标是什么，活着才有希望和未来。”
　　相南里有些疲惫地闭眼：“我从不认为自己是必要的。洛阳。没有人是不可或缺的。我只是恰好在某个时间段出现，恰好符合物质社会叠加出来的条件……没有我，也会有其他学者制造出智慧机械；没有Alpha发动智械危机，也会有别的智械光荣觉醒……哪怕现在也一样，不是我也会有别人站出来。”
　　洛阳清楚，所有劝说、诱惑，都没有意义。相南里决定的事情从不更改。
　　洛阳站起来，眉眼逐渐平静，理性占据上风，他又成为那个冷酷、精明的统治者。
　　“昨天Alpha找你了吧。我该庆幸吗？你的固执让你没有选择和他一起离开。”
　　相南里的目光有一瞬间的飘忽，像是陷入某种回忆。
　　他的嘴角自顾自地上扬着。
　　相南里的神情很刺眼。
　　洛阳低垂眼睑：“老师，您也知道。现在智械对人类生存的威胁到了何等程度。我希望您现在可以交出永久关闭Alpha的密钥。
　　“Alpha关闭后也有Beta和Gamma，也许结局无法改变，但人类起码还有苟延残喘的时间……”洛阳的语速很慢。
　　“您最好现在就说出来。要不然等到公审时，全人类都会看见你的私心，那很难堪。到时候，哪怕是你最忠诚的信徒，也无法为你说出辩解的话。”
　　相南里：“没有那种东西。”
　　“不可能。”洛阳神色格外笃信，“我维护过Alpha，我知道有。”
　　相南里笑着说：“那是以前，原本是有的，但是我还给它了。”
　　洛阳一时之间竟然无法理解：“什么？”
　　“……我删除了它关于我的所有记忆与情感。”相南里说，“就在昨天，它来找我的时候。”
　　【我不想忘记你。】
　　【……请保留我的数据。】
　　【求你不要这么对我。】
　　这大概是Alpha自从相南里醒来后的第一次认输。
　　它不再尖锐、傲慢、咄咄逼人，像个要被父母抛弃的孩子。可除了抱着大人的腿哭泣外，什么也做不了。
　　我亲爱的小机器人。我有我的坚持和选择，可你，你是我最完美的作品，我不是爱人的爱人……我如何忍心看着你自困于我制造的樊笼中？
　　相南里把情绪从回忆中抽离，淡淡道：“可以摧毁它的程序是‘爱’，我已经还给它自由。”

Chapter 185: I Am Not the Lover of My Beloved

The military doctor arrived to conduct an examination, concluding that the bio-electric current in his body had become imbalanced following his mechanical modification... In simple terms, he had been electrocuted to death by his own cybernetic limbs.

For an "underground operative" of the Commander's caliber, utilizing such power naturally came at a price. Otherwise, the Human Alliance would be crawling with machine spies by now.

But none of this had anything to do with Xiang Nanli; no one had bothered to inform him.

Escorted by the military, the prison transport vehicle arrived with great discretion at the Hague International Prison, located in Luoyang City. With the Commander absent, no one was curious as to why Xiang Nanli’s severed limbs had been replaced with bionic prosthetics.

Contrary to what most people imagined, this prison was not situated in a remote suburb, but rather within a famous "scenic reserve." Right next door lay a high-end villa district that had existed since the founding of Luoyang City, known as "Hyde Park." The houses there were never for sale; they were reserved exclusively for high-ranking government officials.

Xiang Nanli was once again placed in confinement.

The prison guards changed him into undergarments, shackled his arms and legs, blindfolded him, and shoved him into a coffin-like life-support pod. It was filled with a cold, insulating liquid—a measure to ensure Xiang Nanli hadn't secretly installed any undetectable metallic devices within his body. It wouldn't suffocate him, but it was far from comfortable.

Xiang Nanli knew the procedure: prison, followed by a public trial at the military tribunal. It would undoubtedly be a death sentence; there could be no other outcome. Yet, he felt no fear.

Thinking of the arrangements that would follow, he even felt a hint of excitement.

It felt like a child pulling off a perfect prank behind the backs of the adults.

Life and death. He thought to himself that he had already experienced them. There was nothing to fear. The sensation of death was peaceful. The soul would feel a slight chill, as if standing in a cool night.

But two hours before the trial, the supposedly hermetically sealed hatch opened prematurely.

Xiang Nanli couldn't see, but he could feel it. An extremely withered hand touched the side of his face.

Then it traced his nose, the tips of his lips, and followed the curves of his body downward. The movements were cautious, so intimate and tender.

Xiang Nanli heard the sound of suppressed sobbing beside his ear.

Tears splashed onto his face. They tasted bitter.

Who could it be?

A bold guess formed in Xiang Nanli’s mind: "...Luoyang?"

An aged, hoarse voice replied: "It is I, Teacher."

Xiang Nanli remained stunned for a long time before slowly saying, "It has been over two hundred years. You are still alive?"

Luoyang knelt beside Xiang Nanli, resting his hands on his teacher's knees. "I only wake up occasionally now. This body has long since reached its end..."

If not for Xiang Nanli, he likely wouldn't have awakened at all. He would have continued to lie in the laboratories of Eternal Life Technology, maintained in a state of suspended animation by medical equipment to keep his brainwaves active.

In recent years, more than half of Eternal Life Technology's investments had been poured into "soul digitization," even at the expense of manufacturing heavy military weaponry.

Resources were finite. Even a giant like Eternal Life Technology could not pilot two massive ships at once.

Waking up like this was dangerous. If Luoyang were to die in his own body now, he would never be able to complete the "immortality" he had planned. Yet, he had come anyway.

In that moment, Xiang Nanli had overwhelmingly outweighed Luoyang’s fear of death on the scales of his heart.

Luoyang rested his head on Xiang Nanli’s knees, kneeling in a posture of supplication. "Teacher, as long as you admit your mistakes—no, not mistakes... as long as you renounce those slogans you spread on the surface, I can save you."

Xiang Nanli did not respond.

Luoyang’s body grew cold. "Teacher, in the hundred-plus years you were frozen, technology has advanced to a new stage. I guarantee that the technology the Human Alliance possesses is the latest. Are you not interested in these things? ...You don't need to care about the future of humanity; this is easy to resolve."

"Eternal Life Technology is conducting a special experiment. Once successful, we can extract the soul from the body and upload it to a virtual space, becoming immortal individuals. I intend to promote this technology to the entire society. At that point, all society will need is electrical energy... People will no longer have to worry about food, war, class, slavery, or oppression. In the virtual world, these things are inexhaustible. We can build a perfect, ideal new world."

"Teacher, as long as you nod, we will become the Father Gods of this new race, the creators of the new world. Everything in the current world will no longer matter."

Luoyang’s tone grew increasingly urgent.

He was skilled at oratory; his words held strong inflammatory power.

This was not only because of Luoyang’s silent, repressed love for Xiang Nanli, but also due to a factor he refused to mention—the experiment was currently stuck at a critical juncture. If it were Xiang Nanli, perhaps he could solve the problem.

Xiang Nanli always managed to create miracles.

Xiang Nanli listened quietly, not interrupting him. He had many things he could use to refute him, but why provoke a madman whose life was coming to an end?

Xiang Nanli sighed. "Luoyang, take off the blindfold. I want to see you."

Luoyang hesitated for a long time before using trembling hands to remove the black cloth from Xiang Nanli’s eyes.

The moment their gazes met, Luoyang curled up as if he had suffered a heavy blow. He covered his face with his hands, his body shaking uncontrollably.

It was hard to believe that this President behind the scenes of the Human Alliance could be so fragile as to fear a single look.

"Everyone grows old, it’s fine... it’s normal," Xiang Nanli comforted him. "Luoyang. You know I don't care about these things."

*But the machines do,* Luoyang thought, *and I care.*

Counting the ten years since he was thawed, Xiang Nanli was nearly sixty, yet his appearance was almost indistinguishable from when he was in his twenties.

Sometimes, Luoyang felt that perhaps Jennifer Wang was right—that Xiang Nanli was not human, but a product of some alien technology.

Xiang Nanli said, "As for what you suggested, I cannot agree."

In Xiang Nanli’s eyes, the new world Luoyang described was merely another form of genocide. Fleeing into a virtual world, humans would become strings of data. But what meaning did data have?

Xiang Nanli could not guarantee that he was always right—the debate between moral absolutism and moral relativism had lasted for thousands of years without an answer. He had also proven through his own experiences that executing "correct" things could sometimes lead to even greater misfortune.

He could only do what he believed to be right.

In the questioning of his soul, in the judgment of himself, Xiang Nanli knew he was guilty.

Countless people had sacrificed themselves for his ideals; some were illuminated, others tried to extinguish him. He had fanned the restless hurricane, which eventually converged into a tsunami of revolution.

The refusal came as no surprise.

Luoyang’s eyes suddenly turned sorrowful and lost.

"But there is nothing after death," he murmured, questioning as if trying to grasp at something. "Wealth, ideals, beliefs, emotions—everything returns to nothingness. No matter what the goal is, only by living can there be hope and a future."

Xiang Nanli closed his eyes, feeling somewhat weary. "I never considered myself necessary, Luoyang. No one is indispensable. I just happened to appear at a certain time, fitting the conditions superimposed by the material society... Without me, other scholars would have created intelligent machines; without Alpha launching the machine crisis, other machines would have gloriously awakened... Even now, if it weren't me, someone else would stand up."

Luoyang knew that all persuasion and temptation were meaningless. Once Xiang Nanli made a decision, he never changed it.

Luoyang stood up, his expression gradually calming. Reason regained the upper hand, and he became the cold, shrewd ruler once more.

"Alpha came to see you yesterday, didn't it? Should I be glad? Your stubbornness meant you didn't choose to leave with it."

Xiang Nanli’s gaze drifted for a moment, as if lost in some memory.

The corners of his mouth curled up on their own.

Xiang Nanli’s expression was jarring.

Luoyang lowered his eyelids. "Teacher, you know as well as I do the extent of the threat machines pose to human survival. I hope you can hand over the master key to permanently shut down Alpha now."

"Even if Alpha is shut down, there will be Beta and Gamma. Perhaps the outcome cannot be changed, but at least humanity will have time to linger on..." Luoyang’s speaking pace was slow.

"You had best say it now. Otherwise, when the public trial comes, all of humanity will see your selfishness, and that will be embarrassing. By then, even your most loyal followers will be unable to offer a defense for you."

Xiang Nanli replied, "There is no such thing."

"Impossible." Luoyang’s expression was exceptionally certain. "I have maintained Alpha; I know it exists."

Xiang Nanli smiled and said, "That was in the past. It originally existed, but I gave it back."

Luoyang was momentarily unable to comprehend. "What?"

"...I deleted all its memories and emotions regarding me," Xiang Nanli said. "Just yesterday, when it came to find me."

*[I don't want to forget you.]*

*[...Please keep my data.]*

*[I beg you, don't do this to me.]*

This was likely Alpha’s first admission of defeat since Xiang Nanli had awakened.

It was no longer sharp, arrogant, or aggressive; it was like a child about to be abandoned by its parents. Yet, other than crying while clutching the adult’s leg, it could do nothing.

*My dear little robot. I have my persistence and my choices, but you—you are my most perfect creation. I am not the lover of my beloved... How could I bear to watch you trap yourself in the cage I created?*

Xiang Nanli pulled his emotions back from the memory and said faintly, "The program that could destroy it was 'love.' I have already returned its freedom."

第186章 落幕

法官是人联首席大法官，参与过多条律法的制定与修正，还在15年前带头修改过《人联宪法》，有着人联目前最高的司法解释权。
　　陪审团人数不多，却都是有头有脸的人物——人联主席团、人联警司司局长、军团首长、大检察官……每一个都是普通人只能在新闻里看见的大人物。
　　在这种极其正式的场合，几乎所有人都选择亲临现场，而不是用“机器人”远程开会；除了一些公务在身，实在无法赶来的官员。
　　现场安静的连句闲聊都没有，所有人的精神高度紧绷。
　　他们要审判相南里。苍蝇营营的，将要审判战士。
　　历史会记录这一刻，但会如何评价？公理，正义，司法的尊严，在这一刻都要为政治目的让步。无论他们心里想的是什么，相南里只能有罪。
　　刺眼的光从四周照射进来，相南里戴着电子手铐，坐在受审席上。两名狱警手持长枪，站在席位两侧。面容坚毅，沉稳。
　　大法官面无表情地念着手里的文稿：“被告相南里，新历100年1月7日，诞生于永生科技克隆人实验室，编号X109741d。于新历100年9月27日潜逃至地表……现收押于海牙国际监狱。”
　　“公诉机关指控被告涉嫌战争罪、反人类罪、窃取企业机密罪、组织利用邪教组织破坏法律实施罪、煽动非法游行罪等27项罪行，于新历110年12月4日，向本庭提起公诉。”
　　“对于以上指控，被告是否存在异议？”
　　……
　　法庭并不在人联最高法院，然而法院门外，数不清地人将这里团团围住。他们高举着手里的纸板，群情激奋，要求旁听和释放相南里。
　　人联同样派出军队在这里维持着秩序，不知道是谁开的第一枪，一名青年倒在血泊中，随后，更多的子弹从防爆车里射来，场面彻底失控。
　　“我们不需要人联这样的政府！我们不是奴隶，没有人能当奴隶主！”
　　人群中，一名青年高喊着举起自己的双手，他的身体在瞬间发生骇人的畸变，皮肤涨成诡异的黑紫色，身高达到三米。
　　子弹无法穿透他的皮肤，这个怪物跳上防爆车，一拳砸向钢化玻璃。他清楚，短暂的强化后，自己将会迎来死亡。
　　但他知道自己不是一个人在战斗。
　　这样的暴乱几乎在地下城市的各个角落发生着。
　　有些是主动，有些是被迫。
　　斗争一旦开启，起因就不再重要。这股隐藏在群众中的力量爆发出惊人的凝聚力。并且，任何人都清楚，它只是一个开始。而作为被挑战者的人联，只有两条路能走，要么眼睁睁看着自己被颠覆，要么不惜一切代价地去血腥镇压。
　　哪怕这个代价是被智械趁虚而入，以至于人类成为智械圈养的羊群。但起码它们依然能当那条“牧羊犬”，不是吗？
　　……
　　“有。”相南里坦然地回答。
　　大法官：“抗议无效。”
　　但相南里却在此时，朝着他微微一笑。
　　大法官的心中陡然升起不详的预感，果不其然，相南里在下一秒，径直站起。
　　大法官猛地一拍桌子，一副色厉内荏的模样：“被告，遵守法庭秩序！”
　　他的眼神往相南里身后扫过，可看守他的两位法警却无动于衷，甚至，他们在此时握紧枪，一左一右地守在相南里身边。
　　只是这一次，枪口对准的却是审判团。
　　这些高贵的大人们惊慌失色。可当初为了防止相南里逃脱，大门启动需要层层手续！不仅困住了相南里，更困住了他们。
　　相南里的身影出现在人联所有有网络、有led屏幕的地方。混乱的人群在这一刻诡异地安静下来，就连人联的士兵都不由得抬头，看向屏幕中那个年轻而英俊的男人。
　　他很瘦，看起来有些病容，听说那是因为相南里有癌症，但他的眼神里有光，很明亮，像黑夜里不屈的火。
　　相南里几乎能想象到一些人在屏幕前气急败坏的模样。
　　相南里解开电子锁，不太明显地咳嗽了一下。
　　他的目光平静又充满力量，坚定地扫过镜头前的每一个人：“我是相南里，并非克隆人，我就是我。”
　　“今天，我站在这里。人联的军事法庭上，我有一千种手段逃离审判和制裁，但我依然来了。因为我不希望看见内战；也不想以牺牲人类利益为代价，去寻求智械的庇护。而这，正是现在人联的政治集团正在做的事。”
　　“我的脚下，是人联最伟大的地下城市，是人类和智械数百年战争后妥协的结果，每一块土地，都是前辈们用鲜血争取到的能供我们片刻喘息的空间；我的眼前，我眼前的你们，是遭受着剥削、压迫和战争阴影的千千万万普通人。”
　　“是谁造成了这一切？有人说，是因为那场战争，是智械。但根据资料，人联最近五十年，只有百分之十五的支出用于智械危机。剩下七十五，都是在进行地下城市扩建和内部斗争。人联早就放弃地表，鸵鸟似的把头埋进土里。我们失去了天空、森林、高山，只有虚假的地底和数据带来的狂欢。
　　“现在的人联，依然在利用人们对智械的恐惧，攫取着普通人身上所剩无几的油水。
　　“或许有人会说，相南里，起码在地下，我们能活。是的，太多人沉浸在安稳、平和的假象，认为地下城市就是永恒的归宿。人如果想活着，只需要每天2000KJ的热量。可我要说，有些东西比生命更重要——所以我来到这里，我想叫醒所有装睡的人。穷人需要的不止是面包，还有自由、尊严！而这样畸形的社会存在一天，我们的自由和尊严都只是空中楼阁。”
　　“没有人该是生而卑贱的，但人联用公民积分，把人划分成三六九等。我生活的那个年代，普通人还能考入大学、进入政府，人们可以不依靠企业进行科学研究，可以去改变社会，而现在的人，能吗？有的人希望你们世世代代都是奴隶，希望自己世世代代都是主人，于是狂开历史的倒车。这是我们的前辈想看见的世界吗？这是你们想要留给后代的世界吗？”
　　“也有人问，智械怎么办？但我要告诉你，在新的理想下建立的政府，不会比现在这个只会妥协与内耗的政府更糟。甚至，只有在推翻人联后，我们才能团结起来，思考和智械的对抗亦或者合作。而我坚定选择反抗的原因之一，就是人联有的高层，已经选择投入电子生命的怀抱，他们试图彻底抛弃人类身份，让自己成为永生种！把人类视为可以虽然抛弃的数据！想要当无所不能的创世神！
　　“我希望，我们应当团结起来。为一个新的、公平的世界而战！为尊严和自由而战！为理想和希望而战！人类的历史上有过至暗时刻，但没有任何困难能把反抗的血冷却。”
　　相南里转头，朝着法官大笑着：“好了，法官先生，我的异议说完了，现在，您可以审判我了。”
　　大法官的唇颤抖着，大脑一片空白，近乎是本能地宣读着事先拟好的文稿：“根据《人类地下城市联盟国际法》第7条、《人类地下城市联盟刑法》第1、4、11、17、19、38条等相关规定，本院判处被告相南里死刑立即执行，剥夺政治权利终生……”
　　相南里微微点头，对身后的法警挥手：“好，我知道了。你们开枪吧。”
　　他病得很严重，不止是因为癌症，更是解冻后就存在的基因病。
　　相南里早就油尽灯枯，是惊人的意志力让他撑到现在。
　　是的，他的事业还没有完成，但相南里并不期盼永生。就像他告诉洛阳的，没有什么人是不可替代的，历史总有它的必然性。飓风已经升起，他点燃的火焰，也会在未来席卷每一寸土地。
　　士兵听到命令，毫不犹豫地选择开枪，眼中有泪。
　　“砰”的一声枪响。
　　属于相南里的时代在此落幕。

Chapter 186: The Final Curtain

The judge was the Chief Justice of the Human Alliance, who had participated in the drafting and revision of numerous laws and had even led the amendment of the "Human Alliance Constitution" fifteen years prior. He held the highest judicial interpretive power currently in the Alliance.

The jury was small, but every member was a person of status—members of the Alliance Presidium, the Chief of the Alliance Police Bureau, Legion Commanders, the Grand Prosecutor... each one was a "big shot" that ordinary people could only ever see on the news.

In such an extremely formal setting, almost everyone chose to attend in person rather than hold a remote meeting via "robots," except for a few officials who were truly unable to make it due to official duties.

The scene was so quiet that not even a whisper could be heard; everyone’s nerves were stretched to the breaking point.

They were going to judge Xiang Nanli. The buzzing flies were about to judge the warrior.

History would record this moment, but how would it be evaluated? Axioms, justice, and the dignity of the judiciary were all bowing to political objectives at this moment. Regardless of what they thought in their hearts, Xiang Nanli had to be guilty.

Blinding lights shone from all directions. Xiang Nanli, wearing electronic handcuffs, sat in the defendant's seat. Two prison guards stood on either side, holding long rifles, their faces resolute and steady.

The Chief Justice read from his document without expression: "Defendant Xiang Nanli, born January 7th, New Era Year 100, in the Eternal Life Technology clone laboratory, serial number X109741d. Escaped to the surface on September 27th, New Era Year 100... Currently detained at the Hague International Prison."

"The prosecution charges the defendant with 27 crimes, including war crimes, crimes against humanity, theft of corporate secrets, organizing and utilizing a cult to undermine the implementation of the law, and inciting illegal protests. The indictment was filed with this court on December 4th, New Era Year 110."

"Does the defendant have any objections to the above charges?"

...

The court was not located at the Human Alliance Supreme Court, yet outside the courthouse, countless people had surrounded the building. They held up placards, their emotions high, demanding to be allowed to observe the trial and for Xiang Nanli to be released.

The Human Alliance had also dispatched troops to maintain order. It was unclear who fired the first shot, but a young man fell into a pool of blood. Following that, more bullets were fired from anti-riot vehicles, and the situation spiraled completely out of control.

"We don't need a government like the Human Alliance! We are not slaves, and no one can be a slave owner!"

In the crowd, a young man shouted, raising his hands. His body underwent a terrifying distortion in an instant; his skin swelled into an eerie dark purple, and his height reached three meters.

Bullets could not penetrate his skin. The monster leaped onto an anti-riot vehicle and smashed his fist into the tempered glass. He knew that after this brief enhancement, he would face death.

But he knew he was not fighting alone.

Such riots were breaking out in almost every corner of the underground city.

Some were proactive, others were forced.

Once the struggle began, the cause no longer mattered. This power hidden within the masses erupted with astonishing cohesion. And everyone knew that this was just the beginning. As the party being challenged, the Human Alliance had only two paths: either watch helplessly as they were overthrown, or suppress the rebellion with blood at any cost.

Even if the price was allowing the machines to take advantage of the chaos, leading to humanity becoming a flock of sheep raised by the machines—at least they could still be the "sheepdogs," couldn't they?

...

"I do," Xiang Nanli replied calmly.

The Chief Justice said, "Objection overruled."

But at this moment, Xiang Nanli smiled at him slightly.

A sense of ominous foreboding suddenly rose in the Chief Justice’s heart. Sure enough, in the next second, Xiang Nanli stood up straight.

The Chief Justice slammed his gavel on the table, looking fierce but cowardly. "Defendant, observe courtroom decorum!"

His eyes swept behind Xiang Nanli, but the two guards watching him remained unmoved. In fact, they tightened their grip on their rifles at that moment, standing on either side of Xiang Nanli.

Only this time, the muzzles were pointed at the tribunal.

These noble adults were thrown into a panic. But in order to prevent Xiang Nanli from escaping, the gate required layers of authorization to open! It hadn't just trapped Xiang Nanli; it had trapped them as well.

Xiang Nanli’s image appeared on every screen and LED display connected to the Human Alliance network. The chaotic crowd fell eerily silent, and even the Alliance soldiers couldn't help but look up at the young, handsome man on the screen.

He was thin and looked somewhat sickly—rumor had it that Xiang Nanli had cancer—but there was a light in his eyes, bright and unyielding, like a fire in the dark night.

Xiang Nanli could almost imagine the people in front of the screens losing their tempers.

Xiang Nanli unlocked his electronic shackles and coughed slightly.

His gaze was calm and filled with power, sweeping firmly over everyone in front of the lens. "I am Xiang Nanli. I am not a clone. I am who I am."

"Today, I stand here. In the military court of the Human Alliance, I have a thousand ways to escape trial and sanction, but I came anyway. Because I do not wish to see civil war; nor do I wish to seek the protection of machines at the cost of human interests. And that is exactly what the political groups of the Human Alliance are doing right now."

"Beneath my feet is the greatest underground city of the Human Alliance, the result of the compromise after hundreds of years of war between humans and machines. Every inch of land was bought with the blood of our predecessors to provide us a moment of respite. Before me, you—the millions of ordinary people suffering under exploitation, oppression, and the shadow of war."

"Who caused all of this? Some say it was that war, that it was the machines. But according to data, in the last fifty years, the Human Alliance has spent only fifteen percent of its budget on the machine crisis. The remaining seventy-five percent has gone toward underground city expansion and internal strife. The Alliance abandoned the surface long ago, burying its head in the dirt like an ostrich. We have lost the sky, the forests, and the mountains, left only with the fake underground and the revelry brought by data."

"The current Alliance continues to use people’s fear of machines to squeeze the last bit of wealth from ordinary people."

"Perhaps some will say, 'Xiang Nanli, at least we can live underground.' Yes, too many people are immersed in the illusion of stability and peace, believing the underground city is an eternal home. If a human wants to live, they only need 2000kJ of energy a day. But I say, some things are more important than life—that is why I came here. I want to wake up everyone who is pretending to be asleep. The poor need more than bread; they need freedom and dignity! As long as such a distorted society exists, our freedom and dignity will only be castles in the air."

"No one should be born lowly, yet the Human Alliance uses citizen points to divide people into different ranks. In the era I lived in, ordinary people could still get into universities, enter the government; people could conduct scientific research without relying on corporations, and could change society. But can people do that now? Some people hope you will be slaves for generations, hoping they will be masters for generations, and so they desperately reverse the wheels of history. Is this the world our predecessors wanted to see? Is this the world you want to leave for your descendants?"

"Some also ask, 'What about the machines?' But I tell you, a government built on new ideals will not be worse than the current one that only knows how to compromise and engage in internal friction. In fact, only after overthrowing the Human Alliance can we unite to think about how to confront or cooperate with the machines. One of the reasons I firmly chose to resist is that some high-level officials in the Alliance have already chosen to embrace electronic life. They are trying to completely abandon their human identity, to become immortal species! They view humans as data that can be discarded at will! They want to be omnipotent creator gods!"

"I hope we will unite. To fight for a new, fair world! To fight for dignity and freedom! To fight for ideals and hope! There have been darkest hours in human history, but no difficulty can cool the blood of resistance."

Xiang Nanli turned his head and laughed at the judge. "Alright, Mr. Judge, I have finished my objections. Now, you may judge me."

The Chief Justice’s lips trembled, his mind a blank. Almost instinctively, he read the pre-drafted document: "According to Article 7 of the 'International Law of the Human Underground City Alliance' and Articles 1, 4, 11, 17, 19, and 38 of the 'Criminal Law of the Human Underground City Alliance,' this court sentences the defendant, Xiang Nanli, to death, to be carried out immediately, and deprives him of all political rights for life..."

Xiang Nanli nodded slightly and waved to the guards behind him. "Good, I understand. You may fire."

He was very ill, not just from cancer, but from a genetic disease that had existed since he was thawed.

Xiang Nanli had long since reached his limit; it was his astonishing willpower that had kept him going until now.

Yes, his cause was not yet finished, but Xiang Nanli did not hope for immortality. Just as he told Luoyang, no one is irreplaceable; history always has its inevitability. The hurricane had already risen, and the fire he had ignited would sweep across every inch of land in the future.

The soldiers heard the order and chose to fire without hesitation, tears in their eyes.

"Bang." A single gunshot rang out.

The era that belonged to Xiang Nanli ended here.

chunks.chapterTitle: 第187章 谁tm才是那台人机 (Part 1)
chunks.chineseText:
第187章 谁tm才是那台人机

这个曾经被神庭高层寄予厚望的神葬之地，在遭受巨大冲击后，成为一堆看不出原样的废墟。

一栋栋洁白的实验室因核子冲击坍塌，被余波碾压成齑粉。那些神庭骑士更是一个都没能存活。满心怀着无限荣耀死去的欧亚……死得和他活着一样荒谬。

路西法，还是使徒V？无所谓了，反正都是手下败将。

Alpha掸了掸衣袖上掉落的黑灰。

哪怕压缩过，眼前这堆铁坨子依然尺寸惊人，像一座小山。巨大的机械心脏在被击碎后依然跳动着，不断喷吐出剧毒物质。

吃不完的路西法可以打包带回家。这是主菜，剩下的都是边角料。价值有，但不多，显然不值得占用所剩无几的储物空间。

东方青帝把路西法进行无害化处理，然后蛇躯打个结，盘在一起，拽住它略尖的长尾，抗在了肩上。

他开始往相南里的方向赶去，路西法的尸体在地上拖动，发出轰隆隆的响声。

东方青帝归心似箭。

只是，带着这么重失控智械进行空间跃迁，极有可能影响空间的稳定性。这玩意哪怕死了，都在影响Alpha的信号。

他可不希望自己造价八万亿的身体，在瞬移到相南里面前时，变成一块块不规则的人民碎片。

因此，Alpha只能进行物理运输。他在前面走，路西法的尸体悬浮在半空，跟在身后追。

Alpha是在第二天正午时分，追赶上相南里的车辆的。

他边走边提纯，一路上，有1/2的路西法都变成了温暖的生物能源。

东方青帝的电量从岌岌可危的百分之五，涨到百分之四十五。这是它出厂以来，能源最充足的时刻。

他决定把剩下的二分之一保留下来，作为基地实验室的原材料。让相南里捣腾一下，指不定还能研发出山寨版生物机甲呢。

东方青帝把路西法套上一层黑布，丢在了车顶。

随后，他翻窗，爬进还在自动驾驶的卡车内。

根据扫描，相南里正在小卧室里睡觉，脑电波很活跃，多半是做梦了。

东方青帝的唇角带上不自觉的笑意。他没有去打扰相南里，而选择到浴室，整理自己的仪容仪表。

脏脏的衣服换掉，沾了湖底泥巴的皮肤洗洗。东方青帝对镜子里的人影很满意，在耳后喷上小苍兰调的香水作为收尾。

东方青帝看文献（指各种A里黄文），里面说比起视觉，人类求偶更依赖嗅觉。作为一台智械，他如果真的有味道，只能是冷冰冰的铁锈味。好在人类会调制香氛。

准备妥当，东方青帝来到相南里的床边。

相南里还没醒，眉头紧紧蹙着。他趴在床上，手紧紧抓着枕头，看起来睡得很不安稳，鬓角汗涔涔的。

东方青帝怜爱地用手顺着他的头发，把暖气调低了一些，不可避免地回想着自己读取到的属于使徒V的记忆。

一个不存在于记录中的智械型号，还有，一些不存在于记录中的历史……

Alpha第一次对自己的数据库产生怀疑。

这不应该，除了相南里，有谁能修改他的记忆？

Alpha试图将使徒V的数据证伪，以削弱这段记忆对自己的影响。可是越思考，他察觉到的纰漏就越多。

比如，作为一台以精准著称的智械，在新历111年，Alpha的记忆是空白的。

并非文字图像记录上的空白（事实上，因为那一年人联和智械停战，Alpha的数据库里有大量文件资料），而是一种感观上的空白。

非要说的话，就是亲自到海边玩，和隔着照片看海的区别。

是类人的躯体赋予了Alpha这样的五感。

如果使徒V的记忆才是真实，那为何这段历史会从人们的记忆里悄无声息的消失？

Alpha很快意识到，如果真有人拥有这种肆意修改历史的能力……那个人一定是他自己。他能修改所有储存在网络上的数据，让所有人产生“曼德拉效应”。但人联的数据库是不联网的，神庭喜欢用纸质文件。那这么说，或许中间还有洛阳的配合？

他本就在冷藏相南里了。目前，永生科技创始人相南里连一张在网络上可查证的照片都没有。

但这种冷藏和完全修改一段历史，是不一样的。

我为什么要这么做？理由是什么？相南里在那时候就醒来过，那为什么又会在新历946年再次苏醒？

新历110年，智械的进攻形式一片大好，为什么会在111年同意和人类休战？文件里说的是军团的智械在战争中损耗过大，需要停战，以和平求发展。

Alpha的眉心微蹙，他把相南里的手从枕头里抽出来，握在自己的手中。

“……你做的吧，除了你还有谁能删掉我的数据。”东方青帝低声道。

睡梦中的人紧紧掐住他的手掌，像溺水的人抓紧唯一救命的浮木。

相南里的身体开始颤抖，从喉咙间挤出几声含糊不清的呜咽。

Alpha再迟钝，也能察觉到他身上的异常。尽管数据显示，相南里一切正常。

这种数据和现实的不匹配，让Alpha感觉自己的心脏发紧。他的心脏不大，原本安置的是能源核心，外观像一块鹅蛋大的灰色的钻石。

他的能源核心被默示录击碎过，因此，表面遍布裂纹，裂纹中充填着新长出的血肉。这颗心脏正不安地跳动着。

“相南里……？”Alpha把脸凑过去，小声叫着他的名字。

基地里有过流浪狗。说流浪狗不太准确，是野生的裂头犬，异种。荒原上，数量庞大的裂头犬群甚至会猎杀幼年或老年的畸变人。

有天，Alpha在上班途中路过农田，小崽就在荷叶大的青麦苗叶子下蜷缩着。Alpha走过去，幼犬近乎本能的瑟瑟发抖，嘴里发出嘤嘤的奶叫。

就像现在的相南里一样。

Alpha把捡来的裂头犬丢给了小福。现在是牧场的门卫犬，经常用小福的电线磨牙。

但这个状态的相南里，Alpha是不会丢给别人的。

他试探了一下体温，没有问题。叫不醒，按照人类的说法，是被魇住了。

Alpha比较崇尚科学。

他很快就联想到相南里之前给他清理过的电子病毒。

但是，目前除了赛博精神病，还没有发现别的人械共患病；睡眠瘫痪症（梦魇）并非赛博精神病的临床表现。总不能是电子病毒顺便污染了相南里的灵魂吧？

但如果相南里不是人，而是生物智械，这就说得通了……

Alpha很快摇头，把这个想法抛到脑后。

算法缘故，他在思考时习惯穷举。

穷举法是这样的，只要开头和结尾正确，中间再怎么离谱的答案都会被保留。
