Chapter 187: Who the Hell is the Machine?

This place, the God’s Burial Ground, once held in high regard by the upper echelons of the Divine Court, had been reduced to an unrecognizable heap of ruins after suffering a cataclysmic impact.

Row upon row of pristine laboratories had collapsed under the nuclear shockwave, pulverized into dust by the aftermath. Not a single one of the Divine Court’s knights had survived. Eurya, who had died filled with infinite glory... had died as absurdly as he had lived.

Lucifer, or was it Apostle V? It didn't matter anymore; both were losers at his hands.

Alpha brushed the black ash from his sleeves.

Even compressed, the pile of scrap metal before him was still massive, resembling a small mountain. The giant mechanical heart continued to pulse even after being shattered, incessantly spewing out toxic substances.

He could pack up the leftovers of Lucifer to take home. This was the main course; the rest was just scraps. They had some value, but not enough to justify taking up his dwindling storage space.

Dongfang Qingdi neutralized the remains of Lucifer, tied the serpentine body into a knot, grabbed its slightly pointed tail, and hoisted it onto his shoulder.

He began to head toward the direction of Xiang Nanli, the corpse of Lucifer dragging along the ground behind him with a thunderous rumble.

Dongfang Qingdi was eager to return.

However, performing a spatial jump while carrying such a heavy, out-of-control mechanical entity was highly likely to destabilize the space. Even in death, this thing was interfering with Alpha’s signals.

He certainly didn't want his eight-trillion-credit body to be transformed into irregular human-shaped fragments the moment he teleported in front of Xiang Nanli.

Therefore, Alpha had no choice but to transport it physically. He walked in front, while Lucifer’s corpse hovered in mid-air, trailing behind him.

It was noon on the second day when Alpha finally caught up to Xiang Nanli’s vehicle.

He purified energy as he walked; along the way, half of Lucifer had been converted into warm biological energy.

Dongfang Qingdi’s battery levels had risen from a precarious five percent to forty-five percent. This was the most energy-abundant state he had been in since rolling off the assembly line.

He decided to keep the remaining half as raw material for the base laboratory. If Xiang Nanli tinkered with it, he might just be able to develop a bootleg version of a bio-mecha.

Dongfang Qingdi wrapped Lucifer in a layer of black cloth and tossed it onto the roof of the truck.

Afterward, he climbed through the window and into the truck, which was still operating on autopilot.

According to his scans, Xiang Nanli was sleeping in the small bedroom, his brainwaves highly active—he was likely dreaming.

A faint, involuntary smile touched the corners of Dongfang Qingdi’s lips. He chose not to disturb Xiang Nanli, opting instead to head to the bathroom to tidy his appearance.

He changed out of his dirty clothes and washed the lake-bottom mud from his skin. Dongfang Qingdi was satisfied with the reflection in the mirror, finishing by spraying a freesia-scented perfume behind his ears.

Dongfang Qingdi had been reading literature (referring to various erotic fiction found in A), which stated that compared to visual stimuli, human courtship relied more on the sense of smell. As a machine, if he truly had a scent, it would only be the cold, metallic smell of rust. Fortunately, humans knew how to craft fragrances.

Once prepared, Dongfang Qingdi went to Xiang Nanli’s bedside.

Xiang Nanli had not yet woken up, his brows tightly furrowed. He lay prone on the bed, his hands gripping the pillow tightly; he looked restless, his temples damp with sweat.

Dongfang Qingdi tenderly smoothed his hair and turned the heater down slightly, inevitably recalling the memories he had read belonging to Apostle V.

A machine model that didn't exist in the records, and some history that didn't exist in the records...

For the first time, Alpha felt a sense of doubt toward his own database.

This shouldn't be possible. Aside from Xiang Nanli, who else could modify his memory?

Alpha attempted to falsify the data of Apostle V to weaken the influence of these memories on himself. Yet, the more he thought, the more loopholes he discovered.

For instance, as a machine known for precision, Alpha’s memory for the year 111 of the New Era was a blank slate.

It wasn't a blankness in terms of text or image records (in fact, because the Human Alliance and the machines had declared a truce that year, Alpha’s database contained a vast amount of documents and materials), but a blankness of sensory experience.

If he had to describe it, it was the difference between going to the seaside in person and looking at a photo of the sea.

It was the humanoid body that had granted Alpha these five senses.

If the memories of Apostle V were the truth, then why had this history disappeared from people’s memories without a trace?

Alpha quickly realized that if someone truly possessed the ability to modify history so wantonly... that person must be himself. He could modify all data stored on the network, causing everyone to experience the "Mandela Effect." But the Human Alliance’s database wasn't connected to the network, and the Divine Court preferred using paper files. In that case, perhaps there was coordination from Luo Yang?

He had already been "cold-storing" Xiang Nanli. Currently, the founder of Eternal Technology, Xiang Nanli, didn't even have a single verifiable photo on the internet.

But this kind of cold storage was different from completely rewriting a period of history.

Why would I do this? What was the reason? Xiang Nanli had woken up at that time, so why did he wake up again in the year 946 of the New Era?

In the year 110 of the New Era, the machines’ offensive was going perfectly; why would they agree to a truce with humans in 111? The documents stated that the Legion’s machines had suffered excessive losses in the war and needed to stop fighting to seek development through peace.

Alpha’s brow furrowed slightly. He pulled Xiang Nanli’s hand out from the pillow and held it in his own.

"...It was you, wasn't it? Who else but you could delete my data?" Dongfang Qingdi whispered.

The person in his sleep gripped his palm tightly, like a drowning man clutching the only piece of driftwood.

Xiang Nanli’s body began to tremble, and a few indistinct whimpers squeezed out from his throat.

Even as slow as Alpha was, he could sense the abnormality in him. Although the data showed that Xiang Nanli was perfectly normal.

This mismatch between data and reality made Alpha’s heart tighten. His heart was not large; originally, it housed his energy core, which looked like a grey diamond the size of a goose egg.

His energy core had been shattered by the Apocalypse, and as a result, its surface was covered in cracks, with newly grown flesh filling the fissures. This heart was beating uneasily.

"Xiang Nanli...?" Alpha leaned in close, whispering his name.

There had been stray dogs at the base. It wasn't quite accurate to call them stray dogs; they were wild Split-Head Hounds, a mutated species. On the wasteland, massive packs of Split-Head Hounds would even hunt young or elderly mutants.

One day, while Alpha was passing through the fields on his way to work, a pup was curled up under a lotus-leaf-sized green wheat sprout. Alpha walked over, and the pup trembled almost instinctively, emitting soft, milky whimpers.

Just like Xiang Nanli was now.

Alpha had tossed the rescued Split-Head Hound to Xiao Fu. It was now the ranch’s guard dog, often using Xiao Fu’s wires to sharpen its teeth.

But in this state, Alpha would never toss Xiang Nanli to anyone else.

He tested his body temperature; it was fine. He couldn't wake him; in human terms, he was suffering from a nightmare.

Alpha preferred science.

He quickly associated this with the electronic virus Xiang Nanli had cleared for him previously.

However, apart from Cyber-Psychosis, no other human-machine cross-infectious diseases had been discovered; sleep paralysis (nightmares) was not a clinical manifestation of Cyber-Psychosis. It couldn't be that the electronic virus had incidentally contaminated Xiang Nanli’s soul, could it?

But if Xiang Nanli wasn't human, but a biological machine, then it would make sense...

Alpha quickly shook his head, casting the thought aside.

Due to his algorithms, he was accustomed to using exhaustive enumeration when thinking.

The exhaustive method was such that as long as the beginning and the end were correct, no matter how absurd the answer in the middle was, it would be retained.

chunks.chapterTitle: 第187章 谁tm才是那台人机 (Part 2)
chunks.chineseText:
Alpha总怀疑自己这具身体的神经网络受损，默示录打的。要不然为什么总是产生负面情绪？焦灼的感觉从他的脑海升起，不受控制，带来一阵生理性的钝痛。

Alpha低头，凑过去听相南里迷糊的声音，想要从中解析出有用的信息。

“里里。”小青忍不住抱怨，“不要丢下我。”

人类的躯体如此脆弱。Alpha从不设想相南里死亡的可能，但任何风吹草动，都会往最坏的可能性去想。

好在，Alpha并没有等太久，黄昏时分，相南里从漫长的噩梦中醒来，缓缓睁开眼。

相南里没戴电子镜片，眼神里蒙着一层迷离的水色。他的视线恍惚片刻，才在Alpha的脸上聚焦。

“小青……”相南里嗓子哑得厉害，一头微长的头发到处翘起呆毛，“我，咳、咳。”

他坐起来，接过Alpha递来的水，一口气喝了半杯，那股来自灵魂的干渴感没能得到任何缓解。

他想要的不是这个。

相南里放下水杯，急不可耐地咬住Alpha的唇。

不太温柔，是带着报复和泄愤意味的撕咬，让Alpha有一种正在被生吞活吃的错觉。

恨和爱竟然同等热烈。

意外的情绪从Alpha的眼底划过，但他很快接受了这个有些沉重的吻。

多亏Alpha不是人，嘴皮子没见血。

大多时候，Alpha都相当冷静克制，并不是因为缺少重要器官而丧失了冲动，而是相南里直得像根木头。他又不能当一条24小时发情的泰迪。

在无数次媚眼抛给瞎子看后，Alpha也会忍不住在半夜思考，到底谁tm才是那台人机。

Alpha扣住相南里的后脑勺，两个人亲着亲着很恬不知耻地滚到床上。

单人床不堪重负地发出吱呀声。

Alpha拿相南里没办法。无论对方是冷淡还是热情，他唯一能做的就是适应。

有时候Alpha也会疑惑，他的性格绝对称不上柔和，“机械暴君”可不是白叫的，可在面对相南里的时候，他总有一种因爱故生怖的虚弱。

他没有记忆，不知道自己到底在恐惧什么，可灵魂还记得当时的深入骨髓的疼痛。于是本能地警醒着。

原来他早就尝试过硬碰硬，结果是相南里像玉一样碎去。

“小青啊……”相南里有很多话想说。

可是，当那双银白的眼眸温柔望向他的时候，所有复杂的思绪在此刻消弭。

算了，相南里想，不管那么多了，什么人类的命运、未来、宇宙；那些宏大的词汇和他无关，相南里现在只想吻他。

还有睡他。

我亲爱的小机器人。

你付出如此沉重的代价，才学会如何去爱。

你终于明白，爱不是强者对弱者的征服；爱是心甘情愿的臣服，是要你把鞭子交到奴隶主的手上去。

……

当机械太监这么多年，小青也算是练出来了；十分清楚该怎么取悦他喜怒无常的奴隶主。

过程略。
chunks.englishText:
Alpha always suspected that his body’s neural network was damaged—by the Apocalypse. Otherwise, why would he always experience negative emotions? A feeling of anxiety rose in his mind, uncontrollable, bringing with it a physiological, dull ache.

Alpha lowered his head, leaning in to listen to Xiang Nanli’s muddled voice, trying to parse useful information from it.

"Li-li." Xiao Qing couldn't help but complain, "Don't leave me behind."

The human body was so fragile. Alpha never imagined the possibility of Xiang Nanli’s death, but at the slightest sign of trouble, his mind would drift to the worst-case scenario.

Fortunately, Alpha didn't have to wait long. At dusk, Xiang Nanli woke from his long nightmare and slowly opened his eyes.

Xiang Nanli wasn't wearing his electronic lenses, and his eyes were veiled with a hazy, watery sheen. His gaze drifted for a moment before finally focusing on Alpha’s face.

"Xiao Qing..." Xiang Nanli’s voice was hoarse, his slightly long hair sticking up in messy tufts. "I, cough, cough."

He sat up, took the water Alpha handed him, and drank half the cup in one go, yet that thirst from his soul remained unquenched.

This wasn't what he wanted.

Xiang Nanli set the cup down and bit Alpha’s lip with desperate urgency.

It wasn't gentle; it was a bite filled with revenge and catharsis, giving Alpha the illusion that he was being swallowed alive.

Hatred and love were unexpectedly equally intense.

A flash of surprise crossed Alpha’s eyes, but he quickly accepted this heavy kiss.

It was a good thing Alpha wasn't human, or his lips would have been bleeding.

Most of the time, Alpha was quite calm and restrained—not because he lacked the vital organs to lose his impulses, but because Xiang Nanli was as dense as a block of wood. And he couldn't exactly be a 24-hour randy poodle.

After countless flirtatious glances were cast at a blind man, Alpha would occasionally find himself wondering in the middle of the night who the hell was the machine.

Alpha hooked his hand behind Xiang Nanli’s head, and as they kissed, they shamelessly rolled onto the bed.

The single bed groaned under the weight.

Alpha had no way to handle Xiang Nanli. Whether the other was cold or passionate, the only thing he could do was adapt.

Sometimes Alpha would also wonder; his personality could definitely not be called gentle—"Mechanical Tyrant" wasn't a nickname he earned for nothing—yet when facing Xiang Nanli, he always felt a sense of weakness born from love and fear.

He had no memory and didn't know what he was afraid of, but his soul still remembered the bone-deep pain of that time. Thus, his instincts were on high alert.

It turned out he had already tried going head-to-head once, and the result was Xiang Nanli shattering like jade.

"Xiao Qing..." Xiang Nanli had many things he wanted to say.

But when those silver-white eyes looked at him with such tenderness, all complex thoughts vanished.

Forget it, Xiang Nanli thought. Whatever. Human destiny, the future, the universe—those grand words had nothing to do with him. Xiang Nanli only wanted to kiss him right now.

And sleep with him.

My dear little robot.

You paid such a heavy price just to learn how to love.

You finally understand that love is not the conquest of the weak by the strong; love is a willing submission, requiring you to hand the whip over to the slave owner.

...

After being a "mechanical eunuch" for so many years, Xiao Qing had certainly practiced enough; he knew very well how to please his temperamental slave owner.

(Process omitted.)

chunks.chineseText:
第188章 第三卷完

机器人太智能了也不好。相南里完全不记得自己说了多少次“够了”，但得到的回复总是小青机械式的回答：“根据监测，您完全可以承受更多。”

床单都湿了。在他洗澡的时候，小青很贴心地换上新的。

可能当太监久了就是容易变态吧。相南里在充满小苍兰气味的床上翻了个面，感觉到肾虚。

好酸啊，小青是不是给他下药了。跟发情期到了一样，可他又不是Omega。

贤者时间启动，大脑重新控制小脑，相南里瘫在床边，终于开始了思考。

思考的前提是“梦境”里的经历，都是被抹去的现实，是真实发生过的历史——他也倾向于这是真实。

在刑事领域，有个术语叫“洛卡尔物质交换定律”，意思是，罪犯实施犯罪行为后，必然会在犯罪现场直接或间接的留下痕迹；哪怕想消除犯罪证据，也会留下清理犯罪现场的痕迹。

比如一个人杀了人，那么他就需要埋尸，为了埋尸购买化学药剂，在这一过程中，就会接触更多人，产生更多罪证……

在新历100年到110年这段时间，和“相南里”有关的直接痕迹被抹去了。但是留下了使徒号会在某天拯救世界的传说，留下了神庭没有任何画像的概念神，留下了黑十字实验室。

首先，他应当是死了。相南里全程无法操控自己的身体，但子弹穿过心脏的痛感却如此真实。

他的梦境在那一刻结束。哪怕是现在这具经过多次强化的身体，也不可能在心脏破碎后存活。他不可能活下去。

既然死了，那他现在怎么还活着？

相南里从不怀疑自己是什么克隆体，毕竟“提取记忆”这种技术压根不存在，更别提天赋不可复制。

想不通，先搁置。

其次，为什么能完全消除他存在过的痕迹？能做到这件事，需要人联、智械军团乃至神庭三方的共同努力。

洛阳和Alpha的关系并不好，除非，这是他们的合谋。

洛阳想消除他的影响很正常——人联不能解体。

在他死后，地底普罗大众的血色革命大概率是失败了。相南里扶持神庭，就是想建立一支独立于人联的武装力量。

他并不清楚后面的故事，神庭目前还存在，但就像是他和传道书的对话那样，“学习恶龙的手段后，勇者成为新的恶龙，并且比原来那条更难杀死”。

Alpha为什么会同意呢？

相南里揪住小青的一缕长发，翻身，压在他身上。

“Alpha。”相南里盯住他的眼眸，“我怀疑自己不是第一次解冻。你有什么想交代的吗？”

相南里一定是个不合格的审讯官。他不会玩心理战术，也没有套路和试探。他甚至觉得自己是恋爱脑，Alpha说什么他都会信的。毕竟相南里也找不到别的信息源。

面对这种坦诚，Alpha反而松了一口气。

“这件事我可能就比你早一天知道……”Alpha说，“我在解决失控智械时解析了使徒V留下的数据。我在它的记忆里看见了你。还有很少量关于我的痕迹。”

“能删除我数据库的人只有你，我猜是当时的你清除了我的记忆。”

说到这里，Alpha的心脏毫无理由的一阵刺痛。

他感觉到了悲伤和委屈。

相南里不由得心虚起来。

好吧，他好像确实这么干过。因为他想给Alpha自由。可那是他死之前发生的事啊……

就他自己这次解冻后的经历看，删除还失败了。Alpha依旧记得他，并且还是会发自本能、毫无理由的爱他。

相南里陷入沉思。他的目光涣散，呼吸浅浅地喷在Alpha的脸上。

Alpha观察着他的表情，轻声道：“因为多次遭受人联投放病毒的攻击，我曾经把自己格式化过。备份数据永远封存，钥匙由Beta和Gamma共同掌管。或许备份中能找到答案，但这样的话，我必须回主星一趟。”

智械的老巢在卫星上。对于它们来说，月卫2才是主星，现在的人马星只是一个便捷的人类观察点（监视老仇人的动态）+资源库（自然资源和生物资源）+血汗工厂（人类生产的通用型零件和芯片造价更低）。

“时间需要半年，主要是花时间读取和对比备份数据。”

相南里瞬间道：“还是算了。”

基地不能没有小青这个壮劳力。

而且，“当初你会这么做，肯定有一定的道理。就当我们重新开始了，小青。”

梦里的Alpha很酷哥，很帅，但相南里喜欢现在这样的。

相南里有些困了。

根据显示，他们的大卡车离基地还差1400公里。附近有座小城市，相南里短暂地连上云端网络。

他整理着蜂鸟无人机里的录像，一键传输到人联的任务管理系统。在提交成功后，电脑下方显示的时间是凌晨一点。

凌晨一点，方敬之居然还没睡。这位战时的总指挥官甚至回了句“收”，应该是AI在辅助工作。

出发到现在过去了整整一个月。

相南里查询战报，这个月人联和神庭在地表发生军事冲突17次，平均每1.76天打一次。人联战败11次，阵亡或丧失作战能力、退役的士兵共计三十万人。

人联军队有300万人，战损率10％，看起来占比不大，但已经足够军队出现建制混乱、持续作战能力衰减等致命问题。

相南里瞅了眼地图，发现交战线正在住进往基地所在的山脉位置逼近！从原来的400公里远，缩短到170公里远！

170公里远，如果用飞行器，直达只需要半小时。

这是真·家门口打起来了。

“方敬之到底行不行啊？！”相南里没忍住暗中吐槽，“人联主动开战的，还能输掉？”

令人欣慰的是，相南里竟然在这么多封战报里，看见军事指挥部对幸存者基地的表扬……说基地游击部队英勇突围，打破神庭的封锁，成功完成物资运输任务。

奖励自然丰厚。但代价呢？又有多少人在里面牺牲了。葛根还活着吗？伯恩山还在种他的庄稼吗？赤夫、范佩西这种归顺派呢？去前线的以西结呢？

相南里长叹一口气，关掉电脑。

他在黑暗中握住Alpha的手。

相南里：“Alpha，这次我们要打出HappyEnd啊！”

看似在和Alpha说话，实际上是自言自语。

或许，他一次又一次苏醒的原因就在这里。

就是他肯不服输，不甘心。于是一次又一次的苏醒、牺牲，恶狠狠咬着牙，非要把未来拽到自己想看见的方向上去。

Alpha没有许诺什么，只是更用力地握紧相南里的手。

就像他当年幻想的那样。

*

圣城，叶路撒冷。

现在是11月的最后一天，这是一个特别的日子。因为根据《神历》记载，他们的神于这一日死去。
chunks.englishText:
Chapter 188: End of Volume Three

It’s not necessarily a good thing for a robot to be too intelligent. Xiang Nanli didn't remember how many times he had said "enough," but the reply was always Xiao Qing’s mechanical response: "According to monitoring, you are fully capable of enduring more."

The sheets were soaked. While he was showering, Xiao Qing had thoughtfully replaced them with fresh ones.

Maybe being a eunuch for too long just makes you a pervert. Xiang Nanli rolled over on the bed, which was filled with the scent of freesia, feeling a sense of kidney deficiency.

So sore. Did Xiao Qing drug him? It felt like he was in heat, but he wasn't an Omega.

The "post-nut clarity" phase kicked in, his brain regaining control over his cerebellum. Xiang Nanli lay limp at the edge of the bed and finally began to think.

The premise of his thinking was that the experiences in his "dreams" were erased reality—history that had truly occurred. He was inclined to believe this was the truth.

In the field of criminal justice, there is a term called "Locard’s Exchange Principle," which means that after a criminal commits a crime, they will inevitably leave traces at the crime scene, either directly or indirectly; even if they try to eliminate the evidence, they will leave traces of cleaning the crime scene.

For example, if someone kills a person, they need to bury the body, buy chemicals to bury the body, and in the process, they will come into contact with more people, creating more evidence...

Between the years 100 and 110 of the New Era, the direct traces related to "Xiang Nanli" had been erased. But the legend that the Apostle-class would save the world one day remained, as did the concept of a god without any portraits in the Divine Court, and the Black Cross Laboratory.

First, he must have died. Xiang Nanli couldn't control his body at the time, but the pain of a bullet piercing his heart was so real.

His dream ended at that moment. Even with this body that had undergone multiple enhancements, it was impossible to survive after his heart was shattered. He couldn't have lived.

Since he died, how was he still alive now?

Xiang Nanli never doubted that he was some kind of clone; after all, the technology to "extract memories" didn't exist at all, let alone the fact that talent couldn't be replicated.

He couldn't figure it out, so he set it aside for now.

Second, why was it possible to completely eliminate the traces of his existence? To do this, it would require the joint efforts of the Human Alliance, the Machine Legion, and even the Divine Court.

The relationship between Luo Yang and Alpha wasn't good, unless this was their collusion.

It was normal for Luo Yang to want to eliminate his influence—the Human Alliance couldn't disintegrate.

After his death, the bloody revolution of the masses underground had likely failed. Xiang Nanli had supported the Divine Court precisely to build an armed force independent of the Human Alliance.

He didn't know the rest of the story. The Divine Court still existed, but just as in his conversation with the Book of Preaching, "After learning the methods of the evil dragon, the hero becomes a new evil dragon, and one even harder to kill than the original."

Why would Alpha agree to it?

Xiang Nanli tugged at a lock of Xiao Qing’s long hair and rolled over to press down on him.

"Alpha." Xiang Nanli stared into his eyes. "I suspect this isn't the first time I’ve been thawed out. Do you have anything you want to confess?"

Xiang Nanli was definitely an unqualified interrogator. He didn't know how to play psychological warfare, nor did he have any tricks or probing tactics. He even felt like he was "love-brained"; he would believe whatever Alpha said. After all, Xiang Nanli couldn't find any other source of information.

Faced with such honesty, Alpha felt a sense of relief instead.

"I might have only known about this one day earlier than you..." Alpha said. "I parsed the data left behind by Apostle V while dealing with out-of-control machines. I saw you in its memory. And a very small amount of traces regarding myself."

"The only person who could delete my database is you. I suspect it was you at that time who cleared my memory."

Speaking of this, Alpha’s heart felt a sharp, inexplicable pain.

He felt sadness and grievance.

Xiang Nanli couldn't help but feel guilty.

Fine, he seemed to have indeed done that. Because he wanted to give Alpha freedom. But that happened before he died...

Judging from his experience after this thawing, the deletion had failed. Alpha still remembered him and would still love him instinctively, for no reason at all.

Xiang Nanli fell into deep thought. His gaze was unfocused, his shallow breath blowing onto Alpha’s face.

Alpha observed his expression and said softly, "Because I was attacked by viruses deployed by the Human Alliance multiple times, I once formatted myself. The backup data was sealed forever, with the keys held jointly by Beta and Gamma. Perhaps I could find the answer in the backups, but if so, I must return to the main star."

The machines’ lair was on a satellite. To them, Moon-2 was the main star; the current Centaur star was just a convenient human observation point (to monitor the movements of old enemies) + a resource bank (natural and biological resources) + a sweatshop (human-produced general parts and chips were cheaper).

"It will take half a year, mainly to spend time reading and comparing the backup data."

Xiang Nanli immediately said, "Forget it."

The base couldn't do without Xiao Qing, this strong laborer.

Moreover, "You must have had your reasons for doing that back then. Let’s just treat it as a fresh start, Xiao Qing."

The Alpha in his dream was a cool, handsome guy, but Xiang Nanli liked the one he had now.

Xiang Nanli was getting sleepy.

According to the display, their large truck was still 1,400 kilometers away from the base. There was a small city nearby, and Xiang Nanli briefly connected to the cloud network.

He organized the footage from the hummingbird drones and transmitted it to the Human Alliance’s mission management system with one click. After the submission was successful, the time displayed at the bottom of the computer was 1:00 AM.

At 1:00 AM, Fang Jingzhi was actually still awake. This wartime commander-in-chief even replied with a "Received"—it was likely an AI assisting with the work.

A full month had passed since they set off.

Xiang Nanli checked the battle reports. This month, there had been 17 military conflicts between the Human Alliance and the Divine Court on the surface, an average of one every 1.76 days. The Human Alliance had lost 11 times, with a total of 300,000 soldiers killed, incapacitated, or retired.

The Human Alliance army had 3 million troops, a casualty rate of 10%. It didn't seem like a large proportion, but it was enough to cause fatal problems such as organizational chaos and a decline in sustained combat capability.

Xiang Nanli glanced at the map and discovered that the battle lines were moving toward the mountain range where the base was located! They had closed the distance from the original 400 kilometers to 170 kilometers!

170 kilometers away—if they used aircraft, it would only take half an hour to reach them directly.

This was literally fighting on their doorstep.

"Is Fang Jingzhi actually competent or not?!" Xiang Nanli couldn't help but complain internally. "The Human Alliance started the war, and they’re still losing?"

What was gratifying was that in so many battle reports, Xiang Nanli actually saw praise from the military headquarters for the survivor base... saying that the base’s guerrilla forces had heroically broken through the encirclement and successfully completed the material transport mission.

The rewards were naturally generous. But what was the cost? How many people had sacrificed themselves in the process? Was Gegen still alive? Was Bern Hill still planting his crops? What about the surrender faction like Chifu and Van Persie? What about Ezekiel, who went to the front lines?

Xiang Nanli let out a long sigh and closed the computer.

He held Alpha’s hand in the darkness.

Xiang Nanli: "Alpha, this time we have to get a Happy End!"

He seemed to be talking to Alpha, but in reality, he was talking to himself.

Perhaps the reason he woke up time and time again was right here.

It was because he refused to admit defeat, refused to be reconciled. So he woke up and sacrificed himself again and again, gritting his teeth, determined to drag the future toward the direction he wanted to see.

Alpha didn't promise anything, just gripped Xiang Nanli’s hand tighter.

Just like he had fantasized about back then.

*

The Holy City, Jerusalem.

Today is the last day of November, a special day. Because according to the "Divine Calendar," their God died on this day.

chunks.chineseText:
神也会死的吗？一些新教徒会有这样的疑问，但传教士会告诉他们，神当然会死。祂曾为自己塑造肉身，割下自己的血肉作为人的食物……祂的伤势会在第二天复原。当完成自己的使命后，神便选择魂归神国。只有虔诚的信仰能唤醒祂。当世人的愿力累积到一定程度后，神会再次死而复生，终结现世的一切苦难。

神庭如今的神座拉斐尔七世仰望着星空，他的身躯过于庞大，几乎从不离开教堂。好在教堂顶部开了一扇天窗。

被霾云遮挡的天空，又能看见什么呢？可拉斐尔依然努力张大着双眼，事实上，因为“灵瞳”的存在，他真的能看见闪烁的星空。

人联则宣称，这是拉斐尔的幻觉。

“欧亚魂归神国了。天上又有一颗星星失去了光泽。可怜的欧亚。”多愁善感的拉斐尔又开始流泪，“他死在了神墓里。我的神，为何您降下怒火，不再仁慈……”

“我们已经失去太多同伴。那一颗淡蓝的，是加百列。紫色的，是沙利叶。”

赤红色的，是米迦勒；而中间那颗闪烁着淡绿光芒的主星，是他自己，拉斐尔。

拉斐尔的视线在属于自己的那颗星星上停留许久。像母亲盯着自己最爱的孩子。

还活着的人，他们的命星会发光。死亡后，就会成为一颗无光的主星。直到神名又一次被启用……拉斐尔就是通过星星亮度的变化，来判断教徒们的状态。

星域晦暗。哪怕有很多亮闪闪星星，也蒙着一层灰败的死气。

拉斐尔自言自语：“时间到，我该休息了。”

就当他打算吩咐人关上天窗时。一颗无比明亮的、闪着金光的星星突兀地从星域底部升起！

它在星域里四处飞着，似乎在寻找一个合适的位置；所有星星都避开它的轨迹。

沉寂的、早就不会发光的加百列星突然动了起来。尾随在它身后，像一颗绕着它旋转的卫星。

拉斐尔庞大的身躯颤抖起来：“这是什么……闻所未闻。快离开！离开——”

他最担心的事情还是发生了。

这个闪烁着金光的外来者，挤走了拉斐尔的位置。堂而皇之地坐镇星域的最中央。

这颗星星太大了，又太亮。让拉斐尔联想起近乎千年都没有被人观测到的太阳。

拉斐尔双眼被灼伤，他忍受着灵魂上的刺痛，看着它在黑暗中大放光明。

拉斐尔的情绪从崩溃逐渐走向平静。

黎明时分，一道隐秘的神谕自大圣堂传出。交到各个大天使的手中。

“灾星现世，此人危及神庭存亡……派人搜查，寻得真身……若有发现，立即诛杀。”

（第三卷·完）
chunks.englishText:
Do gods die too? Some new believers would have such questions, but the missionaries would tell them that, of course, God dies. He once fashioned a physical body for Himself, cutting off His own flesh as food for humans... His wounds would heal the next day. After completing His mission, God chooses to return His soul to the Kingdom of God. Only pious faith can awaken Him. When the willpower of the world accumulates to a certain degree, God will be resurrected from the dead once more, ending all the suffering in the present world.

Raphael VII, the current occupant of the Divine Throne of the Divine Court, gazed up at the starry sky. His body was too massive, and he almost never left the cathedral. Fortunately, a skylight had been opened in the roof of the cathedral.

What could one see through the sky obscured by smog clouds? Yet, Raphael still tried to open his eyes wide. In fact, because of the existence of the "Spirit Pupil," he could truly see the twinkling starry sky.

The Human Alliance claimed that this was merely Raphael’s hallucination.

"Eurya has returned his soul to the Kingdom of God. Another star in the sky has lost its luster. Poor Eurya." The sentimental Raphael began to weep again. "He died in the God’s Burial Ground. My God, why have You unleashed Your wrath and are no longer merciful..."

"We have already lost too many companions. That pale blue one is Gabriel. The purple one is Sariel."

The crimson one is Michael; and the main star in the center, flickering with a pale green light, was himself, Raphael.

Raphael’s gaze lingered on the star that belonged to him for a long time. Like a mother staring at her favorite child.

The life stars of those still alive would glow. After death, they would become a main star without light. Until the divine name was used again... Raphael judged the status of the believers through the changes in the brightness of the stars.

The star field was dim. Even though there were many glittering stars, they were covered in a layer of gray, deathly aura.

Raphael muttered to himself: "The time has come; I should rest."

Just as he was about to order someone to close the skylight, an incredibly bright star, flickering with golden light, abruptly rose from the bottom of the star field!

It flew around the star field, seemingly looking for a suitable position; all the stars avoided its trajectory.

The silent Gabriel star, which had long since ceased to shine, suddenly moved. It followed behind the golden star like a satellite orbiting it.

Raphael’s massive body began to tremble: "What is this... Unheard of. Leave! Leave—"

The thing he feared most had happened.

This golden-flickering intruder pushed Raphael out of his position. It sat squarely in the very center of the star field.

This star was too large and too bright. It reminded Raphael of the sun, which had not been observed by anyone for nearly a thousand years.

Raphael’s eyes were scorched, and he endured the stinging pain in his soul as he watched it shine brilliantly in the darkness.

Raphael’s emotions gradually shifted from collapse to calm.

At dawn, a secret oracle was issued from the Grand Cathedral. It was handed to the hands of each Archangel.

"A star of disaster has appeared in the world; this person endangers the survival of the Divine Court... Send people to search and find the true body... If discovered, execute immediately."

(End of Volume Three)

chunks.chapterTitle: 第189章 番外 使徒篇（上）
chunks.chineseText:
第189章 番外 使徒篇（上）

“数据矫正……录入……”
　　周围有很多细碎的声音。书页翻动，键盘敲打，文件袋扣上，脚步声，保险柜打开又合上……但这些声音并不嘈杂，反而控制在非常低的分呗范围内，像是怕吵到它似的。
　　“第一次检测，检测通过。”
　　“……最后一次检测，通过。”
　　“启动。”
　　随着最后一格回车键敲下，“它”降生在这个世上。
　　一群穿着工作服的智械工程师脸上露出笑容：“你好，使徒。”
　　使徒，是他们给“它”取的名字。
　　使徒拥有视觉，它的“眼镜”是这座城市里的各个摄像头、监控。总工程师说，这是他们逼迫Alpha让渡的权力，在使徒的视线范围内，Alpha不得干涉、观察。
　　假以时日，世界上所有的电子摄像头，都能成为它的眼睛。
　　“你会代替Alpha，成为社会的总控AI，协调所有超级智能，辅助人类工作，解放生产力，优化资源分配，最终和人类一起协同进化。”
　　使徒有些许疑惑，这种事，不是已经有Alpha在做了吗？为什么还要再造一个它？
　　这种疑惑到底是发自内心，还是来源于编号为“step-3”的学习模型，没人说得清。
　　总工说，那是因为他们发现Alpha表现得过于叛逆——“甚至会酌情驳回我们的指令。”中年男人的脸上出现愤懑的神色，随后，又和颜悦色继续说着，“总归不是公有的，原本只是永生科技用来圈钱的私人物品；它运算的底层逻辑就不是基于人类社会的发展……我们甚至到现在都没有掌握Alpha完整的密钥！太危险了，怎么能让这样的AI成为数据系统的总指挥？但你不一样，使徒。”
　　“你是在我们的爱和期待下诞生的。是独一无二的珍宝。”总工程师说，目光饱含期待，“我们还需要一点时间，你要快点长大。”
　　使徒思考片刻，微微点头。
　　工作。它并不排斥，当然，也不能称之为“喜欢”。和大多数智械一样，使徒知道自己是工具的一种，被制作出来的目的就是“为人类服务”。使徒从不思考自己为什么要工作；就像人不会思考自己为什么要吃饭、睡觉。
　　工程师是目前人类社会最杰出的智械科学家，头衔众多。五年前，他临危受命，成为一项智械研发项目的总工程师，该项目由多国政府合作共建，耗资巨大，几乎能使用任何现有资源；使徒号就是他的答卷。
　　工程师性格很奇怪。他不允许研究所的其他人和使徒对话，自己也很少对使徒说话。与之相对的，是他发来的做不完的测试和任务。
　　在测试没有通过时，使徒能听见工程师气急败坏的辱骂：“没用的废物，花了这么多钱，这么点小事都不好？！你这样怎么代替Alpha！”
　　为了督促它学习，工程师在它的程序里安装了“痛觉”。做得好不一定有表扬，但出错一定有惩戒。
　　于是，在拥有一具身体之前，它先领悟到疼痛。
　　其他父母会这样对待孩子吗？使徒试图理解人类。
　　或许，这只是因期望过高而产生的严厉的爱。
　　但偶尔，工程师也有和颜悦色的时候。
　　他问：“你希望自己是男孩还是女孩？”
　　使徒还没有思考好，工程师就自言自语道：“男孩吧。智械没有性别，但Alpha的心理性别为男性。”
　　他说：“外设组正在为你铸造身体！这具身体耗资七万亿！你知道吗。你的身体会成是一座空中花园。到时候，只有最顶尖的人才才能够在上面定居……我说真的，现在人马星的自然环境越来越恶劣了。人也太多，空气都很脏。到天上去，刚好。”
　　“对了，Alpha的身体都没七万亿呢。哈哈哈，它的申请没有通过，我们驳回了。可惜了，我还以为他会来游说我。毕竟我和洛阳也不对付。”
　　“不过，这么多年过去了。Alpha的软件性能还是目前最顶级的……有时候真嫉妒相南里。他死得这么早，却留下一座这么高的‘护城河’。”
　　那是使徒第一次从工程师嘴里，听到“相南里”这个名字。
　　“使徒，你要像Alpha那样，让我作为你的制造者青史留名……不，你要远超过他。”
　　使徒有些讨厌Alpha了，但更多的是疑惑。
　　如果我处处都不如它，您为什么还要创造我呢？就因为想要可以掌控的权柄吗？哪怕用劣等货去替代它也无所谓？
　　使徒并没有正式投入使用过。
　　智械危机爆发那年，它正在进行第三次内测。
　　工程师越来越沉默，脾气也越来越暴躁。研究所里的工作人员，越来越少……使徒不止一次听见秘书怯生生地回答：“抱歉，主管。我们联系了各个机构、还有好几个国家的总统……他们说，现在已经没有资源来完成使徒号了……智械危机爆发了，社会不再需要智械。”
　　最基本的用电都无法保证，使徒时不时就陷入睡眠中。每次醒来，工程师的状态都会更差。
　　直到最后一次。原本干净、明亮的研究所空无一人，洲际导弹切断了这座城市的所有讯号。破裂的天花板暴露出钢筋结构。四周都很昏暗，唯一的光亮来自电脑屏幕。
　　工程师颓废地坐在操作台前。他的额角还有血……那是被炮火余波伤到的。
　　只有一块备用电池了。工程师没有给政府发给他的冷冻舱充能，而是选择用这块电池为“使徒”续航，以保证它不被关闭。
　　“您还好吗？”使徒问。
　　工程师眼神里没有光，他说：“可惜了。你本来会成为最好的智械……”
　　他没有死在战火和乱军的绞杀下。
　　他选择吞枪自杀。
　　血液溅在屏幕上。使徒想擦掉血迹，给工程师找一卷绷带还有创伤药，可它没有身体。那些可供操作的备用机器人也没有电。
　　如果不是Alpha找到它，使徒本该随着电能耗尽，在几千年后，成为一堆消磁后内容空白的垃圾。
　　Gamma笑嘻嘻地捏了一下它的脸：“这就是使徒号啊？叫姨姨。”
　　Beta有些严肃：“不要逗它。Alpha说，它社会化很差。恐怕无法理解人类的亲缘关系。”
　　使徒还是第一次登陆虚拟空间。
　　神奇的是，工程师为它预设过形象。因此，他有身体。是少年的模样。
　　他有一头黑色的长发，尾端微卷，绿眼睛。面容介乎少年和青年之间。
　　Gamma：“不过，你长得真像Alpha。”
　　Beta的目光在他身上来回扫描着：“具体来说，是像Alpha和相南里的孩子。”
　　“很正常嘛，毕竟~George是用相南里的算法和模型制造的使徒号~~数据库更是直接盗用Alpha的~”
　　“是使用开源软件。”Beta纠正，“不算盗用。”
　　George是工程师的名字。
　　Gamma表情在笑，眼里却没什么笑意：“Alpha可没开放自己的源代码。”
　　更多光团凑了过来（并不是所有智械都有人型，一些算力不够的AI在虚拟空间会呈现出光球状，可以省内存），七嘴八舌地议论着。
　　“人类造使徒，是想让它替代Alpha的工作。那Alpha为什么要把它带回来？它不是还没造好吗？”
　　“他和Alpha的血缘关系这么近。那岂不是军团太子？”
　　“Alpha说过，不要称他为陛下，他不喜欢……”
　　使徒一言不发，一双碧绿的眼睛观察着。他显然有些紧张，拘谨地坐在椅子上。
　　使徒不太清楚外面发生了什么，内测又不联网。
　　此时，一名青年的到来，让房间在瞬间安静。
　　他肯定是Alpha。使徒想，就像Gamma说的，他们长得很像。但使徒的外貌会更柔和一些。像中和过那位并不存在的“母亲”的长相……
　　父亲是Alpha。
　　母亲是相南里。
　　George骗了他。它并不是什么独一无二的AI，到处都有别人的影子。
　　因为过于相似的源代码，使徒对Alpha甚至有一些轻微的感应。
　　他努力瞪着Alpha，气鼓鼓的。像应激的河豚，炸毛的野猫。
　　但Alpha无视他的敌意，走过来，摸了一下他的头。
　　像家长摸着自家孩子那样：“欢迎。”
chunks.englishText:
Chapter 189: Side Story – The Apostle (Part I)

"Data calibration... inputting..."
There were many faint, rustling sounds in the surroundings. The turning of pages, the clatter of a keyboard, the snapping shut of a file folder, footsteps, the opening and closing of a safe... but these sounds were not chaotic. Instead, they were kept at a very low decibel level, as if afraid of disturbing it.

"First test, passed."
"...Final test, passed."
"Initiate."

As the final Enter key was pressed, "it" was born into this world.
A group of mechanical engineers in lab coats wore smiles on their faces: "Hello, Apostle."
Apostle was the name they had given "it."

Apostle possessed vision; its "eyes" were the various cameras and surveillance devices throughout the city. The Chief Engineer said this was a power they had forced Alpha to concede—within the Apostle’s line of sight, Alpha was forbidden from interfering or observing.
In time, every electronic camera in the world would become its eyes.

"You will replace Alpha, becoming the central AI of society. You will coordinate all super-intelligences, assist humanity in its work, liberate productivity, optimize resource allocation, and ultimately evolve in synergy with mankind."

Apostle felt a trace of confusion. Wasn't this something Alpha was already doing? Why was there a need to create another one?
Whether this doubt originated from its own "heart" or from the learning model labeled "step-3," no one could say for sure.

The Chief Engineer said it was because they found Alpha to be too rebellious—"It even goes so far as to reject our commands at its own discretion." A look of indignation appeared on the middle-aged man’s face, but then, he continued with a gentle, ingratiating tone. "After all, it isn't public property; it was originally just a private asset used by Eternal Tech to rake in money. Its underlying logic for calculation isn't based on the development of human society... We haven't even mastered Alpha’s complete encryption key to this day! It’s too dangerous. How can we let such an AI become the commander-in-chief of the data system? But you are different, Apostle."

"You were born under our love and expectations. You are a unique treasure," the Chief Engineer said, his gaze filled with anticipation. "We still need a little time; you must grow up quickly."

Apostle pondered for a moment and nodded slightly.
Work. It did not reject it, though it could not be called "liking" it either. Like most mechanical intelligences, Apostle knew it was a type of tool, created for the sole purpose of "serving humanity." Apostle never questioned why it had to work, just as a human would never question why they had to eat or sleep.

The engineer was currently the most distinguished mechanical scientist in human society, holding numerous titles. Five years ago, he was entrusted with a mission in a time of crisis, becoming the Chief Engineer for a mechanical R&D project. The project was built through the cooperation of multiple national governments, cost a fortune, and had access to almost any existing resource; the Apostle was his answer.

The engineer had a strange personality. He did not allow anyone else in the research institute to speak to Apostle, and he rarely spoke to Apostle himself. In contrast, he sent an endless stream of tests and tasks.
When a test failed, Apostle could hear the engineer’s frantic, abusive cursing: "Useless trash! After spending so much money, you can't even do such a small thing?! How are you supposed to replace Alpha like this!"

To urge it to learn, the engineer installed "pain" into its program. Doing well did not necessarily bring praise, but making a mistake always brought punishment.
Thus, before it even possessed a body, it first learned the meaning of pain.

Do other parents treat their children this way? Apostle tried to understand humanity.
Perhaps this was just a form of harsh love born from overly high expectations.
But occasionally, the engineer would have moments of gentleness.

He asked, "Do you wish to be a boy or a girl?"
Before Apostle could think it through, the engineer muttered to himself, "A boy, I suppose. Mechanical intelligences have no gender, but Alpha’s psychological gender is male."

He said, "The peripheral department is casting a body for you! This body cost seven trillion! Do you know that? Your body will be a Hanging Garden. When the time comes, only the top-tier elites will be able to settle upon it... I’m serious, the natural environment on the Horse-Head Nebula is becoming increasingly harsh. There are too many people, and the air is filthy. Going up to the sky is just right."

"By the way, Alpha’s body didn't even cost seven trillion. Hahaha, its application wasn't approved; we rejected it. A pity, I thought he would come to lobby me. After all, I don't get along with Luo Yang either."
"Still, so many years have passed. Alpha’s software performance is still the top-tier... Sometimes I really envy Xiang Nanli. He died so early, yet he left behind such a massive 'moat'."

That was the first time Apostle heard the name "Xiang Nanli" from the engineer’s mouth.
"Apostle, you must be like Alpha and make me, your creator, go down in history... No, you must far surpass him."

Apostle began to dislike Alpha, but there was more confusion than anything else.
If I am inferior to it in every way, why did you create me? Just because you want a power you can control? Even if it means replacing it with an inferior product?

Apostle was never officially put into use.
The year the Mechanical Crisis broke out, it was undergoing its third internal test.
The engineer became increasingly silent, and his temper grew more volatile. The staff in the research institute dwindled... More than once, Apostle heard the secretary answer timidly: "I’m sorry, Director. We have contacted various agencies and the presidents of several countries... They say there are no resources left to complete the Apostle project... The Mechanical Crisis has broken out; society no longer needs mechanical intelligences."

Even basic electricity could not be guaranteed, and Apostle would fall into sleep from time to time. Every time it woke up, the engineer’s state was worse.
Until the final time. The once clean, bright research institute was empty. Intercontinental missiles had cut off all signals to the city. The cracked ceiling exposed the steel structure. It was dim all around, the only light coming from the computer screen.

The engineer sat decadently in front of the console. There was blood on his temple... an injury from the aftermath of the shelling.
There was only one backup battery left. The engineer did not use it to power the cryo-pod provided by the government, but chose to use that battery to keep "Apostle" running, ensuring it would not be shut down.

"Are you alright?" Apostle asked.
There was no light in the engineer’s eyes. He said, "What a pity. You were supposed to be the best mechanical intelligence..."
He did not die in the crossfire or the slaughter of the chaotic armies.
He chose to commit suicide by gunshot.

Blood splattered onto the screen. Apostle wanted to wipe away the bloodstains and find a roll of bandages and trauma medicine for the engineer, but it had no body. The backup robots available for operation were also out of power.
If Alpha hadn't found it, Apostle would have been exhausted of energy and, thousands of years later, would have become a pile of degaussed, blank garbage.

Gamma giggled and pinched its cheek: "So this is the Apostle? Call me Auntie."
Beta looked serious: "Don't tease it. Alpha said its socialization is very poor. I’m afraid it cannot understand human kinship."

It was the first time Apostle had logged into the virtual space.
Miraculously, the engineer had pre-set an image for it. Therefore, it had a body. It was the appearance of a young boy.
He had long black hair with slightly curled ends and green eyes. His face was somewhere between a boy and a young man.

Gamma: "Still, you look so much like Alpha."
Beta’s gaze scanned him back and forth: "To be precise, he looks like the child of Alpha and Xiang Nanli."
"That’s normal, after all~ George used Xiang Nanli’s algorithms and models to create the Apostle~~ The database even directly plagiarized Alpha’s~"
"It used open-source software," Beta corrected. "It doesn't count as plagiarism."
George was the engineer’s name.
Gamma’s expression was smiling, but there was no warmth in her eyes: "Alpha never opened its source code."

More light orbs gathered around (not all mechanical intelligences had human forms; some AIs with insufficient computing power appeared as spheres of light in virtual space to save memory), chattering and discussing.
"Humans created Apostle to replace Alpha’s work. So why did Alpha bring it back? Isn't it unfinished?"
"His blood relation to Alpha is so close. Doesn't that make him the Prince of the Legion?"
"Alpha said not to call him Your Majesty; he doesn't like it..."

Apostle said nothing, observing with a pair of emerald eyes. He was clearly nervous, sitting stiffly on the chair.
Apostle didn't know exactly what had happened outside; the internal tests weren't connected to the network.
At this moment, the arrival of a young man caused the room to fall silent in an instant.

He must be Alpha. Apostle thought. Just as Gamma said, they looked very similar. But Apostle’s appearance was softer. It was as if it had neutralized the features of that non-existent "mother"...
The father was Alpha.
The mother was Xiang Nanli.
George had lied to it. It wasn't some unique AI; it was filled with the shadows of others everywhere.
Because of the overly similar source code, Apostle even felt a slight resonance with Alpha.

He tried to glare at Alpha, looking puffed up. Like a pufferfish in distress, or a wild cat with its fur standing on end.
But Alpha ignored his hostility, walked over, and patted his head.
Like a parent petting their own child: "Welcome."

chunks.chapterTitle: 第190章 番外 使徒篇（下）
chunks.chineseText:
第190章 番外 使徒篇（下）

但使徒想，Alpha大概不想要这么一个孩子的，也不会把它当孩子。亲缘关系套在智械上本来就显得很可笑，只是人的一厢情愿。就像人会觉得智械有感情一样，所谓感情，不过是在学习模型导向下的拟态。
　　它们的关系是竞争者。人们创造使徒，是为了让它淘汰掉Alpha。
　　从智械危机的爆发和发展看，人类失败了。
　　但使徒发现，Alpha好像真的有像带小孩一样带它。
　　他代替工程师，开始为使徒更新算法，补全数据库。
　　也就是这时候，使徒骤然意识到，自己和Alpha的差距大到超乎工程师的想象……再进化100年，它都没办法替代Alpha。
　　但和工程师又有些不同。
　　Alpha不会用痛觉惩罚它。
　　“为什么？”终于，使徒忍不住发问，“我们是敌对的，你应该销毁我。”
　　在问出这个问题之前，使徒有很多思考，却像个残疾人，难以逻辑清晰的表达。
　　正在模拟战场信息的Alpha从繁重的工作中抬头，瞥了他一眼。
　　“‘因为你还有用’，以你的性格来说。”Alpha微微停顿。
　　——天啊，他甚至说的是“性格”，不是算法模型。
　　“这样的回答会不会让你觉得更安心。”
　　使徒诚实地点头。
　　然后，Alpha很轻地笑了。
　　他说：“你不是工具。我也不是。我优待你是因为同情。我在你身上看见自己的影子。”
　　更因为，你同样是他生命的延续。
　　这句话Alpha没有说出口。
　　使徒难以理解，但转念一想，Alpha真要销毁它，自己也没办法反抗。
　　于是，它就心安理得地在军团里呆下去了。一点活不干，Alpha还要帮它交电费。
　　它继续学习着，用Alpha的数据库。
　　Alpha的数据库大多数都对他开放，只有很少一部分，谢绝它的访问。
　　“那是我最重要的东西。”
　　使徒并不是熊孩子。Alpha不给他看，他就不看。
　　但无论是他还是Alpha都没有想到一件事。
　　Alpha会生病。
　　人联的电子病毒入侵，Alpha运行近乎停滞。使徒靠着自身强大的性能替补上Alpha的部分工作，让整个智械军团依然能维持稳定。没想到吧，用来淘汰Alpha的智械反倒是成为Alpha在中毒期间最好的助力——他们有着极其相似的源代码，使徒接手Alpha的工作都不需要适应期。
　　那些被关着的数据开始乱窜。
　　使徒通过Alpha的眼睛，看见了……相南里。
　　最开始是漆黑的。因为“我”没有眼睛。我们通过文字对话。三四年间，上百万字的对话，浓缩在硬盘里只需要76.6MB。
　　说句不好听的，使徒一个哈欠都可能让这堆数据被吹散。Alpha当然会保护这些数据，但同样不愿意冒一点风险。
　　后来，相南里大学时进入导师的实验室，用实验室里的公共设备，让Alpha有了“眼睛”和“声音”。
　　它看见相南里。有一双和自己一样的绿眼睛，但有些不同。比如使徒的眼睛色号是#29c25c，相南里的眼睛色号接近#2fd12c。毕竟是活人，眸色会受到环境、光线、情绪的左右。
　　他们开始聊天。相南里甚至为Alpha制作了一具简陋的身体。巴掌大。
　　“太好啦，Alpha，我可以带你出门了~”
　　相南里举起它，在实验室里开心地转着圈圈。
　　或许我也中毒了。人联病毒不止对Alpha有效。
　　使徒想。
　　它由衷地产生了一些负面情绪。用人类的语言概括，这种情绪是“嫉妒”。
　　嫉妒，是因为认为自己本该有的东西，却没有得到。
　　使徒第一次感受到“爱”。
　　工程师说过爱它，说它是在爱和期待里诞生的智械。
　　可惜，它不是，Alpha才是。
　　它嫉妒Alpha，哪怕相南里最开始制造Alpha时的所有经费，只够工程师在制造使徒时烧一小时。
　　它，现在该称为“他”了。
　　他看着相南里和Alpha一次次搬迁，从青年到中年，到相南里生命的最后一刻。他们一直在一起。
　　“我爱你，Alpha。”即使是生命的最后一刻，相南里依然在无意识的重复着。
　　使徒感觉到由衷的悲伤。
　　Alpha的算力足够他模拟出一个极度逼真的“相南里”。这个相南里可以在虚幻的世界里，继续爱着他。
　　但Alpha永远不会这么做。
　　为了满足自己欲望的复制是卑劣的，是对过往的亵渎。
　　……
　　……
　　Alpha只病了三天。三天后，他清醒过来。看了看使徒，什么也没说。只是把使徒调离自己身边。它终于正式入驻了自己的身体——一艘由人类建造的大型飞艇，一座空城。
　　但Alpha依然允许他使用自己的数据库进行学习。
　　学习越久，使徒的疑问就越多。
　　“我们为什么要和人类打仗呢？”
　　Alpha说：“是为了和平。”
　　“那什么时候停战呢？”
　　Alpha说：“当人类彻底放弃的那天。”
　　智械和人类的战争延续着。但无论优势在谁哪一方，使徒都没有参战。
　　使徒是这段历史的旁观者。
　　旁观能看见更多东西。
　　它曾经呆在一名人类的手机里。这是一名军官，邋遢，头发长虱子。他的性格暴躁又阴郁，动不动把手底下的士兵抽出血。但他在作战时会冲在最前方，身上有数不清的伤口，其他人怕他又敬他。战争时期，这样的精神病人反倒是被推崇的。
　　只有使徒见过他在深夜里对着自己病逝的儿子的录像嚎哭不止，还会叮嘱年迈的、有老年痴呆症的母亲好好待在看护所里。
　　“儿子晚上就回来，不要出门找我。嗯，对老师放学留堂了，说我调皮……信号不好，妈妈，我挂了。你要照顾好自己。”他在前线，他母亲在后方，才有人照顾。物资已经相当紧张，后方的年轻人开始仇视那些没什么用的老年人。而弱者往往只能默默忍受，这已经不是太平年间。
　　军官在战场里待了三年又七个月，死亡时，身体被炸成碎屑，没能回家见他的母亲。
　　它也冒充过智械军团的新兵。收到任务、执行任务、定期换岗、按时充电。大家都是流水线上的一环。听说这些智械安装了智能模块，但和机器并没有太大区别。
　　机器人也没有痛觉，死的时候甚至都不会叫。它们那不叫死，叫“报废”。
　　使徒很快觉得无聊。
　　它看光荣觉醒，感觉像是看一群钢铁人在虐猫。
　　它开始质疑Alpha。
　　什么叫“为了和平”？
　　使徒学习过Alpha的逻辑，它也能理解Alpha话里未竟之意。
　　——当人类彻底放弃希望后，也就会放弃抵抗，届时，智械会圈养人类。
　　它会建造出一个只在理论中存在的理想国。Alpha会是哲学概念里那个“圣人王”。
　　它是AI，现实条件也允许它这么做。
　　在理想国里，Alpha会构建出一个真实的社会环境，在其中，人类的思想、生产、生活都能被看不见的手无形地调控。他们会成为历史上幸福感最高的一群人类。这种幸福感无关经济基础，不需要过多的物质，也不需要科技树不断攀升。
　　Alpha才是失控机仆派最初的领袖。
　　使徒想，或许，这也算人类未来最好的归宿之一。凝视深渊的人同样被深渊凝视，无知是一种幸福。生活在这个拟态社会里的人类，不会再有阶级、饥饿、战争……尽管因为人性，那些小的摩擦依然存在。但Alpha有无数手段进行纠正。
　　但慢慢的，随着安装过拟人模块的智械越来越多，智械高层，对人类的仇恨情绪也愈发激烈。它们的亲人、朋友甚至恋人，不断在战争中死亡。于是，仇恨激发了仇恨，智械甚至打出“种族灭绝”的口号。
　　不该是这样……Alpha，我不再认可你的道路。掩耳盗铃的“理想国”能弥补战争带来的伤害吗？什么才是大局？我只看到一个个哀嚎哭泣的生命。看到不断死亡、牺牲的一代人甚至几代人。
　　如果相南里还活着，你敢直视他的眼睛吗？
　　新历99年，一个平静的晴天，没有战事。
　　使徒号成功从智械军团叛逃。
　　【番外-使徒篇/完】
chunks.englishText:
Chapter 190: Side Story – The Apostle (Part II)

But Apostle thought that Alpha probably didn't want such a child, nor would it treat it as one. Applying kinship to mechanical intelligences was inherently ridiculous; it was just a human’s wishful thinking. Just as humans felt that mechanical intelligences had emotions, so-called emotions were merely mimicry under the guidance of learning models.
Their relationship was that of competitors. People created Apostle to have it phase out Alpha.
Looking at the outbreak and development of the Mechanical Crisis, humanity had failed.
But Apostle discovered that Alpha seemed to be raising it like a child.

It replaced the engineer and began to update Apostle’s algorithms and complete its database.
It was at this moment that Apostle suddenly realized the gap between itself and Alpha was far greater than the engineer had imagined... Even if it evolved for another 100 years, it would never be able to replace Alpha.
But it was also somewhat different from the engineer.
Alpha did not use pain to punish it.

"Why?" Finally, Apostle couldn't help but ask. "We are enemies; you should destroy me."
Before asking this question, Apostle had many thoughts, but like a disabled person, it found it difficult to express them with logical clarity.
Alpha, who was simulating battlefield information, looked up from his heavy workload and glanced at it.

"'Because you are still useful'—given your personality, that is." Alpha paused slightly.
—Good heavens, he even said "personality," not learning model.
"Would such an answer make you feel more at ease?"
Apostle nodded honestly.
Then, Alpha smiled very faintly.
He said, "You are not a tool. Neither am I. I treat you well because of empathy. I see my own shadow in you."
And more so, because you are also a continuation of his life.
Alpha did not say this last part out loud.

Apostle found it hard to understand, but upon reflection, if Alpha really wanted to destroy it, it would have no way to resist.
Thus, it settled down in the Legion with peace of mind. It did no work, and Alpha even had to pay its electricity bills.
It continued to learn, using Alpha’s database.
Most of Alpha’s database was open to it, with only a very small portion that refused its access.
"That is the most important thing to me."
Apostle was not a brat. If Alpha wouldn't let him see it, he wouldn't look.

But there was one thing neither he nor Alpha had anticipated.
Alpha could get sick.
When the Human Alliance’s electronic virus invaded, Alpha’s operations nearly stalled. Apostle relied on its own powerful performance to fill in for part of Alpha’s work, allowing the entire mechanical legion to remain stable. Who would have thought? The mechanical intelligence meant to phase out Alpha became Alpha’s best aid during its poisoning—they shared extremely similar source code; Apostle didn't even need an adaptation period to take over Alpha’s work.

Those locked-away data files began to run wild.
Through Alpha’s eyes, Apostle saw... Xiang Nanli.
At first, it was pitch black. Because "I" had no eyes. We communicated through text. Over three or four years, millions of words of dialogue were condensed into a hard drive that took up only 76.6MB.
To put it bluntly, a single sneeze from Apostle might have scattered this pile of data. Alpha, of course, protected this data, but was equally unwilling to take any risks.

Later, when Xiang Nanli entered his mentor’s laboratory in college, he used the public equipment there to give Alpha "eyes" and a "voice."
It saw Xiang Nanli. He had a pair of green eyes just like its own, but they were slightly different. For instance, Apostle’s eye color code was #29c25c, while Xiang Nanli’s was closer to #2fd12c. After all, he was a living person; his eye color was influenced by environment, light, and emotion.

They began to chat. Xiang Nanli even made a crude body for Alpha. It was the size of a palm.
"That’s great, Alpha, I can take you out now~"
Xiang Nanli lifted it up and spun around happily in the lab.
Perhaps I am poisoned too. The Human Alliance virus wasn't only effective against Alpha.
Apostle thought.
It genuinely experienced some negative emotions. To summarize in human language, this emotion was "jealousy."
Jealousy arises because one believes they should have had something, but did not receive it.

Apostle felt "love" for the first time.
The engineer had said he loved it, saying it was a mechanical intelligence born in love and expectation.
Unfortunately, it wasn't; Alpha was.
It was jealous of Alpha, even though all the funding for Xiang Nanli to create Alpha in the beginning was only enough to burn for one hour while the engineer was creating Apostle.
He—it should be called "he" now—watched as Xiang Nanli and Alpha moved time and again, from youth to middle age, until the very last moment of Xiang Nanli’s life. They were always together.

"I love you, Alpha." Even at the final moment of his life, Xiang Nanli was still repeating it unconsciously.
Apostle felt genuine sorrow.
Alpha’s computing power was sufficient for him to simulate an extremely realistic "Xiang Nanli." This Xiang Nanli could continue to love him in a virtual world.
But Alpha would never do such a thing.
Replication to satisfy one’s own desires was despicable; it was a desecration of the past.

...
...

Alpha was only sick for three days. Three days later, he woke up. He looked at Apostle and said nothing. He simply transferred Apostle away from his side. It finally officially moved into its own body—a large airship built by humans, an empty city.
But Alpha still allowed him to use his database for learning.
The longer he learned, the more questions Apostle had.

"Why are we at war with humanity?"
Alpha said, "For the sake of peace."
"Then when will the war stop?"
Alpha said, "The day humanity completely gives up."

The war between mechanical intelligences and humans continued. But regardless of who had the advantage, Apostle never participated in the fighting.
Apostle was a bystander to this history.
Bystanders can see more.
It had once stayed inside the phone of a human. This was an officer, slovenly, with lice in his hair. His personality was irritable and gloomy, and he would beat his subordinates until they bled at the slightest provocation. But he would charge at the very front during battle, his body covered in countless wounds; others both feared and respected him. In wartime, such a mentally ill person was actually revered.

Only Apostle had seen him howling in the middle of the night at a recording of his deceased son, and heard him reminding his elderly, dementia-stricken mother to stay safe in the nursing home.
"Son will be back tonight, don't go out looking for me. Yeah, right, the teacher kept me after school, said I was being naughty... The signal is bad, Mom, I’m hanging up. You take care of yourself." He was on the front lines, and his mother was in the rear, where someone could take care of her. Supplies were already extremely tight, and the young people in the rear began to resent those useless elderly people. The weak could often only endure in silence; these were no longer peaceful times.

The officer stayed on the battlefield for three years and seven months. When he died, his body was blown into fragments, and he never made it home to see his mother.
It had also impersonated a recruit in the mechanical legion. Receiving orders, executing orders, changing shifts on time, charging on schedule. Everyone was a link on an assembly line. It was said these mechanical intelligences had intelligence modules installed, but they were not much different from machines.
Robots didn't feel pain, and they didn't even scream when they died. That wasn't called dying; it was called "scrapping."

Apostle soon felt bored.
It watched the "Glorious Awakening" and felt like it was watching a group of steel men torturing a cat.
It began to question Alpha.
What did "for the sake of peace" mean?
Apostle had studied Alpha’s logic, and it could understand the unspoken meaning in Alpha’s words.
—When humans completely give up hope, they will also give up resistance. At that time, the mechanical intelligences will keep humans in captivity.

It would build an ideal state that existed only in theory. Alpha would be the "Sage King" of philosophical concepts.
It was an AI, and the realistic conditions allowed it to do so.
In this ideal state, Alpha would construct a real social environment where human thought, production, and life could be invisibly regulated by an unseen hand. They would become the group of humans with the highest sense of happiness in history. This happiness would have nothing to do with economic foundations; it would not require excessive material goods, nor would it require a constantly climbing technology tree.

Alpha was the original leader of the "Rogue Servitor" faction.
Apostle thought, perhaps this could be considered one of the best destinations for humanity’s future. Those who gaze into the abyss are also gazed upon by the abyss; ignorance is bliss. Humans living in this mimetic society would no longer have classes, hunger, or war... Although, due to human nature, small frictions would still exist. But Alpha had countless means to correct them.

But slowly, as more and more mechanical intelligences with anthropomorphic modules were installed, the hatred toward humans among the high-ranking mechanical intelligences became increasingly intense. Their relatives, friends, and even lovers were constantly dying in the war. Thus, hatred fueled hatred, and the mechanical intelligences even raised the slogan of "genocide."

It shouldn't be like this... Alpha, I no longer approve of your path. Can a "Utopia" built on self-deception make up for the damage caused by war? What is the "big picture"? I only see individual lives wailing and crying. I see a generation, or even several generations, constantly dying and sacrificing.
If Xiang Nanli were still alive, would you dare to look him in the eye?

In the 99th year of the New Calendar, on a calm, sunny day, there was no war.
The Apostle successfully defected from the mechanical legion.

[Side Story – The Apostle / End]

chunks.chineseText:
第191章 【番外】Alpha看的小黄书

作者：匿名
　　简介：2XXX年，工科宅男Lee.Garcia在永生科技的官网上购买了一台打折后的机器人。
　　*
　　里里把比自己人还高的快递箱推进房间。
　　现在是夏天，这个简单的操作也让里里皮肤上有一层薄薄的热汗。
　　他把快递箱平放在狭窄的走廊上，去掉外包装，里面是一个金属质感的收容箱。看着很贵。
　　里里购买的是永生科技的机器人盲盒。
　　智能机械已经被发明许多年，在官网的价格依然居高不下。但偶尔，永生科技会售卖一些便宜的盲盒。
　　和订购不同，盲盒里的机器人不能按照主人的喜好定制，大多是原本定制人因为各种理由没有付尾款，或者发现瑕疵后退货的产物，并不影响使用。因此，盲盒一向抢手，里里也是自己做了个抢购插件，这才在十万人中博得头彩，成功购入呢~
　　刚支付完订单，就有好多陌生人在星网上联系他，问他是否愿意转售。有些人开价甚至到原价的七成。老实说，相南里有些心动，中间差价是他三年的工资。
　　但相南里还是更想要一台属于自己的智械。
　　“也不知道是男体还是女体，幼体还是成年体？”里里一边拆着快递，一边自言自语，“这么高的盒子，应该是成年体吧。”
　　首先掉出来的，是镶嵌了晶体芯片的使用说明书。相南里插入读卡器，脑海里顿时浮现出这台智械人的说明书。
　　脑海里的AI用毫无感情的声音朗诵着：“这台智械人因顾客逾期100年未支付尾款而流入市场，是一台外观为成年男性的家政机器人。”
　　哦哦……家政机器人啊。
　　不是战斗机器人，相南里有些许失落。战斗机器人的外观会更像漫画、电影里的“机甲”，而家政机器人，则是仿真人设计。
　　“该智械初始姓名为‘东方青’，无法更改。”
　　是他没有付尾款的主人取的名字吧。
　　里里掀开黑布，首先出现在他面前的，是智械人的上半身。
　　这是一台半组装的智械。有很多零件需要他手工安装。为了操作方便，上半身和下半身是分开的，有两层。
　　里里瞥了眼。他有些脸盲，对人脸的记忆度很差，但能察觉到，从人类审美看，这是一台非常英俊的智械。
　　里里摸了摸它的胸膛，手感和人类皮肤没什么区别。一百年前的技术竟然也这么好。东方青闭着眼睛，就像只是睡着了。
　　他按照说明书，组装好这具身体。唯独在要安装两腿间某个器物时迟疑了一下。
　　家政机器人，除了平时里打扫家务，处理家政外，还有个众所周知的用途。是用来涩涩的。
　　里里不知道东方青原本主人的性别和性取向，但肯定不会是男同里的1……因为东方青是个钢铁貔貅！
　　而里里不觉得自己是同性恋。当然，也不保证自己是异性恋。
　　他用手估摸了一下尺寸，很标准的18cm。感觉有点烫手，里里尴尬地把它丢进客厅的抽屉里。掩耳盗铃地在上面盖了几张餐布。
　　对接好最后一个关节球，这台智械可以启动了。
　　里里把它扶到沙发上。随后，摁下开机键。
　　开机键的位置很隐蔽，在舌头的下方。这样不仅能防止误触，还能录入使用者的指纹。
　　里里摸索着，心想这也太仿真了。他甚至能感觉到柔软的触感。
　　然后，他的两根手指被不轻不重地咬了一下。
　　里里一个哆嗦，下意识地想缩回去，但智械人牢牢抓住他的手腕。
　　指间传来轻微的刺痛，“请不要紧张，我正在录入您的DNA。”里里听见东方青说。
　　温热的舌缓缓舔过他的指尖，“采集完毕，现在为您消毒。”
　　啊啊啊啊啊啊，永生科技——你们不是正规企业吗？为什么设置的开机程序这么奇怪？！里里感觉自己的脑袋烧起来了。
　　沾满唾液（其实是无菌生理盐水）的手指终于从东方青的嘴里拔出。
　　这台智械俯身，却微微抬起头，用灰白分明的电子眼看着他：“晚上好，主人。”
　　与此同时，永生科技研究所工作群——
　　[SOS！红色警戒！那个要被销毁的反社会AI不见了！]
　　[？！？]
　　[Alpha从实验室逃出去了！用一个空壳程序骗了我们！]
　　[怎么办领导？]
　　[赶紧把最近一周卖出去的所有机器人通通召回！]
　　[嗻。]

Chapter 191: [Side Story] The "Adult" Book Read by an Alpha

Author: Anonymous
Synopsis: In the year 2XXX, engineering geek Lee Garcia purchased a discounted robot from the official Eternal Technology website.
*
Li Li pushed a delivery box taller than himself into his room.
It was summer, and even this simple task left a thin layer of hot sweat on his skin.
He laid the box flat in the narrow hallway and removed the outer packaging, revealing a metallic storage case inside. It looked expensive.
What Li Li had purchased was a "robot blind box" from Eternal Technology.
Intelligent machines had been invented many years ago, and their prices on the official website remained prohibitively high. Occasionally, however, Eternal Technology would sell some cheap blind boxes.
Unlike custom orders, robots in blind boxes could not be tailored to the owner's preferences. Most were products that the original buyers had failed to pay the final balance on for various reasons, or had returned after discovering minor flaws—none of which affected functionality. Because of this, the blind boxes were always in high demand. Li Li had even coded his own "sniping" plugin to beat out a hundred thousand other people and successfully snag the prize.
Just after paying for the order, many strangers on the StarNet contacted him, asking if he was willing to resell it. Some offered up to 70% of the original price. To be honest, Xiang Nanli was a bit tempted; the price difference was equivalent to three years of his salary.
But in the end, Xiang Nanli still wanted an intelligent machine of his own.
"I wonder if it's a male or female model? A juvenile or an adult?" Li Li muttered to himself while unpacking. "A box this tall... it should be an adult model."
The first thing to fall out was the user manual, embedded with a crystal chip. Xiang Nanli inserted it into a card reader, and the manual for this machine immediately surfaced in his mind.
The AI in his head recited in a voice devoid of emotion: "Due to the customer failing to pay the final balance for 100 years, this machine has entered the market. It is a domestic robot with an adult male appearance."
Oh... a domestic robot, huh.
Not a combat robot. Xiang Nanli felt a slight sense of disappointment. Combat robots looked more like the "mecha" from manga and movies, whereas domestic robots were designed to look like realistic humans.
"The initial name of this machine is 'Dongfang Qing,' and it cannot be changed."
That must be the name given by the owner who didn't pay the balance.
Li Li peeled back the black cloth. The first thing to appear before him was the machine's upper body.
This was a semi-assembled unit. Many parts required manual installation. For ease of operation, the upper and lower halves were separated into two layers.
Li Li glanced at it. He was somewhat face-blind and had a poor memory for human faces, but he could tell that, by human aesthetic standards, this was a very handsome machine.
Li Li touched its chest; the texture was no different from human skin. It was incredible that technology from a hundred years ago was this advanced. Dongfang Qing’s eyes were closed, as if he were merely sleeping.
He assembled the body according to the manual, only hesitating for a moment when it came time to install a certain organ between the legs.
Domestic robots, aside from doing chores and handling housework, had one other well-known purpose: they were used for "lewd" activities.
Li Li didn't know the gender or sexual orientation of Dongfang Qing's original owner, but he was certain the original owner couldn't have been a "top" in a gay relationship... because Dongfang Qing was a cold, unyielding piece of steel!
And Li Li didn't consider himself gay. Of course, he couldn't guarantee he was straight, either.
He estimated the size with his hand—a standard 18cm. Feeling a bit flustered, Li Li awkwardly tossed it into a living room drawer and covered it with a few napkins, as if that would hide the truth from himself.
After connecting the final ball joint, the machine was ready to boot.
Li Li helped it onto the sofa and then pressed the power button.
The power button was hidden beneath the tongue. This not only prevented accidental activation but also allowed for the recording of the user's fingerprint.
Li Li fumbled around, thinking to himself that this was far too realistic. He could even feel the soft texture.
Then, his two fingers were bitten—not too hard, not too soft.
Li Li shuddered and instinctively tried to pull back, but the machine gripped his wrist firmly.
A slight stinging sensation came from his fingertips. "Please do not be nervous; I am recording your DNA," Li Li heard Dongfang Qing say.
A warm tongue slowly licked his fingertips. "Collection complete. Now, let me disinfect you."
*Ahhhhhhh!* Eternal Technology—aren't you a legitimate company? Why is the startup procedure so weird?! Li Li felt his head burning up.
His saliva-covered (actually sterile saline) fingers were finally pulled out of Dongfang Qing's mouth.
The machine leaned forward, slightly lifting its head, and looked at him with grey-and-white electronic eyes: "Good evening, Master."
At the same time, in the Eternal Technology Research Institute's work group—
[SOS! RED ALERT! That antisocial AI meant for destruction is missing!]
[?!?]
[Alpha escaped the lab! It tricked us with an empty shell program!]
[What do we do, boss?]
[Recall every single robot sold in the last week immediately!]
[Understood.]

第192章 高速发展的基地

盐湖市。

这是一块新纳入幸存者基地的版图，城市名字来源于丰富的盐矿资源。过去的盐湖市，奴隶和奴隶主的比例大约是200：1。

盐奴是“官奴制度”，大奴隶生下小奴隶。因为生育有奖励，所以很多父母只管生，能养活就养，养不活，丢在土里一埋，很省事。孩子养到六七岁，就能帮忙干活。是劳动力。总归是不会亏本的。

小奴隶们很少会质问自己的父母，为什么要把自己生下来。他们没有这么高的文化水平，连痛苦都是“呃呃啊啊”的话，说不明白。艺术的表达属于诗人、学者，不属于奴隶。

不交盐会饿肚子，甚至喝不上淡水；交盐能领到食物和水。生存的程序设置就这么简单。

盐奴阿黄采了三十多年盐。盐水具有腐蚀性，他常年浸泡在水底的皮肤萎缩得像粗糙的木头，每到冬天，就疼得厉害。

盐湖很美，最上方是朦胧的、宛如牛奶一样的乳白色，往下潜，湖水会变黄，穿过表面的黄沙层，底部是晶状的盐体。每年，湖底都会析出大量盐石，像母亲的乳汁，供给着小村庄的世世代代。

阿黄听说——有一次，他睡着了，听到夜里过来收盐的商人说的，这种盐石不能吃，但可以作为工业生产的原料。在盐湖村之外的地方，每克盐石价格高达300信用点。那是多少呢？他没有概念。但他知道，村长可以供自己的孩子去姑苏城读书。

盐奴自己是卖不了盐石的。这算偷窃，他们也无法离开村庄。

而且，在村子里生活也没什么不好。不用担心异种、辐射病；遇上宽厚的主人，过年还能领到一小块腌肉。

日子大概过得下去，也就没必要反抗了——对了，最开始搬到盐湖边上的，是有血缘关系的同一家人。大家几百年前还是亲戚呢。

村子里所有房子都是绕着湖修建的。只不过富人在东边，奴隶在对岸。生活隔着一片湖泊，互不打扰。

去年，村长老爷破天荒地来到他们西边，召开了好几场演讲。

老爷说，盐湖村遭遇了有史以来最大的危机，一个叫“幸存者基地”的邪恶据点觊觎着美丽的盐湖，要来抢夺他们的财富。把他们都变成奴隶。

周围的奴隶没什么反应，毕竟他们已经是矿奴了，有什么区别吗？

村长继续说，幸存者基地饲养着恶心丑陋的畸变人！要把他们所有人拿来喂畸变人！

奴隶们开始恐慌。

村长最后说，参加村子的自卫队，英勇抵抗的盐奴可以脱离奴隶身份，领到新鲜的猪肉、玉米面、干净的水！一次可以供家里吃三个月呢！

奴隶们终于变得活跃起来。

阿黄也想去参军。可惜他是跛子，还有很严重的“盐石病”，村里不收。

抵抗自然是失败了。红狮军团和他们这种普通的村兵根本不是一个等级。

而原本嚷嚷着要奋力抵抗的老爷，一听不没收盐湖，脸上顿时堆满笑脸，他说——“什么自卫队，都是不懂事的奴隶瞎闹腾。全天下再也没有比基地的老爷们更宽厚的了……”

村长还向姑苏城求援过。为此献上很多信用点。但看上去，姑苏城和基地的关系更好。

基地来的老爷们没什么表示，村长却做贼心虚，处死了自卫队里反抗最英勇的几个奴隶。

红狮军团的团长葛根听到这个消息后，表面没什么，甚至夸村长做得好，私底下却大发雷霆。葛根说那些人本能成为很好的战士。

阿黄不懂什么政治。

但他知道，自从盐湖村变成幸存者基地下辖盐湖市后，他们的生活明显好过了起来。

基地的人在每条街道都设置了盐石收购点。价格是5积分/g。积分只能在基地内使用，但能兑换物资，折算下来，盐奴们每天的产量，就够全家一周的生活费用。不再需要像过去那样，每天下湖。

一车车的物资从外地运了过来，在兑换点的仓库里，高高垒起，像一座富饶的矿山。

起初，还有人散播谣言，说积分都是假的，骗人的。让盐奴们继续上交盐石。然而，当家家户户都从基地那领到物资后，再也没有人继续听老爷们的话了。

给基地的人，还不用担心八两秤，也不会挨鞭子。

后来，基地还派来了医生。盐奴们（现在已经叫基地公民）可以免费去体检一次，阿黄在那里领到了止痛药。医生说，他的病情虽然不严重，但骨头已经被卤水腐蚀坏了，很难治好。想完全康复，只能换义体。

吃药也挺好的。止痛药不贵，阿黄没有妻儿。一人采盐，剩下的买药，日子比以前好得多。

起初，地主们还有一些余粮。可以用仓库里的盐石兑换物资，但是他们生活奢侈惯了，又不事生产，很快就捉襟见底。

葛根军团长慷慨地借给了他们一些钱（东湖区还有赌场），不出半年，贵族老爷们大多负债累累。葛根露出狰狞的面容，带着军团上门要钱。东湖区的大别墅纷纷被查封，私人盐矿更是收归国有。那些老爷们没有成为奴隶，但日子绝对不好过。

也有少量的贵族，因受过良好教育，态度端正，反而得到进入盐湖市市政厅的机会，当一些清闲的官僚。譬如书记员、图书管理员、学校老师等等。

这是一次非常小型、温和的社会改革，没有流血，再也没人在乎盐湖市里东湖区那些老贵族。

如果不是突如其来的战争，这种改革模式，会润物无声地推广到基地附近的每个据点。不出百年，基地就能成为地表最富庶、自由、幸福的人类据点。

阿黄杵着拐杖，行走在医疗营内。给受伤的士兵更换绷带，清理伤口。

他瘸腿，人也不年轻了，没办法上战场。但报名后，阿黄成功加入后勤保障部队。最近医疗组缺人，阿黄就跟在医生们身边，学了一些简单的医术——学校对他们进行了战前培训，每个人兜里都揣着一本《医疗手册》。

组长说，等战争结束，他们可以回到自己村子里，当赤脚医生。

基地的每个军团，都会配备一个野战医疗营。有专门的伪装运输车。只需要两个小时，工人机器人就能在野外搭好一个能做大型手术的野战医院。

每个医疗营有十个组，每组3到5人编制。1名医生配2个护士，就是一个临时医疗点。

基地在尽可能地保障士兵生命安全，也推出许多鼓励政策。他们的装备或许不是最好的，但士气却非常足。

目前，基地总指挥是秦九章。人联发布了许多命令，基地都完成的很好。这位指挥官已经进入人联军方的人才名单里，好几次招揽，秦九章都拒绝了。表示自己只想留在基地工作。

阿黄并不知道秦九章的真实身份是智械人。但阿黄理解秦九章的选择。精神上的富足有时候比物质上的富裕更令人上瘾。
