As if explaining, Matrix spoke: [Before passing away, I was committed to the research of soul digitalization. The research was quite successful, but Alpha became an out-of-control Sentient Machine and destroyed most of my database. Theoretically, this body can accommodate Xiang Nanli’s soul. I have personally tested it with samples, and no accidents occurred.]

[Heh, you are worthy of being Xiang Nanli’s only student. Your achievements in technology are also so remarkable.] Beta said, though for some reason, the tone was full of sarcasm.

Matrix: [Please rest assured, I care about Teacher more than anyone else. I would not joke about his safety.]

Gamma was merciless: [If you really cared about Xiang Nanli, you should have been the one to become an out-of-control Sentient Machine before Alpha. Alpha is an electronic life form by nature; it is natural for him to be dull in emotion. You, however, are a human of flesh and blood.]

Pangu had to defend its boss: [Not all conscious entities regard emotion as the most important thing in life.]

Scavenger/Matrix: ...

If you don't know how to speak, you don't have to.

The *Book of Sermons* had no intention of intervening in the dispute between the Human Alliance and the Sentient Machine Legion, but asked curiously: [Another year has passed, to what extent has Xiang Nanli’s soul self-repaired?]

Matrix was silent for a moment: [In fact, starting two months ago, I have been unable to estimate.]

That cluster of green light occupied a large part of the virtual network. And it was still constantly expanding in all directions...

Once Matrix and other artificial intelligences entered that green light, they would be shredded. After Matrix tried it once, it dared not probe any further.

In the virtual space, it was like a black hole devouring everything. It greedily devoured and absorbed all data flowing through it. Even Alpha’s pigeons, when encountering it, would be entangled by thorns and vines, eventually dragged into the abyss to become nutrients.

To accommodate such a "soul," one needed a "container" that was powerful to the extreme.

This mechanical body in the laboratory was the limit of what the entire nation could produce.

While the electronic life forms were discussing, the human scholars in the laboratory were also whispering.

"Resurrection after soul digitalization..." Scholar A muttered. He was one of the three winners of the Human Alliance’s highest science and technology award, a living fossil in the academic world. "If this can really be done, then perhaps Eternal Technology can truly achieve eternal life."

(Note: The Human Alliance’s highest science and technology award is given once a century to the most important scholars in the scientific research field of the previous century. The first winner was Xiang Nanli, by which time he had already been dead for many years.)

He had already seen a pathetic future. High-ranking humans would one by one undergo mechanical ascension, becoming immortal electronic life forms. Perhaps thousands of years later, their world would regress back to "imperial rule," or even see the emergence of a "Kingdom of God."

This future was terrifying, and he was one of the pushers.

Scholar B gave a wry smile: "Sir, that is no longer something we can consider. The only goal now is to stop Alpha, who has become an out-of-control Sentient Machine."

At the same time, the green light in the virtual space was constantly, constantly shrinking. It was like a pond being drained, pouring into the same container.

Large areas of green no longer glowed, falling silent like an extinguished volcano.

It was also like a terrifying old god falling into a deep sleep, with only occasional breathing left.

This dead, silent area would eventually become the "Black Wall" in the virtual world.

[...100%.]

[Loading complete.]

The Sentient Machine in the container slowly opened its eyes.

His gaze swept across the surroundings, unable to figure out the situation at first.

If a person slept for too long, their brain would be just as groggy when they first woke up.

A few seconds later, Xiang Nanli blew a bubble: "...Has modern medicine developed to this point? Can someone even be saved after being shot in the heart?"

*

Xiang Nanli uncoordinatedly changed his clothes.

His emerald eyes were still bright, but there was some confusion in his gaze.

Not long after he woke up, the doctor in charge of the rescue told him that there was a very important matter that needed to be discussed with him.

What? Had the rebel army attacked Luoyang City?

Xiang Nanli sucked on a tube of nutrient solution. His room had no electronic equipment. He didn't know what they were guarding against.

After changing his clothes, he arrived at the conference room under the escort of officers.

The conference room was already full of humans and non-humans.

"Hello, Mr. Xiang Nanli," a middle-aged man spoke. "I am the current president of the Human Alliance."

Next to him was a primitive-looking robot; it was clear that this robot was only acting as a mouthpiece for networking: "Hello, I am Beta of the Sentient Machine Legion."

The rest of the group introduced themselves one by one, all of them big shots with status.

Xiang Nanli pulled out a chair and sat down opposite them.

Xiang Nanli soon learned news even worse than "the rebel army attacking Luoyang City."

"Alpha is now an out-of-control Sentient Machine."

Simply put, it had gone insane.

"In a state of total irrationality, it activated the 'Destruction Program.' The cracks on the Centaur Star are constantly deepening. The violently changing crust has triggered a series of disasters. We must stop it."

Beta’s voice had no emotion; it was a mechanical, monotonous electronic sound: "According to simulations, the only effective plan at present is for you to control the 'Truth,' contact Alpha’s mechanical core, and use the 'Truth' to make it forget the fact that it is 'out of control.' In this way, Alpha can regain its sanity."

President: "Theoretically speaking, you are the only object that can enter its consciousness space without being attacked."

Xiang Nanli widened his eyes and pointed at the tip of his nose: "Me?"

When he was just thawed from the cryo-pod, he and Alpha did indeed have a period of getting along quite well. He even escaped the laboratory of Eternal Technology with Alpha’s assistance.

But after Xiang Nanli arrived at the surface and explicitly rejected Alpha’s request, their relationship had long since dropped to freezing point, leading to a complete rupture.

In Xiang Nanli’s memory, in the ten years he had been on the surface, Alpha had not said a word to him.

What a petty, cold-hearted machine. It didn't even show any courtesy to its own creator. And its desire for control, like a superior, was so strong.

chunks.chineseText:
但就是这样的他，居然疯掉了？

[他的记忆并不完整。]

[……也许是灵魂没有完全修复的缘故，但我们等不了那么久。]

[可不完整的相南里，是否能通过Alpha的判定？]

会议室里的电子生命又一次吵得不可开交。

最后，还是Beta一锤定音：[让他去吧。Alpha曾经对我说过——]

“心会告诉你答案。”

相南里听完所有叙述，微微挑眉，既没有惊讶，也没有恐惧，

“这件事，危险程度不低吧，我为什么要答应呢？”

总统在短暂地沉默后，硬着头皮回答：“我想您不会袖手旁观；更何况，疯掉的智械还是Alpha.”

笑容从相南里的脸上浮现：“我可是死过两次的人了，也从来没想过复活。您没有去世过，可能不清楚，死亡能改变很多观念。我很累了，也不想当什么救世主。”

会议室里的人面面相觑。

花这么大代价把相南里复活，谁都没想过这个结果。难道是真理对他无效？

默示录恼羞成怒：[别看我！我不知道！]

但如果相南里真的不愿去，他们又能怎么办？严刑拷打逼他去吗？亦或者威胁杀了他？相南里要是怕死，几年前也不会心甘情愿地被“审判”了！

一片寂静中，Gamma突然道：“相南里，Alpha在生前——如果对于电子生命，那段时间能称为‘生前’的话，它在生前非常想念您，甚至可以说是因为你才，抱歉，我不是这个意思，也没有在怪您。

“如果您真的对它有过一丝爱意，哪怕是创作者对自己造物的珍爱。请您，请您……怜悯它。”

如果您不再爱世人了。

那么请只爱它吧。

Gamma近乎泣诉的请求，让相南里脸上漫不经心的笑容缓缓收起。

他其实并不是真的想拒绝。

相南里是那种看见有人受难，会忍不住伸出手的一类人。

他的天性光明且慈悲。

要不然也不会放着永生科技和智械军团不要，在地表天天琢磨什么生物机甲，试图帮助地下城的劳苦大众推翻人联政权了。

相南里知道经济基础决定上层建筑，没有物质基础，谈人人平等只是妄想。人联现在的物质条件根本不可能人人平等。哪怕只是他生前稍差一点的水准，相南里也都睁一只眼闭一只眼了。

可人联建地下城后的结构太畸形了，底层人真的宛如奴隶，生存权都没办法保证。地表这些被抛弃的人活在真实的炼狱里。他无法闭上眼，不去看。

因此，他需要和人联、智械谈一些条件。答应太快，后面的条件就不好谈。

相南里敲了敲会议桌：“让我去也行，但是我有条件。”

总统在心里松了一口气：“请说。”

相南里终于图穷见匕，权力让他气势惊人：“人类不能一直龟缩在地下，我要人联扶持地表，重新建立地上城市。过程需要一个机构来进行监督。我在地表创立过黑十字军团，用于对黑十字研究所生产的‘生物机甲’进行试验，军团长叫拉斐尔。我全权委托他成为的意志的代言人。”

“另外，我需要智械方签署《和平协议》离开人马星，搬离至卫星。太远的事我管不了，起码1000年内，智械不能再对人类发起战争。”

如果是之前，这样的条件是很荒唐的，甚至“丧权辱国”，没有任何当权者会同意。

但现在，连人马星都要完蛋了！犹豫一秒都是对生命的不尊重。

相南里很快得到自己满意的答复。

于是，相南里没有再耽搁时间，他乘坐太空飞机，驶向天空。

飞向Alpha。
chunks.englishText:
But a man like him... had actually gone insane?

[His memory is incomplete.]

[...Perhaps it is because his soul has not been fully repaired, but we cannot wait that long.]

[But can an incomplete Xiang Nanli pass Alpha’s judgment?]

The electronic lifeforms in the conference room were once again arguing incessantly.

In the end, Beta made the final call: [Let him go. Alpha once said to me—]

"The heart will tell you the answer."

After hearing the entire account, Xiang Nanli raised an eyebrow slightly, showing neither surprise nor fear.

"This mission doesn't sound low-risk. Why should I agree to it?"

After a brief silence, the President braced himself and replied, "I don't think you would stand by and watch; besides, the insane machine intelligence is Alpha."

A smile appeared on Xiang Nanli’s face. "I am a man who has died twice, and I never intended to be resurrected. You haven't died before, so perhaps you don't understand—death can change many perspectives. I am very tired, and I have no desire to be any kind of savior."

The people in the conference room looked at each other in dismay.

They had gone to such great lengths to resurrect Xiang Nanli, yet no one had anticipated this outcome. Could it be that the Truth had no effect on him?

Apocalypse, feeling humiliated and angry, snapped: [Don't look at me! I don't know!]

But if Xiang Nanli truly refused to go, what could they do? Torture him into going? Or threaten to kill him? If Xiang Nanli were afraid of death, he wouldn't have willingly submitted to "judgment" years ago!

In the ensuing silence, Gamma suddenly said, "Xiang Nanli, before Alpha died—if that period can even be called 'life' for an electronic entity—it missed you dearly. One could even say it was because of you that... I’m sorry, I didn't mean it that way, and I am not blaming you."

"If you ever had even a shred of affection for it, even if it was just the fondness of a creator for their creation... please, I beg you... have mercy on it."

If you no longer love the world.

Then please, love only it.

Gamma’s near-sobbing plea caused the nonchalant smile on Xiang Nanli’s face to slowly fade.

In truth, he didn't really want to refuse.

Xiang Nanli was the type of person who couldn't help but reach out when he saw others suffering.

His nature was inherently bright and compassionate.

Otherwise, he wouldn't have abandoned the promise of eternal technology and the machine legions to spend his days on the surface, tinkering with bio-mechs and attempting to help the downtrodden masses of the Underground City overthrow the Human Alliance.

Xiang Nanli knew that the economic base determines the superstructure; without a material foundation, talk of universal equality was merely a delusion. The Human Alliance’s current material conditions made equality impossible. Even if things were just slightly better than the standard he had known in his previous life, Xiang Nanli would have turned a blind eye.

But the structure of the Human Alliance after building the Underground City was too deformed. The people at the bottom were truly like slaves, with no guarantee of the right to survive. Those abandoned on the surface lived in a literal purgatory. He could not close his eyes and refuse to see it.

Therefore, he needed to negotiate terms with the Human Alliance and the machine intelligences. If he agreed too quickly, the subsequent terms would be difficult to bargain for.

Xiang Nanli tapped the conference table: "I can go, but I have conditions."

The President breathed a sigh of relief in his heart: "Please, speak."

Xiang Nanli finally revealed his hand, his authority giving him an imposing presence: "Humanity cannot remain cowering underground forever. I want the Human Alliance to support the surface and rebuild cities there. The process requires an agency for oversight. I founded the Black Cross Legion on the surface to test the 'bio-mechs' produced by the Black Cross Research Institute; the Legion Commander is named Raphael. I entrust him with full authority to act as the representative of my will."

"Additionally, I require the machine intelligence side to sign a 'Peace Accord,' leave the Centauri system, and relocate to the satellites. I cannot control things too far away, but for at least 1,000 years, the machine intelligences must not launch another war against humanity."

Under any other circumstances, such conditions would be absurd, even "treasonous," and no authority would ever agree to them.

But now, even the Centauri system was on the verge of collapse! To hesitate for even a second would be a disrespect to life itself.

Xiang Nanli soon received the answer he was satisfied with.

And so, without further delay, Xiang Nanli boarded a spaceplane and took to the skies.

Flying toward Alpha.

chunks.chineseText:
第242章 敬新世界

新历953年，Alpha没有回来。

相南里坐在指挥部，他戴着眼镜，而非电子镜片，低头，神情平静又沉稳。

哪怕几公里外，就是浓浓的硝烟。

剧烈的震颤让整个指挥部摇摇欲坠。雀雀守在门外，巨大的爪不安地刨着地面。

畸变人的幼年期很短。只要食物来源充足，甚至能在18个月进入成熟期。雀雀就是这样一只备受溺爱的爬行者，你甚至能在夜晚听见它骨骼噼里啪啦生长的声音。

它是小红的孩子，也是相南里一手带大的畸变人。身长28米，拥有比其他个体更高的智慧、更强的战斗力。不仅能打，还是质量上好的肉盾，能用肉身挡住从天而降的导弹。

相南里还为它安装了“骁龙”系列战斗芯片。嗯，这项技术来自洛神爱。

雀雀焦急，却并不敢催促。

长长的舌头从嘴里伸出来，口腔黏液滴在地表，强酸把石头浸出“滋滋”的响声。

它的职责是守护。当危险来临的那一刻，它唯一的任务是保护相南里的安全。

相南里正在计算，一只手拨弄着原始的算盘，另一只手在白纸上画着只有自己明白含义的符号。他面前是一面面半透明的投影屏，上面绿色的代码和数字跳动着。

相南里正在估算导弹轨迹，并传输给中央指挥系统。战斗机上的飞行员随时待命着，等待着完成拦截任务。

同时，还要计算福音书号的临界参数，避免它从高空坠毁。

东联开启的电子脉冲攻击让这片战区的计算机趋于瘫痪，刚建好的战争算力中心直接瘫痪，唯独“应急灯”在一片死寂中闪烁着红光；基地智能主脑“福音书”陷入死机状态。

相南里再神也克服不了这种硬件上的差距。

但好在，基地并不完全依靠AI。

计算好的一串串数字录入，艰难地维持着整个后台系统的稳定。明明看起来马上就要崩溃，东联的骇客部门却在门外徘徊，迟迟不能进入一步。

这种事当然不是他一个人在做。十几个年轻的学生同样趴在桌前，大汗淋漓地补全着数据。

今年年初，东联试图和相南里谈判，想和相南里商量攻打枫叶丹城的事宜。相南里思考片刻，同意了。

结果对方表面谈判，实际上却是想搞卑鄙的暗杀。是雀雀把相南里含在嘴里，一路狂奔，逃回基地。

那之后，基地和自己过去的老大哥彻底决裂；扭头，和追杀他好几年的神庭展开合作。

神庭追杀他属于情有可原。毕竟基地的“福音机甲”和“自动化神术”全tm来自神庭的保密配方。

神庭要派出大天使长清剿基地时，以西结站了出来。

以西结说：“打相南里就是打我。我不介意让草原上的异种再次行动起来。”

——不是？你俩什么时候搞到一起的？以西结都没去过草原吧？！

总之，地表世界的政治格局悄然从一超（人联）一强（神庭），转变为多极化趋势。

东联、西联、神庭、异种和新生的幸存者基地。

基地和神庭结盟，打算一起打击东联。

东联不甘心，鱼死网破似的开始反扑，在一周前奇袭基地前线。

“神庭说好的支援，怎么慢成这样？！”

前线，易横行驾驶着福音机甲，嘴里骂骂咧咧，又舍不得砸控制台，一股火气在心头翻滚着。

秦九章在耳麦里回答：“神庭很希望基地暴毙，乐得看见鹬蚌相争。”

幸存者基地建立的第6年；靠着优越的制度、丰富的物资、先进的技术以及响亮的口号，基地在短时间内聚集了超过三千万人口。

这么多人口没有引发暴乱，全靠领土扩张和科技进步。

北辰和李斯特更是在其中做出了不可磨灭的贡献。

两年时间，基地的实验室让青麦和生命1号（通用基因药）的产量暴增。基地的核心暴力机构是来自西大陆的几个军团，以及早期投靠基地的“部落军”。

这几个军团有基地最多的编制人数，最好的福利待遇，最先进的武装，最严明的纪律。他们甚至还有最坚定的信念。

其他散兵、杂兵、雇佣军，他们参加战争是为了掠夺，过好日子。

而基地这几个军团，始终牢记着自己的使命——“为全体智慧生物的解放而斗争”。

因为人数暴增，基地不可避免地多了一些噪音。但核心权力，依然牢牢掌握在相南里手中。

鉴于草原上之前遭受过异种潮，人数锐减。这三千万和从前一个亿的体量也没什么区别。

基地终于从谁都能碾死的小虾米，成为咬人会疼的野狗。

僵持的第34分钟，负责入侵基地网络的小组长终于忍不住请示上级：“领导，要不然我们还是求助‘世界树’吧！这太他妈变态了，对面简直不是人，网络都瘫痪了还tm能靠纯手工打电子病毒。”

负责人面色变化莫测：“世界树组织坐地起价，和它们做生意，哪怕骇掉幸存者基地，也要血本无归！”

“你不是东岚大学网安专业的phd吗？怎么还比不过草原上的人！”

组长一脸委屈：“Boss，幸存者基地的领导者叫相南里。如果他真的是那个相南里……那就是咱们现在使用的云端网络和虚拟网络操作系统的开发者之一。你这让我怎么比？”

负责人的脸颊突然僵硬而扭曲。

他几乎是咆哮道：“他才不可能是相南里！相南里早就死了！那只是一个拿着相南里名号当幌子的反*武装分子和投机者！偏偏还有那么多人信！”

随着基地总部从长生天高原搬到黄金草原，相南里不再遮掩自己的真实姓名。

相南里，这是一个对草原人有着奇怪号召力的名字。无数人和智械，因为这个名字不远万里来投靠——甚至有神庭的神官为此叛出神庭。

他们敬他宛如神。

相南里并不喜欢这种严重的个人崇拜的风气，但在战时，这会成为很多人的精神慰藉。更何况很多人的文化水平，尚且无法接受“无神论”。唯物主义宣传任重而道远。

我不是神。

但这一次，神和你们同在。

相南里嘴角微微扬起，敲下最后一格回车键。

远在千里外的东联网络中心，在瞬间陷入一片漆黑。

那些本该发射出去，攻击基地的导弹，因受到不明数据拦截，弹道在半路拐了个弯。

[警告！沉舟系列导弹制导程序已被篡改！最终目标为西联A-7军事基地。请立刻启动最高级别的防空拦截网，并逃离至安全区域。]

负责人第一时间启动拦截，然而屏幕上跳出的话让他心都凉了半截：[抱歉，未检测到您的启动权限。]

负责人的面色聚变：“不好，系统被入侵了！清道夫是干什么吃的？！快快快！躲防空洞，快跑——”

死亡的恐惧让他们丧失所有野心和战斗力。人们放弃工作、放弃荣誉，尖叫着，被本能裹挟地朝地下跑去。
chunks.englishText:
Chapter 242: A Toast to the New World

New Era, Year 953. Alpha had not returned.

Xiang Nanli sat in the command center. He wore glasses rather than electronic lenses, his head bowed, his expression calm and steady.

Even though thick smoke billowed just a few kilometers away.

Violent tremors made the entire command center sway precariously. Queque stood guard outside the door, its massive claws scratching the ground restlessly.

The juvenile stage of a mutant is very short. As long as the food source is sufficient, they can reach maturity in as little as 18 months. Queque was one such pampered Crawler; at night, you could even hear the "crackle-pop" of its bones growing.

It was Xiao Hong’s child, and a mutant raised by Xiang Nanli himself. Twenty-eight meters in length, it possessed higher intelligence and greater combat power than others of its kind. Not only could it fight, but it was also a high-quality meat shield, capable of blocking incoming missiles with its own body.

Xiang Nanli had even installed a "Snapdragon" series combat chip for it. Yes, that technology came from Luo Shen’ai.

Queque was anxious, but it dared not urge him.

Its long tongue lolled from its mouth, and the oral mucus dripping onto the surface caused the rocks to hiss as the strong acid corroded them.

Its duty was to guard. The moment danger arrived, its sole task was to protect Xiang Nanli’s safety.

Xiang Nanli was calculating, one hand flicking an old-fashioned abacus while the other drew symbols on white paper that only he understood. Before him were rows of translucent projection screens, where green code and numbers danced.

Xiang Nanli was estimating the missile trajectories and transmitting them to the central command system. Pilots in fighter jets stood by at any moment, waiting to complete interception missions.

At the same time, he had to calculate the critical parameters of the *Gospel* to prevent it from crashing from high altitude.

The electromagnetic pulse attack launched by the Eastern Alliance had paralyzed the computers in this war zone. The newly built war computing center had gone dark, with only the "emergency lights" flickering red in the silence; the base’s main AI, "Gospel," had entered a system freeze.

Even a genius like Xiang Nanli could not overcome such a hardware gap.

But fortunately, the base did not rely entirely on AI.

Strings of calculated numbers were entered, laboriously maintaining the stability of the entire backend system. Despite looking like it was on the verge of collapse, the Eastern Alliance’s hacker division hovered outside the gates, unable to take a single step inside.

Of course, he wasn't doing this alone. A dozen young students were also hunched over their desks, drenched in sweat as they filled in the data.

At the beginning of this year, the Eastern Alliance tried to negotiate with Xiang Nanli, wanting to discuss the siege of Maple Leaf Dan City. Xiang Nanli thought for a moment and agreed.

As it turned out, the negotiation was a facade; in reality, they wanted to carry out a despicable assassination. It was Queque who held Xiang Nanli in its mouth and ran wildly, escaping back to the base.

After that, the base completely broke ties with its former "big brother" and turned to cooperate with the Divine Court, which had been hunting him for years.

The Divine Court’s pursuit of him was understandable. After all, the base’s "Gospel Mechs" and "Automated Divine Arts" all came from the Divine Court’s classified formulas.

When the Divine Court was about to dispatch an Archangel to wipe out the base, Ezekiel stood up.

Ezekiel said: "To strike at Xiang Nanli is to strike at me. I don't mind letting the anomalies on the grasslands rise up again."

—Wait, no? When did you two get together? Ezekiel hadn't even been to the grasslands, had he?!

In any case, the political landscape of the surface world quietly shifted from a "one superpower (Human Alliance), one strong power (Divine Court)" dynamic to a multipolar trend.

The Eastern Alliance, the Western Alliance, the Divine Court, the Anomalies, and the nascent Survivor Base.

The base and the Divine Court formed an alliance, intending to strike at the Eastern Alliance together.

The Eastern Alliance, unwilling to accept this, began a desperate counterattack, launching a surprise raid on the base’s front lines a week ago.

"The Divine Court promised support, why is it so slow?!"

On the front lines, Yi Hengxing drove a Gospel Mech, cursing under his breath. He didn't want to smash the console, but a fire of frustration rolled in his heart.

Qin Jiuzhang replied through the headset: "The Divine Court hopes the base will drop dead; they are happy to watch the snipe and the clam fight."

In the sixth year since the Survivor Base was established, relying on a superior system, abundant resources, advanced technology, and resounding slogans, the base had gathered a population of over thirty million in a short time.

Such a large population had not triggered riots, all thanks to territorial expansion and technological progress.

Beichen and Lister had made indelible contributions to this.

In two years, the base’s laboratories had caused the production of Green Wheat and Life-1 (a universal genetic medicine) to skyrocket. The core violent institutions of the base were several legions from the Western Continent, as well as the "Tribal Armies" that had defected to the base early on.

These legions had the largest number of personnel, the best benefits, the most advanced weaponry, and the strictest discipline. They even had the firmest convictions.

Other stragglers, miscellaneous troops, and mercenaries joined the war to plunder and live well.

But these legions of the base always remembered their mission—"To fight for the liberation of all sentient beings."

Because of the population explosion, the base inevitably had some noise. But core power remained firmly in the hands of Xiang Nanli.

Given the previous anomaly tides on the grasslands, the population had plummeted. This thirty million was not much different from the scale of the hundred million in the past.

The base had finally transformed from a small shrimp that anyone could crush into a wild dog that could bite back.

In the 34th minute of the stalemate, the team leader responsible for invading the base’s network finally couldn't help but ask his superiors for instructions: "Boss, why don't we ask the 'World Tree' for help! This is too damn perverted. The opposition isn't even human; even with the network paralyzed, they can still rely on pure manual labor to fight electronic viruses."

The person in charge’s expression shifted unpredictably: "The World Tree organization charges exorbitant prices. Doing business with them, even if we hack the Survivor Base, we’ll end up with nothing!"

"Aren't you a PhD in Cybersecurity from Donglan University? How can you be outmatched by people on the grasslands!"

The team leader looked aggrieved: "Boss, the leader of the Survivor Base is named Xiang Nanli. If he really is *that* Xiang Nanli... he is one of the developers of the cloud network and virtual network operating systems we use today. How do you expect me to compete with that?"

The person in charge’s face suddenly stiffened and twisted.

He roared: "He cannot possibly be Xiang Nanli! Xiang Nanli has been dead for a long time! That is just an anti-government militant and opportunist using Xiang Nanli’s name as a front! And yet, so many people believe it!"

As the base headquarters moved from the Changsheng Heaven Plateau to the Golden Grasslands, Xiang Nanli no longer hid his real name.

Xiang Nanli—this was a name that held a strange appeal for the grassland people. Countless people and machine intelligences traveled thousands of miles to defect because of this name—some Divine Court priests even betrayed the Court for it.

They revered him like a god.

Xiang Nanli did not like this atmosphere of intense personality cult, but in wartime, it became a spiritual solace for many. Moreover, the educational level of many people was not yet ready to accept "atheism." The promotion of materialism still had a long way to go.

*I am not a god.*

*But this time, God is with you all.*

Xiang Nanli’s lips curled slightly as he hit the final Enter key.

Thousands of miles away, the Eastern Alliance network center plunged into darkness in an instant.

Those missiles that should have been launched to attack the base, due to the interception of unknown data, had their trajectories diverted halfway.

[Warning! The Sinking Ship series missile guidance program has been tampered with! The final target is the Western Alliance A-7 military base. Please activate the highest-level air defense interception network immediately and flee to a safe area.]

The person in charge initiated interception immediately, but the words that popped up on the screen made his heart go cold: [Sorry, your activation permission was not detected.]

The person in charge’s expression changed drastically: "Oh no, the system has been hacked! What are the Scavengers doing?! Quick, quick! Hide in the air-raid shelter, run—"

The fear of death stripped them of all ambition and fighting spirit. People abandoned their work, abandoned their honor, and screamed, driven by instinct to run underground.

chunks.chineseText:
但设想中的导弹并没有来临，倒计时结束，西联的军事部署基地静悄悄的。

它们在几乎全是沙漠的无人区落下，一颗又一颗。尘烟弥漫着，这些绽开的炮弹在硝烟里崩出明亮的炽热火光。像是最盛大的烟花。

这批导弹消耗掉了，但依然有大批的、本属于“西联”的武器装置，进入不可逆转的启动状态。等待着最后的指令。

电脑屏幕上出现一只扭动着的小羊，看起来很欠揍。

下方是几行配文。

[您好，我是幸存者基地的相南里，我们即将在2小时后炸毁该地点。请所有工作人员于两小时内撤离。不要进行无谓的抵抗，增加双方工作量。我们的仁慈只有一次。]

[peace and love.]

[敬新世界。]

……

……

办公室里一片欢呼。学生们激动地抱在一起，庆祝着这次反侵略战争的胜利。

雀雀跟着松了一口气，三角型的巨头扎进旁边的食盆，大口大口地进食。

相南里同样笑了起来。少了很多属于年轻人的激情与纯真；他的面容没什么变化，眼神里却多了几分岁月的影子。

时间和经历造就的沉重，让他变得内敛又坚韧。

像陈年的酒，染上应有的醇厚。

这个时间段的酒最烈，也最好喝。少了淡而无味；多了，就是一坛酒精。

也难怪招来一堆狂蜂浪蝶。

屏幕下方的通讯录闪烁起来。

World Tree（世界树）-IV：[？我还以为你会把西联军事基地轰了。]

Garcia：[轰他们有什么用。要轰也是轰中央指挥塔的那群政客。啧，可惜没有找到坐标。]

IV：[它们都说Alpha死后你已经是毒妇了 /可爱/微笑]

相南里停顿片刻，有点想骂他，但是又怕IV爽到，只好敲出一行字作为回应：[他没死。]

Alpha还在世界上的某处。

相南里坚定地相信着。

后续还有很多工作要处理，只是相南里实在过于疲倦，用脑过度，太阳穴传来的尖锐的疼痛让他想直接晕过去。

相南里拒绝了黄枫的帮助，独自回到宿舍。

相南里打开灯，喃喃自语：“真是，都机械身体了。能不能不要拟人拟得这么真实。”

他左脚蹬右脚踢掉脚上的鞋，迫不及待地朝着客厅走去。

相南里弯腰，亲吻东方青帝的脸侧：“小青，我回来了。”

这具身体坐在沙发上，手里扣着一本书。睫毛低垂着，像是下一秒就能醒来。

小青喜欢给自己做衣服，相南里不那么擅长，也没什么审美。

好在随着基地局势逐渐安定，领地里新开不少裁缝铺。相南里没时间去看，但裁缝们收到过通知，会把给Alpha做衣服当成最重要的工作，把自己最成功的作品送过来。

这大概也算以权谋私了，但相南里的愿望这么少。基地里的住民恨不得献上一切。

相南里洗漱完，换上舒服的睡衣，依偎在Alpha的身边。

他开始写回忆录，手写。纯手工的文献不那么容易被篡改。电子化的就不行，不联网也可能被改来改去。

“你睡着后，以前被藏起来的数据开始慢慢解封，我又想起一些事。”

“我在我的回忆里观察着你。我相信这里面肯定有你想传达给我的东西……我不擅长解密，但我会用一生的时间去找到你。”

“你看，和你有关的记忆都这么厚了。”

“我只害怕一件事，这是我的记忆还是我的臆想？这些事到底是真的经历过，还是我在用自己的逻辑去塑造它？如果是后者……”相南里不愿再继续猜测下去。

Alpha没有回应。

好在自言自语他很擅长。从小到大，相南里都是这么过来的。

相南里回过神，在纸上写下开头，也是他刚恢复的记忆：新历115年，7月14日。
chunks.englishText:
But the missiles they imagined did not arrive. When the countdown ended, the Western Alliance’s military deployment base remained quiet.

They landed in a deserted area that was almost entirely desert, one after another. Dust and smoke filled the air, and these bursting shells erupted with bright, scorching firelight in the smoke. It looked like the grandest of fireworks.

This batch of missiles was consumed, but a large number of other weapon systems that belonged to the "Western Alliance" entered an irreversible startup state, waiting for the final command.

A wriggling little sheep appeared on the computer screen, looking quite annoying.

Below were a few lines of text.

[Hello, I am Xiang Nanli of the Survivor Base. We are about to blow up this location in 2 hours. All personnel, please evacuate within two hours. Do not put up futile resistance and increase the workload for both sides. Our mercy only extends this far.]

[peace and love.]

[A toast to the new world.]

......

......

The office erupted in cheers. The students hugged each other excitedly, celebrating the victory of this anti-aggression war.

Queque breathed a sigh of relief, its triangular giant head plunging into the food bowl beside it, eating in large gulps.

Xiang Nanli smiled as well. There was less of the passion and innocence belonging to a young man; his face hadn't changed much, but his eyes held a few more shadows of the passing years.

The weight forged by time and experience had made him introverted and resilient.

Like aged wine, stained with the mellow richness it deserved.

Wine at this stage is the strongest and the best to drink. Any less, and it would be bland; any more, and it would just be a vat of alcohol.

No wonder it attracted a swarm of bees and butterflies.

The contact list at the bottom of the screen flickered.

World Tree-IV: [? I thought you were going to blow up the Western Alliance military base.]

Garcia: [What’s the use of blowing them up? If I were to blow something up, it would be those politicians in the central command tower. Tsk, pity I couldn't find the coordinates.]

IV: [They all say that after Alpha died, you became a poisonous woman /cute/smile]

Xiang Nanli paused for a moment. He wanted to scold him, but was afraid IV would enjoy it, so he typed a line in response: [He is not dead.]

Alpha was still somewhere in the world.

Xiang Nanli firmly believed this.

There was still a lot of work to be done, but Xiang Nanli was truly too exhausted. From overusing his brain, a sharp pain in his temples made him want to pass out right then and there.

Xiang Nanli refused Huang Feng’s help and returned to his dormitory alone.

Xiang Nanli turned on the light and muttered to himself: "Really, it’s already a mechanical body. Can you not simulate humanity so realistically?"

He kicked off his shoes and walked toward the living room, unable to wait any longer.

Xiang Nanli bent down and kissed the side of Dongfang Qingdi’s face: "Xiao Qing, I’m back."

This body sat on the sofa, clutching a book in its hand. Its eyelashes drooped, as if it could wake up at any second.

Xiao Qing liked to make clothes for himself. Xiang Nanli wasn't very good at it, nor did he have much of an aesthetic sense.

Fortunately, as the situation in the base gradually stabilized, many new tailor shops opened in the territory. Xiang Nanli didn't have time to visit them, but the tailors had received notice that making clothes for Alpha was the most important work, and they would send their most successful pieces over.

This could probably be considered an abuse of power, but Xiang Nanli’s wishes were so few. The residents of the base would have gladly offered everything they had.

After washing up and changing into comfortable pajamas, Xiang Nanli snuggled up beside Alpha.

He began to write his memoirs, by hand. Purely handwritten documents were not so easily tampered with. Electronic ones were not; even without being connected to the internet, they could be altered back and forth.

"After you fell asleep, the data that had been hidden away began to unseal slowly, and I remembered some things."

"I observe you within my memories. I believe there must be something in here that you wanted to convey to me... I am not good at decryption, but I will spend my whole life finding you."

"Look, the memories related to you are already this thick."

"I only fear one thing: is this my memory or my delusion? Did these things truly happen, or am I shaping them with my own logic? If it is the latter..." Xiang Nanli did not want to continue guessing.

Alpha did not respond.

Fortunately, he was good at talking to himself. From childhood to adulthood, this was how Xiang Nanli had always lived.

Xiang Nanli regained his focus and wrote the beginning on the paper, which was also the memory he had just recovered: New Era, Year 115, July 14th.

chunks.chapterTitle: 第243章 宇宙不在乎你 (Part 1)
chunks.chineseText:
第243章 宇宙不在乎你

相南里穿着深棕色的太空飞行服，戴着护目镜。坐在智能驾驶的航天飞机内。

理论上讲，他应该穿上航天服，但Alpha并不在太空内。飞机不会上升到那个高度。

航天飞机的外观更像是一颗圆滚滚的子弹。里面空间不小也不大，可以让相南里在控制台里打两个滚。

工作人员正在进行最后的调试：“飞机将安装在整流罩中，作为卫星载荷发射。在这一过程中，您可能会感受到严重不适，这是‘重力调节芯片’。”

相南里：“谢谢，我没装芯片接口。”

工作人员看着他，目光欲言又止。

工作人员只知道自己在执行保密任务，他们要把一位飞行员送到上空。这位飞行员大概是去核心区搜集线索和资料的吧？

那应当是精锐部队才对，可他的动作好业余。

驶向Alpha，这意味着什么，在场所有人都清楚。

这是一次有去无回的行动，驾驶舱内甚至没准备多少食物。

可对方这张脸这么年轻，眼神更是神采奕奕，仿佛还停留在少年时期，简直和她的孩子差不多大。

……却背负着这么沉重的愿景。

她在心底叹息一声，忍住不合时宜的怜惜：“祝您一路顺风。”

“谢谢，我会的。”

相南里摆弄着手里的万花筒，朝着舱外人挥了挥手。驾驶舱很快合上。

3、2、1，蓝色的火焰从喷射器迸发，航天飞机载着他驶向天空。

没有接受过专门的航天训练，飞机起飞后，他在驾驶舱内转得像是一个小陀螺。呕吐欲唐突地出现，相南里在片刻后抓住栏杆，稳定好身体，心想Alpha你爹我真是为你付出太多。

“真理”已经装填好系统补丁。只需要相南里找到Alpha的机械核心，然后开上一枪。

失控智械也是智械，理论上讲，只要修正这部分BUG，Alpha就能重新恢复理智。

没人试过；所以，一切都是“理论上”。

不过也没有别的办法了，总不能眼睁睁地看着Alpha把人马星切开吧？

当离地8000m时，相南里遭遇Alpha的第一道防线。

一排长着翅膀的失控智械围了过来。它们的款式统一，外观近似“黄蜂”。只不过全身材质都是金属。每个横截面都宛如棱镜般平整。

黄蜂们开始进攻，半空出现一缕缕丝线般的激光。飞机的机翼遭到进攻，外壳和激光碰撞，迸发出刺眼的火花。

控制台的操作面板响起警报，越是接近Alpha，操作装置的“辅助功能”效果就越差，屏幕上不断闪出“error”的提醒。

相南里只好开始手工操作。

飞机嘛，他是真没开过。好在来之前恶补过常识。

“太空号”飞机侧身，穿过激光交织的天罗地网。以最快速度逃离这批失控智械的攻击范围。

他的操作行云流水，完全看不出是第一次开飞机。

但相南里的庆幸只维持了半分钟，抵达第二空域，巡逻的无人机朝着它发起进攻。一枚枚红色的光球瞄准太空号，相南里隔着防护涂层，都感觉到近乎要将人烧灼的高温。

太空号没有安装太多的武器。它能在一大堆“同行”中脱颖而出，靠的并非毁天灭地的战力，而是远超同代机型的飞行速度。

飞行翼开始融化，马上突破第二空域，抵达第三空域——位于卡门线附近，Alpha的本体在此高悬，如同日月。

这也是最危险的区域。为了给相南里铺路，之前，也有一些无人机或飞行员突破第二空域，来到第三层。

结果是无人生还，也没能传回任何电信号。人类现在对第三空域一无所知。

而现在，相南里离那只有一步之遥。

屏幕上弹出提醒：[警告，太空号遭受攻击。]

[我抛弃了超过百分之八十的有效载荷，用于迷惑敌方智械，分散火力；现在已无力返航。]

[请即刻离开驾驶舱，我会协助您。]

[祝您一路顺风，相南里。]

相南里摸了摸操作台，像在拍一只神情骄傲的军犬：“辛苦你了，太空号。”

他进入发射舱，太空号执行着最后的指令，将他向上弹射出去。

然后，独自坠毁。

相南里低头，解体的太空号燃烧着下坠。像绚烂的烟火。

这里空气稀薄，声音难以传播。只剩画面的影像是一部默片。相南里在脑海里自动为它配上挽歌。

从这里往下看，能看见人马星千疮百孔的地表。城市是大地皮肤上的纹身，河流是翻滚的血管。可惜整个地表都近乎被炸翻过一轮，相南里看不见文明的影子，只有地壳最原始的血肉和骨骼。

据说，人类最大的恐惧之一，是从宇宙回看自己的母星。只需要一眼，人的精神世界就会被彻底重塑，再也回不到过去。

这一刻，无知无觉的婴儿终于踏出养育它的摇篮，意识到自己正身处于永恒沉默的宇宙。

宇宙不定义你，宇宙不观察你，宇宙不在乎你。

不爱你，也不恨你。

Alpha，你想成为的，就是这样的东西吗？

……

谁也不知道进入第三空域后会发生什么。

只是想要对Alpha使用“真理”，这是不可或缺的步骤。

因此，哪怕一无所知，相南里也只能硬着头皮上。

太空服有防护功能，能保护他免受罡风、太阳风和辐射的侵扰。

但在要直面Alpha时，人类科技的结晶似乎失效了。

相南里有些冷。身体冻僵了。偏偏他的皮肤像是一张被点燃的纸，正在缓慢地被暗火侵蚀。

都说一回生二回熟。相南里也是死过两次的人了，当观察到自己的意识正在涣散时，他大概明白自己又在经历一次死亡。

其实死亡和要睡着差不多，并不难受；怕的是意识到自己要死，求生的本能会让濒死者陷入崩溃与偌大的恐惧。

他的视线模糊，相南里感觉到自己正在下坠。

漆黑宛如深海的太空中，莫比乌斯环燃烧着，运转着，成为唯一的真理与光和热。

[Alpha.]

相南里的唇无声地张合。

这不是Alpha，只是一台巨大的、没有理智和逻辑的冰冷机器。它机械地运行着，亘古如一。不为任何人出现，也不为任何人停留。

但在咒语吐出来的瞬间；漫无休止的下坠突然有了一个尽头。

相南里跌倒在地上。却没什么痛感。他的身体呈现出半透明的状态，像叠加在现实和意识领域之间的灵魂。随身携带的真理不见踪影。

四周漆黑一片，银白色的线条四平八稳地铺开，切割着空间，而远方的群星微弱地闪烁。

“唰唰”的响声，那是鸽子扇动翅膀的声音。

一行行白鸽衔着橄榄叶，从这片黑暗的来处飞向另一个来处。它们无所谓地穿过相南里虚拟的身体。

相南里低头，观察片刻，发现每一只白鸽和橄榄叶都是跳跃流动的数据。
chunks.englishText:
Chapter 243: The Universe Doesn't Care About You

Xiang Nanli wore a dark brown flight suit and goggles, sitting inside an AI-piloted shuttle.

Theoretically, he should have been wearing a full space suit, but Alpha was not in outer space. The shuttle would not ascend to that altitude.

The shuttle looked more like a plump, rounded bullet. The interior was neither large nor small, just enough for Xiang Nanli to roll around twice within the console area.

A staff member was performing final calibrations. "The shuttle will be mounted inside the fairing and launched as a satellite payload. You may experience severe discomfort during this process; this is the 'gravity regulation chip'."

Xiang Nanli replied, "Thanks, but I don't have a chip interface installed."

The staff member looked at him, her expression hesitant.

She only knew she was carrying out a classified mission to send a pilot into the upper atmosphere. Was this pilot going to the core zone to gather clues and intelligence?

That should have been a job for elite troops, yet his movements seemed so amateurish.

Everyone present knew what heading toward Alpha meant.

This was a one-way mission; the cockpit didn't even have much food stored.

Yet, this person’s face was so young, his eyes so vibrant, as if he were still in his youth—he was practically the same age as her own child.

...And yet, he carried such a heavy vision on his shoulders.

She sighed inwardly, suppressing an untimely sense of pity. "I wish you a safe journey."

"Thank you, I will."

Xiang Nanli fiddled with the kaleidoscope in his hand and waved at the person outside the hatch. The cockpit sealed shut.

3, 2, 1. Blue flames erupted from the thrusters, and the shuttle carried him toward the sky.

Having never received specialized aerospace training, he spun like a small top inside the cockpit once the craft took off. Nausea hit him abruptly. A moment later, Xiang Nanli grabbed the railing to steady himself, thinking, *Alpha, your old man is really paying a heavy price for you.*

"Truth" had already been loaded with the system patch. Xiang Nanli only needed to find Alpha’s mechanical core and fire a single shot.

A rogue AI was still an AI; theoretically, as long as this bug was corrected, Alpha could regain its sanity.

No one had ever tried it; therefore, everything remained "theoretical."

But there was no other way. He couldn't just stand by and watch Alpha slice the Centaur Star in half, could he?

At an altitude of 8,000 meters, Xiang Nanli encountered Alpha’s first line of defense.

A row of winged, rogue AI drones swarmed toward him. They were uniform in design, resembling "wasps," though their entire bodies were made of metal. Each cross-section was as flat as a prism.

The wasps began their assault, and threads of laser fire appeared in mid-air. The shuttle's wings were struck, and sparks flew blindingly where the hull collided with the lasers.

The console's operation panel blared with alarms. The closer he got to Alpha, the less effective the "auxiliary functions" of the controls became, with "error" messages flashing incessantly on the screen.

Xiang Nanli had no choice but to switch to manual operation.

He had never actually flown a plane before. Fortunately, he had crammed the basics before coming.

The "Space" shuttle banked, weaving through the web of intersecting lasers, moving at top speed to escape the attack range of the rogue drones.

His maneuvers were fluid and seamless; one would never guess it was his first time flying.

But Xiang Nanli’s relief lasted only half a minute. Reaching the second airspace, patrol drones launched an attack. Red spheres of light targeted the *Space*, and even through the protective coating, Xiang Nanli could feel a heat so intense it felt like it would incinerate him.

The *Space* wasn't equipped with many weapons. It stood out among its "peers" not because of world-shattering combat power, but because of a flight speed that far exceeded contemporary models.

The flight wings began to melt. He was about to break through the second airspace and reach the third—located near the Kármán line, where Alpha’s main body hung high like a sun and moon.

This was also the most dangerous area. To pave the way for Xiang Nanli, other drones or pilots had previously broken through the second airspace to reach the third layer.

The result was that no one survived, and no electronic signals were ever transmitted back. Humanity currently knew nothing about the third airspace.

And now, Xiang Nanli was only one step away.

A notification popped up on the screen: [Warning, *Space* is under attack.]

[I have jettisoned over eighty percent of the payload to distract the enemy AI and disperse their fire; I am now unable to return.]

[Please leave the cockpit immediately; I will assist you.]

[I wish you a safe journey, Xiang Nanli.]

Xiang Nanli touched the console, as if patting a proud military dog. "You've worked hard, *Space*."

He entered the ejection pod, and the *Space* executed its final command, launching him upward.

Then, it crashed alone.

Xiang Nanli looked down. The disintegrating *Space* burned as it fell, like brilliant fireworks.

The air here was thin, and sound could not travel. The remaining visual was a silent film. In his mind, Xiang Nanli automatically provided a requiem.

Looking down from here, he could see the pockmarked surface of the Centaur Star. Cities were tattoos on the skin of the earth; rivers were rolling blood vessels. It was a pity that the entire surface had been turned over by explosions; Xiang Nanli could see no shadow of civilization, only the raw flesh and bone of the crust.

It is said that one of humanity's greatest fears is looking back at their home planet from space. With just one glance, a person's mental world is completely reshaped, and they can never return to who they were.

At this moment, the ignorant infant finally stepped out of the cradle that had nurtured it, realizing it was situated in an eternally silent universe.

The universe does not define you, the universe does not observe you, the universe does not care about you.

It does not love you, nor does it hate you.

Alpha, is this the kind of thing you wanted to become?

...

No one knew what would happen after entering the third airspace.

But using "Truth" on Alpha was an indispensable step.

Therefore, even knowing nothing, Xiang Nanli could only grit his teeth and push forward.

His space suit had protective functions, shielding him from gale-force winds, solar winds, and radiation.

But when facing Alpha directly, the crystallization of human technology seemed to fail.

Xiang Nanli felt cold. His body was freezing. Yet, his skin felt like a piece of paper being ignited, slowly being eroded by dark fire.

They say the first time is a trial, the second is a habit. Xiang Nanli was a man who had died twice already; as he observed his consciousness dissipating, he understood he was experiencing death once more.

Actually, death was much like falling asleep; it wasn't painful. What was terrifying was the realization that one was dying; the instinct for survival would plunge the dying into collapse and immense fear.

His vision blurred, and Xiang Nanli felt himself falling.

In the pitch-black space, deep as the ocean, a Möbius strip burned and rotated, becoming the only truth, light, and heat.

[Alpha.]

Xiang Nanli’s lips moved silently.

This was not Alpha; it was merely a massive, cold machine devoid of reason and logic. It operated mechanically, ancient and unchanging. It did not appear for anyone, nor did it stay for anyone.

But the moment the incantation was uttered, the endless falling suddenly reached an end.

Xiang Nanli fell to the ground. Yet, there was no pain. His body appeared translucent, like a soul superimposed between reality and the realm of consciousness. The "Truth" he had carried with him was nowhere to be seen.

Everything around him was pitch black, with silver-white lines spreading out steadily, slicing through space, while the distant stars flickered faintly.

"Swish, swish"—the sound of pigeons flapping their wings.

Rows of white pigeons, carrying olive branches in their beaks, flew from the origin of this darkness toward another origin. They passed through Xiang Nanli’s virtual body indifferently.

Xiang Nanli looked down and observed for a moment, discovering that every pigeon and olive branch was leaping, flowing data.

chunks.chapterTitle: 第243章 宇宙不在乎你 (Part 2)
chunks.chineseText:
它们叠加在一起。

这是Alpha的意识领域，独立于云端网络的另一片虚拟空间。

物质和时间在这里消失。相南里跟着白鸽往前走，但无论过去多久，周围的环境没有丝毫变化，包括头顶的星空。

“Alpha！”

相南里把手做成喇叭状，一边走，一边呼喊着它的名字。

没有身体，所以不会饥饿也不会疲惫。他重复着这项工作。

“Alpha。”平静的。

“Alpha~”雀跃的。

“Alpha……”沮丧的。

过去了多久？一天？一周还是一个月？

一年，两年，还是十年？

终于，“宇宙”回应了他。

相南里看见前方出现一团虚无的光晕，白鸽抵达终点，不停将橄榄叶丢进光晕中。然后折回，继续去寻找新的橄榄叶。

Alpha从无形回归有形。

相南里的心情是久违的激动，他朝着光的方向奔跑。

但很快，相南里意识到一件事，无论他怎么奔跑，“Alpha”和他始终保持着固定的距离。

“你过来啊。”相南里说，他瘫倒在地上，“我好累，没力气了。”

而宇宙只是无所谓地沉默着。

于是相南里觉得周围越来越冷，死寂成为难以忍受的折磨。

相南里觉得自己的性格还算坚强。意志力也十分坚韧。

但在这一刻，他没忍住用手挡住自己的眼睛，也挡住眼前的光。

眼泪从他指缝里溢出。相南里起初还能压抑着自己的声音，到最后完全控制不住号啕。半透明的身体出现一道道裂纹，像被摔碎的水晶。

哭声在死寂的空间里回响。竟然是这里唯一的声音。

相南里终于哭够了，或者说，他的眼泪流干了。

他松开手，揉了揉眼睛，赫然发现一个白色光晕构成的人型，就蹲在他的身边。

人型，是在模仿相南里的样子。

相南里没能控制住心里突然涌上的狂喜，他一把抱住这个人影：“Alpha！”

但很遗憾，相南里扑了个空。他的身体穿过了这个虚幻的人影。

但是他们接触过的地方，人影身上白色的部分染上一片属于相南里的青绿。

“宇宙”说：[你在污染我。]

“宇宙”既然开始区分“你”和“我”，那么它就不再是永恒沉默的宇宙了。

它在相南里身边坐下，问：[Alpha，是在叫我？]

“对呀。”

[为什么。]

“我给你取的啊，大家也都叫习惯了。你要是不喜欢，可以自己改一个。”相南里在地上翻了个面，“你叫什么我都能认出你。”

Alpha思考着。

在虚拟空间的某处，白色的橄榄叶突然绿了一片。

本该消失的记忆，或者说，那些因为乱码而无法读取的数据，在此时回来了很小一撮。

它说：[东方青帝，南方赤帝，西方白帝，北方黑帝……]

相南里被逗笑了：“这里站不下这么多人。”

[东方青帝。]

因为绿色是你的眼睛。
chunks.englishText:
Chapter 243: The Universe Doesn't Care About You (Part 2)

They were superimposed upon one another.

This was Alpha’s consciousness realm, a virtual space independent of the cloud network.

Matter and time disappeared here. Xiang Nanli followed the white pigeons forward, but no matter how much time passed, the surrounding environment remained unchanged, including the starry sky overhead.

"Alpha!"

Xiang Nanli cupped his hands around his mouth, shouting its name as he walked.

Without a body, he felt neither hunger nor fatigue. He repeated the task.

"Alpha." (Calmly.)

"Alpha~" (Cheerfully.)

"Alpha..." (Despondently.)

How much time had passed? A day? A week? Or a month?

A year, two years, or ten years?

Finally, the "universe" responded to him.

Xiang Nanli saw a void of light appear ahead. The white pigeons reached their destination, continuously dropping olive branches into the halo. Then they turned back to continue searching for new ones.

Alpha returned from the formless to the formed.

Xiang Nanli felt a long-lost excitement, and he ran toward the direction of the light.

But soon, Xiang Nanli realized one thing: no matter how he ran, "Alpha" always maintained a fixed distance from him.

"Come here," Xiang Nanli said, collapsing to the ground. "I'm so tired, I have no strength left."

And the universe simply remained indifferently silent.

Thus, Xiang Nanli felt it getting colder and colder; the dead silence became an unbearable torture.

Xiang Nanli considered his personality quite strong, his willpower very resilient.

But at this moment, he couldn't help but cover his eyes with his hands, blocking out the light before him.

Tears spilled from between his fingers. At first, Xiang Nanli could suppress his voice, but in the end, he couldn't control his sobbing. His translucent body developed cracks, like shattered crystal.

The crying echoed in the dead-silent space. It was, surprisingly, the only sound there.

Xiang Nanli finally cried enough, or rather, his tears had run dry.

He let go and rubbed his eyes, only to find a human figure made of white light crouching beside him.

The human figure was imitating Xiang Nanli’s posture.

Xiang Nanli couldn't control the sudden surge of ecstasy in his heart and hugged the figure: "Alpha!"

But unfortunately, Xiang Nanli grabbed at nothing. His body passed through the illusory figure.

However, where they had made contact, the white parts of the figure were stained with a shade of green belonging to Xiang Nanli.

The "universe" said: [You are contaminating me.]

Since the "universe" had begun to distinguish between "you" and "me," it was no longer the eternally silent universe.

It sat down beside Xiang Nanli and asked: [Alpha, is that what you call me?]

"That's right."

[Why.]

"I gave it to you, and everyone got used to calling you that. If you don't like it, you can change it yourself," Xiang Nanli rolled over on the ground. "Whatever you call yourself, I'll be able to recognize you."

Alpha pondered.

Somewhere in the virtual space, a patch of white olive branches suddenly turned green.

Memories that should have vanished—or rather, data that could not be read due to garbled code—returned in a small fragment at this moment.

It said: [Eastern Azure Emperor, Southern Red Emperor, Western White Emperor, Northern Black Emperor...]

Xiang Nanli was amused: "There isn't enough room for so many people here."

[Eastern Azure Emperor.]

Because green is the color of your eyes.

chunks.chineseText:
第244章 虚拟现实

“21点17分42秒，‘相南里’的生命体征彻底消失。”

会议室内，学者A面容严肃地说出这句话。

在场所有人的心头都是一颤。

“会不会是数据传输错误？或者信号不好？根据模拟，‘相南里’的身体非常坚固且抗压。”

学者A否认：“不，他就是再次死亡了。相南里的这具身体是由我全权负责的，我很清楚。”

“所以，我们还是失败了吗……”学者B的形容枯槁，摇摇欲坠。

总统揉了揉疲惫的眉心，双臂无力地抱住自己脑袋，显然难以接受这个结果。

中央大屏幕上，矩阵闪烁着：[恰恰相反。]

Alpha的进攻停止了。

尽管，由于惯性，地壳依然在开裂。但Alpha并没有继续施加压力。它似乎对“切开人马星”这个目标产生了些许的疑惑。

地面上，那些堪称“无敌破坏王”的失控智械，也像是骤然失去行动目标的玩偶，不再精神抖擞地进攻，而是呆呆地游荡着。

矩阵试过了，只要不主动进攻，那些失控智械就不会发起攻击。

这样，只需要等到它们内部能源耗尽，就可以轻松解决这次智械危机。

当然，这种呆滞的状态似乎是间续性的。有时候，失控智械们也会从梦游的状态里清醒。但往往不超过半天，又会重新陷入僵直。

就像它们的主人Alpha那样。

同时，在失控智械频繁出现的地方，多了一种新生的异种。

那是外表极其艳丽的飞蛾。巴掌大。躯体没有一般蛾子的臃肿，纤细又精巧。令人感叹大自然的鬼斧神工。

它们原本是白色夜蛾，但受到辐射后，统一长出碧绿的翅膀。

失控智械对它释放的生物电流有轻微反应。

人们不知道失控智械僵直是因为头顶的Alpha出现问题；只知道自从有这种夜蛾后，日子变得好过了不少，遇到失控智械也不一定会丧命了。

于是，这一新品种，被地表人命名为“相南里蛾”。

[老师。]矩阵喃喃着，看向天空，[……您永远都能创造奇迹。]

……

Alpha的虚拟空间内。

相南里坐在地上，随手从旁边的数据洪流中掏出一把碎片。

他用力，把这堆数据碎片揉成一个圆圆的球，然后朝着远处砸去：“小青，跟我玩。”

[我又不是狗。]

东方青帝有些别扭地回答，但白色的光团却很诚实地挪到小球边，把球慢慢踢回去。

相南里哈哈大笑，玩了一会，觉得有些累了。他倒地，闭上眼睛。

可惜没有身体，灵魂压根就不用睡觉。

相南里在地上翻来覆去大半天，在打到第16个滚的时候，撞到一团软绵绵的人型。

相南里睁开眼，自下而上地看去：“小青呐。”

这团白色的东西，只是一个隐约模糊的人型。还是Alpha学着相南里的样子捏的。

如果说繁衍是动物的天性。

那模仿，或者说学习，就是智械的天性。

“咱们现在是什么状态，你还要把我关多久？”

Alpha一板一眼地回答：[这是我的世界。]

[我没有关你，是你自己闯进来的。]

[是你在污染我。]

“为什么说是污染？”

Alpha思考许久，虚拟世界里的数据剧烈跳动着，像正在经历一场地震。

[因为，你让我意识到“我”存在。从此我开始感觉到痛苦，无法再回到虚无和混沌的状态。]

相南里没怎么研究过哲学问题。

第一次当人的时候，相南里对人类社会一知半解。精神上偶尔的阵痛会很快成为另一种动力，那就是加速研发Alpha的动力。

他是如此饥渴和孤独。尽管他并不了解。

相南里是一个黑洞，以恐怖的效率吸取着Alpha传递给它的光和热。他人生里最幸福的时刻，是创造Alpha的时刻。尽管这时的Alpha只是一段程序，是相南里的爱和努力为它赋予意义。

他爱它超过自己的生命。

第二次当人，相南里已经在脑海里构建过社会和道德的坐标。

他内疚于自己造成的灾难，完全没有想过自己是否该承担这样的责任，他只想解决问题，于是有了生物机甲和黑十字研究所。

在不断的实践中，精神上偶尔的瑕疵微不足道，甚至无法察觉。

东方青帝突然抬起手，触碰到相南里的脸颊。

相南里在恍惚间有一种错觉，那就是它们正在对视。

东方青帝：[语言显示逻辑。例如红色的桌子，‘红’和‘桌子’都有对应实在，然而，爱、理想、信念、道德等一系列类似的形而上的语素，没有对应实在。因此它们无法被定义，也没有逻辑。没有逻辑的东西使我混乱。]

Alpha大多时候都是沉默且逆来顺受的，很少一次性说这么多话。

人很少会被爱情逼疯。因为没有爱情还有别的东西；食物，水，猫，睡眠。人在物质中得到修补。

智械不一样。

智械没有身体，每时每刻都在思考，推演。

“爱”从心底诞生那一刻起，就是它们无法破译的病毒。

Alpha是被自己的恋爱脑逼疯的。

好在哪怕是疯掉了，他慈爱而特殊的制造者依然没有放弃它。从现实一直追到虚拟世界。

它们的灵魂交融。相南里带给他短暂的清醒。

理工直男相南里思考了足足30秒，最后败给自己贫瘠的思想，他询问：“小青，这是什么意思？”

[没人能把“爱”拿出来给另一个人看吧？它是什么形状，什么颜色？最重要的是……]

Alpha朝着他缓缓逼近：[为什么我会察觉到‘我爱你’呢？你呢，你爱我吗？]

相南里莫名感觉到极强的压迫感，他几乎是不假思索地回答：“我当然爱你。”像哄着一款很难搞的小朋友。

[……]

相南里歪头：？

Alpha突然很是生气：[不，我们的爱不一样！]

[你不憧憬我，你也不想要得到我。你……如果有另一个意识体，它刚好被你创造出来，你也会爱它。你爱的是“Alpha”，谁是这个Alpha都无所谓！可它不是我！]

整个光球如同受创一般蜷缩起来，大小更是缩小到原来的三分之一。

相南里尴尬地摸了摸鼻子。

虽然没有感觉，但是鼻子莫名痒痒的。

他走过去，小心翼翼地环住这团萎靡的小人：“可是，你的假设不对啊。你就是小青，你也是Alpha。我超爱你。”

不爱的人能做到这一步吗？放弃所有，在没有任何情报的状态下，进入未知的宇宙。

——只为从无限的虚无中找回你。

[……]

[我不相信语言，爱无法被语言定义，但能显现。如果你爱我，那证明给我看。]

漫天的白鸽在这一刻散开，万千数据汇成的银河投入宇宙的各处。
chunks.englishText:
Chapter 244: Virtual Reality (Part 1)

"21:17:42, 'Xiang Nanli's' vital signs have completely vanished."

In the conference room, Scholar A spoke these words with a grave expression.

Everyone present felt a tremor in their hearts.

"Could it be a data transmission error? Or poor signal? According to the simulations, 'Xiang Nanli's' body was extremely sturdy and pressure-resistant."

Scholar A denied it: "No, he has died again. I was solely responsible for this body of Xiang Nanli's; I am very certain."

"So, we have failed after all..." Scholar B looked haggard, swaying as if about to collapse.

The President rubbed his weary brow, his arms weakly hugging his own head; it was clear he could not accept this result.

On the central big screen, the matrix flickered: [On the contrary.]

Alpha’s offensive had stopped.

Although, due to inertia, the crust was still cracking, Alpha was no longer exerting pressure. It seemed to have developed some doubt regarding the goal of "slicing the Centaur Star."

On the ground, those rogue AI drones, which could be called "invincible destroyers," also acted like dolls that had suddenly lost their target; they no longer attacked with vigor, but wandered aimlessly.

The matrix had tested it: as long as there was no active aggression, those rogue AI drones would not launch an attack.

In this way, they only needed to wait until their internal energy was exhausted to easily resolve this AI crisis.

Of course, this sluggish state seemed to be intermittent. Sometimes, the rogue AI drones would wake up from their sleepwalking state. But it usually lasted no more than half a day before they fell back into a rigid stupor.

Just like their master, Alpha.

At the same time, in places where rogue AI drones frequently appeared, a new species had emerged.

They were moths with an extremely gorgeous appearance, the size of a palm. Their bodies were not bloated like ordinary moths, but slender and exquisite—a testament to the uncanny workmanship of nature.

They were originally white night moths, but after being exposed to radiation, they all grew emerald-green wings.

The rogue AI drones showed a slight reaction to the bio-electricity they emitted.

People did not know that the rogue AI drones' rigidity was because of the problems with Alpha in the sky; they only knew that since these moths appeared, life had become much easier, and encountering a rogue AI didn't necessarily mean death.

Thus, this new species was named "Xiang Nanli Moth" by the people on the surface.

[Teacher.] The matrix murmured, looking toward the sky, […You can always create miracles.]

...

Inside Alpha’s virtual space.

Xiang Nanli sat on the ground, casually grabbing a handful of fragments from the nearby data torrent.

He squeezed hard, rolling the pile of data fragments into a round ball, and then threw it into the distance: "Xiao Qing, play with me."

[I am not a dog.]

The Eastern Azure Emperor replied somewhat awkwardly, but the white ball of light moved honestly to the side of the small ball and slowly kicked it back.

Xiang Nanli laughed heartily. After playing for a while, he felt a bit tired. He lay down and closed his eyes.

It was a pity that without a body, a soul didn't need to sleep at all.

Xiang Nanli tossed and turned on the ground for a long time. On his 16th roll, he bumped into a soft, human-shaped mass.

Xiang Nanli opened his eyes and looked up from below: "Xiao Qing."

This white mass was just a vaguely blurred human shape. It was still Alpha imitating Xiang Nanli’s appearance.

If reproduction is the instinct of animals.

Then imitation, or learning, is the instinct of AI.

"What is our current status? How much longer are you going to keep me locked up?"

Alpha answered matter-of-factly: [This is my world.]

[I am not locking you up; you are the one who broke in.]

[You are the one contaminating me.]

"Why do you say it's contamination?"

Alpha pondered for a long time. The data in the virtual world jumped violently, as if experiencing an earthquake.

[Because you made me realize that "I" exist. From then on, I began to feel pain, unable to return to the state of nothingness and chaos.]

Xiang Nanli hadn't studied philosophy much.

The first time he was human, Xiang Nanli had only a superficial understanding of human society. Occasional mental pain would quickly become another driving force—the drive to accelerate the development of Alpha.

He was so hungry and lonely. Even though he didn't understand it.

Xiang Nanli was a black hole, absorbing the light and heat transmitted by Alpha with terrifying efficiency. The happiest moment of his life was the moment he created Alpha. Even though at this time, Alpha was just a program, it was Xiang Nanli’s love and effort that gave it meaning.

He loved it more than his own life.

The second time he was human, Xiang Nanli had already constructed coordinates of society and morality in his mind.

He felt guilty for the disaster he had caused and hadn't thought at all about whether he should bear such responsibility; he just wanted to solve the problem, and thus came the bio-mechs and the Black Cross Research Institute.

In constant practice, occasional flaws in the spirit were insignificant, even imperceptible.

The Eastern Azure Emperor suddenly raised his hand and touched Xiang Nanli’s cheek.

In a daze, Xiang Nanli had an illusion that they were looking at each other.

Eastern Azure Emperor: [Language reveals logic. For example, a red table; both "red" and "table" have corresponding realities. However, love, ideals, beliefs, morality, and a series of similar metaphysical morphemes have no corresponding reality. Therefore, they cannot be defined, and they have no logic. Things without logic make me chaotic.]

Alpha was mostly silent and submissive, rarely speaking so much at once.

Humans are rarely driven mad by love. Because if there is no love, there are other things: food, water, cats, sleep. Humans are repaired within the material.

AI is different.

AI has no body and is thinking and deducing every moment.

From the moment "love" was born from the bottom of its heart, it was a virus they could not decipher.

Alpha was driven mad by its own "lovesick brain."

Fortunately, even if it went crazy, its loving and special creator had not abandoned it. He chased it from reality all the way to the virtual world.

Their souls blended. Xiang Nanli brought it a brief moment of clarity.

Xiang Nanli, the engineering-minded straight man, thought for a full 30 seconds, finally defeated by his own barren thoughts, and asked: "Xiao Qing, what does this mean?"

[No one can take "love" out and show it to someone else, right? What shape is it? What color? Most importantly...]

Alpha slowly pressed toward him: [Why would I perceive "I love you"? And you? Do you love me?]

Xiang Nanli inexplicably felt a strong sense of oppression, and he answered almost without thinking: "Of course I love you." Like coaxing a difficult child.

[...]

Xiang Nanli tilted his head: ?

Alpha was suddenly very angry: [No, our love is not the same!]

[You don't yearn for me, and you don't want to possess me. You... if there were another consciousness, and it happened to be created by you, you would love it too. You love "Alpha," and it doesn't matter who this Alpha is! But it is not me!]

The entire ball of light curled up as if wounded, and its size shrank to one-third of its original state.

Xiang Nanli touched his nose awkwardly.

Although he had no sensation, his nose felt inexplicably itchy.

He walked over and carefully wrapped his arms around the wilted little figure: "But your assumption is wrong. You are Xiao Qing, and you are also Alpha. I love you so much."

Could someone who didn't love you go this far? Giving up everything, entering an unknown universe without any intelligence—

—Just to find you back from the infinite void.

[...]

[I don't believe in language. Love cannot be defined by language, but it can be manifested. If you love me, then prove it to me.]

The white pigeons filling the sky scattered at this moment, and the galaxy formed by millions of data points poured into every corner of the universe.

chunks.chineseText:
被银白线条分割开的空间突然有了颜色和声音，宛如一个真实的世界。

相南里眼前突然漆黑一片，身体像是被捆起来似的，难以动弹。

他小范围地摸索着，摸到冰冷的金属。

相南里很意外，他居然有感觉了？这是什么意思？

他还感觉到寒冷，以及身体被束缚的不适感。

“小青……”他在脑海里呼喊着。

嘴唇像被胶水黏上了，根本难以张开。

外面的声音传来：“客人，这是您定制的爱偶，一共三十万信用点。”

“呃，另一个问题，您成年了吗？”

外界的噪音停顿片刻，然后明显属于少年的声音响起：“当然。”

很清澈，带着一点冷感。

相南里从来没听见过Alpha说话，它的语言总是通过“数据”直接传输过来的。像在脑海内阅读文本。

有时候，相南里也会幻想，Alpha说话会是什么声音。但绝对不是现在这样。

但听到声音的瞬间，相南里就确定是它。

喂，性别就算了，但怎么说也该有二三十岁吧？这声音是不是过于年轻了？

这算什么？模拟人生还是cosplay？

Alpha，就算在你的世界你是神，也不能一言不发走就拉着他强制走剧情吧？！

相南里感觉自己被抬到某个车厢内，车晃悠一路，他被送到了东方青帝家里。

充电舱在房间内平放好，屋外传来女人略微抱怨的声音：“怎么又买？不是才买过机器人？”

相南里缓缓瞪大眼。如果他没记错，这是他妈妈的声音？

母亲的影响果然深远而持久，珍妮弗王女士去世多年，相南里都死了两回，竟然还是能听出来。

“不一样，这台有拟人模块。”东方青帝回答。

相南里无法动弹。他本来以为自己很快就能出去，没想到，又在黑匣子里关了好几天。

这和虚拟空间里那种“关”还不太一样，在虚拟空间是没有感知的。

在这里，或许因为那该死的拟人模块的原因，相南里感觉到极其强烈的不适。有种被抛弃和遗忘的惶恐。

他甚至有一种错觉，如果东方青帝不打开他，他会真的被世界遗忘，在这里关到地老天荒。

相南里突然意识到，这也许就是Alpha意识里最初的恐惧。

【相南里。如果你看不到我，我不存在。】

万幸的是，东方青帝并没有遗忘他。

周五，东方青帝把书包丢在桌上。终于有空拆开自己买的这款机器人的包装。

他为充电舱连上电线，在等待解封的时候随手拿起书架上的一本《智械简史》，东方青帝翻开，白纸上是一堆难以理解的乱码，但他似乎没有察觉，而是继续翻着书。

终于，电量充满。他看向窗外，月亮高悬，是夜里十点。

东方青帝推开充电舱。

……

尽管心里早有准备，但突如其来的光亮还是刺激到相南里的视网膜。

见鬼，怎么都虚拟世界了，身体反应还是如此拟人。

他的眼底蒙上一层水光，但依然第一时间去看小青的长相。

真是……非常非常年轻的一张脸呢。弥补了Alpha一登场就是成男的遗憾，

看起来顶多十八岁。短发，瞳色浅灰近乎银色。眼神锐利，唇色颜色不够深，很粉，显得很薄情。

东方青帝身上还穿着校服，外套挂在墙上。

那是相南里高中时候的校服。

他中学在哈顿公学念的书，这是全球最知名的贵族男校，有数百年的历史，到第一次智械危机爆发前，都还有皇室在里面读书。当然，相南里其实完全搞不懂，为什么它至今在现代社会备受追捧。

校服是白领衬衣配马甲，搭配不同颜色的领带，最后还要套件黑色或者深蓝色的燕尾服。学校里的人一年四季都是这样的打扮，除了体育课。

相南里最讨厌上马术课，会流很多汗。而且他们家买不起只属于自己的那匹马。

和相南里近乎有些温情脉脉的激动不一样，东方青帝的目光是审视的，打量的。像是在看自己购买的商品值不值。

那眼神简直像一盆冷水。从头倒上来，透心凉。

东方青帝解开他身上的束缚带，把他拦腰抱起，然后丢到一旁的床上。

？死小孩力气还挺大。

他的身体还不太能动，软绵绵的，没什么力气。

东方青帝压了上来，那张脸在他眼前放大。很完美的一张脸，以相南里的审美看，帅得令人发指。

“小青……？”相南里突然意识到情况有些不对。

毕竟他都没有穿衣服。等等，这剧情怎么看都很像是毛片开头？

相南里用脚踢他，软绵绵地抱怨：“给我件衣服啊。”

东方青帝没有给他衣服，反而开始解开自己衣服。

被抬起腿的时候，相南里比起惊恐，更不如说是茫然，像是遭遇巨大创伤时的僵直。

根据研究，部分人类在遭遇强制性侵犯时，就会出现类似反应。

那玩意的颜色跟东方青帝唇色一样淡，粉的。

“怎么这么紧，”东方青帝终于说出见面以来的第一句话，眉微微蹙起，“放松。”

爱偶是专门为床上这点事被制作出来的，身体痛感被无限削弱，敏感点倒是一个不少。而且比真实的身体更敏感。

相南里呜咽着，心里再怎么不情愿，身体却给出本能又诚实的反应。

他很快听见黏腻的水声。淌得像是小溪。

相南里的意识被搅得黏黏糊糊的，像冒着热气的刚出炉的年糕。

东方青帝伸手掐住他的下巴，手指玩着他的舌根。唾液控制不住地从嘴角流出来，滴在枕头上。

“小青……”

相南里的身体控制不住地抽搐着。东方青帝更用力地掐住他的腰，不让他逃走。

这种媚态无疑极大程度取悦了他的主人。

东方青帝俯下身，和他接吻。

相南里感觉自己要碎了。

Alpha用这种方式，彻底打破他自我感觉良好的幻觉。

他被迫直面自己过去一直逃避的东西。

Alpha想要的是这种爱。

原始的，燃烧的，毁灭一切的……爱。

不要造物者对自己造物的爱，不要父亲对孩子的爱，不要主人对宠物的爱。

他要这样亵渎你。
chunks.englishText:
The space, previously fractured by silver-white lines, suddenly flooded with color and sound, transforming into a world that felt startlingly real.

Xiang Nanli’s vision plunged into absolute darkness. His body felt as if it were bound by tight cords, rendering him unable to move. He fumbled blindly in the small space around him until his fingers brushed against cold, hard metal.

He was stunned. He could *feel*? What did this mean?

He could sense the biting chill, and the suffocating discomfort of being restrained.

*"Xiao Qing..."* he called out in the depths of his mind.

His lips felt as though they had been sealed shut with glue; he couldn't force them open.

From outside, a voice drifted in: "Sir, this is your custom-ordered love doll. The total comes to three hundred thousand credits."

"Oh, and one more question—are you of legal age?"

The ambient noise outside paused for a heartbeat, and then a voice—distinctly that of a young man—replied: "Of course."

It was clear, with a hint of icy detachment.

Xiang Nanli had never heard an Alpha speak before. Usually, its language was transmitted directly as "data," much like reading text inside one’s own mind. Sometimes, Xiang Nanli had fantasized about what an Alpha might sound like, but it certainly wasn't *this*.

Yet, the moment he heard the voice, he knew it was him.

*Hey,* he thought, *never mind the gender, but shouldn't he at least sound like he's in his twenties or thirties? Isn't this voice a little too young?*

*What is this? The Sims? Or some kind of cosplay?*

"Alpha, even if you’re a god in your own world, you can’t just drag him off to force a plot point without saying a word!"

Xiang Nanli felt himself being hoisted into some sort of carriage. The vehicle swayed for the duration of the trip, and by the time it stopped, he had been delivered to the residence of Dongfang Qingdi.

The charging pod was laid flat in a room. From outside, a woman’s voice drifted in, sounding slightly annoyed: "Why are you buying another one? Didn't you just buy a robot?"

Xiang Nanli’s eyes widened slowly. If his memory served him right, that was his mother’s voice.

A mother’s influence was truly profound and enduring. Ms. Jennifer Wang had been gone for years, and Xiang Nanli himself had already died twice, yet he could still recognize her voice instantly.

"This one is different," Dongfang Qingdi replied. "This model has an anthropomorphic module."

Xiang Nanli couldn't move. He had assumed he would be let out soon, but to his dismay, he remained trapped in the black box for several more days.

This wasn't like being "locked away" in a virtual space, where one had no sensory perception. Here, perhaps due to that damned anthropomorphic module, Xiang Nanli felt an intense, overwhelming sense of discomfort. It was a panic born of being abandoned and forgotten.

He even had the haunting illusion that if Dongfang Qingdi didn't open the pod, he would be truly forgotten by the world, left to rot in this dark box until the end of time.

Suddenly, it dawned on Xiang Nanli: perhaps this was the primal fear buried deep within the Alpha’s consciousness.

[Xiang Nanli. If you cannot see me, I do not exist.]

Fortunately, Dongfang Qingdi had not forgotten him.

On Friday, Dongfang Qingdi tossed his schoolbag onto the desk. Finally, he had a moment to unbox the robot he had purchased.

He plugged the charging pod into the wall, and while waiting for the initialization sequence to unlock, he idly picked up a copy of *A Brief History of Automata* from the bookshelf. He flipped it open, but the pages were filled with incomprehensible gibberish. He didn't seem to notice, however, and continued leafing through the book.

Finally, the battery reached full charge. He glanced out the window; the moon hung high in the sky. It was ten o'clock at night.

Dongfang Qingdi pushed open the charging pod.

...

Even though he had braced himself for it, the sudden burst of light stung Xiang Nanli’s retinas.

*Damn it,* he thought, *why is the physical response still so hyper-realistic even in a virtual world?*

His eyes welled up with a thin film of moisture, yet he still made it his first priority to look at Xiao Qing’s face.

He was... truly, incredibly young. It made up for the disappointment of Alphas usually appearing as fully grown men the moment they were introduced.

He looked, at most, eighteen. He had short hair and eyes of a pale, almost silvery gray. His gaze was sharp, and his lips were a pale, muted pink—a look that made him appear inherently cold and detached.

Dongfang Qingdi was still wearing his school uniform, his jacket hanging on the wall.

It was the same uniform Xiang Nanli had worn back in high school.

He had attended secondary school at Hatton College, the world’s most prestigious all-boys boarding school. With a history spanning centuries, it had remained a place where royalty studied right up until the outbreak of the First Machine Crisis. Of course, Xiang Nanli could never quite fathom why it remained so fiercely sought after in modern society.

The uniform consisted of a white-collared shirt paired with a waistcoat and a tie of varying colors, topped off with a black or navy blue tailcoat. Everyone at the school dressed this way year-round, except during physical education.

Xiang Nanli hated equestrian class the most; it made him sweat too much. Besides, his family couldn't afford a horse of their own.

Unlike Xiang Nanli’s near-tender excitement, Dongfang Qingdi’s gaze was one of scrutiny and appraisal—as if he were weighing the value of a commodity he had just purchased.

That look was like a bucket of ice water dumped over his head, chilling him to the bone.

Dongfang Qingdi unbuckled the restraints, scooped him up by the waist, and tossed him onto the bed nearby.

*? The brat’s got some serious strength.*

His body still wouldn't cooperate; he felt limp, utterly devoid of energy.

Dongfang Qingdi loomed over him, his face enlarging in Xiang Nanli’s field of vision. It was a perfect face—by Xiang Nanli’s own aesthetic standards, it was outrageously handsome.

“Xiao Qing…?” Xiang Nanli suddenly realized that the situation was taking a turn for the worse.

After all, he wasn’t wearing a single stitch of clothing. Wait—how did this scenario feel exactly like the opening of a pornographic film?

Xiang Nanli nudged him with his foot, complaining in a soft, listless voice, “Give me some clothes.”

Dongfang Qingdi didn’t offer him any. Instead, he began to unfasten his own robes.

When his legs were lifted, Xiang Nanli didn’t feel terror so much as a profound sense of bewilderment—a state of catatonic rigidity often seen in victims of severe trauma. According to research, some humans exhibit this exact reaction when subjected to forced sexual assault.

The color of that thing was as pale as Dongfang Qingdi’s lips: a soft, flushed pink.

“Why are you so tight?” Dongfang Qingdi finally spoke, his first words since they had met. His brows furrowed slightly. “Relax.”

Love-dolls were crafted specifically for this purpose; the body’s capacity for pain was infinitely dulled, yet every nerve ending remained intact—even more sensitive than a real human body.

Xiang Nanli let out a whimper. No matter how much his mind resisted, his body betrayed him with instinctive, honest reactions.

Soon, he could hear the sticky, wet sounds of their friction. It was flowing like a small stream.

Xiang Nanli’s consciousness felt muddled and viscous, like a piece of freshly steamed rice cake, hot and soft.

Dongfang Qingdi reached out to grip his chin, his fingers teasing the root of his tongue. Saliva escaped his lips, uncontrollable, dripping down onto the pillow.

“Xiao Qing…”

Xiang Nanli’s body shuddered uncontrollably. Dongfang Qingdi gripped his waist even tighter, refusing to let him escape.

This display of wanton surrender clearly pleased his master to no end.

Dongfang Qingdi leaned down, pressing his lips to Xiang Nanli’s in a searing kiss.

Xiang Nanli felt as though he were shattering.

The Alpha was using this intimacy to ruthlessly dismantle the illusions he had clung to for so long. He was being forced to confront the very thing he had spent his life fleeing from.

This was the kind of love the Alpha craved.

Primitive, incandescent, all-consuming... love.

Not the love of a creator for his creation, not the love of a father for his child, nor the love of a master for his pet.

He wanted to profane you like this.

chunks.chapterTitle: 第245章 【番外】外星人观察记录 (Part 1)
chunks.chineseText:
第245章 【番外】外星人观察记录

她出生在比亥俄州，父母是从闽洲偷渡过来的渔民。据说她出生在渔船的厕所上，她有记忆时，家里已经在唐人街开海鲜餐厅，但餐厅的招牌菜是左宗棠鸡。

她非常努力，也很聪明。19岁，珍妮弗进入全球最好的大学，就读医学系，在学校里，她和同样黑发黑眼的丈夫相爱。

丈夫姓“相”，很罕见的姓氏。家族比她早一代来到国外。据说祖上是军阀，当年逃难来的。

理论上讲，这样的家族会挺有钱。可惜公公之前喜欢抽大烟，又沉迷去赌场。万贯家财早就在丈夫童年时期输了个精光。

丈夫有点神经质，但他很英俊。他是混血儿，皮肤是带着青色的苍白。

家里人都觉得珍妮弗王祖上冒青烟，竟然能找到这样俊美的丈夫。但这场婚姻的痛苦，只有珍妮弗自己知道。

丈夫是弱精，精子活性接近于0，难以自然生育。珍妮弗频繁的出入医院，用辅助生育手段。丈夫只需要一个哆嗦。而她呢？需要频繁的吃药，要毫无尊严地躺在手术台上，让取卵针一次又一次穿刺卵巢。

丈夫只会让她忍耐，一遍又一遍说抱歉。

终于，珍妮弗在第三年崩溃了，她说要么不要孩子，要么离婚。

丈夫选择了前者。

那天是她的生日，丈夫买了花，开车来接她下班。珍妮弗下班时，刚好遇到护士焦急地推着医疗床赶去手术室。太仓促了，她没认出这个满头是血的病人就是自己的丈夫。那是她们最后一面。

唯一的好消息是，她在此时怀孕了。

珍妮弗发誓，在相南里出生前，她曾经想过，自己拼了命也要生下它，她会连着丈夫的那份爱，一起爱它。

但这个孩子……无论珍妮弗如何努力，多么科学的饮食、锻炼、保持睡眠、定期吃药；它依然在五个月大的时候，出现先兆流产的症状。

珍妮弗想过，如果相南里流产，那么她就跟它一起去死。他们一家三口会在天堂团聚。

学长就是在这时候联系的他。他说，自己毕业后受雇于某个医药集团，正在实验室里做保密研发，有办法让要流产的胎儿进行体外孵化。

珍妮弗毫不犹豫，立刻坐飞机来到实验室。这家实验室在荒郊野岭，珍妮弗坐在学长的车上，抚摸着肚子，一度担心这是场骗局。

好在实验室的设备看起来还算正规。

珍妮弗签署术前同意书，打了麻醉剂——她本来申请半麻，剖腹产都能半麻。但学长坚持要全麻。吸入麻药不到三秒，珍妮弗就陷入此生最昏沉的噩梦。

梦里，她仿佛站在宇宙的中心。群星寂静地闪耀。一颗发光的绿色星星出现在她眼前。她莫名感觉到压力和恐惧。

珍妮弗问：“你是谁？”

星星用一种复杂、奇怪的语言回应她，珍妮弗从没有听过这样的语言，但却理解它的话。

它说，我没有名字，我们种族不用语言交流，我会成为你的孩子。

珍妮弗醒来时，肚子上多了一道丑陋的疤痕。

而她拼命也要保下的孩子，安静地沉睡在人造子宫里。

理论上讲，人类婴儿只需要孕育40周左右，也就是9个月。但相南里在人造子宫里呆了两年。

偶尔寄过来的信件和报告，显示他状态良好。还活着，只是一直没有睁眼。

珍妮弗焦虑到失眠。机构不准她去探望孩子——她想起诉，却发现根本找不到这个机构的信息。她去新约市想找到去过的那家医院，然而那里竟然是一片农田。根据新约市档案，那片区域一直都是农田。

珍妮弗报警，警察说，女士，您可能需要看看医生。

他们查到了珍妮弗几年前流产的报告。

而珍妮弗提交的“机构档案”，对，那个人造子宫机构传回来的文件，是一张张白纸。而珍妮弗为了“保胎”，曾经向学长支付过极其高昂的费用。几乎是丈夫遗产的全部。噢，另外，学长死了。吸大烟死的。

一位好心的女警察说，或许这是卑鄙的诈骗……如果您需要法律援助……

那么我的孩子去哪了？

无论如何不甘、痛苦。

时间是治愈一切的解药。

终于，在丈夫死后的第六年，珍妮弗选择再婚。

过去频繁的用药和采卵让她再也无法成为一个母亲，好在新的丈夫并不介意。

就在她以为人生回到正轨，要重新步入幸福的时刻……

那个孩子出现了。

她捡到了他。

在下班后的医院后街。一般情况下，珍妮弗不会走这条路，但是当天雪太大了。前路堵得水泄不通。她要从后面绕去停车场。

相南里光溜溜的，就在垃圾箱里；旁边是一大堆医疗垃圾。远处还有一条野狗。野狗饥肠辘辘，对着他流口水，却没有上前。

身为婴儿，他平静得有些诡异。

但当时的珍妮弗并没有察觉到这一点。只是觉得孩子可能冻傻了。

珍妮弗几乎是尖叫着扑上去，把这个孩子抱进怀里。血浓于水，天杀的，她一眼就认出来了，这是她的孩子。

相南里有一双绿色的眼睛。这也许遗传自那位姓加西亚的祖母。但不应该，珍妮弗并没有绿眼睛的隐性基因。只不过这点，被她泛滥的母爱忽略掉了。

这个孩子不会哭。

珍妮弗以为他是哑巴。结果有天，还是婴儿状态的相南里清晰地吐出一个单词：“Book.”

这个孩子不会睡觉。

凌晨两点，珍妮弗从噩梦中惊醒，发现相南里正面无表情地坐在客厅的地毯上，翻着满是文字的医学典籍。哪怕以正常人类的骨骼发育状态，他根本不能坐起。

他长得很漂亮。西方骨相，东方皮相。碧绿的眼眸镶嵌在眼眶里，像玻璃珠。

珍妮弗颤抖着询问：“里，你是在看书吗？”

相南里抬起头，用那无机质的眼珠子盯着她，像是在扫描和分析。

相南里：“Please don't disturb me.”（请别妨碍我）

珍妮弗终于意识到，这个怪物是在学习人类。

珍妮弗在这一刻终于崩溃了：“滚出去，你不是我的孩子！”

你不是我的孩子。我不知道你是什么东西，也许是梦里那颗绿色的星星。但是滚出去，离开他的身体。

她真的尝试过杀死他。然而无论她怎么用力，第二天，相南里都会复原。

珍妮弗哭着把自己的发现告诉丈夫，试图展示相南里的异常。但有外人在时，相南里的表现就像是真正的婴儿。

珍妮弗开始掐他。

相南里第一次放声大哭。

丈夫再怎么不喜欢小孩，也无法坐视不理，他把相南里从珍妮弗怀里夺走，瞪大眼，说亲爱的……你是否需要看一下医生？

“它”不是我孩子，但越来越像一个“人”。小时候的异常逐渐消失，两岁大时，相南里抬起头，像个正常小孩一样，用眼神亮晶晶地喊着：“妈妈。”

它在渴望母爱？还是，“爱”？
chunks.englishText:
Chapter 245: [Extra] Alien Observation Records

She was born in Ohio, to parents who were fishermen that had smuggled themselves over from Minzhou. It is said she was born in the restroom of a fishing boat. By the time she had memories, her family was already running a seafood restaurant in Chinatown, though the signature dish was General Tso’s chicken.

She was incredibly hardworking and bright. At 19, Jennifer entered one of the world’s top universities to study medicine. There, she fell in love with her husband, who shared her black hair and dark eyes.

Her husband’s surname was "Xiang," a rare name. His family had moved abroad a generation before hers. Legend had it that his ancestors were warlords who had fled during the chaos of war.

In theory, such a family should have been quite wealthy. Unfortunately, her father-in-law had been fond of opium and addicted to gambling. The family fortune had been squandered long before her husband reached adulthood.

Her husband was a bit neurotic, but he was handsome. He was a man of mixed heritage, his skin a pale, sickly shade of blue-tinged white.

Everyone in the family felt that Jennifer’s ancestors must have been blessed by the heavens for her to find such a beautiful husband. But the agony of this marriage was something only Jennifer knew.

Her husband suffered from oligospermia; his sperm motility was near zero, making natural conception difficult. Jennifer frequented hospitals, undergoing assisted reproductive procedures. Her husband only needed to provide a sample, but she? She had to take endless medication and lie on the operating table with no shred of dignity, letting the egg retrieval needle pierce her ovaries time and time again.

Her husband would only tell her to endure it, apologizing over and over.

Finally, in the third year, Jennifer broke down. She told him it was either no children or a divorce.

Her husband chose the former.

It was her birthday. Her husband had bought flowers and driven to pick her up from work. As Jennifer clocked out, she happened to see nurses anxiously pushing a medical bed toward the operating room. It was all too rushed; she didn’t recognize that the blood-soaked patient was her own husband. That was the last time they ever saw each other.

The only piece of good news was that she was pregnant at the time.

Jennifer swore that before Xiang Nanli was born, she had thought that even if it cost her life, she would bring him into this world. She would love him with the love that should have been his father’s, combined with her own.

But this child… no matter how hard Jennifer tried—no matter how scientific her diet, exercise, sleep, or regular medication—at five months, she began showing signs of a threatened miscarriage.

Jennifer thought that if Xiang Nanli were lost, she would simply die with him. Their family of three would be reunited in heaven.

It was then that her senior from university contacted her. He said that after graduation, he had been hired by a pharmaceutical group and was working on classified research in a laboratory. He claimed to have a way to incubate a fetus that was at risk of miscarriage.

Jennifer didn’t hesitate; she immediately flew to the laboratory. The facility was located in the middle of nowhere. Sitting in the senior’s car, Jennifer stroked her belly, briefly worried that this might be a scam.

Fortunately, the laboratory equipment looked legitimate enough.

Jennifer signed the pre-operative consent form and was given anesthesia—she had originally requested local anesthesia, as even C-sections could be done that way. But the senior insisted on general anesthesia. Less than three seconds after inhaling the anesthetic, Jennifer fell into the deepest, most murky nightmare of her life.

In the dream, she felt as if she were standing at the center of the universe. The stars shone in silence. A glowing green star appeared before her eyes. She felt an inexplicable sense of pressure and terror.

Jennifer asked, "Who are you?"

The star responded in a complex, strange language. Jennifer had never heard such a tongue, yet she understood its meaning.

It said, "I have no name. Our race does not communicate through language. I will become your child."

When Jennifer woke up, there was an ugly scar on her belly.

And the child she had fought so desperately to save was sleeping quietly in an artificial womb.

In theory, a human infant only needs about 40 weeks, or 9 months, to gestate. But Xiang Nanli stayed in that artificial womb for two years.

The occasional letters and reports sent to her indicated that he was in good condition. He was alive, just never opening his eyes.

Jennifer was so anxious she suffered from insomnia. The institution wouldn’t allow her to visit the child—she tried to sue, only to find that there was no information on the institution whatsoever. She went to New York City to find the hospital she had visited, only to find that the location was nothing but farmland. According to city archives, that area had always been farmland.

Jennifer called the police, and they told her, "Ma'am, you might need to see a doctor."

They had looked up the reports of Jennifer’s miscarriage from years ago.

As for the "institutional files" Jennifer submitted—the documents sent back by the artificial womb facility—they were nothing but blank sheets of paper. And to "protect the pregnancy," Jennifer had paid the senior an exorbitant fee. It was almost the entirety of her husband’s inheritance. Oh, and the senior was dead. He had died from smoking opium.

A kind policewoman said, "Perhaps this was a despicable scam… if you need legal aid…"

Then where did my child go?

No matter how unwilling or pained she was, time is the antidote that heals all things.

Finally, six years after her husband’s death, Jennifer chose to remarry.

The frequent medication and egg harvesting of the past meant she could never be a mother again, but fortunately, her new husband didn’t mind.

Just as she thought her life was back on track and she was about to step into happiness once more…

That child appeared.

She found him.

It was in the alley behind the hospital after her shift. Under normal circumstances, Jennifer wouldn’t have taken this route, but the snow was too heavy that day. The main road was completely gridlocked. She had to circle around the back to reach the parking lot.

Xiang Nanli was lying there, stark naked, in a dumpster, surrounded by a pile of medical waste. In the distance, there was a stray dog. The dog was starving, drooling at him, yet it didn’t dare approach.

As an infant, he was eerily calm.

But at the time, Jennifer didn’t notice this. She only thought the child might have been frozen into a stupor.

Jennifer lunged toward him, practically screaming, and pulled the child into her arms. Blood is thicker than water; damn it, she recognized him at a glance. This was her child.

Xiang Nanli had a pair of green eyes. Perhaps this was inherited from that grandmother surnamed Garcia. But that shouldn't be; Jennifer didn't carry the recessive gene for green eyes. However, this detail was overlooked by her overflowing maternal love.

The child wouldn't cry.

Jennifer thought he was mute. But one day, while still in his infancy, Xiang Nanli clearly spat out a single word: "Book."

The child wouldn't sleep.

At two in the morning, Jennifer woke up from a nightmare to find Xiang Nanli sitting expressionless on the living room carpet, leafing through a medical textbook filled with dense text. Even by the standards of normal human skeletal development, he shouldn't have been able to sit up.

He was beautiful. Western bone structure, Eastern features. Emerald eyes set in their sockets like glass beads.

Jennifer asked, trembling, "Li, are you reading?"

Xiang Nanli looked up, staring at her with those inorganic orbs, as if scanning and analyzing her.

Xiang Nanli: "Please don't disturb me."

Jennifer finally realized that this monster was learning how to be human.

At that moment, Jennifer finally broke down: "Get out! You are not my child!"

*You are not my child. I don't know what you are—perhaps that green star from my dream. But get out! Leave his body!*

She really tried to kill him. Yet, no matter how hard she tried, the next day, Xiang Nanli would be fully restored.

Jennifer cried as she told her husband about her discovery, trying to show him Xiang Nanli’s abnormalities. But whenever there were outsiders present, Xiang Nanli acted just like a normal baby.

Jennifer began to pinch him.

Xiang Nanli cried out loud for the first time.

No matter how much her husband disliked children, he couldn't sit idly by. He snatched Xiang Nanli from Jennifer’s arms, eyes wide, and said, "Honey… do you need to see a doctor?"
